We mentioned this, brothers, but apparently you forget.

In His saying: ﴿So whoever is compelled by hunger⁠﴾, that is, in famine; ﴿not inclining toward sin⁠﴾, that is, leaning toward sin, by eating without necessity, or by exceeding necessity. But ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing⁠﴾ [Al-Baqarah 173] in another verse: some said that ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing⁠﴾ explains the verse of al-Ma'idah, and the verse of al-Ma'idah is among the last revealed, so ﴿neither desiring⁠﴾ means eating carrion, and ﴿nor transgressing⁠﴾ means eating more than necessity, and this explanation matches the other verse.

Others said: ﴿neither desiring⁠﴾: the rebels (al-bughat) are those who rebel against the imam; ﴿nor transgressing⁠﴾ means disobedient in his journey. But one may ask: where is this meaning in the verse? It is very far. For this reason they said: whoever is disobedient in his journey, even if he is compelled and even if he dies, he does not eat carrion, because it is a condition that the journey be permissible. The correct view is otherwise: the Qur'an explains part of itself by part, and His saying ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing⁠﴾ corresponds exactly to His saying ﴿in famine, not inclining toward sin⁠﴾.

In the noble verse He says: ﴿So whoever is compelled in famine, not inclining toward sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Do we derive from this a ruling for the one compelled to eat carrion? ﴿whoever is compelled⁠﴾, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾. What do you understand from the verse?

Student: There is no sin upon him if he is compelled to eat.

Shaykh: That is, whoever is compelled, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning Allah forgives him?

Student: He is not held accountable.

Shaykh: That is, Allah forgives him and has mercy on him: He forgave his sin by eating this forbidden thing, and had mercy on him by permitting it to him. We mentioned to you about this verse, or others, that what a verse ends with is used to derive a ruling. Did we mention this or not?

Student: We mentioned it.

Shaykh: We mentioned this, and among its examples is this verse, and among its examples is His saying regarding highway robbers: ﴿except those who repent before you overpower them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 34], meaning the punishment is dropped from them. We also mentioned to you the story of a Bedouin who heard a reciter recite the saying of Allah: "And as for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as recompense for what they earned, a punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty and Wise," and the Bedouin said to the reciter: "You made a mistake; recite." He repeated it as he had first recited it: "a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." He said: "Repeat it, is it not so?" Then he recited: ﴿a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 38]. He said: "Now you are right." What is the reason? He said: "Because He is Mighty and judges, so He cut off the hand; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut it." This is correct, and it is a clear deduction.

So ﴿whoever is compelled in famine, not inclining toward sin⁠﴾ is forgiven his sin by eating, and moreover it is made lawful for him by the mercy of Allah. We have taken its benefits, I think?

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: Good.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them⁠﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 4]. The doer of ﴿they ask you⁠﴾ is the Companions, and the Companions only asked the Messenger ﷺ about something beneficial for them, either in religion or in worldly affairs, and also because it was unclear to them. Allah mentioned in the Qur'an about twelve instances of the Companions' questions to him. Did the Messenger answer them? The verse indicates that he did not answer them, as evidenced by Allah saying to him: ﴿Say⁠﴾, meaning in answer to them: ﴿Lawful for you are the good things⁠﴾ and so on.

Know that the word "as'ala" (to ask) is sometimes used to mean asking for property, and sometimes used to mean inquiring. When it is used for asking for property, it takes two objects; when it is used for inquiring, it takes one object and then reaches the second with "ʿan" (about). Pay attention: if you want to ask a man for a dirham, you say: "I ask you a dirham." From this is the saying of Allah: "Whoever asks me, I will give to him," meaning whoever asks me for something, so the second object is omitted, its meaning understood from the context. And if you want to ask about a lost item that you lost, you say: "I ask you about my lost item," and you say: "So-and-so asked me about such-and-such a matter." It transfers—I told you—to the second object with what? With "ʿan."

If someone says: what is the answer to His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a torment that will befall⁠﴾ [Al-Ma'arij 1]? We say: the answer to this is disputed among scholars. Whoever says: when a verb is transitive to an object with a preposition it does not normally take, it is given a meaning suitable to the preposition it takes; and whoever says: the preposition is interpreted by the preposition suitable to the verb. Do you understand this? If the verb reaches its object with a preposition that is customarily used with it, the matter is clear; if the customary preposition is not used with it, the grammarians differ: is the preposition interpreted by what suits the verb, or the verb interpreted by what suits the preposition? Do you understand? Let us see. Allah says: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink⁠﴾ [Al-Insan 6]. ﴿from which the servants of Allah drink⁠﴾: what suits ﴿drink⁠﴾?

Students: "Minha" (from it).

Shaykh: "Minha," as He says: ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them⁠﴾ [Al-Baqarah 249]. But the verse came with ﴿bihā⁠﴾ (with it). On the view that the preposition takes the meaning of the preposition suitable to the verb, we say: the "bi" in ﴿yashrabu bihā⁠﴾ means "min" (from). On the second view, we seek a meaning suitable to "bi": so ﴿yashrabu⁠﴾ includes the meaning of ﴿yarwā⁠﴾ (to quench one's thirst), and then the meaning is: a spring by which the servants of Allah quench their thirst. Do you understand? Which is more eloquent?

Students: The first.

Other students: The second.

Shaykh: The second is more eloquent, because quenching thirst entails drinking, not the reverse, and then the figurative usage is in the verb, not the preposition. This is the view of the grammarians of Basra, and it is what Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, chose in the introduction to the Tafsir.

Returning to the verse: ﴿A questioner asked about a torment that will befall⁠﴾. Whoever says the figurative usage is in the preposition says: "bi" here means "ʿan." And whoever says the figurative usage is in the verb says: ﴿asked⁠﴾ here includes the meaning of answering: someone asked and was answered with a torment that will befall. This is more correct, as we said.

In our verse: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them⁠﴾: is the question about property or knowledge?

Students: Knowledge.

Shaykh: Knowledge. ﴿What has been made lawful for them⁠﴾: "dha" here means "alladhi" (that which). Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said:
"And like 'mā dhā' after an interrogative..."

That is, like the general relative forms, "dhā" after "mā" interrogative, that is, after the interrogative "mā": what is it that has been made lawful for them? The deputy subject refers to "mā," and who is the one who makes lawful? Allah.

﴿Say: Lawful for you are the good things⁠﴾, that is, lawful for you are the good foods. Allah says describing the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the evil things﴾ [Al-A'raf 157]. The meaning of the two verses, and Allah knows best, is that everything Allah made lawful is good, and everything He forbade is evil; yet not every evil thing is forbidden. This is shown by the Prophet ﷺ describing garlic as an evil tree but not forbidding it.

﴿And what the trained hunting animals have caught for you, training them⁠﴾: meaning, and lawful for you is what hunting animals catch, that you trained, ﴿trained them as Allah has taught you⁠﴾, that is, teaching them. ﴿Trained them as Allah has taught you⁠﴾. It may be that ﴿mukallibīn⁠﴾ means ﴿wounding⁠﴾, meaning these predators wound what they catch; ﴿you train them⁠﴾, that is, the animals; ﴿as Allah has taught you⁠﴾, that is, in how to hunt.

﴿So eat of what they catch for you⁠﴾: ﴿eat⁠﴾ is for permission, and the imperative here is for permission; ﴿of what they catch for you⁠﴾: "min" here is explanatory, not partitive. ﴿Catch for you⁠﴾ means for you; and here we say what was said before: ﴿of what they catch for you⁠﴾, that is, of what they hold back for you, or what they hold back upon you, meaning carried to you, or what resembles that, according to the view of interpreting the verb; and as for the view that the figurative usage is in the preposition, "ʿalā" means "lām," that is, what they catch for you.

﴿And mention the name of Allah over it⁠﴾: mention the name of Allah over it when? At eating, or at releasing the animal?

Students: At releasing...

Student: Both.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 4 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: The truth is that both apply. The Sunnah indicates that one says the basmalah when releasing the hunting animal, and the Qur'an indicates that one says it when one holds the game and intends to eat. So the basmalah is pronounced both at eating and at release.
﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ "And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning." ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ means: take a shield against His punishment, by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ "Indeed, Allah is severe in punishment." This sentence is declarative and emphasized with (inna). Its purpose is to warn against neglecting taqwa: whoever does not fear Allah will be punished, and Allah is severe in punishment.
* A student: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾. Yes, I made a mistake. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ means: Allah will call you to account for your deeds, and He is swift in reckoning. This includes swiftness of execution in one respect and swiftness of time in another. As for swiftness of time, how quickly the world passes; suddenly a person has finished. As for swiftness of execution, Allah will reckon all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, despite their number; He will reckon them in half a day, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا﴾ [al-Furqan 24].
* The verse contains many benefits, among them: the eagerness of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) for knowledge, based on His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ﴾.
From this we learn that what the Companions did not ask about, of the matters of the unseen that arise in question in our age, asking about it is an innovation (bid'ah), because we know that if there were good in knowing it, Allah would have inspired the Companions to ask about it until the matter became clear.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: permitting and forbidding belong not to the servants but to Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has warned us against making things lawful or unlawful according to our desires, saying: ﴿وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ هَذَا حَلَالٌ وَهَذَا حَرَامٌ لِتَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ [al-Nahl 116].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not independently make things lawful or unlawful. What is its basis?
* A student: Because he did not answer them (ﷺ), rather (...) Allah, glory be to Him.
* The Shaykh: The Messenger did not answer them, but Allah answered them. The Prophet (ﷺ) himself made this explicit, when he said to the Companions: "Whoever eats of this foul plant, let him not come near our mosques." The Companions began saying: "It has been forbidden, it has been forbidden." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Indeed, it is not for me to forbid what Allah has made lawful, but I dislike its smell."[[Narrated by Muslim (565 / 76) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]
* A student: Shaykh, do the nuṣub mean idols, or every built thing?
* The Shaykh: What is meant is what is set up (nuṣiba).
* The student: Shaykh, now people slaughter at graves; they slaughter for Allah but seek intercession through them.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: If they do not slaughter for the grave itself, it is lawful. But their act is a kind of shirk.
* The student: Did they not slaughter for the arzam?
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* The student: Was it slaughtered on the nuṣub?
* The Shaykh: No, they did not slaughter upon them. They slaughtered for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but believed this place to be more excellent.
* A student: In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ (...)?
* The Shaykh: It has not come; the benefits have not reached us.
* A student: Is it said that one who is compelled by hunger, not inclining toward sin, should seek forgiveness after eating carrion, for example?
* The Shaykh: It is not said that. Rather, he should praise Allah. "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel and praises Him for it, and drinks a draught and praises Him for it."[[Narrated by Muslim (2734 / 88) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]
* A student: O Shaykh, there is a rule in grammar (...) we carry one particle on another particle for the same verb, is it easier (...)?
* The Shaykh: We say:
"If you cannot do something, leave it and pass on to what you can do."
* A student: For example, meaning..
* The Shaykh: No. Ta'diyah (implicit transitivity) is undoubtedly stronger, stronger because it implies the verb that transitively takes this particle plus more. This may, if you wish, be treated as an exception.
* A student: Not all game is eaten, and the verse is specific to what requires hunting. Is the skin eaten?
* The Shaykh: No. If you wish, eat the skin; and if you wish, eat the feathers too; there is no objection!
* The student: How can (...)?
* The Shaykh: Like saying: a ring of iron, and what is similar to that.
* A student: May Allah pardon you. Who said that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عليهمُ الْخَبَائِثَ﴾ is evidence that all foul things are forbidden, by the evidence of the hadith of garlic, when the Prophet (ﷺ) described it as foul, the Companions thought it was forbidden, and since it was not foul in every respect, the Prophet (ﷺ) excepted it, that it is not covered by it..
* The Shaykh: No, this is not sound; because the Companions only said "it has been forbidden" when he who ate it was barred from attending the prayer-place; it is not necessarily because of its foulness.
* The student: Many scholars cite this verse as evidence for the prohibition of tobacco?
* The Shaykh: This is not correct, not at all correct. And this is what made us say so: every forbidden thing is foul, but not every foul thing is forbidden.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ﴾ (...) a beast of which part was eaten by a predator, and part remained and (...)?
* The Shaykh: It is eaten, because He said: ﴿إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾.
Let us continue with the benefits.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: everything Allah has made lawful is good, beneficial to the body, beneficial to the heart, beneficial to the individual, and beneficial to society, based on His saying: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ﴾. By implication, whatever Allah has forbidden is foul.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of what trained hunting animals catch. What are the jawarih? Is every predator's meat eaten, meaning is what it catches eaten? We say: yes, every predator, but on condition that it be trained. The animals most accepting of training are dogs, which is for beasts; then falcons, which is for birds. If it is one of the dogs, it must run out when released, return when recalled, and when it holds the game, it does not eat. How many conditions? Three: it runs out when released, meaning for example when you see the game and release it, it runs; it returns when recalled, meaning when you call it to stop and it stops, because if it overshoots while you ordered it to stop, that means it hunted for itself; third: when it holds, it does not eat. If it eats, that is evidence that it held the game only for itself. And Allah knows best.
* * *
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Do we think the last thing we took was the benefits?
* A student: We did not complete them.
* The Shaykh: We did not complete what?
* A student: The benefits.
* The Shaykh: From where?
* A student: And among them: whatever the trained hunting animal catches, if the animal was trained and the name of Allah was mentioned over it, it is lawful.
* The Shaykh: Did we not mention how training is done?
* A student: Only training of dogs.
* The Shaykh: What did we say?
* A student: The permissibility of what trained hunting animals catch: every fanged thing that can be killed and that it strikes, on condition that it be trained, and the best trainable animals are dogs, which is for beasts; then falcons, which is for birds. If it is one of the dogs, it must run out when released, and so on; we mentioned three conditions.
* The Shaykh: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: some animals accept training, based on His saying: ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوَارِحِ﴾.
* Also among its benefits: the virtue of knowledge, because Allah, Exalted is He, distinguished between hunting by what is not trained and by what is trained, making the second lawful and not the first, and this indicates the excellence of teaching even among animals.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of mentioning the name of Allah, Exalted is He, when releasing the trained animal, based on His saying: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾. This is according to one of the possible readings of the verse, for there is another possibility: that the meaning is mention the name of Allah over it when eating; and a third meaning: mention the name of Allah over it if you reach it alive before the predator kills it. All of these are possible in the verse, so they are all taken together.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the blessing of mentioning the name of Allah. Its evidences are many, among them: the permissibility of slaughtered animals, the permissibility of game, the completeness of purity in wudu', that blessing descends on food, and that the lamb is protected from the harm of jinn and devils. In short, the blessing of the name of Allah, Exalted is He, is abundant and has many evidences.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: its apparent meaning permits what the predator hunts whether or not it wounds; this is based on the view that al-jawarih means the hunters (al-kawasib). But if we say that al-jawarih is the plural of jarih, which is what wounds a thing, then it is necessary that the blood flow out. This is illustrated by an example: if the dog brings the game strangled, with no wound at all and no blood flowing from it, is it permitted or not?
If we say that al-jawarih means the hunters, it is permitted. If we say that it means those that wound the skin so that blood flows, then it is not permitted. The matter is disputed among the scholars. Some say it is a condition that the dog wound; if it does not wound, it is not lawful, and they cite the generality of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "What makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah is mentioned, eat."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2488) and Muslim (1968 / 20) from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij.]]
Others say that the jawarih are the hunters, and whatever they hold for their masters is lawful, whether it was wounded or not. There is no doubt that caution is to abandon it: if the dog brings you game that was not wounded, caution says leave it. But to say definitively that it is forbidden, we do not say that definitively, because of the generality of: ﴿كُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ "Eat of what they hold for you."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: cutting off what causes self-admiration. His saying: ﴿تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ﴾ "you teach them" attributes teaching to humans, and a person may take pride in himself, be deceived, and feel conceited. Therefore Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ "of what Allah has taught you," indicating that your knowledge which you teach them, from where is its source? From Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: knowledge is not restricted to the religious sciences; rather, every thing has its knowledge according to its nature. The knowledge here is not knowledge of the legal rulings, that this is obligatory, that this is forbidden, and the like; it is knowledge of training hunting animals to hunt. So this is evidence that knowledge is specific to what the context requires, and each thing has its own kind.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the vastness of Allah's mercy, Mighty and Majestic, in permitting to us what we slaughter with our hands and what we slaughter through an intermediary, meaning through the trained animals. This is undoubtedly one of Allah's expansions of provision for us.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: hardship brings ease. Since it is hard for a person to hunt game himself at all times, perhaps in mountains, plains, or valleys where he cannot hunt personally, he is granted a concession to hunt through his trained animal. This is among Allah's expansions upon His servants in the means of provision.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of mentioning the name of Allah, Exalted is He, including when releasing the game. If one forgets, it is not lawful, based on the generality of the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [al-An'am 121], and because the Prophet (ﷺ) made mentioning the name of Allah a condition, and a condition does not lapse through forgetfulness. This is the preponderant view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is what the evidences require.
Some scholars said: the basmalah lapses through forgetfulness, based on the generality of the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا﴾ [al-Baqarah 286], and Allah said: "I have done so." But we say: one who did not mention the name of Allah over the slaughtered animal or the game, if he forgot, is undoubtedly excused and not held accountable. If he deliberately omitted the basmalah and slaughtered or hunted, he is sinful for that, because it is a waste of property and a kind of mockery of the signs of Allah. So this one who forgot is not held accountable.
But the consideration now is not the slaughterer or the hunter; the consideration now is the eater. We say to whoever wishes to eat of this game over which the name of Allah was not mentioned: this game was not mentioned over with the name of Allah, and you have been forbidden to eat it. If he eats forgetfully, there is nothing upon him, because the matter here has two aspects: the aspect of the hunter and slaughterer, and the aspect of the eater, and neither is held accountable for forgetfulness. But if the slaughterer or hunter forgot, he is not held accountable; then the prohibition is directed at whom? At the eater, and it is said to him: do not eat what the name of Allah was not mentioned over.
The claim of one who says that what "the name of Allah was not mentioned over" means carrion is a mistaken claim, because Allah explicitly mentioned the prohibition of carrion, saying: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3]. Had Allah intended that, He would have said: "and do not eat carrion." On this basis, what Shaykh al-Islam chose, may Allah have mercy on him, is the true view.
But Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir that there is a consensus that what was left unmentioned by forgetfulness is lawful. Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, criticized him and said: Ibn Jarir is among those who do not regard the saying of one or two as breaking a consensus, and this contradicts what the scholars hold. The correct position is that a consensus requires that no dissenter exist; if a dissenter exists, even one of the qualified jurists, then there is no consensus.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of fearing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾.
* Among its benefits: an indication that whoever eats what Allah has not made lawful is not one who fears Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of reckoning, based on the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾.
* Also among them: that Allah, Exalted is He, is swift in reckoning. Among this is what we mentioned in the tafsir: that it means the swiftness of meeting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through death, and the swiftness of Allah's judgment between the servants, which is on the Day of Resurrection, for Allah judges between people and reckons them in half a day, based on His saying: ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا﴾.
If someone asks: is swiftness of reckoning one of Allah's essential attributes or His active attributes? We say: it is among the active attributes, because reckoning is an act connected to His will; and on this basis it establishes the affirmation of active attributes.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 5 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾. As for "today" (al-yawm), it may refer to that particular day, as opposed to a past time, or to the present day, which is a specific day.

﴿Have been made lawful for you﴾: By whom? By Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The agent has been omitted because it is known, as in His saying: ﴿Man was created weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 28]. The Creator is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and this is known; the one who makes lawful and unlawful is Allah, and this is known. For this reason the agent is omitted in the matter of creation, which is a matter of the universe, and in the matter of the Law (shar'), which concerns what is lawful and unlawful. Accordingly, whoever is known to be the one who makes lawful or unlawful, or who brings into existence or annihilates, there is no harm in omitting him and using the passive form of the verb (al-fi'l al-mabni lima lam yusamma fa'iluh, the passive voice).

﴿Today has been made lawful for you﴾, that is, Allah has made lawful. ﴿The good things﴾ are the opposite of the wicked (khabith). Allah says: ﴿Say: The wicked and the good are not equal﴾ [al-Ma'idah 100]. So what is the measure of the good? Is it in the taste of each person, or in the customs of people, or something else? We say: the reference in this is to what the Law (shari'ah) has brought. What the Law has made lawful is good, and what it has made unlawful is wicked.

If someone says: What is the basic rule concerning foods?
* A student: Permissibility (al-hill).
* The Shaykh: Permissibility? What is the evidence?
* The student: ﴿Made lawful for you﴾ (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 29]. So the basic rule is permissibility. If a claimant asserts that this thing is unlawful, whether a bird, a creeping creature, or other, we say to him: What is the evidence for that? And what Allah has made lawful is good, without doubt.

﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them﴾. ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture﴾ means the Jews and the Christians. It does not mean everything they eat of grain and fruit; no. It means everything they eat of meat. Moreover, it does not mean every meat they eat when it does not require slaughter (dhakah), because what does not require slaughter is lawful without their action, and grains and fruits are lawful without their action. Thus they are not part of their specific food, and it is not possible that Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture﴾ while meaning by it a food that is common to everyone. For example, if the People of the Scripture ate only barley, is the permissibility of barley for us derived from this verse? No, because this is not among their distinctive foods, and its permissibility did not depend on their action. What has its permissibility depending on their action? It is slaughtered animals. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) interpreted their food as their slaughtered animals [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/136), and al-Bukhari in a suspended narration (7/92).]]. Accordingly, ﴿the food of those who were given the Scripture﴾ means their slaughtered animals, and they are the Jews and the Christians.

The apparent meaning of the noble verse is that there is no difference between whether they have altered and distorted their scripture or adhere to their laws, because of its generality, and because this verse is in the same surah in which Allah reports that they say: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the third of three﴾ [al-Ma'idah 73].

﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food﴾, that is, what you have slaughtered, ﴿is lawful for them﴾. Thus foods are of three types: food whose permissibility does not depend on any human action, which is lawful for all; food whose permissibility depends on a person slaughtering it. If we slaughter it, it is lawful for them; if they slaughter it, it is lawful for us.

﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾. ﴿And the chaste women (al-muhsanat)﴾ means: and there has been made lawful for you the chaste women. Accordingly, it is coordinated with His saying ﴿the good things﴾.

﴿And the chaste women from among the believing women﴾: The chaste women from among the believing women are the free women, which is lawful for us. It is also possible that what is meant is the modest women (al-'afifat). As for the first, it is supported by the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of believing slave-girls﴾ [an-Nisa' 25]. The meaning of "chaste" here is clearly free women.

As for the second, that what is meant is the modest women, it is supported by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [an-Nur 23], and His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ [an-Nur 4]. The meaning here is women modest regarding fornication. However, what appears is that the meaning of "chaste" here is free women, and the verse is open to interpretation; there is nothing in it that indicates this or that.

﴿The chaste women from among the believing women﴾, meaning the free women. As for female slaves, it is not permissible for a person to marry them except under conditions that were mentioned earlier in Surat an-Nisa'.

﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾: What are "the chaste women"? Free women or modest women, according to the difference of opinion.

﴿From among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, but on condition that ﴿when you have given them their bridal payments, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking secret lovers﴾. Allah made the giving of their wages a condition for the permissibility of chaste women from among the believing women and from among those who were given the Scripture. The wages are the dowries (mahr) that are given in exchange for enjoying the woman, and for this reason Allah called them a wage (ajr), because the ajr is what is taken in return for a compensation.

﴿When you have given them﴾, that is, you have given them, ﴿their wages﴾, that is, the wages of these chaste women, which are the dowries.

﴿Desiring chastity﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in His saying ﴿you have given them﴾, meaning: while you are desiring chastity, that is, seeking to be chaste, guarding the chastity of the woman and the chastity of the man, because marriage achieves the chastity of both husband and wife.

﴿Not unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, that is, not openly committing fornication, ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾, that is, secretly committing fornication.

Accordingly, sexual intercourse is of three types: the first is what is lawful through the dowry; the second is what is open through lewdness and immorality; the third is what is secret through lewdness and immorality. Which of these is lawful?
* Students: The first.
* The Shaykh: The first is the one that is lawful, and it is the one in which he marries her, being chaste, not committing unlawful sexual intercourse, and not taking secret lovers.

His saying ﴿akhdan﴾ means friends (asdiqa'), and the khidn is applied to a friend, whether male or female. For this reason Allah said in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿Nor those who take secret lovers﴾ [an-Nisa' 25], and here He said: ﴿nor those who take secret lovers﴾, which shows that the khidn can be used for men and for women.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And whoever rejects faith, his deeds have become worthless﴾. ﴿Whoever rejects faith﴾: Is faith something that can be rejected or not rejected, or is faith the opposite of disbelief? Faith is the opposite of disbelief. But what is meant by faith here is the requirements of faith, which is adherence to the Law, because Allah mentioned here lawful and unlawful things. Whoever acts upon them and fulfills them is a believer, and whoever does not act upon them is not a believer.

So, ﴿whoever rejects faith﴾, that is, rejects what faith requires of adherence to the rulings of Islam, ﴿his deeds have become worthless﴾, that is, they have been nullified, lost, and gone. The word "deeds" ('amal) is singular and made possessive, so it includes all deeds, because apostasy nullifies deeds, provided that the person dies in his apostasy, may Allah protect us, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide forever﴾ [al-Baqarah 217].

﴿And in the Hereafter he is among the losers﴾: Allah mentioned that he is a loser in the Hereafter, because the manifestation of his loss will be at that time; otherwise, in reality, he has lost both this world and the Hereafter. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

And Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [at-Tawbah 69].

* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and your feet up to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to place upon you any difficulty, but He intends to purify you and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Before we begin explaining this verse, do you think there are any remaining benefits from the previous verse?
* A student: ﴿Today has been made lawful﴾.
* The Shaykh: Good.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them, and the chaste women from among the believing women﴾, and so on to the end.

We mentioned previously that ﴿al-muhsanat﴾ has two readings: with a kasrah on the sad and with a fathah on the sad; ﴿al-muhsinat﴾ as an active participle, and ﴿al-muhsanat﴾ as a passive participle. I think I forgot to alert you to it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that permitting and forbidding belong to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; no one has the right to make lawful or unlawful, because of His saying ﴿Today has been made lawful﴾. This is by the consensus of the Muslims. Indeed, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah﴾ [an-Nahl 116].

What has passed us already clarifies the ruling on permitting and forbidding, and we said: the basic rule regarding acts of worship is what? Prohibition and prevention unless there is evidence; and the basic rule regarding other matters is permissibility. The discussion of the jurists (usuliyyun) on this subject, and on what the basic rule of things is before the Law, and similar matters, is all talk with no benefit except blackening pages that were white; it is merely disputatious speech with no benefit, because we have in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger what suffices from all the topics they mentioned and extended discussion about.

We say: there are two important principles. The basic rule regarding acts of worship is prohibition unless there is evidence: prohibition in origin and in description, unless there is evidence. The basic rule regarding non-acts of worship, absolutely, whether customs, transactions, objects, benefits, or other things, is what? Permissibility, except what the evidence indicates is forbidden. The evidences for this have apparently been mentioned earlier, and there is no need to repeat them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that everything Allah the Exalted has made lawful is good, but is this good lawful for everyone? The answer: if it includes harm for some people, it is unlawful even though it is good. So if it is said to a person, for example: If you eat this kind of food, it will harm you, it becomes unlawful for him, not because it is wicked, but because it is harmful to this specific person.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the food of the Jews and Christians is lawful for us, because of His saying ﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Is anyone else like them? The answer: no. Whoever said that His saying ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾ is a title (laqab) was wrong; rather, we say it is a descriptive attribute (wasf), and a descriptive attribute excludes whatever else does not possess it. For example, ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾ — analyze it as a passive participle? "The food of those who have been given the Scripture." When you analyze it as a passive participle, it becomes a derived attribute, and so it is not a title as was claimed, because a title is known to have no concept (mafhum). For example, if I say to you: "Honor Zayd," it does not mean: "Do not honor anyone else," because this is a title. But if I say: "Honor the diligent one," this is a descriptive attribute that excludes the one who is not diligent.

Some scholars, especially the later ones, said that ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾ is a title and not a descriptive attribute, in order to find a pretext for making lawful the food of people other than Jews and Christians, because a title, as is known among the usuliyyun, has no concept. A title has no concept, and you have known the example: "Honor Zayd" does not mean you should not honor anyone else; but "honor the diligent one" means: do not honor the negligent one.

In any case: * Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of the food of those who were given the Scripture, namely the Jews and Christians.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that those other than them, their slaughter is not lawful, such as the Magians, the idolaters, the communists, the polytheists, and those like them. From where do we take this? From the concept (mafhum) of ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in making lawful the food of those who were given the Scripture, because those who were given the Scripture possess heavenly knowledge, so they are among the people closest to accepting the Islamic Law. There is no doubt that the condition of the People of the Scripture changed greatly after the revelation of the Noble Qur'an, and between the Muslims and the Jews, and between the Muslims and the Christians, there arose great and devastating wars, which led these Jews and Christians to arrogance and to their refusal to accept what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the People of the Scripture regard as slaughtered (dhaki) is slaughtered; because if they regard it as slaughtered, it becomes food, and "slaughtered" here does not mean "clever" (fatin), but rather what has been ritually slaughtered (mudhakka). So whatever they regard as slaughtered is food for them. Accordingly, what they invoked other than the name of Allah over is lawful from their food; that is, if the Christian says "in the name of the Messiah" or the Jew says "in the name of 'Uzayr," or something similar, the animal is lawful, because they believe this is food, and Allah, the Exalted, stated it without restriction, saying: ﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾.

Also from this: whatever they regard as slaughtered from what is struck to death (mawquodh) is lawful. What is the mawquodh? That which is killed without the blood being made to flow, by electrocution or the like. It is lawful, because Allah said: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture﴾, so whatever they regard as food that is ritually slaughtered and that they eat is lawful.

If someone asks: Has anyone adopted this view? We say: As for what they invoked the name of the Messiah over, some of the early generation (salaf), from among the Companions and others, held this view, and said that this does not return to the essence of the slaughtered animal or to its impurity, but returns to the intention, and we are not concerned with their intention. As for the second, that if what they regard as slaughtered has died even by strangulation, some said that the verse is unrestricted, but we do not know that any of the early generation said this.

However, the later scholars who said it said: if some of the early generation permitted what was invoked with other than Allah's name — meaning some of the early generation — then this is similar, because the Prophet ﷺ made the mention of Allah's name over the slaughtered animal and the flowing of the blood, what? Two companions, he made them two in a single ruling, when he said: «Whatever makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2488), and Muslim (1968/20), from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij.]].

But the majority of scholars say that this generality in ﴿the food of those who were given the Scripture﴾ must be restricted, by restricting it with His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am 121], and His saying: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am 118], and it is also restricted by the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: «Whatever makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2488), and Muslim (1968/20), from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij.]].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 5, verse 5 (part 2 of 3):

If these two conditions restrict the general permission to eat the slaughter of a Muslim, then restricting them for the slaughter of a non-Muslim is what? It is a matter of greater priority. If a Muslim, for example, strangled a sheep, it would become unlawful to eat. Likewise with the People of the Book (ahl al-Kitab), since the slaughter of a People of the Book cannot be better than the slaughter of a Muslim. This is the view held by the majority (jumhur) of scholars, and it is the correct view. So the correct position is that His words, ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾, although general in wording, must be restricted by what? By what has been reported restricting it: the mention of Allah's name over the slaughtered animal and the flowing of its blood.

But if a slaughtered animal is brought to us from a Jew or a Christian, and we do not know whether the name of Allah was mentioned over it, or whether they strangled it and then cut its throat, what is the basic ruling? The basic ruling is permissibility (hill), based on what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari [(5507)] from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Some people came to the Messenger of Allah and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, some people bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mentioned the name of Allah over it or not.' He said: 'Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat.'" She said: "They had recently embraced disbelief." That is, they had recently become Muslims, and a recent Muslim may be unaware of many rulings of Islam. Nevertheless he said: "Mention the name yourselves," what? "Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat."

The author of al-Muntaqa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: From this it is derived that every act performed by its proper person is basically permissible, and one does not probe into it. For if we were obligated to investigate, then even what is sold to us in our markets that was slaughtered by Muslims would require us to ask: Did the slaughterer mention the name of Allah or not? Did he cut the windpipe and the veins or not? Does he pray or not? And similar matters. And if we were obligated to investigate, then when a man sold us a garment we would have to say: "Come, where did you acquire it?" Correct? Because it may have been stolen. If he said: "I acquired it from so-and-so," then we would say: "Go to so-and-so, come, where did he acquire it?" Because so-and-so may have stolen it. We would continue until we reached the tree from which it was woven!! This is something that cannot be borne.

In any case, the basic ruling for an act performed by its proper person is what? Permissibility.

If a claimant argued that what is meant by His words, ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture﴾, is what they cook, such as bread, broth, and similar things, would that be accepted?

* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Why?
* A student: This is lawful for them and for others.
* The Shaykh: Because this is lawful from the People of the Book and from others by consensus. This is lawful by consensus, even if a Magian (majusi) prepared bread for us to eat. The lawful things are divided into two categories. The first: that whose lawfulness does not depend on the action of an agent. This is lawful from a People of the Book and from a non-People of the Book. The second: that whose lawfulness depends on the action of an agent. This is unlawful from non-People of the Book. These are two categories. I mentioned this so as to correct what we said earlier, that they are three categories, when in reality they are two. The first: that whose lawfulness does not depend on the action of an agent, such as what?
* A student: Slaughtered animals.
* The Shaykh: No, that is a mistake. That whose lawfulness does not require the action of an agent.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Are you saying: like slaughtered animals, or like non-slaughtered things? Fine, what do you say about fish? Does its lawfulness require the action of an agent? I am asking you.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No? Are you certain? Do you all agree on this? If you found a dead fish on the seashore, all of it, with nothing wrong with it, this is lawful, whether it is the food of the People of the Book or of others. There is no difficulty with this. The difficulty lies in food whose lawfulness requires the action of an agent, namely the animal that needs to be slaughtered properly (dhakah). This is what the verse means.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no harm in our feeding the People of the Book and their feeding us, based on His words: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them﴾. Then we ask: is it permissible to exchange gifts (muhadah) between us and the People of the Book?
The answer: Yes, it is permissible. The Prophet ﷺ accepted their gifts, just as the woman at Khaybar sent him a poisoned sheep. This woman "asked: 'What does Muhammad like?' They said: 'He likes the foreleg of the sheep.' So she filled the foreleg with poison and sent it to the Messenger, peace be upon him." [Reported by Abu Dawud (3781) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] The Prophet, peace be upon him, did not know the unseen. He ate, and those who ate with him, some of them died. As for him, peace be upon him, his palate was affected [reported by Muslim (2190/45) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik], but by the permission of Allah the poison did not harm him at all. Yet in his final illness he said, as 'A'isha narrated from him: "The poisoned morsel of Khaybar has continued to afflict me, and this is the time when my aorta (al-abhar) is severed" [reported by al-Bukhari (4428)]. The abhar is a well-known vein; when it is severed a person dies. For this reason al-Zuhri and others said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died as a martyr [reported by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (4/263)], killed by whom? Killed by the Jews.

The point is that their food being lawful for us and our food being lawful for them indicates the permissibility of exchanging gifts between us and the People of the Book, especially if we hope they will embrace Islam, or if we wish to show them that Islam is a religion of peace, and that Allah, mighty and majestic, did not send Islam to compel people to become Muslims. Rather, Allah has imposed on mankind that His word be the highest, whether through Islam or through the jizyah (poll tax). Therefore, if a disbeliever said that he would pay the jizyah and remain upon his religion, we would say: No, you must become Muslim? Answer me.
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, not at all. We say: remain upon your religion, but pay the jizyah. Of course, when is the payment of jizyah? When we, the Muslims, hold the word, not as is our situation today. Our situation today, may Allah have mercy on our weakness, is the opposite of that. The highest word belongs to others, because we have not upheld the religion of Allah as it should be upheld. If we had upheld the religion of Allah as it should be upheld, the religion of Allah would necessarily prevail over all religions: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾, for what? ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ [al-Tawbah 33]. But who among us, except those whom Allah wills, desires this? Most people today, and I mean Muslims as well, are contrary to that. In the lands of the Muslims there is shirk, which if the Messenger were alive he would fight them over. There is exaggeration (ghuluww) regarding righteous people or other than righteous people. These matters are not hidden from many of you. In any case, the religion of Islam is in reality a religion of peace, but at the same time it is a religion of resolve, strength, and caution against enemies and their plotting, their deceit, and their treachery.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lawfulness of the chaste women (muhsanat) from the People of the Book is like the lawfulness of the chaste women from the Muslims, because Allah said: ﴿and the chaste women from among the believing women﴾. In reality, someone might say: this has no point, because it is well known. But He, glorified and exalted, wished to make clear that just as the chaste women from the believing women are lawful to us, so too the chaste women from the People of the Book are lawful to us. The lawfulness of the chaste believing women is well known, and in Surah al-Nisa', which comes before this surah, it is explicitly stated. But He, glorified and exalted, wished, and Allah knows best, to show that the lawfulness of the chaste believing women and the chaste women from the People of the Book is equal in lawfulness. However, equality in lawfulness does not require equality in undertaking marriage with them. Something may be lawful, yet we say: it is better that you do not undertake it. Do you understand this? That is, it does not follow from the lawfulness of the chaste believing women and of those given the Scripture that they are equal in terms of undertaking marriage. A woman may be lawful for a man, and it may be said: do not proceed with her, is that not so? What is meant by "muhsanat"?
* A student: Free women.
* The Shaykh: There are two opinions on it, but which is the preferred one?
* Students: Free women.
* The Shaykh: The meaning is free women. This is the correct view. As for the chaste ( 'afifat), it comes in Surah al-Nur that: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur 3].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the elevated rank of the believer even if he is not a scholar, because of His words: ﴿the chaste women from the believers﴾. He placed the believing women before ﴿the chaste women from those who were given the Scripture﴾, even though the People of the Book have knowledge and the believer may not have knowledge.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the requirement of a dower (mahr) for the lawfulness of a woman. From where is this taken? From His words: ﴿when you have given them their due compensation (ujur)﴾. This matter has been disputed among scholars, and it has several forms. The first form: a man marries a woman on the condition that she has no dower. This is one. That he marries her on the condition that she has no dower: is the contract valid? The apparent meaning of this verse, and the apparent meaning of the verse in Surah al-Nisa', indicate that the contract is not valid.
In Surah al-Nisa', Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, what? ﴿that you seek with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisa' 24]. That is, not for free. A dower is necessary. In this verse: ﴿when you have given them their due compensation﴾. This opinion is the preferred one: if a man marries a woman on the condition that she has no dower, the marriage is invalid. What is the reason? When he marries her on the condition that she has no dower, this marriage becomes a gift, and the marriage of a gift (nikah al-hibah) is permissible only for whom? Only for the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and his family, based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not for the [rest of the] believers﴾ [al-Ahzab 50]. So if a condition of no dower is stipulated, this is a gift.
Some scholars said: the marriage is valid, but the condition is void, and in that case she is owed the customary dower (mahr al-mithl). But this view is weak, because the evidences prevent it.
The first form: he married her without a dower. We mentioned two opinions regarding it.
The second form: he married her and remained silent, not mentioning a dower. The marriage is valid by the text of the Qur'an, but she is owed the customary dower, based on the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dower﴾ [al-Baqarah 236], then He said: ﴿and provide for them, the wealthy according to his capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]. We say: if he has consummated the marriage with her, she is owed the customary dower. If he divorces her before consummation, she is owed a provision (mut'ah) according to her husband's ease and hardship.
Is the difference between this and the first clear? What is it? The first stipulated no dower, while the second remained silent.
The third form: he marries her on condition of a dower. Is this permissible or not?
* Students: Permissible.
* The Shaykh: Permissible. Stipulating the dower is merely an emphasis, an affirmation of what the contract requires. And if a dower is stipulated, must it be specified or not? It is not required to specify it. If he specified it, she is owed what he specified. If he did not specify it, she is owed the customary dower.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the dower is like a wage (ujrah), because of His words: ﴿their due compensation (ujur)﴾. Then a difficulty arises. It is said: a wage requires knowledge of the consideration and what is consideration for, and knowledge of both. Here the consideration may be unknown, namely the dower that is not named, and the item for which it is given is likewise. The item for which it is given is the woman's benefit (manfa'ah), until when? Until death or divorce. This is an unknown matter. She may remain with her husband for twenty years, thirty years, or a hundred years, or she may die in her first week, or he may divorce her in her first week. The dower of the first and the second is the same, is it not? If a man married a woman for a thousand riyals and she stayed with him for a hundred years, divide the year by a hundred riyals; each year costs how much? One riyal. And another woman he married for a hundred riyals, and she died after a hundred days; how much? One riyal per day. There is a difference between this and that.
But if someone says: how can you say it is like a wage given this great difference? We say: in view of the Lawgiver's desire for marriage, because of the abundance of the community, the preservation of chastity, and the great benefits, this matter was made lenient. If we said that knowledge of this and that is required, it would cause great hardship, and women would differ in the amount of the dower. We would return to a second matter prohibited in the Shari'ah, which is temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah). That is, if we said that knowledge of the consideration and the item is required, one would ask: how long is the marriage? Just as if a woman were hired as a servant, we would ask: how long is the service? Therefore, because of these great benefits, the Lawgiver overlooked the length and the consideration, the consideration and the item.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is required in marriage, or rather the greatest purpose of marriage is chastity (ihsan), because of His words: ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that marriage should be announced, why? Because He said: ﴿not fornicators, nor those who take secret lovers﴾. Marriage must therefore be announced openly. Is it sufficient in its announcement that it take place with witnesses, or must it be made known and proclaimed? The answer: the second, according to the preferred view. But if there are witnesses with a condition of secrecy, then if secrecy is stipulated it is invalid; it must be repeated and announced. If secrecy is not stipulated, there is a difference of opinion: some scholars say it is invalid, and some say it is valid. But all the scholars agree that announcing the marriage is better and further from suspicion, and further from taking secret lovers.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: enjoyment of women (istimta') is divided into categories: chaste marriage, fornication (sifah), and taking secret lovers (akhdan). The difference between them: the first is a legal contract; the second is open adultery; the third is hidden adultery.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if one intends fornication or taking a lover (khadn), it is not a valid marriage, because Allah stipulated: ﴿not fornicating﴾. The scholars of the Sunnah have used this to prove the invalidity of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah), because temporary marriage, if announced, is fornication, since the man intends only to enjoy her, not to preserve chastity. He wants a pleasure that he discharges into this woman's private part and then it ends. And if it is hidden, it is of the same kind as taking secret lovers. This view, that temporary marriage is unlawful, is held by the consensus of the people of the Sunnah.
It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "It is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection" [reported by Muslim (1406/21) from the hadith of Sabrah al-Juhani]. This indicates that it cannot be abrogated, because his saying, peace be upon him, "It is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection," is a statement that includes a ruling, and a ruling limited by what? By the Day of Resurrection. When a statement includes a ruling limited until the Day of Resurrection, it cannot be abrogated (naskh), because abrogation (naskh) is the lifting of a ruling, and what is limited to the Day of Resurrection cannot be lifted.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, a woman gave birth after she had gifted herself to a man?
* The Shaykh: He asks: if a woman gifts her dower to her husband, is that valid or not?
* The student: The dower returns to the woman.
* The Shaykh: She gifted it to him and then he gifted it back? What is the end result?
* The student: The man (...) had it and he gave her...
* The Shaykh: He gave her an amount of ten riyals, then she returned it to him, then he returned it to her.
* The student: No, the man left the entire dower. First the woman donated to the man...
* The Shaykh: Do you know what you are saying or not?
* The student: I know.
* The Shaykh: Now the woman said: "So-and-so, the dower you gave me is a gift to you"?
* The student: No, she did not give it to him. I mean the man did not have it, and this woman herself offered herself to the man.

* Shaykh: Do you mean you gave her money so it would be her dowry? I had not pictured it that way. This too is fine; there is no harm in his giving her money. But I fear that if he gives her the money, he will say, "Praise be to God (...)" because she gave it to him, end of quote. As for the matter of him returning the dowry to her once the contract is complete, this happens often, it happens often. In the past, among us here in our country, a man would give a woman a dowry while he was poor. In one case, a man married a woman and gave her a dowry of one riyal, one riyal only. On the morning of the wedding day, a man knocked on the door while he was with his family on the first day, and said: "Give me the riyal, because I am asking you for it." He said: "I have nothing." He said: "Give it to me or I will complain about you." Their voices rose, and she came out and said: "What does he want?" He said: "He is demanding a riyal from me and saying, 'Give it to me or I will complain about you.'" She said: "Take it, give it to him." So he gave her the dowry and paid it in full. There is nothing wrong with this.
* Student: The Exalted's saying: ﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. We mentioned that it refers to their slaughtered animals. Does ﴿and your food is lawful for them﴾ mean our slaughtered animals, or is it general?
* Shaykh: Yes, our slaughtered animals are lawful for them.
* There remains a benefit we forgot, which is: does this verse indicate that the body of a disbeliever is pure? Yes, it indicates that, because contact with food is inevitable, and in marriage too there must be contact between the husband and his wife; if their bodies were impure, that would necessitate contamination. It also indicates that their vessels are pure, and that is so, except what is known to be impure, which is impure, like the vessels of Muslims.
* Student: There is something (...), which is what is called the deferred (mu'akhkhar) (...).
* Shaykh: Some people say: he gives the dowry promptly and deferred, all of it deferred. There is no harm; there is no obstacle, because this dowry is now established as a debt upon him; if he died, it would be demanded from him.
* Student: (...) the young woman stipulated to the husband, she said to him: "Do not pay the dowry"?
* Shaykh: Who? The wife's father?
* Student: The wife's father.
* Shaykh: But will he be paying it on his behalf?
* Student: No, he will not pay it.
* Shaykh: That is not permissible.
* Student: He said to him: do not pay the dowry.
* Shaykh: It is not permissible, meaning whether the husband stipulates it or the woman's guardian does. But it is said to the woman's guardian: may God reward you with good, as long as you (...) this man, and you buy the man at a high price, give him yourself as a dowry so he may give it to the girl.
* Student: Is the slaughter of the Rafidah lawful?
* Shaykh: Every disbeliever who is not among the People of the Book, his slaughter is not lawful, any person.
* Student: O Shaykh, may God be good to you, the verses clearly show permissibility of marrying women of the People of the Book and believing women without condition, even if they are not righteous. So how, O Shaykh, do we reconcile this with what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad with a sound chain from the Prophet ﷺ: "Three whose supplication is not answered," and he mentioned among them a man whose wife... I do not recall the exact wording; I think she is immoral, or a man with a disobedient wife whom he did not divorce[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (17312, 20621), and al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (2530), and the wording of Ibn Abi Shaybah is: "And a man whose wife had bad character and he did not divorce her or separate from her."]]?
* Shaykh: This is understood to refer to a woman who is not chaste, if the hadith is authentic. It is understood to refer to a woman who is not chaste, because if he keeps his family, who lack chastity, he becomes a dayyuth (a man who tolerates immorality among his family), so this is a warning against this matter.
* Student: If the act proceeds from his family, do we now definitively say that Jews and Christians are misguided Muslims?
* Shaykh: You are certain?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The word "gharim" (...) has already prevented certainty.
* Student: Shaykh, if a person knows that the food that comes from the People of the Book was not slaughtered in the correct manner, should he inform people that this food is not slaughtered in the Islamic manner, or leave it to people and it is lawful for them?
* Shaykh: This is an important question. If a person knows that this meat is unlawful, because it is carrion, or because it was slaughtered by someone whose slaughter is not lawful, or because the one who slaughtered it did not slaughter it in the prescribed manner, it is obligatory upon him to inform, obligatorily. The scholars, may God have mercy on them, mentioned something similar, saying: whoever knows that water is impure must inform anyone who wants to use it. Is it clear? Likewise, if you see a person eating something harmful, it is obligatory upon you to inform him that it is harmful; this is part of giving sincere advice.
* Student: Regarding the People of the Book existing today, they have no known religion; they merely claim affiliation...
* Shaykh: Yes, they claim affiliation to the Jews and Christians.
* Student: They have no connection...
* Shaykh: Did not God say about those who claim affiliation to the Christians or Jews: ﴿Certainly, those who said, "God is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾ [al-Ma'idah 73]? He declared them disbelievers. They were disbelievers before the Messenger's time, and yet God made their women lawful and their slaughter lawful.
Likewise, if you see a person eating something harmful, it is obligatory upon you to inform him that it is harmful; this is part of giving sincere advice.
* Student: Regarding the People of the Book existing today, they have no known religion; they merely claim affiliation...
* Shaykh: Yes, they claim affiliation to the Jews and Christians.
* Student: They have no connection...
* Shaykh: Did not God say about those who claim affiliation to the Christians or Jews: ﴿Certainly, those who said, "God is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾ [al-Ma'idah 73]? He declared them disbelievers, they were disbelievers before the time of the Messenger, and yet God made their women lawful and their slaughter lawful.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands to the elbows, and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and to complete His favor upon you that you might be grateful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6].
* Shaykh: All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds. I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. The Exalted said: ﴿Today, the good things have been made lawful for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5], and we are still extracting benefits from it:
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: female slaves from the People of the Book are not permitted to a Muslim even if he fears sinning. Its evidence is: ﴿and chaste women from those who were given the Scripture﴾.
If someone says: then all believing women are likewise, since God said: ﴿and chaste women from among the believing women﴾. We say: Yes, were it not for the verse on women, which is His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [an-Nisa 25]. Were it not for this, we would say so. But a Muslim slave girl becomes lawful to a Muslim in necessity, according to what preceded in Surat an-Nisa.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that deeds are included in faith, due to His saying: ﴿and whoever disbelieves in faith﴾, and what is mentioned in this verse is deeds, so this indicates that deeds are included in faith. This is what the People of the Sunnah and the Community agree upon: that deeds are part of faith, and it has evidence from the Book and the Sunnah.
From the Qur'an: the Exalted said when mentioning the redirection of people to the Sacred Mosque after they used to face Jerusalem: ﴿And God would not let your faith go to waste﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. The commentators said: that is, your prayer toward Jerusalem. From the Sunnah, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Faith has seventy-some branches, the highest of which is the saying 'There is no god but God,' and the lowest of which is removing harm from the path," which is a deed; "and modesty is a branch of faith"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (9), and Muslim (35/58) from Abu Hurayrah, and the wording is Muslim's.]]; and this is an inner emotional response arising from the heart, and it is one of the deeds of the hearts. This indicates that deeds are included in the designation of faith. But when deeds are mentioned alongside faith, deeds become outward and faith is in the heart, like: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ [al-Baqarah 277].
* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever disbelieves in this faith, his deed has become void; that a deed may become void after a person has done it; we have mentioned the detail of this; and that apostasy does not nullify deeds unless the person dies upon it. Did we mention in the verse the affirmation of the Hereafter?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: Add it.
* Among the benefits of the verse: affirmation of the Hereafter.
* And among its benefits also: that people in the Hereafter are divided between losers and winners; due to His saying: ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾. This indicates that in the Hereafter there are winners and there are losers.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 1 of 7):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6]. The address with ﴿O you who have believed﴾ has already been discussed several times, so there is no need to repeat it here.

His saying ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾ means: when you intend to pray. It is not a condition that a person be standing on his feet; rather, whenever he intends it, even while seated, what Allah has commanded applies to him.

His saying ﴿to prayer﴾: Prayer (al-salah) is a known act of worship, opened with the takbir and concluded with the taslim. This is how the scholars defined it: that it is a known act of worship (they did not mention its manner, because both the elite and the common people know it), opened with the takbir and concluded with the taslim.

Their saying "opened with the takbir" is a distinguishing feature that excludes everything other than prayer, since all acts of worship other than prayer do not begin with the takbir. And "concluded with the taslim" excludes that which begins with the takbir but is not concluded with the taslim, such as the circumambulation of the House (tawaf). Although beginning the tawaf with the takbir is not a pillar, but is among the recommended acts, it is excluded by our saying: what? "concluded with the taslim," for the tawaf is not concluded with the taslim. This indicates that the hadith narrated as a marfu' report from the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, "That the tawaf around the House[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi (960) and al-Darimi (1889) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas as a marfu' report; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (3931) narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf report. al-Tirmidhi (960) said: This hadith has been narrated from Ibn Tawus and others, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a mawquf report, and we do not know it as marfu' except through the hadith of 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib..]] is a prayer," is not authentic as a marfu' report; rather it is from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and it is not sound either in its general application or its exception. For this reason the preponderant view is that purity is not a condition for the tawaf, since it is not included in prayer, and it cannot be included in this verse because it is not prayer. When it becomes clear that the marfu' hadith, which is in reality mawquf, is not sound in its general application or its exception, it becomes clear that purity is not a condition for it. We will discuss this, Allah willing, in the benefits.

﴿to prayer﴾: Would someone not say: prayer in the language means supplication, so the meaning would be: when you rise to supplication? We say: No. It is not established that it was transferred from its linguistic meaning to a legal meaning; but when it occurs in the speech of the Lawgiver it is understood according to the legal reality (al-haqiqah al-shar'iyyah), meaning its legal meaning. For this reason the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah does not accept the prayer of one of you when he has broken his wudu' until he performs wudu'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6954) and Muslim (225/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Do we say: the meaning is, "Allah does not accept the supplication of one of you"? No one says that, although prayer in the language means supplication. But we say: when linguistic realities are transferred to legal realities, they must be understood according to the legal realities in whose speech? In the speech of the Lawgiver.

﴿wash your faces﴾: Washing (al-ghasl) is well known: it is passing water over the limb so that it flows over it, that is, that water passes over it in flow, as opposed to wiping (al-mash) over the limb.

"Wujuh" is the plural of "wajh" (face). It is called "wajh" because confrontation (al-mawajahah) takes place by it. It is also a "wajh" from another angle: it is the face of the heart, for a person's inner state is recognized from his face. For this reason, when a person is pleased his face brightens, and when he is grieved his face contracts. So it is the place where sensory confrontation takes place, and it is truly the face of the heart, because it reveals what is in the heart.

What is the face? We said: it is that by which confrontation takes place. The scholars defined it: its breadth is from ear to ear, so the whiteness that lies between the sideburn and the ear is considered part of the face. Its length is from the hairline of the forehead down to the bottom of the beard. This boundary, "from the hairline of the forehead," is more precise than the view of some who said: "from the roots of the head hair," because if you say "from the roots of the head hair," it would be necessary to add "the usual," so as to exclude those with a receding or a high hairline; for some people's hair roots extend down to the forehead, and some people's rise at the forehead. But when we make the boundary the hairline of the forehead, this is more precise, and it also matches reality, because what faces people at meeting is what lies below that line; as for what is beyond it, it faces upward toward the sky.

Does the hanging part of the beard belong to the face or not? Some scholars said: it is part of the face, and on this basis, if a person has a long beard, it is included in the face. Other scholars said: the hanging part of the beard is not part of the face, because it has the status of something separated, for we have three things in the human body that have the status of separated parts: hair, nails, and teeth; these have the status of separated parts. So they say: since that has the status of something separated, it does not enter the definition of the face. But the correct view is that it enters the definition of the face, because confrontation takes place by it, and because it has been narrated from the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, in a hadith with a good chain, "that he would pass his fingers through his beard in wudu'"[[Reported by Abu Dawud (145) and Ibn Majah (431) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]].

If someone says: this is an action, and an action does not indicate obligation? We say: in principle it does not indicate obligation, but when it occurs as an explanation of an explicit text, it takes the ruling of that explicit text.

﴿your faces and your hands to the elbows﴾: "Aydi" is the plural of "yad" (hand).

﴿your hands to the elbows﴾: Pay attention. Here the hand is restricted by being "up to the elbows," so the hand must be washed from the tips of the fingers to the elbow.
