* The Shaykh: Yes. The correct view is that he must stop, because the presence of water nullifies tayammum. So he is like one who breaks wind during prayer, and he must repeat the prayer from the beginning.

* A student: O Shaykh, if a junub's whole body is covered with water, is it sufficient in place of wudu'?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it suffices instead of wudu'. Yes, because Allah said: ﴿If you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves﴾. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shayṭān.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that one who needs to relieve himself should conceal himself until he is out of people's sight. The basis for this is His saying: ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾. This is the sunnah of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, during the lifetime of their Prophet (ﷺ). This is evidence that concealment from eyes is part of their guidance, and there is no doubt that it is part of complete good manners. However, a person being in front of people when he has covered his nakedness is not a blameworthy matter, because it was done by the most modest of people, Muḥammad, Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "when he came to the refuse dump of a people and urinated there, standing, while Ḥudhayfah was beside him"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (225), Muslim (273 / 73), from Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān.]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of the Sharī'ah in purification. Minor impurity is limited to four limbs, because these limbs are generally the tools and instruments of action: striking with the hand, walking with the foot, and sight, smell and speech in the face, and hearing, imagination and thinking in the head. So the purification of these four limbs was prescribed. As for major impurity, it was prescribed that a person purify his whole body, because janabah loosens the whole body. This is why a person becomes weak when janabah happens to him, and he is commanded, when he wants to return, to perform ghusl, and if that is not possible, then he should perform wudu'. What supports this, meaning that janabah affects the whole body, is that a man who commits adultery while married is stoned to death, so that his whole body tastes the pain of the punishment just as it tasted the pleasure of the forbidden desire.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: euphemism for what is disliked to mention, by His saying: ﴿from the place of relieving oneself﴾ and His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: tayammum is permissible with all that is on the earth, whether it is sand, or dust, or stone, or other things.

If someone says: We dispute this benefit, because of His saying: ﴿then wipe your faces and hands with it﴾, and "min" (from) implies partiality, and it is not possible that anything adheres to the hand from the earth unless it is dusty?

We say: This objection is undoubtedly valid, and it is the evidence for those who say that tayammum must be done on ground that has dust. As for tayammum on ground that has no dust or powder, it is not valid. But the answer to this objection is that it is known by necessity that the Messenger (ﷺ) would travel long journeys in the winter and in the summer, and on his journeys he would pass over sand and pass over rain-soaked land, and it is not reported that he carried dust with him, nor that he did not perform tayammum on such lands. With this, the objection is resolved. We have previously said in the exegesis that "min" here may be partitive, and it may also be for the starting point.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the earth used for tayammum must be pure (ṭayyib), which is the opposite of impure (najis). But there is no earth that is impure, rather it must be contaminated, and what is contaminated is like what is impure. Accordingly, tayammum on contaminated ground is not valid, because of the Exalted's saying: ﴿then seek clean earth (ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban)﴾.

* Among its benefits: the obligation to cover the whole face in wiping in tayammum, because of His saying: ﴿your faces﴾. Hence, we must alert some common people who, when they perform tayammum, wipe their nose and what is around it and leave the rest. It is said: this is undoubtedly not sufficient, because the verse is explicit: ﴿your faces﴾, meaning all of it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when the word "yad" (hand) is used without qualification, it does not include the forearm, because of His saying: ﴿and your hands﴾. The indication is that when Allah wanted to go beyond the palm, He restricted it, in this very verse before us, and that was in purification by water for wudu', where He said: ﴿up to the elbows﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of order (tartīb) in tayammum between the face and the hands, so one begins first with what? With the face, then with the hands. And is this order consistent with the order of wudu'? Certainly, brothers: washing the hands before or after washing the face? After. So it is consistent.

If someone says: The "wa" (and) does not imply order, rather it is merely for joining?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 6 of 7):

We say: it is required by the context (qarina). The context here is that Allah the Exalted began with the face, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I begin with what Allah began with" [Narrated by Muslim (1218 / 147) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the absence of hardship (haraj) in this religion of Islam, based on His saying: ﴿Allah does not want to put upon you any difficulty﴾, meaning: any hardship. The religion of Islam, praise be to Allah, is entirely built upon ease (yusr), and ease is not tied to the desires of every person; for if it were tied to the desires of every person, some people would find it hard to get up and pray Fajr in winter. Rather, the meaning is that everything Allah has prescribed is made easy and contains no hardship.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the affirmation of will (irada) for Allah; based on His saying: ﴿Does not want﴾ and ﴿but He wants﴾. Allah affirmed will for Himself by negating the will for hardship and affirming the will for purification.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: if we say that hardship is negated, does that mean that the prescribed act is entirely removed, or that it is lightened, either in itself or by substitution with something else?
The answer: sometimes hardship is removed by dropping the prescribed act altogether, sometimes by lightening it, and sometimes by performing a substitute for it. These are three categories: either the obligation concerning that burdensome thing is entirely lifted, or it is lightened, or a substitute is provided for it.
For example, in the expiation (kaffarah) for killing, if a person is unable to fast two consecutive months, what happens? It is dropped; it is entirely lifted. In standing during prayer, if a person is unable to do it, what happens? It is lightened, so he prays sitting if he cannot pray standing.
The third: there is a substitute. The person who is permanently unable to fast is not required to fast, but he must pay the substitute, which is feeding a poor person for each day. So the matter, praise be to Allah, becomes broad.
Based on this principle that we have taken from the words of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, we say: whoever is unable to perform expiations, whatever the expiation may be, at the time it becomes obligatory, it is dropped from him.
As for the statement of some scholars that only the expiation for intercourse during menstruation and the expiation for intercourse during the day of Ramadan is not dropped when one is unable, this restriction has no evidence; the correct view is that all expiations are dropped if one is unable to perform them at the time they become obligatory, just as we said regarding zakat: if a person is poor, he owes no zakat. And if he becomes wealthy, do we say: pay for the years that passed after he became accountable? We do not say this.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the vastness (si'ah) of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He negated hardship from His servants. But if someone asks: is there not some hardship in the worship of the Children of Israel? We say: yes, but that was due to themselves; they were the ones who caused it, ﴿So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been made lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 160], and so on.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: His saying ﴿but He wants﴾. Is the will here legislative (shar'iyyah) or universal (kawniyyah)? Legislative; the will here is legislative.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: that tayammum (dry ablution) purifies and does not merely permit (mubih). How is this to be understood? Some scholars hold that tayammum permits what was forbidden without water; that is, it permits prayer without water, because the basic ruling is that prayer without water is forbidden, but when water is unavailable or its use would cause harm and one performs tayammum, prayer becomes permitted.
Some scholars therefore say that the purity of tayammum is permission for what was prohibited. Based on this, if one performs tayammum for reciting the Qur'an, he may not pray a voluntary prayer with it, because the voluntary prayer is higher than recitation of the Qur'an; or if you prefer, because the requirement of purity for voluntary prayer is stronger than the requirement of purity for reciting the Qur'an. Indeed, wudu for reciting the Qur'an is a sunnah, not an obligation, and touching the mushaf is the thing for which purity is obligatory.
If he intends a voluntary prayer, he does not thereby pray an obligatory prayer, because the obligatory is higher than the voluntary. And if the time passes while he is still in his state of purity, his tayammum is invalidated, because necessity is limited by its measure, and this man performed tayammum only for the present prayer, and the present prayer ends when its time ends.
However, this view is weak, and the correct view is that tayammum purifies. The evidence for this in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): where is it in the Book of Allah? ﴿but He wants to purify you﴾. After mentioning wudu, ghusl and tayammum, He said: ﴿but He wants to purify you﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur)." Tahur, with a fatha on the ta, is that by which purification is achieved. On this basis, tayammum purifies and removes the minor impurity (hadath). So if he performs tayammum for reciting the Qur'an, may he pray a voluntary prayer with it?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Why? He is purified. And if he performs tayammum for a voluntary prayer, he may pray an obligatory prayer with it; and if he performs tayammum for prayer and its time ends, he may pray the other prayer with it as long as his wudu has not been nullified, and so on. And if he performs tayammum for major impurity (janabah) the first time, it suffices him, so he does not perform tayammum again except for minor impurity only. Why? Because when he performed tayammum for janabah, he was purified from it and the janabah was lifted; there is no need to say: repeat the tayammum for janabah whenever the prayer time enters. We say: no, it is finished; because Allah named that what? Purification, and the Prophet (ﷺ) named the earth a tahur.

It remains to ask: if we say it purifies, does it purify with a restricted purity conditional on the presence of water, or with an absolute purity? That is, if he finds water, is he still in a state of purity so that he is not obliged to use water? The first. On this basis, if he performed tayammum for janabah and then finds water, is ghusl obligatory for him? Has he not been purified from his janabah? Yes. Then why do you require ghusl for him, since he has been purified from his janabah?
We say: we have evidence for this. The evidence is the story of the man whom the Prophet (ﷺ) saw after the Fajr prayer, I think, or one of the prayers, and he said: "What prevented you from praying?" He said: I was in janabah and had no water. He said: "Upon you is the clean earth (sa'id); it will suffice you." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (348) and Muslim (682 / 312) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.] Then water came afterwards and he commanded him to perform ghusl, even though he had performed tayammum and prayed; he commanded him to perform ghusl. That is one.
The second evidence: "The clean earth is the wudu of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years; when he finds water, let him fear Allah and let him touch his skin with it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (332), al-Tirmidhi (124) and al-Nasa'i (322) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.] So we have two pieces of evidence from the Sunnah.
Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: the consensus (ijma') is established on this. That is, the scholars agreed that whoever performs tayammum due to lack of water and then finds water must purify himself with it. In that case the general principle that it purifies has some exception, but this exception is indicated by the text and the consensus. It is known that we do not prefer anything over the text; since we said it purifies by the text, if we find water and say that you must use it, we say that on the basis of what? The text. We have no escape from what the Book and the Sunnah indicate.
A man performed tayammum due to lack of water for the Fajr prayer, and remained until 'Isha: does he repeat the tayammum at the time of each prayer? If you say no, you are wrong; if you say yes, you are wrong. We say: it is based on the disagreement. If we say it purifies, he does not repeat it; he prays 'Isha with the tayammum of Fajr. If we say it does not purify, he repeats the tayammum; whenever the prayer time passes, the tayammum is invalidated. Accordingly, if he wants to pray Duha with the tayammum of Fajr? According to the view that it permits but does not purify, he must perform tayammum again for that.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: if a person performs tayammum and puts on khuffs, then finds water, may he wipe over them?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: How quickly you answer without reflection and without deliberation! O my brothers, now we have said that the preponderant view is that tayammum purifies. Do you agree with this?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. Is this putting on khuffs in a state of purity?
* Student: He must wash.
* Student: He must perform wudu.
* The Shaykh: He must perform wudu, but that is not sufficient; he must perform wudu. This is your ruling. But we say: the tayammum is not connected with the purity of the feet; the feet have no bearing on tayammum, is that not so? The Prophet (ﷺ) said to al-Mughirah: "Leave them, for I put them on while they were in a state of purity (tahiratayn)." This indicates that one wipes over the khuff only in a purity that includes both feet. Your answer is correct, but I do not know whether it is based on knowledge or not; however, this reasoning, that the feet are not connected with the purity of tayammum, and the hadith of al-Mughirah says: "I put them on in a state of purity."
So, if a person is in the desert without water, puts on khuffs without purity, and the time for prayer comes and he performs tayammum, do we say to him: take off the khuffs?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: Why? Because purity by tayammum is not connected to them; so if he remains wearing the khuffs for ten years with tayammum as his purity, there is no hardship upon him.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of wisdom in the law of Allah, the reason stated: ﴿and to complete His favor upon you﴾; and this is indicated by the Book and the Sunnah in countless ways, that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, is wise in all that He creates and in all that He legislates.
* Branching from this benefit: submission to the decree of Allah, both legislative and universal. As long as you believe that this ruling is based on wisdom, you will submit and say: since it is for a wisdom, we are content. Likewise with Allah's universal decree: when Allah wills drought, poverty, illness, or much death, we know that this is for a wisdom, not in vain nor merely by will, but for a wisdom; and then we submit to the universal and the legislative decree.
Among the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) are those who deny wisdom, saying that Allah does not act for a wisdom and does not legislate for a wisdom, but it is merely will. They bring doubts, among them the hadith of 'A'ishah: "We would experience that (i.e., menstruation), and we were commanded to make up the fast but not commanded to make up the prayer." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321) and Muslim (335 / 69) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] But it is said: what is the legislative command for the believers? Wisdom. That is, merely knowing that Allah legislated it, I believe that it is for a wisdom. 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) entrusted the wisdom to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that this is what He commands us, and that is sufficient as wisdom.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: that purification in its three divisions, ghusl, wudu and tayammum, is a blessing from Allah the Mighty and Majestic upon His servants, based on His saying: ﴿and to complete His favor upon you﴾. There is no doubt that it is a blessing. Whoever sees the virtues of wudu and what it expiates of sins recognizes the blessing of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in this, and likewise ghusl from janabah, especially in the days of winter and the days of hardship.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. Those who say that two prayers may not be performed with one tayammum argue from the verse, that Allah said: ﴿then you find no water﴾, conditioning tayammum on the absence of water. They said: a person must search for water at every prayer.
* The Shaykh: But this one has no water.
* The student: If he does not find it, he performs tayammum.
* The Shaykh: No, Allah permitted tayammum if he does not find water, if you know that around me there is no water.
* The student: We say: it is obligatory for him to search.
* The Shaykh: This is nonsense. Would Allah obligate a person, saying: search for water, while I know I have no water? Not at all; this contradicts wisdom and also contradicts the law.
* A student: It is said that wiping part of the head suffices in wudu; do they say this regarding tayammum?
* The Shaykh: They may be bound by that, but I do not know whether they say it or not; in reality, they would be bound by it.
* A student: May Allah reward you well. The authentic hadith is that the Prophet (ﷺ) struck the wall and performed tayammum so that he could return the greeting to that Companion. How is this hadith to be understood? Because some say it is permissible to perform tayammum with anything; tayammum on a wall, even though there were things in it that are not from the earth?
* The Shaykh: Is the wall not earth?
* A student: They use this as evidence for the permissibility of tayammum on a wall covered with plaster, even if it is painted with paint.
* The Shaykh: In the time of the Messenger there was no painting with paint. But in any case, we say: if it is painted with paint and there is dust on it, it suffices.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, must the earth (sa'id) be connected to the ground? That is, if he takes a stone or sand and moves it to another place, and similarly if a person sometimes lifts a rug or carpet and finds dust beneath it, is tayammum with this permissible?
* The Shaykh: Yes, permissible, without doubt, permissible.
* A student: The order (tartib)... is tayammum not definitive?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is not definitive, but the apparent meaning of the Sunnah, "I begin with what Allah began with," indicates that one must observe the order.
* The student: But if one contradicts the order?
* The Shaykh: The jurists say, if one contradicts the order: in the case of janabah there is no harm; if the tayammum is for janabah, there is no harm in contradicting the order, because ghusl does not require order, and tayammum is a substitute for ghusl. But for minor impurity, order is necessary. However, it is said that the purity of tayammum cannot be analogized to the purity of water, because of the many differences between them, and attaching a branch to a root requires that there be an agreement that unites them.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, one who performs tayammum and then finds water after putting on khuffs must wash, because he did not put them on in a state of purity?
* The Shaykh: No, no, he must perform a complete wudu.
* The student: Shaykh, if they argue against us, they say: you now say that he is pure by this verse if he put them on while they were in a state of purity, and the hadith of al-Mughirah is absolute; the Prophet (ﷺ) did not say: after you washed them, but said: in a state of purity; so this case is covered.
* The Shaykh: But his specifying what he said: "I put them on in a state of purity," so that we would say it includes when he purified by tayammum. He said: "I put them on in a state of purity," and this indicates that one wipes only in a purity connected to the feet.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you, a group went out into the desert, and they had water that was not sufficient to purify them all (...) it is shared; what do they do if the water falls short of purifying everyone?
* The Shaykh: They draw lots over it; the use of lots is necessary, because here, did you hear his question? He says: a group sharing water, and the water is not sufficient for all of them to purify themselves with; what do they do? If one of them prefers the other, we say: preference (ithar) in an obligatory matter is not permissible, so nothing remains for us except lots.
* A student: And the little water that remains from their purification, enough for part of the purification, so...?
* The Shaykh: He performs wudu with it.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How, what (...)?
* The student: I mean, it remains roughly half a small bottle, not enough.
* The Shaykh: So it means it is only enough to wash his face and hands, for example? He uses it and performs tayammum for the rest.
* A student: Shaykh, we said that one may not combine two purities; so how (...)?
* The Shaykh: We did not say this; who said this? We said one may not combine two complete purities, meaning one performs wudu and tayammum. But if he finds only part, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16].
* A student: If we say he performs wudu with this remaining water, is this an act of worship? The one who takes a portion of water and washes his face and hands with it, but it is not sufficient for the rest of the body.
* The Shaykh: He washes.
* The student: That is, he washes them; but is this an act of worship? And is there evidence for it?

Shaykh: Yes, indeed. The generality of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "What I have forbidden you, avoid it; and what I have commanded you, do of it as much as you are able" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7288) and Muslim (1337 / 130) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. And we have been commanded to perform wudu', and we are unable to do all of it except some of it.

Student: Does he dry his hands before striking the earth (for tayammum), or does he strike even if...?

Shaykh: If we say that dust is required, then he must dry them beforehand. And if we say that it is not a condition, then there is no harm.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ (7) ﴿O you who have believed, be steadfast in [standing firm] for Allah, witnesses in justice. And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 7-8].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾. Among the benefits we have mentioned previously, did we mention that this verse establishes that Allah possesses wisdom (hikmah)?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good.

Did we mention that this verse is evidence that gratitude (shukr) is acting righteously? Yes, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that you may be grateful﴾.

If someone asks: What is gratitude? We say: The Prophet ﷺ explained it in his saying: "Indeed, Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, and He said, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿O messengers, eat from the good things and do righteous deeds﴾." [Recorded by Muslim (1015/65) from Abu Hurayrah.]

So gratitude, the gratitude to Allah, is righteous action. There is no doubt that interpreting the words of the Messenger and the words of Allah by means of one another takes precedence over seeking other interpretations. But we have mentioned previously that the seat of gratitude is the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, and that it occurs only in return for a blessing. As for praise (hamd), it occurs in return for a blessing, or for the perfection of a praiseworthy attribute, and it is done with the limbs and the tongue.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾. Allah, exalted is He, only commanded us to remember the blessing so that we would know His grace upon us, so that obedience to Him would become easy for us, because every person, by the requirement of his innate nature and disposition, must submit to one who has done good to him. So He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾: remember it.

﴿And His covenant with which He bound you﴾, meaning the pact by which He made you bind yourselves, and it is His saying: ﴿when you said, "We hear and we obey"﴾. The believer's saying "We hear and we obey" means his commitment to the entire Sharia, without distinction between what his heart desires and what it does not desire.

His saying ﴿We hear﴾ means: what is said. ﴿And we obey﴾ means: in what is commanded and prohibited. It includes affirming the report, carrying out the command, and avoiding the prohibition.

﴿And fear Allah﴾: take a protection from Him, mighty and majestic, by doing His commands and abandoning His prohibitions with knowledge and insight.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾: this sentence is a reason (ta'lil) that contains a warning. That is to say: piety must be founded upon the soundness of the heart, and it is not merely a statement on the tongue. Rather, a person's piety must be in his heart and his limbs. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of the owner of the breasts. And what is "the owner of the breasts"? It is the hearts.

Know that the word (dhāt) is used in the Arabic language with several meanings. Among them, it is used as a relative pronoun in the dialect of Ṭayy, as Ibn Malik said:

"And like al-latī, there is likewise among them dhāt ∗∗∗ ...................."

So the dialect of Ṭayy, for example, says, in place of "the woman who obeyed Allah came," "the woman dhāt obeyed Allah came," so it means (allatī) to them.
It is used to denote direction, as in His saying: ﴿So fear Allah and amend the state of affairs (dhāta baynikum) among you﴾ [al-Anfal 1], meaning: the direction or the relation between you.

And it is used to mean (ṣāḥibah), in the sense of "possessor of," as in this verse: ﴿bi-dhāt al-ṣudūr﴾, meaning: the possessor of the breasts.

It is not used to mean the self (nafs) except in the terminology of the theologians (mutakallimūn), for they use dhāt to mean the self, that is, that which is opposed to the attribute (ṣifah). For this reason you find, in the speech of those who discuss creed, that they often say: "the essence and the attributes," expressing by "essence" the self.

So His saying: ﴿Allah warns you of Himself (nafsahu)﴾ [Ali 'Imran 28], if we wish to interpret it according to the terminology of the theologians, we say: "nafsahu" means His essence (dhātahu). The self of Allah, mighty and majestic, is not an attribute other than the essence; rather, it is the essence itself. So the saying of some scholars of creed, "and we affirm for Allah a self (nafs)," may lead some people to understand that the self is an attribute added to the essence. That is not so. Rather, they mean that we describe Allah as having a self, but it is not a separate attribute; it is the essence itself.

So His saying ﴿Allah warns you of Himself﴾ is exactly like saying: "Allah warns you of Allah," meaning that Allah, mighty and majestic, has a self.

And His saying: ﴿You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Yours﴾ means: what is with You and what is with me. So be attentive to this, because some people, when they read in books of creed, "We affirm for Allah a self," think that this is an attribute added to the essence, and it is not so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is prescribed for a person to mention the favour of Allah. Is that obligatory or recommended? In this there is detail: if failing to mention it leads to forgetting an obligation, then mentioning it is obligatory, such as when a person sees that his soul has strayed and drifted away from performing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden. Then let him remind it of Allah's favour, saying, for example: "Remember, O soul, the favour of Allah upon you: health, well-being, the sending of messengers, the revelation of books, the clarification of the truth, and the like."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah, exalted is He, has a favour upon us. This is a matter that needs no proof. But is the favour for the believer and the disbeliever, or for the believer alone?

We say: As for the general favour, which humans and animals share, it is for the believer and the disbeliever. The disbeliever enjoys Allah's favour as an animal enjoys it. As for the special favour, which is Allah's favour upon the servant in faith and knowledge, this is specific to the believer.

If someone asks you: Does Allah have a favour upon the disbeliever? Say: In this there is detail. As for the general favour, yes: ﴿And whatever favour you have is from Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 53]. As for the special favour, the disbeliever is not included in it, because it is specific to the believers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon a person to remember the covenant by which he bound himself to Allah, which is the pledge of hearing and obedience.

If someone says: We do not remember this covenant? We say: The covenant is established by speech and it is established by action. As for speech, we do not recall it, even if the hadith is authentic: "Indeed Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins and took from them the covenant and the pledge."[Recorded by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4703) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and by Ahmad in his Musnad (21232) from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

As for action, yes, it is established, and that is by the innate nature (fitrah) with which Allah created the human being, including monotheism and acknowledgment of Allah, mighty and majestic. Likewise, by the intellect He gave him, with which he distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between honesty and lying. This is a covenant; we say: a covenant by what? By action. That is to say, you do not recall that you pledged to Allah, mighty and majestic, by speech, but by the intellect and innate nature He gave you, that has become a covenant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: mere hearing is of no avail. It must be hearing that is accompanied by response. Mere hearing is not enough. This is shown by His saying: ﴿We hear and we obey﴾. And the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, supports this: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 21]. Allah negated hearing from them because they did not bring the benefit of hearing, which is obedience. Therefore mere listening is not sufficient; rather, listening is a proof against the servant, so when he hears he must comply.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of piety (taqwa), and that it is founded upon remembering the covenant and the pledge, by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah﴾. We have said that the most comprehensive definition of taqwa is what? It is taking a protection from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He, by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions with knowledge and insight.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning to whoever departs from piety, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the seat of piety is the heart, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: make the basis of piety on what? On the hearts. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart."[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599/107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.] We ask Allah to set right all our hearts.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, and that it encompasses what is apparent and what is hidden. What is the indication from the verse? The comprehensiveness of knowledge, because He informed us that He is Knowing of what is within the breasts, which requires that He knows the apparent and the hidden.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 8:

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8].

First: In the verse there are two readings of ﴿shana'an﴾: one with a sukun, ﴿shan'an﴾, and one with a fatha, ﴿shana'an﴾. The apparent reason (and Allah knows best) for the reading with sukun is lightness, because ﴿shana'an﴾ contains some heaviness due to the succession of two vowels; when it is said ﴿shan'an﴾, it becomes lighter.

In any case, this explanation is an explanation of what has occurred, not of what will occur. That is to say, it is not for us to alter and choose the easier word on the tongue; rather, we explain the readings that have come down, because recitation is tawqifi (based on transmission). So we say: there are ﴿shan'an﴾ and ﴿shana'an﴾.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and we have previously mentioned this form of address many times and what follows from it.

﴿Be persistently standing firm﴾: ﴿kونوا﴾ is a command to be. Is it a legislative or a cosmic command? Legislative.

﴿qawwamin﴾ means possessors of standing firm. I say this so that it is not thought that the command concerns frequency of standing, and not the standing itself. We say: ﴿qawwamin﴾ here, its doubling indicates attribution (nisbah) and not intensity. It is also possible to take it as indicating intensity with reference to the plurality of the addressees: if they are a community, and one stands for this, another for that, and another for that, the whole becomes numerous, and so it becomes ﴿qawwam﴾. In any case, if (fa''al) is taken to indicate intensity, it is with reference to the whole, so when each one is standing firm for justice and they are a community, it is correct to say (qawwamin). And if you take it as not intensive, it indicates attribution, i.e., be people possessing standing firm.

﴿qawwamin lillah﴾: the lam here indicates sincerity, i.e., make your standing firm for justice, that is, for justice, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Do not fear anyone in that, and do not show favouritism to anyone in that.

﴿shuhada' bil-qist﴾: as to its i'rab (grammatical analysis), ﴿shuhada'﴾ may be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of ﴿qawwamin﴾: standing firm while being witnesses. It may also be a second predicate of (kana), since multiple predicates are permissible. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ [al-Buruj 14-15]. How many predicates? Forgiving, Loving, Lord of the Throne, Glorious: four.

﴿shuhada'﴾ is the plural of (shahid) or of (shahid): the meaning is that when you bear witness, bear witness with justice.

﴿bil-qist﴾ means with justice. There has come in a hadith: "Those who act justly will be on pulpits of light on the right hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."[[Narrated by Muslim (1827/18) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.]]

﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾: ﴿la yajrimannakum﴾ means do not let them move you.

﴿shana'an﴾ means hatred.

﴿qawm﴾ means a group of people. When one says qawm and women are mentioned along with them, then qawm refers to men and women to females, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them﴾ [al-Hujurat 11]. When (qawm) is mentioned alone, it includes men and women: ﴿We sent Noah to his people﴾ [al-A'raf 59], meaning males and females.

﴿shana'anu qawmin 'ala alla ta'dilu﴾: who parses ﴿alla ta'dilu﴾?

* A student: (ʿalā) is a preposition.

* The Shaykh: (ʿalā) is a preposition.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Prohibitive? (lā) is prohibitive.

* The student: No, negative.

* The Shaykh: Negative?

* The student: No, prohibitive; it has apocopated the verb.

* The Shaykh: Prohibitive, it has apocopated the verb, or is it extra? Start from (lā).

* Student: (lā) is negative.

* The Shaykh: Negative or prohibitive?

* The student: Negative.

* The Shaykh: Negative.

* The student: ﴿ta'dilu﴾ is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive governed by (an), its subjunctive sign being the deletion of the nun; the waw is the subject; and the verbal noun is in the position of a genitive, a prepositional object.

* The Shaykh: And (an) and what it governs is in the position of ...?

* The student: Genitive.

* The Shaykh: The estimate?

* The student: Upon your not being just.

* The Shaykh: Upon your not being just. Do you agree with this?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Correct.

﴿'ala alla ta'dilu﴾: that is, their hatred should not move you to not be just, which is injustice.

Then He said: ﴿Be just﴾, even toward whom you hate? Even toward whom you hate, yes. ﴿Be just﴾ means speak with justice. So what is justice? Justice is giving every holder of a right his right. This is justice.

﴿Huwa﴾ means justice. Do you agree? Justice has not been mentioned previously; we say that justice is understood from the verb ﴿'dilu﴾ (be just), because the referent of the pronoun may be explicitly stated by its wording, and may be by a wording that indicates it. Here ﴿'dilu﴾ indicates that the verb derives from justice, so ﴿huwa﴾ means the justice you have been commanded.

﴿Nearer to righteousness﴾: He did not say "it is righteousness" but said ﴿nearer to righteousness﴾; this is because justice may be motivated by fear of Allah and thus be righteousness, and it may be motivated by love of praise from people and thus not be righteousness. Therefore the noble verse says ﴿nearer to righteousness﴾.

﴿And fear Allah﴾: after commanding us to be persistently standing firm, and forbidding that hatred move us to abandon justice, then commanding justice, He says ﴿And fear Allah﴾, and this is like a seal upon what preceded.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: we say about this sentence what we said about the previous ﴿Indeed Allah knows the secrets of the breasts﴾; that is, it is a sentence that includes a warning against opposing taqwa.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed Allah is Acquainted﴾, they said: al-khabir is more precise than al-'alim, because it (al-khabir) derives from al-khubr, which is knowledge of the inner realities of a matter. That is why the farmer is called khabir, and cultivation is called mukhabarah, because he buries the seed in the earth and it disappears; so the khabir is the one who knows hidden matters.

﴿With what you do﴾ means with what you do of speech or action. The benefit of Allah mentioning this is that we should remain upright in His command, because if we opposed His command, He would be aware of us, glorified and exalted is He.

* There are benefits in this verse. First: the obligation of sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in testimony, by His saying: ﴿Be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾, and He said in another verse: ﴿And establish testimony for Allah﴾ [al-Talaq 2].

Know that if you are sincere to Allah in testimony, you will not show favouritism to a relative or a friend, and your hatred of a person will not move you not to testify for him as long as you are sincere to Allah, the Exalted, in testimony.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory for a person to testify with justice, with fairness. Good. And if the one testified against is your relative, your father, your brother, your uncle, even so, by His saying in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives﴾. Testifying against one's father and mother is not counted as disobedience to them; rather it is righteousness, because when you testify against them you prevent them from wrongdoing. The Prophet ﷺ made preventing the wrongdoer from wronging as helping the wrongdoer, and he said: "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." They said: O Messenger of Allah, this one is oppressed, so how do we help the oppressor? He said: "You prevent him from his oppression."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6952) from the hadith of Anas.]]

* Among the benefits of this verse: the obligation to testify with justice even if you are unwilling, because some people may be moved by dislike of a person, or dislike that a person be harmed by concealing testimony, so you find yourself in turmoil: will he testify or not? So it is obligatory that the closeness of a relative or the hatred of a distant one not move you not to testify. Testify with justice.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the methods of the Noble Qur'an, if this expression is correct (methods), or if you prefer, and this is better: the Qur'an's expression of justice indicates the falsity of the saying of those who claim that the religion of Islam is a religion of equality. This, in its absolute form, is problematic, because they mean by it that one should not distinguish between man and woman, and they also mean that one should not distinguish between Muslim and disbeliever, and between the pious and the wicked. Allah, the Exalted, has denounced this with great denunciation: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ [al-Qalam 35]. What comes after it, O people? ﴿What is wrong with you?﴾: say, what is this judgment? What moved you to it? How do you judge this judgment? ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar 9]?

If you reflect upon the Qur'an, you will find the negation of equality in it more than its affirmation, and that what is in the Qur'an is justice, which is giving every holder of a right what he deserves. Therefore the sound expression is to say: the religion of Islam is the religion of justice, which is what Allah commanded in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives﴾ [al-Nahl 90].

Yes, if people agree in rights, it is correct to say it is a religion of equality; when they are alike in the cause of a ruling and its purposes, then we say it is a religion of equality. That is, if a noble person steals and a lowly person steals, here we say there is no harm in its not distinguishing between noble and lowly, and that it equalizes between them, because equalizing here is justice.

Based on this, when equality is justice, then yes; but the equality these people aim at is not correct. Religion distinguishes completely in every situation where the wisdom is distinction. Therefore, you, O students of knowledge, must, when you see some books of contemporary modernists saying the religion of Islam is a religion of equality, say: Wait, who said this? Bring me one verse establishing equalization, and I will bring you many verses denying equalization. But instead of saying it this way, bring the beloved word that comes to the heart like cool water to the liver of the thirsty: it is justice.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that justice is closer to righteousness, and this is explicit.

* Among its benefits: that good deeds include some that distance from righteousness and some that draw near to it, and upon this is built the superiority of deeds; the superiority of deeds is indicated by the Book, the Sunnah and reason, and that deeds vary, and doers also vary: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to all Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Hadid 10], even though they are all Companions, yet they are not equal.

Among its benefits: that good deeds include some that distance from righteousness and some that draw near, and upon this is built the superiority of deeds; the superiority of deeds is indicated by the Book, the Sunnah and reason; deeds vary, and doers also vary. ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ — read the verse — ﴿those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to all Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Hadid 10], even though they are all Companions, yet they are not equal. Until the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Khalid ibn al-Walid when what happened between him and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf occurred: "Do not revile my Companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uhud, it would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor half of it."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3673) and Muslim (2541/222) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] This is between whom? A Companion and another. How then do those after them return?! So this is the difference of doers. Likewise the difference of deeds: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives﴾ [al-Nisa' 95], and so on. Deeds vary in superiority, and I say: the superiority of deeds necessitates the superiority of doers. This is what Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah hold: that deeds vary, doers vary, and that faith increases and likewise decreases.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of taqwa. Observe how Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, repeats taqwa in many verses, because in reality the religion of Islam revolves around it. If a person fears his Lord, he will uphold the religion of Allah, the Exalted, as Allah wills.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to those who oppose the taqwa of Allah, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the vastness of Allah's knowledge, and that He, glorified and exalted, knows the inner realities of matters. Allah said of Himself: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Apparent and the Hidden﴾ [al-Hadid 3], and the Prophet ﷺ explained "the Hidden" as that beyond which there is nothing.[[Narrated by Muslim (2713/61) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] Nothing is beyond Allah. He sees everything, knows everything, has power over everything, everything is in His grasp, nothing is beyond Him. This is close to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah's awareness encompasses action. Know that when (ʿamal) is said, it includes speech and deed. Pay attention: when (ʿamal) is said, it is for speech and action. Speech is a deed of the tongue, and action is a deed of the limbs; but "action" (fi'l) is generally applied only to the deeds of the limbs, whereas "deed" (ʿamal) applies to both. Indeed Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, in the Wasitiyyah creed, that blessed creed, said: religion and faith are speech and deed: speech of the heart and tongue, and deed of the heart, tongue and limbs. He made the heart have a deed and a speech, and so it is: the speech of the heart is its affirmation, assent and faith, and its deed is its hope, fear, reliance and the like; so there is in it a kind of inward movement, whereas speech is affirmation and assent.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verses 9–10 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 9].

﴿Wa'ada﴾ (promised). It is said "wa'ada" and it is said "awada." They said "awada" is used for evil and "wa'ada" for good, and on this they based the verse of the poet:

*Indeed I, whether I threaten him or promise him,*
*I will break my threat and I will fulfil my promise.*

What is *al-iy'ad* (threatening) used for?
* Students: For evil.
* Shaykh: And *al-wa'd* (promising)?
* Students: For good.
* Shaykh: For good. Here He says ﴿wa'ada Allah﴾ and did not say *awada*, because it concerns those who believe and do righteous deeds. But what some scholars have said may be disputed, because Allah the Exalted mentioned *al-wa'd* in punishment, saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein﴾ [al-Tawbah 68]. This shows that *al-wa'd* comes in good and also in evil.
* Student: May Allah reward you well. If one of the witnesses says, "I do not want to testify, for fear that harm will befall me," is that permitted for him?
* Shaykh: The scholars say: if he fears harm that cannot be borne, then there is no harm, but he must give the testimony at another time. As for harm that can be borne, such as the person he testifies against being hostile to him or something similar, then concealing the testimony is not permitted.
* Student: We said that *al-wa'd* is for good and *al-iy'ad* is for evil. Now, O our Shaykh, does Allah's threatening of the disbelievers with Hell not carry the sense of mockery, because of His saying ﴿Give the hypocrites glad tidings﴾ and that glad tidings...?
* Shaykh: No. That would be an irregular usage, but it is regular. The Qur'an does not contain *awada*. Otherwise it could be understood as I have said.
* Student: (...) Allah the Exalted's taking the offspring of Adam from his loins is based on the hadith. If it is authentic, then this is valid, and the statement may be held. But there is a hadith that appears in the two Sahihs, as far as I recall, certainly in Sahih al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Prophets, which explicitly states this. So how...?
* Shaykh: And what is it?
* Student: I do not recall the wording of the hadith, but in it Allah...
* Shaykh: Bring it, bring it, may Allah reward you with good.
* Student: The difference between our saying that ﴿qawwamin﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8] is a *nisbah* (attributive form) and saying that it is an intensive form (*mubalaghah*): what follows from the disagreement?
* Shaykh: What follows from the disagreement is that if we say ﴿qawwamin﴾ is an intensive form, then its meaning must be applied to the collective. Why? Because if we say the command in the intensive form is addressed to an individual, then the command becomes only for frequent standing, and standing once would not fall under the command, because Allah said ﴿Be maintainers of justice﴾. But if we say it is a *nisbah*, it includes the few and the many.
* Student: Shaykh, why is it not correct to say that the command is for us to be (...) *qawwamin* and to stand frequently in the mosques?
* Shaykh: Yes, but is the command to do it frequently, or to stand even once?
* Student: To do it frequently.
* Shaykh: No. Even if a person upholds justice once, he has complied. Because if we say it is addressed to frequency, then the one who does it only once is not complying with the command. That would have to be derived from another verse, for example.
* Student: Shaykh, so if someone says he stood once, we would say that is enough, and he need not stand for justice a second time?
* Shaykh: No, because if it is commanded once, then all the more so each time is commanded.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, the explanation of this form, or the disagreement regarding this form...
* Shaykh: Where?
* Student: The form *fa''al* in ﴿qawwamin﴾. The disagreement over whether it is a *nisbah* or an intensive form leads to a disagreement among the scholars, as in his saying "*zawwarat al-qubur*" (women who frequently visit graves) [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1574) from the hadith of Hassan ibn Thabit.]]. So what is the criterion? How do we sometimes take it as intensive and sometimes as *nisbah*?
* Shaykh: No, "*zawwarat al-qubur*" does not fall under this, because the hadith is authentically reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he "cursed women who visit graves" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3236) and al-Tirmidhi (320) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].
* Student: Is there a criterion for distinguishing the two meanings? When do we take it in this sense?
* Shaykh: Yes. For example, take His saying ﴿and your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat 46]. If someone said this is for multiplicity, the meaning would not hold, because then what is negated would be only the frequency of injustice. But if we say it is a *nisbah*, it is correct to say that Allah negated from Himself the attribution of injustice to Himself, even once.
* Student: So it depends on the context?
* Shaykh: In any case there is an indicator. If you say, for example, "Do not be *akulan*" (a great eater), or "*akkalan*," which is better so that it matches the form, does the meaning mean "do not eat ever"?
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: "Do not eat much."
* Student: May Allah reward you well, O Shaykh. We said that *al-wa'd* is for good and *awada* is for evil. Is this a consistent rule?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: It is not consistent.
* Shaykh: As we said, some scholars stated it, but it is not consistent, and we refuted it by His saying ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah 68].
* Student: Shaykh, the answer to the difficulty in the verse has not become clear to me. That is, removing the difficulty in the verse.
* Shaykh: Which verse?
* Student: His saying ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾. The answer has not become clear to me.
* Shaykh: Is this a threat or not?
* Student: A threat.
* Shaykh: Then although He used ﴿wa'ada﴾ and did not say *awada*...
* Student: Can a promise fail to be fulfilled? Does *al-wa'd* sometimes not apply to good?
* Shaykh: What do you mean?
* Student: Does *al-wa'd* sometimes fail to be fulfilled, and not be for good?
* Shaykh: No. The word *wa'ada* is used for good and for evil.
* Student: Some scholars mentioned that in His saying ﴿and let not the hatred of a people...﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8] there is a second reading with a *damma* on the *ya'*. Shaykh: What?
* Student: Some scholars mentioned that there is a second reading in His saying ﴿wa la yajrimannakum﴾ with a *damma* on the *ya'*.
* Shaykh: ﴿yujrimannakum﴾?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: By Allah, I have noted the readings in my Mushaf and I did not find it. It is not there.
* Student: Al-Kisa'i mentioned it in (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but is this one of the seven (canonical readings)? We note the seven.
* Student: What is the validity of the statement of those who say that the covenant here is the covenant which the Prophet, peace be upon him, took from the Companions in the Pledge of al-Ridwan and the Pledge of al-'Aqabah, when they said, "We have heard and we obey"?
* Shaykh: No. Even the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, when the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims﴾ [Al 'Imran 102], they said, "We cannot bear this." So they were commanded to say, "We have heard and we obey," and then it was lightened for them.
* Student: In the verse you mentioned a little earlier, ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾, is it not possible to take the word *wa'ada* in its original sense, as good, but in this context like His saying ﴿give the hypocrites glad tidings﴾, for example, that this...?
* Shaykh: That is (...), but it does not hold. Indeed, if *awada* were consistently used for evil, we could say that this is placed in the position of *wa'd*. But *awada* in the sense of promising evil never occurs in the Qur'an even once.
* Student: Shaykh, some people prohibit writing on the Mushaf. Is his statement valid?
* Shaykh: Marginal notes, you mean?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes. In the earlier period the writing was not vocalized, neither in the text nor in what was written in the margins, so some of the early generations disliked writing anything alongside the Mushaf, because the Qur'an would become mixed with the written material or with other things. But now it does not get mixed. So if this does not affect the letters, meaning you do not write between the lines so that they become mixed, then there is no harm in it.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward (9). And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Blazing Fire (10). O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ [al-Ma'idah 9–11].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. ﴿Believe﴾ means in what must be believed in. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained that faith is "that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, its good and its evil" [[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]].
As for ﴿they did righteous deeds﴾, meaning they performed righteous works, ﴿righteous﴾ is then an adjective of an omitted noun, and the implied phrase is "righteous deeds." So when is a deed righteous? A deed is righteous when it includes two matters. First: sincerity to Allah. Second: following the Sharia of Allah, whether it is from the community of Muhammad or from earlier nations. Two things are necessary:
First: sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because worship is the right of Allah alone, so it is not permitted to associate anyone with Him in it. The many proofs that indicate the obligation of sincerity to Allah in worship include: ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar 2]; ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah 5]; "Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (54) and Muslim (1907/155) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]. The texts on this are numerous.
As for following, the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. Any deed for which there is no command of Allah and His Messenger, whether an act of worship or a transaction, is rejected by its doer. Therefore the deed must have the command of Allah and His Messenger behind it, and following is not realized unless the deed agrees with the Sharia in six matters: first, the cause; second, the kind; third, the type; fourth, the quantity; fifth, the place; sixth, the time. So the deed must conform to the Sharia in these six matters: the cause, the kind, the type, the quantity, the time, and the place.
Whoever worships Allah through an act tied to a cause that Allah and His Messenger did not make a cause, the worship is void and a rejected innovation. An example: a person says every time he puts on a garment, "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad." If he is asked why, he says, "I remember the Prophet putting on a garment, so I send blessings upon him." What do we say to him?
We say: this act of worship is an innovation, because it was not reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him, nor from his Companions, that they used to send blessings upon the Prophet when they wished to dress.
It is also necessary that it agree with the Sharia in the kind of worship. If someone worships Allah with what its kind has not been legislated, the worship is rejected from him. An example: he sacrifices a horse instead of a cow, for instance. We say: this sacrifice is not accepted, because it is not of the kind that Allah and His Messenger legislated, so it is not accepted.
The type, which is more specific than the kind: whoever worships Allah the Exalted with an act whose type has not been legislated, it is not accepted. As if he invented dhikr that is legislated in kind but in another type, it is not accepted, because of the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."
Likewise, what? The quantity. If he worships Allah the Exalted with an act that is increased or decreased, it is not accepted from him. So if he prays Zuhr three rak'ahs, it is not accepted; if he prays it five, it is not accepted, because it opposes the Sharia in the number.
Also in the manner: if it opposes the Sharia in its manner, it is not accepted. As if he prostrated before bowing, it is not accepted because it opposes the Sharia in its manner.
* Student: That makes seven.
* Another student: This is new, Shaykh, this is new.
* Shaykh: Why, brother?
* Student: You did not mention it; you did not mention the manner.
* Shaykh: Yes. In reality it replaces the type. Sometimes we express it as type and sometimes as manner.
* Student: What is the type, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: The type is in reality the manner.
The fifth: the place. If a person performs i'tikaf in his house instead of the mosque, and devotes himself to worship in the house, it is not accepted, because it does not conform to the Sharia in place.
The time: if a person fasts in other than Ramadan in place of Ramadan, it is not accepted, because it is outside the legislated time. Likewise, if he stands at 'Arafah on a day other than the day of 'Arafah, or throws the pebbles outside the season of Hajj, or what is similar.
So the righteous deed is that which conforms to the Sharia in these six matters: the cause, the kind, the quantity, the manner, the time, and the place. The type is replaced by the manner, because it is clearer.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says of those who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾, and this is in return for sins; ﴿and a great reward﴾ is in return for good deeds. So bad deeds are forgiven, and good deeds are rewarded with this great reward.
* From the benefits of this verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds. The proof of this is what is ordained for them of reward, because every deed for which a reward is ordained is virtuous and commanded.
* And from its benefits: faith alone is not sufficient, rather deeds are necessary. For this reason we find many people focusing on creed, saying, "Our creed is sound, praise be to Allah," and not paying attention to deeds. This is a shortcoming. Rather, with creed there must be righteous deeds.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's forgiveness, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾. We have repeated the meaning of forgiveness, that it is the covering of sin and overlooking it.
If someone says: forgiveness here is unrestricted; He did not say "from Allah."
The answer: it is unrestricted, but Allah the Exalted said ﴿and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Al 'Imran 135]. It is known necessarily from the religion of Islam that the one in whose hand is forgiveness and mercy is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants, in that He made the reward in the position of a wage, as if the worker were a hired person who, when he completes the work, is given his wage, although the favour belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, first and last.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of the reward of the believers who do righteous deeds, since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, magnified it. The magnification of the Great for a thing indicates that it is great with a greatness that a person cannot imagine or conceive, and it is so.
Since this Qur'an is *mathani* (oft-repeated), as Allah described it: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating﴾ [al-Zumar 23], when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the reward of the believers who do righteous deeds, He followed it by mentioning their counterparts, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾ [al-Ma'idah 10]. ﴿Disbelieve﴾ is in opposition to righteous deeds, and ﴿deny﴾ is in opposition to faith. They denied what must be affirmed and disbelieved in what must be acted upon. ﴿They disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾. They were not upright regarding the command or the report: they met the report with denial and met the action with disbelief.
﴿And denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. The question here: are the signs meant here the legislated signs or the cosmic signs?
* Students: Both.

Sheikh: Both. Whoever denies the Lordship of Allah, His creation of created beings, and His disposal of the universe is one who denies the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-kawniyyah). Whoever acknowledges that but does not carry out obedience to Allah has disbelieved and denied the legislative signs (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah).

The signs of Allah the Exalted are of two kinds: cosmic and legislative.

As for the cosmic signs, they are this universe with what it contains: the sun, the moon, the stars, night and day, the seas and the rivers, and other great creatures, some of which no one can encompass because of their vastness, and some of which no one can encompass because of their smallness. You will sometimes examine a book and find within its folds tiny insects, extremely small, that can scarcely be seen with the eye. These are creatures of Allah, whom Allah provides for. He knows their resting place and their repository, and their affairs are not hidden from Him, as the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾ [Hud 6].

As for the legislative signs, they are what the messengers brought, and they are signs indicating Allah the Exalted, because human beings cannot produce their like. Who can bring a law suited to mankind in every time and place, in comparison with the Muhammadan Sharia? No one. Likewise, the earlier laws given to the previous nations were perfectly fitted to their conditions, their eras and their places. No one can bring the like of these legislative signs.

The Exalted said: ﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire﴾. ﴿Those﴾ here is the second subject (mubtada' thani), and ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ is the first subject (mubtada' awwal), and ﴿companions﴾ (ashab) is the predicate of the second subject. The second subject and its predicate are in the position of a nominative predicate of the first subject, and the link is the demonstrative.

﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire﴾: that is, the people of the Hellfire who are constantly bound to it. ﴿Al-Jahim﴾ is the Fire, may Allah protect us and you from it, and it was so named for its depth and its blackness.

* In the verse there are benefits:
* Among them: the Noble Qur'an is paired (mathani); when it mentions the people of righteous deeds, it mentions the people of evil deeds. The benefit of this, O students, is that neither the aspect of hope nor the aspect of fear should prevail. This is because if a person has before him only the descriptions of believers and the reward of believers, that may lead him to what? To hope, forgetting fear. And if he has before him only the descriptions of disbelievers and the punishment of disbelievers, he may be overtaken by what? By fear and despair of Allah's mercy. Therefore Allah the Exalted mentions this alongside that, so that despair of Allah's mercy does not overtake a person when mention is made of what instills fear, nor a sense of security from Allah's plan when mention is made of what instills hope.

If someone says: Which is better for the doer: that he give precedence to the aspect of fear, or that he give precedence to the aspect of hope?

The answer: The best of what has been said on this is that at the time of doing a righteous deed, he gives precedence to the aspect of hope, and at the time of intending a sin, he gives precedence to the aspect of fear. This is because when he does a righteous deed and gives precedence to hope, he thinks well of Allah, that Allah will accept his deed and reward him for it, so he is energized to act and seeks his reward from Allah. And at the time of intending disobedience, if he gave precedence to hope, his soul would say to him: Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, this is an easy sin, and if you commit it, repent; the door of repentance is open, and similar things. But if he gives precedence to fear and fears that he will not be granted repentance and that his heart will swerve, then he restrains himself from disobedience. So the best of what is said on this is that a person look to his own state: when he performs acts of obedience, he gives precedence to hope, and when he intends sin, he gives precedence to fear.

If someone says: Did not Allah the Mighty and Majestic say: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful that they will return to their Lord﴾ [al-Mu'minun 60], thus clarifying that among the descriptions of these noble people is that when they give what they give, their hearts are fearful, fearing that it will not be accepted from them, as has been reported in its interpretation?

We say: Yes, that is so. This applies when a person fears that he may be pleased with his deed, in which case he must fear. But if he is free of that, and knows that this righteous deed is by Allah's help, then let him think well of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted has said in a hadith qudsi: "I am as My servant thinks I am."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7405) and Muslim (2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: disbelief may be accompanied by denial, and it may not be. For this reason, sometimes Allah mentions disbelief alone, as in His saying: ﴿And beware the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 131]; and sometimes He mentions denial alone: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ [al-Zumar 32]; and sometimes He combines the two. This is because each of them alone may be sufficient to necessitate eternal abiding in the Fire, and when both are combined, that becomes more severe and greater, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: a person must submit completely to the signs of Allah, affirming their reports and implementing their rulings, because Allah threatened those who deny the signs and disbelieve in them with being what? With being the companions of the Hellfire.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic has mentioned in Surah an-Nisa' an emphatic oath that they do not believe except under conditions, saying: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in full acceptance﴾ [an-Nisa' 65]. This is one condition; ﴿and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged﴾ is the second; ﴿and submit in full acceptance﴾ is the third. So whoever makes other than Allah and His Messenger a judge is not a believer; and whoever makes Allah and His Messenger a judge but finds tightness in his heart, his chest not expanded by what Allah and His Messenger have judged, is not a believer. For this reason He said: ﴿then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged﴾. And whoever finds no discomfort but becomes lax and negligent in submitting, he has not believed. Then the negation of faith from him may be complete, or it may be partial, according to what is established in his heart and his deeds.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the disbelieving deniers are eternal in the Fire, due to His saying: ﴿companions of the Hellfire﴾. Whenever the word ﴿ashab﴾ comes, what is meant by it is constant, perpetual attachment, like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "By He in whose hand is my soul, no one from this Ummah hears of me, be he a Jew or a Christian, and then does not believe in what I have brought—or he said: does not follow what I have brought—except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."[[Narrated by Muslim (153/240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verses 9–10 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 9].

﴿Wa'ada﴾ (promised). It is said "wa'ada" and it is said "awada." They said "awada" is used for evil and "wa'ada" for good, and on this they based the verse of the poet:

*Indeed I, whether I threaten him or promise him,*
*I will break my threat and I will fulfil my promise.*

What is *al-iy'ad* (threatening) used for?
* Students: For evil.
* Shaykh: And *al-wa'd* (promising)?
* Students: For good.
* Shaykh: For good. Here He says ﴿wa'ada Allah﴾ and did not say *awada*, because it concerns those who believe and do righteous deeds. But what some scholars have said may be disputed, because Allah the Exalted mentioned *al-wa'd* in punishment, saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein﴾ [al-Tawbah 68]. This shows that *al-wa'd* comes in good and also in evil.
* Student: May Allah reward you well. If one of the witnesses says, "I do not want to testify, for fear that harm will befall me," is that permitted for him?
* Shaykh: The scholars say: if he fears harm that cannot be borne, then there is no harm, but he must give the testimony at another time. As for harm that can be borne, such as the person he testifies against being hostile to him or something similar, then concealing the testimony is not permitted.
* Student: We said that *al-wa'd* is for good and *al-iy'ad* is for evil. Now, O our Shaykh, does Allah's threatening of the disbelievers with Hell not carry the sense of mockery, because of His saying ﴿Give the hypocrites glad tidings﴾ and that glad tidings...?
* Shaykh: No. That would be an irregular usage, but it is regular. The Qur'an does not contain *awada*. Otherwise it could be understood as I have said.
* Student: (...) Allah the Exalted's taking the offspring of Adam from his loins is based on the hadith. If it is authentic, then this is valid, and the statement may be held. But there is a hadith that appears in the two Sahihs, as far as I recall, certainly in Sahih al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Prophets, which explicitly states this. So how...?
* Shaykh: And what is it?
* Student: I do not recall the wording of the hadith, but in it Allah...
* Shaykh: Bring it, bring it, may Allah reward you with good.
* Student: The difference between our saying that ﴿qawwamin﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8] is a *nisbah* (attributive form) and saying that it is an intensive form (*mubalaghah*): what follows from the disagreement?
* Shaykh: What follows from the disagreement is that if we say ﴿qawwamin﴾ is an intensive form, then its meaning must be applied to the collective. Why? Because if we say the command in the intensive form is addressed to an individual, then the command becomes only for frequent standing, and standing once would not fall under the command, because Allah said ﴿Be maintainers of justice﴾. But if we say it is a *nisbah*, it includes the few and the many.
* Student: Shaykh, why is it not correct to say that the command is for us to be (...) *qawwamin* and to stand frequently in the mosques?
* Shaykh: Yes, but is the command to do it frequently, or to stand even once?
* Student: To do it frequently.
* Shaykh: No. Even if a person upholds justice once, he has complied. Because if we say it is addressed to frequency, then the one who does it only once is not complying with the command. That would have to be derived from another verse, for example.
* Student: Shaykh, so if someone says he stood once, we would say that is enough, and he need not stand for justice a second time?
* Shaykh: No, because if it is commanded once, then all the more so each time is commanded.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, the explanation of this form, or the disagreement regarding this form...
* Shaykh: Where?
* Student: The form *fa''al* in ﴿qawwamin﴾. The disagreement over whether it is a *nisbah* or an intensive form leads to a disagreement among the scholars, as in his saying "*zawwarat al-qubur*" (women who frequently visit graves) [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1574) from the hadith of Hassan ibn Thabit.]]. So what is the criterion? How do we sometimes take it as intensive and sometimes as *nisbah*?
* Shaykh: No, "*zawwarat al-qubur*" does not fall under this, because the hadith is authentically reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he "cursed women who visit graves" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3236) and al-Tirmidhi (320) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].
* Student: Is there a criterion for distinguishing the two meanings? When do we take it in this sense?
* Shaykh: Yes. For example, take His saying ﴿and your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat 46]. If someone said this is for multiplicity, the meaning would not hold, because then what is negated would be only the frequency of injustice.
