But if we say it is a *nisbah*, it is correct to say that Allah negated from Himself the attribution of injustice to Himself, even once.
* Student: So it depends on the context?
* Shaykh: In any case there is an indicator. If you say, for example, "Do not be *akulan*" (a great eater), or "*akkalan*," which is better so that it matches the form, does the meaning mean "do not eat ever"?
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: "Do not eat much."
* Student: May Allah reward you well, O Shaykh. We said that *al-wa'd* is for good and *awada* is for evil. Is this a consistent rule?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: It is not consistent.
* Shaykh: As we said, some scholars stated it, but it is not consistent, and we refuted it by His saying ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah 68].
* Student: Shaykh, the answer to the difficulty in the verse has not become clear to me. That is, removing the difficulty in the verse.
* Shaykh: Which verse?
* Student: His saying ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾. The answer has not become clear to me.
* Shaykh: Is this a threat or not?
* Student: A threat.
* Shaykh: Then although He used ﴿wa'ada﴾ and did not say *awada*...
* Student: Can a promise fail to be fulfilled? Does *al-wa'd* sometimes not apply to good?
* Shaykh: What do you mean?
* Student: Does *al-wa'd* sometimes fail to be fulfilled, and not be for good?
* Shaykh: No. The word *wa'ada* is used for good and for evil.
* Student: Some scholars mentioned that in His saying ﴿and let not the hatred of a people...﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8] there is a second reading with a *damma* on the *ya'*. Shaykh: What?
* Student: Some scholars mentioned that there is a second reading in His saying ﴿wa la yajrimannakum﴾ with a *damma* on the *ya'*.
* Shaykh: ﴿yujrimannakum﴾?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: By Allah, I have noted the readings in my Mushaf and I did not find it. It is not there.
* Student: Al-Kisa'i mentioned it in (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but is this one of the seven (canonical readings)? We note the seven.
* Student: What is the validity of the statement of those who say that the covenant here is the covenant which the Prophet, peace be upon him, took from the Companions in the Pledge of al-Ridwan and the Pledge of al-'Aqabah, when they said, "We have heard and we obey"?
* Shaykh: No. Even the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, when the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims﴾ [Al 'Imran 102], they said, "We cannot bear this." So they were commanded to say, "We have heard and we obey," and then it was lightened for them.
* Student: In the verse you mentioned a little earlier, ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾, is it not possible to take the word *wa'ada* in its original sense, as good, but in this context like His saying ﴿give the hypocrites glad tidings﴾, for example, that this...?
* Shaykh: That is (...), but it does not hold. Indeed, if *awada* were consistently used for evil, we could say that this is placed in the position of *wa'd*. But *awada* in the sense of promising evil never occurs in the Qur'an even once.
* Student: Shaykh, some people prohibit writing on the Mushaf. Is his statement valid?
* Shaykh: Marginal notes, you mean?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes. In the earlier period the writing was not vocalized, neither in the text nor in what was written in the margins, so some of the early generations disliked writing anything alongside the Mushaf, because the Qur'an would become mixed with the written material or with other things. But now it does not get mixed. So if this does not affect the letters, meaning you do not write between the lines so that they become mixed, then there is no harm in it.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward (9). And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Blazing Fire (10). O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ [al-Ma'idah 9–11].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. ﴿Believe﴾ means in what must be believed in. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained that faith is "that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, its good and its evil" [[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]].
As for ﴿they did righteous deeds﴾, meaning they performed righteous works, ﴿righteous﴾ is then an adjective of an omitted noun, and the implied phrase is "righteous deeds." So when is a deed righteous? A deed is righteous when it includes two matters. First: sincerity to Allah. Second: following the Sharia of Allah, whether it is from the community of Muhammad or from earlier nations. Two things are necessary:
First: sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because worship is the right of Allah alone, so it is not permitted to associate anyone with Him in it. The many proofs that indicate the obligation of sincerity to Allah in worship include: ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar 2]; ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah 5]; "Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (54) and Muslim (1907/155) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]. The texts on this are numerous.
As for following, the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. Any deed for which there is no command of Allah and His Messenger, whether an act of worship or a transaction, is rejected by its doer. Therefore the deed must have the command of Allah and His Messenger behind it, and following is not realized unless the deed agrees with the Sharia in six matters: first, the cause; second, the kind; third, the type; fourth, the quantity; fifth, the place; sixth, the time. So the deed must conform to the Sharia in these six matters: the cause, the kind, the type, the quantity, the time, and the place.
Whoever worships Allah through an act tied to a cause that Allah and His Messenger did not make a cause, the worship is void and a rejected innovation. An example: a person says every time he puts on a garment, "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad." If he is asked why, he says, "I remember the Prophet putting on a garment, so I send blessings upon him." What do we say to him?
We say: this act of worship is an innovation, because it was not reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him, nor from his Companions, that they used to send blessings upon the Prophet when they wished to dress.
It is also necessary that it agree with the Sharia in the kind of worship. If someone worships Allah with what its kind has not been legislated, the worship is rejected from him. An example: he sacrifices a horse instead of a cow, for instance. We say: this sacrifice is not accepted, because it is not of the kind that Allah and His Messenger legislated, so it is not accepted.
The type, which is more specific than the kind: whoever worships Allah the Exalted with an act whose type has not been legislated, it is not accepted. As if he invented dhikr that is legislated in kind but in another type, it is not accepted, because of the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."
Likewise, what? The quantity. If he worships Allah the Exalted with an act that is increased or decreased, it is not accepted from him. So if he prays Zuhr three rak'ahs, it is not accepted; if he prays it five, it is not accepted, because it opposes the Sharia in the number.
Also in the manner: if it opposes the Sharia in its manner, it is not accepted. As if he prostrated before bowing, it is not accepted because it opposes the Sharia in its manner.
* Student: That makes seven.
* Another student: This is new, Shaykh, this is new.
* Shaykh: Why, brother?
* Student: You did not mention it; you did not mention the manner.
* Shaykh: Yes. In reality it replaces the type. Sometimes we express it as type and sometimes as manner.
* Student: What is the type, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: The type is in reality the manner.
The fifth: the place. If a person performs i'tikaf in his house instead of the mosque, and devotes himself to worship in the house, it is not accepted, because it does not conform to the Sharia in place.
The time: if a person fasts in other than Ramadan in place of Ramadan, it is not accepted, because it is outside the legislated time. Likewise, if he stands at 'Arafah on a day other than the day of 'Arafah, or throws the pebbles outside the season of Hajj, or what is similar.
So the righteous deed is that which conforms to the Sharia in these six matters: the cause, the kind, the quantity, the manner, the time, and the place. The type is replaced by the manner, because it is clearer.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says of those who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾, and this is in return for sins; ﴿and a great reward﴾ is in return for good deeds. So bad deeds are forgiven, and good deeds are rewarded with this great reward.
* From the benefits of this verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds. The proof of this is what is ordained for them of reward, because every deed for which a reward is ordained is virtuous and commanded.
* And from its benefits: faith alone is not sufficient, rather deeds are necessary. For this reason we find many people focusing on creed, saying, "Our creed is sound, praise be to Allah," and not paying attention to deeds. This is a shortcoming. Rather, with creed there must be righteous deeds.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's forgiveness, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾. We have repeated the meaning of forgiveness, that it is the covering of sin and overlooking it.
If someone says: forgiveness here is unrestricted; He did not say "from Allah."
The answer: it is unrestricted, but Allah the Exalted said ﴿and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Al 'Imran 135]. It is known necessarily from the religion of Islam that the one in whose hand is forgiveness and mercy is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants, in that He made the reward in the position of a wage, as if the worker were a hired person who, when he completes the work, is given his wage, although the favour belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, first and last.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of the reward of the believers who do righteous deeds, since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, magnified it. The magnification of the Great for a thing indicates that it is great with a greatness that a person cannot imagine or conceive, and it is so.
Since this Qur'an is *mathani* (oft-repeated), as Allah described it: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating﴾ [al-Zumar 23], when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the reward of the believers who do righteous deeds, He followed it by mentioning their counterparts, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾ [al-Ma'idah 10]. ﴿Disbelieve﴾ is in opposition to righteous deeds, and ﴿deny﴾ is in opposition to faith. They denied what must be affirmed and disbelieved in what must be acted upon. ﴿They disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾. They were not upright regarding the command or the report: they met the report with denial and met the action with disbelief.
﴿And denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. The question here: are the signs meant here the legislated signs or the cosmic signs?
* Students: Both.

Sheikh: Both. Whoever denies the Lordship of Allah, His creation of created beings, and His disposal of the universe is one who denies the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-kawniyyah). Whoever acknowledges that but does not carry out obedience to Allah has disbelieved and denied the legislative signs (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah).

The signs of Allah the Exalted are of two kinds: cosmic and legislative.

As for the cosmic signs, they are this universe with what it contains: the sun, the moon, the stars, night and day, the seas and the rivers, and other great creatures, some of which no one can encompass because of their vastness, and some of which no one can encompass because of their smallness. You will sometimes examine a book and find within its folds tiny insects, extremely small, that can scarcely be seen with the eye. These are creatures of Allah, whom Allah provides for. He knows their resting place and their repository, and their affairs are not hidden from Him, as the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾ [Hud 6].

As for the legislative signs, they are what the messengers brought, and they are signs indicating Allah the Exalted, because human beings cannot produce their like. Who can bring a law suited to mankind in every time and place, in comparison with the Muhammadan Sharia? No one. Likewise, the earlier laws given to the previous nations were perfectly fitted to their conditions, their eras and their places. No one can bring the like of these legislative signs.

The Exalted said: ﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire﴾. ﴿Those﴾ here is the second subject (mubtada' thani), and ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ is the first subject (mubtada' awwal), and ﴿companions﴾ (ashab) is the predicate of the second subject. The second subject and its predicate are in the position of a nominative predicate of the first subject, and the link is the demonstrative.

﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire﴾: that is, the people of the Hellfire who are constantly bound to it. ﴿Al-Jahim﴾ is the Fire, may Allah protect us and you from it, and it was so named for its depth and its blackness.

* In the verse there are benefits:
* Among them: the Noble Qur'an is paired (mathani); when it mentions the people of righteous deeds, it mentions the people of evil deeds. The benefit of this, O students, is that neither the aspect of hope nor the aspect of fear should prevail. This is because if a person has before him only the descriptions of believers and the reward of believers, that may lead him to what? To hope, forgetting fear. And if he has before him only the descriptions of disbelievers and the punishment of disbelievers, he may be overtaken by what? By fear and despair of Allah's mercy. Therefore Allah the Exalted mentions this alongside that, so that despair of Allah's mercy does not overtake a person when mention is made of what instills fear, nor a sense of security from Allah's plan when mention is made of what instills hope.

If someone says: Which is better for the doer: that he give precedence to the aspect of fear, or that he give precedence to the aspect of hope?

The answer: The best of what has been said on this is that at the time of doing a righteous deed, he gives precedence to the aspect of hope, and at the time of intending a sin, he gives precedence to the aspect of fear. This is because when he does a righteous deed and gives precedence to hope, he thinks well of Allah, that Allah will accept his deed and reward him for it, so he is energized to act and seeks his reward from Allah. And at the time of intending disobedience, if he gave precedence to hope, his soul would say to him: Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, this is an easy sin, and if you commit it, repent; the door of repentance is open, and similar things. But if he gives precedence to fear and fears that he will not be granted repentance and that his heart will swerve, then he restrains himself from disobedience. So the best of what is said on this is that a person look to his own state: when he performs acts of obedience, he gives precedence to hope, and when he intends sin, he gives precedence to fear.

If someone says: Did not Allah the Mighty and Majestic say: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful that they will return to their Lord﴾ [al-Mu'minun 60], thus clarifying that among the descriptions of these noble people is that when they give what they give, their hearts are fearful, fearing that it will not be accepted from them, as has been reported in its interpretation?

We say: Yes, that is so. This applies when a person fears that he may be pleased with his deed, in which case he must fear. But if he is free of that, and knows that this righteous deed is by Allah's help, then let him think well of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted has said in a hadith qudsi: "I am as My servant thinks I am."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7405) and Muslim (2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: disbelief may be accompanied by denial, and it may not be. For this reason, sometimes Allah mentions disbelief alone, as in His saying: ﴿And beware the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 131]; and sometimes He mentions denial alone: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ [al-Zumar 32]; and sometimes He combines the two. This is because each of them alone may be sufficient to necessitate eternal abiding in the Fire, and when both are combined, that becomes more severe and greater, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: a person must submit completely to the signs of Allah, affirming their reports and implementing their rulings, because Allah threatened those who deny the signs and disbelieve in them with being what? With being the companions of the Hellfire.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic has mentioned in Surah an-Nisa' an emphatic oath that they do not believe except under conditions, saying: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in full acceptance﴾ [an-Nisa' 65]. This is one condition; ﴿and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged﴾ is the second; ﴿and submit in full acceptance﴾ is the third. So whoever makes other than Allah and His Messenger a judge is not a believer; and whoever makes Allah and His Messenger a judge but finds tightness in his heart, his chest not expanded by what Allah and His Messenger have judged, is not a believer. For this reason He said: ﴿then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged﴾. And whoever finds no discomfort but becomes lax and negligent in submitting, he has not believed. Then the negation of faith from him may be complete, or it may be partial, according to what is established in his heart and his deeds.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the disbelieving deniers are eternal in the Fire, due to His saying: ﴿companions of the Hellfire﴾. Whenever the word ﴿ashab﴾ comes, what is meant by it is constant, perpetual attachment, like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "By He in whose hand is my soul, no one from this Ummah hears of me, be he a Jew or a Christian, and then does not believe in what I have brought—or he said: does not follow what I have brought—except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."[[Narrated by Muslim (153/240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 11].

The discussion of His saying ﴿O you who have believed﴾ has preceded at length, and I presume it is not obscure.

As for His saying ﴿remember the favor of Allah﴾: Allah the Exalted commanded us to remember His favor, not merely for the sake of mentioning it and reporting it, but in order to perform the thanks due for this favor. For simply saying "Allah saved me from the enemy," "Allah enabled me over the enemy," "Allah gave me victory over the enemy," or "Allah humiliated my enemy" is not sufficient; it must be thanks to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If it is thanks, in that a person speaks of Allah's favor as praise of Allah, then this is from thankfulness.

As for His saying ﴿the favor of Allah upon you when﴾: this is connected to His saying ﴿the favor of Allah upon you﴾, so it stands in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

﴿When a people determined to extend their hands against you﴾: Who were the people? The polytheists. They determined to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), and they also determined to fight him in Makkah. But Allah said: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had given you victory over them﴾ [Al-Fath 24], and He said in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you﴾ [An-Nisa' 90]. So there were several incidents in which the disbelievers determined to extend their hands against the Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions, but Allah the Exalted withheld their hands and kept the Messenger and his companions safe.

﴿So He withheld their hands from you﴾ and they were unable to reach you with harm. This is a great favor: that your enemy determines upon something and then Allah restrains him from it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿When there came to you armies, so We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ [Al-Ahzab 9], and He said in it: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting﴾ [Al-Ahzab 25].

﴿And fear Allah﴾: He commanded the remembrance of the favor and taqwa. Taqwa is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by performing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: meaning, let the believers rely upon Allah. We all know that His saying ﴿upon Allah﴾ is connected to (let them rely), and it is placed before it to convey restriction (ḥaṣr). The fa' was added to beautify the expression; otherwise, if it were said "wa-'alā Allāh liyatawakkal," the statement would still be correct.

As for His saying ﴿fa-l-yatawakkal﴾: the lam is the lam of command (lām al-amr), and its original form is with a kasra, but it is made sukūn when preceded by... who knows?

* A student: the fa', the waw, and thumma.

* The Shaykh: The fa', the waw, and thumma. Correct.

In the verse before us, what precedes it? The fa'.

And in His saying ﴿thumma l-yaqḍi' fa-l-yanẓur﴾ [Al-Hajj 15], (thumma).

﴿wa-l-yaṭṭawwafū﴾ [Al-Hajj 29], the waw.

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: so the lam is the lam of command, and the best thing said about tawakkul is that it is the sincere reliance upon Allah in bringing about benefits and repelling harms, with trust in Him, may He be blessed and exalted, and entrusting the matter to Him. This is tawakkul upon Allah: that you rely upon Allah in bringing benefits (and a person is in need of benefits) and in repelling harms, with trust in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and entrusting the matter to Him. From this the difference becomes clear between a person's reliance upon a servant and his reliance upon the Lord. A person's reliance upon the Lord is absolute entrustment, and he believes that Allah, the Exalted, is the One who holds the judgment in it and the authority over it. His reliance upon a person whom he has appointed to buy a need for him is not like that; it is not entrustment to him, but he appointed him, believing that he is below him in rank, isn't that so? That is, when you rely upon a person you have appointed to buy something for you, is it like your reliance upon Allah?

No. My reliance upon Allah is reliance of worship, entrustment and submission, whereas my reliance upon a person whom I appointed is nothing but dependence upon someone whom I manage, whom I wish to act on my behalf, and in whose hand is the cancellation of his agency. So the difference between reliance upon Allah and reliance upon a servant is a great difference. Nevertheless, a person should not say, "I relied upon so-and-so to buy such-and-such," but rather say, "I appointed so-and-so," so that the word which is used only for Allah is not applied to a servant.

As for His saying ﴿the believers﴾: meaning those who believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and so on.

* In this noble verse there are benefits, among them: it is obligatory for a person to remember Allah's favor upon him in bringing benefits and repelling harms. From where is this taken? From Allah's command to remember His favors by withholding the hands of enemies from us.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that withholding harm and injury is among the favors, and so it is. Many people think that favors are only bringing things into existence, but this is deficiency; a favor is either bringing into existence what did not exist or withholding what exists, and for this Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is thanked for both.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of fearing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when mentioning favors, so that a person does not transgress, become arrogant, or exalt himself; because of His saying ﴿and fear Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: the obligation of relying upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because of His saying ﴿and upon Allah let them rely﴾.

* Among its benefits: sincerity of tawakkul to Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and this is from placing forward what is what? From placing forward the object (al-ma'mūl), and the rule among the rhetoricians is that placing forward what should be delayed conveys restriction.

If someone says: Does tawakkul prevent taking the means?

The answer is: No. Rather, tawakkul is not complete except with taking the means. Let me give you an example from the master of those who rely upon Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ). Despite that, he guarded against heat and cold, wore armor in battle, and at Uhud he wore two coats of mail (ﷺ). All of that was guarding against arrows. So performing the real, beneficial means does not contradict tawakkul; rather, it is part of its completion. Therefore, if someone said, "I will not strive to seek provision; the One who provides for the snakes in their holes will provide for me, I am relying upon Allah," we would say: this is incapacity and laziness. Tawakkul upon Allah is entrustment when the means are not available. Yes, when a person is unable to use the means, all that remains for him is entrustment; and so you find that the disbelievers, when waves overshadowing like shades overwhelm them, call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion, entrusting the matter to Allah. Likewise, when something befalls a person which he cannot repel, you find that he has no power or strength. But when he is able to take the means, he must take them.

If a person said, "I want to travel to Makkah for Hajj," we would say, "Take provision with you." If he said, "I do not need it, I am relying upon Allah," what do we say about this?

This is incapacity, negligence and laziness. If you are truly relying upon Allah, then take the means: take with you what suffices you for expenses, or hire yourself to some people with whom you will travel and who will cover your needs, or something similar.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that tawakkul is part of faith, because of His saying ﴿so let the believers rely﴾; the command is directed to the believers because they are the people of tawakkul.

* Among its benefits: that abandoning tawakkul upon Allah is a deficiency in faith. But does it contradict the completeness of faith or the root of faith?

There is detail here. Whoever relies upon a dead prophet—and all the prophets are dead except Jesus, who is in the heavens alive—this contradicts the root of faith. Whoever relies upon a grave, this contradicts the root of faith. Whoever depends upon a known means, whether a legislated means or a natural/decreed means, this does not contradict faith; but do not make this means your ultimate reliance. Rather, make it a means, and the one who causes effects is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason we often find that means fail to produce their effects, because the matter is in whose hand? In the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 12 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah 12]. The sentence here is emphasized by three emphatics, as the brother will count for us: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant﴾. The sentence is emphasized by three emphatics.
* Student: The lam.
* The Shaykh: The lam in ﴿la-qad﴾; the second is (qad); the third is the oath.
This is a rule: whenever an expression of this form occurs, it is emphasized by three emphatics. ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin 4]: this is emphasized by three emphatics. ﴿We have certainly created man in toil﴾ [al-Balad 4]: it is emphasized. ﴿And We certainly created you and then formed you﴾ [al-A'raf 11]: emphasized by three emphatics.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We said that innovation (bid'ah) is opposing the Shari'ah in one of the six matters we mentioned. Shaykh, may Allah bless you, for example what takes place on certain days celebrated in some countries: such-and-such a day, and such-and-such a day, and such-and-such a day, which are not drawn near to Allah by. Some scholars say these are innovations that were introduced, while others say these are not innovations; we do not draw near to Allah by them, they are only occasions, enlivenment and commemoration. What is the basis for calling them an innovation?
* The Shaykh: Some scholars say they are not an innovation; for example, the Day of the Tree, such-and-such a day, and such-and-such a day. They say the purpose of these is to remind people. But if the occasion is the occasion of installing an amir in leadership, or a president in presidency, or a king in kingship, then these are done for glorification, and it is not permitted; because festivals can only be established on legitimate occasions. It is not permitted for them to be anything but legitimate occasions; what is not a legitimate occasion is not prescribed. But as for what is mentioned about the days of the Tree and the like, they say: we do not take them as festivals; therefore we do not single them out with a specific day. Rather they are a reminder, an enlivenment, and like a beginning of work. But in my view, if people abstained from them, that would be better.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. ﴿And certainly﴾, we said there are three emphatics. What are they?
* The Shaykh: Yes: the lam, (qad), and the oath; because the implied wording of the sentence is: "By Allah, indeed."
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Is it permissible to apply the word (ayah) to a passage of the Torah or the Gospel, or is it said that the ayah is specific to the Qur'an, since we know of no challenge except for the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: The challenge is not a necessary condition.
* Student: It is not necessary?
* The Shaykh: It is not necessary. If this Shari'ah is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then it is an ayah; because, as we said, the Shari'ah of this kind is something humans cannot produce its like.
* Student: If some object to one who says that this ayah is from the Torah or the Gospel, is he correct in his objection?
* The Shaykh: I do not see this unless he objects out of fear of confusion, because the common person, when he hears it, thinks this is the Torah and the Gospel is Qur'an.
* Student: Regarding the reason that these days are not festivals?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: That these days are not festivals; they are for rousing resolve. But is it not objected to them that they resemble (others)? Such-and-such a week, and such-and-such a day, and such-and-such a day (...) their reason is the reason of resemblance, so does this have (...) consideration?
* The Shaykh: The reason of resemblance is confused for many people, although the imams have stated that if the source of a thing is from non-Muslims and then it spreads and Muslims come to practice it, the resemblance is removed; because the reality of resemblance is that a person does what is specific to others. And since this matter has become widespread, then no. For example, the wearing of trousers: where did it come from?
* Students: From the West.
* The Shaykh: It came from the disbelievers, but Muslims followed them, and now both the Muslim and the disbeliever wear it.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. A person seeking out times when people gather, for example for a party or a wedding, so he seeks out that location and goes to address them with good and admonishes them with good. Likewise, if he sees them gathered at a condolence in a house or elsewhere, does this, that is, does this enter or not enter into our statement: restricting it to a place or time?
* The Shaykh: As for admonition: when a cause for it exists, it is done in any place. But if this is made a regular practice, as though it were the cause, we say this is wrong. For example, gathering at a wedding or at a large banquet: if the person sees from the occasion that he should speak, because he sees people eager for his words, and people differ in this respect; among people are men whom people long to hear and wish that they would speak, here we say: speak, it is good; or if he was asked to speak, here too we say: speak, because you were asked about knowledge, so when asked about knowledge, explain. But a person who is not of importance to people, and whom people are not awaiting his words, who imposes himself upon them and then speaks at such occasions, this is a burden upon people. Many people come to these parties, and some gather with one another over a long time, asking about their conditions and their relatives; this cuts off from them what they want. Or they speak and become notorious among people. This is one point.
Likewise condolence is even more severe: that a person comes and gives a sermon to those present is an innovation upon an innovation, because the basic gathering for condolence is not legislated, as the scholars have stated; some of them disliked it and declared it disliked, and some said it is an innovation, and the books of the jurists are before you.
Likewise also what some people have introduced at burial: one of them stands up as a preacher, sermonizes and admonishes the people. This too is among the innovations, because the Messenger did not do it. The most that is reported from the Messenger (ﷺ) is that "he came to the grave with his companions while it had not yet been lined (with stone)" – meaning the grave had not yet been finished with its niche – "so they sat, and the Prophet (ﷺ) sat with them and began to scratch the ground with a stick he had, scratching the earth, and he spoke to them about the condition of a person at death and after burial"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4753) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]]. This was not a khutbah; it was an admonition, not a regular practice. The Messenger did not do it whenever he buried someone. He did it because he was waiting for the lining, so instead of remaining silent or speaking about something unsuitable, he (ﷺ) spoke.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised from them twelve chiefs. And Allah said, "Indeed I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the sound way."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 12].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾. The sentence here is emphasized, with how many?
* Student: Two emphatics.
* The Shaykh: What are they? Identify them.
* Student: The lam and (qad).
* The Shaykh: The lam and (qad), yes. And we mentioned to you before that when this expression comes, the emphasis is with three emphatics: the lam, (qad), and the implied oath, and the implied wording is: "By Allah, indeed." Do you understand?
﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., their pledge. The context here is the context of the third person: ﴿Allah took﴾.
He said: ﴿And We raised from them﴾. This is a shift (iltifat) from the third person to the first person plural; had the speech been in one pattern, it would have said: "and He raised."
﴿We raised from them twelve chiefs﴾, i.e., We made from them twelve supervisors (raqib). ﴿Twelve﴾: we do not parse this as "ithnay" alone or "ashara" alone if it were with other words, meaning like: thalath 'ashrah, arba' 'ashrah, thalathat 'ashar, arba'at 'ashar; we do not parse these as the first part alone and the second part alone, except for ithna 'ashara and ithnata 'ashrah. The first part is inflected according to the governing factors: in the nominative we make it with the alif, and in the accusative and genitive with the ya', because it is attached to the dual, and we said it is attached to the dual and did not make it a true dual because it has no singular; for (ithnan) does not have the singular (ithn), but its singular is wahid. So for this reason they parse it as attached to the dual, and its inflection is with the alif in the nominative and with the ya' in the accusative and genitive. But it is not added to "ashar"; rather it is said that (ithna) is compounded with (ashar), and (ashar) is built on the fatha, having no place in the inflection.
﴿Twelve chiefs﴾: ﴿naqiban﴾ is a specification (tamyiz). Whenever a word that explains the number, which is the counted item, comes, parse it as a tamyiz; for example: thalatha 'ashar rajulan, we say "rajulan" is a tamyiz; ﴿twelve chiefs﴾, we say ﴿naqiban﴾ is a tamyiz. And for this the author of the Alfiyyah says:
A noun in meaning "min" that is indefinite and clarifying, is put in the accusative as a tamyiz by what explained it.
﴿Naqib﴾ is fa'il in the sense of fa'il: "naqqib" in the sense of "munaqqib", i.e., one who inspects, searches; and they are the 'urafa' (overseers), because the 'arif inspects those over whom he has been made 'arif. The root meaning of tanqib is inspection, and from it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And how many generations before them did We destroy, which were stronger than them in strength, and they went through the lands﴾ [Qaf 36], i.e., they searched in them. So (naqib) is fa'il in the sense of fa'il, i.e., munaqqib; and tanqib is inspection, and its meaning is the overseers. Allah made from them twelve naqibs, overseers over their people; every tribe had an 'arif, because they were twelve tribes.
﴿And We raised from them twelve naqibs﴾, and this is from Allah's care for them, the Mighty and Majestic, that He placed over them overseers so that they might direct and discipline them.
﴿And Allah said, "Indeed I am with you"﴾: ﴿Allah said, "Indeed I am with you"﴾, i.e., in support and assistance; and this companionship is special, and we will speak about it, Allah willing, when we take up the benefits.
Then He said: ﴿If you establish﴾: this is the beginning of the covenant. ﴿If you establish the prayer﴾, i.e., you perform it upright. The prayer is well known; it is worship of Allah the Exalted through the specific sayings and actions known, opened with the takbir and concluded with the salam; this is the basis. On this basis, the prayers of the Christians and Jews now are altered prayers; just as they altered in interpretation, they also altered in actions.
﴿And give zakah﴾: ﴿ataytum﴾ means gave, and ﴿zakah﴾ is an obligatory amount of wealth in specific types of property.
As for His saying: ﴿give zakah﴾, to whom? To those entitled to it. Therefore we say that (ata) takes two objects: the first is zakah, and the second is omitted, i.e., you gave zakah to its people. And zakah is the wealth we mentioned to you; it is called zakah because it purifies the character of the one who gives it, i.e., it develops it; for giving wealth certainly develops character. And if you want your chest to be expanded, give much in charity, but without extravagance.
﴿And believe in My messengers﴾: i.e., you affirmed with an affirmation that entails acceptance and submission; this is the meaning of faith: affirmation that entails what? Acceptance and submission. Mere affirmation is not considered faith; if mere affirmation were faith, Abu Talib would have been a believer, because he affirmed the prophethood of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.
﴿And believe in My messengers﴾: ("rusul") is the plural of rasul, and they are those whom Allah the Exalted sent to the Children of Israel; most of the prophets mentioned to us were from the Children of Israel.
﴿And support them﴾: i.e., you helped them, because ta'zir means support, and its origin is strengthening. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him﴾ [al-Fath 9]: support whom? The Messenger ﷺ.
He said: ﴿And loan Allah a goodly loan﴾: His saying ﴿and loan Allah﴾ means you spent wealth seeking reward from Him; for the lender gives a loan on the basis that its equivalent will be returned to him; so lending to Allah means seeking reward from Him, as though you gave the thing seeking His pleasure so that by it you might attain His reward.
If someone says: ﴿aqraðtum﴾ with His saying ﴿ataytum al-zakah﴾, is it of the type of conjoining two different things, or is it of the type of conjoining the general to the specific, or what?
Some scholars hold that it is of the type of conjoining the general to the specific, because zakah is in reality a loan to Allah; if a person pays it seeking its reward, it is a loan to Allah, and the mention of lending, which is more general than zakah, comes after the mention of zakah in order to include zakah and other things.
It was said: what is meant by lending here is charity, i.e., what exceeds zakah, and on this basis the conjunction is of the type of conjoining different things.
His saying: ﴿a goodly loan﴾: the goodly loan is that which is sincerely for Him in accordance with the law of Allah; this is the goodly loan. The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that excellence in worship of the Creator is the perfection of faith and vigilance, when he said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].
His saying: ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds﴾: this is the answer, but the answer to what? It is the answer to His saying: ﴿If you establish﴾, and it is the answer to the conditional particle (in), or the answer to the implied oath indicated by the lam in His saying: ﴿If you establish﴾?
* Student: Which of them is more correct?
* The Shaykh: The second, so it is the answer to the oath; and for this reason it is not joined with fa'. Had it been the answer to the condition, it would have been joined with fa'. And in this Ibn Malik says:
Omit, when a condition and an oath gather, the answer of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory.
So what was placed later here? The oath or the condition?
* Student: The condition.
* The Shaykh: The condition. So what was omitted is the answer to the condition.
﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds﴾: I make them expiated by the good deeds you did: establishing prayer, giving zakah, believing in the messengers and supporting them, lending Allah a goodly loan; so misdeeds are expiated by these good deeds.
﴿And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: this is conjoined with ﴿I will surely remove﴾, and when you combine it with (ukaffir), there comes with it deliverance from what is feared and attainment of what is sought. Deliverance from what is feared is in His saying: ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds﴾, because when they are expiated, one is not punished for them; attainment of what is sought: ﴿And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾.
By tracing and induction we find that most often the deliverance from what is feared is presented before the sought-after, so that the sought-after arrives upon a place free of what is feared; so clearing comes before adorning. That is, clear the thing before you adorn it; sweep the place before you spread it. Is that clear?
Now reflect on the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and in other things as well, and you will find that negation is generally placed before affirmation; (There is no god but Allah), the word of sincerity, has negation placed before affirmation so that affirmation arrives upon a place free of impurities.
﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: ﴿gardens﴾ means the Garden of Refuge, and it is, as you see, sometimes mentioned in the singular and sometimes in the plural. ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is﴾ [al-Hadid 21]: ﴿a garden﴾, what is it?
* Students: ﴿Whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth.﴾
* The Shaykh: No, no. Is it singular or plural?
* Students: Singular.

**The Shaykh:** It is singular, and ﴿Jannat﴾ (gardens) often appears in the plural. Its singular form is used with regard to the genus, and its plural form with regard to the types, because Paradise has several types. In the end of Surah al-Rahman, Allah the Exalted mentions four types. He says: ﴿But for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman 46], then He says: ﴿And besides them are two other gardens﴾ [al-Rahman 62]. Which of them is more honourable, the first two or the latter two?

**The students:** The first two.

**The Shaykh:** The first two?

**The students:** Yes.

**A student:** ﴿besides Him, gods﴾.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, meaning: other than Him. ﴿Do not worship besides Allah﴾, meaning: other than Him.

**The students:** The descriptions, meaning... (...).

**The Shaykh:** Good. Who will volunteer to explain the differences for us? Ibn al-Qayyim, in his *al-Nuniyya* (a poem), mentioned that the differences are ten, but he said: "The verse-form tires me, so I cannot present it." So who can volunteer to mention the differences?

So, the garden (jannah) is pluralized as gardens (jannat) with regard to what? With regard to the types. And it is singularized with regard to the genus. ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Now, if we were to interpret ﴿gardens﴾ by what we interpret gardens of this world by, and say: gardens are orchards with many trees and abundant fruit, the mind would not travel far, and the bliss of the Hereafter would seem small. But if we say: the Garden is the abode which Allah the Exalted has prepared for His friends, may Allah make us among them, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined, which of these two is more stirring to the emotions?

**The students:** The second.

**The Shaykh:** The second, without doubt. For this reason we may find fault with some people who interpret the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa) as an orchard with many trees, and who say it is named so because its trees are intertwined with one another, so they shelter those within them. We say: this undoubtedly diminishes the imagining of the Garden and its greatness. Rather, we say: the Garden is the abode which Allah the Exalted has prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined. This stirs the emotions and makes a person hasten and compete towards it.

As for His words ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, it is known that it does not mean beneath its earth, for if a river flowed beneath the ground, what benefit would there be in it?! For this reason we do not benefit from underground rivers. Rather, ﴿beneath them﴾, the scholars said: beneath its palaces and trees. How beautiful is the flow of rivers beneath shady trees and grand, majestic palaces; it has a scene that a person cannot imagine in reality.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾. These rivers are not like the rivers of this world. Their types are four: ﴿rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 15], meaning it can never change, whereas the rivers of this world do change. The second: ﴿rivers of milk whose taste never changes﴾ [Muhammad 15], rather it is of the finest flavour. ﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾. Allah has negated in it ghawl (harmful intoxication): ﴿No headache is in it, nor are they affected by it﴾ [al-Saffat 47]. ﴿And rivers of honey, purified﴾ [Muhammad 15], pure, with nothing in it of what is in the honey of this world. These are four rivers that flow with a true flow. (Water): a person may imagine how it flows. (Milk, whose taste never changes): one may imagine how it flows, because milk flows. (Wine): can it be imagined or not? It can be imagined, and it may not be, because wine is not all alike. The fourth: (honey). In our imagination now, it does not flow; its flow is impossible. But in the Garden it flows, a river.

Then Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in the *Nuniyya* that these rivers flow without a ditch, and he said:

*Its rivers flow without any trench,*
*Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing!*

Allahu akbar! A river flows without a trench to restrain it from right or left, and without any channel, on a surface, a flat place. Yet even so, it flows only where its Owner wills; He directs it however He wishes. There are no workers and no operators, only wills: ﴿Therein is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you therein will abide eternally﴾ [al-Zukhruf 71].

We say: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. So here is a covenant between two contracting parties: a small deed in exchange for a great reward.

He says: ﴿Whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾. The ﴿man﴾ (whoever) here is conditional, and its answer is ﴿then he has certainly strayed﴾, meaning: whoever disbelieves after this covenant and does not fulfil what he pledged to Allah, then he has strayed from the even way. ﴿Dalal﴾ (straying) means loss and bewilderment; that is, he has gone astray from the straight path. And ﴿sawa' al-sabil﴾ (the even way) means its straight course that leads to the goal.

In this verse there are many benefits. Among them: reminding this nation and reminding the Children of Israel of the covenant Allah took from them. As for reminding the Children of Israel, the matter is clear: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah 70]. As for reminding us, the Islamic nation, it is because there is no covenant between human beings and the Creator that includes favouritism, except by the grace of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. If we fulfil what is obligatory upon us, we have a double reward, according to what has come in the texts from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah mentioning Himself in the third person, as a glorification and magnification of Him, may He be exalted. Is this derived? What did you say?

**A student:** (...).

**Another student:** That Allah mentioned Himself in the third person as a glorification.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, and as a magnification. ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant﴾; He did not say "we took". This is like a king saying to his soldiers: "The king commands you to do such-and-such." He does not say: "I command you." He says: "The king commands you." A parallel to this is: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾ [al-Nisa' 58].

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a method of eloquence is to shift from one style to another in order to alert the addressee. It is derived from His words ﴿And We raised up﴾ after His words ﴿And Allah had already taken﴾. And there is no doubt that a change of style necessitates attentiveness.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah the Exalted created the deeds of the servants, because of His words ﴿And We raised up from them twelve chiefs﴾, for the chiefs (naqib) are inspectors. If Allah is the One who raised them up, then their actions must be created by Allah.

From the verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree) in His words ﴿And We raised up from them﴾. So they acted by whose command? By the command of Allah. The Qadariyyah say: the actions of the servant are not created by Allah, nor does Allah have any connection with them.

Also derived from it is a refutation of the Jabriyyah (those who hold that man is compelled) in His words ﴿chiefs﴾, because the naqib is one who investigates, and Allah attributed the action to them. This shows that a person is not compelled. This has been established, praise be to Allah, many times: the texts of the Book and the Sunnah indicate the falsity of the saying of the Qadariyyah and the falsity of the saying of the Jabriyyah.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is fitting for people to take chiefs to whom they refer in their affairs. In disputes they are reconcilers, and in matters that are unclear they are clarifiers, and similar things. For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that when they are three on a journey, they should appoint one of them as leader, so that he may direct them and manage their affairs and they will not be in disorder.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2609) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's favour upon the Children of Israel in that He is their helper. This is derived from His words ﴿And Allah said: Indeed I am with you﴾.

Know that Allah the Exalted described Himself as being with (ma'iyyah) in several verses. Sometimes He mentioned it in general, sometimes He mentioned it specifically with a description, and sometimes He mentioned it specifically with a person. All of these are true.

The general form implies encompassing the creation in knowledge, power, authority, management, sovereignty and other things. From this is His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid 4], and His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadilah 7].

From its mention, meaning the being-with, restricted by a description, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl 128]. But this, together with the general encompassing, implies support, assistance and defence: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed﴾ [al-Hajj 38].

Third: restricted to a person, such as His saying to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46], and such as the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), as Allah related it, to his companion Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah 40].

Is this being-with real, or is it a metaphor for knowledge, encompassing, support, assistance and similar things?

The answer: the first. It is like the other attributes: it is real, and in every context it implies what is appropriate to it. But if we say it is real, does that contradict what has been mentioned about Allah's elevation (uluww)? No, never. He is with us and He is above His Throne. And "with us" does not mean He is in the earth, certainly not: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 67]. And one whose matter is like this, how could any intelligent person, let alone a believer, imagine that He is with us in our places? Rather He is with us and He is exalted. There is no obstacle, because Allah encompasses all things. Even when the Companions raised their voices with takbir, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent," and "Indeed the One you call upon is closer to one of you than the neck of his mount."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (6384) and Muslim (2704/44) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] [[Narrated by Muslim (2704/46) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] We believe in this. But that does not mean He, glory be to Him, is in the same place, because if you said that, you would be among those who acted upon the texts while looking at them with the vision of one-eyed people, that is, from one side only. For this reason, when the Jahmiyyah looked at this from one side only, they said: Allah is with us in the same place, in every place. But they neglected elevation. We say: Allah the Exalted is with us in reality, and on His Throne in reality, and there is no contradiction.

If someone says: Can the mind conceive that a thing may be described as being with you while it is far from you?

We say: Yes. First: it can be conceived in created matters. Travellers say the moon is with us, and the star is with us, and the sun is with us, and where are these places?

**The students:** In the sky.

**The Shaykh:** In the sky. The Arabs say: the moon is with us, the Pole Star is with us, the Little Dipper is with us. They speak this way and express it as real, while its location is in the sky, and this is not considered a contradiction. Then, supposing it were a contradiction in created things, and that being-with in reality and elevation in reality cannot be combined, can the Creator be measured by the created?

**The students:** No.

**The Shaykh:** It cannot be measured. It is said: we affirm for Allah what He affirmed for Himself of His elevation and His being-with, and we know there is no contradiction. Rather He is exalted and with us, and there is no incompatibility.

So the answer to this is: first, there is no contradiction between them, for the following reasons:

(a) Allah combined the two for Himself, and what Allah combined in His Book contains no contradiction. Otherwise His saying would not be true: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa' 82]. This is one: every two things that Allah has combined, know that there is no contradiction between them.

Second: there is no contradiction and no incompatibility between being-with in reality and elevation in reality, never, because we perceive the observed reality agreed upon by the scholars of language: a thing is said to be with us, while it is in its place in the sky, far from us.

Third: supposing this is impossible in the created, it is not impossible for the Creator, because Allah, glory be to Him, "there is nothing like Him" in all His attributes. He is exalted in His nearness and near in His exaltedness. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, indicated this in the blessed creed, namely al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah. By this we are also saved from the objection of the people of ta'wil (reinterpretation of texts away from their apparent meaning) against Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah), when they say: "You reject ta'wil from us while you yourselves interpret." For when you read: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and earth in six days, then He established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Hadid 4], all these pronouns refer to whom?

**The students:** Allah.

**The Shaykh:** To Allah. What removes being-with from this? What removes it?

**A student:** Nothing.

**The Shaykh:** If ﴿created the heavens﴾ means Allah, ﴿established Himself above the Throne﴾ means Allah, ﴿knows what enters﴾ means Allah, and ﴿He is with you﴾ means Allah, then, as Shaykh al-Islam said, this understanding must be safeguarded from false assumptions, such as that a person believes He is with us, meaning in our place, or that He is above the sky, meaning that the sky carries Him, or that when He descends to the lowest heaven the other heavens shade Him. This must be guarded against, because Allah the Exalted is above, and His elevation is inseparable from His essence. It is among the attributes of what? The essential attributes, which are never separated from Him, just as His hearing and seeing are never separated from Him. Pay attention to this. However, it has been reported from the Salaf (the early generations), may Allah have mercy on them, that many of them explained being-with as knowledge. This is an explanation by necessary implication, because whoever is with you necessarily knows you. There is no doubt this is a correct explanation, not objectionable, and explanation by necessary implication is a correct explanation, but it is not the exact meaning. This is because implications are of three kinds: implication by inclusion (tadammun), implication by correspondence (mutabaqah), and implication by necessary consequence (iltizam). This is an implication of necessary consequence. They were compelled to this in order to refute those Jahmiyyah who used to say that Allah is with us in the same place. For this reason 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "We say Allah is with us by His knowledge, and we do not say as these Jahmiyyah say: He is with us here," meaning on the earth.

Thus it becomes clear why most of the Salaf's expressions say that being-with means knowledge. We say: this explanation is correct and not objectionable, because it is an explanation by what? By necessary implication. The Salaf used explanation by necessary implication in many verses, and this is not considered going outside what the verse requires. But the interpretation that is rejected for a person is to interpret in a way that contradicts the wording, by the three types of implication: correspondence, inclusion, and necessary consequence.

The specific being-with by description is frequent in the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl 128]. When a person believes in this verse, it will make him confident in himself, but not because he is strong and capable, rather because Allah is with him. So if a person truly fears his Lord with true fear, he will obtain victory and support, and ﴿indeed Allah defends those who have believed﴾. But what truly lacks in us is taqwa (God-consciousness), and for this reason we find ourselves failing in every battle we have fought against the brothers of apes and pigs, namely the Jews.

By the three types of implication: correspondence, inclusion and necessary consequence.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 12 (part 3 of 3):

The special companionship (al-ma'iyyah al-khassah) tied to a quality occurs often in the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [An-Nahl 16:128]. When a person believes in this verse, it will make him confident in himself, but his confidence will not be because he is strong and capable, rather because Allah is with him. If a person fears his Lord with true godwariness, he will receive victory and support, and indeed Allah defends those who believe. What is truly lacking in us, however, is godwariness (taqwa). That is why we find ourselves failing in every battle we have fought with the brethren of apes and swine, namely the Jews.

We also find that the brothers who had, as it appears to us, and Allah knows best, godwariness and strength, overcame those who were previously the greatest state. Who were they?

* A student: The Persians.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the Persians previously, that is correct. But those who defeated them had a godwariness that we do not have now. They say: in Chechnya, the Russians were more humiliated than dogs among them. When their officers, commanders and armies ordered them to gather, they would descend from the mountain peaks and assemble. One of them says, swearing by Allah, that there were seven hundred armoured vehicles for war, seven hundred led, of course, by the Russians. He says: the Chechens said, "It is impossible for you to advance around us except with the flag on which is written (There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah) at the front." They began to lead it with "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." This one says: they were as humiliated as can be. And those of them who were killed, they say: seventy thousand Russians. We had not thought this.

So I say to you: when a person trusts himself because of what he has of the fear of Allah and excellence in the worship of Allah, let him be given good news that Allah the Exalted is with him and that Allah the Exalted supports him.

Furthermore, it should be known that victory does not necessarily mean that a person is given victory in his lifetime. Rather, if what he calls to is given victory after his death, that is a victory for him, without doubt. For this reason we believe that the victory of the Companions, in their conquest of the easts and wests of the earth, is a victory for whom? For the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. That is, even if it is supposed that one who calls to Allah, sincere to Allah and following the law of Allah, dies or is killed, but the call remains and it is victorious after him, then in reality that is a victory for him. Thus the saying of the Exalted is fulfilled: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who are doers of good﴾.

As for the companionship specifically attached to a particular person, it is greater and greater still. The saying of the Messenger: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with us﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:40] is more eloquent than ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who are doers of good﴾, because it is a specification, a specification of the individual. Likewise, Musa and Harun: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:46].

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except for a few of them. So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾ (13). ﴿And from those who said, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:13-14].

* The Shaykh: We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. After mentioning the admonition of these people concerning the covenant that was taken from them, Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if these people had fulfilled the covenant of Allah, Allah would have fulfilled His covenant to them, as He said: ﴿And fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:40]. This is derived from His saying: ﴿If you establish prayer and give zakah﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:12], and so on to the end.

* Among its benefits: prayer and zakah were prescribed for the earlier nations. This is so; the prayers and the zakahs were prescribed. But it does not follow from their being prescribed that they must be identical to what has been obligated upon us in manner, time and amount. The important thing is that the category of prayer is prescribed, and the category of zakah is prescribed, though they may differ. This is like His saying: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become mindful of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:183]. The comparison here is with the obligation: the obligation was likened to the obligation. It does not follow that their fasting must be like our fasting. And we remain with the Hajj. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that the Hajj was legislated for the earlier nations. So these great pillars, the pillars of Islam, are legislated for every nation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon the Children of Israel to believe in all the messengers, and at their head Muhammad ﷺ, because Allah the Exalted did not guarantee them this reward except if they believed in His messengers, by His saying: ﴿And you believe in My messengers﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:12].

It is well known that whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 26:105], although no messenger had come before Nuh. But when they denied Nuh, their denial of him became a denial of all the messengers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the obligation to support the messengers, by His saying: ﴿And you support them﴾. Supporting them during their lifetime means being with them in jihad, in defence and in other things. Supporting them after their death means supporting their laws and establishing them among people. So it is obligatory upon us now to support the law of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the grace of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon His servants, in that He gives them provision and then says: ﴿You have lent Allah﴾, while He is the Giver first and the Rewarder second, by His saying: ﴿And you have lent﴾. We have already mentioned the wisdom in expressing spending in the way of Allah as a loan. What is it?

* A student: Borrowing, in the sense that the borrower is bound...

* The Shaykh: As if Allah made spending in His way like a loan which obliges the borrower to repay it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the deeds by which a person draws near to Allah must be good. From where is this taken? ﴿And you lend Allah a good loan﴾, to exclude deficiency in what is obligatory and extravagance in giving, because extravagance is not good and deficiency is not good.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: good deeds expiate evil deeds, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds﴾. What supports this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ [Hud 11:114], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Follow the evil deed with a good deed, and it will wipe it out"[1].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: deliverance from what is feared is mentioned before the attainment of what is sought, by His saying: ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and I will surely admit you﴾. This is evidence for what is well known among the scholars: that takhliyah (clearing) precedes tahliyah (adornment), that is, removing impurities and obstacles before the desired goal is attained.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Paradise is not one. This is by His saying: ﴿Gardens﴾. This is if we say that this plural refers to the gardens, not to those who enter them, because there is a possibility that it refers to those who enter them, and that each one has a garden, even though Paradise is one, but it is multiplied by reference to its inhabitants. We say: this is possible, but the Qur'an indicates that they are plural gardens, the gardens themselves. In Surah Ar-Rahman: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman 55:46], and He said about the second: ﴿And below them are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman 55:62].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the bliss of Paradise is bliss for the soul, the heart, the hearing, the sight, and everything. This is because He mentioned that these gardens have rivers flowing beneath them, and there is no doubt that this delights the hearing. The rustling of flowing water delights the ear. That is why you find a person standing at waterfalls enjoying listening to them. Likewise the sight, and likewise the heart and soul find rest.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: in Paradise there are rivers, not a single river. From where is this taken? ﴿The rivers﴾ is the plural of (nahr, river). Allah the Mighty and Majestic has mentioned their types in Surah Al-Qital, Surah Muhammad. The brother will recite it to us: the rivers, the types of rivers that are in Surah Al-Qital, which is Surah Muhammad: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised﴾.

* A student: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 47:15].

* The Shaykh: Yes, well done, four types.

If someone says: how do we reconcile His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river (nahr)﴾ [Al-Qamar 54:54-55], where He mentions a single river, and here He mentions rivers? How do we reconcile?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The indefinite noun (nakirah) is not general except in the context of a condition, negation, prohibition, and the like.

* A student: The genus, the genus of the action.

* The Shaykh: Which of them?

* A student: The verses contain mention of details.

* The Shaykh: The singular is for the genus, so it does not contradict multiplicity. Correct. We say: the intended meaning is the genus, so it does not contradict multiplicity.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against whoever disbelieves after the covenant, and the declaration of his clear misguidance, by His saying: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:12].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the believer walks upon the sound way (sawa' as-sabil), that is, its middle, without its two edges. The reasoning: if misguidance of the way is established in the ruling for the disbeliever, then its opposite is established by its ruling, and the opposite of his ruling is established for him, because when deeds are opposed, their recompenses are opposed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an alert that the general rule is that the middle of the path and way is the truth, because sawa' means middle, by His saying: ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat 37:55], that is, in its middle or in its place of settlement. This is the general rule: whatever deviates to the right or to the left is misguidance. That is why it has come in a hadith: "The religion of Allah lies between the one who exaggerates in it and the one who neglects it"[2].

---

[1] Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (1987) from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and Mu'adh ibn Jabal.

[2] Narrated by ad-Darimi (222) as a statement of al-Hasan, a mawquf report, with a similar meaning; its wording is: "Your sunnah, by Allah, the One besides whom there is no god, lies between them: between the exaggerator and the neglecter..."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant We cursed them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 13]. ﴿So for their breaking﴾: the fa' (فاء) is conjunctive (عاطفة), and conjunction with fa' indicates sequence (الترتيب). When it conjoins a verb to a verb, it indicates causation (السببية) together with sequence. If you say, "Zayd came, then 'Amr," this is pure sequence, because the conjunction here joins a single noun to a single noun. When a clause is joined to a clause, it may indicate sequence together with causation, and this is the more common usage, as when you say, "So-and-so disbelieved, and so he is in the Fire; so-and-so believed, and so he is in Paradise," meaning: because of it. Sometimes it indicates mere sequence, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And how many a town We destroyed, and Our punishment came upon it [by night or while they were napping]﴾ [al-A'raf 4].

Here, ﴿We destroyed﴾ comes after the arrival of the punishment. Here, ﴿So for their breaking﴾: I said that this fa' is conjunctive, indicating sequence and causation, even though the bi' (باء) that follows it also indicates causation.

﴿So for their breaking﴾: the bi' (باء) indicates causation and is a particle of preposition (حرف جر), and the ma (ما) is a verbal-source particle (مصدرية), the sign of which is that it converts what follows it into a verbal noun (مصدر). Here, ﴿So for their breaking their covenant We cursed them﴾: I said that it is a verbal-source particle, but the correct view is that it is superfluous (زائدة), because what follows it is a verb. ﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾ means: "So by their breaking their covenant," and so the ma here is superfluous for emphasis.

The ma (ما) comes as superfluous, as verbal-source, as relative (موصولة), and as conditional (شرطية). Some scholars gathered its meanings in one verse:
"Its carryings are ten; if you wish to count them, then preserve a sound verse from poetry.
You will understand the condition of connection; marvel at its denial, with a palm and negation, the superfluous one, the magnifying verbal-source..."

Among the meanings we have mentioned, it is superfluous, as in this verse (with a palm and negation, the superfluous one is added). If someone asks: what is the benefit of the superfluous one? We say: the benefit is emphasis, and likewise all superfluous particles, whether governing or non-governing, have emphasis as their benefit.

﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾: al-naqd (النقض) is the opposite of the 'aqd (العقد), i.e., their undoing of the covenant (الميثاق). And His words ﴿their covenant﴾ mean the covenant by which Allah made them pledge, which is His words: ﴿If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan﴾. So these people broke the covenant because of it.

﴿We cursed them﴾: al-la'n (اللعن) is expulsion and distancing from the mercy of Allah, so they were, may Allah protect us, expelled and distanced from the mercy of Allah, and Allah does not reach them with mercy. ﴿We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾. And whomever Allah curses, the cursers curse, as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه) said: "What is wrong with me that I do not curse whom Allah cursed, or whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5939), and Muslim (2125 / 120)].

﴿We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾. In one reading it is ﴿qasiyyah﴾ (قَسِيَّةً). ﴿Qasiyah﴾ (قَاسِيَةً) is an active participle (اسم فاعل), and ﴿qasiyyah﴾ (قَسِيَّةً) is an adjective of quality (صفة مشبهة). Which is stronger?
