The adjective of quality is stronger, because it is a constant attribute, as Ibn Malik (رحمه الله) said:
"... like tahir al-qalb, jamil al-zahir."
So the sifah mushabbahah is constant. Thus, when two readings come, ﴿qasiyah﴾ and ﴿qasiyah﴾, the meaning is that both matters are present: she is qasiyyah, this is her attribute, and qasiyah, when something that softens the heart occurs, she hardens, may Allah protect us. So she is qasiyyah as an attribute and qasiyah in action. As we said in the reading ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah 4] and ﴿King﴾: we said we combine the two readings, so the meaning is that He is a King with authority, a Master who owns. Some worldly kings are a king but not an owner; many people are owners but not kings. We all own money, but we are not kings.

So qasiyah and qasiyah are close to this: qasiyyah is its constant attribute, qasiyah when there occurs what would soften the heart, it hardens, may Allah protect us.

﴿And We made their hearts hard, they distort the words from their places﴾. This is also from their misguidance, may Allah protect us, and their breaking of the covenant. ﴿They distort the words﴾: the words of whom? The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Al-kalim﴾ (الكلم) is a collective noun (اسم جمع) of kalimah, whose plural is kalimat, but kalim is a collective noun.

﴿They distort the words﴾: the origin of tahrif (التحريف) is change, changing a thing from its direction. Hence you say: "the animal deviated," meaning its course changed; "the ship deviated," meaning its direction changed. So ﴿yuharrifun﴾ means they change the words from their places. Change of words from their places, among them, is of two types: change in wording, and change in meaning. From their change in wording: when they were told, "Say: hittah (حطة)," what did they say? "Hintah (حنطة)." They did not say "hittah," meaning remove our sins; they said "hintah," meaning give us food. When the punishment of stoning was required for the married adulterer, they distorted it and said: this applies to the lowly, not to the noble; they stoned the lowly but did not stone the noble. This is distortion of meaning, that is, they applied the texts to other than what Allah intended. So their tahrif includes both verbal and semantic distortion.

﴿They distort the words from their places﴾: meaning from the places Allah intended for them.

﴿And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾. ﴿Nasu﴾ (نَسُوا) has two meanings: nasu means "they abandoned," and nasu means "after being reminded." The first is practical forgetting, the second is forgetting of knowledge. Which is intended? Both. They abandoned it deliberately, and they abandoned it through lack of knowledge, that is, they forgot the knowledge they had possessed before. So forgetting is of two kinds: practical forgetting and forgetting of knowledge.

If someone asks: what is the evidence for dividing forgetting this way? We say: read the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [al-Baqarah 286]; this is forgetting of what kind? Of knowledge. And read the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾ [al-Hashr 19]; this is practical forgetting. ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 67]; this is also practical forgetting.

His words ﴿a portion﴾ mean a share (نصيبًا), and hazz may be in good or in evil. The words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And none is granted it except one of great portion﴾ [Fussilat 35]; is this praiseworthy or not? Praiseworthy. If it is said, for example, "So-and-so's share of the Last Day is the Fire," this is blameworthy. ﴿A portion﴾ means a share.

﴿Of what they were reminded of﴾: meaning of the revelation sent down to them so that they would be reminded by it. They forgot a portion of the Torah, since the discussion now concerns the Jews, they forgot a portion of the Torah; they abandoned it deliberately as a result of distorting the words from their places, or they forgot it in the sense that they forgot it after knowing it, because their books were lost. When they were lost, they began to grope in them and write in them what they wished. This is the sense of forgetting that is the opposite of remembrance, and the forgetting that is the opposite of practice.

His words: ﴿They forgot a portion of what they were reminded of, and you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 13]. "You will not cease": O addressee, or O Messenger? The first; that is, O human being, since no prior mention of the Messenger (ﷺ) has occurred. That is, O human being, or O one who reflects on their condition, you will not cease to discover treachery from them.

The word ﴿khaina﴾ (خَائِنَةٍ) may be a verbal noun (مصدرًا) or an active participle (اسم فاعل). If it is a verbal noun, the meaning is: you will not cease to discover treachery from them. If it is an active participle, the meaning is: you will not cease to discover a treacherous group among them, so it is an attribute of an omitted noun.

As for it being an active participle, there is no difficulty, since the active participle comes on the pattern fa'il. But how can it be a verbal noun, and does the verbal noun come in the pattern fa'il? We say: yes, it does. The word al-'afiyah (العافية): "O Allah, I ask You for al-'afiyah." Is it an active participle?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know! You hesitate over something you ask Allah for night and day! "Asaluka al-'afiyah" is a verbal noun: I ask You to grant me well-being. Al-'aqibah is likewise a verbal noun. The Arabic language is vast.

Based on this, we say: the word ﴿khaina﴾ in the noble verse may be a verbal noun like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah, and it may be an active participle; and on this assumption, it needs what? It needs an omitted noun: either we say the estimate is "over a treacherous group," or "over a treacherous self."

Could it not be an active participle with the ta' (تاء) being for intensification (للمبالغة), and the original being "over a treacherous one among them," with the ta' for intensification, as one says of da'in: da'iyah?

We say: it is possible, because among them (i.e., the Jews) there are those whose nature is treachery, so it applies to him that he is khA'inah, i.e., the ta' in it is for intensification. This is from the breadth of the meanings of the Noble Qur'an: you find a single word bearing many meanings. The rule is that whatever admits more than one meaning, with no preponderance and no contradiction, is to be understood as carrying every meaning it admits.

﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them﴾: except a few of the Jews, for they are safe from these attributes and defects, such as who? 'Abdullah ibn Salam (رضي الله عنه). 'Abdullah ibn Salam was one of the rabbis of the Jews, a scholar of their scholars, and there was nothing of these attributes in him. From the time the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he believed in him, followed him, and testified to the truth. There are similar cases; some are safe from these attributes, defects, and blameworthy qualities, but they are few. Therefore He said: ﴿except a few of them﴾.

Then He said: ﴿So pardon them and overlook; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾. ﴿Pardon them﴾: is this about the few who have no treachery, or about all of them? Allah is the One sought for help. It is said that it refers to the nearest mentioned, which is the few: so pardon those few who previously showed harm and hostility toward your message, and then their bad attributes ceased; pardon them for what has passed. So the meaning is: pardon what has passed of their evil deeds. On this meaning there is no difficulty in the verse at all, is there not? O brothers! Pardon the few who were safe from the blameworthy attributes, because these few were Jews, and there had been from them what there had been of hostility and breaking of the covenant, but they believed.

We say: on this assumption there is no difficulty. If we say "pardon them" regarding all of them, together with their being characterized by these attributes and their treachery, then a difficulty remains: the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the Jews by Allah's command. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not prohibit what Allah and His Messenger have prohibited, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah 29]. So how is the combination?

Many exegetes went to the view that this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword, that is, by the verses commanding fighting them. Do you understand?

And how many people, when they are unable to reconcile texts, say "this is abrogated," so much of the Sharia becomes abrogated, although some verifying scholars say abrogation does not exceed ten rulings in total. In any case, we say: some scholars said this verse is abrogated, but there is a difficulty in its being abrogated:
First: because we do not know the chronology (التاريخ), and it is well known that a condition of abrogation is knowledge of the chronology, so that we know this came after that and so abrogates it.
Second: also a condition of abrogation is that reconciliation is impossible; if reconciliation is possible, there is no abrogation, because if reconciliation is possible and you say "this is abrogated," that cancels the other text, and cancelling a text is not light. For example, to say that a ruling is void while it is established by the Qur'an and the Sunnah is no small matter. Therefore it is not permitted to advance the claim of abrogation except with an unavoidable proof. When reconciliation is possible, claiming abrogation is forbidden, because, as I told you, abrogation means nullifying one of the two proofs, and it is difficult for an established proof to be claimed void.
Third: Surat al-Ma'idah is among the last to be revealed, so much so that some scholars said there is no abrogation in it, and that all its rulings are muhkam (محكمة), not abrogated. This is well known among scholars: that Surat al-Ma'idah is among the last revealed, and that there is no abrogated ruling in it.

So the claim of abrogation is not correct. What remains is reconciliation: some scholars reconciled this with the command to fight, saying that the Messenger (ﷺ) forgave those who betrayed and those who rejected him; he pardoned them, that is, he lightened the punishment for them, so he did not kill them. Did the Messenger kill Banu Qaynuqa' and Banu al-Nadir? He did not kill them, although they broke the covenant between them and the Messenger (ﷺ), and this is a kind of pardon and overlooking. Banu Qurayzah too, he in fact pardoned them, for he placed them under the judgment of those whose judgment they accepted, is that not so? Under the judgment of whom? Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. He placed them under his judgment, which they themselves proposed. This is a kind of pardon; otherwise the Messenger would have put the sword among them, because they betrayed the Prophet (ﷺ) and incited the confederates against him. Yet he placed them under the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, whom they accepted; this is a kind of pardon.

So the verse is now muhkam, and the meaning of pardon is not the complete pardon that requires no punishment of them of any kind, but a partial pardon. Without doubt this is better than the claim of abrogation; indeed, claiming abrogation when reconciliation is possible is, as we said, forbidden, because it nullifies a text claimed to be abrogated.

* Student: ﴿So he has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾ [al-Ma'idah 12]. Can we not consider this as an instance of the attributive construct, the annexation of a noun to its adjective: the original being "the sound way"?

* The Shaykh: Yes, correct, and that is so.

* Student: His words: ﴿They distort the words from after their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41], and here: ﴿from their places﴾. How is this?

* The Shaykh: ﴿From their places﴾ means they divert it from it, and ﴿from after their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41]: the reason will come to us, God willing, for why it was expressed with the words ﴿from after their places﴾.

* Student: May Allah be good to you, what is the difference between pardon (العفو) and overlooking (الصفح)?

* The Shaykh: Pardon is non-punishment; overlooking is turning away from the sin in such a way that it is not mentioned, because you may pardon a person but sometimes mention his sin. The origin of safh is turning the side of the neck, which implies that the person turned his back and left the matter as though it had never been. Is the difference clear?

So this is a progression from the lower to the higher: pardon may exist, but the sin is sometimes mentioned; he pardons him and says, "I have forgiven you and will not demand my right," but later says, "This is my reward; I pardoned you, but today you say such-and-such!" Is this overlooking or not? This is not overlooking. But pardon accompanied by overlooking is never mentioned at all; I mean the sin is not mentioned.

* Student: His words, glorified and exalted be He (...).

* The Shaykh: No, because we are not aware that the Messenger mentioned them again after carrying out what he carried out among them.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No; because you lightened this. We are not aware that the Messenger said, "We have pardoned you once and you broke it," for example, or "We permitted you to leave Madinah."

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, it is not directed at a specific person; the deeds or actions are not directed at a specific individual.

* Student: What is the difference between our saying that tahrif occurs in texts, and ta'til (التعطيل) occurs in the meaning (المدلول)?

* The Shaykh: What?

* Student: That tahrif occurs in the evidence (الدليل), and ta'til occurs in the meaning (المدلول)?

Shaykh: Yes. Do you know the difference? I have not mentioned it just now, but I mentioned it before. Distortion in the evidence: "He istawa over the Throne," and he tells you: "istawa" means "istawla" (seized). He has distorted the evidence, and they have distorted the meaning. The meaning indicated (al-madlul) does not establish istiwa' for Allah, whereas the verse does indicate istiwa' for Allah. So he has nullified the indicated meaning. Every person who distorts the evidence will nullify the indicated meaning, and will claim a meaning that the wording does not indicate, thereby wronging the text in two ways: First: nullifying the text from what it was intended to mean. Second: establishing a meaning that is not intended by it.

Student: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾ What is the emphasized element?

Shaykh: The breaking of the covenant.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: That is, due to our emphatic act of their breaking the covenant, such-and-such occurred.

Student: How can the two particles come together and both indicate causation?

Shaykh: Yes. How can two witnesses testify to one and the same thing witnessed? Multiplicity of causes does not necessitate multiplicity of the caused. Is it clear? "You believed in My messengers."

Student: Is it closer to ﴿لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلَاةَ﴾, because faith in the Messenger precedes establishing the prayer..?

Shaykh: Yes. Because they claim that they pray and give zakat. Do you understand? And they do indeed pray, they pray and give zakat, but they did not believe in the messengers.

* * *

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَأَغْرَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 14].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾ to the end. Its discussion and its benefits have already been covered.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ وَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى خَائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 13].

We continue the discussion of the verse. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ﴾. Al-'afw (pardon) is leaving off punishment for a sin, and al-safh (overlooking) is turning away from it. Pardon does not necessarily entail overlooking, but generally overlooking entails pardon. An example: a man wronged you and you pardoned him and did not seek retribution from him; this is pardon. If you turn away and never speak of what happened from him at all, this is called overlooking. ﴿فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.

﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ This serves as a reason for what preceded; that is: We only commanded you to pardon and overlook because Allah, the Exalted, loves the good-doers. It also implies that if Allah loves this, you should not delay in acting upon it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse, first: the affirmation of causes. Is this derived?

Student: From the fa' and the ba'.

Shaykh: How so? From the fa' and the ba', how so? Because they indicate causation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that breaking the covenant is a cause of Allah's curse, the Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ﴾.

* And among its benefits: that cursing is a punishment, since Allah, the Exalted, punished with it those who broke the covenant. Here is a question: Is it permissible for us to curse whom Allah and His Messenger have cursed?

The answer: Yes, we may curse whom Allah and His Messenger have cursed, but in a general manner. When the curse comes in general terms, we curse in general terms; when it comes in specific terms, we curse specifically. For example, we say: "May Allah curse the transgressors, may Allah curse the wrongdoers," and the like. But we do not specify a particular person, even if he is among the wrongdoers, because we do not know how this man will end. He may end with good, and even if he was a disbeliever and died in disbelief, we do not curse him, because this falls under reviling the dead, and "they have passed on to what they earned" (2:134). There is no benefit in it, for if he deserved the curse, he is cursed whether or not you curse him; and if he did not deserve it, you bear the sin.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that whenever a person disobeys his Lord, his heart hardens, by His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً﴾. The reverse of this is that whenever a person obeys his Lord, his heart softens. Many people seek that their hearts be softened and ask what the remedy for hardness of heart is! We say: the remedy for hardness of heart is abundant obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that hearts have states, hardness and softness, and so it is, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابًا مُتَشَابِهًا مَثَانِيَ تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar 23].

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that sins are a cause of diminished understanding of the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or of transgression in understanding it, by His saying: ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ﴾. Distorting words from their places may stem either from ignorance and lack of knowledge, or from arrogance and transgression. In either case, the clause is conjoined to what preceded, or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from His saying ﴿قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾, meaning "while they are...", or from the subject of ﴿قَاسِيَةً﴾, meaning "while they are distorting words from their places." The main point is that sins are a cause of not adhering to the texts, and a cause of distorting them.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that sins are a cause of forgetting what a person has been reminded of. We have mentioned that forgetfulness is of two kinds: forgetting knowledge and forgetting action, and undoubtedly sins cause both. That sins cause the forgetting of knowledge is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زَادَهُمْ هُدًى وَآتَاهُمْ تَقْوَاهُمْ﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Since guidance is a cause of increased knowledge, sin is a cause of its decrease. As for sins causing the forgetting of what is to be abandoned, this is due to Allah's saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49], meaning: if they turn away and withdraw, know that the cause of that is that they sinned, so Allah wills to afflict them for some of their sins.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that these people had the proof established against them, yet they abandoned acting upon it after the proof was established, by His saying: ﴿مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that hardness of heart, distorting words from their places, and forgetting what a person has been reminded of are among the characteristics of the Jews. Since these are among their characteristics, it is obligatory upon a person to keep far from them and flee from them as one flees from a lion.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that the treachery of the Jews remains; by His saying: ﴿وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى خَائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾. We have already explained the word ﴿خَائِنَةٍ﴾. Whoever reflects on their history will know that they are as Allah described them: they remain treacherous, and no pledge from them can be relied upon, nor can a promise from them be trusted. Since they are treacherous, if they see strength opposing them, they weaken before it, and if they see weakness, they grow strong against it. They follow their interests and do not care whether they fulfil a promise or covenant or not, because they remain treacherous.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that among the Jews are some who were purified from that; by His saying: ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾. This is indeed the reality, for among the Jews were those who believed in the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, bore witness to his truth, had excellent Islam, and became callers to their people.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellent treatment of Islam toward its enemy, when Allah commanded pardon and overlooking toward them, especially when victory has become ours. At that time the role of pardon comes, for true pardon, for which a person is praised, is pardon with the ability to punish; pardon out of incapacity is not pardon, and a person is not praised for it.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of love for Allah, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾. The love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is established by the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus of the early generations, and sensed experience, for a person senses the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning that he loves Allah and acts in obedience to Him. Likewise, when one loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, allies for the sake of Allah, and opposes for the sake of Allah, he becomes a friend of Allah and tastes the sweetness of faith.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that refraining from punishing for a sin is part of excellence (ihsan), by His saying: ﴿فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾. This indicates that refraining from punishing for a sin is considered excellence. Many people understand ihsan only as something positive, meaning giving, charity, gifts, and donation. That is not so: ihsan includes two things: either delivering what is desired, or pardoning what is feared.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the exhortation to excellence (ihsan), by His saying: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.

Then, it passed us not long ago that ihsan is divided into two parts: ihsan in the worship of the Creator, and ihsan in dealing with creation. Ihsan in the worship of the Creator was explained by the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, in his saying: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4777) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]. Ihsan in dealing with creation is that you extend kindness to them, and that you do not transgress against them in what is not customary. Some have said: ihsan is giving generously and withholding harm. This has the same meaning as what we have said. This verse indicates that withholding harm is considered part of ihsan.

Then He said: ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾ [al-Ma'idah 14]. That is: We took the covenant of those who said, "We are Christians." He did not say "and from the Christians," but said ﴿those who say, "We are Christians"﴾, even though in another verse Allah affirms this description for them, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians﴾ [al-Hajj 17], where He affirms this description for them. But here He said ﴿who say, "We are Christians"﴾, and its benefit is to establish the proof against them, since they claim that they are Christians and that they are people who support the truth, yet they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of.

﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾. So Allah took the covenant from the Jews, and Allah took the covenant from the Christians, and likewise from this Ummah, for Allah took a covenant from it, as He said: ﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 7].

Allah has taken the covenant from all the children of Adam that they should believe in Him and His messengers, affirm His oneness, and not associate anything with Him. Allah took the covenant from the Christians, from those who said, "We are Christians," ﴿but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ [al-Ma'idah 14].

﴿Forgot﴾ means they abandoned it. This is forgetting in the sense of action. Can it be forgetting in the sense of knowledge? It cannot. If we say that the Children of Israel were relieved of accountability for forgetfulness, since if accountability was lifted from them they are not punished; but if we say that the exemption from accountability for forgetfulness is specific to this Ummah, then we say that His saying ﴿they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ encompasses both forgetting knowledge and forgetting action. There is no doubt that forgetting action is worse than forgetting knowledge, even on the view that they are held accountable for forgetting knowledge.

His saying ﴿a portion [ḥaẓẓ]﴾ means share: they forgot a share of what they were reminded of.

﴿So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Allah did not mention for these Christians the same as what He mentioned for the Jews, because He mentioned for the Jews that He cursed them, made their hearts hard, and they were tested with distorting words from their places, and forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. As for these, He says: ﴿We stirred up among them enmity﴾. This is for punishment.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So We stirred up among them enmity﴾, meaning: We cast it among them. But He expressed it with "stirring up" as if each one were incited against the other because of the intensity of enmity among them. Enmity and hatred: enmity by word and deed, and hatred in the heart. That is, there is no loyalty between them and no affection, but rather enmity, which is the opposite of allegiance, and hatred, which is the opposite of affection.

﴿We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. That is, until our present time. The Christians are divided and hostile, misguiding one another and declaring one another disbelievers.

If someone says: We now find that the Christians are united?

We say: This unity is an apparent unity; otherwise, in their hearts is hatred toward one another that none knows but Allah. Then, what are they united upon? Upon a third enemy, like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. So they are united against a third enemy, and otherwise they are divided among themselves, their hearts are repelled, and their aggressions are evident.

As for His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾: we say that enmity and hatred now among the Christians and between their sects certainly exist, because Allah's report is true, and He said ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾. But what we observe of apparent unity contradicts what is within. Then, as I told you, their present apparent unity is against what? Against an enemy common to all, and this is not strange in worldly affairs and their politics.

As for the Day of Resurrection, it has passed with us that it is the day on which people are resurrected, and it was named so for three matters:

First: that people stand in it from their graves before the Lord of the worlds.

Second: that witnesses are established in it.

Third: that justice is established in it.

﴿And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾: "Sawfa" is for certainty, but it indicates delay, and its sister "sa-" is for certainty but indicates immediacy. If you say: "Zaydun sayaqumu" (Zayd will stand), the meaning is that he will stand now; if you say "sawfa yaqumu," it means later. Yet both indicate certainty, that the matter is certain and must occur.

﴿And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾, meaning: He will inform them of what they used to do. His announcing that He will inform them is a warning, because once He informs them of what they did, nothing remains but recompense according to what they deserve.

His saying ﴿of what they used to do﴾ means: of what they used to do of forgetting a share of what they were reminded of.

* The verse contains benefits, among them: establishing proof against the opponent by his own claim, from His saying ﴿who say, "We are Christians"﴾. As we mentioned, the wisdom in saying ﴿who say, "We are Christians"﴾ rather than "and from the Christians" is to establish proof against them for what they claim: they claim to be Christians, yet they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, did not neglect any community from the covenant He took from them; as we mentioned, He took it from the Jews, from the Christians, from this Ummah, and from all the children of Adam.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: neglecting the right of Allah is among the causes of casting enmity and hatred among people. That is, whenever you find enmity and hatred among people, it is due to what? Their turning away from the religion of Allah, based on His saying ﴿so they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of, so We stirred up﴾, where the "fa" indicates causation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the reverse holds in reverse. That is, when people obey Allah and unite upon it, Allah casts among them affection, love, and loyalty.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: distinguishing between enmity and hatred. The opposite of enmity is allegiance, and the opposite of hatred is love. There is a difference between a beloved who is not an ally and a beloved who is an ally, and between one who is hated and not an enemy and one who is hated and is an enemy, since the hated may transgress against you and thus be an enemy, or may not transgress but merely dislike you, so he is not an enemy.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming the Day of Resurrection, based on His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, which is certain to come, based on Allah's saying ﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves﴾ [al-Hajj 7].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning to these Christians who forgot a portion of what they were reminded of, in His saying ﴿And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming Allah's knowledge, derived from His saying ﴿will inform them﴾, since there is no informing except after knowledge, and so it is.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists) in His saying ﴿what they used to do (yasna'un)﴾, where He attributed the action to them. The principle is that when an action is attributed to someone, he is its performer and chooses it. So it contains a refutation of the Jabriyyah, who say that a person is compelled in his actions, even in voluntary movements; they say he is compelled, so that even if a person wishes to eat or drink, they say he is compelled to that. There is no doubt that this saying contradicts what is perceived, what is rational, and what is transmitted.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture and pardoning much.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 15] to the end of the verse.

﴿O People of the Scripture﴾ refers to the Jews and the Christians. Since this is the case, the word "the Scripture" here refers to the category, namely the Torah and the Gospel. Allah the Exalted attributed them to the Scripture and named them its people in order to establish proof against them and to remove any excuse, as if He were saying: O People of the Scripture, you are people of the Scripture, you have knowledge and understanding. There has come to you Our Messenger, and you recognize this Messenger just as you recognize what? Your sons.

His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you Our Messenger﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿making clear to you﴾: ﴿making clear﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to "Messenger", meaning: while he makes clear to you, that is, manifests to you, much of what you were concealing of the Scripture, while the remainder he pardons. So he makes clear much of what you were concealing of the Scripture that is necessary for establishing proof against you, and he pardons much that there is no need to mention. Whoever reflects on the Qur'an finds in it many reports about the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Who revealed the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance for mankind, which you put into pages, showing them and concealing much?﴾ [al-An'am 91]. This is the habit of the People of the Scripture.

﴿making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture﴾ means: He makes clear to you its ruling, because there is need for it. ﴿and pardoning much﴾ means: He leaves it and does not mention it, because there is no need to mention it.

Then He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book﴾. His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you﴾ ... ﴿a light and a Book﴾: Is the intended "light" Muhammad (ﷺ), or is it the guidance that results from the Book and the Sunnah? The second; the intended meaning is the second. On this basis, His saying ﴿and a Book﴾ is conjoined to ﴿light﴾ by way of conjoining the cause to the effect. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light﴾ [an-Nisa' 174]. So Muhammad (ﷺ) brought the light, which is the radiant, shining guidance in which there is no darkness.

﴿and a clear Book﴾: the clear Book is the Qur'an, and it was called a Book for three matters:
First: that it is written in the Preserved Tablet.
Second: that it is written in the scrolls that are in the hands of the angels.
Third: that it is written in the scrolls that are in our hands. And "fi'āl" is in the sense of "maf'ūl" as is frequently found in the Arabic language, such as "ghirās" (planted) and "binā'" (built).

He said: ﴿clear﴾ — is the intended meaning: making clear to others, or clear in itself? Both; the intended meaning is both, because the quadriliteral "abāna" is used intransitively and transitively. You say: "abāna al-ṣubḥ" meaning it became clear, and you say: "fulān abāna al-ḥaqq" meaning he manifested the truth. When a word is used in two meanings, it is taken to mean both, under the two conditions we mentioned previously: that they do not contradict each other, and that the word is equally capable of bearing them. Here the word bears this and that, even though one of them necessarily follows from the other, for when it makes clear to others it is itself clear.

﴿Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ [al-Ma'idah 16]. ﴿Guides by it﴾: the "bā'" here indicates causation, and the guidance here, if what is meant by "it" is its indication, then the guidance here is guidance of indication; and if what is meant by His saying ﴿by it﴾ in ﴿Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ is by following it, then the guidance is guidance of enabling (tawfīq) and also of indication.

Let us look at the rest of the context: ﴿Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure﴾: ﴿whoever﴾ is the first object, ﴿ways﴾ is the second object, and ﴿His pleasure﴾ is the object of ﴿follows﴾. So the one guided is the follower of His pleasure, and that to which he is guided is the ways of peace.

﴿Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure﴾ means: he seeks it and desires it, and sees what pleases Allah and acts upon it.

﴿the ways of peace﴾: He did not say "the way of peace," although the common usage is to express the path of Islam in the singular and the paths of error in the plural. But here, when He said ﴿follows His pleasure﴾, it became necessary that the intended "ways" here are the legislations of Islam, meaning: if one follows Allah's pleasure, he has been guided, submitted, and believed; but Islam has legislations, it has ways, and therefore He said ﴿the ways of peace﴾. The attribution of "ways" to "peace" is an attribution of a thing to its cause, meaning: the ways through which peace is attained. Peace from what? Peace from the Fire, peace from deviation, peace from doubts. Mention every meaning that the word "peace" can bear.

﴿the ways of peace and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission﴾: ﴿brings them out﴾ means Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and by His saying ﴿brings them out﴾ is meant ﴿whoever follows His pleasure﴾; the pronoun returns to "whoever" (man) in the plural form, observing its meaning, because "man" is singular in form but may be intended as plural in meaning, so it is correct for the pronoun to return to it in the plural. This is a rule regarding "man," whether it is a relative pronoun or a conditional particle: one may return the pronoun to it in the plural form in view of meaning, and in the singular form in view of wording. Look at Allah's saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ [at-Talaq 11]. You will find that Allah returned the pronoun to it once in the plural and once in the singular, and returned it a second time in the singular: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness﴾ (singular), ﴿He will admit him﴾ (singular), ﴿abiding﴾ (plural), ﴿Allah has certainly perfected for him﴾ (singular). The rule is that the wording of "man," whether relative or conditional, allows the pronoun to return to it in the singular, observing the wording, and to return to it in the plural, observing the meaning. When is it observing the wording? When it returns in the singular; and observing the meaning when it returns in the plural.

* Student: Shaykh, in matters of creed, we say what we say in issues of belief: it is established by sense, reason and transmission. Some say: established by reason and transmission, while Shaykh al-Islam says: established by the sensory and transmission. What is the difference between "sensory" and "reason"?
* The Shaykh: "Sense" is what you perceive through the senses, such as touch, smell and taste; "reason" is what you perceive with your heart, with your intellect. That is the difference. Yet it is possible that it comes with the transmitted, rational and sensory evidence together. For example: the hand is attributed to a human, attributed to a camel, and attributed to a mule; the difference in them is perceived by what? By the senses; everyone knows this is its hand like this, and this is its hand like that. Reason is that you say, concerning the attributes of Allah: if the essence of the Creator does not resemble the created, then likewise His attributes. This is a rational proof, not a sensory proof.
* The Student: Shaykh, you said that in the Qur'an and Sunnah, Allah named those who claimed to follow Jesus "the Naṣārā," but in reality today they are not called by this name; they say they are Christians. What is the reason they have fled from this name? No, Shaykh, even now among Arabs, when one says to them, "Are you a Naṣrānī?" they say: "No, I am not, I am a Christian."
* The Shaykh: The reason is that when they ascribe themselves to the Messiah, they ascribe themselves to a religion, to a messenger whose religion is true, and this is easier than if they said: "We are Naṣārā," especially if we say that "Naṣārā" is a relation to a town called "Nazareth"; for the relation then becomes a relation of land and homeland. But if we say "Masīḥiyyūn" (Christians), the relation becomes to a messenger who is followed. Just as the people of distortion call themselves what? "The people of interpretation." They said that to soften the matter and make the thing acceptable, for if they had said "the people of distortion," no one would have followed them.
* Student: Shaykh, first, what is the validity of the saying of one who said: "If one draws near through action, it is not from (...) to the Book and Sunnah; they reproached him with the term Christianity"?
* The Shaykh: It may be this and that.
* Student: Shaykh, we said: if one deserves the curse, as is the custom here in general terms, then if we know that a certain person among people deserves to be cursed by name, is it permissible for us to specify him?
* The Shaykh: No. From where do you know?
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct. That is why, when the Messenger used to invoke a curse upon a people: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and curse so-and-so," Allah forbade him, saying: ﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He relents toward them or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 128][[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4069) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]].
* Student: It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he may curse one who does not deserve cursing; is this possible?
* The Shaykh: Like what?
* The Student: As was related from him (ﷺ): "O Allah, I am a human who gets angry as humans get angry, so whichever man I curse, make that an expiation for him"[[Narrated by Muslim (2601/91) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], or the meaning of the hadith. Is it possible that the Prophet (ﷺ) cursed a man not worthy of cursing, and we do not know..
* The Shaykh: Actually "cursing" here means reviling. When the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, does a man curse his father?" he said: "He reviles a man's father, so he reviles his father, and reviles his mother, so he reviles his mother"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5973) and Muslim (90/146) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]].
* Student: Shaykh, is the specific cursing of Allah understood, especially if the person died as a disbeliever in Allah and we are certain of that?
* The Shaykh: I told you: what is the benefit? If Allah has cursed him, there is no need for your supplication; and if he is not worthy, then you are sinful.
* Student: Shaykh, we mentioned that not being held accountable for a sin is considered a kindness; does this apply absolutely, specifying...?
* The Shaykh: Absolutely, just as the loss of reward is considered a punishment: "Whoever keeps a dog, except a herding dog or a hunting dog, his reward is reduced by a qīrāṭ every day"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5480) and Muslim (1574/53) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. This is a punishment, though not a punishment of pain or torment, but the loss of something beloved.
* Student: (...) Shaykh, that a person persists in sin and disobedience, is it permissible, that (...).
* The Shaykh: He, may Allah bless you, is the origin of pardon. Pardon is not legislated except when it involves reform. We are not examining whether this counts as kindness or not; rather we are examining whether pardon is in its proper place or not. Allah the Exalted made a condition of pardon that it be reform, saying: ﴿whoever pardons and reforms﴾ [ash-Shura 40]. Therefore, if pardoning this man would lead to his domination and aggression against people, we would not pardon him.
* The Student: The specific prohibition regarding cursing, is all supplication against him analogous to it, all supplication against him?
* The Shaykh: As for supplicating against him, it apparently does not fall under cursing, because cursing is not light; cursing is expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. But if you ask Allah to destroy him or the like, apparently this does not fall under it.
* The Student: This is specific to (...) the Prophet (ﷺ), who supplicated against a particular man other than by cursing.
* The Shaykh: I do not recall, but I do not think it is free of it; it must have occurred.
* Student: Shaykh, what is the rhetorical benefit..
* The Shaykh: The Messenger supplicated against Quraysh in general: "O Allah, make it upon them as years like the years of Joseph; O Allah, upon You be Quraysh, O Allah, upon You be Quraysh"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6200) and Muslim (675/265) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And I do not rule out that supplication against a specific person exists.
* The Student: Those who harmed him, when he was prostrating, he supplicated against them openly: "O Allah, destroy so-and-so..?"
* The Shaykh: Yes, but he supplicated against them; I do not recall that the supplication was specified.
* Student: The rhetorical benefit of placing the prepositional phrase first in ﴿And among those who said, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾.
* The Shaykh: Emphasis, because whenever a thing is repeated, its emphasis increases.
* * *
* Student: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture and pardoning much. There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book (15). Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path (16)﴾ [al-Ma'idah 15–17]. Ṣadaqa Allāhu al-ʿaẓīm... 
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture and pardoning much. There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book (15). Allah guides by it whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ [al-Ma'idah 15, 16]. First: who is intended by "His Messenger" here? The Prophet Muhammad, or Moses, or Jesus?
* Student: It is the Prophet (ﷺ), because (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying ﴿making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture﴾ — do we want an example of that?
* Student: The ruling on stoning the married adulterer, for the Prophet (ﷺ) (...).
* The Shaykh: The ruling on stoning the married adulterer is present among them in the Torah, and yet they conceal it. And what else? More important than that is the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Torah and the Gospel: they find it written among them in the Torah and the Gospel, and yet they conceal this and deny it.
His saying ﴿and pardoning much﴾: what is meant by pardoning here?
* Student: He does not mention it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, he does not mention it. And it was called pardon because in it there is a covering of their disgraceful acts, which they used to commit by concealing what Allah revealed; so Allah the Exalted named it pardon. ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾: what is meant by the light?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "Ridwān" belongs to what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The Qur'an, good. And "Book"? "Light and Book"?
But we conjoin "Book", and there is no doubt that the intended "Book" is the Qur'an; we conjoin "Book" to "light", and it is the same thing. That is, a thing is conjoined to itself.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is not an idāfah; "light and Book", and the basis of conjunction is difference.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Why? The light is what the Messenger brought of the Shari'ah.
Concealing what Allah revealed, so Allah the Exalted named it pardon.
﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾: what is meant by the light?
* Student: The Qur'an.
* The Shaykh: The Qur'an. ﴿And a Book﴾? ﴿Light and Book﴾?
* Student: The written Qur'an.
* The Shaykh: But the description of "Book", and there is no doubt that the intended "Book" is the Qur'an, is "Book" an attribute of "light", and it is the same?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, conjoining a thing to itself?
* Student: Attributing a thing to itself.
* The Shaykh: It is not an idāfah, "light and Book", and the basis of conjunction is difference.
* Student: Light is applied to the Messenger (ﷺ), and it is applied to the Qur'an, because all of it is true.
* Another student: (...) with the Qur'an and Sunnah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 15–16 (part 2 of 3):

* The Shaykh: Why is the light (nur) the Shari'ah that the Messenger brought, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have sent down to you a clear light﴾ [An-Nisa 174]? It has also been said that it is the Qur'an, as you mentioned. In that case, the conjunction of "the Book" (al-kitab) to it is the conjunction of a thing to its attribute, for example: ﴿Who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought forth the pasture﴾ [Al-A'la 2–4], and it is one (thing).
The Shaykh: The statement: ﴿Whoever follows His pleasure into the ways of peace﴾. What is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿whoever follows His pleasure﴾?
* A student: The saying of the Exalted: ﴿By it Allah guides whoever follows﴾. Here "man" (whoever) is an object (maf'ul bihi).
* The Shaykh: An object of what?
* The student: An object of "yahdi" (guides).
* The Shaykh: An object of "yahdi". And ﴿subul﴾ (ways)?
* The student: ﴿subul﴾ is a second object.
* The Shaykh: A second object. And ﴿ridwanahu﴾ (His pleasure)?
* The student: ﴿ridwanahu﴾ is also an object.
* The Shaykh: An object of what?
* The student: An object of ﴿ittaba'a﴾ (follows).
* The Shaykh: An object of ﴿ittaba'a﴾? Are you sure? Do you all agree with this?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Here He said ﴿the ways of peace﴾, and it is well known that the way of Allah is one?
* A student: What is meant is the laws of Islam.
* The Shaykh: What is meant is the laws of Islam, yes; because the "way", which is Islam, is taken from His saying ﴿followed His pleasure﴾.
What is meant by guidance here: guidance of enabling (tawfiq) or guidance of indication (dalalah)?
* A student: Both.
* The Shaykh: Wrong. As long as you are looking at grammar, it is wrong. I said: what is meant by guidance? You said: both. Guidance is feminine.
* The student: Both of them (kilta-huma).
* The Shaykh: Yes, both of them are meant: the guidance of enabling and the guidance of indication.
He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿and brings them out of darknesses into the light by His permission﴾. The darknesses: the darknesses of ignorance, of shirk, of sins, of transgression, and other things.
His saying ﴿by His permission﴾: the permission here is the permission of decree (idhn qadari), and the permission of decree means will (mashi'ah) and means desire (irada). It is contrasted with the permission of Shari'ah (idhn shar'i), as in His saying: ﴿Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you invent against Allah?﴾ [Yunus 59]. It is known that Allah permitted them by decree, but He did not permit them by Shari'ah.
From the permission of Shari'ah is His saying: ﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [Ash-Shura 21].
From the permission of decree is this verse, ﴿by His permission﴾, and also His saying: ﴿Who is it that intercedes with Him except by His permission?﴾ [Al-Baqarah 255]. So permission is of two kinds: permission of decree and permission of Shari'ah. The difference between them: the permission of Shari'ah occurs only in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is pleased with, while the permission of decree occurs in what He is pleased with and in what He is not pleased with. This is one.
The second difference: what He has permitted by Shari'ah may or may not occur, since people may comply or may not comply; but what He has permitted by decree must occur.
﴿and brings them out of darknesses into the light by His permission and guides them to a straight path﴾. When guidance is followed by "ila" (to), it is the guidance of indication. Accordingly, the meaning of ﴿and guides them to a straight path﴾ is: He indicates it to them, and this means opening the doors of knowledge for them, so that they know what they did not know before.
* In this noble verse there are many benefits. Among them: the address to the Jews and Christians as "People of the Book" (ahl al-kitab).
It may be said: is there in this an honouring of them and an exalting of them, in that He named them "People of the Book"?
The answer to that: we say, He named them "People of the Book" not as an honour to them, but to establish the proof against them, because the People of the Book are those who must be the first to act upon it, as Allah said at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 41].
So those who now make a great show and want to bring the religions close together, and say that Allah named them People of the Book, supposing or deceiving that this is a matter of honouring them and approving of what they are upon, we say, what do we say? We say: Allah did not address them with that as an honour to them. How could it be an honour to them when Allah says: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine and those who worshipped Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 60]! Rather, He addressed them with this description to establish the proof against them, and that their conduct is far from reason, because the People of the Book must be the first to act upon it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the elevation of the status of the Prophet (ﷺ), in His saying ﴿Our Messenger﴾, for attributing his message to Allah is undoubtedly an honour, and everything attributed to Allah is an honour, even inanimate things when attributed to Allah are an honour for them: ﴿And purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand [in prayer]﴾ [Al-Hajj 26].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, is sent to the People of the Book, because of His saying ﴿There has come to you Our Messenger﴾, and so it is. The Prophet (ﷺ) even swore that "no Jew or Christian hears of him and then does not believe in what he was sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire"[[Recorded by Muslim (153 / 240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. So he is sent to them with the Qur'an, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslims.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, is a clarifier; ﴿He makes clear to you﴾. He, peace and blessings be upon him, is a radiant lamp, clarifying to creation, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [An-Nahl 44]. The clarification which Allah mentions here includes clarifying the wording and clarifying the meaning, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 67].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the People of the Book are people who conceal knowledge, because of His saying ﴿much of what you used to conceal from the Book﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever among this Ummah conceals knowledge has a resemblance to the Jews and Christians, because this is their habit; whoever conceals has imitated them, imitating them in the most ugly trait, may Allah protect us, which is concealing the knowledge that came to them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, remained silent about some of the faults of the People of the Book and did not make them clear to them.
If someone says: why did he not clarify them and expose them? We say: their exposure in what he did clarify is sufficient, and silence about what he did not clarify is because the public interest requires it. This may also contain a kind of winning hearts (ta'lif), that is, the winning of their hearts.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that everything the Messenger Muhammad brought is light that shines. If you reflect on its reports, you are illuminated by it; its rulings likewise. It is a light on the path by which a person is guided on his way to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and on his way to dealing with the servants of Allah.
It is also a light in the heart: whoever adheres to the Shari'ah of Muhammad (ﷺ) increases in light in his heart, in insight, in deriving the legal rulings, and so on.
It is also a light in the face, because the one who adheres to the Shari'ah of the Prophet, peace be upon him, must have this affect his speech, actions and state, so his face becomes radiant. For this reason you find the godly scholars have a light in their faces that is almost perceptible. As for the inner light, it is well known; even if the godly scholar's skin is not, that is, not white, his face still shines, for light is one thing and colour is another.
It is also a light in the grave: when a person is a believer, may Allah make us and you among them, his grave is made spacious as far as his eye can see, and there comes to him the breeze and delight of Paradise.
It is also a light on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right﴾ [Al-Hadid 12].
So the word "light" is comprehensive and general in everything in which darkness may exist; the Islamic religion illuminates it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is written. Where is it written? We have mentioned that it is written in the copies of the Mushaf in our hands, in the Preserved Tablet, and in the scrolls in the hands of the angels.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Noble Qur'an clarifies things, and clearer than that is His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ [An-Nahl 89]. The word "mubin" (clear), we mentioned in the tafsir, may be transitive or intransitive. If it is intransitive, the meaning is that it is clear in itself; if transitive, the meaning is that it makes others clear. There is no doubt that the Qur'an's clarity in itself and its making things clear to others is its attribute.
If it is clear and an explanation of all things, does it not follow from this that it is not fitting for us to turn away from reflecting upon it? Rather, we must reflect upon it, and the first of the matters that come to us we seek in what? In the Book of Allah. If we are unable to ascertain it in the Book of Allah, then in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Sunnah of the Messenger clarifies the Qur'an by the command of Allah: ﴿And We sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [An-Nahl 44].
If the matter is not in the Qur'an nor in the Sunnah, and we are unable to grasp the Shari'ah ruling in the Book and the Sunnah, then either we ask the people of knowledge, as He says: ﴿So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl 43], or we suspend judgement.
If a person is qualified for ijtihad (independent reasoning), there is no blame upon him for exercising ijtihad, like the person who does not know the qibla himself and no trustworthy person has informed him of it: he must strive and seek to determine it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that guidance is in the hand of Allah. There are many proofs for this: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one guided, and whomever He leads astray, you will not find for him a guiding ally﴾ [Al-Kahf 17]; ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾ [Al-'Imran 73]. The verses on this are many. In whose hand is guidance? In the hand of Allah: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [Al-Qasas 56].
Since it is from Allah, the following follows from it:
First: that we should not ask for guidance except from Allah, and that we should persist before our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in asking for guidance: "O Allah, guide me, O Allah, guide me," constantly. This is the first.
Second: that we know our actions are not independent, but are by the enabling (tawfiq) of Allah. In this there is a refutation of whom? Of the Qadariyyah. If Allah guides, it means that our actions have a relation to the guidance of Allah, and in that there is a refutation of the Qadariyyah who say that man is independent in himself, in his deeds, in his will, and in his power.
Does it agree with the Jabriyyah? The answer, listen: ﴿whoever follows His pleasure﴾, ﴿follows﴾, so He attributed the following to him, unlike the Jabriyyah who say that a person's deed is not attributed to him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whenever a person follows what pleases Allah, his knowledge of the Shari'ah of Allah increases; by His saying: ﴿By it Allah guides whoever follows His pleasure into the ways of peace﴾. Mention it in reverse: whoever turns away from the pleasure of Allah, he is not guided to the ways of Allah, because he is not worthy of guidance.
Accordingly, we say to any student of knowledge: do you want Allah to guide you and grant you knowledge? He will say: yes. We say: then you must follow the pleasure of Allah. Whenever you see something that pleases Allah, do it, and whenever you see something that angers Allah, avoid it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of pleasure (ridwan/rida) for Allah, by His saying ﴿His pleasure﴾. Pleasure is one of the active attributes (sifat fi'liyyah) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it is connected to His will and has a cause, and its cause is the servant's action by the enabling of Allah.
Every attribute of Allah that has a cause is among the active attributes, because the cause occurs by the will of Allah, and the attribute that follows it occurs by the will of Allah. So pleasure, anger, joy, laughter, wonder and what resembles them are all active attributes.
Is the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, like the pleasure of the created? No, by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]. This is the textual proof. The rational proof: if the essence of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, does not resemble the essences of the created, then likewise His attributes, because discourse about attributes is a branch of discourse about the essence. This is what the People of the Sunnah adhered to, and they said: it is not for us to dictate about the words of Allah and His Messenger according to our understandings, nor, I say, according to our intellects; for our intellects are followers, requiring that they follow the Book and the Sunnah, but according to our understandings.
As for these Mu'attilah, as Shaykh al-Islam said: they were given understandings but were not given knowledge; they have understanding but no knowledge and no intellect; they were given intelligence but not purity (zaka').
The People of the Sunnah believe in these attributes and believe that they do not resemble the attributes of the created. The people of ta'til say: no, we do not believe in them, for these are attributes of deficiency: pleasure is a deficiency, love is a deficiency, anger is a deficiency, so they must be interpreted by their concomitant, this is one; or we keep silent and say: we do not know their meaning. That is, for the people of ta'til there is no way to pass beyond one of the two paths: either they negate (ta'til) or they delegate (tafwid). The meaningful tafwid, not the modal tafwid, and on this the author of the Khulasah says:
"Every text that gives the impression of resemblance, delegate it, or interpret it, and aim at declaring Him transcendent."
The reality is that this does not declare Him transcendent; rather, on the contrary, we say: pleasure is an attribute established for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which entails reward and honour. They say: no, pleasure is reward and honour, and He expressed it by its concomitant cause. So we say: woe to the person who hears the words of Allah saying of Himself that He is pleased, then says: no, He is not pleased; He has no pleasure, no anger, no joy. La ilaha illa Allah! How can that be, when He is the One who informed of Himself? Are you more knowing or is Allah? How can He describe Himself with what He is not described by, when He says to His servants: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ [An-Nisa 26]? Is this not a riddle, that He speaks with words, may He be glorified and exalted, while intending the opposite? This is a riddle and a concealment.
If the one who negates would reflect a little, he would find that his negation is among the greatest transgressions against Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We say: reward results from pleasure and is a proof of it, that is, a rational proof of pleasure, because whoever rewards you indicates what? That he is pleased with you. Glory be to Allah! You find that the people of falsehood, whether in practical or theoretical matters, are contradictory.
Accordingly, the original and firm principle is: that you affirm what Allah has affirmed for Himself in the Qur'an or the Sunnah; that is one. Second: that you negate from Him resemblance to the created, and by that you will be safe. As for interpreting, and in reality distorting, this is misguidance.
Among misguidance too is to delegate: "By Allah (...), pleasure, I do not know what it is; I recite the Qur'an and say nothing." This is also a great evil. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the doctrine of the Mufawwidah is among the worst of the statements of the people of innovation and atheism, and he spoke the truth, may Allah have mercy on him. If you reflect on the statement of the Mufawwidah, you will know that it is disbelief and atheism. How can Allah send down to us a Qur'an, the most noble of whose content is that we know of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His names, His attributes, His rulings and His acts, and then we find no way to understand its meaning, and make it for us like: alif, ba', ta', tha'?
Glory be to Allah! How is it fitting for a believing man to say: what Allah related to us about Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun is of known meaning, but what He related about Himself is not of known meaning? What benefit is there for us in the Qur'an? As long as it is not known, we will not benefit from it: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who know not the Book except in wishful thinking﴾ [Al-Baqarah 78], that is, except recitation; meaning that we have no portion or share except mere recitation.
In any case, our creed is this: that we believe in everything Allah affirmed for Himself in the Qur'an or in the Sunnah, without likening Him to anything, and by that we are safe in our creed.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the paths of safety are many and various, by His saying: ﴿the ways of peace﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 15–16 (part 3 of 3):

For example, how many are the pillars of Islam? Five, and each one is a path (sabil). The gates of Paradise are eight, and each gate has people specifically assigned to it. So there are paths (subul) and there are gates (abwab), and what is meant by that is the legal laws (shara'i'). As for Islam as a whole, it is one path.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever follows the Shari'ah has attained peace (salam). From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿the paths of peace﴾. Peace from what? Peace in every sense of the word: peace in his creed, in his deeds, and in his recompense, because this path will lead him to the Abode of Peace to which Allah invites, ﴿And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [Yunus 25].
* Student: May Allah bless you. Some of the apostate writers have come out with a new innovation, namely that the People of the Book are not disbelievers. Now, regarding this, it is said: whoever does not declare the disbeliever a disbeliever is himself a disbeliever, because this matter is known as a necessity of the religion: the disbelief of the People of the Book. Or is it said that he may be excused in this matter due to his ignorance?
* The Shaykh: No, he is not excused. This is among what is known as a necessity of the religion of Islam. If he says that the People of the Book, meaning the Jews and Christians, are not disbelievers, then he has denied the Qur'an and is considered an apostate. Either he affirms and says, "Yes, they are disbelievers; the proof has been established against them, and if they die upon what they are upon, they are among the companions of the Fire." Or else he is to be executed so that he may join them.
* Student: We said in the explanation that Shaykh al-Islam said: "The people of innovation were given understanding (fuhum) but were not given knowledge (ulum)." Is that the text?
* The Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: Shaykh, did he not say: "They were given knowledge but not understanding"?
* The Shaykh: No, on the contrary: they were given understanding but not given knowledge.
* Student: May Allah bless you. We mentioned that the permission here is the permission of divine decree (al-idhn al-qadari). Is not bringing them out of darkness into light a matter loved by Allah, Mighty and Majestic?
* The Shaykh: No. Bringing out is a loved matter, but this bringing out is a divine decree permission: Allah, exalted is He, permits them to come out, and He permits them not to come out.
* Student: May Allah bless you. What is the duty of the students of knowledge regarding this issue?
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: That is, not declaring the People of the Book to be disbelievers. O Shaykh, among the students of knowledge there are those who say: I tested this in the mosques and I tested it in the schools. He asks: "Who are the disbelievers?" And many of them, the young ones and the old ones, many of them... perhaps a quarter of those present do not declare the People of the Book disbelievers. They say: "These Jews and Christians are not disbelievers."
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah.
* Student: Yes, Shaykh. This is transmitted with an unbroken chain that they do not know this at all.
* The Shaykh: He must clarify it. And this innovation, we have not heard of it until now.
* Student: No, O Shaykh, it is widespread.
* The Shaykh: No, no. He must clarify, may Allah bless you, that they are disbelievers by the explicit text of the Qur'an.
* Student: If this is in lands where (...)?
* The Shaykh: ﴿Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 73]. ﴿Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 72]. This matter is clear. Did the Messenger not fight the People of the Book?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And he took the jizyah from them, and whoever did not pay it, he killed. Does he kill Muslims?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: The discussion of creed has become rare. People talk about the softening of the heart (raqa'iq) and such matters; creed is hardly discussed anymore except by a few.
* The Shaykh: In any case, it must be clarified. If it is now confused for people, it must be clarified on every occasion. And as we have mentioned now, Allah addresses them as "People of the Book" to establish the proof against them, not as an affirmation of what they are upon, nor as an honoring of them.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He wished to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely? And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent."﴾ (17) ﴿And the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are but human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the return."﴾ (18) [al-Ma'idah 17, 18].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary"﴾, and the discussion of it has preceded... and the benefits, have we finished them?
Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and brings them out from darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿and brings them out﴾: a refutation of the Qadariyyah who say that Allah has no connection to the actions of the servant. The verse is explicit: ﴿brings them out from darkness﴾.
* And among its benefits: sins are darknesses, and disbelief and polytheism are the greatest of them in wrongdoing. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. Fabricating lies against Allah is among the greatest of them in wrongdoing: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ [al-An'am 21]. Preventing the mosques from having the name of Allah mentioned in them is among the greatest of them in wrongdoing: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mention of His name in the mosques?﴾ [al-Baqarah 114].
In sum, all sins are from the darknesses. Ignorance is also a wrong, because it blinds a person to the way, so he does not know where he is going, where he returns, or how he should act.
Likewise, among wrongs is wronging the servants by transgressing against them in their wealth, their bodies, or their honor.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Shari'ah is light, and it is so; it is light without doubt, and none perceives this except one whom Allah has given complete faith and certainty. Whenever faith is perfected, a person grows in light, and the light of the Shari'ah becomes clear to him. We ask Allah to make it clear to us and to you.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of permission (idhn) for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. I do not mean by "permission" the kind that is heard, because that is a matter we do not know; rather, the permission that is will (iradah). It is of two kinds: legal permission (idhn shar'i) and universal/decreed permission (idhn kawni).
Legal permission is what Allah has legislated. Everything Allah has legislated is permitted by the Law, and legal permission does not necessarily entail the occurrence of what Allah has permitted.
Decreed or universal permission is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, and this permission must occur, because it is the will of Allah, glorified and exalted.
So here, ﴿by His permission﴾: is it legal permission or decreed permission?
* Student: Legal.
* The Shaykh: No, decreed; because bringing them out from darkness into light relates to Lordship, to decree.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whenever a person holds fast to the Shari'ah of Allah, Allah, exalted is He, guides him; this is based on His saying: ﴿and guides them to a straight path﴾. This has many witnesses in the Qur'an: that sins are a cause of deviation, and that obedience and compliance are a cause of guidance and righteousness. There are many examples of this in the Qur'an, and there is no need to enumerate them, because they come up before us often.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the paths include the straight and the crooked. The path of Allah, exalted is He, is straight, and whatever else of paths is crooked; it has no uprightness and does not lead to a result, because it is crooked.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture and pardoning much.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 15] to the end of the verse.

﴿O People of the Scripture﴾ refers to the Jews and the Christians. Since this is the case, the word "the Scripture" here refers to the category, namely the Torah and the Gospel. Allah the Exalted attributed them to the Scripture and named them its people in order to establish proof against them and to remove any excuse, as if He were saying: O People of the Scripture, you are people of the Scripture, you have knowledge and understanding. There has come to you Our Messenger, and you recognize this Messenger just as you recognize what? Your sons.

His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you Our Messenger﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿making clear to you﴾: ﴿making clear﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to "Messenger", meaning: while he makes clear to you, that is, manifests to you, much of what you were concealing of the Scripture, while the remainder he pardons. So he makes clear much of what you were concealing of the Scripture that is necessary for establishing proof against you, and he pardons much that there is no need to mention. Whoever reflects on the Qur'an finds in it many reports about the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Who revealed the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance for mankind, which you put into pages, showing them and concealing much?﴾ [al-An'am 91]. This is the habit of the People of the Scripture.

﴿making clear to you much of what you were concealing of the Scripture﴾ means: He makes clear to you its ruling, because there is need for it. ﴿and pardoning much﴾ means: He leaves it and does not mention it, because there is no need to mention it.
