Consider also their saying ﴿And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter﴾: they emphasize their entry if those [people] leave. And if those [people] leave, would the entry need to be emphasized? It does not need to be. But, glory be to Allah, if one reflects on the state of this angry nation, one finds that they are in utmost foolishness of mind, just as they are in utmost misguidance in religion.

Whoever seeks further clarification on this matter should refer to the book of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, Ighathat al-Lahfan, for he spoke about the characteristics of the religious communities in a manner that cannot be surpassed.

﴿Said two men from those who feared [Allah] and upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, "Enter upon them through the gate."﴾

First: we ask about the structure of this noble verse: ﴿Said two men from those who feared [Allah] and upon whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾. Is ﴿rajulan﴾ known to be indefinite, or definite?

* Student: Indefinite.

* Shaykh: Reflect? ﴿Said two men﴾?

* Students: Indefinite.

* Shaykh: By consensus? Is there no dissenter? Yes, ﴿rajulan﴾ is indefinite.

﴿From those who fear﴾ must be a description (sifah) of ﴿rajulan﴾.

[The following repeats the earlier passage of the commentary, as in the source, with minor variation.]

Next: ﴿from those who fear﴾ must be a description of "rajulan"; for what follows an indefinite noun from a clause or its equivalent is a description of it.

And ﴿yakhafuna﴾ here is the relative clause (silat al-mawsul). ﴿From those who fear﴾ is the relative clause.

﴿Upon whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾: is ﴿anʿama﴾ here the object of ﴿yakhafuna﴾, or is it governed by an omitted verb? I am asking about ﴿anʿama﴾, not about its i'rab; I ask whether it is the object of ﴿yakhafuna﴾ or not.

* Students: A verb.

* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿anʿama﴾ is a verb, not an object. The object of ﴿yakhafuna﴾ is omitted, and we will estimate it shortly, God willing. ﴿Anʿama﴾ is a verb; ﴿from those who fear, Allah had bestowed favor upon them both﴾: ﴿anʿama﴾ is a verb, a verbal sentence, whose place in i'rab is a description of ﴿rajulan﴾, and it may be a circumstantial state (hal) from it, since it is an indefinite noun that has been specified; when an indefinite noun is specified, a circumstantial state may occur from it. Do you understand?

But someone may say: is it not more appropriate in construction to say: "Said two men upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, from those who fear"?

The answer: No; because if it is considered a circumstantial state, then the description that directly follows its head is more suitable for proximity. If "Allah had bestowed favor upon them" is taken as a state, then the description that is attached to its described noun in i'rab is more suitable for adjacency; for the state follows its described noun in meaning but is separate from it in i'rab, unlike the descriptive adjective (na't). So we say: if we make this a state, it will be placed after the directly preceding description.

Second: ﴿from those who fear﴾ is a prepositional phrase, so it is in the category of a single word, and ﴿anʿama﴾ is a clause; a description with a single word is more suitable for adjacency than a description with a clause. Since the description may be a single word, a prepositional phrase, or a clause, eloquence requires placing ﴿from those who fear﴾ first.

﴿Said two men﴾: Allah the Exalted did not specify who these two men were, and we have no necessity in knowing their identities. The important thing is what they said. As for knowing who they are: if this were among matters on which belief is based, Allah would have clarified it either in the Qur'an or through the tongue of the Messenger ﷺ.

As for His saying ﴿from those who fear﴾: fear of whom? They fear Allah; therefore we say the object of ﴿yakhafuna﴾ is omitted, its estimate being: Allah.

And His saying ﴿Upon whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾: with what did He bestow favor? Allah bestowed favor upon them in several matters:

First: the fear of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, for fear of Allah is among the greatest blessings, since fear of Allah entails avoiding Allah's prohibitions and performing His obedience.

Second: Allah bestowed upon them strength, strength of soul; for they are now confronting whom? They confront a nation; all of Moses' people said to him: ﴿We will never enter it﴾; these two men faced the whole nation, which indicates courage and sincere resolve. Undoubtedly this is a blessing when Allah grants the servant strength and courage and indifference to numbers, since numbers are nothing in the face of truth.

Allah also bestowed upon them soundness of judgment; for everyone who read the glad tidings that Moses, peace be upon him, mentioned will surely advance: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾ [al-Ma'idah 21], and the second: ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 21]. Yes. So Allah bestowed favor upon them in these three respects, and it may be more than this. He says: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate.﴾

First: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾. What is the meaning of "holy"?

The scholars said: its meaning is purified, purified from polytheism, because this land was the land of the prophets, (...).

Then what is this land? What is intended by it?

The scholars said: it is the land of al-Sham, the land of al-Sham which includes what is called in the present age Syria, Palestine, and the entire region of Jordan and others; all of the land of al-Sham. This is the Holy Land, because it was the land of the prophets, peace be upon them.

* Student: The Exalted's saying: ﴿So today We will save you in your body that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾ [Yunus 92]. Some interpret this verse as referring to the existence of some dead bodies of Pharaoh's family, like those present in Egypt and elsewhere; indeed some say that in some of them is Pharaoh, meaning they claim Pharaoh is in some of them. Is this meaning correct?

* Shaykh: You know that the period is long, and that people create something from nothing. Do you not know that the head of al-Husayn is in Najaf, in Syria, and in Egypt? He has three heads! Exalted is Allah! A man in his life had only one head, and when he died he had three heads! We do not believe such things. The apparent matter to us is that when Pharaoh floated on the surface of the water and the Children of Israel saw him, his affair ended, and the fish devoured him, or we do not know about him. As for saying that what is now found in the pyramids is Pharaoh, we neither affirm nor deny this.

* Student: (...) ﴿that you may be a sign for those who come after him﴾?

* Shaykh: Yes, for those after him. Who is "after him"?

* Student: They say: all people.

* Shaykh: Not at all; we do not care. We believe in the words of Allah whether we see the body or not; our sign is the word of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. But it is a sign that you destroyed the Children of Israel, the one who terrorized them.

* Student: We said: (...) it is the land of al-Sham. Certainly the Children of Israel argue, by our acknowledgment, that this land was originally theirs, since the Children of Israel lived in it. What is the response to this doubt?

* Shaykh: We respond to this doubt by saying: yes, it was written for them in their time, because they were the righteous servants of Allah, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105]. But after they disbelieved and faith in the Ummah of Muhammad came, to whom is it written? To the Ummah of Muhammad. The words of Allah confirm one another.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 5, verses 21–26 (part 2 of 5):**

﴿That the land, My righteous servants shall inherit it.﴾ They, after they disbelieved in Muhammad, are not righteous. We say: Musa was addressing a people in his time who believed in him and affirmed his message. Therefore, when righteousness was lost, and I say this with bitterness, when righteousness was lost in this Ummah, this domination, the domination of the Jews over this part of the land, came about.

* Student: Some have confined the matter of the conflict with the Jews to being a conflict over land, rather than a conflict of creed in this sense?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is from the loss of righteousness. It is obligatory upon us to fight the Jews and others who have disbelieved in Allah, not on the basis of land, but on the basis of creed. For this reason they have become stronger. Therefore, it is necessary to correct the intention and reform the action before anything else. If the intention is corrected and the action is reformed, much good will result.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And when We appointed for Musa forty nights, then you took the calf [as deity] after him while you were wrongdoers. Then We pardoned you after that that you might be grateful. And when We gave Musa the Scripture and the criterion that you might be guided. And when Musa said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf [as deity], so repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator." And He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah outright," and the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on. Then We revived you after your death that you might be grateful. And We shaded you with clouds and sent down upon you manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 51–57].

* Shaykh: Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf"﴾, meaning: Remember, or remember, O Children of Israel, ﴿when Musa said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves."﴾

His words ﴿indeed you have wronged yourselves﴾: The original meaning of *zulm* (wrongdoing) is deficiency. From it is the statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Both gardens brought forth their produce and did not fall short therefrom in anything﴾ [Al-Kahf 33], meaning they did not diminish from it anything. It is applied to transgression and negligence: transgression in violating the prohibitions and negligence in the obligations.

Here He says: ﴿you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf﴾, meaning by your taking the calf as a deity. For this reason we say that ﴿the calf﴾ is the first object, and the second object is omitted, the sense being: by your taking the calf as a deity. It has already been mentioned that this calf was a statue of gold which they had taken from the family of Pharaoh, and then they made it into a statue in the form of a calf which has a lowing sound. The exegetes said: This lowing was only through the wind. They left its back end open, and the wind would pass winding through this hollow, then exit from the mouth, so it had a sound like the lowing of a bull. They said to one another: Musa, peace be upon him, has gone to his god to seek him, and he has delayed in searching for him, because he had gone intending to be absent for thirty days, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, added ten to it: ﴿So the appointment with his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾ [Al-A'raf 142]. This was a wisdom from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and a trial and test. They said: Musa went to seek his god, and this is his god. They say: ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾ [Ta-Ha 88]. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them any speech and does not possess for them any harm or benefit?﴾ [Ta-Ha 89]. They took the calf as deities, wronging themselves thereby, because the self is a trust with you which you must safeguard with due care. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do not kill yourselves﴾, so He made us trustees over ourselves and forbade us from killing the self. He said: ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [At-Tawbah 36], so He forbade us from wronging ourselves. This indicates that our selves are a trust with us, and it is not permissible to neglect this trust. For this reason He said to them: ﴿Indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf, so repent to your Creator﴾. In another reading: ﴿to your Creator (Bari')﴾ [i.e., *Bariykum*].

(*Tubu*) means: return ﴿to your Creator﴾, so they repented. But how was their repentance?

He said: ﴿and kill yourselves.﴾ Kill yourselves. This is the way of their repentance. They said: Allah cast darkness upon them, and they were gathered in one place, and each one of them was given a dagger, and it was said to them: Kill whoever is in front of you. So they killed themselves. The meaning is not that He called them to suicide, that each one kills himself. No, each one kills his brother. You know that one tribe is considered as one soul. ﴿And kill yourselves﴾, and they did.

Musa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿That is best for you in the sight of your Creator.﴾ ﴿That﴾ refers to repentance in this manner. ﴿Best for you in the sight of your Creator﴾, meaning in the sight of your Creator, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And He accepted your repentance﴾: meaning when you repented, He accepted your repentance, even though their sin was great. But Allah, the Exalted, accepts the repentance of whoever repents. ﴿And He accepted your repentance﴾, meaning He removed from you the sin and the punishment.

﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ This sentence is a justification for the preceding ruling, which is His statement ﴿He accepted your repentance﴾. *At-Tawwab* is an intensive form (plural of *ta'ib*, "one who repents"). Allah's acceptance of repentance from a servant is divided into two parts. The first part: His enabling him to repent. The second part: His accepting the repentance. As for the first, which is His enabling him to repent, it is the statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until, when the earth closed in on them despite its vastness and their souls confined them and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him, then He turned to them that they might repent﴾ [At-Tawbah 118]. That is, He enabled them to repent so that they would repent. As for the second, which is accepting repentance, it is in His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [Ash-Shura 25]. So Allah's acceptance of repentance is of two kinds, as you have heard.

﴿Ar-Rahim (the Merciful)﴾ means: possessor of mercy. The mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted, is vast, encompassing the believer and the disbeliever. This is the general mercy. As for the specific mercy, it is for the believers, as He said: ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾ [Al-Ahzab 43]. *Ar-Rahim* has come in this form, and in the form *Ar-Rahman* which indicates vastness and greatness, and in the verbal form, as He said: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 21].

* In this verse there are benefits, among them: the demonstration of the sincere advice of Musa, peace be upon him, to his people, in that he made clear to them the sin and urged them to repent from it. He said: ﴿Indeed you have wronged yourselves﴾, and he said: ﴿so repent﴾.

* And among them: that a person's disobedience is a wronging of himself. On this basis, this contains a refutation of the statement of the Mu'tazilah, the Qadariyyah, because when they say that a person is independent in his action, we say: then a person would be a wrongdoer toward himself when he commits sins.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon a person to treat himself with justice just as he treats others with justice. Because of His statement: ﴿you have wronged yourselves﴾, just as we are forbidden from wronging people, we are forbidden from wronging ourselves.

Can we derive from it that it is not permissible for a person to donate any of his organs to another? Yes, we can, because if he donates some of his organs, he is wronging himself. If it is after his death, this is a violation of his sanctity after death. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Breaking the bone of the dead is like breaking it while alive."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3207) and Ibn Majah (1616) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] If it is during his life, it is a wronging of himself by losing this organ which he donated. Let us say it is one of the two kidneys. In this there is undoubtedly a wronging of himself, because Allah did not create them in vain. Rather, they cooperate in purifying the nourishment which permeates the veins and the body. If one of them is lost, the work falls upon the one remaining, and it is close to becoming fatigued, weary, and damaged. It cannot be said that it stands in place of two, just as the eye stands in place of two eyes, because there is a difference between the function of the kidneys and the function of the eyes. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: If a person injures the eye of one who has only one eye and it is lost, he must pay the full blood-money, because the loss of it removes his sight, unlike the kidney.

* So from this noble verse we may take: it is prohibited for a person to donate any of his organs, because the remaining organ will remain in severe hardship. Then we say: Suppose he has performed the function, but if illness befalls him, there is nothing to take its place, and he perishes. As for the matter that this is from the category of assistance and compassion and the like, meaning compassion toward the patient, it is said: But your own self has the greater right, begin with yourself, then with those you support. Here there is no room for another.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of repentance, because of His statement: ﴿so repent to your Creator﴾. Repentance is the return of a person from disobedience of Allah to obedience of Allah. It has conditions:
The first condition: sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
The second: remorse over the sin that has occurred.
The third: ceasing from it immediately.
The fourth: resolve not to return to it.
The fifth: that the repentance occurs at a time when repentance is accepted.

These are five conditions.

First: sincerity. Its evidence is the statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar 2]. Repentance is a form of worship. And His statement in the Hadith Qudsi: "Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association."[[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

The second condition: remorse over what has occurred, and that he wishes with all his heart that it had not happened. Because if he does not feel remorse, repentance cannot be realized. That is, if it is the same to him whether he did it or did not do it, then where is the repentance? Remorse is necessary. A speaker may say: Remorse is an emotional response, so how can a person manufacture an emotional response? We say: He manufactures it by grieving and wishing he had not done it.

The third: ceasing from the sin immediately. Because how can a person repent from something he is engaged in? This is a rational proof. Its impossibility is rational, and its impossibility is legal as well. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and they do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ [Ali 'Imran 135]. Among this: if the wrong is against a human being, it is necessary to be free from this right, either by delivering it to him or by seeking his pardon. For example, if a person stole money from someone and then repented to Allah, what should he do? His repentance is not complete until he returns the stolen property to its owner. It is necessary. Otherwise, he is lying. If he cannot find its owner and despairs of his existence or the existence of his heirs, then let him give it in charity on the owner's behalf, and Allah knows that.

The fourth condition: resolve not to return. That is, he resolves within himself that he will never return to this sin. Because if he repents while speaking to himself that he may return to it, he is not truly repentant. The condition here is resolve not to return, or the condition is not to return? The resolve not to return. Based on this, we say: If he returns after resolving not to return, does the repentance become void? No. The first repentance is not invalidated, but he must renew his repentance for the new sin.

The fifth: that it be at a time when repentance is accepted. If repentance occurs at a time when repentance is not accepted, it does not benefit him. This is of two kinds: a specific time and a general time. The specific time is the arrival of one's appointed term. If a person's appointed term arrives, repentance does not benefit him, because of the statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"﴾ [An-Nisa' 18]. These have no repentance. Allah, the Exalted, has explained the occurrence of this in practice in the story of Pharaoh: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾ [Yunus 90]. It was said to him: ﴿Now?﴾ [Yunus 91], meaning: Now you repent? ﴿And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus 91]. As for the general time, it is the rising of the sun from its west. The sun, as you know, travels from its east to its west. When Allah permits the annihilation of the world, the sun will return from its west. When people see it, they will all believe, but at that time ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or had not earned through its faith some good﴾ [Al-An'am 158].

If these are the conditions, this indicates the obligation of hastening to repentance, because a person does not know when death will overtake him. So let him hasten to repent to Allah regarding the right of Allah, and hasten to repent regarding the rights of the servants by discharging the rights to their people. For this reason the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, said: "Procrastination by the wealthy is injustice."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2287) and Muslim (1564/33) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that repentance is accepted even from shirk, because of His statement: ﴿repent to your Creator﴾. And it is so: Allah accepts repentance even from shirk.

* And among its benefits: that a person may become better after repentance than he was before it, because of His statement: ﴿That is best for you in the sight of your Creator.﴾

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the requirements of the Names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what the scholars call (the ruling or effect that follows from the Name), from His statement: ﴿So He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

So His acceptance of their repentance is a requirement of His Name *At-Tawwab*. It is known that the Most Beautiful Names of Allah are not affirmed in faith except with three conditions for transitive names, and two conditions for intransitive names. For example, *Al-Hayy* (the Living): faith in it is not complete unless you believe that Allah is the Living and that He has life. But if the Name is transitive, it is necessary to affirm the Name, affirm the attribute, and affirm what this Name transitively affects, which is the effect or ruling. (*Ar-Rahim*): is it transitive or intransitive? Transitive, because you say: "Allah had mercy on so-and-so." So you must believe in *Ar-Rahim* as a Name of Allah, and in the mercy it indicates. The third: and that He, the Exalted, shows this mercy to whomever He wills. These principles are well known among the people of knowledge, in contrast to the people of innovation who said: The Names of Allah may be separated from their attributes, so they say: He is All-Hearing without hearing, and All-Knowing without knowledge. Is this rational?! All languages of the world do not allow anything but that the derived word indicates its root of derivation. It is impossible to describe the blind as seeing, nor the deaf as hearing, nor the mute as speaking. This is impossible in all the languages of the world.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsir al-Qurʾan al-Karim) on Surah 5, verses 21–26 (part 3 of 5):**

* **Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ (22) ﴿Said two men from among those who feared [Allah], upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, "Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers."﴾ (23) ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here."﴾ (24) ﴿[Moses] said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people."﴾ (25) ﴿[Allah] said, "Indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people."﴾ (26) [Al-Ma'idah 22–26].

* **The Shaykh:** Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Said two men from among those who feared [Allah], upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, "Enter upon them through the gate"﴾, and so on to the end. In this noble verse [there is a lesson] that Allah, exalted is He, may bestow His favour upon some people and open for them [doors of success] that He has not opened for anyone else.

﴿Said two men from among those who feared﴾: Allah left the two men unnamed. This is because identifying the two men by name is not necessary for understanding the matter or grasping the circumstances. For this reason, many verses and many hadiths do not specify the particular individual, since the intended purpose is to understand the matter.

As for His saying: ﴿from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾: we have mentioned that the object of ﴿feared﴾ is omitted, and the implied meaning is "feared Allah." We have also mentioned that ﴿upon whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ is a descriptive clause (ṣifah) for ﴿two men﴾, and it may also be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). If it is a circumstantial clause, then there is no difficulty, because although a ḥāl describes its referent, it differs from it in grammatical case (iʿrāb). A ṣifah (adjective), by contrast, is a descriptive that follows its referent in iʿrāb. For this reason, ﴿from among those who feared﴾ was placed before ﴿upon whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾. If it is treated as another descriptive, then it has been placed after ﴿from among those who feared﴾, because a descriptive consisting of a prepositional phrase (shibh al-jumlah) is more closely attached to the described noun than a full clause (jumlah). This is because we have three possibilities: either the described noun is qualified by something that agrees with it in number (singular/dual/plural), or it is qualified by a prepositional phrase, or it is qualified by a full clause. Which of these is closer: the prepositional phrase or the full clause? The prepositional phrase.

As for His saying: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾: that is, proceed toward them and do not let them know that you are on your way. Come upon them suddenly.

﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾ [means] without any prior knowledge on their part, because no people have ever been fought in their own homeland except that they were humiliated. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to fight the people of Makkah and conquer Makkah, he asked his Lord, exalted is He, to conceal the news about them so that he could surprise them in their own dwellings.[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/233) from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah.]] Do you understand? For this reason they said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾, that is: do not warn them, and do not inform them that you are coming upon them.

The word ﴿the gate﴾ contains the definite article (al), and this (al) here indicates a known reference (al-ʿahd). Which reference? The mental (known) reference (al-ʿahd al-dhihnī), that is, the gate of the city.

﴿And when you have entered it, you will be victorious﴾: that is, when you enter the gate, you will be victorious, and they will not defeat you. Victory will be yours. This is guidance and direction.

﴿And upon Allah rely﴾: when these two men commanded these people to take the beneficial means, they guided them not to depend on themselves but to rely upon Allah. So He said: ﴿And upon Allah rely﴾. The prepositional phrase in His saying ﴿and upon Allah﴾ is connected to ﴿rely﴾, and the fāʾ in ﴿fa-tawakkalū﴾ is an added particle for the beauty of the expression. For this reason, if it were said "wa-ʿalā Allāhi tawakkalū," it would be correct. We cannot take the fāʾ here as a conjunction, because if we did, and the wāw were also a conjunction, the sentence would not be sound. Rather, it is said that it was added for the beauty of the expression. As for His saying: ﴿fa-tawakkalū﴾, what is tawakkul (reliance)?

Tawakkul: the scholars said it is sincere dependence upon Allah, that is, that a person depends upon his Lord with sincere dependence, along with trust in Him, good opinion of Him, and taking the means. There are four attributes: sincere dependence upon Allah; second, along with trust in Him; third, and good opinion of Him; and fourth, taking the means. When these four attributes come together, this is the reality of tawakkul. Whoever depends upon Allah but is in doubt is not truly a person of tawakkul. Likewise, if he depends upon Allah but does not have that full trust, either because of what he knows of his own sins, or because of what he knows of the insufficiency of the means, or for some other reason, then he has not realized tawakkul. The third is good opinion: good opinion in tawakkul is that a person thinks well of his Lord, blessed and exalted, that He is sufficient for him, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [At-Talaq 3]. As for His saying "with taking the means": this is indispensable, because Allah, exalted is He, decrees a thing through its cause, and this is part of the completeness of His wisdom. Look at His saying: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you, so walk through its slopes and eat of His provision﴾ [Al-Mulk 15]. So striving is necessary. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek of Allah's bounty﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah 10]. So taking the means is necessary, but on the condition that the means be lawful (sharʿī), either explicitly mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah, or known through experience that is witnessed by the decree (qadar).

He says: ﴿And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾: this is a condition for the sincerity of reliance upon Allah, mighty and majestic is He, since no one relies upon Allah with complete reliance except one who has faith in what Allah has promised in His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾, and ﴿so rely, if you are believers﴾. After this counsel and this good, beneficial direction, look at the reply: ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it"﴾, ﴿indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it﴾. And is this negation a negation of their lawful action, or a negation of Allah's decreed action? The first, the first: that is, they cannot enter it while [the tyrants] are in it, and when they leave, they will enter. Is this a statement?!

It is well known that if you find a village that is empty with no one in it, and you wish to enter, you will surely enter. But this is the mentality of the Children of Israel: ﴿we will never enter it as long as they remain in it﴾.

﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight﴾: they say to Moses, "Go, you and your Lord." Who is his Lord? Some exegetes said: his Lord is Aaron. They meant Aaron, because the word "lord" (rabb) is applied to a master, and Aaron was older than Moses, and the elder of two brothers is the master of the younger. But this is far-fetched. The apparent meaning is that they meant the Lord of the worlds, mighty and majestic is He, because Moses was calling them to Allah and to their Lord, blessed and exalted is He. So it is as if, out of their arrogance, pride and insolence, they were saying: since you have a Lord, ﴿go, you and your Lord, and fight﴾. They wanted Allah to enter the battlefield, may Allah curse them, and fight alongside whom? Alongside Moses. ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight﴾. And despite that, ﴿indeed we are sitting right here﴾.

﴿Here﴾: in a nearby place, because (hunā) is for what is near, and (hunālika) is for what is far. [They mean]: here in our place we will not go beyond it. We will remain spectators watching you and your Lord.

﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight, indeed we are sitting right here.﴾ There is no hiding the arrogance, haughtiness, pride and rudeness in this speech, we seek refuge in Allah. So what did Moses say?

He said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother﴾. ﴿My Lord﴾: to whom is he speaking? He is speaking to his Lord, the Lord of the worlds. ﴿Indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother﴾: that is, I do not control any matter except my own matter and the matter of my brother. By "my brother" he means Aaron.

﴿So part us from the defiantly disobedient people﴾: he asked Allah, exalted is He, to separate him from the defiantly disobedient people, so that he and his brother would be on one side and the defiant transgressors on another side. So what was Allah's response? Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, it is forbidden to them﴾, that is, to the Children of Israel who were commanded to fight. ﴿It is forbidden to them﴾: is this a legislative prohibition or a decreed prohibition? A decreed prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿And We had already forbidden to him the wet nurses﴾ [Al-Qasas 12]. That is, prohibition may be legislative, like ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3], and it may be decreed, as in His saying: ﴿And We had already forbidden to him the wet nurses﴾, meaning a decreed prohibition. And here also, ﴿it is forbidden to them﴾ means a decreed prohibition.

﴿For forty years﴾: is the ﴿year﴾ (sanah) solar or lunar? Lunar, because timekeeping by the moon is what Allah said: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say, "They are measures of time for the people and for the Hajj"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 189]. Until a not-so-distant era, timekeeping was by the moon. Even when the Jews fasted the day of ʿAshura, the Messenger (ﷺ) fasted it and said: "We have more right to Moses than they do."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3943) and Muslim (1130/127) from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas, and its wording is: "We have more right to Moses than you."]]

﴿For forty years they will wander in the land﴾: that is, they will be lost. Subhan Allah, how far is the distance between Egypt and the land of Sham? How much do you estimate? About a month. They remained for forty years without finding the way. Not a year or two, but forty years in this small area of land. This is because Allah blinded them. He blinded them, so they were deprived of this good, which is entering the Holy Land. They were deprived of it because of this obstinacy and this defiance. ﴿They will wander in the land﴾: they will not find the right path. But why was the wandering specified as forty years? We have two answers:

The first answer: such decreed or legislated matters that are fixed by a specific number cannot be fully understood by a person in terms of their wisdom, because there is no room for the intellect in them. Much of this has already passed before us: that what is fixed by law or by decree has no room for the intellect, except for a few minor matters within the decreed affairs.

The second answer, or second aspect: some scholars said that they were lost for forty years, and forty years is a long period in which a new generation can grow up unlike those obstinate people. From a theoretical standpoint this is not far-fetched. But it may be objected: is this period sufficient? The answer: yes, it is sufficient. Peoples can change when the motivation is strong and the obstacles are weak. They can transform into new customs and character within how long? Less than forty years, depending on the strength of the motive and the weakness of the obstacle. They can transform into customs and character in such a period or less.

﴿So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people﴾: ﴿do not grieve﴾ (lā taʾsa) means do not be sad, as He said: ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you﴾ [Al-Hadid 23], that is, do not be sad. So do not grieve over the defiant transgressors for what Allah has punished them with, because they deserve this punishment.

* **And in the verses there are benefits:**

* Among the benefits of these verses, first: His saying about Moses: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾.

* In it there are benefits, among them: the virtue of the land of Sham, from His saying ﴿the Holy﴾. It has already been explained that the meaning of "holy" (muqaddasah) is purified from idols and polytheism, because it is the land of the prophets. The virtue of this land is shown by the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Exalted is He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ [Al-Isra 1]. This too is part of its sanctification.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that Allah prescribed the land of Sham for the Children of Israel, from His saying: ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾.

* And among its benefits: that the caller to Allah should mention what stirs souls and draws them toward acceptance, because here He mentioned that the land is holy, and that Allah prescribed it for them. The third: His saying ﴿enter the land﴾, and it seems this is good news that they would be victorious and would enter the land. So there is good news here from three angles. What are they? His saying ﴿enter﴾; the second ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾; and the third ﴿the holy﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: writing (kitābah) is of two types: legislative and decreed. The verse refers to decreed writing, and decreed writing is usually connected with the preposition "lām," while legislative writing is usually connected with "ʿalā." This is generally the case, not always, as shown by His saying: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾ [Al-Hashr 3]. Is the writing here decreed or legislative? Decreed. There is no difficulty: Allah did not impose exile upon them as a legislative obligation, but as a decreed one. But the general rule is that the decreed is with "lām" and the legislative is with "ʿalā."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Children of Israel had more right to the land of Sham than others, from His saying: ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾. What do you say? We say: they had more right to it, and it was written for them while they were believers. It was written for them not because they were from the Children of Israel, but because they were believers. There is no doubt that in the time of Moses they were the best people on earth. Allah said: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms, after the reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [Al-Anbiya 105]. So the statement of the Children of Israel that this is the land of promise, we say: "If Allah wills, it is a land of promise for your destruction." As for it being a land prescribed for you legislatively or by decree, no. By decree, it is possible; but legislatively, they have no right to it at all: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants﴾ [Al-Aʿraf 128]. Just as Allah gave the Children of Israel the lands of Pharaoh and his realm, because they were Muslims, so likewise the Muslims who believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) inherit from the Children of Israel.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: matters are not accomplished except by the presence of benefits and the absence of harms, from His saying: ﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾. For this reason, you find that the Shariʿah consists of commands and prohibitions, because worship is not complete unless a person compels himself to perform acts of obedience and to refrain from sins and prohibited things. So you find that the Shariʿah contains both action and abstention, so that the test and examination may be complete. Let me give you an example with fasting: what does it contain? Abstention from what is beloved. In zakat: giving away what is beloved. And this is what completes the examination.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: disbelief is apostasy (riddah), an apostasy from uprightness, from His saying: ﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾. So is the apostate now behind or ahead? Behind. If we say this, then faith becomes progress. For this reason, we say to those people who want the Islamic nation to go back, which they consider progress, that you are mistaken. They see the return of people to the era of the pious predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ) as backwardness, and we say to them: opposing the path of the pious predecessors is what is backwardness, because in the Qur'an it is called riddah or irtidad ʿalā al-dubur (turning back on one's heels). But agreeing with the pious predecessors is truly progress, though it requires resolve, strength, and implementation.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verses 21–26 (part 4 of 5):**

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: turning back on one's heels is a cause of loss. What loss is meant? The loss of both this world and the Hereafter. Allah says: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."﴾ [az-Zumar 15]. I said that turning back on one's heels causes loss because the *fa'* (فاء) in His words ﴿then you would turn back⌋ (فَتَنْقَلِبُوا)﴾ is the *fa' al-sababiyyah* (فاء السببية), the "fa'" of causation (the fa' that marks a result). This is why the verb after it is in the subjunctive, because it follows a prohibition: ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, lest you turn back as losers.﴾
* Another lesson from this noble verse: the one who calls to Allah should mention the consequences of sins in order to deter souls. It is true that calling to Allah is achieved by saying, "This is forbidden, this is permitted, this is obligatory." But when one mentions both encouragement and warning, this stirs souls to comply. Here Musa said to his people: ﴿then you would turn back as losers.﴾
* Another lesson from this noble verse: mentioning worldly punishment in order to deter people from sins does not contradict sincerity (*ikhlas*, إخلاص). Pay attention, is that right? Mentioning the bad consequences in this world in order to deter people from disobedience does not contradict sincerity. This is why the messengers used to say this, warning their peoples. Likewise, mentioning the good consequences in order to urge people to perform acts of obedience does not contradict sincerity. Have you not seen that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded for him and his lifespan be extended, let him maintain his ties of kinship"? [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5986) and Muslim (2557/21), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Is this not a worldly matter? It is worldly, yet the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned it as a means to an act of obedience, which is maintaining the ties of kinship. The saying of some people, that sincerity in reality means that you worship Allah for Allah's sake and not for the reward from Allah, is a mistake that contradicts the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ). Read the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval.﴾ [al-Fath 29]. They seek bounty and approval. But the saying you referred to is the saying of some Sufis (الصوفية), who say that if you consider the reward, you have associated partners with Allah in worship. We ask Allah for well-being. Allah the Mighty and Majestic guides us to this, and shows that this is the path of the Messenger and his Companions. And you say that this is shirk?! It is true that whoever desires the world with an act of the Hereafter has some kind of shirk. But if he makes his share of the world a help for him in obeying Allah, then there is no shirk in it at all. Look at the grave sins: does adultery, for example, have a punishment or not? It has a punishment. Why the punishment? So that it deters people from it, so that people refrain from it, and fear that if they commit adultery they will be flogged or stoned. The cutting off of the hand for theft is the same: so that people fear theft and do not approach it. One should not say, "The faith-based restraint is enough." We should not say this, because if we said the faith-based restraint is enough, we would have to suspend all the prescribed punishments (*hudud*, حدود). Rather we say: the faith-based restraint is undoubtedly the foundation, but the restraint of the ruler (*al-radi' al-sultani*, الرادع السلطاني) supports or strengthens this foundation, and there is no harm in it.

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants."﴾

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, I think, and Allah knows best, it is taken into account based on the majority.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, that is not valid, because how could ﴿two men﴾ be said in addressing Musa's people? The two men are other than the one calling. If we said it refers to Musa and Harun, the meaning would be corrupted.
* Student: (...) seeking immediate reward through righteous deeds. Does (...) the feeling of ease (*inshirah*, انشراح) count as one of the righteous deeds?
* Shaykh: This is from the immediate reward. That is, it is one of Allah's blessings upon the servant that he finds ease in worship, and this is from the immediate reward, and one of the early glad tidings for the believer. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease.﴾ [al-Layl 5–7].
* Student: (...) In worship a person finds more ease than in seeking knowledge (...)?
* Shaykh: The reason for that is that our sincerity in seeking knowledge has some blemish in it. Otherwise, if we felt now that we were seeking knowledge while striving in the way of Allah, our hearts would become far more open. But unfortunately many students of knowledge intend by knowledge, or by seeking knowledge, only to broaden their knowledge, and this is without doubt a deficiency. I say: the student of knowledge should intend by seeking knowledge to support this religion and to protect it from its enemies, and by this the heart is opened, by this the heart is opened. For this reason, you will find that when a person observes this intention, when he understands a matter of knowledge he sees it as a treasure, a pearl of the diver, which he could never give up at all.
* Student: Regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ to the end of the verses, which indicate the sanctity and holiness of the land of al-Sham (the Levant), may we say, may Allah pardon you: the further we move from al-Masjid al-Aqsa and the land of al-Masjid al-Aqsa, the less sanctity there is?
* Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt, but as we move away, the sanctity recedes. We cannot say this. Rather we say: if we leave it, the sanctity recedes. But this was in the time of Musa. In the time of Muhammad (ﷺ), there is no doubt that al-Masjid al-Haram is holier, and al-Masjid al-Nabawi is holier.

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And [mention] when Musa said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings and gave you that which He had not given anyone among the worlds. O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back on your heels, for you would turn back as losers." They said, "O Musa, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 20–22].

* Among the lessons of this verse: the coarseness of the Children of Israel. Musa addressed them with ﴿O my people﴾ in this gentle manner, while they said, ﴿O Musa.﴾ They did not say, "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah." This is from their coarseness and the harshness of their natures.
* Another lesson from this noble verse: the bad opinion of the Children of Israel about Allah. Their prophet (ﷺ) had promised them that Allah had assigned the Holy Land to them, but they relied on material matters and said, ﴿Indeed, there are in it a people of tyrants﴾, which shows their bad opinion of their Lord, glorified and exalted be He.
* Among its lessons: the cowardice of the Children of Israel. ﴿We will never enter it until they leave it.﴾ This is the utmost of cowardice. For who would say, "I will not enter the town, village or city if its people have left it"? A coward. So they said, ﴿We will never enter it until they leave it﴾, and this is evidence of the utmost cowardice among them.
* Among its lessons: the emphasis on their cowardice a second time: ﴿So if they leave it, then we will enter.﴾
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: among a people who are arrogant and opposing there may be someone with good, righteousness and reform, as in His words: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, said.﴾
* Also in ﴿So if they leave it, then we will enter﴾ there is emphasis on their entering if these tyrannical people leave it: ﴿then we will enter.﴾ This does not need emphasis, but it shows their foolishness, because every person knows that once the land is empty of its enemy and they have left it, entering it does not need emphasis. Who would deny that a person may enter when his enemy's land is empty of him?

So we take the lesson we mentioned: Allah the Exalted may place among the stubborn and opposing people someone with good, righteousness and reform, from His words: ﴿two men from among those who feared﴾.

* And among its lessons, meaning His words, ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, said﴾: fear of Allah is something that moves the servant to obey Allah, because He said ﴿who feared﴾. Without doubt fear moves one to obedience, just as hope also moves one to obedience. But generally fear leads to avoiding what is prohibited, and hope leads to complying with commands through acts of obedience.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: fear of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is one of the blessings. Without doubt, it is one of Allah's blessings upon the servant that Allah bestows on him the fear of Him, from His words: ﴿upon whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾.
* Among the lessons of this verse: when one wishes to raid a land, he should conceal news from its people. This is from the words of these two sincere advisers: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾, meaning that they will not know about you until you enter the gate. We have mentioned a witness for this in the conquest of Makkah, where the Prophet (ﷺ) asked Allah to conceal the news from the Quraysh until he could surprise them in their land. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/233), from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah.]]
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: whoever is attacked in the very heart of his home is humiliated. This is a well-known proverb: "No people were ever attacked in the heart of their homes except that they were humiliated." This is derived from His words: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious,﴾ and the people of the town are overcome.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: entering a town is not done by scaling its walls, but through its gate. For this reason, when the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, besieged the garden of Musaylimah the Liar, they did not climb the wall, but opened the gate and then entered. Al-Bara' ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, was famous for his bravery and strength, and he asked them to throw him over the wall so that he could open the gate for them. They did so, and he entered and opened the gate for them. He opened the gate for them, the people entered this garden, and victory was achieved. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/44), from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Sirin. The story is in Usd al-Ghabah (1/363) and al-Isabah (1/280).]]
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: trust in Allah (*tawakkul*, توكل) is one of the causes of victory, as stated by these two men: ﴿And upon Allah rely, if you are believers.﴾
* Among its lessons: a person should not rely on himself or on the sensory cause. This is from His words, after He directed them to enter through the gate: ﴿And upon Allah rely.﴾ The meaning derived from this verse is supported by the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not become incapable." [[Narrated by Muslim (2664/34), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] "Be eager for what benefits you": this is by doing what you are able to do of the means. "Seek help from Allah": that is, do not rely on yourself; ask Allah the Mighty and Majestic for help until the aim is achieved.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: it is obligatory to single out Allah the Exalted alone for trust, from His words: ﴿And upon Allah rely﴾. This requires explanation. Absolute trust, in which the one who trusts entrusts his affair completely to the one he trusts, is not permissible except toward Allah. The one who relies on Allah in this sense feels his need and dependence upon Allah the Mighty and Majestic. As for reliance (*i'timad*, اعتماد) in a partial sense, where the one relying does not feel that he has entrusted his affair entirely to that person, and that he (the one relied upon) is the one who can fulfill his need, there is no harm in this. For this reason the Sunnah came with permission to appoint another as an agent and to depend on him in what he is appointed for. For example, you say, "O so-and-so, buy such-and-such for me." You are now relying on him, but is this a reliance of need or a reliance of assistance? The second, assistance. You now feel that you are not in need of this man; if you wished, you could dismiss him. Nor can he necessarily achieve your aim: he may fall ill, or be prevented, and so on. But the servant's trust in Allah the Mighty and Majestic (and I ask Allah to make me and you among those who rely on Him) makes a person feel that he is in need of Allah, and that he has entrusted his affair to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore we cannot say that trust in other than Allah is shirk, because, as I told you, the great difference between this and that is clear. But a person may rely and depend upon someone who supports him financially, for example: a son relies on his father for his livelihood. Here the matter is very subtle. Likewise an employee relies on his job. This is a subtle matter: if you make yourself feel that this is a mere cause, and that the one who made it a cause is Allah, and that Allah is able to prevent the effect of this cause, and you place the whole matter with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, then this does not contradict trust, neither its root nor its perfection. But if you rely on it and attach your heart to it, this is without doubt a kind of shirk, if you forget Allah entirely, and Allah forbid, and you make this the one that brings matters to you by itself; this is major shirk, or else minor. Among this is what often happens to the sick, who rely entirely on the doctor, to the extent that he feels that the cure came from him. This is a great danger. But if you rely on the doctor as a cause, while the one who causes is Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and if Allah decrees healing for you, it is He who heals you; otherwise the doctor will not benefit you. The most that can be said is that I go to the doctor as I light a fire to cook my food, for example. This is not objectionable, and there must be some attachment in the heart to whoever benefits him, but we must make the first and last of all things Allah the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: singling out Allah for trust is part of faith, from His words: ﴿if you are believers﴾. And deficiency in trust in Allah is a deficiency in faith, because whatever is contingent upon something increases with its increase and decreases with its decrease.

Then He the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it [while they are in it]..."﴾ to the end of the verse.

In this verse there is what we mentioned in the previous verse: the coarseness of the Children of Israel, as they address their prophet by his personal name without describing him by his messengership and prophethood.

* Among its lessons: the persistence of the Children of Israel in disobedience, and in cowardice and weakness, from their words: ﴿We will never enter it, ever, as long as they are within it.﴾ It is clear that they insisted on disobeying their prophet, who had said: ﴿Enter the Holy Land.﴾
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the great arrogance of the Children of Israel, when they said to Musa (ﷺ): ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾ Even the imperative "go" (*idhhab*, اذهب) in this form is as if they were commanding Musa, in haughtiness and pride: ﴿Go, you and your Lord.﴾ That is, they did not hope for it as a request. They did not say, "Would you not go, O Messenger of Allah, or O Prophet of Allah," or something similar. ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight.﴾ Then there is a third aspect of arrogance: ﴿Indeed, we are sitting here﴾, meaning we will not move, nor will we go with you. They did not say, for example, "We will be a support for you, protecting your back," or something similar. So in this too is the complete arrogance of the Children of Israel.

Then Allah the Exalted said about Musa: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother."﴾

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Musa (ﷺ) despaired of the Children of Israel when they showed this stubbornness and expressed themselves in this manner. This is from His words: ﴿Indeed, I do not possess except myself and my brother.﴾ Compare them, that is, the Children of Israel, with the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who hastened to obey his command and raced to it. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2731), from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah.]] You will find the great difference between this Ummah, praise be to Allah, and the previous nations.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Musa (peace be upon him) had authority over Harun. He says: ﴿My Lord, I have power over none but myself and my brother﴾. As for whether he was older than Harun or Musa was older, that requires a sound proof. But Musa (peace be upon him) had command over Harun.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to ask his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to separate him from the people of wickedness and immorality, based on His words: ﴿So make a separation between us and the defiantly disobedient people﴾. Can it be derived from this, or does it follow from this benefit, that it is permissible to shun sinners? Shunning is a form of separation, so it may be derived from it. But we say: the Sunnah indicates that shunning is to be done if it serves a benefit, and otherwise not.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: abandoning jihad in the way of Allah is a form of wickedness, based on His words: ﴿So make a separation between us and the defiantly disobedient people﴾.
Should we say: among its benefits is taking the majority view, since among the Children of Israel, the people of Musa, there were those who were upon the truth, namely the two men who said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾? Are they two wicked men?
No. But by considering the majority, it is correct to describe the people generally as wicked. It may also be said that ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾ here is a general term intended to refer to a specific group, and that Musa (peace be upon him) never at all had in mind that the two men would enter. On this basis, the description here applies specifically to those who said: ﴿We will never enter it as long as they are in it﴾.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is forbidden for them﴾ until the end of the verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the answering of supplication, based on His words: ﴿He said: It is forbidden for them﴾. Allah's answering of supplication includes several attributes: among them responsiveness, among them knowledge, among them hearing, among them power. All of these are established by the answering, because if He did not hear, He would not respond; if He did not know what the supplicant wants, He would not respond; if He were not able, He would not respond either.

* Among its benefits: prohibition may be applied to decreed prevention (al-man' al-qadari). This is based on His words: ﴿He said: It is forbidden for them for forty years﴾. We know that Allah the Exalted did not mean that Allah prohibited them from entering it by legislation (shar'an), but by decree (qadaran). And so it is: prohibition may be cosmic (kawniyy) and it may be legislative (shar'iyy). We have given examples for this during the explanation of the verse. From cosmic, decreed prohibition is His words about Musa: ﴿And We had prohibited the wet-nurses to him before﴾. Is this a legislative or a decreed prohibition? It is decreed. And from legislative prohibition is His words: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion and blood﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], and His words: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾ [al-An'am 146].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it guides a person not to grieve over the wicked. For when he exerts his effort in what is required of da'wah (calling to Islam), guidance of creation is not his to give; it belongs to Allah. So he should not grieve. This is why Allah said: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people﴾. And He said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 3]. And He said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow﴾ [al-Kahf 6]. The verses on this are many. So when a person exerts his effort to the extent of his ability, he should not grieve, and he should not occupy himself with the faults of others rather than his own faults. And he should not despair over the defiantly disobedient people. Many people have zeal, and you find them occupied with the sins and faults of others and forgetting themselves. This is a mistake. The most important thing is yourself: correct yourself, then strive to reform others. Here the matter ends. And He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾ [al-Ma'idah 27].

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, it has come from the early generations (as-salaf), may Allah have mercy on them, that they used to shun the people of bid'ah (innovation in religion). But, based on the principle that shunning is subject to a benefit: we have seen a person of bid'ah, a person tried with him but (...) this innovation, and he sees that if he shuns him, (...) nothing. Rather perhaps this continues for them, meaning you are prevented from them and you cannot call them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because this person of bid'ah (...). Is it better, O Shaykh, that a person go along with them while calling them to the straight and correct path?
* The Shaykh: This is what we see: if shunning a sinner or an innovator only increases the matter in severity, then why did you shun him? For reform, and so that he would refrain. If he does not refrain, perhaps he will increase in evil. We also give an example of a person of sins: if you saw a man shaving his beard and you shunned him, would he cease from that? If he would cease, then there is no harm; so shun him. But if he does not cease, and rather increases in resentment towards you and towards what you call to of truth, and it will continue, then what is the benefit?! Furthermore, we have the authentic hadith: «It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6065), and Muslim (2558/23), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]], and this is Muslim's wording.
* Student: O Shaykh, what made the early generations (as-salaf) incline toward (...) in their reform?
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt: for their reform, or out of fear that people would be deceived by them.
* The Student: Alright, does this happen, that people are deceived by them?
* The Shaykh: How would they be deceived when you openly declare that he is in error?
* The Student: No (...) in error openly (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) In any case, if you specify them by their persons, that is correct. But if you say: "Some people say such-and-such," or "It is said such-and-such," they do not become averse.
* Student: May Allah bless you. What is the ruling on describing Musa (peace be upon him) with zealotry (al-'asabiyyah) because of these positions? First: his anger and throwing down the tablets; his rebuking of Harun before asking him, and seizing him by his beard; his killing of the Pharaonic man; his hastiness in asking about the story of al-Khidr; and his choosing of the lesser outcome, when he said to him: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this, then do not accompany me﴾ [al-Kahf 76]? So what is the ruling on describing Musa (peace be upon him) with zealotry because of these...?
* The Shaykh: We say to the one who described him with zealotry: Are you merely reporting a piece of news? Do not present the matter in this description. Rather say: Musa (peace be upon him) had zeal and had strength, and what is similar to that, of descriptions that you make praise, not disparagement. As for if you wish to disparage him, then disparaging him is disbelief, disbelief that removes one from the religion. For example, say: Musa (peace be upon him) is well known for being strong and forceful. This is why, when the Angel of Death came to take his soul, he slapped him until he gouged out his eye[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1339), and Muslim (2372/157), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. He is known for severity. But as for saying that he is known for foolishness and hastiness and what is similar to that, that is not permissible at all. Furthermore, he has great good deeds that overwhelm such things, and a severe person may sometimes do such a thing.
* Student: (...) a critic of Musa, or should we look at his intention...?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, we see that he did act impolitely, without doubt, right away. As for whether it is disparaging or not, Allah knows his intention. But there is no doubt that he acted impolitely.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. What has been problematic for me is our saying that the two men who informed their people how to enter upon those people of the town, and Musa's saying: ﴿He said: My Lord, I have power over none but myself﴾ [al-Ma'idah 25], O Shaykh. So why did he not make an exception for them with himself?
* The Shaykh: We said: either this is based on the majority, or he did not intend them at all. As for ﴿I have power over none but myself and my brother﴾, although the two men had given advice, he did not know whether they would have possession. He does not possess complete ownership and complete control except over his brother.
* Student: The story of al-Bara' ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, which we mentioned[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in as-Sunan al-Kubra (9/44), from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Sirin.]], and we mentioned images of (...), and some people, O Shaykh, have cited this story as evidence for the permissibility of suicide operations. So what is the answer to this objection, may Allah bless you?
* The Shaykh: Suicide operations, may Allah bless you: are they a certain death? I ask you: it is a certain death. Is the story of al-Bara' ibn Malik a certain death? Then there is no evidence in it.
* Student: They say he fell in the land of the enemy?
* The Shaykh: But there is, for example, one in a thousand who succeeds, and the suicide bomber has two thousand who die. That is a tremendous difference.
* Student: Is it possible that (...) good deed is specific while bad deed is general?
* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: (...) ﴿It is forbidden for them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 26], and among them were reformers, such as ﴿those who fear, upon whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾ [al-Ma'idah 23]...?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, punishment is general: ﴿And beware of a trial that will not beset those who have wronged among you exclusively﴾ [al-Anfal 25].
* Student: May Allah reward you with good. If a person is known for cowardice, and is created with this disposition, for example if he is unable to fight in the way of Allah and it is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn), then what is the situation? Also, what is narrated about Hassan ibn Thabit concerning this: is it true that he did not fight? I read this with some writers.
* The Shaykh: Some later writers, in truth, have no courtesy toward the Companions. There is no doubt that Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, is not like Khalid ibn al-Walid in boldness and bravery. But our saying that he was a coward, and that a woman was braver than him, is a tremendous error, especially since he defended the Prophet (ﷺ) with his tongue, with a defense more severe upon them than the fall of arrows.
* Student: Shaykh, (...) their disposition is like this?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, they are advised, and it is said: Do not be among the last of this nation who curse its first. Fear Allah.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning the matter is one of ruling: if it is an individual obligation, it is required of them. If they neglect it, they are sinful.
* Student: If a person is afflicted with an illness and abandons treatment, and he argues for that with the story of 'Imran ibn Husayn that is in Sahih Muslim[[Muslim (1226/167).]], where he said to one of the Companions: "He used to greet me, but when I was cauterized, that ceased; and when I left it, he greeted me again." And the story of Abu Bakr when he fell ill and it was said to him: "Will you not seek treatment?" He said: "The physician has already seen me." They said to him: "What did he say?" He said: "I am doing what I will; He is capable." [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (35443) in similar wording.]] Does he have any proof, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: We have the Sunnah, and we have the action of the Companions. Which of them do we give precedence to? The Messenger commanded seeking treatment. However, we do not treat with what is forbidden. Then the action of some people, whether among the Companions or those after them, is understood to reflect a strength of trust in Allah that suffices them without medicine. So the strength of his trust in Allah takes the place of medicine. And one of the brothers told me about (...) someone who is cauterized in the morning and recovers by the end of the day, and similar cases are many. Did not the Messenger (ﷺ), when he mentioned the black seed, say that it is a cure for every disease except death?[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5688), and Muslim (2215/88), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] What was his purpose in this? That people should seek healing through it.
* Student: A person afflicted with a heart illness or such, who fears that if he goes to doctors and undergoes the operation, they will not perform it well, because this is an illness...?
* The Shaykh: That is another matter. If he does not have confidence in the physician, that is another matter, especially if his illness is dangerous and he should not risk himself. But if it is a known matter, for example the appendix now: if the appendix affects a person, if he hastens to remove it and cut it out, he will be saved by Allah's permission; and if he leaves it, he dies. It is an easy operation. Hemorrhoids are now easy with physicians, are they not? Although some scholars say: it is forbidden, cutting hemorrhoids is forbidden, because in their time there was danger, a danger of bleeding and the person dying. But now knowledge has advanced, thanks be to Allah, the knowledge of medicine.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Is it incompatible with tawakkul (trust in Allah) to begin with treatment through means such as medical drugs, and to leave off lawful recitation and spiritual means, or is that not so...?
* The Shaykh: Not at all. This is like what we said: some people incline toward treatment with physical medicines without recitation. For some people, recitation may be more beneficial than these, because the sick person does not accept this recitation; he is doubtful about it, and it will not benefit him if he is doubtful about it, or he does not trust the reciter. But in physical matters he trusts them greatly. However, there are illnesses in which physical medicines do not help, such as psychological illnesses. For these, nothing helps except recitation and the physicians... you find him examining the patient several times and saying: "There is nothing there." For these, nothing helps except recitation.
* Student: Does one who doubts the recitation of the reciter, or the benefit of recitation from the Mushaf, fall into a deficiency of trust in Allah?
* The Shaykh: He does not benefit. No, we do not know, is he doubting this on account of the medicine, which is the verses, or on account of the reciter?

Student: ﴿Which God has prescribed for you. And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers.﴾ (21) They said, "O Moses, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter." (22) Said two men from those who feared [Allah] and upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, indeed, you will be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers." (23) They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here." (24) [Moses] said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people." (25) [Allah] said, "Indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years, [during which] they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people." (26) [Al-Ma'idah 20-26].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He made among you prophets and made you possessors of dominion and gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds."﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O my people﴾, concerning Moses, peace be upon him.

﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾. The address here, ﴿O my people﴾, contains two things. The first: there is in it some [attempt at] appeasing them, and that they would not pay attention or listen to the speech unless it came with the address and the term "people." The second: he said ﴿O my people﴾ to win their sympathy, because there is a difference between the addressee being from your people or not from your people.

﴿Enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you﴾. The word ﴿enter the land﴾: he did not say "fight until you enter," he said ﴿enter the land﴾.

Then his saying ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾ also contains good news that they would be victorious. In these two phrases there are two glad tidings: the first is ﴿enter the land﴾; the second is ﴿which Allah has prescribed for you﴾. The prescribing here is the decreed prescription (kitabah qadariyyah), because prescription is of two kinds: legislative prescription (kitabah shar'iyyah), such as the Exalted's saying: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you that you may become righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah 183], and decreed prescription, such as the Exalted's saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105].

As for His saying ﴿Allah has prescribed for you﴾, I say: the prescription here is decreed prescription, not legislative; if it were legislative it would have been construed with ʿalā: "kutiba ʿalaykum," and the meaning would not be sound.

﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾, i.e., do not return, after you had been advancing toward fighting, on your heels, because retreating on one's heels and turning back is defeat and humiliation; for this reason, turning one's back on the day of battle was strongly forbidden.

﴿For you will turn back as losers﴾. Do not turn back and so turn back [as losers]. Turning back (inqilab) implies disappointment; therefore He said ﴿you will turn back as losers﴾, and ﴿losers﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal) from the waw in His saying ﴿you will turn back﴾.

So what was the answer? The answer, as you hear now, was: ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants."﴾

Notice the address ﴿O Moses﴾. They did not say "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah"; they said ﴿O Moses﴾. This is undoubtedly rudeness in address, that they addressed their prophet by his name; for this reason Allah forbade this Ummah to address the Messenger ﷺ by his name in His saying: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [an-Nur 63], according to one of the two interpretations of His saying ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾. Some scholars say the meaning is: do not call him by his name as one of you calls another, though the verse includes this meaning and also includes the second meaning, which is: when he calls you, do not make his call like the call of one of you to another; if you wish you respond, and if you wish you do not respond. Rather, it is obligatory upon you to respond. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal 24].

Here they said: ﴿O Moses, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants﴾, so they mentioned a cause that indicates their cowardice, their weakness, and the weakness of their resolve, indeed the absence of their resolve.

﴿Indeed there are in it a people of tyrants﴾.
