Then the action of some people, whether among the Companions or those after them, is understood to reflect a strength of trust in Allah that suffices them without medicine. So the strength of his trust in Allah takes the place of medicine. And one of the brothers told me about (...) someone who is cauterized in the morning and recovers by the end of the day, and similar cases are many. Did not the Messenger (ﷺ), when he mentioned the black seed, say that it is a cure for every disease except death?[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5688), and Muslim (2215/88), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] What was his purpose in this? That people should seek healing through it.
* Student: A person afflicted with a heart illness or such, who fears that if he goes to doctors and undergoes the operation, they will not perform it well, because this is an illness...?
* The Shaykh: That is another matter. If he does not have confidence in the physician, that is another matter, especially if his illness is dangerous and he should not risk himself. But if it is a known matter, for example the appendix now: if the appendix affects a person, if he hastens to remove it and cut it out, he will be saved by Allah's permission; and if he leaves it, he dies. It is an easy operation. Hemorrhoids are now easy with physicians, are they not? Although some scholars say: it is forbidden, cutting hemorrhoids is forbidden, because in their time there was danger, a danger of bleeding and the person dying. But now knowledge has advanced, thanks be to Allah, the knowledge of medicine.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Is it incompatible with tawakkul (trust in Allah) to begin with treatment through means such as medical drugs, and to leave off lawful recitation and spiritual means, or is that not so...?
* The Shaykh: Not at all. This is like what we said: some people incline toward treatment with physical medicines without recitation. For some people, recitation may be more beneficial than these, because the sick person does not accept this recitation; he is doubtful about it, and it will not benefit him if he is doubtful about it, or he does not trust the reciter. But in physical matters he trusts them greatly. However, there are illnesses in which physical medicines do not help, such as psychological illnesses. For these, nothing helps except recitation and the physicians... you find him examining the patient several times and saying: "There is nothing there." For these, nothing helps except recitation.
* Student: Does one who doubts the recitation of the reciter, or the benefit of recitation from the Mushaf, fall into a deficiency of trust in Allah?
* The Shaykh: He does not benefit. No, we do not know, is he doubting this on account of the medicine, which is the verses, or on account of the reciter?

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. The latter said, "I will surely kill you." The former said, "Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous. If you should raise your hand against me to kill me, I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds. Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, so you will be among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers." So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother, and he killed him and became among the losers. Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the body of his brother. He said, "Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal the body of my brother?" And he became among the regretful. Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain all mankind; and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved all mankind. And our messengers had already come to them with clear proofs; then indeed many of them thereafter became transgressors in the land.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 27-32].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded him to recite this story to them because of its importance. Otherwise, it is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an and to explain it to them, both its wording and its meaning, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to mankind what has been sent down to them﴾ [an-Nahl 44].

As for His words ﴿nabaʾ﴾: it means news (khabar). It has been said that nabaʾ is used only for a matter of great importance, whereas khabar may be used for both important and unimportant matters. His words ﴿the story of the two sons of Adam﴾: these two were sons of the same father; otherwise all mankind are the children of Adam. But these two were sons of one father. One of them was named Habil (Abel), and the other was named Qabil (Cain).

As for His words ﴿in truth﴾: that is, with established truthfulness. Know that the word "truth" (ḥaqq) may be applied to a report and may be applied to a judgment. If it is a report, it means truthfulness; if it is a judgment, it means justice, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am 115]. So His words ﴿in truth﴾ mean: with established truthfulness, about which there is no doubt and no disagreement.

As for His words ﴿when they each offered a sacrifice﴾: this is connected to ﴿nabaʾ﴾, meaning: the news of them when they offered a sacrifice. It is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the news; that is, the circumstance was that they both offered a sacrifice. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not specify whether it was gold, silver, food, or livestock. Allah did not specify it, and if there were a benefit in specifying it, Allah would have specified it. Accordingly, there is no need for us to burden ourselves by determining what this sacrifice was. This is a principle upon which you should build everything you follow in tafsir: whatever Allah has left unspecified remains unspecified, and there is no need to burden oneself to determine what that thing is which Allah has left unspecified, because Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Allah wants to make clear to you﴾ [an-Nisa' 26], and He says: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [an-Nisa' 176]. If there were a benefit in clarifying this unspecified matter, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would have clarified it. As for His words ﴿when they each offered a sacrifice﴾, what is meant is that by which one draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other﴾: the one who accepts is Allah, and He is left unnamed because He is known, as in His words: ﴿and man was created weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 28], where the Creator is undoubtedly Allah, and He is left unnamed because He is known.

﴿it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other﴾: from which one was it accepted? From Habil. Allah accepted it from him. But how do we know that Allah accepted it from him? Either it is as has been mentioned concerning earlier peoples, that when they gained spoils they gathered them, and a fire would descend from heaven and consume them; if there was embezzlement among them, the fire would not descend. Accordingly, the sign of acceptance would be that Allah sent down a fire upon this offering and consumed it. It is also possible that they both knew this through other signs, either through a dream or otherwise. The point is that both of them must have known that this one was accepted and that one was not. As for ﴿and it was not accepted from the other﴾, why? Because the other had no taqwa (God-consciousness) toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as will come in the explanation of the reason for acceptance. He was a wrongdoer toward himself, either by this offering which he made, meaning that he had usurped it, stolen it, or possessed it by an unlawful means, or by many sins which prevent the acceptance of righteous deeds.

﴿The latter said, "I will surely kill you."﴾ The speaker was the one from whom it was not accepted. He said this out of envy toward his brother.

﴿"I will surely kill you"﴾, because Allah accepted from you and did not accept from me. Then the other said to him: ﴿"Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous"﴾, meaning: indeed Allah does not accept except from the righteous. For this reason some of the early generations said: "If I knew that Allah had accepted from me a single righteous deed, I would be proud of it and rejoice in it, because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous.﴾" The sentence here, ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾, is a restrictive sentence, and the means of restriction in it is (innama), meaning Allah accepts only from the righteous. The righteous one is the one who obeys Allah, doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden.

﴿He said, "Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous."﴾ He said that not out of pride in his piety nor self-admiration, but to urge his brother to be among the righteous, and as an explanation, because Allah, glorified and exalted, accepts for a wisdom and withholds for a wisdom.

* This verse contains benefits. Among them: the importance of this story. Its basis is that Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to recite it to the community with a specific command, by His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam﴾.

* Among them: it is fitting for us to know the reports of those who came before us, especially where there is benefit, because Allah commanded that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it to us so that we may know from it and take lessons from it. The greater the matter, the stronger the concern with it. For example, it is fitting for us, indeed it is emphasized or obligatory upon us, to know the biography of the Prophet (ﷺ) from his birth until his death, especially his life after Allah honored him with prophethood, so that we know his circumstances, character, worship, call, deeds, and manners, and so that emulation of him may be complete for us. There is no doubt that knowing the biography of the Prophet (ﷺ) increases a person in faith and love for him and strengthens emulation of him, peace and blessings be upon him.

* Among the benefits of this verse: everything Allah reports is true, from His words ﴿in truth﴾. One should not say that this is a restriction, and that what the Prophet (peace be upon him) recites might sometimes be untrue. Rather, this is a description of reality, for everything Allah reports is true.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: two men may share in one deed, and yet there may be between them a difference as wide as between heaven and earth, either in the rejection of the second one's deed, or in the increase of the reward of the first, although the second is not deprived of reward. In this story, the second was deprived of reward. So two men may perform what appears to be one deed, yet between them there is a difference in reward, acceptance, and rejection as wide as between heaven and earth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, has the judgment regarding acceptance and rejection; He accepts and He does not accept. However, it is well known that Allah has made a measure for acceptance and a measure for rejection. Whenever worship is sincere for Allah and conforms to His law, it is accepted. Whenever you act in the lawful manner, your worship is accepted, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ [Ghafir 60]. Whoever is granted success in supplication, let him be glad of an answer; whoever is granted success in deeds, let him be glad of reward. Were it not for this hope a person has in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he would not be eager to act or to perform it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: taqwa is a cause of the acceptance of deeds, from His words ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾. Does this mean the acceptance of deeds only, or the acceptance of deeds and supplication? The apparent meaning is generality. Therefore, whoever is more God-fearing toward Allah is closer to the answering of his supplication and the acceptance of his deed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: one who is not God-fearing will not have his deed accepted. Does this mean it is not accepted in the very act of worship in which the violation occurred, or does it mean generally? We say: as for the very act of worship in which the violation occurred, there is no doubt that it is not accepted, for Allah does not accept a deed built upon disobedience, because Allah does not approve of that and so does not accept it. If a person gives charity from usurped property, that is, he usurped something and gave it in charity, it will not be accepted from him, because the sin occurred in the very deed which he performed for his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. And if a person prays a prayer that is not permissible at a time of prohibition and prays it at that prohibited time, it will not be accepted, because his praying it at that time is an act of disobedience, so how could he draw near to Allah through disobedience to Him? As for when taqwa is deficient in other than this deed, a person may be deprived of an answer because of his bad deed, and he may be answered and his righteous deed accepted; then the balance will be made in the Hereafter as to which outweighs, the good deeds or the bad.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, is described with attributes of action, from His words ﴿it was accepted from one of them﴾ and His words ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾. This is the belief of Ahl as-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah: that Allah, Exalted, is described with attributes of action, such as istiwa' (settling) upon the Throne, descent to the lowest heaven, coming for the judgment between His servants on the Day of Resurrection, speech, and others. Know, however, that the root of the attribute of action is an eternal attribute, while what occurs are the objects of action and the action concurrent with the object. As for the root of the action, it is an eternal attribute, because Allah, Exalted, has never ceased and never ceases to be doer. But His objects of action are not known to us; that is, there are things before the heavens and the earth which we know Allah created, but we do not know what they are, and we know nothing except what Allah, glorified and exalted, has taught us.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouragement toward taqwa, from His words ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no harm for a person to report a praiseworthy quality if he does not intend boasting, but intends the benefit of others, from the words of this one from whom it was accepted: ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾. For this sentence, O brothers, may be suitable for the speaker to be boasting about himself, and may also be suitable for the speaker to want to urge this one toward taqwa. Which is more probable concerning him? The second is closer, because the man is among the righteous.

Then he said: ﴿Even if you stretch out your hand against me to kill me﴾. "Basṭ" means stretching it out, extending it so that it reaches me.

﴿to kill me﴾: the lām here indicates purpose (ta'līl), meaning "in order that you kill me."

﴿I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you﴾. The meaning is that this man said to his brother: "If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you," and the meaning is that I will not kill you. This is explicit in this sense. But does this imply that I will not defend myself? There is a possibility that what is meant is: I will not defend myself; rather, I will surrender. Or the meaning may be: I do not intend to kill you. What actually happened was that the man killed his companion, as will come at the end of the story.

﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. When he said: ﴿I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you﴾, his brother might suppose that he was incapable of doing so, so he made clear that he was not incapable, but that he fears Allah.

His saying: ﴿I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ means: the Creator of them, their Owner, and the Manager of their affairs. The "worlds" (al-'ālamūn) are everything other than Allah, and they are called that because they are a sign (‘alam) pointing to their Creator. In all created things there is a sign indicating the oneness of Allah, the perfection of His dominion and authority, and other things required by His lordship.

From this verse: this man who was threatened with killing refrained from killing his companion. Can it be taken from this that whoever is intended to be killed by another should surrender? This is possible and also not possible, because we said that it is possible he means: "I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you," while as for defending myself, I will defend myself, but with a defense that does not reach killing. In any case, whether this possibility is what is meant or the first, our Sharia has come with something different. The Prophet ﷺ "commanded whoever intends to take his life to fight him, and whoever intends to take his property to fight him, and whoever intends to take his family to fight him, and he explained that the one who is killed while defending is a martyr"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4772) and al-Tirmidhi (1421) from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd; the hadith is in the Two Sahihs in abridged form from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr; al-Bukhari (2480) and Muslim (141 / 226).]], and that the aggressor who is killed is in the Fire, because he intended to kill his companion. However, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: this in relation to the Islamic Sharia differs according to the interest involved. In a time of strife it is proper to surrender; in a time of security, defense is obligatory. This is the correct view, because in a time of strife, defending oneself may result in the shedding of much blood. For this reason 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, surrendered to the killers, and the Companions asked him to defend himself, but he refused, because if they had defended him they would have clashed with these Kharijites, and much blood would have been shed. This is the most correct position: a person must defend himself to the extent he is able, even if that leads to the killing of his attacker if defense is not achieved except by killing, except in a time of strife where defense by killing would cause greater harm; here surrender is obligatory to prevent the greater evil.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when a person refrains from something forbidden, he should make clear to his companion that he refrains not from incapacity or fear, but for the reason that motivates his refraining. This is in His saying: ﴿I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you, indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. A parallel to this is that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the fasting person: "If someone fights him or insults him, let him say: I am fasting"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1894) and Muslim (1151 / 160) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], to make clear that he did not refrain from fighting out of incapacity or weakness, but because of the fast, during which a person is forbidden to fight and to revile.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: fear of Allah is the strongest deterrent from disobeying Him, as in His saying: ﴿I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you, indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. There is no doubt about this: fear of Allah is the strongest deterrent from transgression, just as hope is the strongest motivation for obedience and desire for what is with Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the comprehensive lordship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾.

Then he said: "Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin" (﴿إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ﴾). There is a reading known to us: ﴿لِأَقْتُلَكَ إِنِّيَ أَخَافُ اللَّهَ﴾ with the ya' pronounced with a fatha, and another reading: ﴿إِنِّيَ أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ﴾. He said: ﴿إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ﴾. Irada (will, desire) is the inclination of a person, or the inclination of the soul, toward what brings benefit or repels harm.

His saying ﴿أَنْ تَبُوءَ﴾ means: that you return (with).

﴿بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ﴾. As for his returning with his own sin, that is clear. But how does he return with his brother's sin? We say: the brother's not fighting him is a safety from sin. It is as if the brother who did not fight and was safe from sin had made the killer bear his sin. So the meaning of the sin that can be upon the killer, which this man wishes him to bear, is this. The meaning is not that the killer would have two sins: a sin for the one he killed had he killed him, and a sin for killing him. Rather, the apparent meaning is: ﴿إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ﴾, i.e., that his own safety from sin is as if the other had taken it upon himself and borne it.

﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾. ﴿فَتَكُونَ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أَنْ تَبُوءَ﴾, i.e., "so you will be among the companions of the Fire," because you killed a soul without right.

﴿وَذَلِكَ﴾ means: your being among the companions of the Fire.

﴿جَزَاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾. Every wrongdoer is punished, because the right is the right of the human being. Then, if his wrong is great, he will be among the companions of the Fire and will abide in it; otherwise, not.

In His saying ﴿إِنِّي أُرِيدُ﴾ is an affirmation of will for the servant, and that this has been known since humankind was created: that the servant has a will. Thus this is a refutation of the Jabriyya, who say that a person has no will, and that he only does a thing by compulsion and coercion.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever is intended to be killed and does not defend himself out of fear of sin, there is no blame upon him. But how is it fear of sin? We say: because he may kill the aggressor and hasten; for the obligation in repelling an aggressor is that he be repelled by the easiest means, then the easiest. If he desists from his assault by threat, he is not struck; if he desists by light striking, he is not struck heavily; if he desists by heavy striking, he is not killed; and if he is not repelled except by killing, the ruling is that he is killed. However, the scholars, may God have mercy on them, made an exception to this matter, and said: so long as one does not fear that he will forestall him by killing. If he fears that he will forestall him by killing, there is no harm in killing him at the first instant. That is, for example, if this aggressor has a weapon and brandishes it at his companion, and his companion fears he will fire at him and kill him; then there is no blame in forestalling him by killing, because this may not give you an opportunity to repel him by your hand, for example, or to shout at him, or the like; and then there is no harm in forestalling him by killing.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that killing is a cause of entering the Fire, by His saying: ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ﴾. Allah the Exalted has mentioned in His mighty Book: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذَابًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [An-Nisa 93]. Is he abiding in it forever?

We say: the Ummah has differed on this. Among them are those who said he abides in it forever, namely the Khawarij and the Mu'tazila; but the difference between them is that the Khawarij declared him a disbeliever, whereas the Mu'tazila did not declare him a disbeliever, rather they said he is in an intermediate position between two positions. What the People of the Sunnah and the Community hold is that he enters the Fire but does not abide in it. But does he enter the Fire with certainty, or is he included in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ [An-Nisa 48]? The well-known position of the People of the Sunnah is that he is included under the Will (of Allah). But the right of the one killed remains: does it fall under the Will?

The answer: if the killer repents a sincere repentance, then he is included in that, meaning that Allah does not punish him for the right of the one killed, by the generality of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا (٦٨) يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا (٦٩) إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا فَأُولَئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ [Al-Furqan 68-70]. The apparent meaning of the verse is that if he repents a sincere repentance, Allah the Exalted bears it for him and does not punish him; and this is regarding a right other than property. That is, we say: if this killer repents, does the blood money (diyya) fall from him?

The answer: No, because it is a right of the human being. For this reason the jurists, may God have mercy on them, expressly stated that a highway robber who repents before being apprehended has his repentance accepted and the legal penalty (hadd) lifted from him, but what is a right of the human being in worldly matters does not fall from him. So we say: if the killer repents, what is the ruling? Allah accepts his repentance even regarding the right of the one killed, so he is not punished for the killing, by the generality of His saying: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ﴾. As for if he dies without repenting, the right of the one killed must necessarily be taken from him, and the right of Allah is under the Will; so the killer is not guaranteed to be saved from the Fire, rather he is under the Will of Allah: if Allah wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He does not forgive him. This applies to the otherworldly recompense. As for the worldly one, which is the blood money, it must be collected for the heirs of the one killed, whether he repented or not.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that wrongdoing is a cause of entering the Fire, whether the wrong is against Allah or against a creature, by His saying: ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾. It may be said that ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ here is a general term intended in a specific sense, namely whoever commits this kind of wrong, which is killing a soul, because the wrongdoer may not deserve entering the Fire. But the first is more correct, by the generality of the verse, and because every wrongdoer's recompense is entering the Fire, unless Allah pardons him, as in other than polytheism.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother easy for him﴾. ﴿Made it easy for him﴾ means: it made it easy for him to kill his brother, even though his brother had admonished him with this advice, but, Allah forbid, it did not benefit him. ﴿Made it easy for him﴾ refers to the killer.

﴿his soul made the killing of his brother easy for him, so he killed him﴾, because his soul made the killing easy for him.

﴿So he became among the losers﴾, meaning he became one of the losers. We say "asbaha" (أصبح) means "became" (صار), because the basic meaning of al-isbah (الإصباح, morning) is the beginning of the day, but it may be used to express mere becoming, as when you say: "So-and-so became (أصبح) sad over this calamity," even though the calamity may have struck him in the middle of the day.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: caution against the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammarah bi-l-su', the soul that commands to evil). It may make the greatest sins appear easy to a person, so a person must be firm and watchful regarding his own soul, and must not follow it in what it makes easy for him of disobedience to Allah.

* Also among the lessons of this noble verse: killing a soul does not take one out of faith, because of His saying: ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother easy for him﴾. Allah the Exalted called him a brother after clarifying that he had killed him. Otherwise, someone might say that before he killed him, the sin of the killer did not apply to him even though his soul had made it easy for him, so the brotherhood remains. But Allah the Exalted mentioned the brotherhood after the killing had been completed. This is supported by the explicit statement of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, prescribed for you is qisas (retaliation) concerning the murdered: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned by his brother [i.e., the victim's heir] in any degree, then grant him reasonable compensation and pay him with good conduct﴾ [al-Baqarah 178].

Does fighting a believer necessitate disbelief, or take one out of faith and brotherhood?

No. This is because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if two groups among the believers fight, then make settlement between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly. The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your two brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat 9-10].

From this explanation we know that the word kufr (disbelief) in the Book and the Sunnah may mean lesser disbelief (al-kufr al-asghar). The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Cursing a Muslim is wickedness (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr)" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (48) and Muslim (64/116), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud]. In this noble verse, fighting did not remove the two fighting groups from the brotherhood of faith, and this is evidence that one who fights does not become a disbeliever. By this, the response to the view of some people is known: they say that every disbelief which Allah has mentioned without qualification is originally major disbelief that takes one out of the religious community (al-kufr al-akbar al-mukhrij 'an al-millah), unless there is evidence otherwise. The truth is the reverse: every disbelief which Allah has mentioned without qualification is lesser disbelief (kufr dun al-kufr), unless there is evidence that it is major disbelief.

* Also among the lessons of this noble verse: this man who killed his brother, and thought that he had won the field such that he had no rival, became one of the losers. From it is derived that every person who envies his brother and tries to come between him and success, the loss will return upon this envious person.

Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on Surah 5 (al-Ma'idah), verse 31:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the corpse of his brother. He said, "Woe to me! Am I incapable of being like this crow and concealing the corpse of my brother?" And he became among the regretful.﴾

﴿Allah sent a crow﴾: He dispatched it. The crow is the well-known bird. One should not ask: why did Allah choose it over the rest of the birds? Such questions cannot be explained with certainty, and one cannot fully comprehend them.

As for His saying ﴿scratching in the earth﴾: the commentators mention that two crows fought, and one killed the other, and the killer then scratched the earth and buried the dead crow. However, the apparent meaning of the verse differs from this, because Allah says ﴿Allah sent a crow﴾, and He did not say "two crows." The apparent meaning is that the crow only saw how to scratch the earth in order to bury its brother, and it seems that this killer, because of the strength of what had taken hold of his soul, was as if he were oblivious to this matter. So Allah sent this crow to scratch the earth, meaning: to dig it, until this killer sees what to do with his brother.

He said: ﴿to show him how to conceal the corpse of his brother﴾. ﴿To show him﴾ means: to make him see it with his own eyes.

﴿How to conceal﴾: how to cover?

﴿The corpse of his brother﴾: meaning his nakedness ('awrah), because the entire dead body is 'awrah. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded that the whole dead body be shrouded, and nothing of it be left uncovered, except that a man in the state of ihram has his head left uncovered, due to his saying (ﷺ): "Do not cover his head."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1265), and Muslim (1206 / 93), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]]

The man said: ﴿Woe to me! Am I incapable﴾. ﴿Woe to me﴾: al-Wayl is ruin, hardship and exhaustion, and it is said in every situation in which regret occurs. The origin of ﴿Woe to me﴾ is "yā waylatī" (O my woe), but the yā was changed into an alif for the sake of elongation: ﴿yā waylatā﴾, he elongates it when crying out. Here he calls upon woe, as if he were saying: "O woe, come, for I am regretful."

As for His saying ﴿Am I incapable of being like this crow﴾: the interrogative here is for reproach, meaning: how can I be incapable of being like this crow? Because the children of Adam are more honoured than the animals. He has here declared that he was incapable of equaling or matching the crow: ﴿so that I could conceal the corpse of my brother. And he became among the regretful.﴾

As for His saying ﴿a'ajaztu﴾ and ﴿fa-uwāriya﴾: they are in the accusative here, because they are the answer to the interrogative.

* * *
* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul without a soul having been killed or corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely; and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And our messengers had already come to them with clear proofs; then indeed many of them, after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 32].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the corpse of his brother﴾, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this verse: the actions of animals other than humans are created by Allah and by His will, due to His saying: ﴿So Allah sent a crow﴾. So are the actions of human beings created by Allah and by His will?

The answer: Yes, our actions are created by Allah and by the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what the People of the Sunnah and the Community hold, in contrast to the Qadariyyah Mu'tazilah who say that a person is independent in his deeds. Nevertheless, we say that a person's act occurs by his choice and will; so a person has choice and will, in contrast to whom? In contrast to the Jabriyyah, who said that a person has neither will nor choice. The People of the Sunnah and the Community, may Allah grant them success, have taken the texts from all their aspects. The Mu'tazilah took some texts, and the Jahmiyyah Jabriyyah took some texts, so they look at the texts like the one-eyed man who looks with one eye. As for the People of the Sunnah—and praise be to Allah, may Allah make us and you among them—they look at the texts with both eyes.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: animals may serve as guides for humans, as in this story. The crow guided the son of Adam to dig for his brother and bury him, and this has remained the practice of mankind until our day, except for those who have strayed from the straight path, such as those who burn their dead and scatter them into the sea and similar things. Otherwise, this has remained the practice of mankind to this day. Does a distinction in a specific matter require absolute preference?

The answer: No. This is a principle we should know: when someone is distinguished in one thing, this does not entail absolute superiority over him. An example of this is what is established from the Prophet ﷺ that in the last times there will be days of patience, for the one who acts in them there is the reward of fifty of the Companions.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4341), and Ibn Majah (4014), from the hadith of Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani.]] Does it follow that those who exist in those days are superior to the Companions absolutely?

No. Rather, they are distinguished by a particular merit. Likewise, we find that the Messenger ﷺ sometimes preferred some Companions over others in a specific matter, and that does not require absolute preference, as in his saying: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3009), and Muslim (2406 / 34), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]] So to whom did he give it? To 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. This does not mean he is superior to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and similar examples are many. Therefore we must know the difference between absolute virtue and specific virtue. Do we say that crows are superior to the children of Adam? No. Although crows have a merit in the manner of covering the dead, this does not entail preference.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glory be to Him, makes things easy for a person when the earth becomes narrow for him, in ways he had not thought of. This man was constrained: what would he do with his brother whom he had killed? So Allah relieved him by sending this crow.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation in burial is that the nakedness be covered, meaning the body be covered by it. However, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, added a condition that is indispensable: that the burial must cover the nakedness and prevent wild animals and the smell, meaning it must be that wild animals cannot dig up the grave and the smell does not come out of it. So if a person digs a shallow pit, then covers it with earth, but wild animals can easily dig it up and its smell comes out, this does not suffice. It is necessary to deepen the grave in a manner that prevents wild animals and the smell, and the deeper it is in the earth, the better.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the entire body of the dead is 'awrah, because the grave covers the whole body. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: the entire body of the dead is 'awrah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: intentional killing does not take a person out of faith, due to His saying: ﴿So his soul permitted him the killing of his brother﴾, and due to His saying in this verse: ﴿how to conceal the corpse of his brother﴾. This is the truth: intentional killing does not take one out of faith, in contrast to two misguided, deviant groups, the Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah. The Mu'tazilah said that one who intentionally kills a soul leaves faith but does not enter disbelief; rather he is in an intermediate position between two positions. This is his ruling in this world, but in the Hereafter he is abiding in the Fire. As for the Khawarij, they said he disbelieves, because there is only believer and disbeliever: ﴿He is the One who created you; among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun 2]. Creating an intermediate position between two positions is an innovation. The Khawarij were more courageous than the Mu'tazilah, because they stated what the evidence requires according to their claim, and declared him a disbeliever; but the Mu'tazilah resorted to this stratagem that he does not disbelieve, yet is in an intermediate position. Both opinions are erroneous.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the intense regret shown by this man who killed his brother, by His saying: ﴿Woe to me﴾. Its origin is "yā waylī" and "yā waylatī," and it is an expression of grief and sorrow. From this we derive another benefit: that the doer of sin, if he does not repent from it, will be requited with loss, regret and constriction of the soul.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this killer's acknowledgment, according to what the situation required, together with the self-reproach and condemnation it involves, by His saying: ﴿Am I incapable of being like this crow, so that I could conceal the corpse of my brother?﴾

* Among the benefits of the verse: this killer became among the regretful. Regretful over what? Over killing his brother, and over his inability to know how to cover his brother's nakedness. Thus he combined regret for both matters.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 32 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Because of that, We decreed for the Children of Israel﴾.
﴿Min﴾ here is for causation (ta'lil).
And ﴿ajl﴾ means "cause"; that is, "because of that cause."
﴿We decreed for the Children of Israel﴾ means a legislated prescription (kitabah shar'iyyah).
﴿For the Children of Israel﴾: Israel is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq.
﴿We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless for a soul or for corruption on the earth, it is as if he had slain all mankind; and whoever gives life to one, it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾. The referent of "that" (dhalika) is what occurred in the story of the two sons of Adam. The son of Adam who killed was the first to establish killing among humanity, and upon him is a share of the burden for every soul slain unjustly. Thus his killing of this soul is as if he had killed all mankind, because the burden of every soul slain unjustly falls upon him in its like.

As for His saying ﴿that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul﴾, this qualification is indispensable, because killing may be rightful and may be unrightful. Killing may be a soul for a soul, which is retaliation (qisas). Retaliation is a rightful killing, but retaliation is not absolute; that is, we do not kill a soul for a soul in every case. Rather, there must be conditions. For the establishment of retaliation there are conditions, among them: that the killer is not superior to the one killed in religion, freedom, or ownership. This is an indispensable condition: that the killer is not superior to the killed in these three matters: religion, and freedom (or, if you prefer, slavery and ownership). If he is superior, he is not subjected to retaliation. An example: a disbeliever killed by a Muslim; this cannot lead to execution, because the killer is superior to the one killed. The Prophet ﷺ has been established as saying: "A Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (111) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.]]. An example of freedom and slavery: a free person kills the slave of another man; this too is not executed, why? Because this is free and that is a slave, so the killer is superior and is not killed for him. Ownership, for example: a mukatab slave (one contracted to buy his freedom) owns a slave he bought to trade with, then he kills him. Here both are slaves, because the mukatab is a slave as long as a single dirham remains upon him. Is this mukatab to be killed for this slave?
The answer: No, because he is his owner. Both are slaves, but this one is an owner. Conditions are necessary.

His saying ﴿unless for a soul or for corruption on the earth﴾: Allah, blessed and exalted, stated "corruption" without restriction, and what is meant by corruption is corruption whose harm is widespread, not particular corruption. If a person burns another's shop, that is corruption, but he is not killed for it. Rather, the intended meaning is general corruption. An example: highway robbers who waylay people on the roads and mounts and seize their wealth openly by force of arms; these are without doubt corrupters on the earth. Among this, according to many scholars, is the wine-drinker who, when flogged, is flogged again and again and does not desist, and he is killed. Among it are also aggressive thieves. In short, this general corruption makes its perpetrator liable to be killed, because he has spread corruption on the earth. ﴿It is as if he had slain all mankind﴾: it is as if he had slain all mankind, though he has killed only one. The "ka" (as if) here is for comparison. What is the point of comparison? It has been said: this refers to one who deems lawful the killing of a soul without right or corruption on the earth; one who deems lawful the killing of a sacred soul is as if he had killed all people, because the intended meaning is the category (jins), as we said regarding one who denies a messenger: he is a denier of all the messengers. So this one who killed so-and-so, deeming his killing lawful while the victim is protected, is like one who killed all people, since he has deemed lawful the killing of the entire category of protected souls, and so is like the killer of all mankind.
It has also been said: the meaning is that whoever kills a soul whose killing causes strife, such as the killing of a ruler and the like, since when a ruler is killed strife arises and people begin to kill one another; this is then the killing of a soul as if he had killed all people. It has also been said: the meaning is "as if he had slain all people," because if he kills one soul he is killed for it, and if he kills ten he is killed for them, and if he kills all people he is killed for them; that is, he will not escape execution even if he kills all people or some of them, so the meaning is that the punishment of the killer by retaliation makes no difference between killing one or killing all people.
The fourth point: whoever kills a soul, it is as if he had killed (...) all; this refers to the punishment in the Hereafter, because whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever, and there is no greater recompense than this. If he killed two souls, it is the same; if he killed all people, it is the same. This is the greatest recompense: ﴿Hell, abiding therein, and Allah is angry with him, and has cursed him, and prepared for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa' 93]. But the first meaning is the most apparent: that whoever kills a soul deliberately, without a soul or corruption on the earth, kills it deeming killing lawful; then, when he deems killing lawful for one sacred soul, it is as if he deemed it lawful for all people.

﴿And whoever gives it life, it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾. His saying ﴿gives it life﴾ means he rescues it from death. It does not mean that he breathed the spirit into it, because that is not possible except for whom? Except for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Rather, the meaning is: whoever gives it life, rescuing it from killing. This includes several things:
Firstly: if a person intends to kill someone and his soul enticed him to kill his brother, then he awakens, sees that this is forbidden, and refrains from this killing, this is one who gave life to the soul; after his soul had made killing him seem appealing, he turned back. This is one.
Secondly: repelling an aggressor who wants to kill a person, so he repels him, and here he has given life to a soul by rescuing it from killing.
Thirdly (i.e., among the meanings): that a person falls into peril, such as fire, drowning, or collapse, and another person comes and rescues him. This one has given life to the soul; is that not so? He has given life to a soul, and is like one who gave life to all people. In what respect? In the reward he is rewarded with, or in the goodness of his intention in rescuing this protected soul. So it is as if he rescued all people, because his inner disposition is good and his intention is one of mercy; when he shows mercy to one creature, it is as if he showed mercy to all people.

As for His saying ﴿for the Children of Israel﴾, why did He single out the Children of Israel? He singled out the Children of Israel because they are the people most given to killing among the prophets and in killing those among mankind who enjoin justice. He specified them with this because of their abundant transgression.
If someone says: Is there also abundance of giving life among them? We say: No; but a thing may be mentioned together with its opposite for completeness of the division.

Then He said: ﴿And indeed Our messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾. ﴿And indeed they came to them﴾: the sentence here is emphasized with the lam, qad, and an implied oath. This construction has many examples in the Qur'an. So we say about such a structure that it is emphasized with three emphatics: the oath implied by the lam, the lam itself, and qad.
﴿Our messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾: ﴿Our messengers﴾ are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent; He attributed the messengers to Himself because He is the one who sent them. Perhaps we may also say: as an honouring of them, since a messenger is honoured by the honour of the one who sent him. Allah, glorified and exalted, honoured them by attributing their message to Himself, and the message may also come attributed to the one to whom it is sent. ﴿Our messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, and there is no opposition or contradiction between the two. They are messengers of Allah, because He—?
* Students: He sent them.
* The Shaykh: And they are messengers to the creation, because they conveyed to them the message of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. His saying ﴿with clear proofs﴾: this is an adjective of an omitted noun; the estimate is "with clear signs" (bi-al-ayat al-bayyinat), that is, the manifest, evident ones that none brings except a messenger from Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the signs of the messengers suited to their age, as the scholars have mentioned regarding Musa, peace be upon him, who brought the staff and the hand, because in his time sorcery had spread, so he brought signs that the sorcerers could not oppose. ʿIsa, peace be upon him, came at a time when medicine had advanced, so he brought signs that medicine could not oppose: raising the dead, bringing them out of graves, and healing the blind-born and the leper. Muhammad ﷺ was sent to a people among whom eloquence had grown strong and spread, and they took pride in it. So Allah made His greatest sign to him, peace be upon him, this noble Qur'an, which no human can match, nor even the jinn: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants﴾ [al-Isra' 88].
﴿With clear proofs, then﴾: after these clear, manifest proofs that came gradually afterward.
﴿Indeed, many of them after that are, in the land, transgressors﴾: here He says ﴿then indeed many of them after that﴾, that is, after the coming of the messengers with clear, manifest signs, many of them become transgressors in the land. Here we ask about the i'rab of ﴿musrifun﴾. Yes?
* Student: It is the predicate of (...).
* The Shaykh: The predicate of (inna)? Is it not the predicate of (inna) ﴿after that﴾? Do you agree with this?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: The lam here did not prevent the governing of what follows over what precedes it, because ﴿in the land﴾ is related to ﴿musrifun﴾. The known rule is that the lam of commencement does not govern what follows over what precedes it; but the grammarians said the lam here is "displaced" (muzahlaqa): its original position is before (inna), but the Arabs disliked two emphatics occurring in one place, so they shifted the lam—as the grammarians say—shifted it until they placed it on the predicate. Hence it is correct to say that ﴿after that in the land, indeed they are transgressors﴾ is related to ﴿musrifun﴾. Transgression (israf) is exceeding the limit by overstepping the bounds of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, violating His sacred prohibitions, and disregarding the denial and killing of the messengers.
* In this verse there are benefits, among them: the affirmation of causes (ʿillah) for the legal rulings. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿because of﴾, which is one of the strongest expressions of causation. The affirmation of causation, which is wisdom (hikmah), is undoubtedly part of the perfection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: that Allah, exalted, does not legislate anything except for a wisdom, and does not decree anything except for a wisdom. As for the one who says it is not permissible to affirm wisdom for Allah, and that Allah acts merely by will and legislates merely by will, this is a false statement in about a thousand ways, as some scholars have mentioned. Moreover, it is a disparagement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that His acts and legal rulings should be founded on no wisdom. Allah, blessed and exalted, has refuted this in several verses: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth﴾ [ad-Dukhan 38–39]. He, exalted, said: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. He mentioned that He sends down water from the sky by which He gives life to the earth after its death; the verses and texts on this are many. Affirming wisdom for Allah is the utmost exaltation above deficiency and defect, in contrast to those who say it is not permissible to affirm wisdom and causation in Allah's acts and legislation. Why? They say: because if you affirm a cause for Allah, you make Allah act for a purpose, and purpose is impermissible. Hence among their common, false phrases is: "Glory be to the One who is exalted above accidents, parts, and purposes." If an ordinary person heard this phrasing, which is ornate and embellished, he might weep. "Glory be to the One exalted above parts, accidents, and purposes": what do they mean by parts? The face, the hand, the eye, the foot, the shin, which cannot be attributed to Him because these are parts. Accidents are actions, since an action is an accident, such as istiwa' upon the Throne, descent to the lowest heaven, and the like. Purposes are wisdoms. We say: Glory be to the One who is described with what befits Him, and the greatest of what befits Him is wisdom, that His acts and legal rulings be founded on wisdom.

So we say: wisdom contains no deficiency. If someone says: If you make wisdom one of the attributes of perfection, then make it obligatory upon Allah what wisdom requires; make it binding upon Allah that He legislate this thing, that He obligate this thing, that He forbid this thing, because wisdom requires it; and then you would have made it obligatory upon Allah by your own minds?
We say: This is an error. Rather, we know that what Allah legislated is for a wisdom, and we are not the ones who obligate Allah to act, nor are we the ones who assign this thing to this specific wisdom. If Allah has prescribed upon Himself mercy and made mercy obligatory upon Himself, should He not make it obligatory upon Himself to do a thing when wisdom requires it? Because that is the requirement of this attribute. So we say: we do not obligate Allah by our intellects to do anything, because our intellects are too limited and deficient to grasp that this is the wisdom, and that it is necessary to rule for this wisdom is even more deficient. But when we know that Allah obligated or forbade it, we know that this is for a wisdom.
If someone asks: Do you obligate Allah to obligate when wisdom requires it?
The answer: Yes, but by His obligating it upon Himself. He described Himself as the Wise and the Most Wise of judges. As for us, we do not obligate this by our intellects.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnification of Allah's Self, exalted, in His saying ﴿We decreed﴾. Examples of this are numerous in the Qur'an. The Christians cited this expression—attributing a matter to Allah with the plural of majesty or the plural pronoun—to support their falsehood that Allah is the third of three. There is no wonder in this, since those in whose hearts is deviation follow the ambiguous. As for us, we say: Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Baqarah 163]. And Allah, blessed and exalted, says to ʿIsa son of Maryam: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two deities besides Allah"? He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not say to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord'"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 116–117].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted, multiplied the punishment upon everyone who kills a soul without a soul or corruption in the land, by making him like one who killed all people.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of specifying a particular group within a general ruling, since it is the most common people to act upon it. Its explanation: Allah specified this prescription for the Children of Israel although it is general, because they are the ones who most violated the sacred prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by killing souls.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the retaliatory killing of a soul for a soul, from His saying ﴿without a soul﴾. But there must be conditions; the conditions of retaliation must be present:
Among them: that the killer is not superior to the killed in religion, freedom, and ownership, whose explanation has already passed. Is a Jew killed for a Christian? Yes, because disbelief is one community, and likewise for a Magian.
Among them—that is, among the conditions of retaliation—is the absence of parenthood: that the killer is not the parent of the one killed. If he is the parent, he is not killed for him, and this is for two reasons:
The first: what came in the hadith: "A parent is not killed for his child"[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (1400), Ibn Majah (2662), and Ahmad (346), with his wording, from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.]].
The second: the parent is the origin of the child's existence; for were it not for him, the child would not have come into being, so it is not fitting that the branch should be the cause of the annihilation of the root.

Is a child killed for his father? Yes, he is killed. Some scholars held that a father is killed for his child if he killed him deliberately with clear aggression, and this is the preponderant view, indeed the required one, because of the generality of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a life for a life﴾ [al-Ma'idah 45]. Likewise the Sunnah has come with: "A life for a life" [agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh); al-Bukhari (6878) and Muslim (1676/25), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud].

As for the prohibition of killing a father for his child, the evidence cited for it is weak. First, the hadith: "A father is not to be killed for his child" is weak. Second, even if it were authentic, it is to be understood as applying where there is a doubt (shubhah), because it is extremely rare for a father to deliberately kill his child, extremely rare. On this basis, since a mistake is presumed in the case of a father killing his child, the ruling of retaliation (qisas) is lifted. When do we say this? If the hadith is authentic. But if it is not authentic, then we have been spared it.

As for the reasoning that the father is the cause of the child's existence: it is said, yes, he is the cause of the child's existence, but when we kill the father for his child, what is the cause of the father's being killed? The father. So he is the cause of his own killing. Then we say: this view is strengthened if we say that a father killing his child is among the greatest severances of kinship, is it not so? And the Messenger (ﷺ) informed that among the greatest sins is: "That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6001) and Muslim (141/86), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud]. This is among the greatest sins, so how can we reward this father by lifting retaliation from him? Therefore the correct view, without doubt, is that a father is killed for his child, whether the father is the mother or the father, provided that we establish deliberateness.

The third condition: we must know that it was deliberate. If it was quasi-deliberate (shibh 'amd), such as striking him with an instrument that does not usually kill, then we do not kill him even if he dies from it. So if he strikes him with a stick, a whip for example, and he perishes, he is not killed for it, because the original state is inviolability, and that this one struck with the stick died is due only to a defect in him and his lack of endurance, and a stick does not usually kill such a person, so he cannot be killed for it. As for what was mentioned earlier regarding freedom and ownership: know that there is disagreement over killing a free man for a slave, and the correct view is that a free man is killed for a slave, because of the generality of the evidence showing that a life is for a life. The hadith that has come: "A free man is not killed for a slave" [related by Abu Dawud (4517) and al-Darimi (2403), from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub] is weak, and there has come in the hadith of al-Hasan from Samurah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills his slave, we will kill him" [related by Abu Dawud (4515) and Ibn Majah (2663)]. So if a person is killed for his slave, who is his property, then killing him for another's slave is all the more so. The correct view is that a free man is killed for a slave, and an owner for the owned, but on condition that the killing is deliberate, with clear aggression.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that corruption on earth permits the taking of a life; by His saying: ﴿or corruption in the land﴾. Among this is highway robbery, meaning those who confront people with weapons on the roads...

From Samurah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills his slave, we will kill him" [related by Abu Dawud (4515) and Ibn Majah (2663)]. So if a person is killed for his slave, who is his property, then killing him for another's slave is all the more so. The correct view is that a free man is killed for a slave, and an owner for the owned, but on condition that the killing is deliberate, with clear aggression.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that corruption on earth permits the taking of a life; by His saying: ﴿or corruption in the land﴾ [al-Ma'idah 32]. Among this is highway robbery, meaning those who confront people with weapons on the roads, seizing their wealth, and perhaps killing them; these are corrupters in the land. Likewise, among the corrupters in the land at the present time are those who bring narcotics and import them into Muslim countries; they are corrupters in the land, without doubt. If they say, for example: "We did not force people to buy," we say: but you placed the matter before them, so you are promoters and importers, and your evil will not be repelled except by what? Except by killing. So every person whose evil cannot be repelled except by killing, from these corrupters, is to be killed.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, how is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿wa-laqad﴾ (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, the oath particle is present; here the sworn element is not present. What is present is the response of the oath, ﴿wa-laqad﴾.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: In the response of the oath.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, the Khawarij say there is no third stage: either disbelief or faith. They say: whoever commits a major sin is a disbeliever. So what do they say about the established legal punishments in the Book and the Sunnah? The established punishments, i.e., cutting off the hand and flogging for slander, what do they say about them?
* The Shaykh: About what?
* The student: About the established punishments, I mean for slander now?
* The Shaykh: The consequence of their principle is that they are disbelievers.
* The student: So whether they are flogged or not?
* The Shaykh: Whether he is flogged or not, yes. Even if the punishment is carried out on him. But in any case, the details of their doctrine on this we cannot know unless we read their books. Generally, however, every major sin for them takes a person out of faith into disbelief, yes.
* Student: May Allah honour you, Shaykh. We mentioned that intentional killing does not take one out of faith. Does not the wrath in the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah has become angry with him﴾ [al-Nisa' 93], indicate his exclusion?
* The Shaykh: No, it does not indicate that. The One who said this is the One who said regarding retaliation: ﴿But if anything is remitted to him by his brother, then pursuit should be made in a reasonable manner and payment should be made to him with good conduct﴾ [al-Baqarah 178].
* The student: What do we understand from this verse?
* The Shaykh: They say this verse is not a problem regarding His anger, because the anger of Allah may cease; the problem is in His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾, and the scholars have answers to it, which we will mention, God willing.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast: ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides or be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. Except for those who repent before you overpower them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33-35].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33]. This sentence is a restriction (hasr); it contains restriction, and its means is ﴿innama﴾, and what follows ﴿innama﴾ is restricted.
* Student: The benefits of the previous verse?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the previous one?
* The student: We stopped at the sixth, that corruption on earth permits the taking of a life.
* The Shaykh:
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that corruption on earth permits the taking of a life, but it is restricted by other evidences showing that not every corruption permits the taking of a life; rather, some corruption permits killing and some permits less than killing. So this verse is understood in light of the other verses or texts indicating specification.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that saving a protected person is like saving all protected people, by considering the genus. Whoever saves a protected person from destruction, it is as if he saved all of mankind, considering the genus, just as whoever denies one messenger, it is as if he denied all the messengers.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul, or for corruption in the land, it is as if he killed all of mankind, by considering the genus, because permitting it for one is permitting it for the genus, if there is no cause that permits his blood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted, established the proof against the servants by sending the messengers with clear evidences.
* Among its benefits: the honouring of the rank of the messengers, by attributing them to Allah: ﴿And surely Our messengers came to them with clear evidences﴾ [al-Ma'idah 32]. Every object that Allah attributes to Himself, Exalted is He, indicates honour, and for this the scholars said regarding His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 114], and in the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (900) and Muslim (442/136), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar], and in His saying: ﴿And purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [al-Hajj 26], and what is similar to that. They said: this attribution indicates what? Honour and elevation of rank. And there is no doubt that the messengers are the best of the human species.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the messengers were supported with clear signs that indicate the truth of their message, by His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾.
* Among its benefits: the love of Allah, Exalted is He, for giving excuse and establishing proof, in that He placed with every messenger a clear sign by which mankind believes, so that people do not say: who said this is a messenger? Where is the evidence that he is a messenger? So when he brings clear signs, the proof is established.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever has not received the message is excused, by His saying: ﴿And surely Our messengers came to them with clear evidences﴾, and this is for establishing the proof against them. The verses and texts on this are clear, Allah says: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that mankind will not have any argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165], and Allah says: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the messenger must make clear to his people what he was sent with, by His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾, for it includes the signs indicating their truthfulness, and it includes the laws they brought and that they are clear and plain. And the matter is so, for Allah, glorified and exalted, did not conceal from the servants what He obliges them to, since His mercy and wisdom reject that. For this Allah said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then indeed upon Us is its explanation﴾ [al-Qiyamah 16-19]. So Allah, Exalted, has made things clear to creation, and Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people to make [the message] clear for them﴾ [Ibrahim 4].

From here we derive the importance of translation. That is, upon this benefit, namely the benefit of clarification, is based the importance of translation: that Muslims must translate the Sharia into the language of those they address, so that the proof is established. For if you came to a non-Arab people and spoke among them with the most eloquent and most eloquent Arabic speech, they would benefit nothing from it, and would not know what you are saying. Accordingly, whoever wishes to go to a people calling them to Allah must learn their language, so that he can call them, or accompany a person who translates, who is knowledgeable in both the original and the target languages, and who has familiarity with the subject of the translation, that is, the subject of what he translates. For example, if he wants to translate a discussion on tawhid, he must have familiarity with that, so that the matter is not understood contrary to what is meant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Children of Israel, despite the clarifying messengers, did not become guided; rather, many of them after this clarification and after these messengers are polytheists who transgress the limit. Among examples of this: they used to kill the prophets without right, and kill those among people who enjoin justice, and they disparaged the messengers and harmed their particular messenger sent to them, namely Musa, as Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said﴾ [al-Ahzab 69].

It follows from this benefit: knowledge of the obstinacy of the Children of Israel, that they are a people of arrogance, pride and denial, and they remain with this description until our present day.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that when there is need to emphasize a report, eloquence calls for emphasizing the report, and the context calls for emphasizing the report, even if the speaker is one of the truthful, so that the listener may be reassured. For His saying: ﴿Then indeed many of them﴾ is emphasized with two emphasizers: (inna) and the second: the lam.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth [in] corruption is only that they be killed﴾. (Innama) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and restriction establishes the ruling for what is mentioned and negates it for anything else. When you say: "No one stands except Zayd," you affirm standing for Zayd and negate it for others. When you say: "Innamā al-qā'im Zayd" (the one standing is only Zayd), you affirm standing for Zayd and negate it for others.

Know that (innama) is followed by the restricted element. That is, only the restricted element follows it, whenever it occurs. When you say: "Innamā al-qā'im Zayd," you restrict standing to Zayd. "Innamā Zayd shujā'" (Zayd is only brave), you restrict Zayd to bravery, because it is the most prominent of his traits.

﴿Those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾: ﴿yuḥāribūna﴾ is a verb that denotes mutual action (mushārakah), because the pattern (fā'ala) always indicates mutuality, though it may sometimes not indicate it. The saying of someone: "Safara Zayd" (Zayd traveled) has no sense of mutual travel here; it means travel from two sides. However, (qātala) (fought), (shātama) (insulted) and (ḍāraba) (struck) and the like all indicate mutuality. So the usual meaning of this verb is that it indicates mutuality. Thus the meaning of ﴿yuḥāribūna Allāh﴾ is that they confront the war of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And with what? Does it mean that they bear weapons against Allah? Certainly not. The meaning is that they oppose Allah in His command, doing what He has forbidden and abandoning what He has commanded, out of arrogance and obstinacy. This is warfare: they wage war against Allah and wage war against the Messenger. Regarding the Messenger, it may be said that war can include both armed war and war through rejecting what he called to. But regarding Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it does not include armed war, because that does not occur and cannot occur.

﴿And strive upon the earth in corruption﴾: that is, they corrupt the earth by hastening (to it), based on the words ﴿and strive﴾, and sa'y means hastening; that is, they hasten to corruption on the earth. This is by shaking security, domineering over people, taking their wealth and killing souls. For this reason the scholars said that this verse was revealed concerning the muḥāribūn, who are the highwaymen (quṭṭā' al-ṭarīq). Highwaymen are people who ambush people in the desert on the roads. When someone passes by them, they kill him and take his wealth, or they take his wealth and leave him, or they frighten and terrify him. The point is that their crimes vary, but they ambush people, seize their money, and perhaps kill them. This is found widely in lands whose security has been shaken.

Also among the corruption on the earth is: raiding safe homes and killing their people or stealing from them, or the like, where there are factions, gatherings and groups that harm people. This differs from a single thief, who has a separate ruling. But these people who form factions and become groups that terrify people raid others in the built-up areas or in the desert.

﴿That they be killed﴾: this ﴿an﴾ and what follows it is the predicate (khabar) of what? It is the predicate of ﴿penalty (jazā')﴾, meaning their penalty is killing. Here He said ﴿yuqattalū﴾ with the doubled letter (tashdīd), and did not say "an yaqtalū." It seems, and Allah knows best, to be an indication of the heinousness of their killing and also of its multiplicity; because when the object is plural or the action is plural, it is correct to use a form that indicates multiplicity. Here, if we say the intended meaning of ﴿yuqattalū﴾ is when they are a large group, this is due to the plurality of what? The object: such as Zayd, 'Amr, Bakr and Khalid, and so on. And if we say it is for the heinousness of killing, it means we kill him with a dreadful killing by which others are deterred. That is one point.

﴿Or be crucified﴾: meaning they are crucified. Is the intended meaning crucifixion after killing, thus combining both? Or is it crucifixion alone without killing? The apparent meaning of the noble verse is the second: that he is crucified until he is disgraced by his crime, and then the ruler considers his case as he sees fit. However, it is known that crucifixion occurs after killing.

﴿Or their hands and their feet be cut off from opposite sides﴾: hands and feet are cut off from opposite sides. The scholars explained this as the right hand and the left foot being cut. The cut on the hand is from the joint of the palm at the wrist, and the cut on the foot is from the joint of the foot at the heel. For the foot has a sole and a heel; the heel that is called the ʿirqūb (Achilles tendon), the ʿirqūb is not cut, rather the cut is made at the joint of the foot at the ʿirqūb.

﴿Or be exiled from the land﴾: this is the fourth. ﴿Yunfawā min al-arḍ﴾ means they be driven out from it and removed far from it. The alif-lām in ﴿al-arḍ﴾ is for a specific reference (ʿahd), meaning the land in which they strove in corruption, so that this is further from the places of corruption for them and more painful to them.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That﴾, meaning what has been mentioned of this severe punishment, ﴿is a disgrace for them in this world﴾, meaning humiliation and shame, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ (33). ﴿A great punishment in the Hereafter for them﴾: thus they are combined in punishment in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, due to the magnitude of their crime, its heinousness, its ugliness, and their aggression against the servants of Allah.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾: ﴿except those who﴾ is an exception from what preceded. And His saying ﴿repented﴾ means they returned to Allah and refrained from their striving in corruption on the earth and from warring against Allah and His Messenger. Here it is necessary that a period pass by which the soundness of their repentance is known, by their laying down weapons and refraining from harm, and that signs of repentance and sincerity appear upon them.

His saying ﴿before you gain power over them﴾ means they repented of their own accord, laying down their weapons and refraining from highway robbery.
