Some of them said: One does not perceive the Mu'tazilism in his book except with the tweezers (al-manaqish); meaning it is hidden, just as a thorn is not removed except with tweezers, so the Mu'tazili doctrines of the author of the Kashshaf cannot be extracted except with tweezers.

He gave an example of this, saying: He said, may Allah pardon us and him, concerning the Almighty's saying: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185], he said: What success is greater than a person being drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise? Does anyone feel that there is deviation in this statement?

* Student: No.

* The Shaykh: One may not feel that there is deviation in it. But when we know that the man is clever and that he wraps meanings in a way hidden from many people, then he intends by this to deny the vision of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, because the vision of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is a greater success than a person entering Paradise and being drawn away from the Fire. But the man is clever, so such an expression a person reads as a sound statement with nothing wrong in it, yet its outward appearance contains mercy while its inner meaning from its source is punishment.

So upon which tafsir do we rely? We say, first: The tafsirs based on transmission (al-tafasir al-athariyyah), that is, those that explain the Quran by reports from the Companions and the senior Followers, are the first to be consulted, and at their head is the tafsir of Ibn Jarir. But there is a flaw in the tafsir of Ibn Jarir: he transmits tafsir from the Companions and the Followers with chains, some of which are sahih, some hasan, and some da'if. It seems that he, may Allah have mercy on him, wanted to collect what was narrated; either death overtook him before he sifted it, or he wanted to leave this to the reader. Therefore, if something difficult from tafsir by transmission in Ibn Jarir or others passes before you, return to the chain of narration; perhaps you will find in it a flaw that requires rejecting what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, or from Mujahid, or others.

Among the best tafsirs we see is the tafsir of Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him. It is a tafsir by transmission and also reasoned, but at times it overlooks the discussion of some Isra'iliyyat (narratives from Israelite sources) or some stories, and this is undoubtedly a flaw. But as I told you: whenever your heart rejects something of this, return to the chains of narration, or to the origin of this narrated text, which may be from the Children of Israel, and it is among the things permitted in the hadith: «Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm» [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3461) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him both.]]. But the tafsir is good.

As for the tafsirs of the later scholars, some of their tafsirs contain long and wide discussion on the verse, and then when you want to gain something from it you find nothing; it is chaff, of little benefit, except for rare exceptions. In any case, the student of knowledge can distinguish between the worthless and the valuable.

But here there is a matter I want to point out: I want you first to try to understand the Quran yourselves. Read the verse, ponder its meaning, and then you will have some meaning. After that, return to the statements of the mufassirun, because accustoming oneself to deriving meanings, or in other words to explaining the Quran by oneself, gains a great deal of understanding, because it is compliance with the command of Allah: ﴿that they may ponder its verses﴾. But do not be certain if the matter is not clear except after reviewing the books of tafsir.

Among the mufassirun there are those who take another course, such as the matters of jurisprudence, like al-Qurtubi, may Allah have mercy on him; he takes this course, and you find his tafsir contains many jurisprudential issues. This is good; there is no doubt it is good and beneficial to the student of knowledge.

The second matter in tafsir: The scholars said: One first refers to the explanation of the Quran by the Quran, and this is abundant; then to its explanation by the Sunnah; then to the explanations of the jurist-Companions, especially those who had care for the tafsir of the Quran, such as Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud; then to the senior Followers who received tafsir from the Companions.

For example, if someone says to you: What is the strength mentioned in Allah's saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [al-Anfal 60]? We look in the Quran and do not find an explanation of it, but we find in the Sunnah that the Prophet ﷺ said: «Indeed, strength is archery; indeed, strength is archery» [[Narrated by Muslim (1917/167) from the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. So we explain strength as archery, that is, learning archery, and archery is according to every time and place. The people in the beginning shot with what?

* The students: With arrows.

* The Shaykh: With bows and the like. Then they began to shoot with gunpowder, with rifles, with bullets; then now they shoot with missiles, short-range and long-range. The strength the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, spoke of is archery, and it includes any shooting that corresponds to the methods of warfare of its time.

Likewise, if someone says to you: What is the Day of Religion? We look in the Quran, which explains it: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense? Then what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense? It is the Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Infitar 17-19]. This means that the Day of Religion is the day on which nothing benefits except deeds, and on which no one possesses any benefit for another. Similar examples are many.

So we explain the Quran by the Quran first, then by the Sunnah second, then by the sayings of the Companions, especially those who cared for tafsir, then by the sayings of the Followers who took tafsir from the Companions, such as Mujahid.

This does not mean that if we see the verse may bear other meanings than what was mentioned, we should restrict ourselves to what was mentioned; for the speech of Allah, the Exalted, is too broad for humans to encompass. They may understand one meaning and we understand another meaning of the verse. But if it contradicts what the Companions and Followers understood, we do not accept it. As for if it does not contradict it, there is no harm in saying: the verse is what? Broad. The verse is broad, including this and that, because the speech of Allah is broad.

The third principle: The verse may bear two or more meanings, so what do we do? If it bears two or more meanings, we say: Which of these meanings is more apparent? If one of these meanings is more apparent, it is obligatory to take it according to the more apparent, especially if the less apparent conflicts with the apparent, then we take the apparent.

For example, the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. It bears two meanings, one of which is more apparent than the other. The first meaning is what? That the intended "two hands" are the real two hands with which Allah grasps and withholds. The second meaning is strength. But this second meaning in relation to the first is weak, very weak. So we say: It is not possible to take it to the second meaning, because the first meaning is more apparent, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, cannot address His servants with what is more apparent while intending the less apparent; this is impossible, because Allah said: ﴿Allah intends to make clear﴾ [al-Nisa 26], and He says: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa 176]. So it is not possible to take the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the less apparent meaning when the apparent exists; rather, it is necessary to take the apparent.

But if both meanings are possible, meaning that it is suitable for this and that, then if the two meanings do not conflict, it is obligatory to take the verse to both meanings together, and there is no harm. If they are mutually exclusive, it is necessary to seek a preponderating factor from outside, because the wording before us has no preponderance, and we need a preponderating factor from outside.

An example of the first: The saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And by the night when it departs [or: when it approaches]﴾ [al-Takwir 17-18]. "Wa al-layli idha 'as'as" (when the night ʿasʿasa): some said its meaning is "it turned back (adbara)," and some said its meaning is "it approached (aqbala)." Both are suitable in context and in the Arabic language. So what do we say about such a case? We say: it is taken to both meanings together, and there is no harm, because the speech of Allah, the Exalted, is broad.

And like: ﴿And the sea filled with fire [or: kindled]﴾ [al-Tur 6]. Al-bahr al-masjur: is the meaning what will be kindled and become fire on the Day of Resurrection, or "masjur" means filled, or "masjur" means prevented from overflowing onto the earth? There are statements. Does each statement negate the other? No. Is "masjur" apparent in one of them to the exclusion of the others? No. It is suitable for all of them; then we say: "masjur" means that which will be kindled, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir 6]; and "masjur" means filled, as the Arabs say: "dalw masjurah," meaning filled; and "masjur" means restrained, as it is said: "sajarat al-dabbah bil-qayd," meaning I restrained the animal from running away. So the verse is suitable for all of them; it is taken to what? To all of them, and there is no harm, because the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as I told you, is broad.

Another example: the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'[menstrual cycles or periods of purity]﴾ [al-Baqarah 228]. Some scholars hold that by "quru'" is meant periods of purity (tuhr), and others hold that by "quru'" is meant menstruation (hayd). These two meanings cannot both be taken from the verse together, because they are what? Mutually exclusive. So an external preponderating factor is necessary: the external preponderating factor is either from the Sunnah, or from the usage of the Arabs, or from something else; the point is that a preponderating factor is necessary. When we return to the external preponderating factor, we find that «the Prophet ﷺ applied the term quru' to menstruation when he said to the woman with istihadah: "Sit for the amount of time your quru' detain you"» [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (280), al-Nasa'i (211), and Ibn Majah (620) from the hadith of Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh.]] or words similar to this. Here we say: the intended "quru'" is what? Menstruation; this is specified because the Sunnah indicates it.

This is a beneficial principle for the student of knowledge: whenever a verse may bear two or more meanings, and there is no preponderance for either of them, and no contradiction between them, it is taken to both of them together.

Likewise, the fourth principle in tafsir: Is it permissible for a person to explain the Quran by his own opinion (ra'y) or not? It is not permissible. Explaining it by opinion means that you bear the Quran upon what you believe, making the Quran follow your opinion and creed. This occurs frequently among the people of desires, who bear the Quran upon what they believe, so they have spoken about the Quran by their own opinion. This is a flaw from which few are safe. Even the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, when a text comes to them that is contrary to what they hold, you find them trying to turn it toward what? Toward what they hold. This is not permissible. This means that the person has made himself a lawgiver alongside Allah: Allah wants such-and-such, and he bears it upon something else. This is among the greatest of prohibitions: "distorting words from their places."

Suppose you bear it upon other than its apparent meaning because of a proof from the Quran or the Sunnah; then there is no harm. But merely because you believe something contrary to what the apparent meaning indicates, this is not permissible at all and is not lawful; it is of the "distortion of words from their places," and of a person taking himself as a lawgiver alongside Allah. You find this frequently among the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, in some issues. You find that a person distorts the evidence in an obvious way because he believes contrary to what it indicates. There are examples of this.

For instance: The jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, hold that a man may not perform ablution with the leftover water of a woman, but a woman may perform ablution with the leftover water of a man. Then they cite the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «A man should not bathe with the leftover water of a woman, nor a woman with the leftover water of a man; rather let both take water together» [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (81) and al-Nasa'i (238) from a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.]]. What do we say now? Contradiction! How do they cite this hadith to prohibit a man's ablution with a woman's leftover water and permit a woman's ablution with a man's leftover water, when the hadith is one? The hadith is one. What compelled them to this is their belief that this is the correct position.

Likewise the well-known hadith of 'A'ishah: «Whoever dies while owing fasts, his guardian shall fast on his behalf» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1952) and Muslim (1147/153) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. Some jurists bore this hadith upon the meaning of vows (nadhr), and said: If a person dies owing the obligatory fast of Ramadan or an expiation (kaffarah), then no one fasts on his behalf.

So let us consider, our brothers: what made them divert the hadith from its generality? Their belief that obligations are to be performed by the person himself, and no one fasts for anyone, and no one prays for anyone. Observe how they bore the hadith upon rarely occurring issues and diverted it from frequently occurring issues. Which is more common: that a person dies owing the fast of Ramadan, or owing a fast of vow?

* Students: The fast of Ramadan.

* The Shaykh: The first, without doubt. This is an error in inference. A few nights ago in our study of Iqtida' al-Sirat al-Mustaqim it passed us that Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed out that it is not permissible to bear texts upon rare issues and leave aside frequently occurring issues.

Related to the Quran and its tafsir: consideration of meanings. Some people take a position that does not fit the meaning, and this matter requires the person's understanding, not the symbols found in printed editions of the Mushaf, because some of these symbols are wrong, clearly wrong; rather, one returns to the person's understanding.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 41 (part 2 of 4):

I strike for you an example. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21]. Some people join and say: "﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth﴾ [and] ﴿they raise the dead?﴾", and this spoils the meaning, because the clause ﴿they raise the dead﴾ is independent of what precedes it, and its meaning is: "Or do they have gods from the earth? Do they raise [the dead]?", meaning: "Do these gods raise and give life to the dead?!" So the clause here is a new, independent sentence, and it is also interrogative, with the interrogative particle deleted, in order to refute the claim of these people regarding their gods that they worship.

Likewise, some people recite: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾ [an-Nisa' 43], and they stop at ﴿do not approach prayer﴾. This is not permissible, because if he reads ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer﴾ and then begins anew, the meaning is entirely corrupted.

As for the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So woe to those who pray (4) who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'un 4, 5], there is no harm in pausing at His saying: ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾. Why? Because it is the end of a verse (ra's aya), and Allah the Exalted knows best His Book. So when it is the end of a verse, pause, and there is no objection, even if what follows is connected to what precedes. Furthermore, there may be a benefit in pausing: if you recite ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾ and then stop, the listener will say to you, "How is this?" and he will pay attention, and you will find him eager for what comes next. Then when you recite ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾, his heart is cooled and his chest is expanded. So making that the end of a verse has a benefit in it.

Likewise, with regard to the division of the Qur'an into ahzab (sections): Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) criticised the existing division. Sometimes you find that a hizb ends on a verse whose continuation is connected to it as the soul is connected to the body, yet it is written, for example: "hizb", "three-quarters of a hizb", "a eighth", and the like. Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "This is not how the Companions divided it. The Companions divided it while observing the meaning. If the meaning remains complete at a line or two lines, they delayed the division." This is correct. In some of the ahzab you are amazed how this is the end of the hizb when what follows is clearly connected to it!

This is what comes to my mind now of some of the rules of tafsir. We have composed a small book on the rules of tafsir, which is studied in the institutes, so whoever wishes may refer to it.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you. If a person wishes to understand a verse, does he proceed in this order: the Qur'an first, then the Sunnah, then the sayings of the Companions? Or may a person go to the verse only among what the Companions have said, or only to the words of some exegetes?
* The Shaykh: Yes. It is not necessary to return [to them all]. But if he is compelled to consult tafsir, he returns to this. However, if the understanding is clear from its basis, he has no need to return. For example, if someone says: "How do I perform wudu'?" This is clear in the verse ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], so what need is there to return to tafsir?
* The Student: Very well, O Shaykh. When, then, do we return to this order that the scholars established?
* The Shaykh: At the point of disagreement, we must return to: tafsir of the Qur'an by the Qur'an, then by the Sunnah, then by the sayings of the Companions, then by the sayings of the Successors (tabi'un).
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, this is general; this is like an open session.
* Student: May Allah bless you. Some contemporary exegetes link the verses of the Qur'an with modern discoveries, for example..?
* The Shaykh: Yes. Some contemporaries now try to link modern discoveries with the Qur'an, but some of them go too far and exceed the limit in this, interpreting the Qur'an in a way that matches the present while it is far from it. But if the meaning is close, there is no harm.
For example, when it was first said that they had reached the moon, I saw some people who began to hum over the interpretation of Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority﴾ [ar-Rahman 33], and he said: "These people have passed through, they passed through to the regions of the heavens, and the 'authority' (sultan) means knowledge." This is forbidden and impermissible. Interpreting the verse in this sense is forbidden, without any doubt; because the verse is very clear that this is a matter of challenge and that they are unable [to do it]. And Allah says: ﴿from the regions of the heavens and the earth﴾. Has anyone passed beyond the regions of the heavens? If we said: "They passed beyond the regions of the earth and transcended gravity", they did not pass beyond the regions of the heavens. And the verse is clear that it is on the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish (26) but the Face of your Lord will remain, full of majesty and honour﴾ [ar-Rahman 26, 27]; ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks of Him; every day He is upon some matter﴾ [ar-Rahman 29]; ﴿We will attend to you, O two heavy ones﴾ [ar-Rahman 31]; ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority﴾ [ar-Rahman 33]; ﴿There will be sent against you two a flame of fire and molten copper, and you will not be victorious﴾ [ar-Rahman 35]; ﴿So when the sky is split open﴾ [ar-Rahman 37]. It is very clear that this will be on the Day of Resurrection.
Then, who said that "authority" in this verse means knowledge? It is true that sultan comes with the meaning of knowledge, as in: ﴿You have no authority for this﴾ [Yunus 68]; but in this verse the intended meaning of sultan is power, because He said: ﴿if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority﴾, and you have no authority. So sultan comes with various meanings according to each context.
My intention is that those who interpret the Qur'an according to what has happened, some of them go to excess in this and transgress the limit, and they do not realise that a day may come when the theory to which the Qur'an was forced turns out to be a mistaken theory, and then the Qur'an's meaning will have been misunderstood.
* Student: O Shaykh, sometimes you find in the Qur'an a verse that has been explained by the scholars either by the Qur'an or by the Sunnah, in order, and the explanation that this person cites is not mentioned there, but the wording allows it linguistically. For example, His saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my home as a believer﴾ [Nuh 28], he applies it to the door of the apartment, for example; or ﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 101], and so on?
* The Shaykh: This means that some people use verses, or argue from verses, for meanings that are not intended. For example, we often see on houses, or on commercial markets, or even on government offices: ﴿And say, "Do [as you will], for Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers"﴾ [at-Tawbah 105]. This is not permissible, because the Prophet (ﷺ) cannot see this deed; Allah the Mighty and Majestic sees it, and the believers who are present see it, but the Messenger does not see it. So how do we lie and say: "Allah will see your deeds and His Messenger and the believers"?! This is not permissible.
Likewise, if a verse is applied to a meaning other than what is intended, that is also not permissible, because turning the verse to the meaning chosen by this man is forbidden if the verse does not indicate it.
* Student: O Shaykh, how does one extract the correct view from the statements of the scholars of tafsir, when their tafsir contains some things (that are problematic)?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, this is true; there is a difficulty in it. For example, if a person returns to the tafsir of al-Zamakhshari and admires its eloquence and fine style, while he is young and does not know [better], he must be warned about this and it must be said: take what relates to rhetoric, what relates to grammar, and what relates to meaning; but as for matters of 'aqidah, beware, and warn against this.
* Student: (...) the exegetes (...) the connection (munasabah) between each verse and verse and between each surah and surah?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The connection between verses is truly part of the science of tafsir, and a person should, if possible, know the connection between a verse and the verse before it. But excessive insistence on this and forced speculation is not necessary, because it is enough for us to say: "Allah knows best what He intends." If a person says "Allah knows best" regarding what he does not know, that is good. For this reason, some verses cannot have their connection known, such as: ﴿Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 238] in the context of the divorced women. You cannot know a connection for this. This is part of the wisdom: that Allah, blessed and exalted, cuts off the hopes of creation of encompassing His speech with knowledge.
* Student: Some exegetes adopt the method of interpreting the Qur'an through the Arabic language without regard to the Qur'an, the Sunnah, or the sayings of the Companions. Is this method correct?
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that this is an erroneous method. Returning to language absolutely is wrong, because if we returned to it and said: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾ [then], what is "prayer" (salah) in language?
* Students: Supplication (du'a').
* The Shaykh: Yes, so it would mean: "Establish supplication." This is wrong.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Is (...) the tafsir of the Qur'an by the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: By name and title, the tafsir of Shaykh al-Shinqiti (may Allah have mercy on him), because it is titled: Adwa' al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Quran bil-Quran.
* Student: And Ibn Kathir, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Ibn Kathir is fine, but he is not of the same kind as Adwa' al-Bayan.
* Student: In this era, few of the scholars are skilled in tafsir. Should we tell the student of knowledge to turn to reading to fill this gap?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, my opinion is that the student of knowledge must give attention to tafsir. Now, many students of knowledge give attention to 'aqidah, and this is good; many give attention to fiqh, and this is good; many give attention to hadith, and this is good; but few, in my view, and Allah knows best, give attention to tafsir, and this is one of the wonders. The Noble Qur'an is filled with every good. Sometimes you try to find the ruling of a matter from the statements of the jurists and you cannot find it, and yet it is present in the Qur'an, and Allah the Mighty says: ﴿We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾ [an-Nahl 89]. Therefore the Qur'an contains great treasures. Even a person sometimes stops to reflect: what is the connection of this with that? Or why is this word nominative or accusative, or the like? So give attention to tafsir.
* Student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. Should the student begin from the very beginning of tafsir, or (...)?
* The Shaykh: He must take this and that. Even if he wishes to read tafsir alone, without having first acquired knowledge of the instruments, the sciences of language in its various kinds, he may not grasp anything.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And among those who are Jews are listeners for falsehood, listeners for another people who have not come to you. They distort words from their places. They say, "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And whomever Allah intends to test, you cannot avail him against Allah at all. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Messenger, let not those hasten into disbelief distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41]. The "Messenger" here refers to Muhammad (ﷺ).
In His saying ﴿lā yaḥzunka﴾ there are two readings: ﴿yuḥzin﴾ and ﴿yaḥzun﴾, and both are authentic canonical readings (sab'iyyah). That is: "Let them not make you grieve by the saying of those who hasten into disbelief." They hasten into it, meaning they compete in it.
Kufr (disbelief) linguistically means concealment, and from it is named the kafur or kafra, which is the sheath of the date-palm spathe, because it conceals the blossom within it. The meaning of kufr here is disbelief in Allah the Mighty. Disbelief in Allah revolves around two things: either denial and rejection, meaning refutation, or arrogance together with acknowledgement. Iblis's disbelief was of which of the two types? Of arrogance, because he was a believer but arrogant, and Allah forbid. The disbelief of Quraysh who say: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God?﴾ [Sad 5] is disbelief of denial and refutation.
﴿Among those who say "We believe" with their mouths﴾: "min" here explains the first relative noun, which is ﴿those who hasten﴾.
﴿Among those who say "We believe" with their mouths﴾, ﴿And among those who are Jews﴾, ﴿those who say "We believe" with their mouths﴾: ﴿with their mouths﴾ is connected to ﴿say﴾, meaning: they said with their mouths "We believe", while their hearts did not believe. This description applies exactly to the hypocrites, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah 8]. And these, in disbelief, are like the Jews and Christians, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were hypocritical say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you"﴾ [al-Hashr 11], meaning the Jews.
His glorified and exalted saying: ﴿And among those who are Jews are listeners for falsehood, listeners for another people﴾ explains the conditions of the Jews who are "those who are Jews" (alladhina hadu), and they are those who said: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back [in repentance] to You﴾ [al-A'raf 156], meaning: we returned to You from disobedience to obedience. They are called "those who are Jews" and they are called "the Jews". The first name is from their saying "Indeed we have turned to You," and the second is attributed to their forefather Yahudhah (Judah).
The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And among those who are Jews are listeners for falsehood, listeners for another people﴾. ﴿Listeners for falsehood﴾ means they accept it, they accept falsehood from their rabbis who say that Muhammad is not a prophet, and this is among the greatest of lies, indeed the greatest lie after lying against Allah the Mighty.
﴿Listeners for another people who have not come to you﴾: His saying ﴿listeners for another people﴾ admits two meanings:
The first meaning: they are listeners to falsehood from those who came to you and from those who did not come to you; so they respond to falsehood from any person, whether he comes to you or not.
﴿Listeners for another people who have not come to you﴾, meaning: listeners to their falsehood. So Allah the Mighty mentions that these Jews hear falsehood absolutely, and listen to another people who have not come to the Messenger ﷺ.
The second possibility in His saying ﴿listeners for another people﴾ is: they listen to you in order to convey it to another people; so they are, as it were, an intermediary between the Messenger ﷺ and those to whom the report is conveyed. That is: they listen to you for the sake of what? For the sake of another people, to whom they convey what you say. When they convey it to those other people, they distort it, alter it and change it; and for this reason He said: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾. That is, the other people, namely the rabbis of the Jews to whom the common folk convey what they hear from the Prophet ﷺ, these distort words from their places. "Tahrif" means alteration, that is, changing them from their proper sense, so that what is meant is one thing while the intended meaning of Allah and His Messenger is another.
Is the intended meaning that they distort the words of the Torah, or the words of the Torah and other than it? The more general reading is preferable: they distort words of the Torah and they distort words of the Qur'an.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 41 (part 3 of 4):

﴿They say: "If this is given to you, take it; but if it is not given to you, then beware."﴾ That is, they specify for them a particular thing, a particular ruling. The rabbis (al-Ahbar) specify for these people, to whom they convey reports, a particular thing, a particular ruling, and they say: ﴿"If this is given to you"﴾ by whom? By Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"take it"﴾, accept it. ﴿"But if it is not given to you, then beware"﴾, meaning: beware of accepting it. So these rabbis, who relay speech from the Messenger (ﷺ), now say to their followers: Present this to Muhammad. If he gives it to you, take it; otherwise, beware.

The exegetes gave an example of this in the story of stoning (al-Rajm). Stoning of the adulterer was prescribed in the Torah, and the Children of Israel used to stone whoever committed adultery. When adultery became widespread among their nobles, it was hard for them to stone their nobles, so they said: "We will not stone, but we will blacken the face (tahmim al-wajh), that is, make it black, and mount the two adulterers on a donkey, each facing the other's back, and parade them through the markets only, without stoning." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decreed that a man and a woman among them (the Jews) committed adultery, so they referred the matter to the Prophet (ﷺ). Their rabbis said: "If Muhammad gives you this," meaning what?

* Students: Blackening the face.
* The Shaykh: Blackening the face, blackening the face (tahmim al-wajh) and parading them through the town; ﴿"take it"﴾. But if he does not give it to you and orders stoning, then beware. This is an example and not a restriction of the meaning of the verse. Rather, the intended meaning is that they (the rabbis) specify rulings for their common people and say: If Muhammad rules by them, accept them; if he does not rule by them, beware.

﴿They distort words from their places; they say...﴾ Their distortion of the words here is a distortion of meaning (tahrif ma'nawi), in the sense that they made stoning abrogated (mansukh) and that it is not obligatory to act upon it. We will mention, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id), that distortion (tahrif) is divided into two kinds.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to test﴾, that is, to misguide, ﴿you will not avail him anything against Allah﴾. This is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ). That is, when Allah wills to test someone, no one among the creation can repel this will; it must occur. But is Allah's will to test anyone among people based on no wisdom? No, it is based on wisdom. The wisdom is stated in the words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5]. Thus they are the cause. When Allah knew there was no good in their hearts, He caused them to deviate, as He said: ﴿O Prophet, say to those prisoners in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Anfal 70].

So we say: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to test﴾, that is, to misguide, ﴿you will not avail him anything against Allah﴾. This applies to one who is deserving of being misguided, as Allah said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones...﴾ ("Those," referring to these Jews who accept from the truth only what agrees with their desires.) ﴿"If this is given to you"﴾, meaning: what we want of the ruling, take it; and if it is not given to you, beware.

﴿Those﴾, meaning these people who accept from the truth only what agrees with their desires, ﴿...whom Allah has not willed to purify their hearts﴾. The use of a demonstrative indicating distance is not to elevate their status, but to distance them from praise and from being upon the truth.

﴿Allah has not willed to purify their hearts﴾. From what? From doubt, polytheism, atheism, and other things. He mentioned the hearts because the heart is the seat of righteousness and corruption. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599/107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, that is, humiliation and shame. Their humiliation and shame: as for the Jews, it is by fighting them and overpowering them, and that has occurred, praise be to Allah, for the Jewish tribes in Medina were all either killed or exiled. This is disgrace in this world. As for the hypocrites, their disgrace is that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, made them known and exposed their faults, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks, and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad 30]. The Prophet (ﷺ) knew the names of some hypocrites and informed Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, about them; for this reason he is called "the keeper of the secret."

﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire. We ask Allah to protect us and you from it. The hypocrites are in the lowest level of the Fire.

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: the testimony that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a Messenger, from His words: ﴿O Messenger﴾.
* Among them: Allah's glorification of His Messenger, since the form of address in this manner is a sign of honor, as you say: "O King," "O Amir," "O Generous one," and similar. This form of address, that is, the calling, conveys honor.
* Among the benefits of this verse: strengthening the Prophet (ﷺ), that is, strengthening his heart, and consoling him with His words: ﴿Let not those who race to disbelief grieve you﴾, meaning: do not be concerned about them, for their end is that they have disgrace in this world and a great punishment in the Hereafter.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: people differ in disbelief. Some race toward it with hurried steps, and some are less than that, because the verse says: ﴿Let not those who race to disbelief grieve you﴾, meaning there are people who do not race toward it. The one who calls to disbelief, is he racing toward it or not? He is racing toward it, and the non-caller is not racing, but the caller is racing toward it, and this is clear.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that faith is centered in the heart, from His words: ﴿Among those who say "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts have not believed﴾. Verbal faith is not faith unless it is based on what? On faith of the heart. Otherwise it does not benefit its possessor.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: faith's seat is the heart, from His words: ﴿but their hearts have not believed﴾.

But if someone says: Are we not commanded to take people by their outward appearance?

The answer: Yes, we are commanded to do this. But whoever's hypocrisy is evident, we treat him according to what his state requires. For example, if he openly declares hypocrisy, we do not remain silent about him. As for one who does not openly declare his hypocrisy, we have only the outward; the inward is with Allah.

Just as, if we see a disbelieving man, we treat him as what? As a disbeliever, and we do not say: "We do not declare him a disbeliever specifically." As some students have become confused now, saying: "If you see someone who does not pray, do not declare him a disbeliever specifically." How can I not declare him a disbeliever specifically? If you see someone who prostrates to an idol, do not declare him a disbeliever specifically, because perhaps his heart is at peace with faith! This is a grave error. We judge by what? By the outward. When we find a person who does not pray, we say: "This is a disbeliever, without any doubt." When we see someone prostrating to an idol, we say: "This is a disbeliever, and we identify him and hold him to the rulings of Islam. If he does not comply, we kill him." As for matters of the Hereafter, yes, we do not testify for any specific person as being in Paradise or in the Fire, except one for whom the Prophet (ﷺ) testified, or what has come in the Qur'an.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that among the Jews there are those who listen to lies and transmit lies, meaning that he believes lies, does not verify them, accepts them, and also transmits lies. This is something observed.
* From this benefit it follows that whoever is in this state has a resemblance to the Jews. The one who accepts lies and speaks of them, and takes them as settled, resembles the Jews, and the one who transmits lies likewise resembles the Jews. Whoever lies or believes lies resembles the Jews without doubt, and this calls for caution against this blameworthy trait.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the arrogance of the Jews, meaning their rabbis, and their pride in not coming to the Prophet (ﷺ). It is as if they think that if they came, that would be humiliation and abasement. But Allah humbled and abased them, praise be to Allah, through their disbelief in the Prophet (ﷺ).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: clarifying this blameworthy trait of the Jews, which is distorting words. What is meant by "words" here is the revelation that the Messengers brought: the Torah, the Qur'an, and others.

The scholars said: distortion is of two types. The first: distortion of meaning (tahrif ma'nawi), and its proponents are many. The second: distortion of wording (tahrif lafzi), and its proponents are few.

As for the first, distortion of meaning: it is to turn the speech of Allah and the speech of His Messenger (ﷺ) away from what Allah and His Messenger intended, whether in matters of creed or in legal rulings. If one turns a text away from what Allah and His Messenger intend, he is distorting the words, and this, as I said, is widespread.

The second, distortion of wording: this is also forbidden, but it is rare. This is because someone who distorts the wording, if the meaning is not changed by it, we do not hold him accountable, since it benefits nothing; but people will notice it, even the layman will object to it. If the meaning is changed by it, then he has combined distortion of wording with distortion of meaning.

So, the one who says: "Allah established Himself upon the Throne," but means by "istawa" "istawla" (seized control), is he distorting it? What kind of distortion?

* Students: Meaningful (ma'nawi).

* The Shaykh: Meaningful. And the one who recited: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾, with the word Allah in the accusative (Allaha), this is a distortion of wording and meaning, because if he says "Allaha Musa taklimah" (Allah spoke to Moses), the speech becomes from whom? From Moses, and this is distortion of meaning. If he puts the word for the Name of Majesty in the accusative (naṣb), it is distortion of wording. And the one who says: "Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-'alamin" (all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds) with the word "Rabbi" changed in case, is distorting the wording, meaning the meaning does not differ but the wording differs.

All types of distortion, of meaning and of wording, are forbidden. Furthermore, if one deliberately does something while knowing what Allah and His Messenger intended, this may reach the level of disbelief, may Allah protect us, because he has said about Allah what he knows is contrary to the truth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the blameworthy distortion is that which occurs after a person has come to know the truth, from His words: ﴿from after its places﴾, and in another verse: ﴿from its places﴾. They want to remove the words from their places. As for a person who interprets with a valid interpretation, he is not blamed, and his act is not considered distortion for which he is sinful. However, if we agree with him while knowing that he is wrong, we may consider it distortion for which we would be sinful.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever distorts the words from their places in this nation has a resemblance to—?

* Student: To the Jews.

* The Shaykh: He resembles the Jews. This calls for warning against distorting words from their places, so that a person does not fall into resembling the Jews.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Jews accept from the truth only what agrees with their desires, from His words: ﴿They say: "If this is given to you, take it; but if it is not given to you, then beware."﴾

* Among its benefits: the condemnation of those who accept from the truth only what agrees with their desires, and when it does not agree with their desires, they go seeking concessions from this nation. Many people are of this kind: if they are given a fatwa that satisfies their hearts, they accept it; otherwise they go seeking others who will issue the fatwa they desire. We say of this: it has a resemblance to the Jews.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the intense aversion of the Jewish rabbis to the truth, from His words: ﴿but if it is not given to you, then beware.﴾ He did not say "then do not take it." He said: ﴿then beware﴾, and this is harsher in effect than saying what? "Then do not take it." ﴿If this is given to you, take it﴾, and the expected parallel would be: "and if it is not given to you, then do not take it," but they said "beware," which is harsher in effect than saying "do not take it."

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, Mighty and Majestic, and that it encompasses even the will of a human being, from His words: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to test, you will not avail him anything against Allah.﴾

Know that will (irada) is divided into two kinds: legislative will (irada shar'iyya), which means love, and cosmic will (irada kawniyya), which means decree (mashi'ah). Here, ﴿And whoever Allah wills to test﴾ is cosmic will, that is, whoever Allah decrees to test.

In the words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And Allah wants to accept your repentance﴾ [al-Nisa 27], this is legislative will, because if it were decreed will, Allah would have accepted the repentance of all people, but it is legislative will, meaning Allah loves to accept their repentance. So the difference between the two wills in terms of their reality is that legislative will means what?

* Student: Legislative will may happen and may not happen.

* The Shaykh: We have not yet reached "may happen or may not happen." And cosmic will?

* Student: Decree.

* The Shaykh: In the sense of decree. The difference between them: cosmic will necessarily results in the occurrence of what Allah wills by it, while legislative will may occur or may not occur. The second difference: cosmic will applies to what Allah loves and to what Allah does not love, while legislative will applies only to what Allah loves.

So if someone asks: Does Allah will disbelief? We say: there is detail. By cosmic will, yes; by legislative will, no. By this we recognize the error of one who says: "Everything that occurs is beloved to Allah," and this is a serious mistake, because if we took this view it would follow that Allah loves disbelief, transgression, and disobedience, and He, Mighty and Majestic, does not love this, nor does He love corruption.

If someone asks: Is faith willed by Allah cosmically or legislatively?

* Students: Legislatively.

* The Shaykh: The answer: if it occurs?

* Students: Both cosmically and legislatively.

* The Shaykh: Then it is willed both cosmically and legislatively. And if it does not occur, it is willed legislatively.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no one can change what Allah wills, from His words: ﴿you will not avail him anything against Allah.﴾

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that righteousness and corruption revolve around the heart, from His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has not willed to purify their hearts.﴾

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a person who derives rulings must consider the texts from all angles. If you look at His words: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has not willed to purify their hearts﴾, you would say: Allah's will to purify the heart is mere desire. But if you restrict it by other texts, you know that Allah's not willing to purify the hearts of these people is because they are not worthy of it, as He Exalted said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5], and as is made clear in the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is a clear witness to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599/107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* Among its benefits: a person should always ask Allah to purify his heart and should take care of the deeds of the heart. A person's care for the deeds of the heart must be greater than his care for the deeds of the body, because the deeds of the body in reality occur from every person, whether believer or hypocrite, but the deed of the heart is what is important. I ask Allah to make our hearts all sound.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the good news from the Prophet (ﷺ) that these people have humiliation and shame in this world, and a great punishment in the Hereafter.

* And among them, that is, among the benefits of the verse: the warning to these people, perhaps they will return. The warning against disobedience is among the causes of turning away from it, so that one does not commit it, and if he does, he seeks forgiveness and repents.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that the children of Adam have two abodes. What are they?

Student: "The worldly life and the Hereafter."

Shaykh: The worldly life and the Hereafter. In this worldly life, the punishment comes either from Allah or from the servants of Allah: ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [al-Tawbah 14]. This is through the hands of the Messenger and his Companions. It may also come from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, such as when they are afflicted with diseases, drought, famine, and other things. The punishment of the Hereafter, from where does it come? From Allah alone. No one can punish anyone in the Hereafter, nor reward them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 42 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful gain﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:42).

His saying ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "They are listeners to falsehood." The mention of "listeners to falsehood" here serves as emphasis and as a preparation (tawtiah) for His saying ﴿devourers of the unlawful gain﴾. These people combined two things: corruption of speech and corruption of food. They are listeners to falsehood: they accept it, they speak of it, and they take it as settled.

﴿devourers of the unlawful gain﴾ means: of unlawful wealth. It has two readings: ﴿as-suht﴾ with a sukun on the ha' (suhtun), and ﴿as-suhut﴾ with a dammah on the ha' (suhutun), like nahr and nahar.

﴿devourers of the unlawful gain﴾: as-suht. I have told you: it is every unlawful wealth. It includes bribery, which was widespread among the Jews. It includes usury (riba), which was also widespread among the Jews. It includes fraud and betrayal. The rule is that as-suht is every unlawful wealth, meaning every wealth a person acquires through what is forbidden, and it is called suht because there is no blessing in it; it is "uprooted of blessing" (masHoot al-barakah). It also "uproots" other wealth. So as-suht is a description of itself and a description of other than itself.

As for it being a description of itself: it is because there is no blessing in it itself. This is as reported in the hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the one who earns unlawful wealth: if he spends it, it will not be blessed for him; if he gives it in charity, it will not be accepted from him; and if he leaves it behind, it will be his provision to the Fire.[Narrated by Ahmad (3672) with the wording: "No servant earns wealth from what is unlawful, then spends from it and it is blessed for him, nor gives it in charity and it is accepted from him, nor leaves it behind him except that it becomes his provision to the Fire."]

Student: Some scholars who are known for good intention have made errors in creed (...) from its place. Do these fall under the hadith (...)?

Shaykh: Yes, these fall under this. The correct view is that there is no difference between what is called "principles" (usul) and "branches" (furu'), as long as the text permits ijtihad and a person interprets it. Then one does not say that this person is sinful in every case. But this error that he committed, from one who is known for goodness and intending goodness: do we follow him in it or not? No. For this reason, the one who says it may be excused, but the one who follows him is not excused.

Student: The one who is between two parties and deviates from (...) or a legal fatwa?

Shaykh: Yes, this differs.

Student: He deviates from his own desire to the desire of the second.

Shaykh: This, may Allah bless you, differs according to circumstances. It may reach the level of disbelief and it may not reach disbelief.

Student: Some people revile even (...), meaning even (...). What they see is known among people to be the truth (...) a fatwa from the shaykhs, and he reviles...

Shaykh: There is no doubt. Some people hate the truth and hate the one who speaks the truth.

Student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. You divided disbelief into two parts and did not mention the second part: ignorance?

Shaykh: Disbelief of ignorance?

Student: (...) worshippers of the cross, or worshippers of (...) who was neither obstinate nor supportive. What is his ruling?

Shaykh: No. If these were ignorant, Allah would pardon them. But now, after the sending of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, they were obstinate, not (...) ignorance.

Student: (...) obstinate or...?

Shaykh: No, we say: obstinate, there is no doubt. The Christians are obstinate. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, then does not believe in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire."[Narrated by Muslim (153 / 240) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]

Student: In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they found therein a wall about to collapse﴾ (al-Kahf 18:77). Is this evidence that inanimate objects have a will?

Shaykh: Yes. ﴿about to collapse﴾: inanimate objects have a will. Did not the Prophet ﷺ say: "This is Uhud, it loves us and we love it"?[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4422) and Muslim (1392 / 503) from the hadith of Abu Humaid al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him.] Answer.

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: Did he not say so? Was the glorification of the pebbles not heard in the presence of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him?[Narrated by al-Bazzar (4044) and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (1244), from the hadith of Abu Dhar.] Does Allah not say: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their exalting﴾ (al-Isra' 17:44)? All of this indicates that inanimate objects have a will.

Student: May Allah reward you with good, O Shaykh. We said that as-suht has two descriptions: a description of itself, because there is no blessing in it, and a description of other than itself (...)?

Shaykh: Yes. Its description of itself is that there is no blessing in it itself. Its description in relation to others is that it uproots the blessing of others. That is, when unlawful wealth enters lawful wealth, it uproots it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever you give in usury that it may increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah. But whatever you give in zakah, seeking the countenance of Allah, those are the multipliers [of reward]﴾ (al-Rum 30:39).

Student: It indicates that inanimate objects...

Shaykh: Yes. ﴿they found therein a wall about to collapse﴾ (al-Kahf 18:77). Inanimate objects have a will. Did not the Prophet ﷺ say: "This is Uhud, a mountain that loves us and we love it"?[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4422) and Muslim (1392 / 503), with the wording: "And this is Uhud, a mountain that loves us and we love it," from the hadith of Abu Humaid.] Answer.

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: Did he not say so?

Student: Yes indeed.

Shaykh: Is the glorification of the pebbles not heard in the presence of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him?[Narrated by al-Bazzar in al-Musnad (4040) and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (6 / 64), from the hadith of Abu Dhar.]
Does Allah not say: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their exalting﴾ (al-Isra' 17:44)? All of this indicates that inanimate objects have a will.

Student: May Allah reward you with good, O Shaykh. We said that as-suht has two descriptions: a description of itself, because it has no blessing in it, and a description of other than itself (...).

Shaykh: The description of itself is that there is no blessing in it itself. The description of other than itself is that it uproots the blessing of others. That is, unlawful wealth, when it enters lawful wealth, uproots it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever you give in usury that it may increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah. But whatever you give in zakah, seeking the countenance of Allah, those are the multipliers [of reward]﴾ (al-Rum 30:39).

Student: May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. The kawni (universal, cosmic) decree, when it is brought in the sense of accusation, does it indicate what the shar'i (legislative) decree indicates?

Shaykh: No. The shar'i decree is legislation (tashri'), and the kawni decree is in the sense of creation (khalq).

Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you: whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion, and then it becomes clear to him that it is not correct, does not retract his interpretation. What do we say to him?

Shaykh: We say: this is a distorter of words (muharrif lil-kalim). It is obligatory upon whoever interprets the Qur'an, or the Sunnah, or understands the words of the scholars with an understanding contrary to the truth, to return and announce this. This is an elevation for him in this world and the Hereafter.

Student: May Allah be good to you. Is the distortion of verses about the attributes (ayat al-sifat) more severe than the distortion of other verses?

Shaykh: Yes. The distortion of verses about the attributes is more severe for two reasons. First: because of the nobility of its subject, since research into the names and attributes of Allah is the most noble of the sciences; so much so that they used to call it al-Fiqh al-Akbar (the Greatest Jurisprudence, i.e., creed).
Second: because the intellect has no scope in it. The obligation upon a person regarding it is submission and not engaging in distortion. Distortion, then, is more severe than when a person distorts a verse about a legal ruling, for example, or a hadith, because the former relates to the Creator, and the latter relates to the created.

Student: We said: those whom we consider good and (...) the Sunnah in many matters. But regarding some verses, the verses of attributes, they interpret them. We said: they are excused in that if the interpretation is permissible (sa'igh). But is there no permissible interpretation for the verses of attributes?

Shaykh: No. There is, because they understood, and it is a mistaken understanding, that affirming them according to their apparent meaning entails anthropomorphism (tashbih). For example, one says: if I say "He istawa over the Throne" meaning that He rose above the Throne and settled upon it, then I have made Him a body, and bodies are alike, and similar objections. Likewise regarding the matter of the two hands and the two eyes. But if one says: "istawa over the Throne" meaning that He (...) the Throne, we say: that does not hold, because it is not permissible.

Student: The permissible interpretation.

Shaykh: Every interpretation that has a basis in the language is a permissible interpretation.

Student: This has no basis.

Shaykh: No, it has a basis: that istiwa' means the figurative elevation (al-'uluww al-ma'nawi), and figurative elevation means sovereignty and dominance (...). In any case, these are their objections.

Student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. You mentioned that in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:41), this has occurred. Is this only when it occurred to them, or does it continue until the Day of Resurrection?

Shaykh: How?

Student: For them in this world...

Shaykh: No. The apparent meaning is that when punishment befalls a people for a cause, whenever that cause is found, its people deserve that punishment.

Student: That means this (...).

Shaykh: But we cannot judge it upon each individual by name. What occurred has occurred, and whoever shares in their deeds deserves a similar punishment.

Student: Only the Jews of Khaybar and others.

Shaykh: And others, upon whom humiliation fell during the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him (...).

* * *

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful gain. So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly. (42) And how would they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And they are not believers﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:42-43).

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you﴾. Are there two readings here?

Student: ﴿yuhzinka﴾ and ﴿yahzunka﴾.

Shaykh: Two readings: recite them for me verbally.

Student: ﴿la yahzunka﴾ and ﴿la yuhzinka﴾.

Shaykh: ﴿la yahzunka﴾ and ﴿la yuhzinka﴾: vocalize them for me.

Student: The first with a sukun on the ha', and the second with a dammah.

Shaykh: Wrong. Both have a sukun on the ha'.

Student: ﴿la yahzunka﴾, the first with a dammah on the zay.

Shaykh: With a dammah on what?

Student: With a dammah on the zay.

Shaykh: With a dammah on the zay, and the second?

Student: With a kasrah on it.

Shaykh: Good. Do they not differ in anything else? They do not differ in anything else?

Student: The first has a sukun on the ya', and the second has a dammah.

Shaykh: The first has a sukun on the ya'? That is not possible, you cannot pronounce that?

Student: The first has a fathah on the ya', and the second has a dammah.

Shaykh: Good, excellent.

How does He say: ﴿Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you﴾? Is the address to the Messenger ﷺ, or to everyone to whom the address is directed?

Student: The address here is to the Messenger: ﴿O Messenger﴾.

Shaykh: To the Messenger, you are correct. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among those who are Jews are listeners﴾. Is the sentence resumptive (mustanafah), or conjoined (ma'tufah) to what precedes it?

Student: Resumptive.

Shaykh: Resumptive. How would you parse it (i'rab) if it is resumptive?

Student: ﴿among those who are Jews are listeners﴾: "listeners" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being...

Shaykh: Wrong.

Student: "They are listeners."

Shaykh: Wrong.

Student: "Listeners" is an adjective for an omitted noun: "they are listeners."

Shaykh: Yes, but what is its place in the parsing?

Student: A subject (mubtada').

Shaykh: A subject. Where is the predicate?

Student: ﴿among those who are Jews﴾.

Shaykh: ﴿among those who are Jews﴾ is the fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam). His saying, exalted is He: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾. Does it have two meanings?

Student: "Listeners to falsehood" means they listen to those who lie about them, and they are their rabbis, whose lies are told to them.

Shaykh: Then the lam is for transitivity (ta'diyah) or for emphasis, as you wish? The second meaning?

Student: The second meaning: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾, meaning they listen to the words of the Prophet ﷺ and distort them and lie.

Shaykh: And lie concerning it. Then the lam is?

Student: ﴿lil-kadhib﴾ is causal (ta'liliyyah).

Shaykh: Causal, correct. Shall we adopt one of them without the other?

Student: We adopt both meanings.

Shaykh: Both meanings, on what principle?

Student: On the principle that if a verse includes two valid meanings with no preponderance of one over the other, we adopt both meanings together.

Shaykh: Two valid meanings, and no preponderance of one over the other...

Student: We adopt both meanings together.

Shaykh: Do we not say there is a third? And there is no contradiction?

Student: Between them.

Shaykh: It is carried to both meanings. On the first view: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾, with the lam being for transitivity or for emphasis, what is its meaning?

Student: The lam is for transitivity, the verb...

Shaykh: When we say "for transitivity or for emphasis," the meaning becomes "listeners, falsehood."

Student: When the governing element is weak.

Shaykh: Leave it. I am not saying that. What is the function of the lam? I am asking what its meaning is.

Student: It means they accept the lie as true.

Shaykh: Yes. And the lie comes from whom?

Student: From their rabbis.

Shaykh: From their rabbis, good.
﴿listeners to falsehood﴾: meaning they listen to what their rabbis tell them, and it is a lie. This is when we make the lam for what?

Students: For emphasis.

Shaykh: For emphasis. On the second view, that the lam is causal?

Student: That they hear the speech from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and then distort it according to what their desires dictate.

Shaykh: That is: in order that they may say, "We heard such-and-such," while they are liars?

Student: Yes, so that they distort it to what they hold, and present it to the common Jews.

Shaykh: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾: meaning they listen to the words of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in order to lie, and say to the people: "Muhammad told us such-and-such"?

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: This is the meaning. His saying: ﴿listeners to another people who have not come to you﴾. Who are these other people?

Student: The other people are the common Jews who did not come to the Prophet ﷺ.

Shaykh: Are they their leaders, or ordinary people? Good. ﴿they distort words after their places﴾. What is the meaning of "distort"?

Student: They change and alter.

Shaykh: They change it, either in wording or in meaning.

What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿If you are given this, take it, and if you are not given it, beware﴾?

Student: ﴿If you are given this﴾: the distorted ruling, so take it. ﴿And if you are not given it﴾: beware, meaning do not take it.

Shaykh: That is: if Muhammad agrees with what you want, take it, is that right?

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: And otherwise?

Student: Beware.

Shaykh: Beware.

It is well known that giving (ita') occurs with tangible, transferable things, but it may also be used for meanings, as here. For the meaning of ﴿If you are given this, take it﴾ is: if Muhammad agrees with you, take it; otherwise reject it and beware of him. The origin of this verse was revealed concerning what? Concerning two Jews who committed adultery.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify﴾. Is the will here legislative or universal?

Student: Universal.

Shaykh: Universal. What is the difference between the universal will and the legislative will?

Student: The legislative will is what Allah loves, and the universal will does not necessarily mean that He loves it.

Shaykh: The legislative is what Allah loves, and it does not necessarily entail...?

Student: That Allah loves it.

Shaykh: How can you say "what Allah loves," then say "it does not necessarily mean that Allah loves it"?
Now, the legislative will is found in what?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 42 (part 2 of 3):**

* The student: In what He loves.
* The Shaykh: And it does not necessarily entail it?
* The student: It does not necessarily entail it, Shaykh, that it occurs.
* The Shaykh: It does not necessarily entail the occurrence of what is willed, the universal (kawniyyah) will?
* The student: It does not necessarily entail it..
* The Shaykh: It occurs?
* The student: It occurs in what Allah loves and what He does not love.
* The Shaykh: It occurs in what Allah loves and what He does not love, and it entails?
* The student: That it occurs.
* The Shaykh: It entails the occurrence of what is willed.

The Exalted said: ﴿If Allah intends some harm for me, can they remove His harm?﴾ [al-Zumar 38]. What is the will (iradah) here?

* Student: The will here is universal (kawniyyah): ﴿If Allah intends some harm for me﴾.
* The Shaykh: Universal?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Correct. The Exalted said: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41]. What is the disgrace in this world?
* Student: The disgrace in this world is that Allah, glorified and exalted, exposes them.
* The Shaykh: Is the exposure in defeat and clarification?
* The student: In the clarification of their condition.
* The Shaykh: And the clarification of their condition. As for the Hereafter, they have a great punishment whose reality is not known, because it is among the unseen matters.

* * *

The Exalted said: ﴿They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawfully gained﴾ [al-Ma'idah 42].

﴿Listeners﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject; that is, they are listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful gain. Is this sentence an emphasis (ta'kid) of what preceded, or is it different from it?

It admits both meanings. It may be an emphasis of what preceded, meaning the situation is grave and requires repeating the description of their ugly qualities. It may also be different from what preceded, by taking the lam in the first case as reinforcing and in the second as causal (lam al-ta'lil).

Now we say: is the sentence here an emphasis of what preceded, or is it not an emphasis?

We say: on this there are two opinions among the scholars. The first: it is an emphasis, and emphasis was needed because the situation is important and requires stressing by describing their qualities, to be wary of them. The second: it may be different from the first, by taking the lam in the first as reinforcing and this one as causal, or the reverse.

And His words ﴿devourers﴾ (akkalun) is an intensive form indicating their great consumption of the unlawful gain.

And (al-suht) has two readings: ﴿lil-suhuti﴾ with a damma on the ha', and ﴿lil-suhti﴾ with a sukun on the ha'; both are canonical (sab'iyyah) readings.

So what is al-suht? Is it consuming wealth falsely? Is it consuming usury (riba)? Is it bribery (rashwah)?

The answer: it includes all of that. The general meaning is that al-suht is everything acquired through a forbidden earning. Whatever is acquired through a forbidden earning is suht, and this includes usury, bribery, usurpation (ghasb), theft, and other things. Its reason is that the unlawful uproots (yasht) the lawful, removing its blessing, or that the unlawful itself is suht, it is uprooted and disappears and has no blessing in it.

﴿Then if they come to you﴾ means: to judge between them.

﴿So judge between them or turn away from them﴾. The address here is to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and his community is likewise addressed: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example﴾ [al-Ahzab 21].

But the subject in His words ﴿if they come to you﴾: does it refer to the dhimmis or the mu'ahadun (those with treaties), or to every disbeliever, or to every believer, or what?

We say: as for the believer, it is not permissible to turn away from judging among Muslims. It is not permissible to turn away from judging among Muslims, especially one who has been entrusted with that matter. Like whom?

* Student: Judges.
* The Shaykh: Judges. It is not permissible for any judge, when two litigants bring their dispute to him, to excuse himself; rather he must judge between them. The arbitrator (muhakkam) who is not a judge may judge or may not judge. But if he is asked for a fatwa, he must give a ruling according to the law of Allah. As for arbitration, it is optional: if he wishes he accepts, and if he wishes he does not. For example, if there is a dispute between two relatives who say: "We do not want to go to the judge, but we will appoint so-and-so as arbiter," he is not obliged to rule. But there is no doubt that it becomes more binding upon him to rule, because it ends the dispute and clarifies the ruling of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Yet he should not rule until he has secured the trust of all parties.

As for non-Muslims, the correct view is that a person is free: if he wishes he judges, and if he wishes he does not judge, whether they are dhimmis under our rule, or mu'ahadun separated from us, or harbis (belligerents). The harbi generally cannot come, because if he came he would be killed, since his blood is lawful to shed.

﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them﴾. Here we say: is the (aw) here for diversification (tanwi') or for choice (takhyir)?

* Students: For choice.
* The Shaykh: It is for choice. And if it is for choice, is it a choice of desire or of benefit? We say it is a choice of benefit, which we will mention in the benefits, if Allah wills.

﴿And if you turn away from them, they will never harm you at all﴾: neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. If you turn away from them and do not judge between them, they will not harm you. But they may hurt you, and hurt does not necessarily entail harm. The proof is that Allah, glorified and exalted, affirmed that the children of Adam hurt Him, and negated that anyone could harm Him. He, may He be exalted, said: "O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me" [narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from Abu Dharr]. Likewise in the Quran: ﴿Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all﴾ [Ali 'Imran 176].

Hurt is affirmed in the Quran and in the sacred hadiths. Allah said in the Quran: ﴿Indeed, those who hurt Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Ahzab 57]. And He said in a sacred hadith: "The son of Adam hurts Me; he reviles time" [agreed upon: al-Bukhari (4826) and Muslim (2246/2) from Abu Hurayrah]. So harm is negated of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by the Quran and the sacred hadiths, while hurt is affirmed?

* The students: Affirmed.
* The Shaykh: Affirmed. It is known that hurt does not necessarily entail harm. The proof: if a man sits beside someone eating onions, does he feel hurt by it or not?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Does it harm him?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: It does not harm him. ﴿If you turn away from them, they will never harm you at all﴾. But it may be hurt; harm, however, is not.

And His words ﴿at all﴾ (shay'an) is an indefinite noun in a negative context with (lan), so it is general: any harm at all, they will never inflict upon you, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

﴿And if you judge﴾ means: if you choose to judge. ﴿Then judge between them with justice﴾.

﴿If you judge﴾ means: if you see fit to judge and choose to judge. ﴿Then judge between them with justice﴾. What is justice (qist)?

* Student: Fairness (al-'adl).
* The Shaykh: Fairness, even if the judgment is for a disbeliever against a Muslim, correct? If it is for a disbeliever against a Muslim, does he judge against him?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: He judges with fairness. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, even said: one must be fair between the two litigants, even between a Muslim and a disbeliever, in speech, in glance, in seating, in precedence, and in everything, because this is a judgment in which one must be just. 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, sent him to estimate the fruit for the Jews, gathered them and said: "I have come to you from the most beloved of people to me." Who is meant?

* The students: The Messenger, peace be upon him.
* The Shaykh: The Messenger, peace be upon him. "And you are more hateful to me than your numbers of monkeys and pigs" — may Allah be pleased with him, a brave word — "and my love for him and my hatred for you do not compel me to be unjust to you." Otherwise it is known that human nature inclines toward those it loves and against those it hates. But he says: I cannot fail to be just to you. "They said: By this the heavens and the earth stand" [narrated by Abu Dawud (3410) and Ibn Majah (1820) from Ibn 'Abbas]. And he was just with them, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿So judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾. This is an exhortation to justice in everything. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ in everything, meaning the just. For this reason there is the authentic hadith: "Indeed, those who act justly will be on pulpits of light at the right hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, those who are just regarding their families and what they are entrusted with" [narrated by Muslim (1827/18) from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

So who is the muqsit?

* Students: The just one.
* The Shaykh: The just one. What is the muqsit?
* Student: The just one.
* The Shaykh: And the qasit?
* The student: The oppressor.
* The Shaykh: The tyrant. ﴿As for the qasitun, they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Jinn 15]. But the muqsit is the just one.

* In the verse there are many benefits, among them: affirming that these Jews are listeners to falsehood, by His words ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾.

If someone says: the well-known rule objects to your statement "emphasis": when speech is between foundation (ta'sis) and emphasis (ta'kid), it is taken as what?

* The students: As foundation.
* The Shaykh: As foundation. We say: yes, this is an objection, but it has a response, an answer.

The answer: if we say it is foundation, then the first sentence indicates one meaning and the second indicates one meaning. If we say it is emphasis, then each of them indicates two meanings, and therefore it is preferred that it is emphasis.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: warning against this ugly attribute, which is what? Listening to falsehood or transmitting falsehood, because Allah emphasized the description of this ugly attribute among the Jews.

* And from it: whoever is characterized by that has a resemblance to the Jews.
