The diseases of the hearts are likewise varied, but they revolve around two things: either doubt (shubhah) or desire (shahwah). All diseases of the hearts do not depart from these two matters. Doubt: in that the truth becomes confused for him with falsehood — may Allah protect us — and he is not guided to the truth. This is the disease of what? Doubt, and its cause is ignorance. For this reason every person must remove this disease from himself by learning — learning the Shari'ah.

The second is the disease of desire: that is, a disease of will and craving, such that he does not want the truth despite knowing it. This is worse than the first, because the first may hope for its rectification — when? When he learns. But this one is not hoped to be rectified, except if Allah wills, because this person knows the truth but has not acted upon it, and this is more severe.

But know that the disease, as I said, is of kinds. In the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾ [al-Ahzab 32] — who is this? A disease of desire, in love of women and delight in their voices, whose hearing is forbidden, and the like.

But in the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them defilement upon their defilement﴾ [al-Tawbah 124-125] — I seek refuge in Allah. ﴿In whose hearts is a disease﴾ means doubt and hypocrisy. These do not increase by the verses except in defilement added to their defilement. May Allah protect us and you from that, and we ask Allah for us and for you steadfastness.

* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, is there a desire greater than doubt?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The student: And innovations, O Shaykh, are founded upon doubts.

* The Shaykh: No — and desires too. For this reason, one argues with the innovator using the evidences from the Book and the Sunnah; it is said: "The intended meaning is such-and-such."

* A student: We have understood the form of allying with the disbelievers. What is the form of allying with the people of innovation? And is this not only in times of war?

* The Shaykh: Yes, like the alliance with the disbelievers. Among their alliance is lessening their innovations and attempting to mix these with those — the people of innovation with the people of the Sunnah and the followers of the Salaf.

* A student: O Shaykh, does the use by many Muslims of the Christian calendar (birth date) instead of the Hijri calendar count as alliance?

* The Shaykh: Yes. The Muslims' shift now from the Arabic Hijri calendar to the calendar of the Jews and Christians is undoubtedly a kind of alliance. For this reason Imam Ahmad disliked saying (Adhar-mah) — yes, and the like. And it is strange of us, we Arabs: our adherence now to the Hijri calendar requires two things. The first: Arabness. The second: religion, because it is based on a great occasion, which is the Hijrah by which the Islamic state was formed. For this reason, when they differed in the time of 'Umar about whether to make the calendar from the Mission (al-Ba'thah) or from the birth of the Messenger, he said: No, from the Hijrah, because the Hijrah is what brought about the formation of the Islamic state. Thus they made the calendar from the Hijrah, and did not make it from Rabi' al-Awwal, because the occasion of it being in Muharram is stronger than the occasion of it being in Rabi' al-Awwal, since people return from the season — the season of Hajj — after they have performed the obligation of Hajj.

* * *
* A student: ﴿They hasten toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us. But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him, and they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful." (52) And those who believed will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers." (53) O you who believed, whoever of you reverts from his religion — Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah and not fearing the blame of a blamer. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Ma'idah 52-54].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. When Allah, glorified and exalted, forbade the believers from taking the Jews and Christians as allies, He made clear that among people there are those in whose hearts is a disease who hasten toward these Jews and Christians. So He, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them﴾, and we have explained this before. ﴿They say, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾ — we explained that they say this with their tongues among themselves, or when a blamer blames them, and they also say it in their hearts.

And al-Dā'irah (the misfortune) is that which destroys. Then Allah Most High said: ﴿But perhaps Allah...﴾

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾

We have spoken about disease, the diseases of the hearts, and that they are varied like the diseases of the bodies; and that His saying ﴿hastening toward them﴾, rather than "hastening in their alliance", is because this is more general — meaning in their alliance and their affection...

I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. When Allah, glorified and exalted, forbade the believers from taking the Jews and Christians as allies, He made clear that among people there are those in whose hearts is a disease who hasten toward these Jews and Christians, so He, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 52], and we have explained this before.

﴿They say, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾ — we explained that they say this with their tongues among themselves, or when a blamer blames them, and they also say it in their hearts.

And (al-Dā'irah) is that which destroys. Then Allah said: ﴿But perhaps Allah...﴾ — before that?

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾ — we spoke about the diseases of the hearts and that they are varied like the diseases of the bodies.

And that His saying ﴿hastening toward them﴾, and He did not say "hastening in their alliance," because this is more general: in their alliance, their affection, and in all their affairs.

﴿They say﴾ — that is, they say with their tongues to one another, and with their hearts also.

﴿We fear﴾ — that is, we are afraid. ﴿That a misfortune may befall us﴾ — that is, a calamity of the calamities of time, so we ally with these in order that we may have a hand with them in which we seek refuge.

The Exalted says: ﴿But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest﴾. ("Perhaps," 'asā, is among the verbs of hope, but with respect to Allah, Exalted — that is, to His act, glorified and exalted — we cannot say that it is for hope, because hope is the wishing for what is somewhat difficult to attain, and nothing is difficult for Allah, Exalted. For this reason some exegetes said, and I think it is Ibn 'Abbas: "'Asā from Allah is obligatory."[[Ma'rifat al-Sunan wa al-Athar (17626).]] That is, it means truly it will occur. But He, glorified and exalted, expresses it with "'asā," as in ﴿Perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾ [al-Nisa' 99] and the like, so that the heart is attached in hope to Allah, Exalted. For if He had informed that this would happen, one would rely on this truthful report, that it would occur; but when it is said "fa-'asā," the heart becomes attached in hope to Allah, blessed and exalted.)

﴿But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest﴾ — al-fath (the conquest) here means victory, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿If you seek a conquest, then the conquest has certainly come to you﴾ [al-Anfal 19] — meaning: if you seek victory, then victory has come to you.

It is said that what is meant by the conquest is the conquest of Makkah, but the correct view is the first, namely that what is meant is victory, so that it includes the conquest of Makkah and other than it.

﴿Or a command from Him﴾ — "a command from Him" means an affair from Him: in exposing the disgraceful deeds of those in whose hearts is a disease, who are the hypocrites, so that He exposes them. Allah, blessed and exalted, has exposed them with the utmost exposure in the Qur'an, in Surat al-Tawbah, in Surat al-Hashr and elsewhere. Allah exposed them and made clear their disgraceful deeds. So "a command from Him" is what?

* Students: The matter.

* The Shaykh: The command is the matter, but what is meant by it? The exposure of those in whose hearts is a disease, because those in whose hearts is a disease come to the Muslims and say, "We are Muslims," and they pretend to be Muslim: ﴿And when they go privately to their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].

﴿Then they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾ — the word "yusbihu" (they will become) here means: their affair will lead to this, whether they perceive that in the evening or perceive it in the morning. This is a common linguistic expression: one says "so-and-so became regretful" (asbaha fulan nadiman), and his regret may be in the night or in the evening, so the expression "becoming morning" (al-isbah) is sometimes used for the occurrence of a thing at any time whatsoever.

He said: ﴿Then they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾. ("Yusbihu") — where is the nun in it?

* Students: It is omitted.

* The Shaykh: Why?

* Students: Because it is conjoined (ma'tufah).

* The Shaykh: Conjoined to what?

* Students: To ﴿an yaʾtiya﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring a conquest, or a command from Him﴾, so "that they become" (an yusbihū) ﴿over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾ — it falls under the report of "'asā."

And His saying ﴿over what they had concealed within themselves﴾ means what they hid within themselves, from whom? From the believers, for they hide from the believers that they hasten toward these, but Allah, Exalted, exposes them. ﴿Over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾ — "regretful" is the predicate of "yusbihu," and for this reason it came with the "yā'" (nādimīn, in the masculine plural).

And "al-nadam" (regret) is an emotional reaction to what has escaped a person of something whose doing or saying is ugly. This is regret, and each one of us feels within himself the sense of regret, because it is an emotional reaction that arises from what? From grief over what has passed of something whose doing or saying is ugly. For this reason, regret is among the conditions of repentance.

In this noble verse, Allah, blessed and exalted, makes clear that those in whose hearts is a disease, who are the hypocrites, hasten in their affection. * Several benefits are derived from it. Among them: that everyone who hastens in befriending the disbelievers and in supporting them has a disease in his heart, and it follows from this that this disease may increase until it reaches disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* Among its benefits: the strong warning against allying with these disbelievers and hastening toward them.

* Among its benefits: that whoever hastens toward them has a disease in his heart.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the weakness of the hypocrites' reliance upon Allah, and that they only rely upon material matters in which they expect victory; from His saying: ﴿They hasten toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾.

* Among its benefits: that whoever advises the rulers to hasten in affection for the disbelievers and in supporting them, there is in that a resemblance to these hypocrites. Shaykh Muhammad Rashid Rida has spoken well on this verse in his tafsir, that the rulers of the Muslims — by which he means the rulers of the Muslims in the place where he is, who have been made subservient by the disbelievers — hasten in affection for the disbelievers and in supporting them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the good tidings to the believers that conquest and victory will be theirs; from His saying: ﴿But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the hypocrite will inevitably be exposed by Allah; taken from His saying: ﴿or a command from Him﴾. This is observed, as al-Hasan said: "No one conceals a secret except that Allah makes it appear on the features of his face and in the slips of his tongue,"[[See Sharh al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah (1/152).]] the hypocrite's hypocrisy must appear unless he repents to Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the hypocrites of what will befall them of regret over what they concealed within themselves; from His saying: ﴿Then they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed will say﴾. In this verse there are three readings: ﴿wa-yaqūlu﴾, ﴿wa-yaqūla﴾, and a third reading ﴿yaqūlu﴾ without the waw. This is among the strange readings, that a letter is dropped from the Qur'an in one of the readings. A similar case passed us in which surah?

* A student: Al 'Imran.

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* A student: ﴿wa-sāriʿū﴾ [Al 'Imran 133].

* The Shaykh: How is ﴿wa-sāriʿū﴾?

* A student: ﴿wa-sāriʿū﴾ is read with the waw and without the waw.

* The Shaykh: I don't know; if that is so, I have forgotten it. But one passed us in—?

* A student: Al-Fatihah.

* The Shaykh: Al-Fatihah?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, that is different; the word is one, but a letter dropped passed us in al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing (115). And they say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾ [al-Baqarah 115-116]. In it there is a reading: ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing (115). Qālū ittakhadha Allāhu waladan﴾ with the waw dropped.

As for Al 'Imran, ﴿wa-sāriʿū﴾, review it now: there is a reading with the waw omitted. So there are now three verses: in al-Baqarah, in Al 'Imran, and in surat al-Ma'idah.

The point is that there are three readings: with raf', and with nasb while the waw is retained, and with raf' while the waw is omitted.

﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 53:

﴿Those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they were truly with you?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 53] The interrogative here is for expressing wonder; meaning: marvel, O people, at those who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they were truly with you. There is no doubt that the hypocrites swear by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they are with the believers: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14], and ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah"﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

﴿Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths?⁠﴾ So for what is the interrogative? It is for expressing wonder; meaning: marvel, O human being, at these who say, "Indeed we are with you," how their state was.

﴿Those who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths⁠﴾ ("swore by Him") means they took an oath by Him. Iqsam (swearing), hilf (swearing) and yamin (oath) have one meaning, which is affirming a matter by mentioning something revered, in a specific form. This is the qasam: affirming a matter by mentioning something revered in a particular form, namely the letters waw, ba' and ta', which are the particles of oath: you say "wallahi," you say "billahi," and you say "tallahi." Thus there must be an affirmation, the sworn-by must be revered, and it must be in this form.

There are things that carry the meaning of an oath but are not an oath in technical terms, such as swearing by divorce, swearing by a vow, and swearing by saying "la'amruka" and what resembles them; these are not technically oaths, even though their meaning is the meaning of an oath.

﴿They swore by Allah⁠﴾: thus ﴿they swore⁠﴾ means they took an oath, and iqsam, hilf and yamin mean affirming a matter by mentioning something revered in a specific form.

﴿With their most emphatic oaths⁠﴾ means with the strongest of oaths. The strongest of oaths is either by the form, or by linking it with testimony, or by linking it with a curse upon the one swearing, and the like. For example, if he says, "I testify by Allah, swearing by Him, that such-and-such," this is emphasized by testimony; and if he says, "By Allah, I will certainly do such-and-such," this is emphasized by the form. These people swore with the strongest and most intense form of swearing.

﴿Indeed they are with you⁠﴾: with whom? With the believers. They swear by this that they are with them, but they are not with them.

As for His saying, ﴿Their deeds have become void⁠﴾: it has been said that it may be part of what is said, and it may be a fresh statement from Allah. If we say it is part of the speech, it becomes like a reason or an explanation for His saying, ﴿Indeed they are with you⁠﴾; as if He said: "And they are not with you, because their deeds have become void," and deeds are not voided except by disbelief, and the disbeliever is certainly not with the believer.

It has also been said that it is from Allah: that is, Allah informs the believers that these people's deeds have become void, even though they feign Islam, for their deeds are void. The voiding of a thing means its going away in vain, not benefiting from it and not being counted.

﴿Their deeds have become void⁠﴾: here "deeds" (al-'amal) includes speech, action and belief when used absolutely; and when deeds are linked with speech, the intended meaning becomes the deeds of the limbs.

﴿Their deeds have become void, so they became losers⁠﴾: we have said that "asbaha" here means "saara" (became), meaning that by this deed they became losers. Thus there is regret for them, as mentioned in the first verse, and there is loss for them, may Allah protect us, and they have not profited and will not profit either, even though the hypocrites believe that they are the successful ones, that they are the reformers, that they are the ones who intended goodness and success; but in reality they are the corrupters, and there is no goodness or success for them, rather they are the losers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to speak in the manner of expressing wonder about one who deserves to be wondered at, and this is not considered backbiting, because Allah the Exalted mentioned this about the believers and did not disapprove of it, but mentioned it as one praising them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lying of the hypocrites, and that they promote their falsehood and hypocrisy through oaths. For this reason some people have said: if you see one who multiplies oaths where no multiplication of oaths is needed, know that he is a liar, because he wants to promote his lie through multiplying oaths; otherwise the truthful person does not need to multiply oaths, nor even to swear at all, for he is confident in himself, unless the addressee is denying or doubtful, in which case he may affirm it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the hypocrites swear by Allah and display the glorification of Allah, just as they mention Allah, pray and give charity, but all of this does not benefit them because of the absence of faith in their hearts—may Allah protect us and you from that. Because of the absence of faith, all of this does not benefit them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the deed of the hypocrite is void, as His saying shows: ﴿Their deeds have become void⁠﴾, and his deed cannot benefit him. If he gives charity, does charity benefit him? It does not benefit him; in the Hereafter, certainly it does not benefit him; in this world he may be rewarded for it with blessing in his wealth and its increase, so that it benefits others, but in the Hereafter he certainly does not benefit from it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the hypocrite is a loser, whatever profit he imagines, for he is a loser. The reason is that if Allah exposes him in this world, he is made clear, loses, and becomes hated among people; and if Allah does not expose him in this world, then in the Hereafter. Then he does not benefit from his worldly life, because he has lost both this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 54 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion - Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54]. We have already discussed His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾ and the purpose of introducing the address with the vocative and then with the description of faith.

As for His words ﴿whoever reverts﴾ (man yartadd), there are two recitations: yartadid, with the doubled letter unmerged (fakk al-idgham), and yartadd, with idgham (assimilation). On the recitation yartadid, the verb is jussive (majzum), and the jazm is apparent through the conditional particle (man). But what is the case of ﴿man yartadd﴾?

* Student: It is jussive.
* The Shaykh: No, it is in the fatha, brothers!
* Student: The sukun is merged into the vowel of the yā'.
* The Shaykh: We say: when the dal was assimilated into the other, the second was given a fatha because two sakins came together (iltiqa' al-sakinayn).

﴿whoever among you reverts from his religion﴾. ﴿From his religion﴾ means: from his practice by which he worships Allah, which is worship ('ibadah).

﴿Then Allah will bring forth a people﴾. The fa' is the connecting particle (rabitah) for the answer, i.e., the answer of the condition, because this is one of the seven positions in which the fa' must accompany the answer when it comes as the answer of a condition. The rest are mentioned in the verse of which is it? 

It is a nominal clause, an imperative or prohibitive, and with a rigid (non-derived) word, and with ma, qad, lan, and with the particles of future (tanfis).

These are seven positions which, when they occur as the answer of a condition, whether the condition is a jussive particle or not, must be accompanied by the fa', and it may be omitted only rarely, especially under the necessity of poetry, as in the words of the poet:

Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them...

The correct form is to say (fa-Allah), because it is a nominal clause.

﴿So Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾. They said: sawfa and the sin agree in indicating emphasis, but they differ in that the sin indicates immediacy, while sawfa indicates delay.

﴿a people He loves and who love Him﴾: ﴿a people﴾ means: other than the apostates. We have not yet spoken about what apostasy is. Apostasy from the religion is confined to two things: either denial (juhud) or arrogance (istikbar).

If you read everything the jurists mention in the book on the apostate, you will find that it does not go beyond these two matters: juhud, which means denying reports, and istikbar, which means refusing to comply. All apostasy returns to these two matters, and what is mentioned of details is an elaboration and branching out of this sentence.

﴿So Allah will bring forth a people﴾ and He mentioned attributes, so let us enumerate them: ﴿whom He loves﴾, ﴿and who love Him﴾, ﴿humble toward the believers﴾, ﴿mighty against the disbelievers﴾, ﴿who strive in the way of Allah﴾, ﴿and who do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾. Six attributes. That is, if you apostatize, you will not harm Allah at all, nor will you harm Islam at all; rather, Allah will bring forth a people with these attributes.

﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾. So what is the meaning of love? Love is love itself, and you cannot define it more clearly than its own word. Likewise, all emotional matters cannot be defined by more than their own word. If you say: what is anger? Anger is anger.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in the book attributed to him, Rawdat al-Muhibbin, mentioned many names for love, meaning many definitions, but he said: all of them are not valid; each is an explanation of it by its concomitants or its effects or the like.

﴿He loves them﴾ refers to Him, glorified and exalted. ﴿And they love Him﴾. But we must know that the love of Allah differs from the love of a human in its causes, its effects, and its manner, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11].

﴿He loves them and they love Him, humble toward the believers﴾. ﴿Humble toward the believers﴾ means: they do not act arrogantly toward the believers, nor do they exalt themselves over them; rather they lower themselves to them, and they abase themselves before them, i.e., they show humility, as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath 29]. For this reason, ﴿humble﴾ is followed by (ʿalā, "toward") rather than (lām, "to"); that is, He did not say "humble to the believers," but said "humble toward them," meaning: possessing compassion and tenderness toward them, without superiority or arrogance.

﴿Humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾. ﴿Mighty﴾ means: strong, showing the disbelievers strength, dignity, and pride in the religion they follow.

Third: ﴿who strive in the way of Allah﴾. Jihad is exerting effort to attain something, and what is meant here is exerting effort to fight the enemies. Then, if it is to elevate the word of Allah, it is jihad in the way of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ explained jihad in the way of Allah as the fighting that is so that the word of Allah is the highest, not so that he himself may rise. He was asked about the man who fights for courage, for zeal, and for show: which of these is in the way of Allah? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7458) and Muslim (1904 / 150), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] The way of Allah is the path that leads to Him. Allah has attributed it to Himself and attributed it to others, saying: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [al-Nisa 115].

Allah attributed the way to Himself in many verses, and there is no contradiction. Allah attributed the way to Himself for two reasons: first, that He is the One who legislated it and opened the path to Him; second, that it leads to Him, as you say: "This is the road to Makkah," meaning the road that leads to it. As for its attribution to the believers, it is because they are the ones who travel it. So it is attributed to Allah in one respect and to the believers in another, and since the respects differ, there is no contradiction.

He said: ﴿and who do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾. Blame is reproach. That is, a person, when he strives in the way of Allah and becomes mighty against the disbelievers and humble toward the believers, does not fear, and it does not matter to him whether he is blamed or not, because he seeks another goal. He does not want to be praised by people nor dispraised by them; he only seeks the good pleasure of Allah, glorified and exalted.

﴿and who do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾. His words ﴿blame of any blamer﴾ mean: any blame from any blamer. We took "any blame" from the word ﴿blame﴾ alone.

﴿blamer﴾ is indefinite, so it includes everyone who blames, whether from relatives or strangers, friends or others. They do not fear the blame of any blamer.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to having these attributes.

﴿The bounty of Allah﴾ means: His gift and His provision.

﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾. But whenever you read something linked to His will, know that it is necessarily accompanied by wisdom. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills; indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30]. He does not will anything except that He knows that wisdom lies in His will, until He does it, glorified and exalted.

His words ﴿Wide﴾ (wasi'): is it wide in His bounty or in all His attributes? Which is more general?

* Students: In all His attributes.
* The Shaykh: In all His attributes. When a meaning comes to you that is more general, take it, if the text allows it, whether in the Book or the Sunnah. If we say "wide in His bounty and His giving," yes, He is wide in His bounty and giving; but if we say "wide in all His attributes," that is more general, and taking the more general is preferable, because the more specific is included in it.

His words ﴿Knowing﴾ mean: possessing knowledge. Is knowledge wide or not wide? ﴿Wide﴾, as He said: ﴿Wide, Knowing﴾, and Allah said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir 7].

* Among the benefits of this verse: First, an indication that among the believers there will be those who apostatize, from His saying: "whoever reverts, then..." Many exegetes said this: that it is an indication that there will be among the believers those who apostatize. In my own mind there is something about this, because the verse may intend a warning against apostasy regardless of whether it occurs or not. As for its occurrence, there is no doubt that apostasy has occurred.

The scholars said: eleven groups have apostatized: three in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, seven in the time of Abu Bakr, and one in the time of 'Umar, from among the Arab tribes. In the time of the Messenger, Musaylimah, al-Aswad al-'Ansi, and the ruler of Ghassan appeared. In the time of Abu Bakr there were seven groups, all of whom apostatized, but Allah, glorified and exalted, crushed them, and praise be to Allah, and they had no standing, and their lies and apostasy became known.

In short, this is the benefit: that the verse indicates that there will be among the believers those who apostatize. Many exegetes, earlier and later, said this, but it does not appear to me to be clear, since the intention may be a warning, like His saying: ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ [Al 'Imran 144].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah is free of need of the servants; if a people apostatize, Allah brings others, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad 38].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that apostates are hated by Allah. From where is this taken? ﴿So Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah's power, and that when He removes peoples, He brings others better than them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts which He performs by His choice. From where is this taken? ﴿So Allah will bring forth﴾, and (sawfa) is for the future. I mention this because many of the theologians, from the Ash'aris and others, deny that voluntary acts subsist in Allah. They say: there is nothing except the eternal; there is nothing of Allah's attributes except what is eternal; as for something occurring anew, it is not possible. Their reasoning is that occurring events subsist only in an occurring thing. This is without doubt an error. Rather, that Allah's acts are occurring shows His perfection, glorified and exalted, and that He is the doer of what He wills. If we say He does not act, then there is no doubt that this is pure negation and a deficiency ascribed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of love from Allah and to Allah. "From Allah" is in which word? In ﴿He loves them﴾, and "to Allah" in ﴿and they love Him﴾. This verse combines Allah's love for His righteous servants and the love of the righteous servants for Allah.

In many verses there is affirmation of love from Allah toward His righteous servants who deserve it. It is, according to us, the people of the Sunnah who follow what the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) followed, a true love befitting Allah, Mighty and Majestic. According to others, it is not true love; rather they distort it, either as reward or as the will to reward: either as reward, according to those who do not affirm the seven attributes, who affirm reward because reward is separate and created, but they do not make love an attribute subsisting in Allah; or as the will to reward, according to those who affirm the seven attributes, like the Ash'aris. For this reason, you find the Ash'aris interpreting it either as the will to reward or as reward. But they are inconsistent in reality, because reward occurs only through will, and the will to reward something not loved is an impossible and rejected notion, for Allah does not reward a deed except that He loves it and rewards it for it. But they are inconsistent. Likewise, all false doctrines, keep this in mind: you will find all false doctrines inconsistent. The evidence is: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa 82]. For this reason, one of the greatest indications of the weakness or falsehood of a view is that it is self-contradictory. If you see a view is contradictory, know that it is weak and cannot be true.

So we believe that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves and is loved, and that the love a person finds in his heart for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not equaled by any other love. A person loves his child, loves his father, loves his mother, loves his family, loves his friends, but love for Allah is other than this, of another kind, in which a person finds a pleasure and a comfort that none knows except one who has lost it, may Allah protect us. It is a great love, unlike a person's attachment to other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the verse contains a refutation of whom? Of the Ash'aris, the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah, and everyone who does not affirm voluntary acts or does not affirm love.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise for the one who is humble toward the believers, who lowers his wing to them, abases himself, and is humble, for this is among the attributes that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves. The opposite of that...

* A second benefit is derived from it: the opposite of that, namely a person's exalting himself over his believing brothers, is not praised by Allah, nor even by people. Therefore know that the more your faith increases, the more humble you become, and the more your knowledge increases, the more humble you become. Some people, may Allah keep us from them, when their knowledge increases, swell up and become arrogant, and speak to people only through their noses, and when people speak to them, they pretend not to hear, saying: "What are you saying?" while knowing that their hearing is filled with what they say, but out of arrogance. This is without doubt a great deficiency, for the more your knowledge grows, the more your humility should grow.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise for self-respect and strength of character before whom? Before the disbelievers: that we should be mighty over them, seeing in ourselves superiority over them and dominance over them, not by our own persons but by the religion we have, for Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [al-Tawbah 33], for what? ﴿to make it prevail﴾, meaning the religion, or the Messenger who bears the religion.

It is obligatory upon us, the Muslims, to know our worth in the international community, that we are the most worthy of people to remain on the earth, the most worthy of Allah's provision, and the most worthy that we should be superior to them. This is so when we have an Islamic character. But because of weak faith and weak reliance upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, we have become tails to others, mighty among our own people, but humble before the disbelievers. We ask Allah for safety and well-being. We ask Allah to bring about for this Ummah a matter of rectitude in which the people of obedience are honored and the people of disobedience are humbled.

* Student: This, O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, includes even the sinners (...) faith, but a person sees the people of sin and his state is such that even when he sees them he is repulsed by them (...) but he does not leave faith.

* The Shaykh: Look, may Allah bless you. The one who is not free of faith, you do not see yourself as mighty over him nor humble before him; because he has faith which requires that you be humble to him, and he has sin which requires that you be mighty over him. But not as your might over the disbeliever; rather love him for what faith he has, dislike him for what sins he has, and try to reform him. Many sinners now turn away from uprightness because they find from some of those who command good and forbid evil harshness, difficulty, and repulsion. But if they had followed the path of gentleness, much good would have resulted.

* Student: Sometimes a person meets someone (...) simple, and in a good manner he says: "What is it to you? What is it to you, are you anxious?"

* The Shaykh: It is not contrary [to the Sunnah] if he says "What is it to you," and you say: "Brother, you are my brother, and the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. Be patient, be patient over what has befallen you." But to say (...) from you, you are a sinner, we must educate you, we must discipline you, this is not right.

* Student: Is it correct to say that in proportion to the attributes of hypocrisy present in a person, his corresponding deeds are nullified, or must there be a specific description of hypocrisy?

The shaikh: Complete nullification of deeds does not happen except in full hypocrisy. In contrast there is a weighing, meaning a balance between good deeds and bad deeds, whether or not the bad deeds are among the actions of the hypocrites.

A student: But can it not be said that if a person has among him the characteristics of the hypocrites, such as breaking promises, lying, and many other things...

The shaikh: We cannot say that his good deeds are nullified in exchange for that; that is not possible, because another person will come to us and say: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾ [Hud 11:114], so it is said: there is a weighing. But there is no doubt that the one who has the apparent traits of the hypocrites is feared to have those traits turn into the hidden traits of the hypocrites, because one thing draws another, and an apparent resemblance may lead to an inner resemblance.

* * *

A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish prayer and give zakat while they bow [in prayer]. And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - indeed, the party of Allah will be the victorious. O you who believe, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:55-57].

The shaikh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

From the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of jihad in the way of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿they strive in the way of Allah﴾.

And from its benefits: an indication of sincerity (ikhlas) in His saying: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, because fighting, which is jihad, is driven by several motives, and praiseworthy jihad is the jihad in the way of Allah. If someone says: what is jihad in the way of Allah? We say: the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it as: «Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is in the way of Allah»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7458) and Muslim (1904/150) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]].

And from the benefits of this noble verse: a person should not be deterred in (his service to) Allah by the blame of any blamer, as long as he is upon the truth, and he should not be concerned with anyone, because every worshipper must have an enemy. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾ [al-Furqan 25:31], and the followers of the prophets likewise must have enemies from among the criminals. But ﴿your Lord suffices as guide and helper﴾ [al-Furqan 25:31]. Notice why He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿your Lord suffices as guide and helper﴾: because these enemies either mislead people through ideas and doubt and the like, so He cut off their hope with His saying: ﴿and your Lord suffices as a guide﴾; or they try to turn people away by force, so He answered that with His saying: ﴿and as a helper﴾. Therefore there must be blame; every person who holds to the Shari'ah must face blame, and most people will blame him, because out of every thousand of the children of Adam, nine hundred and ninety-nine are in the Fire and one is in Paradise - may Allah make us and you among them.

Before we pass this benefit: does His saying ﴿and they do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾ include that a person acts rashly and does not use wisdom, or is it necessary to use wisdom?

The second: wisdom must be used, because rashness leads to the reversal of the intended aim. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) would leave what might be said, or what might be done, out of fear of corruptions, to the extent that he would rebuke a man for his bad character or religion, but when that man asked permission to enter, he would meet him with a cheerful face. All of that was for the sake of reconciliation, because Allah gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: these great qualities are from the grace of Allah, ﴿That is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: whoever strives in doing good, Allah, exalted is He, will be generous to him, because His saying ﴿whom He wills﴾ is not an absolute will but a restricted will. Restricted by what? By wisdom; it is restricted by wisdom. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 6:124]. So whoever is worthy of the message, He sends it to him. Likewise, Allah knows best where to place the effects of this message and the followers of this message; whoever is worthy of that, He gives it to him, and whoever is not worthy, He withholds it from him. Read the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [as-Saff 61:5], and read what passed over us a few nights ago: ﴿But if they turn away, then know that Allah intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:49].

And from the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the will of Allah, mighty and majestic, regarding the actions of the servant, based on His saying: ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾. This is what the pious predecessors (salaf as-salih) held, and what the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah and the leaders of the Muslims hold: that Allah has a will regarding the actions of creation, just as He has a will regarding His own actions, exalted is He. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿for whoever among you wills to go straight (28). And you do not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 81:28-29]. For this reason, a person often wants to do something, and then suddenly turns away from it without any apparent cause, but it is the will of Allah, mighty and majestic.

It was said to a Bedouin: By what did you know your Lord? He said: By the breaking of resolutions and the turning of aspirations. Its meaning: a person may resolve upon something, and then his resolve is broken; the turning of aspirations means his aspiration is directed toward a specific thing, and then suddenly it turns away without any apparent cause, but it is the will of Allah, blessed and exalted.

The will of Allah, mighty and majestic, regarding the actions of His servants is part of the completeness of His lordship, so that nothing in His dominion is something He does not will. Because those who say that a person is independent in his will and that Allah has no will in his action are obliged to say that in the dominion of Allah there is what He does not will.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: an explanation of the vastness of Allah, mighty and majestic, in everything; in encompassing creation with knowledge, power, authority, mercy, and other things. Allah is All-Encompassing, and He suffices in everything, glorified and exalted is He.

And from its benefits: affirmation of knowledge for Allah, mighty and majestic, based on His saying: ﴿All-Knowing﴾. Knowledge is the perception of a thing as it actually is. Whoever does not perceive a thing is ignorant, and his ignorance is simple (basit). Whoever perceives it contrary to what it is, is ignorant, and his ignorance is compound (murakkab), because he does not know and does not know that he does not know.

And in this verse there are benefits: affirmation of these two names of Allah, mighty and majestic: Wide-Encompassing (al-Wasi') and All-Knowing ('Alim). Based on this, you may call upon Allah with them, saying: "O Wide-Encompassing, expand my provision for me. O All-Knowing, choose for me what is good for me," and the like, because Allah said: ﴿And to Allah belong the best names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf 7:180].

Know that all the names of Allah are derived (mushtaqqah), meaning they indicate a meaning. There is no name of Allah that is an inert noun (jamid) which indicates no meaning at all, not even the name (Allah) itself. (Allah) is derived, contrary to the one who said it is inert, because it is derived from what? From divinity (al-uluhiyyah), and divinity is a verbal noun that indicates a meaning. So all the names of Allah indicate a meaning, and if we did not say they indicate a meaning, they would not be "the best," because an inert noun contains no praise or commendation. So, all of Allah's names are...?

* A student: "The best."

* The shaikh: "The best." But are all the names of Allah derived?

* The student: Yes.

* The shaikh: Yes. For this reason we say: every name must include an attribute, but not every attribute gives rise to a name. Among the attributes, some cannot be derived as a name for Allah, such as: ﴿they plot and Allah plots﴾ [al-Anfal 8:30]. It is not possible to affirm for Allah the name "Plotter" (makir), because this is a description, and a description is restricted to what it is restricted by.

Something important remains regarding the matter of apostasy (riddah). Allah, glorified is He, did not mention here the worldly punishment that follows it. Rather, He said: ﴿Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:54].

We mentioned that apostasy is what? It is leaving Islam, and it revolves around two things: denial (takdhib) and arrogance (istikbar). Here there are several discussions. First: can every apostasy be repented from?

The answer: Yes, every apostasy can be repented from, due to the general statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins"﴾ [az-Zumar 39:53]. And due to His saying in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ [al-Furqan 25:68], meaning? They do not associate partners with Allah; ﴿and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾, they do not transgress against lives; ﴿and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, they do not transgress against honor. ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty (68). The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein forever in humiliation (69). Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those Allah will replace their bad deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 25:68-70].

So the preponderant view is that every person who has committed a sin, however great, and then repents to Allah with sincere repentance, his repentance is accepted. Some scholars made exceptions to this, in several matters. First: the innovator (sahib al-bid'ah). They said: the innovator, even if he repents, his repentance is not accepted. But it is said: where is the evidence that he is excluded from the general statements?

They said: because his harm extends to others. We answer this: this extended harm can be remedied by the innovator saying that he has returned from his innovation and that the correct position is such-and-such, as happened with Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him. Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari was at first a complete Mu'tazili, a stubborn Mu'tazili who would not yield, and he remained so for a long period of time. Then he repented and announced his repentance in the congregational mosque, took off his turban, and said: "Whoever knows me, knows me; and whoever does not know me, I am so-and-so." Then he sternly denounced the Mu'tazilah. This is repentance, and perhaps his reward for denouncing the innovation is greater than his punishment for that innovation, although the punishment was erased by repentance. Likewise, to make the innovator's repentance genuine, he must write something that nullifies his innovation, so that he is sincere in his repentance.

If someone says: What if those who followed his innovation refused to return when he returned, would he be sinful for the sin of those remaining? The answer: He is not sinful, he is not sinful, because he has fulfilled what was obligatory upon him of repentance and clarified the truth, and if these people persist in their falsehood, they are upon their falsehood.

The second issue: is the repentance of one who curses Allah accepted or not? On this there is a disagreement among the scholars. Some scholars said: the repentance of one who curses Allah is not accepted, because his apostasy is extremely grave, since he cursed the Lord of the worlds, exalted is He; so his repentance is not accepted due to the greatness of his crime through this apostasy. But this reasoning opposes the texts, and reasoning that opposes the texts is rejected, like analogy opposing a text. Therefore this is rejected. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not insult those whom they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾ [al-An'am 6:108]. The verse shows that among the disbelievers are those who curse Allah, exalted is He, when their gods are insulted.

Then it is said: Allah, glorified is He, said about the hypocrites: ﴿The hypocrites are wary lest a surah be revealed about them informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock, indeed Allah will bring out what you fear." (64) And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing"﴾ [at-Tawbah 9:64-65]. That is: they speak words whose meaning they do not intend, talking the talk of a caravan in order to pass the road. Then Allah said to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? (65) Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [at-Tawbah 9:65-66]. This is a clear text that the one who mocks Allah or His verses or His Messenger is a disbeliever. But He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a group among you, We will punish another group﴾ [at-Tawbah 9:66]. This shows that among them there may be a group that is pardoned, and they cannot be pardoned except through repentance. Based on this, the preponderant view is that whoever curses Allah and His Messenger and then repents, his repentance is accepted. But whoever curses the Messenger (ﷺ) and then repents, his repentance is accepted, yet he is killed. Is he killed as an apostate or as a Muslim? He is killed as a Muslim, because this is a right of a human being, namely the Messenger (ﷺ), so we must avenge him; we must kill whoever insulted him.

As for one who curses Allah: Allah, mighty and majestic, has told us about Himself that He turns in repentance to such a person. But does the Messenger (ﷺ) accept the repentance of one who cursed him? We do not know. For this reason, there were people who insulted the Messenger (ﷺ) during his lifetime, and he pardoned them, because the right was his right; when they repented, he pardoned them, since the right is his. But after his death, the right is upon us, his followers. We must avenge our Messenger (ﷺ) and kill whoever insulted him. Then, praise be to Allah, what happens to him when he is killed? He passes from this world to the Hereafter, and passes as a Muslim. The one who does not die today will die tomorrow, but if we take revenge for the Messenger (ﷺ), that is among the least of our obligations.

The fourth: the sorcerer who disbelieves through his sorcery. Sorcery is of two kinds: a kind through which the sorcerer disbelieves, and a kind through which he does not disbelieve. As for the sorcerer whose sorcery does not make him a disbeliever, he is executed as a prescribed punishment (hadd), as was reported from the Companions, and to restrain his corruption, because he is among those who strive in the land for corruption. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:32], and no one doubts the corruption of sorcerers in the land, so they are killed to restrain their evil and as a deterrent to others.

But the disbelieving sorcerer, if he becomes Muslim (and the disbelieving sorcerer is one who seeks help from devils and rebellious jinn to harm the servants of Allah, by placing sorcery that lures a devil or rebellious jinn so that they settle in a person's body and refuse to leave him except by undoing the sorcery), this one becomes a disbeliever. In the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:102]. Look: two of the angels of Allah, on whom Allah sent down knowledge of sorcery, and they are angels, but not so that they would make it a profession, rather for the sake of testing. For this reason He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And they did not teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:102]. So this one is killed as I have said, killed for disbelief and apostasy. But if he repents, is his repentance accepted? On this there is a disagreement among the scholars: some said it is not accepted, and some said it is accepted. Which of them is better supported by evidence?

* Students: Whoever said it is accepted.

* The shaikh: Whoever said it is accepted. So we accept his repentance and lift the killing from him, and we make him one of our brothers, but there must be evidence of his uprightness and the goodness of his condition, and it is not enough for him merely to say, "I have repented."

Well, these are four. The fifth: the hypocrite of hypocrisy that amounts to disbelief (nifaq kufr) is a disbeliever without doubt: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:145].

Hypocrisy is among the worst of the traits of the children of Adam. When we know a person's hypocrisy with certainty, and not merely from suspicion and circumstantial indications, then (we judge him accordingly). For mere suspicion and circumstantial indications do not permit us to accuse anyone of hypocrisy, since we have not been commanded to probe into the hearts and inner thoughts of people. But if we know with certainty that we have seen this man go to the gatherings of the Jews, the Christians and the atheists and say that he is with them, and then come to the Muslims flattering them and saying that he is a Muslim, then his hypocrisy has become apparent and we judge him as a hypocrite. Should he be killed or not?

He should be killed, because his hypocrisy is known. However, the hypocrites in the time of the Messenger ﷺ were spared execution for a reason, namely so that people would not be turned away from Islam and from faith in the Messenger ﷺ. For this reason he said: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]] And he ﷺ knew them, but out of fear of turning people away from Islam he refrained from killing them, for this great benefit, and he dealt with them according to their outward appearance. But if he repents, if a hypocrite repents, is his repentance accepted?

* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: The (prevailing) school of thought is that his repentance is not accepted, because the man from the outset says that he has not disbelieved; he says that he is a Muslim. If we say to him, "You are a hypocrite," he says, "Never! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and you will find me in the front row at all the prayers." So they say that it is not accepted. Al-Saffarini, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Because nothing of his faith appeared except what he proclaimed with his tongue, so we do not accept it, since from the outset he says that he is a Muslim." But the correct view is that his repentance is accepted when circumstantial indications point to his sincerity, based on the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper. (145) Except for those who repent and amend and hold fast to Allah and make their religion sincerely for Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 145, 146]. Look at the conditions! Because the matter is not easy. This man displays his faith... ﴿Except those who repent﴾ after that? ﴿Except those who repent and amend and hold fast to Allah and make their religion sincerely for Allah. Then those will be with the believers﴾.

The conditions are heavy in their repentance, because they only show Islam. So if we become certain of that, then Allah says: ﴿Then those will be with the believers, and Allah will give the believers a great reward﴾, and among them are these hypocrites who repented, because Allah says: ﴿Then those will be with the believers﴾.

If someone says: the question is whether an apostate is to be asked to repent or not? That is, if his disbelief has been established, is he to be asked to repent?

The answer: as for those whose repentance is not accepted, according to the view of those who say it is not accepted, they do not need to be asked to repent. Why? The ones who say that the repentance of these is not accepted, do they say that they should be asked to repent?

* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No. Why?
* Students: Because their repentance is not accepted.
* The Shaykh: Because their repentance is not accepted; even if they repent, it is not accepted. As for those whose repentance is accepted, among them the categories we have mentioned according to the preponderant view, this is referred back to the opinion of the Imam. This is the preponderant view, because some of the texts include killing the apostate without asking him to repent, and some include killing the apostate after asking him to repent. So this is referred to the opinion of the Imam or his deputy in judgment, such as the judges. If they see that he should be asked to repent, he is asked; and if they see that he should not be asked, he is not asked.

If someone says: asking to repent is his right, so why do you prevent him from it?

We say: it is not an absolute right. Rather, it is a right when the public interest calls for it. And when the public interest lies in not asking him to repent, then the right now belongs to the Muslims, and preventing them from trifling with the religion is more important than this particular man's personal right.

If someone says: if a group of people or a tribe among the tribes apostatizes, is it permissible to fight them?

The answer: It is obligatory to fight them, because this is what the Companions unanimously agreed upon, under the leadership of whom? Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. So it is obligatory for us to fight them, but on condition that we have the strength with which we can fight. If we do not have the strength, then Allah did not make fighting obligatory upon the Muslims in Makkah, because they lacked strength.

It is well known that it is recklessness, which the Shari'ah does not command and reason does not require, for a person to fight massed armies armed with advanced weapons while having nothing but kitchen knives. This is neither wise nor something the Shari'ah could command or reason could require. Wait until you have strength, and then fight.

If someone says: did Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, not send out the army of Usamah, although he needed them in fighting the people of apostasy?

The answer: Yes, but this is answered in two ways. The first: the army of Usamah was under a banner tied by Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. For this reason Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I will not untie a banner that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tied."[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3168) from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, with the wording: "I would not untie a knot that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tied."]]

The second: in that there was a demonstration of the honour and strength of the Muslims. For this reason, when the apostate Arabs saw that the people of Madinah had begun sending armies to al-Sham, they said: "These people have power and capability," and some of them returned. Thus, in following the example of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there was a great blessing that spared them from fighting for months. This is one of the things that shows us that adherence to Islam has great blessings, which a person may not perceive until after some time.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 55 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing [in prayer].﴾ [al-Ma'idah 55].

﴿Your guardian is only Allah﴾: This form (innama) indicates restriction (hasr, exclusivity), because it is equivalent to saying: "Your guardian is none but Allah," meaning: do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger﴾, and what excellent guardians they are: the Lord of the worlds and the Seal of the Prophets, peace be upon him.

﴿And His Messenger and those who believe﴾: Because the believers are allies of one another, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said in Surah al-Tawbah. Read!

* A student: ﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another; they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [al-Tawbah 71].

* The Shaykh: Excellent. ﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another.﴾ And thus the believers must be allies of one another, for the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. Consider a man whose guardian is Allah and His Messenger, and the believers, such that no one can defeat him.

﴿And those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾: ﴿Who establish prayer﴾ is a description of ﴿those who believe﴾. Thus they combined faith, which is the creed, with the establishment of prayer. The second is ﴿give zakah﴾, which is the portion of wealth prescribed in zakatable property. To whom do they give it? They give it to its rightful recipients, those entitled to it. ﴿While bowing﴾: Is this clause a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah, a clause describing the state of the subject)? That is, do they give zakah while bowing in prayer? Or is it a resumptive clause (jumlah isti'nafiyyah, an independent new clause)?

* Students: Resumptive.

* The Shaykh: Resumptive. Then, on the view that it is resumptive, is the intended bowing the bowing that is a part of prayer, which is the bending of the back in glorification of Allah, mighty and majestic? Or is the intended meaning submission to the law of Allah?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second. For this reason the poet said:

"Do not humiliate the poor man, lest you bow one day, while time has raised him up."

(Tarka'a, "bow") means "submit." (One day, while time has raised him up) means: do not look at the present; look at the future. It may be that one day you will be rich, and this poor man may become rich while you are poor.

So the clause ﴿while bowing﴾ is a resumptive clause, not a circumstantial clause, and the bowing here means submission to the law and humility before it.

* From the lessons of this noble verse: the virtue of the believers, a virtue above which there is nothing, as shown by His saying ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾: three things, Allah, the Messenger, and those who believe. If someone says: The guardianship of Allah, mighty and majestic, is fitting for every time and place, but how is the guardianship of the Messenger?

The answer: As for what was during his lifetime, the guardianship is clear and evident. As for after his death, our adherence to his Sunnah is his guardianship over us, because by it we are supported and aided. It is as if he, peace be upon him, is with us, supporting us and helping us. As for those who believe, it is clear that the believers will continue to be dominant upon the truth until the command of Allah comes.

* From the benefits of this verse: the virtue of whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies.

* And from its benefits: the virtue of prayer, because prayer is always placed first. There is no doubt that prayer is the best of acts of worship after monotheism and testifying to the message. For this reason it was enjoined by Allah, mighty and majestic, upon the Messenger directly without intermediary. It was enjoined upon the Messenger at the highest place a human being can reach, and it was enjoined upon the Messenger on the most noble night he had. It was enjoined upon the Messenger as fifty prayers. That it was fifty prayers indicates that Allah loves it, because fifty prayers would occupy most of the time. But Allah, by His bounty and generosity, made them five. Yet it is as though they were fifty: they are five in deed and fifty in the scale.

* And also from the benefits of this noble verse: the rank of zakah in the religion of Islam comes after the rank of prayer. Likewise in the noble verses and the prophetic hadiths, zakah comes after prayer.

If someone says: Zakah and fasting. Fasting is harder on a person than zakah, so why was it not placed first?

We reply: First, we do not concede this, because a person's love of wealth is intense, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-'Adiyat 8], meaning: for the love of wealth is intense. He said: ﴿And you devour inheritance with all greed, and you love wealth with immense love﴾ [al-Fajr 19-20]. And it may be easy for a person to fast ten days but not to pay ten dirhams. That is the first point.

Second: zakah has a benefit that extends beyond the individual. It benefits Islam and benefits the Muslims, for among the categories of zakah recipients is "in the way of Allah," and this benefits whom? It benefits Islam. And among the categories of zakah recipients are the poor, the needy, and the debtors, and these are what? A benefit to the Muslims. So the benefit of zakah extends to others, whereas fasting does not extend. By this, and Allah knows best His wisdom, glorified and exalted, zakah came to follow prayer.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: these righteous deeds must be accompanied by humility and submission to Allah, mighty and majestic, such that a person feels that he is worshipping Allah and submitting to Him. Many people miss this. Most people perform prayer only as an obligation upon them, but they do not feel that they are worshipping Allah through it. The same applies to zakah. From where do we take that one must be attentive to this? From His saying: ﴿while bowing﴾.

It is strange that the Rafidah (Rawafid, an extremist Shi'i sect) claimed that no one acted upon this verse except 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. They said that he gave charity while bowing, and they made this one of his virtues. May Allah forbid that this was his action, radiya Allahu 'anhu. For movement in prayer: is it praiseworthy or not? It is not praiseworthy. So if, when he bowed, the poor came to him and he said, "Take, take this," that is not a virtue; it is a blemish. But the Rafidah do not understand. They have foolishness, as they said in praising him that he prayed a thousand units (rak'ah) between Maghrib and 'Isha'. Who prays a thousand units between Maghrib and 'Isha'? Yes, if a man wanted to do this, he would be dancing rather than praying, and he could not manage a thousand units. Yet they made this one of his virtues, when in reality it is one of his faults. We testify that he would never have done this, and he did not do this, neither this nor that.

We have no doubt that 'Ali, radiya Allahu 'anhu, has virtues and merits that are unique to him among the caliphs, and he shares with the caliphs virtues and merits in common. And the caliphs have virtues and merits that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib did not attain. Is that not so?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Without doubt. 'Ali has merits, and the caliphs have merits. They share some of them, and some of them are unique to each. But absolute superiority, in this order: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali. For example, 'Ali's kinship to the Messenger, peace be upon him, is not shared by Abu Bakr, 'Umar, or 'Uthman. That the Messenger married 'Ali his daughter Fatimah? 

'Uthman shares it, indeed he has a better claim, because when the Messenger's daughter died first, 'Uthman married the second one. So he married two daughters of the Messenger, peace be upon him, two daughters of the Messenger! Then, at the end of his life, the Messenger, peace be upon him, made a proclamation that could not happen for anyone other than Abu Bakr. He said while on the pulpit, and his words reached the whole Ummah: "Indeed, the person who has been most generous to me in his companionship and his wealth is Abu Bakr." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3904) and Muslim (2382/2) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.] God is greatest! Who attained this? And he said: "If I were to take a close friend (khalil) from my Ummah, I would have taken Abu Bakr. But it is the brotherhood of Islam and its affection." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (466), the wording is his, and Muslim (2382/2) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.] No one else attained this. He appointed him to lead the prayer, and appointed him to lead the Hajj. Is it clear?

He appointed 'Ali ibn Abi Talib over his household during the expedition of Tabuk. When 'Ali said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you leave me among the women and the weak?" he said: "Are you not pleased to have the position relative to me that Harun had relative to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4416), Muslim (2404/31), the wording is his, from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.] This virtue was not attained by Abu Bakr. And 'Ali was his successor over his household, just as Musa said to Harun: ﴿Take my place among my people﴾ [al-A'raf 142].
