* A student: May Allah be good to you. The distinction between the sorcerer who (...) and the one who is killed as a hadd punishment. These two share one thing, which is (...), and the sorcerer who disbelieves through his sorcery adds disbelief.

* The Shaykh: But, may Allah bless you, whoever's sin is disbelief, Allah says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they cease, they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ [al-Anfal 38]. For this reason, if the apostate repents, we accept his repentance and lift the killing from him. But if the adulterer repents after he has reached the judge, does repentance benefit him? No, although the apostate's repentance benefits him even before the judge.

* A student: If it is said about one who insulted the Messenger, peace be upon him, that if we say he is to be killed, his repentance is accepted, then it would be said that permitting the killing of a soul (...) with his Islam means it requires investigation, and the Messenger, peace be upon him, through what is established in the Sunnah, is the most deserving of people of forgiveness and pardon.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but this is not present. We must avenge the Messenger, peace be upon him.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Not at all (...). If I were a judge, and it was presented to you, say: strike him with the edge of the sword and do not hesitate.

* A student: We mentioned that in the preferred view regarding the sorcerer and the hypocrite, his repentance is accepted. Does this restrict what was restricted (...)?

* The Shaykh: Not at all. If he disbelieved through his sorcery, it is accepted in every case, because of the verse I mentioned to you. But what results from his act is open to question, because if disbelievers harm the Muslims, kill some of them, and take their wealth, and then they become Muslim, liability for them is dropped.

* A student: It passed for us that the greatness of prayer in the religion of Islam in worship is that Allah has His servants worship through it. Yes, Shaykh, I have experienced this: there is no need of the needs of this world and the Hereafter, of fasting and prayer and worldly actions, in which thoughts struggle against me, like prayer. I do not know what it is, Shaykh, what is the wisdom? And fasting and other needs, do thoughts struggle against me in them like prayer?

* The Shaykh: You mean that thoughts increase during prayer, is that what you mean? Yes, because prayer is the best subject, and Satan wants to corrupt this prayer for us. If we performed it in the required manner, the matter would be as Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 45]. It restrains a person from immorality and wrongdoing, and also helps him toward righteousness. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. This is the reason. For this reason, when a servant's faith is strong, Satan comes to him from every direction, whispering to him about the foundation of faith. Why? Because he knows that if a person's faith is strong, he is saved from this vile enemy, and if his faith is weak, he is overpowered.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion as a mockery and amusement, from among those who were given the Scripture before you, nor the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you are believers. And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason. Say: O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believed in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient? Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as to recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine and those who worship the Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ [al-Ma'idah 57-60].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion as a mockery and amusement.﴾ Previously we discussed in the verses the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾. His saying ﴿while bowing﴾: what did we say its meaning is?

* A student: Its meaning is submission.

* The Shaykh: The meaning of ruku' (bowing) is submission, not bending in prayer. Do you have evidence from the Arabic language that ruku' means submission?

* A student: It is a line of poetry I do not memorize.

* The Shaykh: A line of poetry that its speaker said.

* A student:
"Do not humiliate the poor man, lest you bow one day, while time has raised him up."

* The Shaykh: This is what the grammarians cite as evidence that the imperfect verb is built on fatha even when the energetic nun (nun al-tawkid) is dropped. The original of "la tuhin" is "la tuhinanna." And this is more correct than interpreting it as meaning...?

* A student: The well-known bowing.

* The Shaykh: What is the well-known bowing?

* The student: In prayer.

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* The student: Bending.

* The Shaykh: Bending in prayer. Because the one who gives charity while bowing is not deserving of praise, since in giving charity during his bowing he is occupied with something outside the prayer, so he is not praised for it. And charity is not like jihad, because a person can pray and finish his prayer, and then give charity.

* Tafsir of verse 56.

His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies﴾: "whoever" (man) is conditional. That is, any person who takes these three as allies, namely Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe, takes them as guardians, befriends them with love, affection, and support, and everything that guardianship requires.

If someone says: ﴿Whoever takes Allah as an ally﴾: Does Allah need to be taken as an ally?

Then the answer is: yes, Allah has no need for anyone to take Him as a protector (walī), but the religion has need for its people to take it up. Whoever takes up the religion of Allah has indeed taken Him as a protector, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you﴾ [Muhammad 7]. It is well known that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has no need of help, but ﴿if you support Allah﴾ means: if you support His religion. ﴿He will support you and make your feet firm.﴾

﴿And His Messenger﴾: The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, needs those who take him as a protector during his lifetime, who take up his Sunnah and defend it. After his death, taking the Messenger as a protector means taking up his Sunnah and supporting it, just as we said that taking Allah as a protector means taking up His religion and supporting His religion.

﴿And those who have believed﴾: The believers are to be taken as protectors until the Day of Resurrection, because "a group from this Ummah will continue to be upon the truth until the Hour comes"[[Narrated by Muslim (156 / 247) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah]], meaning: until the Hour draws near, for the Hour will not be established except upon the most wicked of creation[[Narrated by Muslim (1924 / 176) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As]].

As for His saying: ﴿So indeed, the party of Allah – they are the predominant﴾, the Mighty and Majestic did not say "then He is the predominant," but said ﴿the party of Allah﴾, in order to indicate two things:

The first thing: whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and those who have believed as protectors is of the party of Allah.

The second: the intended generality, that the party of Allah must be predominant, because the religion of Allah must be predominant. So the one who holds fast to the religion of Allah is of the party of Allah, and he is predominant, without doubt. But predominance may occur during life, and it may occur after death.

For this reason we find that the imams for whom it was not decreed to prevail completely during their lifetimes did prevail completely after their deaths. Imam Ahmad, Ibn Taymiyyah, and others among the scholars and imams suffered the humiliation from the rulers of evil that befell them, yet predominance was theirs, either in life or after death.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the exhortation to take Allah, His Messenger and the believers as protectors.
* Following from this, or rather being its very reality in the sense of taking as protector, is that a person should always be bound to these three: the Book of Allah; second, the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and third, the way of the believers.
For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah an-Nisa: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will give him what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ [an-Nisa 115]. So always remain bound to these three.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the complete praise of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the believers, and that their taking as protectors is among the causes of predominance; as for Allah's taking as protector, it is a matter above that.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Exalted, has a party (ḥizb), and who is His party? His party is the one opposed to His enemy (ḥarb), for Allah has a party and has an enemy. Whoever abides by His law is His party, and whoever opposes His law is His enemy, especially in matters explicitly stated to be war against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such as usury (ribā), highway robbery, and what is similar to them.

If someone says: Can this verse be used as evidence by those who establish parties (aḥzāb) in their countries?

The answer: No, it cannot, because it is assumed that the Muslims are one party that does not divide. Rather, if they divide, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has said: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects – you, [O Muhammad], are not [associated] with them in anything﴾ [al-An'am 159]. So the Prophet ﷺ disassociated himself from them and said: ﴿you are not [associated] with them in anything﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾ [al-An'am 159]. If this is the state of those who divided their religion, each one saying "the religion is with me," then how can it be said that establishing parties in the Islamic religion is permissible, because Allah said: "the party of Allah"?

We say: all Muslims are, what? A party of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and whoever opposes it has departed from this partisanship. But that does not mean that we say it is necessary to establish parties within the Islamic religion. For this reason, look now at the nation that built its entity upon the establishment of parties: what has come of it? Evil and great calamity, until, when the upright party came to the forefront and had predominance, evil occurred.

There is no need to give examples from Algeria and Turkey. For instance, when the Refah Party nearly achieved victory, what happened? The army and officers rose against this party, and now they are trying to abolish it. In any case, we say: the Islamic religion is one party.

Can we establish an Islamic party opposed to a communist party, or not? It is possible; it is necessary, because Allah made a party for Allah and a party for Satan: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan – they are the losers﴾ [al-Mujadilah 19]. This is unavoidable, because all the children of Adam are of two parties: what are they? Faith and disbelief: ﴿He is the one who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghabun 2]. This is unavoidable. But parties within the one party is contrary to Islam, and it cannot be established. For this reason great disintegration occurs when these parties are established.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the glad tidings to the party of Allah. Of what?
* Students: Of predominance.
* The Shaykh: Of predominance. They are the ones who prevail over their enemies. Read the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And another [favor] you love – victory from Allah and an imminent conquest. So give good tidings to the believers﴾ [as-Saff 13]: give good tidings to the believers that they will have victory.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 57:

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you are believers.﴾

In this verse there are two words that have two readings.

The first: (*huzuw*) with a waw, with a *damma* on the *zay* and nothing else: ﴿*huzuwan*﴾. It is not correct to say (*huzwan*) with a *sukun*. Rather, the *zay* must have a *damma*, so you say ﴿*huzuwan*﴾.

With the hamza there are two readings: ﴿*huzu'an*﴾ and ﴿*huz'an*﴾. So altogether there are three readings.

The second word is ﴿*wal-kuffara*﴾ (وْالْكُفَّارَ), which has two readings: ﴿*wal-kuffari*﴾ and ﴿*wal-kuffara*﴾.

On the reading with the *jarr* (kasra), it is coordinated with what? With the second ﴿*alladhina*﴾ in ﴿*min alladhina utu al-kitab*﴾. That means: "and from among the disbelievers."

On the first reading, it is coordinated with the first ﴿*alladhina*﴾, meaning: "Do not take as allies those who have taken your religion in ridicule, and do not take the disbelievers [as allies]." Have you understood now?

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Consider now how many times ﴿O you who have believed﴾ has come to us on a single page, which indicates complete concern with what is mentioned in these verses, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, repeated the address to the believers.

﴿Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement﴾, and He mentioned their categories.

﴿*Tattakhidhu*﴾ (تَتَّخِذُوا) means "to make" (*tusayyiru*), and it takes two objects. The first object is ﴿*alladhina*﴾ and the second object is ﴿*awliya'*﴾. That means: do not take them as allies. It is similar to the previous verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies﴾.

His saying ﴿those who have taken your religion﴾ means: those who made it [into that]. And "religion" (*din*) here means action.

The word (*al-din*) has come in the Noble Qur'an meaning recompense, and it is also used meaning the action for which one is recompensed.

An example of the first is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Fatiha 4], meaning the Day of Judgment.

Another example is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense? Then what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense?﴾ [al-Infitar 17-18].

It also comes meaning action very often, such as His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun 6], and like this verse, meaning the action by which you worship Allah and hope for its reward from Allah. From it comes the word (*al-dayn*) in transactions. The root is one. *Al-dayn* in transactions is giving something while awaiting its return.

He says: ﴿in ridicule and amusement﴾, meaning they made it an object of mockery, scoffing at it with their tongues, and they believed in their hearts that it was amusement. Amusement is that which has no aim and no benefit. They said: What is the meaning of a person coming, for example, to the mosque and moving standing, sitting and prostrating, and the like? They said: This is amusement, this is not religion, and they mock it.

His saying ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture﴾ means the Jews and Christians.

His saying ﴿from before you﴾ is a clarification of reality, not a restriction, because no one was given the Scripture with us or after us. Rather, all those who were given the Scripture were before us. But what is meant by them here, as is the Qur'an's method, is the Jews and Christians.

His saying ﴿and the disbelievers﴾: we have said there are two readings. That means: do not take the disbelievers as allies, whether or not they have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement. Is this on which reading?

* Students: The accusative (*nasb*).

* Shaykh: Confirm it, the accusative.

On the reading with the *jarr*, it means: do not take as allies the disbelievers who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement.

Each of the two readings is very beneficial. So here we say: if we make it with the *jarr*, it indicates that the disbelievers other than the People of the Book who have taken our religion as, what? In ridicule and amusement.

On the reading of the accusative, it indicates that we should avoid the disbelievers and not take them as allies at all.

But there is an indication, on the reading of the *jarr*, that the disbelievers who are not People of the Book take our religion in ridicule and amusement, so there combines in them mockery of us, the belief that our religion is amusement, and disbelief.

﴿Awliya'﴾ is the plural of (*waliy*), meaning one who is supported; you support them, help them, draw near to them, and the like, which requires that they be allies to us and not enemies.

Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾. ﴿Fear Allah﴾ means: take a protection against His punishment, and that is by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, seeking nearness to Him, Blessed and Exalted.

For this reason some of them defined taqwa (God-consciousness, piety): that you act in obedience to Allah with light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah.

So here it combines action, sincerity, and knowledge: that you act in obedience to Allah, that is action; with light from Allah, that is knowledge; hoping for the reward of Allah, that is sincerity, not hoping for the worldly life. And that you leave what Allah has forbidden, with light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.

For this reason, when we say that taqwa is taking a protection by performing the commands, sincerity must be taken into account, because if there is no sincerity, there is no obedience.

His saying ﴿if﴾ (*in*): ﴿if you are believers﴾, this is a conditional in the manner of challenge, meaning: if you are truthful in your faith, then fear Allah, because one who is truthful in his faith must fear Allah, avoid what He has forbidden, and carry out His commands. If he does not do so, his faith is deficient and weak.

Is the conditional here connected to what precedes it, such that we estimate the answer of the condition as what precedes it? Estimate it now: "And fear Allah, if you are believers, then fear Allah." Does the speech work or not?

* Students: It works.

* Shaykh: It works. Then it is connected to what precedes it.

Sometimes the conditional is not connected to what precedes it, such as the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'a 9]. This conditional is not connected to what precedes it, because the meaning would be reversed. If we said: "That is better for you if you knew," then if you did not know, it would not be better for you. Does that work or not? It does not work. For this reason, in the second verse that you just recited, one should pause at ﴿That is better for you﴾, because if you connect it, it would be understood that it is better if we know, and if we do not know, it is not better, even though it is better in any case. But the meaning of this is: if you are among those of knowledge, then understand this. This is its meaning in summary.

In any case, the verse we have: ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾. We say: this condition is connected to what precedes it, meaning: if you are believers in truth, then fear Allah, because true faith requires taqwa.

* In this noble verse there are benefits:

* Among them: the prohibition of taking the Jews, Christians and disbelievers as allies. This is more general than the previous verse, ﴿Do not take the Jews and Christians as allies﴾, because the disbelievers have been added to them in this verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: complete incitement away from taking them as allies, by arousing zeal and jealousy in His saying ﴿those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement﴾. That means: any person who feels that someone mocks his religion and says, "This religion is amusement with no benefit," undoubtedly will become enraged.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the manifestation of these disbelievers, from the People of the Book and the disbelievers, of their enmity toward Islam, and that their enmity is apparent, since they used to mock its adherents who held firmly to it.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that knowledge may be a burden on its possessor. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture﴾, for these were given knowledge, and the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) was described to them in the Torah and the Gospel in a description by which they recognized him as they recognize their sons, yet this knowledge did not benefit them.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: encouragement toward taqwa, of which one part is distancing oneself from taking these people as allies, because of His saying ﴿and fear Allah﴾.

* And among its benefits: that true faith requires, what? Taqwa, because of His saying ﴿fear Allah, if you are believers﴾.

If someone says: Is taqwa specific to Allah? We say: as for the taqwa of worship, it is specific to Allah, and it is not permissible to be wary of anything in the manner of worship except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

As for the taqwa of what is feared, this is for Allah and for others: ﴿Fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqara 281]. ﴿A Day﴾, and it is known that this is not taqwa of worship. That is, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not command us to worship the Day with taqwa, but this is guarding against what is feared, what, what is feared from it?

And it is said: "Guard against the evil of one to whom you have done good." Is this taqwa of worship? No. That is, beware, and fear, and this is not taqwa of worship.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We have understood the wilayah (allegiance) of Allah and of His Messenger. So what is the meaning of war against Allah and war against His Messenger?

* Shaykh: Yes. War means: declaring opposition.

* Student: One or two that are in some [reports] from Allah and His Messenger?

* Shaykh: That is: declaring opposition to the Messenger is a kind of warfare.

* Student: O Shaykh, how can one wage war against Allah and His Messenger? Allah defeats him, but the Messenger (ﷺ)?

* Shaykh: The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did he not wage war against the disbelievers and defeat them?

* Student: Yes. And after his death?

* Shaykh: And after his death, his sunnah.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Some people have a partner in work or the like who is a disbeliever, and we call him "work friend." Is this taking him as an ally?

* Shaykh: We have spoken about the word *sadiq* (friend) and *rafiq* (companion). Did we or not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: We discussed it. Do you remember it?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: We discussed it, and some of you explained it and said: *sadiq* is said of one category of people, and *rafiq* of another. I don't know. It was perhaps in another session, not in your session, I don't know. But certainly we discussed it, and they said: the *sadiq* (...).

It is known that those who have not backed us against us and have not fought us are not like those who wage war against us. They say: we are courteous with them in expression, but we do not mean that being "friends" means that we are truthful with them.

* Student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. The saying "Guard against the evil of one to whom you have done good," is it correct?

* Shaykh: No, it is not correct. Is it a hadith, then?

* Student: I mean its meaning.

* Shaykh: By Allah, at some times, yes. If you do good to him, he may say, "This one fears me," and then he takes advantage of you.

* Student: As for someone who has disbelieving relatives, is he commanded to resist natural love, that is, if his father, son or brother...?

* Shaykh: No. Whoever has disbelieving relatives, natural love does not affect his religion, because this is a matter that cannot be avoided, and it is impossible to flee from it.

* Student: May Allah pardon you, Shaykh. Why, from what we have learned from experience, Shaykh, that every person wants to honor himself by any means, whether from religion or from outside religion, the Lord turns the hearts of servants away from Him, from His love, and what he loves is only because he fears Him. Some of us watch over Allah, Exalted is He, and submit themselves to the legal matters, and they become honored by the love of people, and Allah honors them by a clear thing that we fear, Shaykh. If people followed the religious interest, nothing of their affairs would be lost...

* Shaykh: True.

* Student: And if people had not neglected the command of Allah and neglected Islam.

* Shaykh: This is true. It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "We were humble, then Allah honored us with Islam, so whenever we seek honor in other than it, Allah will humiliate us."[[Reported by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (208) from a hadith of Umar.]]

* Student: May Allah be good to you. We said: ﴿*huzuwan*﴾ with their tongues, and ﴿*la'iban*﴾...

* Shaykh: In what they believe.

* Student: Is this the difference between *huzu'* and *la'ib*?

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: Shaykh, can it be derived from the verse that among the tools of the party of Satan is warring against the party of the Merciful (...)?

* Shaykh: It is among their signs. There is no doubt that it is a sign of the party of Satan to be at war with the party of the Merciful.

* Student: Relying on ridicule and amusement in warring against the party of the Merciful.

* Shaykh: No. We mentioned the purpose of that: incitement, arousing determination, and zeal to distance oneself from these people.

* Student: May Allah bless you all. The matter has still not been established, it has not been clarified for me: the matter of *tawalli* (taking as allies). We explained it, as I recall, as support.

* Shaykh: Yes, support.

* Student: Yes, support. So must this support be coupled with love, or is it support even without love? If it is one of the two, then how is the action of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to be understood when he allied with Khuza'a by his alliance at al-Hudaybiyya? And may Allah reward you with good.

* Shaykh: What is the difficulty?

* Student: Yes, since the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made a covenant with them for support from them and from them?

* Shaykh: No. He made them allies who would help him and he would help them. But love does not necessarily follow from this. He wanted to be supported by them, and this shows that it is permissible for Muslims to seek help from Christians if the need arises.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason. Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except that we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?" Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as to requital from Allah? [It is those] whom Allah has cursed and with whom He has been angry and made of them apes and swine and slaves of Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound way."﴾

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We have already discussed the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement.﴾

So what is the benefit of His saying ﴿those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement﴾?

* Student: Incitement and warning the believers against taking them as allies.

* Shaykh: Inciting the Muslims to distance themselves from them and not to take them as allies, because they mock their religion.

﴿The disbelievers⁠﴾ has two readings.

* Student: The accusative and the *jarr*.

* Shaykh: Explain both.

* Student: ﴿*al-kuffari*﴾ (...) is coordinated with ﴿those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, and the meaning is that taking the disbelievers as allies.

* Shaykh: The main point is this explanation. And on the accusative?

* Student: On (...) the first, ﴿do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement﴾...

* Shaykh: On the first relative pronoun. The explanation of both: on the reading of the *jarr* it is coordinated with the second relative pronoun, and on the reading of the accusative it is coordinated with the first relative pronoun.

His saying ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿if you are believers﴾?

* Student: Encouragement to faith, so that their faith may lead them to the fear of Allah.

* Shaykh: It is like a challenge to them, meaning: if they are believers in truth, then let them fear Allah.

Sometimes the condition is not a restriction on what precedes it, like what?

* Student: The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'a 9].

* Shaykh: Well done. Like the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

What is the reason it is not a restriction on what precedes it?

* Student: Because (...).

* Shaykh: If we said that, then attending the prayer would be better only if we knew, and if we did not know, it would not be better.

And when you call to the prayer, [Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says,] ﴿And when you call to the prayer﴾, showing the state of those who were given the Scripture, and likewise the disbelievers.

﴿When you call to the prayer﴾: that is, when you summon the people to it in its well-known manner. When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, and the community had a Islamic state and a large society, they consulted among themselves on how to gather the people for the prayer.

Some of them proposed that fires be lit, so that when the time entered it would be known by them that the time had come. This proposal was rejected, because this is the custom of the Magians, and because fires in the daytime achieve nothing.

A bell (naqus) was proposed, and this proposal was rejected, because it is a sign of the Christians' prayer.

A horn (buq) that is blown, with a sound, was proposed; this proposal was rejected. Why? Because it is a symbol of the religion of the Jews.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, facilitated that one of the Companions, 'Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn 'Abd Rabbih, may Allah be pleased with him, "saw in a dream a man with a bell, or a horn, and he said to him: Will you sell this? He said: For what purpose? He said: I will announce the prayer with it. He said: Shall I not direct you to something better than this? Then he made him hear the adhan, he made him hear the whole adhan. When he woke in the morning, he went early to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: 'Indeed, this is a true vision,' and the Prophet ﷺ approved it, and ordered 'Abdullah ibn Zayd to convey it to Bilal, and he gave the reason for that, saying: 'Indeed, he has a sweeter voice than you'"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (499) and Ibn Majah (706) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Zayd.]].

He did not say, "Convey it to him" and remain silent; for if he had remained silent, there would have been something in the heart of 'Abdullah ibn Zayd, since it was he who saw it, and he was the most worthy of the people to carry it out. But it is the custom of the Messenger ﷺ to explain the wisdom behind a matter so that the heart may be reassured. So he explained that he had a sweeter voice than him, and he called with it.

What an excellent call! It glorifies Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it testifies to His Oneness; it testifies to the Messenger's prophethood; it is a call to righteousness; a call to success; it concludes with exaltation and Oneness. What call is better than this? None. It is a great call. For this reason, the one who answers the muezzin says: "O Allah, Lord of this perfect call"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (614) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]].

To the extent that the Messenger ﷺ made it one of the symbols of the Islamic lands: "When he arrived at a people, he would wait; if they called the adhan, he would withhold from fighting them"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2943) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. This is because the adhan is among the apparent symbols of Islam, which Muslims may not abandon, and it is not permissible for non-Muslims to attack a town in which the adhan is called. Perhaps this is the sign that a land is a land of Islam: that the adhan is raised in it. Because when the Messenger ﷺ heard the adhan he would refrain from them, and knew that their lands were lands of Islam, and this would be the decisive criterion for the meaning of the "abode of Islam."

Now, ﴿when you call to the prayer﴾ with what? With the adhan.

His saying ﴿to the prayer﴾ is a general term that includes: the Friday prayer and the five obligatory prayers. Should we say: and others?

The answer: No, we do not say "and others." So it is a general term intended as a specific one, and it is not the general term that was specified; for the general term that was specified was intended in its generality first, and then specification was applied to it secondly, whereas the general term intended as specific was never intended in its generality at all. Do you understand? Accordingly, we say: "the prayer" here is a general term intended as specific.

The prayer for rain (istisqa') is not called with the adhan, although people gather for it; the two festivals are not called with the adhan, although people gather for them; the eclipse prayer is not called with the adhan, although people gather for it; the night prayer in Ramadan is not called with the adhan, although people gather for it.

But the eclipse prayer has been singled out with a special call, so that it not be equated with the obligatory prayers that recur every day, and that call is: "The prayer is gathering" (as-salatu jami'ah), because it comes suddenly while people are heedless.

So ﴿when you call to the prayer﴾ refers to six prayers, correct? The five daily prayers and the Friday prayer.

﴿They take it as a mockery and a game﴾, that is, they began to scoff and ridicule.

And ﴿huzuwan﴾ — I forgot to point out that it has three readings: ﴿huzuwan﴾ with a damma on the zay when it is with the waw, ﴿huz'an﴾ with a sukun on the zay and a hamza, ﴿huzu'an﴾ with a damma on the zay and a hamza. And the difference between huzw and la'ib (play) has already been discussed earlier.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is because they﴾ — ﴿that﴾ refers to what? To their saying, or to their taking it? Their taking it as a mockery and a game.

﴿Because they﴾: the ba' here indicates causation; ﴿that is because they﴾, that is, because of the fact that they, ﴿are a people who do not reason﴾, that is, they do not have minds, that is, sound minds; but they have perceptive minds. The difference between them: perceptive minds are those upon which obligation (taklif) is based, which is the attribute you find in the books of jurists, such as among the conditions of prayer: discernment (tamyiz) and reason ('aql). This is the reason of understanding.

But the reason of guidance ('aql al-irshad) is what is absent from every disbeliever. Every disbeliever is not rational — what reason? The reason of guidance. He has no reason to guide him; he has intelligence, and he has the perception of affairs, and he knows of reality what many Muslims do not know, but he is not rational. Why? Because of his disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and reason guides to the truth.

So ﴿because they are a people who do not reason﴾, that is, they do not have the reason of guidance. And if they had reasoned, they would have venerated this great prayer, which, as far as we know, there is nothing greater in the religion of Islam except Oneness and prophethood, because it has been singled out with great distinctions.

It is not hidden from many of you that it was prescribed by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His Messenger without intermediary, and it was not prescribed upon the Messenger while he was on the earth, but in the highest place humans can reach. Also, it was not prescribed upon him in this quantitative measure, meaning five prayers; rather fifty prayers were prescribed, occupying much of the time, if not most of the waking time.

This indicates Allah's love for it, and since Allah loves it, it became the coolness of the eye of the Messenger ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Women and perfume have been made beloved to me of your world, and the coolness of my eye has been placed in prayer"[[Narrated by an-Nasa'i (3940) from the hadith of Anas.]]. O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.

Could any rational person of guiding reason take this great prayer as a mockery and a game? Never. Rather, he takes it as a station of veneration and respect; for when a person comes to pray, whom is he conversing with? And before whom does he stand? He stands before Allah and converses with Allah; no one is between him and Him. He says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah 2], and Allah says: "My servant has praised Me"[[Narrated by Muslim (395/38) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

Then he comes to a garden, a garden of acts of worship: Qur'an, takbir, glorification of Allah, bowing to Allah, prostration to Allah; a great garden among the gardens of worship. How could a rational person take it as a mockery and a game? By Allah, if one of us were told: "Now you have an audience with the King, or with the President," what would he do? He would prepare himself, adorn himself, perfume himself, and make ready provisions and preparations for that. So how much more when he is about to stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the most beloved of things to Him. This would have a great effect if we were rational; but our reason is little, brothers.

We know that one is half of two; this is reason. But the reason of guidance is scarce. Indeed, many Muslims today — and we ask Allah to pardon us and them — come to prayer and perform it as a body without a soul, and the devils do not overwhelm them with whisperings except when they enter the prayer; then when they finish the prayer it is as if they were a cloud driven away by the wind: all those whisperings depart, and they find no benefit from them either.

Therefore, those who take the prayer as a mockery and a game are without doubt a people who do not reason, while those who venerate it and give it its due station are the people of reason and guidance.

* In this noble verse there is a statement of the severity of the impact of the prayer upon our enemies, the disbelievers: the Jews and the Christians. The reason: when He mentioned in the previous verse that they take our religion as a mockery and a game, He singled out the prayer after this, and singling out a thing from the general indicates care for it and its superiority over the general.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the legislation of calling to the prayer, since He says ﴿And when you call to the prayer﴾; and as we have said, "calling" here means the adhan.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that calling to the prayer is a matter known necessarily from the religion; since He says ﴿And when you call to the prayer﴾, as if this is a matter... what? Known and settled.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that if calling to the prayer is legislated, it is an act of worship by which the caller draws near to Allah; is it not so? And it is so. The adhan is among the best deeds, to the extent that Allah has singled out the muezzins with a distinction on the Day of Resurrection that others do not have: "They will be the longest of people in necks"[[Narrated by Muslim (387/14) from the hadith of Mu'awiyah.]]; Allah raises their heads by the length of their necks, because of their raising His remembrance among the servants. So they are distinguished by this distinction, which no one else shares with them.

If someone says: What do you say, is it better, or leading the prayer (imamah)?

The answer: It is better than leading the prayer, because the texts concerning it are more numerous than the texts concerning leading the prayer in terms of virtue.

If someone says: This objection arises against you: if it is better than leading the prayer, why did the Messenger ﷺ not call the adhan, nor did Abu Bakr, nor 'Umar, nor 'Uthman, nor 'Ali?

We say: because they were occupied with what was more important. And we are not now seeking to weigh the adhan against other acts of worship, but between the adhan and what? And leading the prayer. And there is no doubt that if the Messenger ﷺ and the rightly guided Caliphs had bound themselves to the adhan, they would have remained watching the times for a long period; and at that time a watch was not in a person's pocket that he could take out and know the time had come; one who watches the sun knows whether it is about to decline, or not, or has declined, or has not. So they were occupied with what was more important than devoting themselves to the adhan.

If someone says: Could they not appoint someone to watch the times, so that when it entered they would come?

We say: This would relieve them of much of the toil of the adhan, the virtue of which may be for this very meaning, and so the purpose would be lost. The conclusion is that the preponderant view among the scholars is that the adhan is better than leading the prayer, for the reasons you have heard.

If someone says: As for non-muezzins, is there no share for them?

We say: Yes, they have a share, praise be to Allah, and it is the legislation of following the muezzin; that is, we are legislated to say what the muezzin says, so that he does not surpass us with an act in which we have no share. This is from Allah's grace, mercy and wisdom: that He did not deprive non-muezzins of anything for the sake of the adhan. So we are commanded to follow the muezzin by saying what he says, except at "Hasten to the prayer" and "Hasten to success"; we do not say these, for if we said the same we would be calling ourselves; he is now calling us "Hasten to the prayer," so if we say "Hasten to the prayer," the two calls would conflict.

Rather, we say, when he says "Hasten to the prayer": "There is no might nor power except with Allah," which indicates "We hear and obey," as if we had said "We hear and obey," but we ask Allah to help us, for there is no might nor power except with Allah.

If someone says: If it is established that the adhan is an act of worship, what do you say about some people whom desire has led astray, who make a recording at the loudspeaker, and when the time of the adhan comes they turn on the speaker?

We say: This is an error, a grave mistake, and a forfeiture of good for the Ummah. This is not a muezzin; rather it is one reproducing the voice of a previous muezzin. Likewise, if they place a recording of the voice of a person who has died, this is not an act of worship.

In my view, the obligation is not fulfilled by it if there is no other muezzin audible in that place, because this is merely a sound, not a man devoted to worship who stands before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in this adhan. It is merely a sound, like if we made a clock's bell which, when heard, means the time has entered.

This is a point we should know: that the Islamic religion is an act of worship, having a body and a soul; it is not merely rituals that are heard or movements that are performed, but worship. So the adhan is an act of worship, and therefore it must be an act of worship.

If someone were to analogize from this and say: Let us record on tape the prayer of an imam of good recitation and good voice, and place the tape before the worshippers and let it lead them in prayer — would this be valid or not?

By consensus it is not valid, and there is no doubt about it; even though it would say "Allahu akbar" for the opening takbir in the best manner, the recitation in the best manner, and it would say "Allahu akbar" for bowing, and raise its voice slightly, "Subhana rabbiya al-'Azim," to avoid confusion, since it is not seen; but it says: since they cannot see me, I raise my voice with the glorification "Subhana rabbiya al-'Azim," and so on. No one says this suffices. Thus the adhan is likewise exactly as it is; for we do not want merely a sound by which we know the time has entered.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exaltation of the prayer, in that it is called to, and so that people may know its time, so they may pray and attend if they are among those obligated to attend the congregation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that standing for the prayer is a sign of what? Of the perfection of reason; and that whoever does not care for it, that is a sign of deficiency in his reason; since He says ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason﴾. So establishing the prayer is part of the perfection of reason, and neglecting it is a deficiency of reason, just as it is also a deficiency of religion.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 59 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before?"﴾ The address here is to the Messenger (ﷺ), meaning: say to them, argue with them, debate with them.

﴿O People of the Scripture﴾: the intended meaning is the Jews and the Christians.

﴿Do you resent us except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before﴾. The word ﴿هَلْ﴾ (hal) here is interrogative, and what is meant by it? Negation. This is because we have mentioned that when an exception (istithna') comes after an interrogative, it is evidence that the interrogative is for negation.

﴿Do you resent us﴾, meaning: you resent us for nothing except this. It is similar to the saying of the Exalted to the People of the Trench: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj 8].

﴿Do you resent us except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before﴾: by what do you find fault with us, for what thing other than this? And is this a fault? No. Is believing in Allah, and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, a fault? No, it is not a fault. So it is as if He said: you do not find fault in us for anything that is a fault; rather you find fault in us for something that is a perfection, which is belief in Allah and in what was revealed to us. This style, the scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) call: affirmation of praise by means of something resembling blame (ta'kid al-madh bima yushbih al-dhamm).

It is fine to say: affirmation of praise by what resembles blame has two forms.

The first form: negation and affirmation. A quality of blame is negated, and after it is brought a positive quality of praise. Have you understood?

* Student: Give us an example, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Go back. This example we have is the verse itself, but first it negates the quality of fault, and after it affirms a quality of perfection. This is called affirmation of praise by what resembles blame. Listen to the saying of the poet:

﴿And there is no fault in them except that their guest, who stays with them, is blamed for forgetting loved ones and homeland.﴾

"And there is no fault in them except that their guest who alights among them is blamed for forgetting loved ones and homeland," meaning that there is in them a consolation for loved ones and homeland. Is this a fault or a praise?

Students: Praise.

* The Shaykh: But at first you hear: "and there is no fault in them except that," you anticipate a blame. Likewise the saying of the poet:

﴿And there is no fault in them except that their swords, by them, are notched from the clashing of battalions.﴾

The first praises them for generosity, the second for courage. There is no fault in them, but a guest comes who forgets everything, because of their honouring of the guest and their welcoming of him.

Likewise the other: "there is no fault in them except that their swords," meaning: there is in them no cowardice at all, and no fault, except that their swords have become notched from the clashing of battalions, because of their bravery. This is one type and form of affirmation of praise by what resembles blame.

Second: that a quality of praise is brought, and after it an exception is made with a quality of blame. Have you understood? A quality of praise is brought, then after it a quality of blame with an exceptive particle. You say: "This man is a scholar, except that he is brave." What is this, praise or blame? "A scholar, except that he is..." what do you expect? A quality of blame. Then it is said: "except that he is brave." This also is from affirmation of praise by what resembles blame.

Let us look at the verse: ﴿Do you resent us except that we believe in Allah﴾. This is praise. So the address to these people is: we say to them, you resent nothing from us except this, and this is not something that calls for you to resent us.

﴿Except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and what was revealed before﴾, which is the Torah, the Gospel, the scrolls of Abraham, the Psalms, and other things. We believe in every book Allah has sent down to every messenger. Is this something a person is resented for? No, it cannot be resented.

But these people, we resent from them that they did not believe in what was revealed to us. Rather we say: they did not believe in what was revealed to them either. The People of the Scripture now do not believe in what was revealed to us, and the reality is that they do not believe in what was revealed to them; for if they believed in what was revealed to them, they would believe in what was revealed to us, since what was revealed to us confirms what was revealed to them. But they do not; they deny this and that.

He says: ﴿and that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾. ﴿Do you resent us except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you﴾ is coordinated with what? Is it coordinated with ﴿except that we believe in Allah﴾, or coordinated with the word of majesty (Allah)?

That is: "except that [we believe] and [that]," or coordinated with the word "Allah"?

There are two opinions, but the correct one, which may be the definite one, is that it is coordinated with ﴿in Allah﴾, meaning: except that we believe that most of you are defiantly disobedient, that is, departing from obedience to Allah through disbelief.

One might say: if you take it in this meaning, then they resent us, because they do not want it to be said that most of them are defiantly disobedient; so they resent us for our believing that most of them are defiantly disobedient?

It is said: this is not something they deserve to resent us for, because we did not say "and that you are defiantly disobedient," rather we say ﴿and that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾, and this is justice. For among them were those who were believers and truly believed, such as the Negus among the Christians and 'Abdullah ibn Salam among the Jews. But most of them are defiantly disobedient, and this is justice. It is as if He said: you do not resent us except that we have stood up to what is due to Allah and what is due in the servants of Allah. What is due to Allah? Belief in Him and in what He sent down. And what is due to the servants of Allah is justice: that we give each person what he deserves. So most of these people are defiantly disobedient without doubt, and we believe this; and we believe that among the Jews there are those who believed and whose belief was good, and among the Christians there are those who believed and whose belief was good. This is justice. We do not judge a community by the deeds of its majority; rather we give each person what he deserves.

* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. The second form, O Shaykh, of the forms of resembling praise with what resembles blame?

* The Shaykh: You are a student of knowledge, are you not? If we say: "So-and-so is a student of knowledge, except that he is diligent in worship," this is affirmation of praise by what resembles blame; because if you say "So-and-so is a student of knowledge, except," the listener expects that you will bring a quality of blame, but you have followed it with a quality of praise.

* Student: Shaykh, our saying that it is prescribed for one who hears the muezzin to follow him, that he is not deprived of the reward: does this mean he obtains the same reward the muezzin obtains?

* The Shaykh: No, he does not obtain it, but he shares with the muezzin in some of the reward. A parallel to this in some respects is that it is prescribed for one who does not perform Hajj to sacrifice, so that he shares with the pilgrims in some of their acts, such as slaughtering the sacrificial animal.

It is also prescribed for him to refrain from taking from his hair, nails, and skin; all of this is so that people may know the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: May Allah bless you all, Shaykh. Yesterday we passed in the tafsir of His saying: ﴿So indeed, the party of Allah - they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah 56], the emphasis on the impermissibility of party pluralism among the Muslims. Now there appear, may Allah bless you, Shaykh, in many Islamic magazines, articles by those called Muslim thinkers stating the following:

First: that party pluralism is permissible, because there is an accepted doctrinal plurality among the Muslims. This is one.

The second: some of them said verbatim: the Kharijites represent the first accepted party pluralism under the Islamic state. What is your guidance?

* The Shaykh: As for first, it is said: the plurality of schools is nothing but a plurality of opinions only, but they do not form parties. And even if there existed among the fanatics of the schools what would require it to be partisanship, they deserve blame; otherwise in the medieval period there was fanaticism, to the point that some Hanbalis would strike the Shafi'is, and the Shafi'is would strike the Hanbalis. As for the matter of the Kharijites: the Kharijites fight while considering themselves Muslims, yet many of the scholars of the early generations (salaf) excluded them from Islam, because the Messenger (ﷺ) said: «They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes out of the game» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3610), and Muslim (1065 / 148), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].

As for the matter of thought, and what this "thought" is: if the thought opposes what Islam brought, it is false thought, rejected upon its holder, like the saying of the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a community﴾ [az-Zukhruf 22]. And if it is correct thought, it must be within Islam, and it does not require partisanship.

* Student: In the adhan, in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, that they will be «the longest of people in necks on the Day of Resurrection» [narrated by Muslim (387 / 14) from the hadith of Mu'awiyah], is this about those who persistently call the adhan constantly, or is it about those who call it sometimes (...)?

* The Shaykh: Apparently it refers to the muezzins who always call the adhan, meaning whoever is called a muezzin; otherwise the Messenger would have said: whoever calls the adhan.

* The Shaykh: May Allah bless you, this is based on the authenticity of a hadith, which is following the one who makes the iqamah, and the correct view is that the hadith is weak, and that following the one who makes the iqamah is not sunnah. Among these practices also is saying: "May Allah establish it and perpetuate it." * The Shaykh: True.

The Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ) is not plural; it is one Sunnah, one creed. How, Shaykh, can this be palatable to their hearts?

* The Shaykh: Say: "O Allah, guide me to the truth in what has been disputed, by Your permission, for You guide whom You will to a straight path. O Allah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the ability to follow it."

* Student: Shaykh, we mentioned that the preponderant opinion is that the adhan is superior to leading the prayer. Is this in terms of reward or rank?

* The Shaykh: No, in terms of reward, and in terms of rank as well. It is true that the imam is followed, but the muezzin bears great hardships; in earlier times he would climb the tall minaret five times a day and night. * The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement﴾. We have taken its benefits.

* Student: Praise.

And this style is called?

* The Shaykh: Yes; because you are opposed to this. And in His saying: ﴿and that most of you﴾ there is a caution against whom?

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us"﴾ to the end.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the challenge to those who resent the good of the people of goodness; based on His saying: ﴿Do you resent us only﴾ ﴿...?﴾ and this is not a place for resentment or aversion.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: this Ummah has merit and distinction over the earlier nations, because it believes in God, in what was revealed to it, and in what was revealed before. This is not found among the other nations; it is found only in this Ummah. For this reason God the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. And it is not possible for us to be witnesses over the people unless they have preceded us, so that we know what happened to them.

* Thus it is derived from this: the virtue of this Ummah, because it believes in God, in what was revealed to it, and in what was revealed before.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the believer should be forthright and not be hypocritical, based on His saying: ﴿and that most of you are defiant﴾, and this is a direct confrontation by describing them with defiance (fisq).

* Another benefit of this noble verse also: the precaution by which justice is observed, based on His saying: ﴿and that most of you are defiant﴾, and He did not say: "and that you are defiant", because if we believed that they were all defiant, this would be a matter for criticism; but we only say that most of them are defiant.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: that fisq (defiance) may mean kufr (disbelief). This is clear even in the Qur'an, in verses other than this one, which show that fisq may mean kufr and may also mean departure from obedience short of kufr. So the saying of the Blessed and Exalted in Surah as-Sajdah, when He said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiant?﴾ [as-Sajdah 16-18], the intended meaning of "defiant" here is the disbeliever, based on His saying: ﴿And as for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it, and it will be said to them: "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [as-Sajdah 20]. And whoever denies the Fire, his fisq is kufr, because he has denied the report of God the Mighty and Majestic.

The fisq that does not take one out of the religion is like the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, if a defiant person comes to you with a report, then verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat 6].

So the intended meaning of this verse, ﴿and that most of you are defiant﴾, is fisq of kufr, because they denied Muhammad (ﷺ).

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah?﴾ ﴿Say﴾ means: O Muhammad. ﴿Shall I inform you﴾ O People of the Book, that is: I will tell you of a matter of great importance, because the word naba' (news of great significance) is only used for a matter that is weighty and momentous, as Allah said: ﴿It is a great news﴾ [Sad 67], and He said: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ [An-Naba' 1-2]. This is in contrast to khabar (information), which may concern trivial matters, whereas naba' is only used for important matters. And perhaps, Allah knows best, this is because one of its derivations is from nubuwwah (elevation), and nubuwwah means elevation.

﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that﴾: the referent of "that" is the prayer of the Muslims, which these people took as a mockery and a game, saying: "What is this work? What is this play?" They mocked it, and it is well known that mocking an act entails mocking the one who performs it.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah?﴾ ﴿Mathubah﴾ means: outcome (consequence). It is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification), because it clarifies the indefiniteness of the comparative in His words ﴿bi-sharr﴾ ("something worse"), since the original form of sharr is (asharr), a comparative noun. The noun in the accusative that follows the comparative and clarifies it is called by them a tamyiz, as when you say: "Muhammad is more knowledgeable than you" ('ilman), where "'ilman" is a tamyiz because it clarifies the ambiguity of the comparative.

So ﴿mathubah﴾ we parse as what? As a tamyiz. And mathubah means "outcome," because it derives from (thaba, yathubu), meaning to return, so it means consequence and final destination.

﴿From Allah﴾, and this is the important part: what matters is the standing with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not with creation. If your standing is high and good with Allah, that is what matters, and that is what is sought.

Know that whenever you are in a high position with Allah, you will be in a high position with people, and the reverse is also true. For this reason a hadith says: "Whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah at the cost of the displeasure of people, Allah will suffice him against the burdens of people. And whoever seeks the pleasure of people at the cost of the displeasure of Allah, Allah will be displeased with him and will cause people to be displeased with him."[[Reported by at-Tirmidhi (2414) and Ibn Hibban (276) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and the wording is his.]]

﴿Worse than that as a recompense from Allah: whoever Allah has cursed﴾: "man" here is a relative pronoun, and it is the predicate of an omitted subject; the implied meaning is: it is "whoever Allah has cursed." This is the worst recompense with Allah, for those who have suffered these great calamities.

﴿Whoever Allah has cursed﴾ means: He expelled him and removed him far from His mercy. They are the Jews and the Christians, whom Allah has cursed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 78]. The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "The curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (436) and Muslim (531/22) from the hadith of 'A'ishah and Ibn 'Abbas.]]. So they are cursed and expelled from the mercy of Allah, just as Iblis was cursed. But there is hope that they may believe, whereas Iblis will never believe; this is the difference. Otherwise, they are cursed and expelled from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: ﴿and He was angry with him﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 60]. The anger of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is more severe than His curse, because expulsion and removal from mercy may or may not be accompanied by anger. The intended meaning may be depriving this person of Paradise even without anger, so anger is more severe. What shows that anger is more severe is the statement of the Blessed and Exalted in the verses of li'an. What is the cause of li'an?

* Student: The cause of li'an is that a man accuses his wife of adultery.

* Shaykh: Well done. Its cause is that a man accuses his wife of adultery. You know that no one can accuse his wife of adultery unless he is truthful, because it defiles his bed. Therefore the oaths take the place of witnesses. If a non-husband accuses a woman of adultery, we say: either produce four witnesses or receive the hadd punishment on your back. The husband does not need us to say this to him; we say to him: perform li'an. If the wife does not confess, then perform li'an. The man is brought forward and says: "I testify four times that this wife has committed adultery," and he testifies. In the fifth, he says: "And the curse of Allah be upon him." The pronoun here must be a first-person pronoun when the husband speaks it, but this is a way of avoiding attributing the curse to the speaker's own pronoun, because the curse is not upon the speaker. Upon whom is the curse? Upon the husband... 

If the wife does not confess, perform li'an. If the wife does not confess, then perform li'an. The man is brought forward and says: "I testify four times that this wife has committed adultery," and he testifies. In the fifth, he says: "And the curse of Allah be upon her." The pronoun here must be a first-person pronoun when the husband speaks it, but this is a way of avoiding attributing the curse to the speaker's own pronoun, because the curse is not upon the speaker. Upon whom is the curse? Upon the husband. For this reason he says: "upon me," and he testifies five times that his wife has committed adultery. In the fifth he says: "And the curse of Allah be upon me if he is among the liars." She testifies in rejection of the husband's words four times that he is a liar, and in the fifth: "And the anger of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful." It is well known that her lying is more serious than the husband's lying, because the husband is closer to truthfulness than she is, and she may do this to ward off a bad reputation from herself and her people. But the husband cannot be expected to take this into account. For this reason the anger is on her side and the curse on the husband's side, and by this we know that anger is more severe than curse.

﴿Whoever Allah has cursed and with whom He was angry﴾. So the Jews are those upon whom anger falls, because they knew the truth and did not act upon it. As for the Christians, this verse shows that the Christians are also those upon whom anger falls, since the address is to whom? To the People of the Book. There is no doubt that the Christians, after their denial of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), are among those upon whom anger falls, and there is no difference between them and the Jews. Indeed, they are more malicious than the Jews toward the Muslims. Anyone who reads the Crusades understands the intensity of Christian hostility toward the Muslims. Today they are a support for the Jews, backing them and defending them, with no inspection of their weapons and no rebuke of their crimes, and this is something that is not hidden from the blind, let alone the sighted. So "He was angry with him" in this verse applies to whom? To the Jews and the Christians, because after the sending of the Messenger, the Jews knew the truth, and the Christians after the sending of the Messenger knew the truth and rejected it. So they are all under this umbrella, the umbrella of anger.

﴿And made from them apes and swine and worshipped the Taghut﴾: ﴿made from them apes and swine﴾. The cause of the apes is that they devised a way to hunt the fish, which was forbidden for them to hunt on Saturday, so they contrived to catch them on Sunday. The scholars say: they would set nets on Friday, and on Saturday, glory be to Allah, Allah tested them by making the fish come up to the surface in great numbers, overflowing because of their abundance, yet hunting was forbidden to them. It was as if they could not bear this ruling, so what did they do? They devised a trick: they set the nets on Friday, the fish came into the nets on Saturday, and when Sunday came they took them. The outward act appeared permissible, since they did not hunt on Saturday but on Sunday. When this forbidden act resembled the lawful, Allah the Mighty and Majestic transformed them into apes, because it resembles the human. See, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. They became apes. Did they become apes in meaning or in reality? In reality: they became apes in reality. This is the view of the majority of the exegetes and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, although some contemporary scholars held that they were apes in meaning, that is, they became like apes, without the thinking or intellect of the children of Adam. But it is said: the original is what? The reality. The original is the reality, and Allah is capable of all things. The One who created man with this description is able to change him into another description. For this reason He said: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [Al-Baqarah 65], so they became apes. But did they remain?

The answer: No, because the purpose of their becoming apes was that they serve as a lesson and a deterrent, and it does not follow that their offspring continue. For this reason the scholars said: those who were transformed into an animal as a punishment have no offspring; they have no descendants. Whoever died, died.

﴿Swine﴾: where is this? Is there in the Qur'an that the Children of Israel became swine?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, besides this verse? Yes. We say: this verse says "made from them swine." As for knowing how they were or by what means, that is not necessary. If Allah reports about them that they became swine, then they are swine. Perhaps, and Allah knows best, and we do not speak about Allah what we do not know, perhaps those who were transformed into swine had their trickery in adultery, because it is known that swine have no jealousy at all. Other animals are jealous; no one approaches their female unless the male is absent. But the swine dismounts from its female and tells its companion: "Mount." They say it has no jealousy, and this is part of Allah's wisdom in forbidding swine, because it has no jealousy. In any case, if this is correct, Allah knows best; we do not know. The main point now is that we believe Allah made from the People of the Book what? Apes and swine.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And made from them apes and swine and worshipped the Taghut﴾. ﴿Worshipped the Taghut﴾ has two readings. The first: ﴿'abada al-taghut﴾, where ﴿'abada﴾ is a past-tense verb and ﴿al-taghut﴾ is the object. On this reading it is coordinated with the relative clause, which is His words: ﴿cursed by Allah, and with whom He was angry, and made from them apes and swine﴾. Have you understood? So ﴿'abada﴾ is a past-tense verb, in which there is a hidden pronoun referring to whom? To His words ﴿whoever Allah has cursed﴾. And ﴿al-taghut﴾ is the object, meaning: he worshipped the Taghut.

﴿Whoever Allah has cursed, and with whom He was angry, and made from them apes and swine, and worshipped the Taghut﴾: he worshipped it through bowing, prostration, and obedience in what it commands.

The meaning of Taghut is what Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, stated in the most comprehensive definition: he said: "Everything by which the servant exceeds his limit, whether an object of worship, one who is followed, or one who is obeyed."

Anyone who exceeds the limit in worshipping someone other than Allah, that object of worship is a taghut. Anyone who exceeds the limit in following something other than the law of Allah has taken it as a taghut. Anyone who exceeds his limit in obeying a ruler or a commander has taken him as a taghut. So taghut is: everything by which the servant exceeds his limit, whether an object of worship, one who is followed, or one who is obeyed. For this reason, it is what the servant exceeds his limit by, because the root of taghut is from tughyan (transgression); the root of taghut is from tughyan.

If someone asks: how do we call this object of worship a taghut? How do we call this one who is followed a taghut? How do we call this one who is obeyed a taghut? We say: taghut here means tughyan (transgression), and tughyan is not an attribute of the object, but an attribute of the agent: the worshipper who worshipped other than Allah, or who obeyed other than Allah in disobedience to Allah, or who followed other than the Messenger of Allah in disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second reading: ﴿wa-'abuda al-taghuti﴾, but on this reading al-taghut is in the genitive, and ('abud) is a singular noun, as one says: "as-subu'" and "as-subu'," so one says: "al-'abd" and "al-'abud." These are two dialects: 'abd and 'abud. On this reading, we say: ﴿'abuda al-taghuti﴾, and it is coordinated with what? With ﴿al-qiradah﴾, meaning: and made from them one who worships the taghut.

The People of the Book worship the taghut by taking their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. Allah said about them: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah son of Maryam, though they were commanded only to worship one God﴾ [At-Tawbah 31]. 'Adi ibn Hatim said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, we do not worship them." So he explained to them that obeying them in disobedience to Allah is worshipping them[[Reported by at-Tirmidhi (3095).]].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way.﴾ This sentence is among the finest in establishing that these people are worse than the Muslims in position. For this reason it was not a reply from the Messenger; rather it came as a reply from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The beginning of the verse: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾ One might say: "Yes, inform us," and then He mentions the attributes. But Allah said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, those described by these attributes: the curse, the anger, the transformation, and the fourth, worship of the taghut, these are worse in position than whom? Worse in position than the believers in Allah, those who believed in Allah and in what was revealed to them and what was revealed before, are worse in position. That is because their position is the Fire, and Allah's refuge is sought, while those believers have the Garden as their abode.

If someone says: it is well known that the comparative form shares the meaning between the one preferred and the one compared with in the basic sense, so is there any worse in Paradise? The answer: No, there is nothing bad in it. But this is like the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "The best rows of women are the last, and the worst of them are the first," the worst of them being the last row that has nothing bad in it, "the best rows of men are the first, and the worst of them are the last"[[Reported by Muslim (440/132) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And the opposite, like His words: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better resting place and a finer place of repose﴾ [Al-Furqan 24], although the companions of the Fire have neither good nor a fine resting place. Such comparison, the scholars of rhetoric say, is a comparison in which the other side has nothing of the meaning at all, whether in good or in evil.

His words: ﴿those are worse in place﴾: does "place" refer to what is opposed to time, or does "place" mean standing and rank, or both? Both. Their place is worse because it is the Fire, and their standing is worse because they are the most despicable.

﴿And further astray﴾ is coordinated with ﴿worse﴾, meaning: and those are further astray from the right way. "Further astray" is a comparative from what? 

* The student: from astray (...).

* The shaykh: From straying, yes. That is, more intensely astray from the straight, level path. It resembles the attribution of an adjective to its noun, since the way is level, and these are worse in place and further astray from the level way.

Is there any straying among the believers? No, but we say about it what we said about ﴿worse in place﴾. There is no straying.

Someone may say: perhaps this is a manner of conceding to the opponent, because the opponent claims that the believers are worse in place and further astray from the right way, so it is said: you are worse in place and you are further astray from the right way. But what we established first is clear and has no difficulty: a comparison may occur between two things where one of them has no part of the meaning.

And what happened to the righteous predecessors when they said: "If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us with swords over it"[[Reported by al-Bayhaqi in az-Zuhd al-Kabir (80) from Ibrahim ibn Adham.]].

* Student: (...) that the saying of Allah, "not of those who earn anger, nor of those who are astray" [Al-Fatihah 7] (...)?

**Shaykh:** If we say this is a matter of meaning (ma'nawi), then it may befall them. One may be turned upside down, God forbid, and gain no benefit from the truth. And if we say it is physical (hissi), it is the same. Did the Prophet ﷺ not say: "Does the one who raises his head before the imam not fear that Allah will turn his head into a donkey's head," or "make his form the form of a donkey"?[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (691) and Muslim (427/115), from Abu Hurayrah.]]

**Shaykh:** No. "Wahhabi" is attributed to this school of thought. They think that Shaykh Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, invented a new school. It is true that it is a new school in relation to them and their polytheism, but in relation to the People of the Sunnah, what do we say? In relation to the People of the Sunnah, it is not independent.

They described the Messenger as a sorcerer, a liar, a madman, and a poet. Indeed Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "A sorcerer or a madman"﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 52].
