**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe," but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing (61). And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and their consumption of the unlawful. Wretched is what they have been doing (62). Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them from their saying of sin and their consumption of the unlawful? Wretched is what they have been producing (63). And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and they are cursed for what they have said. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it, and they strive upon the earth in corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ [al-Ma'idah 61–64].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. In the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿and [some of them] worshipped the taghut﴾, are there more than one reading?

**Student:** Two readings.

**Shaykh:** Two readings.

**Student:** The first reading is ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, with ('abada) in the past tense. The second reading is ﴿wa 'abuda al-taghut﴾, because ('abud) is a noun.

**Shaykh:** A noun, meaning ('abud) and ('abd) are both one, like *subu'* (lion) [and] *sab'* (lion)?

**Student:** Like *sub'*.

**Shaykh:** *Subu'*, no.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Like *subu'in* and *sab'in*, yes.

**Shaykh:** On the reading of the verb ﴿'abada al-taghut﴾, where does this conjoined phrase attach, to what?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** It is conjoined to ﴿la'anahu Allah﴾ (whom Allah has cursed). Yes, meaning: whom Allah has cursed and who worshipped the taghut.

We mentioned that the most comprehensive of what has been said about the meaning of *taghut* is?

**Student:** Everything by which the servant transgresses.

**Shaykh:** Everything by which the servant transgresses his limit.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Or what is obeyed. Who said this?

**Student:** Ibn al-Qayyim.

**Shaykh:** Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him.

**Shaykh:** His saying: ﴿Those are worse in position﴾. The grammatical analysis of ﴿makanan﴾ (in position)?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** It is a specification (tamyiz) of what?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Because the comparative form was indefinite. Is there a rule on this matter?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** As a specification for it, like: ﴿I am more numerous than you in wealth﴾ [al-Kahf 34], ﴿mightier in men﴾ [al-Kahf 34], and so on.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾. In ﴿when they come to you﴾, the address is to the Prophet ﷺ and those with him.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of worse than that in recompense from Allah?"﴾

* From the benefits of this noble verse: presenting the address in the form of a question, because that is more effective upon the soul and more present to the heart: ﴿Shall I inform you﴾. Similar is His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 221], and similarly His saying: ﴿Say, "Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ [al-Kahf 103].

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that those Jews who mocked the Prophet ﷺ and his companions are worse in position and further astray from the right way, because of the attributes mentioned.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that what matters is one's standing with Allah, due to His saying: ﴿recompense from Allah﴾.

It follows from this that we should not look to our standing among people, but rather to our standing with Allah the Mighty and Majestic. If we set this right, Allah will spare us the burden of people.

* And from the benefits of this verse: that the comparative form may be used between two things that do not share the basic meaning, due to His saying: ﴿worse in recompense than that﴾, because the meaning is: "more evil than that." Similarly for good: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, are better in resting place﴾ [al-Furqan 24], and there is no good in the resting place of the people of the Fire.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that those Jews, indeed the People of the Book in general, were characterized by these four attributes: the curse, anger, transformation, and worship of the taghut.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of anger for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, due to His saying: ﴿and with whom He became angry﴾. In Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿not of those who have earned anger﴾ [al-Fatihah 7]. Anger is one of the attributes of His essence, the Mighty and Majestic, but it is among the active attributes. We say "of His essence" so that no one says that anger is retribution, and retribution is something separate from the essence of Allah. This is what the People of the Sunnah wal-Jama'ah (the followers of the Sunnah and the community) hold: that anger is an attribute of Allah, affirmed for Allah in reality, without distortion (tahrif). The people of distortion explained it as meaning retribution or the will to retribute. Whoever affirms will (irada) says: it means the will to retribute, and whoever does not affirm it says: it means retribution. But this interpretation is rejected:

First: because it contradicts the apparent wording, and the basic rule regarding reports is that they are taken according to their apparent meaning unless there is valid evidence otherwise.

Second: because it contradicts what the Salaf (early generations) held. Not a single word has come from the Companions, nor the Successors, nor the imams, explaining anger as retribution or its will.

Their silence about interpreting it in a way that contradicts the apparent meaning is evidence of what? It is evidence of their consensus (ijma') that its intended meaning is its apparent meaning. Therefore, interpreting it as retribution or the will to retribute contradicts the consensus of the Salaf. This is a beneficial principle that serves you in all the attributes of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Third: the Qur'an refutes it, because this interpretation is nullified by the Noble Qur'an in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all﴾ [az-Zukhruf 55]. The meaning of ﴿angered Us﴾ is ﴿made Us angry﴾, and ﴿We took retribution from them﴾. It is well known that the response is other than the condition. ﴿We took retribution﴾ is the answer to the condition, and ﴿angered Us﴾ is the verb of the condition, and the answer of a condition undoubtedly differs from the condition. This noble verse refutes that interpretation.

Fourth: even if we concede and say that it is the will (the will to retribute) or retribution itself, it necessarily follows that there is anger, because the will to retribute, or retribution itself, occurs only as a result of doing something the avenger does not approve of, and this results from anger. Whatever they try, they must accept the affirmation of anger for Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Here there is a phrase that some scholars mention, even among the verifiers (muhaqqiqun): "The method of the Salaf is safer, and the method of the later scholars (khalaf) is more knowledgeable and wiser." This phrase contains truth and falsehood. The truth is their saying that the method of the Salaf is safer. The falsehood is their saying that the method of the later scholars is more knowledgeable and wiser, because this last clause completely contradicts the first. How can safety exist with ignorance or foolishness? The opposite of knowledge is ignorance, and the opposite of wisdom is foolishness. How can there be safety without knowledge and wisdom? Therefore, if the method of the Salaf is safer, it must also be more knowledgeable and wiser. Evidence for this is that the books of the Salaf, praise be to Allah, are filled with explanations of the verses and hadiths about the attributes, and not a single word has come from them saying, "By Allah, we do not know this meaning, we do not know the meaning of the verse, we do not know the meaning of the hadith," never. Rather, they used to say: "The meaning is known and the modality (kayf) is unknown," and they said: "Let them pass as they came, without asking how." So the method of the Salaf is safer, more knowledgeable, and wiser.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic to transform a human into an ape and a pig, due to His saying: ﴿and made of them apes and pigs﴾. Is this making a cosmic making (kawni) or a decreed making (qadari)?

* Students: (...).

**Shaykh:** Yes, the cosmic and the decreed are one. Cosmic or legislative? Cosmic. His saying: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [al-Baqarah 65] is a cosmic command, not a legislative command.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that asking Allah for something should not seem impossible to a person, as long as the request does not involve transgression. For example, take a man afflicted with cancer. Some people say: cancer is a disease from which recovery is not hoped for, and this is generally true without doubt. But some people despair and say: how can I ask Allah to heal me from this disease, when usually one does not recover from it? This is a grave error, because the One who created the disease is able to remove it, and the One who created you when you were nothing is able to restore you as you were. For this reason, when Zakariyya, peace be upon him, said: ﴿How can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?﴾ [Maryam 8], Allah said: ﴿Thus said your Lord﴾ [Maryam 9], ﴿and I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ [Maryam 9]. So do not despair; Allah is over all things competent.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah the Exalted in punishment, where the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Later in the verse of the Jews' saying: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], they were punished with what? With the chaining of the hand. Recompense is always of the same kind as the deed, part for part and whole for whole, equal in reward or in punishment. In a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever frees a slave, Allah frees for each of his limbs a limb of his from the Fire, even the private part for the private part."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6715) and Muslim (1509/22), from Abu Hurayrah.]] This is in reward. As for punishment, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (60) and Muslim (241/27), from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr.]] This is because the neglect occurred in the heels. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, performed ablution hurriedly, so they wiped their feet and did not complete them. So the Prophet ﷺ called out: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whatever is below the two ankles is in the Fire."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5787), from Abu Hurayrah.]] Here the punishment was partial, in proportion to the violation.

Here, the wisdom in making them apes and pigs: we previously said that the ape is closest to the human, and the trick they performed is closest to a permissible loophole, but it is forbidden.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: whoever worships other than Allah has worshipped the taghut, meaning he has performed the worship of the taghut.

If someone asks: does this include what came in the hadith: "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, wretched is the slave of the dirham, wretched is the slave of the velvet cloak, wretched is the slave of the embroidered cloth"?[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2886), from Abu Hurayrah.]]

We say: yes, if wealth becomes his greatest concern, then this is a form of worship.

If someone asks: according to this, would 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, be a taghut? We seek Allah's protection.

The answer: No, because the meaning of "worshipped the taghut" is "performed the worship of the taghut," meaning transgression. So the transgression refers to whom? To the worshipper or the worshipped? To the worshipper. When Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto (98). If these were gods, they would not have arrived there, but all will abide therein﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98–99], the polytheists said to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "So 'Isa ibn Maryam is in the Fire, since he was worshipped besides Allah?" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it﴾[[Narrated by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (985) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3490), from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]] [al-Anbiya' 101], and He showed that their comparison with 'Isa was nothing but argument. He said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾ [az-Zukhruf 58].

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever is characterized by these attributes is the worst of people in position, due to His saying: ﴿Those are worse in position﴾.

* And from its benefits: that whoever is characterized by these attributes is also the most astray of people from the right way, due to His saying: ﴿and further astray from the right way﴾.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe."﴾ The address ﴿come to you﴾ is to the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. The doer of the action is the hypocrites among the Jews, who come to the Prophet ﷺ and say, ﴿"We believe,"﴾ but only with their mouths, while their hearts do not believe. ﴿And they had certainly entered with disbelief and they had certainly left with it.﴾ Regarding ﴿دَخَلُوا بِالْكُفْرِ﴾ (*dakhalū bil-kufr*, "entered with disbelief"), the scholars said that the *bāʾ* here (the *bāʾ* of accompaniment) indicates *mulābasah wa-muṣāḥabah* (being accompanied by something), meaning they were clothed in disbelief. ﴿And they had certainly left with it﴾ means they left while still clothed in disbelief. Thus they were upon disbelief both when they entered and when they left. Even if they say, "We believe," their hearts do not believe; they are hypocrites. ﴿And they had certainly entered with disbelief and they had certainly left with it﴾ previously: they left with disbelief and they will leave, when they enter upon you, with disbelief too. Some of them even support one another against the Muslims: ﴿And a faction of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they will return. And do not believe except those who follow your religion."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 72–73].

﴿And they had certainly left with it, and Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.﴾ ﴿Most knowing﴾ (*aʿlam*, the elative form, *ism al-tafḍīl*) than you, ﴿of what they were concealing﴾, that is, what they were hiding of disbelief. The elative form here is on its proper meaning. Whenever this attribute comes in this form, it is an elative (*ism al-tafḍīl*) in its proper sense. Whoever interpreted it as an active participle has erred when he said, ﴿Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing﴾ and said: "Allah is All-Knowing (*ʿalīm*) or Knowing (*ʿālim*) of what they were concealing," because if one says *ʿalīm* or *ʿālim*, it does not exclude sharing [of the attribute with creation]. But if one says *aʿlam*, what is it? It excludes sharing: nothing is like Him in knowledge. However, they fled from one thing and fell into something worse. They said "*aʿlam*"; but when you say *aʿlam*, the rule is that the elative form indicates that the one preferred and the one compared share the attribute.

We say: Yes, there is no doubt that the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and the created being share the basic attribute, which is knowledge, and this must be so. The affirmation of knowledge for created beings is found in the Qur'an: ﴿Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ [al-Zumar 9]. What is impossible is to make the knowledge of the creature like the knowledge of the Creator. As for sharing in the basic attribute, this is unavoidable. Likewise life, power, hearing, and sight: sharing in the basic meaning is necessary. So we say: You prevented the elative from having its proper meaning out of fear of sharing in the basic meaning. But when you say *ʿālim* or *ʿalīm*, you have equated the Creator and the creature, because the created being is also called *ʿālim* and called *ʿalīm*, is it not so? Therefore, you will never find a person who departs from the implications of the texts of the Book and the Sunnah except that he falls into an evil he was warned against.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the warning against hypocrites, because Allah did not relate their stories or their condition to us except so that we would be warned, not merely so that we would know. We are to be warned.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, knowing what is in the hearts, from His saying: ﴿and Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing﴾. So the affirmation of His knowledge of what is in the hearts is established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: we are not to judge except by what appears, because Allah has informed us of this only so that we would be warned. Had we remained with what appears to us, these people would be what? Believers according to what they say. But Allah informed us of this so that we would be warned.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warning a person against concealing in his heart what contradicts his tongue. This is a matter we must treat in ourselves. Beware of harboring in your heart what contradicts what you utter with your tongue or do with your limbs. You must first purify and cleanse the heart, and then build your actions according to this purification.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 62–63:

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And you see many of them hastening to sin and aggression and consuming of the unlawful gain. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾

﴿You see﴾ is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ), and the apparent meaning is that the seeing here is visual. It is also permissible that it be cognitive (ʿilmiyyah), in which case ﴿many﴾ is the first object and ﴿hastening﴾ is the second object.

﴿You see many of them﴾, i.e., of those who come to you saying that they are believers, ﴿hastening to sin﴾, meaning they race to it, each trying to be the quickest, ﴿and aggression﴾. Sin (ithm) relates to the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and aggression (ʿudwan) relates to the right of the human being. Some have explained sin as lying and aggression as injustice, but when we say that sin relates to the right of Allah and aggression relates to the right of the human being, it is more general and comprehensive.

﴿And their consuming of the unlawful gain (al-suḥt)﴾, meaning they hasten in their consuming of the unlawful gain, racing to it. And what is al-suḥt? Al-suḥt is every unlawful earning; whatever is unlawful gain is suḥt. This includes usury (ribā), it includes bribery (rishwah), it includes fraud (ghash), and every unlawful earning falls under the term suḥt.

It has been described with this repulsive description for two reasons:

The first reason: there is no blessing in it.

The second reason: it is a cause of the destruction (suḥt) of the wealth that exists.

So it is evil in itself and evil in its effect. That is why, when the unlawful enters a person's life, blessing is removed from his wealth and his craving for wealth intensifies; that is, he is afflicted with greed (shuḥḥ).

﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing﴾. The lam here is the lam of the answer to an oath, and the implied sense is: "By Allah, evil indeed is what they have been doing." Bi'sa (بئس) acts like laysa (ليس). Where is its predicate?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, I said it acts like laysa, and it governs that what follows it is the subject (fāʿil), and the specified object (al-makhsūs) is omitted, i.e., "Evil indeed is what they have been doing, their deed," meaning that their deed is blameworthy, and this description applies to them: ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing﴾. What did they do? Hastening to sin, hastening to aggression, consuming unlawful gain. All three of these matters deserve blame.

Sin (ithm) relates to the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and aggression (ʿudwan) relates to the right of the human being. Some have explained sin as lying and aggression as injustice, but when we say that sin relates to the right of Allah and aggression relates to the right of the human being, it is more general and comprehensive.

This includes usury (ribā), it includes bribery (rishwah), it includes fraud (ghash), and every unlawful earning falls under the term suḥt.

The first reason: there is no blessing in it.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And the Jews say, "Allah's hand is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills. What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it, and they strive to cause corruption on the earth, but Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Jews say, "Allah's hand is chained up."﴾ The Jews are those who claim to be followers of Musa, peace be upon him. They were given this name. It is said that it derives from Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf 156], meaning from *al-hud*, which is returning. It is also said that it is a reference to their forefather Yahudha (Judah), but the name was Arabized and became *Yahud*. Whatever the origin, what is meant by it is those who attribute themselves to Musa, peace be upon him.

They said: ﴿Allah's hand is chained up.﴾ They said "Allah's hand" first and did not say "Allah's two hands" with the dual form, because they wanted to diminish the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, both in His essence and in His actions. As for His essence, it is well known that the one with two hands is more perfect than the one with a single hand. As for His actions, their saying that it is chained up means that it is restrained from giving. A hand is either chained up, its owner's arm bound to his neck so that it cannot extend to give, or it is outstretched and gives. For this reason Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely outstretched﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. ﴿Allah's hand is chained up﴾ means it is restrained from giving. They also said in another description: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor﴾ [Al 'Imran 181]. So they described Allah once as miserly and once as poor, may the curse of Allah be upon them until the Day of Resurrection. This is because they are people of wealth and greed, and they want Allah to shower wealth upon them according to their desires. When the wealth is not as they desire, they say: "This is miserliness from Allah, or poverty from Him." ﴿Allah's hand is chained up.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their hands are chained up﴾, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. So their hands were chained up. This is a statement of fact, not a supplication, because it comes from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informs; He does not supplicate. He informed that their hands were chained up, meaning restrained from giving. For this reason we say that the most miserly of all nations are the Jews. A Jew cannot give a dinar without wanting to receive two dinars back, or a fils without wanting to receive two fils back. Do not think of anything else, because their hands are chained up.

﴿And they are cursed﴾, meaning they were expelled from the mercy of Allah and distanced from it because of this statement. For this reason He said: ﴿for what they said﴾. The *ba'* here is very clearly causal. As for *ma*, it may be a verbal-source particle (*masdariyyah*) or a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*). If it is verbal-source, the meaning is: "they were cursed for their saying." If it is relative, the meaning is: "they were cursed for what they said." Had the pronoun *qalu-hu* (they said it) been used, it would have been definite that *ma* is a relative noun, but it was omitted. In any case, whether we take it as verbal-source or relative, it indicates that this punishment that befell them was because of their saying.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾. *Bal* here is for *idrab ibtali* (a retraction that negates the previous statement). What was negated? Their saying "Allah's hand is chained up," so He said ﴿Rather, both His hands﴾, and He did not say "His hand," because He, glorified is He, has two hands. ﴿Are outstretched﴾ means not closed, let alone chained.

﴿Both are outstretched, He spends as He wills.﴾ ﴿He spends﴾ means He gives wealth ﴿as He wills﴾, that is, in whatever manner He wills. If He wills, He expands, and if He wills, He restricts. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts﴾ [al-Ra'd 26]. He may give and He may withhold according to what wisdom requires, not according to what a person desires. For this reason a person may want to earn much by some deed but be deprived, and another may do a small deed that he does not think will bring much gain, and yet gain much from it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief.﴾ Here *zada* (to increase) takes two objects, neither of which originally is a subject and predicate. The first object is ﴿many﴾ and the second is ﴿transgression﴾. As for His saying ﴿what has been sent down﴾, *ma* here is the subject. The meaning is that what was sent down to the Messenger, peace be upon him, increases many of them, though not all of them, in transgression against the servants of Allah and against the right of Allah, and in disbelief in Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The *lam* in His saying ﴿and surely will increase﴾ falls in the answer of an oath. Accordingly the sentence is emphasized, and with three emphases: the implied oath, whose implied form is "by Allah"; the *lam*; and the *nun* of emphasis. Allah emphasized this because of its importance, and so that no one who denies it would object that the revelation, which is a healing for what is in the breasts, which is the Qur'an, increases these people in transgression and disbelief. Do not be surprised. Then, transgression against whom? Against Allah and against the servants. And disbelief, meaning in what was sent down to the Messenger, peace be upon him. They will not benefit from what was sent down to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred.﴾ The *waw* may be resumptive (*isti'nafiyyah*, beginning a new sentence), or it may be coordinated with His saying ﴿their hands are chained up﴾. Its meaning: ﴿We cast among them enmity﴾, that is, We placed it. ﴿Among them enmity and hatred.﴾ *Al-'adu* is the opposite of the ally, and *al-baghid* is the opposite of the beloved. That is, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, cast among them hatred in the hearts and enmity in the bodies and in speech. No one supports another, no one allies with another, no one loves another. ﴿Among them enmity and hatred.﴾ Until when? ﴿Until the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning until the end of the world. The Jews are enemies of one another and hate one another, because Allah the Exalted informed that He cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection, and His report is true and His promise is sincere.

﴿Whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it.﴾ ﴿Whenever they kindle﴾: *kullama* here is a conditional particle, its condition is ﴿they kindle﴾, and its answer is ﴿Allah extinguishes it.﴾ That is, whenever they wish for war and kindle its fire, Allah extinguishes it, and it will never stand for them, rather they are forsaken.

This is supported by Allah's saying in another verse: ﴿Humiliation has been struck upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah and a rope from people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112]. The scholars said: the rope from Allah is Islam, and the rope from people is covenant and pact. It was also said that the rope from people is assistance and the means by which they are supported, because *al-habl* (rope) is used for a means, as in Allah's saying: ﴿Hold fast to the rope of Allah all together﴾ [Al 'Imran 103], meaning to His religion, which is the means to happiness.

So we say: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has shown that these Jews, ﴿whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾, meaning they did not attain their aim through it. It does not mean that war will not occur. War occurs, and it has broken out between them and the Muslims in several battles, but the outcome is that Allah extinguishes it, and does not grant them what they want of consuming their enemy with this fire.

﴿Whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it, and they strive in the earth to cause corruption.﴾ ﴿They strive﴾ means they cast corruption into it. He expressed it with *sa'y* (striving) to indicate their haste in this. For this reason the Jews were the most corrupt people on earth, because of the events attributed to them. Whoever wishes to learn something of that should consult the book *Ighathat al-Lahfan min Masayid al-Shaytan* (The Rescue of the Distressed from the Snares of Satan) by Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him.

﴿And they strive in the earth to cause corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ He did not say "does not love them," in order to indicate generality and to state the reason. For example, ﴿Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ includes Jews and non-Jews. It also indicates that Allah does not love these people because they are corrupters, so the statement is more general here: every corrupter, Allah does not love him.

* In this noble verse: a demonstration of the Jews' aggression, and that they openly transgress even against the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, by their saying ﴿Allah's hand is chained up.﴾
* Also in it: that the Jews affirm the true attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because one does not say "someone's hand is chained up" except of one who has a hand. So the Jews' affirmation of the descriptive attributes is better than their denial, although the Jews have no religion, yet the truth must be accepted from any person.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an allusion to the Jews' greed for wealth. The proof: nothing but avarice and covetousness moved them to this statement.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the purification of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, from miserliness. The reasoning: Allah punished them for this statement, and the Blessed and Exalted punishes only for a forbidden thing.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an allusion to the Jews' miserliness, from His saying ﴿Their hands are chained up﴾, and it was mentioned a little earlier that this is a statement of fact and not a supplication.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Jews were tested with these two matters, miserliness and the curse. So they are the furthest of people from the mercy of Allah, or among the furthest of people from it, from His saying ﴿And they are cursed for what they said﴾. Allah did not specify who curses them, to indicate generality: Allah curses them, and those who curse also curse them. This is like His saying: ﴿not of those who have incurred anger﴾ [al-Fatihah 7] after His saying ﴿those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾ [al-Fatihah 7], and He did not say "not those upon whom You have been angry," to indicate generality, and that these are the ones who incur anger from Allah and from the friends of Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes. Is it to be taken?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. From His saying ﴿for what they said﴾, meaning that Allah, glorified is He, did not chain their hands and curse them except because of their saying. In it is the affirmation of causes. Causes are of two kinds: sensory and legislative, and both are established. Among the legislative causes: righteous deeds are a cause for entering Paradise, and disbelief is a cause for entering the Fire. This is a legislative cause. Among the sensory causes is what we find in the cosmos: fire burns, frost freezes water, and the like. These are sensory causes. Eating is a cause of satiety, and its instances cannot be counted.

Do causes have effect by themselves?

The answer is no. But they have effect by the will of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, through the influential powers He has placed in them. This is the view indicated by the evidence of the Book, the Sunnah, and reason. As for the one who says that they have no effect at all, he has said something that the foolish laugh at. And the one who says that they have effect by their own nature has said something objectionable. As for the first, who says they have no effect, this is a statement at which the foolish laugh. For example, if a person eats while hungry and then becomes full, the cause of his fullness was not the food; rather, fullness occurred at the time of eating. Otherwise, the food did not satisfy him. And if you place a paper in the fire and it burns, the fire did not burn it; it burned near the fire. Glory be to Allah! And if a bottle is struck with a stone and breaks, the stone did not break it; it broke near it, not by it. This is something the least intelligent child knows is wrong.

Those who say that causes have effect by their own nature have also associated partners with Allah, affirming a creator alongside Allah. We refute them by saying that Allah is the Creator of everything, and that Allah may change the realities of these things.

Among that: Allah the Exalted said to the fire that was kindled, which was a great blaze, in which Ibrahim was to be thrown, and when he was thrown into it, Allah said to it: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69], and it became coolness and safety upon Ibrahim. This shows that causes do not have effect by themselves; they have effect by the powers Allah has placed in them. Otherwise, there may be impediments. Even legislative causes may have impediments. For example, the cause of inheritance is kinship, and if a relative differs from another relative in religion, he does not inherit from him.

So the summary is: whoever affirms that causes have effect by their own essence is a polytheist, and whoever negates their effect entirely is a fool. What remains is to say: they have effect by the influential powers Allah has placed in them, which may be prevented by the will and decree of Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. The proof: His saying ﴿for what they said﴾, for His saying ﴿for what they said﴾ indicates the implication of the speech (*fahwa al-khitab*) and the force of the address: they were punished only with the like of what they did.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two hands for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from His saying ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾.

* Among its benefits: that they are two, with no addition or subtraction. The reasoning: whatever is restricted to a number is necessarily neither increased nor decreased. For example, if a man has dirhams, the amount could be three, ten, a hundred, or a thousand, but if he has "three dirhams," it admits no increase or decrease. So everything restricted to a number requires that it be neither increased nor decreased. Accordingly, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has two hands, and this is what the early generations (*al-salaf*) agreed upon, based on the evidence of the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

If someone says: Did not Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: ﴿Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ [Ya-Sin 71]? Did not Allah say: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion﴾ [al-Mulk 1]?

The answer: Yes, but the answer regarding the first verse, ﴿of what Our hands have made﴾, is that it does not mean the literal hand. Rather, what is meant by ﴿of what Our hands have made﴾ is "of what We have done." The Arabs use "hand" to mean the doer. Consider His saying: ﴿And whatever misfortune strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [al-Shura 30]. It is well known that earning is not restricted to the hand; it occurs by the hand, and also by the foot, the tongue, the eye, the nose, the private parts, and the heart. But the noble Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic, so the expressions found in Arabic speech also appear in the Qur'an. For this reason, if the literal meaning of "hand" were intended here, excluding the doer, then camels would be more honorable than us, because we were created by what? By the word. Except Adam, whom Allah created by His hand. And camels, on the supposition that the meaning is that the command of Allah was by His hand, were created by the hand. As for the singular, it does not contradict plurality, because it is a known rule that a singular noun in construct form (*al-mufrad al-mudaf*) includes whatever its referent requires. For example, if a man says, "My wife is divorced," and he has two wives, both are divorced, unless he intended one. If he says, "My slave is free," and he has slaves, all his slaves are freed, unless he had a specific intention. Accordingly, we say: the singular does not contradict the dual, because it is in construct form and therefore general. And the plural does not contradict the dual, because the meaning is not the literal hand but the essence, that is, what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made. It is plural, as in ﴿Our hands﴾, for harmony between the construct and what it is attached to, since *na* (we) is used for plurality or for majesty. So the hands were made plural to glorify and magnify them, and to observe the harmony with the attached pronoun, so that the speech harmonizes. The main point is to affirm that Allah has two hands.

Here are some questions: Are they literal or not?

The answer: Yes, they are literal, two real hands. Whoever interprets them as power has said about Allah what he has no knowledge of, indeed what the text indicates the opposite of. For this reason we say: every person who distorts the text from its apparent meaning has committed two errors. The first: turning it away from its intended apparent meaning. The second: affirming a meaning that was not intended. Is that not so? Then the intended meaning is the two real hands.

Second question: Do these two hands resemble the hands of created beings?

This is impossible, because every attribute whose apparent meaning is likeness is rejected by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [al-Shura 11]. I say "apparent meaning" in the sense of the superficial outward meaning, which is rejected.

Third question: Does this hand grasp, hold, and shake, or not?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 64 (part 2 of 3):**

The answer is yes, because this is established by the Sunnah, and indeed by the Qur'an: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entire will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 67].

Are these two hands described as right and left?

On this there are two opinions among the early scholars (al-salaf). Some said no, and they denied the word "left" (shimal) found in Sahih Muslim[[(2788 / 24) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.]]. Others said yes. Each side has a basis for its view. But the correct position is that they are affirmed, and that the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I chose the right hand of my Lord, and both His hands are right" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3368) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] is abundance of good, blessing and equality. This is because a created being who has a right and a left, or a right and a left hand, has them differing: the right and the left differ in strength, even in physical strength. But the hands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, (and I mean the dual form) do not differ. Both of them are right. This is the correct view: that we affirm the left.

Are these two hands described as right and left (shimal)?

On this there are two opinions among the early scholars. Some said no, and they denied the word "left" (al-shimal) found in Sahih Muslim[[Muslim (2788 / 24) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, and its wording is: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then He will take them in His right hand, then He will say: 'I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?' Then He will fold up the earths in His left hand..."]]. Others said yes. Each side has a basis for its view. But the correct position is that they are affirmed, and that the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I chose the right hand of my Lord, and both His hands are right" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3368) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] is abundance of good (al-yumn), blessing and equality. This is because a created being who has a right and a left, or a right and a left hand, has the right and the left differing. Is that not so? They differ in strength, even in physical strength. But the two hands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (and I mean the dual form), do not differ. Both of them are right. This is the correct view: that we affirm the left for Allah, but not in the sense that it is deficient compared with the right. Rather, both of them are right.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the abundance of Allah's giving and His generosity. This is shown by His saying: ﴿outstretched﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. His hands cannot be restricted when it comes to giving; rather, they are outstretched. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The hand of Allah is full and overflowing, pouring out night and day." "Full" (mala') means filled with goodness, generosity and blessing. "Overflowing" (sahhA') means abundant in giving. "Night and day" is an adverbial expression: He gives by night and by day. "It is not diminished by expenditure" means that what He spends and gives does not reduce it, glory be to Him and exalted is He. Then he gave an example and said: "Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? [The answer is:] Yes, we have seen it, but we cannot count it. Yet He has not reduced what is in His right hand." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4684) and Muslim (993 / 37) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. The wording is al-Bukhari's.]] That is, what is in His right hand, blessed and exalted is He, has not been diminished. So the hand of Allah is outstretched, full and overflowing, pouring out night and day.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah's giving and His withholding follow His will. This is shown by His saying: ﴿He spends as He wills﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. This one He gives much wealth; that one He gives great health and great intellect; and the opposite happens to others; and some are in between, in all that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bestows, whether it is material or immaterial, sensory or non-sensory. He spends as He wills.

You should hold this principle: whatever Allah has linked to His will is also bound by His wisdom. That is, it is not will alone, unaccompanied by wisdom, as some of the Jahmiyyah maintained. They say that Allah does a thing merely by will and not for any wisdom, because He is not questioned about what He does. Therefore one should not say: "What is the wisdom of this?" or "Why did He do that?"

Rather, we say that everything connected with His will is also connected with wisdom. The evidence is beyond counting: Allah described Himself as All-Wise and as the Most Wise of judges. And it is known that the wise does not produce any act except for a wise purpose.

Second: Allah said: ﴿Whoever wills takes a path to his Lord. And you will not will unless Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 29-30]. In this there is an indication that His will follows His wisdom. On this basis, if something occurs in the world, whether an earthly or a heavenly event, and you find it strange and say: "Why did it happen?" then you must say to the mind that raised this question: "For a wisdom." But we are not required to comprehend the wisdoms of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, just as we do not comprehend all His attributes. Likewise, His wisdom. There may be a hidden wisdom that is not known until some time has passed. But you, O believer, must believe that everything Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has done is for a wisdom. It cannot be play or idle sport. Do you understand?

So as to His saying: ﴿how He wills﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]: when you know this, and know that His will is tied to wisdom, then do not say: "Why was this master poor among his people?" or "Why was the wretched son of a wretched man rich?" Do not say such things. Why? Because we know that this giving and this withholding come from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that they are tied to wisdom.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: many people are increased in nothing by the verses except rebellion and disbelief. This is shown by His saying: ﴿What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. Do not be surprised. In the last part of Surah al-Tawbah, Allah mentioned that when a surah is revealed, people divide into two groups: ﴿Among them are those who say: "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it adds to them filth upon their filth﴾ [al-Tawbah 124-125]. And do not be surprised that one thing is a remedy for one people and a sickness for another. Just as this holds in matters of the intellect, it also holds in matters of the senses. Have you seen a patient whom doctors forbid from eating dates? If he eats them, he falls ill, while another who eats them becomes well, even though the date is one and the same. Some people are ordered to take plenty of oil, and others are forbidden it, and there are many such things. So do not be surprised if, in matters of the intellect, there is something that increases some peoples and diminishes others.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the obstinacy of the Jews, and that they cannot submit to what was sent down from heaven, since what was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ) increases them in nothing but rebellion and disbelief.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: justice and fairness in the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is because He said: ﴿many of them﴾ and did not say "most of them" or "all of them." For this reason, when a person sees deviation among a people by some of them, he must not apply the judgment to all of them. Rather, he should say "many," or "some," or "among them," or something similar. If he generalizes while there are upright people among the others, he would be unjust in one respect and lying in another respect. This is why you find that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says: ﴿will surely increase many of them﴾, and does not say "most" or "all."

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is true. This is shown by His saying: ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) was one upon whom revelation was sent down, so he is truly the Messenger of Allah.

* A student: What is the limit of "many"?

* The Shaykh: "Many" depends on the proportion. For example: three out of ten. Is that few or many?

* A student: Few.

* The Shaykh: No, it is many. Three out of ten is about a third.

Thirty out of thirty thousand? That is few.

* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Some scholars say that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, will reveal the wisdom to people on the Day of Resurrection. Is this statement correct, or is there evidence for it?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know. It might be taken from the fact that Allah explained that on the Day of Resurrection He will make clear to people what they were reminded of. Allah knows best. But among the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that He made some of the wisdoms hidden. This is because a person's servitude is not fully realized unless he submits to what is clear in its wisdom and to what is not. If everything were clear, the matter would be obvious. Concealing some wisdoms is undoubtedly part of the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, perfect submission is that a person says: "We hear and we obey," and does not question. I have pointed out an issue that may have been unnoticed by many people. When it is said: "Allah has commanded such and such," or "the Messenger has commanded such and such," a person says: "What kind of command is it, recommended or obligatory?" This is not correct. The perfection of servitude is to say: "We hear and we obey," and then act.

Yes, if you have fallen into a matter and opposed what was commanded, or committed what is forbidden, then at that point there is no harm in asking, so that if it is an obligation you may seek to make amends, and if it is a prohibition in the sense of forbiddenness, you may also seek to make amends.

Glory be to Allah! I believe that it is not part of perfect servitude that when you are commanded, you say: "Is it binding or not binding?" Now, and to Allah belongs the highest comparison: if your father said to you: "O so-and-so, go and buy such and such," would it be right for you to say: "Is it binding or not binding?"

* A student: No.

* The Shaykh: It would not be right. For this reason, the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, I do not know of any one of them who, when the Messenger commanded something, said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it an obligation or a recommendation?" I do not know of such a case. They sometimes sought clarification, and seeking clarification in a matter that is general is a right. When the pen was commanded by the Lord of the Throne, He said: "Write." It said: "What shall I write?" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319), and the wording is Abu Dawud's, from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]

* A student: May Allah bless you, O Shaykh. About the restriction to a number: we said that when something is mentioned with a number, it is necessarily restricted to that number, neither more nor less. Is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying "Seven will be shaded by Allah" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (660) and Muslim (1031 / 91) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] similar to this?

* The Shaykh: No. Were it not for the narrations of (...), this would be... Furthermore, the number in "Seven will be shaded by Allah" is a restriction of attributes, not a restriction of individuals.

* The student: An example other than the seven, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: "Three will not be spoken to by Allah, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2672) and Muslim (108 / 173) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. This was narrated with several attributes, more than three.

* A student: May Allah be good to you. You said: ﴿Their hands were chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. We said it is a statement of fact, not...

* The Shaykh: Not a supplication.

* The student: Yes. We gave the reason and said (...). So can this become a rule (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is the principle: whatever Allah has informed about is a report about Himself, and about its occurrence, unless evidence indicates otherwise. This may be evidence that Allah taught the servants to supplicate. As for Allah, the Exalted, asking Himself to do something, that is not permissible.

* A student: When the brother recited, he paused between the words of Allah: ﴿and they were cursed for what they said﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. He paused here, then said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. And in the Qur'an there is a sign that it is better to pause here. But what prevents me from continuing, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: First, according to the known rules, there is a sign of obligatory pause. Do you now deny its being a pause or not being a pause?

* The student: No, I was not certain. I said (...) paused. I want to know why he paused, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: Why he paused? Well done. He paused because the words that follow are not the words of the Jews.

Of course, I mean ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾, "their hands were chained." As for ﴿they were cursed for what they said﴾, it has a sign of obligatory pause written on it. The reason is that the first is a report about what belonged to the Jews, and the second is a report about the attributes of Allah, blessed and exalted is He. For this reason it is linked with "Rather" (bal).

* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. An additional question about the first question: that when a thing is mentioned with a number, it is restricted to that number. If we were in a debate and it were said: "This is not correct, by the evidence of the hadith of the seven and the hadith of the three," how would the answer be...?

* The Shaykh: The answer to this is that the evidences came with this, by addition. That is, were it not for the evidences, we would say: there is no one except these seven.

* A student: (...) the Messenger (ﷺ), and some who claim to be Muslims denied them, O Shaykh. This, O Shaykh, is great in the soul, and a person imagines it to be something enormous, O Shaykh, and I do not know, O Shaykh (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...) No, he is a Muslim, God willing, but denial is of two kinds: denial of rejection and denial of falsehood, which is disbelief; and denial of interpretation and explanation, which does not make one a disbeliever. Unless it is impossible in any way for that interpretation to be valid, in which case it might be.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure. And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do﴾ [al-Ma'idah 65-66].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We are still explaining the lessons drawn from the preceding verses, namely His saying: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. We reached in them His saying: ﴿and Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. Is that not so?

* Among the lessons of this verse: the affirmation that love (al-mahabbah) belongs to Allah, that Allah loves. It is a real love, which the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah affirmed on a known principle, namely the obligation to apply the texts to their apparent meaning in the matter of Allah's attributes, and that Allah loves.

Is He Himself loved?

The answer: yes, He is loved. Allah stated this in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, whoever of you reverts from his religion, Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54]. So Allah, exalted is He, is loved for His attributes of perfection, and for His acts of kindness and bounty. For this reason it has come in a report: "Love Allah for the blessings He nourishes you with." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3789) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] If someone among people does a kindness to a person, that person loves him for his kindness. How much more so the Creator who brought him into being, sustained him and prepared him. He is more deserving of being loved.

As to His loving, yes, that has come in the Noble Qur'an as well as in the Prophetic Sunnah. The love of Allah is sometimes attributed to an action, sometimes to a time, sometimes to a place, and sometimes to a doer. All of this has come: "The most beloved of lands to Allah are its mosques" [[Narrated by Muslim (671 / 288) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "The most beloved of lands to Allah are its mosques."]]; "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (969) and Abu Dawud (2438) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, and the wording is Abu Dawud's.]], meaning the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah; "The most beloved of deeds to Allah is prayer at its time" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (527) and Muslim (85 / 137) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.]]; ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 222]. The verses on this are many and varied.

Is the love of Allah His reward, or the desire for His reward, or is it an attribute additional to that?

Answer: Third, in contrast to those who explain love (maḥabbah) as reward (thawāb) or as the will to reward, among those who deny that love subsists in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. There is no doubt that these are misguided, because even if we say it is reward, love is necessarily implied by reward, since Allah does not reward anyone except one whom He loves. Even if we explain it as the will to reward, love is still necessarily implied, since Allah does not will to reward anyone except one whom He loves.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of corruption on earth (fasād fī al-arḍ), based on His saying: ﴿Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. Likewise, everything of which Allah has negated His love is forbidden. So corruption on earth is forbidden. But what does corruption on earth consist of? Is it the demolition of houses, the destruction of rivers, and the like?
Answer: No. Corruption on earth is disobedience (maʿāṣī). This is what corruption on earth is, and the evidence for it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rūm 41]. However, demolishing houses without right is among acts of disobedience, so it is part of corruption on earth from this aspect. Accordingly, we say: everyone who disobeys Allah has taken up a pickaxe with which he ruins the earth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when something is established for an attribute, its opposite is established for the opposite of that attribute. Accordingly, we say: if Allah does not love the corrupters, then He loves the reformers (muṣliḥūn). There is no doubt that Allah loves the reformers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And reconciliation is best﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 128], and He said concerning orphans: ﴿Say: Reforming them is best﴾ [al-Baqarah 220]. So reconciliation is good, which Allah the Mighty and Majestic loves, encourages, and urges His servants toward. Reform is likewise good.
Reform has many kinds. In relation to the earth, people fall into three categories: the righteous (ṣāliḥ); the righteous reformer (ṣāliḥ muṣliḥ); and the corrupt corrupter (fāsid mufsid). If you wish, you may add a fourth: the corrupt non-corrupter (fāsid ghayr mufsid), to complete the divisions. But corruption necessarily entails being a corrupter, so we limit ourselves to three categories and say: people in relation to the earth are of three kinds:
The first is one who is righteous but benefits only himself. This is found among many worshippers. Many worshippers are righteous in themselves, but they do not try to reform others. They see wrongdoing before their eyes and do not forbid it, they see neglect of what is good before their eyes and do not command it, and so on. We say that such a person is righteous, although his righteousness is deficient, because perfection of righteousness is to command what is good and forbid what is evil.
The second is the righteous reformer. This is the best of the categories: he is righteous for himself and a reformer for others. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reformers﴾ [Hūd 117]. He did not say "righteous," so there must be a reformer on earth.
The third is the corrupt, and the corrupt is a corrupter on earth. Even if it is supposed that he does not call to his corruption and disobedience, he is still a corrupter, because he is a cause of the corruption of the earth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an descended from Allah. This is shown by His saying: ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. When this is established, two great matters follow. The first: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, because the Qur'an is not a self-subsisting entity, but an attribute that subsists only in a qualified thing (or in one characterized by it). Accordingly, this gives the great benefit that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. This is what the predecessors of the Ummah and its imams agreed upon, and trials (miḥan) befell Imam Aḥmad and other scholars of the Sunnah over it. Some people said: the Qur'an is not the speech of Allah, but is a created thing among the created things. There is no doubt that this statement necessarily entails the complete nullification of the Sharia. For if we say it is not the speech of Allah, then when it is written it would be merely markings and ornamentation which Allah created in this form, and when it is heard it would be mere sounds that signify nothing, just as the thunder, the blowing of winds, and other sounds are heard. Therefore we say: holding that the Qur'an is created necessarily entails the complete nullification of the Sharia, the nullification of command and prohibition, because there would be no command or prohibition. Take something created in this form and this shape only: it indicates no command. ﴿Do not approach fornication﴾ [al-Isrāʾ 32] likewise: it would be something created in these letters, like an engraving on a door, for example. If it is heard, it is only a sound, mere sound, just as we now hear the sounds of thunder and the whistling of winds in trees and so on. Then there is no command, no prohibition, and no report. This is very clear, but whoever Allah has blinded in heart does not realize that this is a necessary consequence.
* Also, the second benefit of His saying: ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾: the second benefit is the exaltedness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. For if the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and it is one of His attributes, and it descends, then the one characterized by it must be exalted; otherwise there would be no meaning to descent. So this is evidence for affirming the exaltedness (ʿuluww) of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.
People regarding this attribute are of three categories:
One category affirmed the exaltedness of Allah in truth.
Another category said: it is not permissible to describe Allah as exalted or as low, and it is not permissible to say that He is above, below, to the right, or to the left. This is pure negation (taʿṭīl). If someone were told, "Describe nonexistence," he could not describe it more precisely than the description with which they described the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.
The third category said: Allah the Exalted is everywhere, and it is not permissible to say that He is in the heights. How could it be permissible to say that He is in the heights, when He says: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 4], and says: ﴿And He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 108], and similar verses of togetherness (maʿiyyah)? So it is never permissible to say that Allah is exalted in His essence. Rather, the exaltedness affirmed for Allah is exaltedness of meaning (ʿuluww al-maʿnā), and as for place, He is in every place. These are the Ḥulūliyyah of the Jahmiyyah, who say that He is in every place. What is astonishing is that many people hold this view, those whom we contact at the Masjid al-Ḥarām and who ask us, non-Saudis; the Saudis, praise be to Allah, do not know this view, and most of the common people do not know this view. They say: "What our scholars establish for us is that Allah is in every place." There is no doubt that this statement, when a person reflects upon it, is found to be utterly false, because it contradicts the Qur'an, the Sunnah, reason, natural disposition (fiṭrah), and consensus. Can anyone accept placing the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, in latrines and filthy places? It is impossible, and the necessary consequence of their statement is exactly that: in every place, in every place.
As for the first statement, upon which we ask Allah to cause us to die and to raise us, it is that Allah the Exalted, in His essence, is above everything, yet He encompasses creation, so it is as though He is with them in their places. There is no objection to saying: He is above everything and He is with us, but not in our place. For this there are examples which Shaykh al-Islām, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned, one in al-Wāsitiyyah and one in al-Ḥamawiyyah. He said: the Arabs say, "We kept traveling and the star was with us." In al-Wāsitiyyah: "We kept traveling and the moon was with us." This is a clear Arabic expression, and whoever addresses or speaks in this way cannot believe that the moon is on the earth or that the star is on the earth. If this is a created thing which encompasses us, is with us, and is above us, then what of the Creator, about whom the Prophet ﷺ spoke, "that the seven heavens and the seven earths, in comparison with the Kursi, are like a ring cast into a desert, and the virtue of the Throne over the Kursi is like the virtue of the desert over this ring"[[Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (361) from the hadith of Abū Dharr.]]? So what of the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.
In any case, we believe that Allah, glorified and exalted, is truly above everything. As for His attributes, none of the Muslims, as far as we know, denies the exaltedness of the attributes; they all say He is perfect in His attributes. But the question remains: do they all affirm everything that has been transmitted of the attributes?
No, but whoever affirms for Him an attribute of perfection says that He knows with that perfect attribute.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the care of Allah, glorified and exalted, for the Messenger ﷺ. This is due to His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, for this particular lordship requires complete, stronger, and more intense care.
Know that lordship is of two kinds: general and specific. Both are combined in His saying about the magicians: ﴿They said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds (121) the Lord of Moses and Aaron﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 121-122]. The general: ﴿the Lord of the worlds﴾. Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, may Allah have mercy on him, said: everything other than Allah is a world (ʿālam), so ﴿the Lord of the worlds﴾ means the Lord of all creation.
﴿the Lord of Moses and Aaron﴾: what is this?
* The students: It is specific.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is specific. Likewise, servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) is general and specific:
General servitude (ʿubūdiyyah kawniyyah) is universal, and among its evidences is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. Everyone in the heavens, by general servitude, is a servant of Allah. Can anyone prevent illness if Allah decrees it upon him? Never. Can anyone turn back the Angel of Death when he comes to take his soul? Never. For this reason Allah challenged them, saying: ﴿Then why, when it reaches the throat (83), while you are at that time looking on (84), and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see (85), then why, if you are not to be recompensed (86), do you not return it, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah 83-87]. It is not possible: even if all creation gathered, they could not return that soul which has reached the throat. Therefore all are servants of Allah in this sense, that is, by general servitude.
As for the second category, specific servitude, it is the legal servitude (ʿubūdiyyah sharʿiyyah), among which is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Furqān 63].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah the Exalted cast enmity and hatred among the Jews; this is due to His saying: ﴿We have cast among them enmity and hatred﴾ [al-Māʾidah 64]. This is a true and sincere statement about which we have no doubt. What we suppose of their unity is contrary to reality. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You think them united, but their hearts are divided﴾ [al-Ḥashr 14]. Do not suppose that they are ever in agreement, and for this reason they are now many divided groups, and even within each group they are divided, because they cannot unite when Allah has cast enmity and hatred among them. But note that when two enemies have a third enemy, they unite against the third enemy. So their present union, the Jews, is not because they are loving and harmonious at all, and we cannot believe it, since Allah says: ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Rather, they have united for one goal and one interest against one enemy common to all. This union is undoubtedly merely outward, intended for something else and not intended for its own sake.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the enmity and hatred among the Jews will continue, but if they believe, will it cease or not? It will cease without doubt. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said to the Anṣār: "You were enemies, and Allah united you through me, and you were scattered, and Allah gathered you through me"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (4330) and Muslim (1061/139) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim.]], and the Anṣār, as you know, had enmities and hatred among them in the Jāhiliyyah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, the day on which people stand before the Lord of the worlds. It is so called for three reasons. The first: people rise on that day from their graves before the Lord of the worlds. The second: justice is established on it, as He the Exalted said: ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in the least﴾ [Yā-Sīn 54], and He said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ 47]. The third: witnesses are brought forth on it; the messengers are called as witnesses, then the nations, then the skins and limbs, and the matter becomes clear and revealed, and what is in the breasts is made manifest. For this reason it is called the Day of Resurrection.
There is a lesser resurrection which is not intended in this verse, namely a person's death, for everyone who dies has had his resurrection, since he has finished with this world and entered the world of the Hereafter.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the complete glad tidings for the Muslims that the Jews will never have a standing in wars, because whenever they kindle a fire of war, Allah extinguishes it, and they do not attain their aim by it. Although they may attain some measure, they will never attain the objective they seek by kindling the fire of war.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts (afʿāl ikhtiyāriyyah), the Mighty and Majestic; this is due to His saying: ﴿He extinguishes it﴾ (aṭfaʾahā). And when is "He extinguishes it"?
* The students: After its kindling.
* The Shaykh: After its kindling. This is a renewing act, and in it is a clear refutation of those who deny that voluntary acts subsist in Allah, and who say that Allah cannot come, cannot istawā upon the Throne, cannot speak by His will and choice, but that His speech is a meaning subsisting in His essence unconnected to His will, and that He does not laugh, rejoice, or become angry, and so on. Every attribute that renews, according to them, is nullified and negated from Allah. Their argument is extremely feeble and refuted before Allah. They say: voluntary acts which renew do not subsist except in something originated (ḥādith). Based on a principle which in reality is not established: they say, "Something originated can only occur through something originated." From where do they get this? Originated things occur through originated and eternal causes. Our acts are originated and subsist in something originated, but the originated acts of the Creator, Majestic is He, are originated yet subsist in something eternal, not originated.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the love of the Jews for corruption on earth and their striving in it with intense effort; this is due to His saying: ﴿and they strive in the earth for corruption﴾. Whoever observes the present reality knows that the verse applies perfectly to the Jews of the present time: they strive in the earth for corruption with everything they can, whether by themselves or through their servants who are servants to them. For this reason we say: the Jews now are both worshippers and worshipped, indeed they are servants and those who make others servants, because they subjugate the great powers to do what serves their interests. They are also tails (adhnāb) to the great powers, because the great powers are safe from them and want to cast them into some place so that they may corrupt the earth. So they strive in the earth for corruption at all times. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to humiliate and frustrate them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 65:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss.﴾ By "the People of the Book" are meant the Jews and the Christians, and the Book referred to is the Torah and the Gospel, based on His saying: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

His saying: ﴿had believed﴾ refers to belief in the heart, and ﴿feared Allah﴾ refers to deeds. This is when the two are combined: belief is in the heart and piety is by the limbs; belief is secret and piety is open. When either one is mentioned alone, the other is included in it implicitly.

﴿Had believed﴾ means: in what must be believed in, and among it is belief in Muhammad (ﷺ), because he is written about in their Torah and Gospel and known by his attributes: ﴿They recognize him as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah 146] and [al-An'am 20]. Does anyone fail to recognize his own son? No. The comparison is made with sons because a person's attachment to a son is stronger than his attachment to a daughter, so his knowledge of a son is more complete than his knowledge of a daughter. Also, the son goes with him in his trade, in his farming, in everything, so he knows his outward and inward affairs, whereas the daughter's place is the house, and no one fully knows her except her mother. So they recognize the Messenger as they recognize their sons, yet they did not believe in him. Is their belief then absent or present? It is absent, because they did not believe. Even if they say they believe in Moses, if they are Jews, or in Jesus, if they are Christians, they are liars.

As for ﴿feared Allah﴾, the meaning of taqwa is: avoiding what Allah has forbidden and carrying out what He has commanded. This applies to the outward, the limbs: sayings and actions. Taqwa is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by doing His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and affirming His reports. This is taqwa.

﴿We would have removed﴾ is the answer to (law, "if"): ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds﴾.

Know that the lam (of emphasis) often falls in the answer of (law), and it may be omitted. This is combined in the end of Surat al-Waqi'ah, where Allah the Exalted says about the crop: ﴿If We willed, We would have made it crumbled debris﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 65], and says about the water: ﴿If We willed, We would have made it salty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 70]. He included the lam in the first and did not include it in the second. As for when its answer is with the negative (ma), the lam is rarely attached to it. As for what is well known among the jurists and many people, namely attaching the lam to (ma), this is a dialect, but it is rare. The more eloquent form is to say: law kana kadha ma hasala kadha ("if it had been so, such would not have happened"). However, there is no harm in saying: lama hasala kadha ("such would have happened"). So affirmation and negation with (ma) are counterparts: the more common in affirmation is what?

* A student: Without lam.

* The Shaykh: No, the more common is with the lam, and the more common in negation with (ma) is omitting the lam. From it is the poet's saying with the lam in affirmation:

"And if we were given the choice, we would not have parted, / But there is no choice with the nights."

The evidence is his saying: "lama iftaraqna" ("we would not have parted"), and "wa lakin la khiyara ma'a al-layali."

His saying: ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds﴾, i.e., their sins, meaning their disobediences, whether by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, because belief and taqwa expiate misdeeds.

﴿And We would have admitted them to Gardens of Bliss﴾ this is the reward of the Hereafter. Thus what they dislike is removed through the expiation of misdeeds, and what they love is attained through admission into the Gardens of Bliss.

His saying: ﴿Gardens of Bliss﴾: "Gardens" is the plural of jannah, and it is pluralized because they are of various kinds. How many kinds did Allah mention in Surat al-Rahman?

* The students: Four.

* The Shaykh: Four kinds. The word jannah originally means an orchard whose trees are so numerous that they cover its ground, because the root of this word (j-n-n) means concealment and hiddenness, and from it the jinn are named jinn.

An orchard with many trees is a jannah. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And present to them the parable of two men, for one of them We had made two gardens of grapevines﴾ [al-Kahf 32]. But one should not say this to the common people, for if you said that the original meaning of jannah is an orchard with many trees, the greatness of Paradise would diminish in their souls. Rather, we explain the jannah mentioned in the Qur'an as the abode that Allah has prepared for His allies, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. This keeps its awe in souls and the strength of desire for it.

His saying: ﴿Bliss﴾: what kind of bliss is it? Is it bliss of the body, bliss of the heart, or both?

* The students: Both together.
