* The Shaykh: Yes, both: bliss of the body, where a person enjoys all kinds of blessings; and bliss of the heart, where no worry, no grief, and no sorrow can reach him, but rather they are always in delight. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and will give them radiance and happiness﴾ [al-Insan 11]. Radiance is in the face, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾ [al-Qiyamah 22], and happiness is in the heart. So what about a bliss in which there is radiance that delights the beholder in the face, and happiness in the heart with no sorrow, worry, or grief? O Allah, make us among those who enter the Gardens of Bliss.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Sometimes a person finds himself, even if he is righteous in himself, not finding in himself the strength and ability to reform others; he feels awe and dread. How does this quality go away?

* The Shaykh: Praise be to Allah. This goes away when you read the saying of Allah: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 16], and you know that you have done what you are able to do. When you do what you are able to do, it is as if you have done the whole perfection, because you are complying with the command of Allah, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. But what enters upon a person in this matter is sometimes rationalization (ta'wil): he says to himself, for example: "This is not the occasion for reminding or commanding or forbidding; perhaps I will speak in another place," or the like. This is ijtihad, and the person is rewarded for it, either two rewards or one. But for a person to burden himself and to want people to be reformed at his hands is impossible. Indeed Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you and your chest would be constricted by it, because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him or an angel not come with him?"﴾ [Hud 12], and He said: ﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself with grief that they do not believe﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 3], and He said: ﴿So perhaps you will consume yourself in grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf 6].

* The student: Shaykh, what if this is a constant state?

* The Shaykh: He should try to treat it. He should not be a coward, nor should he be a burden on people either. The person who constantly asks Allah for success, wisdom, and rectitude will be made easy for it.

* A student: May Allah preserve you, Shaykh. Some scholars divide the highness of Allah, glory be to Him, into highness of essence, of rank, and of subjugation. Under which of these divisions does the highness of attributes fall?

* The Shaykh: The attributes include rank and subjugation. If we say: highness of essence and highness of attributes, this includes rank and subjugation.

* The student: How does highness of subjugation fall under it?

* The Shaykh: Subjugation, because Allah said in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion﴾ [al-Tawbah 33], and He said: ﴿And do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 139]. This is the highness of subjugation.

* A student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: al-Baghd is masculine and al-Baghda' is feminine, and the meaning is one.

* A student: We said: it is necessary that one who is corrupt in himself be a corrupter. But, Shaykh, we find that some truly corrupt people corrupt thousands of people, so they cannot be compared with one who is corrupt in himself or disobedient.

* The Shaykh: Known, there is no doubt, they cannot be compared. Even corruption differs: whoever calls to an innovation, or calls to indecency, or otherwise, differs. But if we say that corruption in the earth is by sins, then every disobedient person has a share in this.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. Is the saying about accompaniment (ma'iyyah) like the saying about nearness (qurb) and the like, that it is a true attribute of Allah befitting His majesty?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, stated this in al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah, and He is truly with us, and truly above His Throne.

* The student: The difficulty, may Allah preserve you, is this: this is what we believe, but is there a difficulty raised by what Shaykh al-Islam himself mentioned about giving the example of the moon and the star? This seems to say that this is an Arabic style and is not interpretation; rather it is what is understood from the context, as we said: ﴿It runs before Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar 14] and the like. So how...?

* The Shaykh: This is correct, and for this reason people make a distinction even in ordinary speech. It is said of a man: "his wife is with him," and it is said: "his goods are with him," and it is said: "his dirhams are with him," and it is said: "his watch and his ring are with him." He makes a distinction, does he not?

* The student: Yes, then the two have the same meaning.

* The Shaykh: The meaning is one. Nearness and accompaniment have the same meaning. But as for this nearness, the contemporary scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, or the scholars of later generations, differed: does it divide, like accompaniment, into general and specific, or not? The apparent view is that it does not divide: nearness is specific to the worshipper and the supplicant only, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 186]. This is with respect to the supplicant.

With respect to the worshipper, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating"[[Narrated by Muslim (482/215) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And we cannot say that Allah is near to the disbelievers, for example, because nearness is honor and elevation; but we say that Allah is with the disbelievers, as Allah said: ﴿And He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 108]. What appears to me is that accompaniment divides into two kinds: general and specific, while nearness is specific only and is not general.

* A student: Some people describe certain beautiful lands as "the Paradise of Allah on earth." Is such an expression correct?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, it is acceptable, but if it is understood from it that it is a piece of the Paradise of eternity, then it is not permissible. Everything on earth belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Nevertheless, among the common people one should not use this expression, as they may understand from it a meaning that is not correct.

* A student: (...) ﴿made by Our hands﴾ [Ya-Sin 71] and ﴿running before Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar 14] (...) in refuting the doubt of these people, this verse differs from that verse, although the apparent refutation is one...

* The Shaykh: The difficulty in this is not the difficulty in that.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, the difficulty differs.

* * *
* A student: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss. And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do.﴾
* The Shaykh: Well done.

I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed﴾ to the end.

* It is derived from this: the perfect justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that whoever believes and fears Allah, even after disbelief and obstinacy, Allah the Exalted accepts his repentance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that one who repents from a sin is rewarded with two rewards: the reward of this world and the reward of the Hereafter. The reward of the Hereafter is in His saying: ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss﴾, and the reward of this world is in His saying: ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary actions, the saying: ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds﴾; for when does this expiation occur? After their belief and their taqwa. So it is evidence for affirming Allah's voluntary actions, and this is what the righteous predecessors (salaf) and the imams of Ahl al-Sunnah hold: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does what He wills at any time and in any manner.

As for the one who says that voluntary actions cannot be attributed to Allah because they are originated, and what is originated cannot subsist except in something originated, his statement is rejected. First, it is a false analogy because it contradicts the text. Second, it is an invalid analogy: who said that the subsistence of events in their subject necessarily makes it originated?!

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the recompense is the deliverance from what is feared and the attainment of what is desired. The first is indicated by His saying: ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds﴾, and the second by His saying: ﴿and We would have admitted them to Gardens of Bliss﴾; so the first brings deliverance from what is feared, and the second brings the attainment of what is desired.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Gardens contain absolute bliss that includes bliss of the body and bliss of the spirit. This is shown by His saying: ﴿and will give them radiance and happiness﴾ [al-Insan 11]; the scholars said: radiance is in the face, and happiness is in the heart.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾. This is a matter above faith and piety, namely upholding the Torah and the Gospel, and that is by affirming their reports, carrying out their commands, and avoiding their prohibitions.

The Torah is the Book revealed to Musa (Moses), and the Gospel is the Book revealed to 'Isa (Jesus). ﴿If they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾, and this includes both categories of the People of the Book, meaning the Jews and the Christians; each of them is obligated to uphold the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿And what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾ is the Noble Qur'an. His saying ﴿what was revealed to them﴾ indicates that these people are obligated to believe in the Qur'an and uphold it, and it indicates that His saying ﴿what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾ is the Qur'an, as shown by His saying: ﴿And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel, before, as guidance for mankind, and He revealed the Criterion﴾ [Al 'Imran 3, 4]. As for the statement of some scholars that ﴿what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾ includes even the earlier Books, there is room for scrutiny in this, because the earlier Books were revealed to those before them, yet they are obligated to believe in them.

﴿And what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them﴾. This is the answer of the conditional clause, the answer to (law, "if"). It has already been discussed that the conditional (law) is specific to verbs, and that the grammarians, in cases like ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah﴾, supposed a verb, namely: "if it had been established that they upheld the Torah," or "if it had come about that they upheld the Torah."

His saying ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ includes several things:

Firstly: ﴿they would have eaten from above them﴾, and that is by the descent of rains which are a cause of the vegetation they eat, and rain descends from the sky. ﴿And from beneath their feet﴾ means the plants of the earth. So Allah, Exalted, has mentioned both the cause of vegetation and the vegetation itself. This is like His saying: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been godfearing, We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾ [Al A'raf 96]. This is one aspect, and it is included in the verse.

It has been said: the meaning is: ﴿they would have eaten from above them﴾ from the fruits of trees, because trees are tall, so they eat from their fruits above. ﴿From beneath their feet﴾ means from crops and the like that grow on the ground and have no stalk, so Allah has made clear that blessing would be bestowed upon them in trees and crops.

It has been said: the meaning is: they would have eaten from every direction; as you say: "This man is in blessing from his head to his thumb," meaning that the blessing envelops him.

In any case, the verse includes this and that; all these aspects are valid interpretations of the verse. We have previously stated an important rule on this matter: when a verse carries two or more meanings equally, with no contradiction between them, it is to be understood as both of them together, and likewise with hadiths.

﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do﴾. Allah divided them into two divisions. ﴿Ummah﴾ here means a group (ta'ifah). In the Arabic language, ummah has several meanings that occur in the Qur'an: it means a group, as in this verse; it means a religion, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾ [al-Mu'minun 52]; it means a period of time, as in His saying: ﴿And he remembered after a period (ummah)﴾ [Yusuf 45]; and it means a leader (imam), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Nahl 120]. Among what came with the meaning of religion is His saying about the polytheists: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (ummah)﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], i.e., upon a creed (millah). This is clearer than our illustration with His saying: ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾ [al-Mu'minun 52], since that could carry the meaning "ummah: a group of people."

In any case, ummah occurs in the Qur'an with four meanings: the first is a group, the second is religion, the third is time, and the fourth is a leader.

He says: ﴿Among them is a community﴾, i.e., a group, ﴿moderate﴾, i.e., upholding the obligation without exceeding or falling short.

﴿But many of them—evil is what they do﴾, i.e., many of them are evildoers, not moderate, but rather excessive and negligent. For this reason He described the deed referred to with His saying ﴿evil is what they do﴾; so the phrase ﴿evil is what they do﴾ shows that the meaning is: many of them are not moderate, but rather wrongdoers in their deeds, so evil is what they used to do. Accordingly, ﴿evil is what they do﴾ is not the predicate of ﴿many﴾; rather its predicate is omitted, i.e., many of them are evil in deed and did not act moderately, and evil is what they do.

There remains a third division which Allah has singled out for this Ummah, namely those who race to good deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We chose from Our servants﴾ [Fatir 32], meaning this Ummah—may Allah make us and you among them—﴿of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one who is foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission﴾ [Fatir 32]. It is as though the foremost in good deeds among the Children of Israel were so few that they are given no weight and are not mentioned in the division; otherwise there is no doubt that among them there were those foremost in good deeds—some of them reached Islam and embraced it, and these are foremost in good deeds. But since the foremost in good deeds were few among the Children of Israel, we find no mention of them, because mention is made only of those who have standing in the division. ﴿And many of them—evil is what they do﴾.

* In this verse there are benefits. Among them: establishing the Shari'ah in every age is a cause of every good, by His saying: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾ to the end.

* Among them: whoever establishes the Shari'ah is rewarded with two things: a reward in this world and a reward in the Hereafter.

* Among them: it is permissible to encourage human souls to perform acts of obedience by mentioning the reward of this world. Pay attention to this point. On this basis, if a person does a righteous deed desiring to attain the good of this world and the Hereafter, he is not blamed; for if there were blame, Allah would not have mentioned the reward of this world, since its mention would then be like idle talk.

Likewise, conversely, for the prohibitions—meaning the forbidden things—you find that Allah has placed deterrents that restrain a person from them; so you find a man may refrain from fornication, for example, out of fear of punishment, and were it not for this, punishment would have no benefit.

So in any case we say: if a person has in his heart a desire for worldly gain but not as the motive for the act, there is no fault upon him. Does not a person recite the litanies (awrad)? Why? To be protected by them from the evils of men and jinn. You find that one who recites a litany may forget that he wants to draw near to Allah through recitation, and instead wants protection. Why? Because human souls are weak and need a material incentive to help them do good deeds. This principle is supported by the fact that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in some campaigns made the spoils of a slain man go to whoever killed him, as encouragement for him [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3142) and Muslim (1751/41) from the hadith of Abu Qatadah.]]. So the saying of some people, that it is not permissible for a person to desire some worldly thing by an act of the Hereafter, is incorrect. Rather Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾ [al-Shura 20], meaning We give him in this world and the Hereafter.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon the People of the Book to uphold the Qur'an as they are obligated to uphold the Torah and the Gospel, by His saying: ﴿and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾. This is indeed so; therefore we say to the People of the Book who claim that they believe in Allah and the Last Day: if you do not believe in the Messenger ﷺ, that faith will not benefit you, because you have not completed your faith.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, by His saying: ﴿and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾. The reasoning is that the Qur'an is an attribute, since it is speech, and speech necessarily requires a speaker, just as an attribute necessarily requires a subject to which it belongs. Since the Qur'an necessarily requires one who speaks it, who is it that spoke it? It is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's elevation, by His saying: ﴿and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾; for if the Qur'an is an attribute of Allah descended from Him, it necessarily follows that Allah is high. This, praise be to Allah, for one whose insight Allah has illuminated, who has not been encircled by the devils, and who remains upon the fitrah upon which Allah created him, is a matter that needs no proof, since it is a matter of innate nature: it is the elevation of Allah in His Essence. We have often noted that those who deny the elevation of the Essence divide into two groups: one group said that Allah is in every place, in the heaven and the earth, and His very Essence is in every place. Another group said: it is not permissible to describe Him as above or below, or right or left, nor as separate from the world nor as joined to the world. The former went to excess in affirming an attribute among the attributes, namely co-presence (ma'iyyah), and the latter went to excess in what they claim as glorifying the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Thus we take from this that it is obligatory upon us to believe in the elevation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of proof against the People of the Book that they are obligated to believe in the Qur'an, by His saying: ﴿from their Lord﴾; for it follows from His being their Lord that they should carry out His command and adhere to His ruling, since He is Lord, and a lord necessarily has one who is lorded over, and He, glorified and exalted, is the Master, while the human being is a servant. So they must fulfil the requirement of this lordship by believing in what Allah revealed to Muhammad ﷺ.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the earth include what is high and what is low, by His saying: ﴿from above them and from beneath their feet﴾; this is something observed. Indeed, some of them are apparent and some are hidden: the minerals within the earth are hidden, while things apparent on the surface of the earth are apparent.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the division of the People of the Book into two groups: one group—what is it? Moderate, upholding the obligation, abstaining from what is forbidden, but without precedence in good deeds; and another group, evil and evildoers in their deeds, either by abandoning obligations or by committing prohibitions; by His saying: ﴿Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the explanation of a great virtue of this Ummah, namely that Allah divided this Ummah into three categories: among them one who wrongs himself, among them one who is moderate, and among them one who is foremost in good deeds. As for the People of the Book, they were divided only into two: the moderate, and the evildoer in deed: ﴿and many of them—evil is what they do﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 67 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. Pay attention to the address and to the description with which the address is directed: ﴿O Messenger﴾. We have mentioned many times that opening a speech with a call indicates the importance and concern given to it. His saying ﴿O Messenger﴾ describes him with messengership, indicating that this description requires that, even if he had not been commanded to convey, he would be a conveyer because he is a messenger.

﴿O Messenger﴾ means Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. On this view, the definite article (al) is for mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni). As for His saying ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil 15-16], the (al) is for reference to something previously mentioned (al-'ahd al-dhikri).

﴿O Messenger﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Convey what has been revealed to you﴾: ﴿Convey﴾ means make it reach (balligh), i.e., deliver it to those to whom you were sent. He, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to the jinn and mankind from the time he was raised until the Day of Resurrection. On this view, his conveying is either direct, as to those who saw him and heard from him, or through those who succeeded him in his community in knowledge and calling, and they are the scholars. The Messenger conveyed the clear message, peace be upon him.

﴿Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾: ﴿what﴾ is a relative pronoun, and a relative pronoun conveys generality, i.e., all that was revealed to him.

His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾ indicates that his being a servant of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, requires that he convey. Furthermore, there is also another matter in it: Allah's lordship over His Messenger, peace be upon him, is a special lordship.

﴿Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. What was revealed to him? The Quran, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may explain to the people what has been sent down to them﴾. The Messenger's conveying, peace be upon him, includes conveying the wording and conveying the meaning. For this reason, you find that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, explains some verses when they are general or obscure; he explains them by his words and explains them by his actions, peace be upon him.

﴿Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, and ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. This is a severe statement. ﴿If you do not﴾ means: if you do not convey all that has been revealed to you, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, even in what you have conveyed, if you concealed part of it, because it will not be conveying; for denying part of what was revealed is like denying all of it. Faith does not divide; you cannot believe in something and deny something else. For this reason He said: ﴿If you do not﴾, what do you do? You convey what was revealed, all of what was revealed, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, even in what you have conveyed you have not conveyed, because you must convey what? All that was revealed. For this reason the Messenger, peace be upon him, conveyed all that was revealed to him, even what contained blame directed at him, peace be upon him. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And you concealed within yourself what Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. This contains a great reproach. If this had been said to one of us, he would have flown into a rage. But the Messenger, peace be upon him, had to convey all that was revealed to him, even what contained blame for him. For this reason 'Aishah said: "If Muhammad had concealed anything of what Allah revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿And you concealed within yourself what Allah is to disclose...﴾"[1]

He says: ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, i.e., the message of your Lord. He attributed the message to Him, glorified is He, because He is the sender. The message may also be attributed to the Messenger, as one says: "This is the message of Muhammad," because he conveys it. So it is attributed to Allah in regard to Him being the sender, and to the Messenger in regard to him being the conveyer.

﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, and Allah will protect you from the people﴾. This means: if you were to conceal something out of fear of the people, do not fear; for Allah will protect you from the people, i.e., He will prevent the people from harming you in any way. This is what happened, praise be to Allah. Otherwise, how many were those who wanted to kill him, peace be upon him! When he first came to Madinah he was afraid. 'Aishah says: "One night the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not sleep; he stayed awake and said: 'O Allah, send us a servant of Your servants who will guard me'" or words to this effect. "No sooner had he finished his supplication than there was the sound of weapons. He said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Sa'd ibn Malik'" – i.e., Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas – "He said: 'What brought you?' He said: 'I feared for you, O Messenger of Allah, so I came to guard you.'"[2] Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent him, and he began to guard him. In some narrations, though not in the two Sahihs, it is related that Hudhayfah also came with him. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded them to disperse. [3] Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, committed Himself to protect him from the people. It is known that when Allah commits Himself to something like this, he is guarded more strictly than the guarding of the sons of Adam: ﴿and Allah will protect you from the people﴾.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾: this means that, if they were to gain power over you, none but a disbeliever would do so.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾: i.e., He does not set right their affair so that they reach what they want. On this view, His saying ﴿does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ means He does not direct them to what they want of killing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. It is also possible that the meaning is: He does not guide them with the guidance of religion, and ﴿does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ refers to those for whom Allah has decreed disbelief and dying upon it. Then this verse is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96-97].

In this verse there is a recitation variant in His saying ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾: ﴿then you have not conveyed His messages﴾. As for the reading in the singular, there is no difficulty in it. As for the reading in the plural, why is it plural when the message is one?

We say: this is in view of the laws brought by this message, for it came with deeds, statements and beliefs: deeds of the heart and deeds of the limbs, it came with doing and with abstaining. So each kind is considered a message, and the plural is therefore correct.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the messengership of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, from His saying ﴿O Messenger﴾.
* Among its benefits: a great virtue for the Messenger, peace be upon him; in that he was a messenger for whom? For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is a virtue. People today honor a messenger for the honor of the one who sent him, and if the one who sent him is of high standing in society, then being his messenger is a what? A nobility for him. Thus the Messenger, peace be upon him, being addressed by Allah with this description is a great virtue for him and a great nobility. If the description of servanthood is a nobility, then the description of messengership is greater, because messengership includes servanthood and more.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon the Messenger, peace be upon him, to convey all that was revealed to him. This has happened, and the community has testified to it, praise be to Allah. "In the greatest gathering in which the Messenger, peace be upon him, met his community, on the Day of 'Arafah, he said to them: 'Have I not conveyed?' They said: 'Yes.' Three times he said: 'Have I not conveyed?' and they said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Allah, bear witness, O Allah, bear witness.'"[4] The testimony of the first of this community extends to the rest of the community until the Day of Resurrection; so we testify by Allah that he conveyed the clear message, peace be upon him, and conveyed the message in full.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of the Rafidah (Rafidites), who say that a third of the Quran was not conveyed and was concealed. We say: the entire Quran has been conveyed, praise be to Allah, and nothing remains. The commentators, may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned this and said: this is a refutation of the Rafidah, because the Rafidah believe that what is in our hands of the Quran is not the Quran, and that Muhammad concealed part of it, may Allah protect us, or those after him concealed it too.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation that the Quran is the speech of Allah, from His saying ﴿what has been revealed to you﴾.
* And in it also: the affirmation of [Allah's] elevation (al-'uluw), which was mentioned shortly before.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah's care for the Messenger, peace be upon him, from His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾.
* Among its benefits: that the Prophet (ﷺ), and far be it from him, if he had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, would not have fulfilled the right of the message. From where is this taken? ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾.
* Among its benefits: the obligation upon the people of knowledge to convey the Sharia. The reason is that the scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and if they are the heirs of the prophets, it is obligatory for them to discharge the right of inheritance and convey what they know of the Sharia of Allah, as an obligation, either by speech or by action, either by writing or by gesture, by whatever means. It is obligatory upon them to convey what was revealed to the Messenger, peace be upon him. Therefore you must remember what I often tell you: the sunan (recommended practices) can be obligatory upon the student of knowledge, the sunan which are sunan but become obligatory upon the student of knowledge, because this is part of conveying the message. That is, if a person who is a student of knowledge, respected among the people, prays and leaves out, for example, raising the hands at the opening takbir, at bowing, at rising from bowing, and at standing up from the first tashahhud, or bows in a way that is not legislated, you would consider him sinful. This is because this action that neglects the sunnah will become a proof, a proof for whom? For the people: if this were legislated, so-and-so would not have left it. Likewise, actions that are disliked for others may be forbidden for him. Also, it is obligatory upon the student of knowledge to do what the people believe to be forbidden, so that they may know it is not forbidden. That is, some people say: any movement in prayer invalidates the prayer. We say: if there is a cause for the movement, i.e., the cause that permits it, then the scholar should do it so that he may make it clear to the people. But in this situation, if he fears that he will be followed, he should clarify by speech that he did it out of need, and that movement in prayer is not a problem if it is for a need, and similar things.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strong emphasis of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on conveying His Sharia. For this statement or sentence ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed﴾ is very severe, which shows that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not approve for His servants that their Sharia be left unconveyed.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that concealing part of the Sharia is like concealing all of it, from His saying ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. This is one of the benefits of the second reading ﴿then you have not conveyed His messages﴾, because someone might say: he conveyed the message in what he did convey. So when He says ﴿then you have not conveyed His messages﴾, it includes what he conveyed and what he did not convey. So this is one of the benefits of the second reading.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's care for the Messenger, peace be upon him, in protecting him from the people; in His saying ﴿and Allah will protect you from the people﴾.

Is this absolute, or restricted to what the conveying requires, i.e., He protects you from the people until you convey the message? If we look at the apparent meaning of the verse, we say it is absolute: ﴿He will protect you from the people﴾. If we look at the fact that a poisoned sheep was presented to the Prophet, peace be upon him, at the Battle of Khaybar, and he ate from it, and its effect on his palate was visible, and in his final illness he informed that the meal of Khaybar kept returning to him, and he said: "This is the time of the cutting of the abhar."[5] The abhar is a vein in the back connected to the heart; when it is cut, the person dies. This indicates that the Messenger, peace be upon him, died because of the poison that came from that Jewish woman, and it has been said that she embraced Islam. If that is so, the verse must be restricted: He will protect you from the people until when? Until you convey the message. Indeed he conveyed the message, and Allah sent down to His Messenger his announcement of death in His saying: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt your Lord with praise and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ [al-Nasr 1-3]. The hadith, meaning the hadith of the sheep, is in al-Bukhari,[6] and he mentioned it in mu'allaq form, with a firm assertion, and a mu'allaq hadith in al-Bukhari is sahih in his view, not in everyone's view. He mentioned it in mu'allaq form with the wording of firm assertion.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that hearts are in the hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that the actions of creatures follow the will of Allah. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿protect you﴾, because the protection of the Messenger from the people is divided into two parts: either by the absence of will, by Allah turning hearts away from killing him; or by incapacity, by the aggressor trying but being unable. This happened. Perhaps you remember the story of Banu al-Nadir: "When the Messenger, peace be upon him, came to them seeking their help, they plotted against him. They said: 'Sit until we come to you.' Then one of them set off with a millstone in order to drop it on the Messenger, peace be upon him, while he was sitting. Jibril informed him of this, so he stood up and entered Madinah."[7] Is this protection from will or from incapacity?

* Students: From incapacity.
* Shaykh: From incapacity, since they did intend it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the disbelievers, even if they plot against the friends of Allah, Allah, glorified and exalted, does not guide them. This is according to the interpretation of what? That the meaning of guidance is their being shown how to carry out what they want. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot, and I am plotting a plot﴾ [al-Tariq 15-16], meaning a plot greater than theirs. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30]. As for the second possibility, that He does not guide them with the guidance of the Sharia, it indicates that whoever Allah has decreed for disbelief, no one can guide him, because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
* Among the benefits of the verse: whoever Allah knows will be a disbeliever is not guided and not granted success. So this verse is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [al-Saff 5].

* A student: May Allah bless you. I did not understand the weakness of the view of those scholars who said that what is meant in ﴿and what was sent down to them from their Lord﴾ is the earlier books. What is the weakness in it?
* Shaykh: Yes. The weakness in it is that what we now know is that they were charged with the Torah and the Gospel. That is one point.

Another explanation: this verse follows the pattern of God's words: ﴿He has sent down the Torah and the Gospel (3), before this, as guidance for mankind, and has sent down the Criterion﴾ [Al 'Imran 3, 4].

* Student: Shaykh, is it not disbelief in one message while disbelieving in all of them...?
* Shaykh: Yes, but it refers to what was sent down to them. One should not say, for example, that the Book revealed to Noah was sent down to the Jews and Christians. Rather, they are obligated to believe in it, just as the Torah and the Gospel were not sent down to us, yet we are obligated to believe in them.
* Student: Shaykh, may God bless you. I did not understand the weakness of the view held by some scholars that what is meant by ﴿what has been sent down to them from their Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah 66] is the earlier scriptures. What is the weakness of it?
* Shaykh: Yes. The weakness is that we now know they were charged with the Torah and the Gospel. That is one point.

Another explanation: this verse follows the pattern of God's words: ﴿He has sent down the Torah and the Gospel (3), before this, as guidance for mankind, and has sent down the Criterion﴾ [Al 'Imran 3, 4].

* Student: But Shaykh, it is not disbelief in one message; it is disbelief in all of them.
* Shaykh: Yes, but it refers to what was sent down to them.
One should not say, for example, that the Book revealed to Noah was sent down to the Jews and Christians. But they are obligated to believe in it, just as the Torah and the Gospel were not sent down to us, yet we are obligated to believe in them.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is indeed one of them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people (51). So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us." But perhaps God will bring a conquest or a decision from Himself, and they will become regretful for what they had concealed within themselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51, 52].
* Shaykh: God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another.﴾ How could the Jews be allies of the Christians and the Christians allies of the Jews, when the Christians say, ﴿The Jews are not upon anything﴾ [al-Baqarah 113], and the Jews say, ﴿The Christians are not upon anything﴾?
* Student: This is when they unite against the Muslims.
* Shaykh: Yes. When they unite against the Muslims, some of them are allies of others. But when each one is considered individually, what are they?
* Student: Some of them are enemies of others.
* Shaykh: Indeed, some of them are enemies of others. Well done.
God's words: ﴿Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, although we know that God guided some wrongdoing people among the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists?
* Student: Meaning, whoever remains in wrongdoing, God does not guide him with the guidance of success and support.
* Shaykh: No, that is not the apparent meaning.
* Student: Those whom God knew would not believe.
* Shaykh: Yes, meaning those against whom God's word has been decreed, and God has decreed for them misguidance and destruction. So this general statement is intended as what? A specific one.

And also in it: a warning against wrongdoing. When a person does wrong, perhaps he will not be guided, God forbid, because God says: ﴿Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. It is like His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, and God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Saff 5].

* Shaykh: His words: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is disease﴾. What is meant by disease here?
* Student: Hypocrisy.
* Shaykh: Hypocrisy. What is your evidence that it means hypocrisy, since it is used for hypocrisy and for other things?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, we want it from the Qur'an.
* Student: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah 8]. ﴿In their hearts is disease﴾ [al-Baqarah 10].
* Shaykh: Because God said of the hypocrites: ﴿In their hearts is disease, so God increased their disease﴾. Good, well done.

Disease is also used for disbelief, as in His words: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice (124). But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in defilement upon their defilement﴾ [al-Tawbah 124, 125].

It is also used for immorality: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet﴾ [al-Ahzab 32]. So what is meant by disease here?

* Student: Hypocrisy.
* Shaykh: Hypocrisy, because they are the ones who hasten to befriend the Jews and Christians, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us."

His words: ﴿But perhaps God will bring a conquest or a decision from Himself﴾ [al-Ma'idah 52]. What is meant by conquest?

* Student: Victory.
* Shaykh: Victory. Well done. ﴿Or a decision from Himself﴾?
* Student: Their guidance.
* Shaykh: Their guidance. Correct, or they will be guided, and then God will bring about a matter that was not in your minds or your thoughts.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿And those who believed will say, "Are these the ones who swore by God with their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers (53). O you who have believed, whoever of you reverts from his religion - God will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of God, and not fearing the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Ma'idah 53, 54].
* Shaykh: God's words: ﴿Whoever of you reverts from his religion﴾. Is there another reading for it?
* Student: ﴿Yartadid﴾ (with the doubled letter separated).
* Shaykh: Yes, with the assimilation undone.
What is the answer to the conditional (man)?
* Student: ﴿Then God will bring a people...﴾.
* Shaykh: What does this answer, together with the condition, convey?
* Student: That the establishment of God's religion does not depend on these people. Rather, if they turn away, God will bring someone better than them, as in His words: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad 38].
* Shaykh: Yes, well done. In this verse there is a refutation of a specific group of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah). Who are they?
* Student: It refutes those who deny the voluntary actions of God, the af'al ikhtiyariyyah (voluntary acts of God), because of His words: ﴿Then God will bring a people﴾. It also refutes those who deny that God's bringing about is a consequence of His action, since He makes God's bringing a people a result of His act.
* Shaykh: This establishes the voluntary actions. What is the other attribute?
* Student: It establishes the attribute of love: God's love for His servants, and the servants' love for God.
* Shaykh: Who among the people of innovation denied this?
* Student: As for the Ghulat (extremists), they denied that God...
* Shaykh: They denied love.
* Student: That God loves or is loved. And the Ash'arites (an Islamic theological school) denied that God loves His servants, and interpreted it as reward, or as the will to reward.
* Shaykh: Good. What is their argument?
* Student: Their argument is that love is one of the originated attributes, and these voluntary actions are originated acts. If God were characterized by them, He would be originated, because whatever originated things inhere in is itself originated.
* Shaykh: Good. Their denial that God is loved: what is their argument?
* Student: This denial is the view of the Ghulat, that God is loved...
* Another student: Shaykh, love is between two equals.
* Shaykh: Between equals. There is no equality between the Creator and the created. In any case, this reasoning is not sound.

How did He say ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾, ﴿humble toward (ʿalā)﴾, and not say "humble to (li)"?

* Student: The prepositions alternate.
* Shaykh: That is an acceptable answer, but it is weak.
* Student: Even with their tenderness and compassion toward the believers, they are in a state of humility (...).
* Shaykh: But He said ﴿ʿalā﴾, ﴿humble toward ʿalā﴾. Does someone say that ʿalā implies height?
* Student: They are in a high position, as if they were above them because of their rank and nobility, and yet they humble themselves to them.
* Another student: Shaykh, it indicates that they are compassionate toward the believers.
* Shaykh: So it is as if it implies compassion: they are compassionate toward the believers.
* Student: The humility is constructed with ʿalā, which carries the sense of strength together with power. With li, it would be with weakness.
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: Humility accompanied by weakness is not perfection, but this is humility from power and dominance. So when a person humbles himself, it is a perfection for him.
* Shaykh: If they were strong against the believers, able to dominate them?
* Student: They are able to do so, but since they restrained themselves from it, it is a perfection for them.
* Shaykh: These are two points.
* Student: That this humility is not from weakness.
* Shaykh: This is close to the meaning of Muhammad's statement.

In any case, some have said, as the first brother said, that ﴿humble toward the believers﴾ implies the sense of compassion, meaning humble out of compassion for the believers.

Others have said: this indicates that the humility arises from height, not from weakness, because a humble person may be humble from weakness and not from loftiness. But this indicates that they are humble while being high and exalted.

In His words: ﴿And God is all-Encompassing﴾, all-Encompassing in what?

* Student: All-Encompassing in everything, all-Encompassing in giving...
* Shaykh: Meaning all His attributes are boundless and cannot be encompassed: in knowledge, power, life, hearing, sight, and so on.
* Student: Shaykh, it is said that wilaya (guardianship/allegiance) is of two kinds: God's guardianship over His servants, and the servants' guardianship over God. The second is by supporting His religion, and the first is by protecting them...
* Shaykh: So we say: ﴿Your only guardian is God and His Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah 55], meaning: what you should take as a guardian is only God, His Messenger, and those who believe, not the Jews and Christians.
Then He encouraged this, saying: ﴿And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - then indeed the party of God will be the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah 56]. Meaning: take God and His Messenger as guardians. ﴿And those who believed, then indeed the party of God, they are the victorious.﴾ So the difficulty is resolved: when we say ﴿Your only guardian is God﴾, the meaning is: what you should take as guardian is nothing but God, His Messenger, and the believers.

Well. The verse establishes ḥizbiyya (partisanship, forming a party). Is partisanship lawful?

* Student: Partisanship among Muslims is not lawful. But forming a party for the religion of God and supporting it is what must be followed.
* Shaykh: Well done. So partisanship among Muslims is not lawful; rather, it is a means of division. As for partisanship between the disbelievers and the Muslims, it is obligatory, because non-Muslims are the party of Satan, is that not so?
So God has made for Himself a party, and made for Satan a party, and this is necessary. But among Muslims it is forbidden, because it leads to division.

If someone says: ﴿Then indeed the party of God, they are the victorious﴾. This sentence contains restriction (ḥaṣr), because victory belongs to whom?

* Student: To the party of God.
* Shaykh: To the party of God, Mighty and Majestic.
If this objector raised his objection and said: we find that the Muslims have suffered defeats, and victory has gone to their enemies, even in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ)?

* Student: But ultimate victory belongs to the believers.
* Shaykh: So they are the victorious in the end? Considering the end, this is good: they are the victorious in the end.
* Student: God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those days We alternate among the people, that God may make evident those who believe, and take from among you martyrs﴾ [Al 'Imran 140]. This is evidence that sometimes there is conquest, sometimes victory, and sometimes...
* Shaykh: That is, a defeat must have a wisdom. The defeat of non-Muslims must have a wisdom. For example, at Uhud, what was its cause?
* Student: Disobedience.
* Shaykh: Disobedience and sin. At Hunayn, its cause was self-admiration. So God may give the disbelievers power over the Muslims for a wisdom: either because of the Muslims' shortcomings, or their excessive self-regard, or any other reason. But in the end, as Mahmud said, victory belongs to whom? To the party of God, who are the allies of God.

* Shaykh: In His words ﴿wal-kuffār﴾ (and the disbelievers), are there two readings?
* Student: ﴿al-kuffāra﴾ and ﴿al-kuffāri﴾.
* Shaykh: Their grammatical analysis (i'rab)?
* Student: If we say ﴿wal-kuffāra﴾, it is coordinated with the first ﴿alladhīna﴾. If we say ﴿al-kuffāri﴾, it is coordinated with the second ﴿alladhīna﴾. Well done, perfect.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ (68) ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous work—no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (69) ﴿We had taken the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group [of them] they denied and a group they killed.﴾ (70) ﴿And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness; then many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ (71) [Al-Ma'idah 68–71].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything﴾. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ. "People of the Scripture" are the Jews and the Christians. They claim that they are upon the truth and that they are the ones who uphold the laws of Allah. Yet some of them say to others: "You are not upon anything," as Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿The Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 113].

Each of them denied that the other was upon anything at all. As for Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, He is the Just Judge, so He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say to them: ﴿you are not upon anything﴾, meaning: you are not upon anything of the religion. He denied that they were upon anything of the religion, because the religion they hold is false until they uphold the Torah and the Gospel. So, you are not upon anything of the religion, because the religion they claim is true is false, and falsehood is nothingness and is not a thing.

﴿until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel﴾: "until" (ḥattā) here indicates a limit, meaning: until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel, i.e., you bring them established, acting upon their commands, abstaining from their prohibitions, and affirming their reports. This is the meaning of upholding them; it consists of three things:
First: carrying out the commands.
Second: abstaining from the prohibitions.
Third: affirming the reports. This is upholding them.
The Torah corresponds to the Jews and the Gospel corresponds to the Christians. It is known that if the Jews upheld the Torah, they would believe in Jesus, and that if the Jews and the Christians upheld the Torah and the Gospel, they would believe in Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾: meaning, and you uphold what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and by this is meant the Qur'an, because the Torah and the Gospel are also among what was revealed. If we say that what is meant by "what has been revealed to you from your Lord" is the Torah and the Gospel, there would be some repetition, and when speech is ambiguous between repetition and introducing something new, the obligation is to take it as introducing something new and distinct. So we say: ﴿and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means the Qur'an.

If someone asks: was the Qur'an revealed to the community of Muhammad?
We say: Yes, it was revealed to the community of Muhammad, and they are of the community of Muhammad, but they are of the community of the call (ummat al-da'wah), as the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this community hears of me, a Jew or a Christian, then dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."[[Recorded by Muslim (153 / 240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one from this community hears of me, a Jew or a Christian, then dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."]]

He said "from this community," referring to his nation, peace be upon him, and what is meant is the community of the call. So ﴿and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means the Qur'an. If an objector raises what we have mentioned, he is answered with what we have answered.

As for His saying ﴿and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, the phrase ﴿from your Lord﴾ indicates that it is obligatory for them to uphold it, it is obligatory for them to uphold it, because it was sent down from the Lord, and the Lord is the Creator, the Owner, the Governor. So if Allah is your Lord, it is binding upon you to uphold what has been revealed to you from Him, because He is your Lord, your master, your God ﴿and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾.

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿and it will surely increase﴾. If the Prophet ﷺ was commanded by Allah to say a statement, do we say that he said it? Answer me.
Students: Yes.
Shaykh: Yes, we say: he said it, without doubt; for if he had not said it, he would not have conveyed the message of his Lord. So he did say that to them, and he announced to them that they are not upon anything until they uphold the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an.

He said: ﴿and it will surely increase many of them in what has been revealed to you from your Lord, in transgression and disbelief﴾. Note the qualification: ﴿many of them﴾, meaning not all of them.
Rather, some of them the Qur'an increased in faith, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they recognize of the truth﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 83]. But many of them increase in transgression and disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Let us parse His saying ﴿and it will surely increase﴾: the lam here is the lam that falls in the answer to an oath, the implied oath, and the estimate is: "By Allah, it will surely increase," and the nun is for emphasis. Accordingly the sentence is emphasized with three emphatics: the implied oath, the lam, and the nun.
﴿and it will surely increase many of them in what has been revealed﴾: ﴿mā﴾ here is the subject of "yazīdanna" (it will increase).
﴿what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿in transgression and disbelief﴾. Why would it increase them in transgression and disbelief?
Because whenever they denied a verse or disobeyed a verse, they increased thereby in transgression and disbelief. This is similar to His saying the Exalted: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾ [At-Tawbah 124–125].

So whenever a verse was revealed, they increased in transgression and increased in disbelief; we ask Allah for well-being.

﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾. There is no doubt that the Messenger, peace be upon him, grieves and is saddened when people do not uphold the command of Allah, because he is a messenger who loves what Allah loves and dislikes what Allah dislikes. So he is grieved, to the point that Allah said to him: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 3].

That is, destroying yourself because they do not believe. Do not be concerned; discharge what is upon you, which is conveying the message, and the rest is with Allah: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah 25–26].

﴿So do not grieve﴾: i.e., do not be sad and grieved over the disbelieving people who rejected your message. This is undoubtedly a consolation to the Messenger, peace be upon him, for his being saddened when his message is not answered, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa ʿalā ālihi wa sallam.

* This verse contains many benefits, among them: the clarification that the Jews and Christians are not upon anything. On this basis, if they claim to be believers, we say to them: you have lied; you are not upon anything unless they uphold the Torah and the Gospel.
* Among the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory for a person to announce his disassociation from the people of shirk and to make clear that they are not upon anything, so that we do not follow them; as shown by His saying: ﴿O People of the Scripture﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: giving each possessor of a right his right, for He addressed them as "People of the Scripture" although in reality they are not worthy of the title, since the People of the Scripture are those who uphold it. Just as you say "O people of the Qur'an" meaning those who uphold it; when a description is given to its owner, it is justice.
* There is also a second benefit: because they are People of the Book, it is obligatory for them to uphold it.
* From the benefits of the noble verse: upholding the Torah and the Gospel is not complete except by upholding the Qur'an, because Allah stipulated three things: "until you uphold the Torah, and the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord."
So whoever claims that he upholds the Torah while disbelieving in the Gospel, we say: this is not correct, it is a false claim. And whoever claims to believe in the Gospel without believing in the Qur'an, we say: this is a false claim.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the nobility of the Qur'an for being sent down from Allah.
* Among its benefits: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. Its basis is that the Qur'an is not a self-subsisting entity, so that we might say it is created; rather it is an attribute that subsists in the one who speaks it, and if it is an attribute, it must be sent down uncreated.
As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾ [Az-Zumar 6], here we say: the pairs are created, because the pairs are self-subsisting entities.
Likewise His saying: ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾ [Al-Hadid 25]: iron too is a self-subsisting entity; it cannot be an attribute of Allah.
As for the Qur'an, it is speech, and speech must subsist in a speaker, so it is sent down uncreated, as the early scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirmation of Allah's exaltedness (uluww), because of His saying: ﴿and what was revealed﴾, and revelation (inzāl) is from above?
* Student: From on high.
* Shaykh: What did we say?
* Student: Revelation comes from on high.
* Shaykh: The benefit we deduced from that is...
* Student: Affirmation of Allah's exaltedness, mighty and majestic.
* Shaykh: Yes, affirmation of Allah's exaltedness, because Allah said: ﴿what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever acknowledges Lordship (rubūbiyyah) must acknowledge divinity (ulūhiyyah) and the Sharia, because of His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, meaning from your Lord whose lordship you do not deny; and since you do not deny His lordship, it is binding upon you to carry out His command.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the ascription of Allah's Lordship to the disbelievers. But this ascription is not an ascription of honor; it is an ascription establishing the proof against them. For example, if you say that Allah the Exalted is the Lord of Muhammad, peace be upon him, this is an ascription of honor; but with respect to the disbelievers it is an ascription to establish the proof against them.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that many of the People of the Book are increased by the Qur'an only in transgression and disbelief, either through denial or through disobedience.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: justice in the speech of Allah and avoidance of exaggeration, because of His saying: ﴿it will surely increase many of them﴾, and He did not say "all of them," because in reality some of them increase in faith through the Qur'an, as you heard in the explanation.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of emphasizing speech with what establishes its truth, even if it is true in essence, because of His saying: ﴿it will surely increase many of them﴾. Although the report of Allah, even without emphasis, is certainly true, what is the purpose of the emphasis here?
Its purpose is that it may seem strange that this Qur'an, which is guidance for mankind, would increase these people only in transgression and disbelief. Since this was a matter of astonishment, Allah, mighty and majestic, emphasized it. Note that the emphasis of speech, when it comes from one who is truthful, must have a cause; otherwise the emphasis would be vain.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the noble Qur'an may increase its hearer in transgression and disbelief, and it may increase him in faith and humility. His saying ﴿it will surely increase many of them﴾ implies that some of them are not increased by it in transgression and disbelief, but rather only in faith, like His saying the Exalted: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [At-Tawbah 124].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that disbelief increases and decreases. Disbelief increases and decreases. What is its basis?
* Students: ﴿and it will surely increase﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿and it will surely increase many of them in what has been revealed to you from your Lord, in transgression and disbelief﴾. On this basis, this serves as a supporting witness to what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "Disbelief is below disbelief" (kufr dūna kufr) [recorded by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3258)].
That is, if it increases and decreases, then the higher must be above the lower, so there is disbelief below disbelief.
Can we say: and in it is evidence that faith increases and decreases?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes, perhaps we can say this, because if disbelief increases and decreases, and faith is its opposite, then faith must likewise increase and decrease.
What the people of the Sunnah and the Community hold is that faith increases and decreases, whether through statements, or through actions, or through certainty. Pay attention to this benefit!
Faith increases through statements: whoever mentions Allah a thousand times is not like whoever mentions Allah a hundred times, for example. Which of them is greater?
* Students: The first.
* Shaykh: The first. Likewise with actions: whoever prays a hundred rak'ahs is not like whoever prays two hundred; the second is greater.
Likewise with certainty. People differ in certainty. A person himself is sometimes in a state of clarity and sometimes in a state of emptiness, and his heart is empty of everything but Allah, so he finds a great pleasure in faith and a great strength, to the point that it is as if he sees Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is why the Prophet, peace be upon him, said about excellence (iḥsān): "That you worship Allah as if you see Him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50), and Muslim (9 / 5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
What supports this is that certainty differs, increases, and decreases: Abraham, peace be upon him, said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but for my heart to be assured'﴾ [Al-Baqarah 260]. This was Abraham the Friend of Allah, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿for my heart to be assured﴾.
This is something witnessed: the report is not like direct observation. If a man whom you trust most told you something, and someone like him or more were with him, your certainty in that report is not like your certainty when you have witnessed it yourself. So faith increases and decreases.
Since it increases and decreases, it is incumbent upon us, brothers, to examine our faith: has it increased, or has it decreased? Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame none but himself.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the care of Allah, blessed and exalted, for Muhammad ﷺ, because of His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾. This lordship is for honor and exaltation, and it shows that he, peace be upon him, cannot add to what was revealed to him, nor diminish it, because it was sent down from his Lord who cared for him with the utmost care.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the consolation of the Prophet ﷺ that he should not grieve over the disbelieving people. Moreover, Allah the Exalted explained to him in another verse that what occurred from them happened by the will of Allah, so that he would be at peace, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated; and We did not make you a guardian over them﴾ [Al-An'am 107].
So if shirk occurred by the will of Allah, the Messenger will surely be content, but this does not prevent him from calling to Allah. He said: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾.
If someone asks: does this also apply to the one who calls to Allah? That is, if someone came to you complaining: "I advised these people, but they did not accept my advice; rather they were arrogant, mocked, and ridiculed," would you say to him: "My brother, do not grieve, do not be sad, do not let your chest be constricted"? Or not?

Yes, I say this so that I may relieve him and give him room, and that he not despair. Therefore, when one of the callers to good, or one of those who enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, comes to a person complaining to him, he should make room for him, give him space, and say: "Do not grieve over these people." But some people, when someone comes to them complaining, say: "By God, people are ruined! Who can deal with them except God?!" And we ask God for well-being, lest anger and retribution befall us. Then he adds grief upon grief, and this is a mistake, because the caller to God, once he has done what is incumbent upon him, whatever lies beyond that is up to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 69 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ means true belief, and it is not as some of them said, that it refers to the belief of hypocrisy (nifaq). This is because the hypocrite cannot be described as a believer (mu'min) as long as he remains in his hypocrisy. Pay attention to this!

The hypocrite cannot be described as a believer as long as he remains in his hypocrisy. But before he became a hypocrite, he could have believed and then disbelieved, as the Mighty and Majestic said about the hypocrites: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved﴾ [al-Munafiqun 3]. However, the hypocrite during his hypocrisy can be described with what? With Islam. He can be described with Islam, but not with faith (iman).

For this reason, the view of the one who said that what is meant by ﴿those who believed﴾ is that they believed with their tongues but not their hearts is weak. We say: this expression can never be used in this sense in the Qur'an.

What led them to this view is that He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿whoever of them believes in Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 126]. They said: how can we say ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ and ﴿whoever of them believes﴾? Would this not be repetition?

It would be repetition, but we can say that ﴿whoever believes﴾ is a shared term (ism mushtarak), so that it is taken in reference to ﴿those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabeans﴾ [al-Baqarah 62], meaning whoever entered into faith, and in reference to ﴿those who believed﴾, meaning whoever remained steadfast in his faith. This is because a person may believe and then disbelieve, and we ask Allah for well-being. This is one aspect.

The second aspect: we say that ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ is the particle ''inna'' (indeed) and its noun. Its predicate (khabar) is omitted, indicated by what follows it, and the sense is: Indeed, those who believed, there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. On this reading, His saying ﴿and those who were Jews﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), so the waw is for resumption (istikhnaf), or it is conjoined to the position (mahall) of ''inna'' and its noun. Have you understood? ﴿And those who﴾ — what is its grammatical status? It is a subject.

﴿Those who were Jews﴾ means the Jews. The meaning of ''hadu'' is "they returned", because they said: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf 156], meaning: we have returned to You and repented.

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians﴾. The Sabeans: the original meaning of "sabi'" is one who departs from the religion of his fathers and forefathers, that is, he leaves the religion of his people. So who are meant here?

It has been said that they are a sect of the Jews. On this view, their conjunction with ﴿those who were Jews﴾ is conjunction of the specific to the general (ʿatf al-khass ʿala al-ʿam).

It has been said that they are a sect of the Christians. On this view, the conjunction of the Christians to them is conjunction of the general to the specific (ʿatf al-ʿam ʿala al-khass).

It has been said—and this is the most apparent view—that they are an independent sect, because Allah mentioned them separately. The Sabeans follow a religion that differs from the religion of the Jews and the religion of the Christians. Perhaps they took some elements from this religion and from that religion and fashioned a religion of their own.

﴿And the Sabeans﴾: the Sabeans are conjoined to ﴿those who were Jews﴾. There is no difficulty in their grammatical case according to the reading we mentioned, namely that ﴿those who were Jews﴾ is a subject, so the Sabeans are conjoined to a subject and are therefore in the nominative.

But an objection arises: they are mentioned in another verse in the accusative form, ﴿al-Sabi'in﴾, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated partners [with Allah]—indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Hajj 17].

It is said that the difference is clear, because the last verse does not mention belief afterward. It only mentions the general categories of disbelievers and believers. Therefore ﴿al-Sabi'in﴾ is conjoined to ﴿those who believed﴾, which is the noun of ''inna'', and the predicate comes afterward.

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabi'in, and the Christians﴾ ﴿and those who associated partners [with Allah]—indeed, Allah will judge between them﴾. So He judges between the believers, the Jews, the Christians, the Sabeans, and the polytheists. Therefore this verse is not a parallel to that verse, and if it is not a parallel, its grammatical structure is not the same as its grammatical structure.

﴿And the Christians﴾: those who supported ʿIsa (peace be upon him). It has been said that the name is derived from ''nusrah'' (support). It has also been said that it is derived from ''Nasirah'', the name of a town. Each of these has some difficulty, because "Christians" does not correspond in form to "nusrah" nor to "Nasirah". But there is no doubt that by agreement (ijma') the term refers to those who followed ʿIsa (peace be upon him).

﴿Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. ﴿Whoever believes in Allah﴾: what is the grammatical status of ﴿whoever believes﴾? Shall we say it is a conditional (sharṭiyyah)? Or shall we say it is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul)?

There are two views. One is that it is conditional, and on this view the apodosis (jawab al-sharṭ) is ﴿no fear will there be concerning them﴾, and the conditional clause is the predicate of the subject, that is, the conditional sentence is the predicate of the subject.

It is permissible for ''man'' (whoever) to be a relative pronoun, so that it is in apposition (badal) or an explanatory apposition (ʿatf bayan) to what precedes it, and its position is the position of what precedes it. That is, its grammatical position is the same as that of what precedes it. On this view the predicate is His saying ﴿no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾, and it is linked with the particle fa' (then), because ﴿those who were Jews﴾ is a relative pronoun, and it resembles a conditional in generality. Is this understood? Yes, understood.

His saying ﴿whoever﴾: what is the grammatical status of ''amana'' (believed)? If we say ''man'' is conditional, then its position is jussive (jazm) as the verb of the condition. If we say it is a relative pronoun, then it has no grammatical position, because it is the relative clause (silat al-mawsul).

﴿Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. If someone asks: where is the returning pronoun (al-ʿa'id) under both assumptions, whether it is conditional or a relative pronoun?

We say: the returning pronoun is omitted, and it is mentioned in another verse in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabeans, whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Baqarah 62]. So the omitted element in this verse is indicated by the other verse.

﴿Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds﴾. Faith in Allah is necessary, and faith in Allah entails faith in His books, His messengers, His angels, and His decree. What remains? The Last Day.

Thus faith in Allah encompasses five pillars of faith: faith in Allah and what? His angels, His books, His messengers, the decree, and the Last Day (...). The wisdom behind this is that the four pillars were summarized under faith in Allah, while the Last Day was singled out, because faith in the Last Day is what moves a person to act. If a person doubts the Last Day, may Allah protect us, he will not act. For what will he hope and what will he fear?

True faith is therefore not possible without faith in the Last Day, because faith in it is what moves a person to what? To carry out the law of Allah. We said that faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, includes faith in His angels, His books, His messengers, and the decree, both its good and its bad.

His saying ﴿the Last Day﴾ refers to the Day of Resurrection. The definite article (al) in it is the article of previous reference (al-ʿahd). ﴿The Last﴾ means the one after which there is no other day, because the final destination of creation is the Last Day, either to Paradise or to the Fire. May Allah make us and you among the people of Paradise.

Faith in the Last Day: Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: faith in the Last Day includes belief in everything that the Prophet ﷺ informed about that will happen after death.
