Everything the Messenger informed about that happens after death is part of faith in the Last Day: the trial of the grave, the punishment of the grave, the bliss of the grave. Likewise what occurs after the establishment of the Hour, such as the reckoning, the scale, the records, the bridge (al-sirat), the basin (al-hawd), intercession, and other matters.

His saying ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾...

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, there is often a saying to someone who complains, for example in da'wah or otherwise: "Do what is upon you, and the rest is up to Allah." Is this expression correct?
* Shaykh: Yes, it is correct.
* Student: Then, Shaykh (...), does "everything is up to Allah"?
* Shaykh: No. "The rest" means what is beyond your capacity, so it is up to Allah; that is, it is not upon you, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 25–26].
* Student: And what about a person's own action, is that also up to Allah?
* Shaykh: That is from Allah, and there must be Allah's help with it. It is like when you say: give so-and-so ten riyals, and the rest is on so-and-so...
* Student: This is clear.
* Shaykh: This is also clear. You now have what is upon you (...) and you have delivered, and the rest is up to Allah. You are not responsible for it.
* Student: May Allah honor you, Shaykh. In tawhid al-rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship) they mention (...) the three attributes: that Allah is the Creator, the Provider, and the Governor. Why were only these mentioned?
* Shaykh: There is nothing beyond them. ''Rabb'' means the Creator, the Owner, the Governor. There is nothing else.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We mentioned that disbelief increases and decreases. What is the response to those who argue that one who abandons prayer is not a disbeliever, and say: the Prophet ﷺ said: "The covenant between us and them is prayer, so whoever abandons it has disbelieved" [Reported by al-Tirmidhi (2621) and al-Nasa'i (463) from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb.] They say: this is disbelief in a lesser sense (kufr duna kufr). So how do we respond to them?
* Shaykh: We respond to them with the same hadith. He said: "between us and them", which is a separator. If this is "between us and them", it means a separator between disbelief and belief. There is also the hadith of Jabir, where the Prophet ﷺ said: "Between a man and shirk and disbelief is the abandonment of prayer" [Reported by Muslim (82/134)].
* Student: They say, Shaykh, that he did not deny it; he is negligent about it, he did not deny prayer...
* Shaykh: Very well. Since the Messenger said: "whoever abandons it has disbelieved", and he gave it an unrestricted statement, how can we restrict it? If we restrict it to one who denies the obligation, we say this is wrong, because one who denies an obligation disbelieves even if he prays. But the hadith says: "whoever abandons it."

If they say the meaning is abandoning it together with denial, we say: this person has disregarded the description the Law has considered and brought a description the Law has not considered, because a person disbelieves by denial by ijma' (scholarly consensus). The exception is a recent convert who does not know, and he is taught.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. Is it true what some say, that the nation of Islam will not rise up until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sends down ʿIsa (peace be upon him) and the Mahdi is raised up? Is this statement correct?
* Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know. The apparent view is that it is not correct regarding the whole nation. But regarding a group, it is certain, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "A group of my nation will continue upon the truth" [Reported by Muslim (156/247) from the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah].

As for the whole nation, I do not know. But it may be so. The reality is that when you look at the Muslims today, and I do not know about the future, you find them in a state that does not lead to victory: scattered, divided, and some of them judge by other than what Allah revealed, mock and ridicule the religion and its people. We ask Allah to restore the glory of the Muslims.

* Student: ﴿And what has been revealed to you﴾: ''ma'' implies generality. Why does the Qur'an not first take it in its general sense, and also the Torah and the Gospel, as emphasis?
* Shaykh: There is no need. Since it mentions the Qur'an alone, independently, and relying on the verse we cited.
* Student: (...) the generality, the Torah was revealed (...) so what prevents (...)?
* Shaykh: There is no need. Since it is explicitly stated: ﴿until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you﴾, there is no need to say the apparent meaning is generality. Making this phrase specific to the Qur'an is more eloquent regarding the exalted status of the Qur'an, so that the Qur'an is parallel to both books together.
* Student: Shall we say this generality is restricted?
* Shaykh: Yes, we say: what is meant is the Qur'an. ﴿And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance for mankind, and He revealed the Criterion﴾ [Al 'Imran 3–4].
* Student: A man got up to speak, and the topic of his talk was the Qur'an, and during his speech he said: "the one about whom his Lord said..."?
* Shaykh: This is a grave error. He is speaking about the Qur'an and says: "the Qur'an is the one about whom his Lord said." This is wrong. It suggests the doctrine of the Jahmiyyah (a deviant sect), although there is a possible linguistic justification if we know that the speaker is one of the pure Ahl al-Sunnah, because the word ''Rabb'' can mean "companion" (sahib), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might﴾ [al-Saffat 180]. ''Izzah'' (might) is an attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but here it means "the Possessor of Might."
* Student: May Allah be good to you. You have given (...) in glorifying Allah, the Glorified and Exalted...
* Shaykh: In any case, the tongue must be kept free of this. I must advise him. This is wrong, because it gives the common people the impression that the Qur'an is created.
* Student: Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿And many of them will surely increase [in rebellion]﴾, and did not say "most of them", even though most Jews and Christians...?
* Shaykh: No. It may be that most of them are imitators (muqallidah), and not (...) disbelief, but they are imitators among the common people.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, is it correct to say the supplication: "O Allah, indeed we have turned back to You" (Allahumma inna hudna ilayk)?
* Shaykh: In the sense of "we have returned"?
* Student: "We have returned" or "we ask..."
* Shaykh: It is correct. If the meaning is known, it is correct.
* Student: (...) action and certainty. A person may mention Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and another mention Him less than him, so the first increases in faith and the other does not increase?
* Shaykh: Yes. This is the cause of certainty. The cause of certainty may be greater in one person than another, but certainty itself differs (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. For example, one may mention Allah a thousand times, and another a hundred times, so the first has more remembrance. But indeed, it may be that the heart of the second, who did not mention Allah as much, has more certainty than that, so each one has increased in something.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a party they denied and a party they killed. And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them, but then many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ [al-Ma'idah 70–71].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Say, O People of the Book, you are not upon anything﴾. What is the meaning of this sentence?
* Student: No, [it means] upon the truth, and not upon any part of it, except that you establish the Torah and the Gospel.
* Shaykh: Yes, but it does not mean ﴿you are not upon anything﴾.
* Student: It means: you are not upon the truth.
* Another student: It means: you are not upon any part of the religion.
* Shaykh: You are not upon any part of the religion, because they claim that they are People of the Book and that they are the people of religion. So He says: ﴿you are not upon anything﴾. Is there a parallel to it?
* Student: From the Qur'an?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: His saying, the Majestic and Exalted: ﴿The Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 113].
* Shaykh: Yes. The point is that each of them said to the other group: "You are not upon anything," meaning: you are not upon a religion.

His saying: ﴿until you establish the Torah and the Gospel﴾. What does establishing them consist of?

* Student: By carrying out the commands, avoiding the prohibitions, and affirming the reports.
* Shaykh: Well said: by carrying out the commands, avoiding the prohibitions, and affirming the reports.

And His saying: ﴿and what has been revealed to you﴾. What is meant by it?

* Student: What is meant is the noble Qur'an.
* Shaykh: Is there something in the Qur'an that supports this?
* Student: Yes: ﴿He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance for mankind, and He revealed the Criterion﴾ [Al 'Imran 3–4].

**The Shaykh:** ﴿He has sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what was before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [3] ﴿before, as guidance for mankind, and He sent down the Criterion﴾. May Allah bless you. How can what is sent down to the Messenger ﷺ increase these people in transgression and disbelief?

**Student:** By their obstinacy along with their disbelief.

**The Shaykh:** So they increase in disbelief. Can it be derived from the verse that disbelief has types, one that increases and one that decreases?

**Student:** Yes, it increases and decreases.

**The Shaykh:** It increases and decreases. And what has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas in this meaning?

**The student:** "Disbelief below disbelief" [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3258).]].

**The Shaykh:** Well done, may Allah bless you.

Regarding His words: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾. What is its meaning?

**Student:** Do not grieve over these people who did not believe in your message. This contains consolation.

**The Shaykh:** Over those who disbelieve in you.

**The student:** Over those who disbelieved in you and did not believe in what was sent down to you. This contains consolation for the Prophet ﷺ.

**The Shaykh:** Consolation for the Messenger ﷺ.

Is there anything in the Qur'an indicating that the Messenger ﷺ used to feel constriction in his chest?

**Student:** Yes, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So do not let yourself expire in regret over them﴾ [Fatir 8].

**The Shaykh:** And ﴿We know that your chest becomes constricted by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr 97], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 3].

Regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians﴾. Is there a difficulty in the nominative case of ﴿al-Sabi'un﴾ (the Sabians)?

**Student:** In..

**The Shaykh:** Because ﴿inna﴾ (indeed) puts the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative, and a conjoined element following its noun must be put in the accusative before the predicate is completed. Here He said ﴿al-Sabi'un﴾, and ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians﴾?

**Student:** It is conjoined to the position (mahall) of the subject of ﴿inna﴾.

**The Shaykh:** It is not permissible to conjoin to the position of the subject of ﴿inna﴾ except after the predicate is completed. Ibn Malik says:

*And permissible is your nominative conjoined to the accusative of "inna", after the completion [of the predicate].*

**Student:** Those who believe.

**Another student:** The predicate of ﴿inna﴾ is omitted, and its estimate is..

**The Shaykh:** No, the difficulty is in ﴿al-Sabi'un﴾: why is it nominative, when it is conjoined to what?

**Student:** Because it is conjoined to the subject (mubtada'), which is ﴿those who were Jews﴾.

**The Shaykh:** So it was not conjoined to ﴿Indeed, those who﴾?

**The student:** No, it was conjoined to ﴿those who were Jews﴾.

**The Shaykh:** ﴿Those who were Jews﴾ is accusative or nominative? Nominative? How can it be nominative when it is conjoined to an accusative?

**Student:** Because here it is conjoining a clause to a clause.

**The Shaykh:** Then what is the grammatical position of ﴿those who were Jews﴾?

**Student:** A subject (mubtada'), Shaykh.

**The Shaykh:** A subject, correct, exactly.

What is it that favours the view that ﴿those who﴾ is a subject and not conjoined to ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾?

**Student:** It is connected to the end of the verse: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, and this applies to those who believed and those after them.

**The Shaykh:** Why?

**The student:** Because for ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ one does not say "those who believed, whoever of them believed," since that would be obtaining what is already obtained (tahsil hasil).

**The Shaykh:** Because they are believers. So the end of the verse favours that ﴿those who were Jews﴾ is a subject.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, and omitted, the Mighty and Majestic, other things from the pillars of faith. ﴿Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ mentions two of the pillars of faith and does not mention the rest?

**Student:** Because belief in Allah necessitates belief in the angels, the messengers, the books, and divine decree, both its good and its bad.

**The Shaykh:** Well done. Belief in Allah includes belief in His angels, His books, His messengers, and divine decree, both its good and its bad.

What is the Last Day?

**Student:** It is the one after which there is no day.

**The Shaykh:** But what is it, its very identity?

**The student:** It is the Day of Resurrection.

**The Shaykh:** Why is it called the Last Day?

**Student:** Because there is no day after it.

**The Shaykh:** Because there is no day after it, well done.

Regarding His words: ﴿So no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. What is its meaning? ﴿No fear﴾, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾.

**Students:** We have not taken it.

**The Shaykh:** Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and does righteousness﴾, meaning he did a righteous deed. Righteous deed is what combines two conditions: sincerity to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and second, following the Messenger ﷺ.

If you wish, say: sincerity to Allah and following His law, so that it is more general and includes those who believed in the earlier messengers and followed their laws. It is said: righteous deed is what combines two matters, sincerity to Allah and following the Messenger whose law is still in force. The opposite of righteous deed is corrupt deed. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'A'isha.]]. This lacks following.

The Prophet ﷺ also said, narrating from his Lord, that He the Exalted said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his association" [[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. This lacks sincerity.

Know that sincerity is not an easy matter. Sincerity is among the most difficult things, to the extent that some of the early generations (salaf) said: "I never struggled against my self over anything as I struggled over sincerity."

For this reason the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge in Allah from associating anything with Allah knowingly, and seek His forgiveness for what he did unknowingly.

Shirk is more hidden than the crawling of an ant on a black rock. Therefore a person must always cleanse his heart of the filth of shirk and examine it, so that he does not fall into it while unaware.

﴿So no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾: first, in grammar. ﴿No fear﴾ and ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, although ﴿lā﴾ here is the negation of the genus (lā al-nafiya lil-jins). It is well known that the negation of the genus puts the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative, as Ibn Malik says:

*Give to "lā" the action of "inna" with an indefinite noun, whether singular or repeated, that comes to you.*

So here we say: "lā" was not in the accusative, because it was repeated, and when it is repeated it is cancelled (ulghiya). So ﴿lā khawf﴾ is a negation (lā nafiya), not of the genus. We do not say "of the genus," we say: there is no fear upon them, meaning regarding the future, because they are secure and tranquil, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with injustice — for them is security, and they are guided﴾ [al-An'am 82].

﴿Nor will they grieve﴾, meaning over what has passed, because all of what has passed they have consumed in obedience to Allah, so they do not grieve over the past, since they are content with its outcome and reward, and they do not fear the future ﴿So no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that among the Jews, Christians, and Sabians there are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, based on His saying: ﴿whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Baqarah 126]. This is indeed so. For example, the Jews who believed in Musa while his law was in force are included among those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and likewise the Christians who believed in 'Isa while his law was in force, and the believers in Muhammad ﷺ.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the reward of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is not based on lineage or descent, but is based on faith and righteous deeds, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat 13].

* Among the benefits of this verse: that when we speak we should refer to the Jews as Jews and the Christians as Christians. But the priests (qissisun) among the Christians have come to give themselves the title "Messianic" (Masihiyyin), to lend the garment of truth to the falsehood they hold. That is, if they attribute themselves to the Messiah, they attribute themselves to his religion, but the Messiah is innocent of them, because they did not accept his good news, nor did they believe in it, nor did they believe in Muhammad ﷺ, whom Allah took the covenant from the prophets that they would believe in and support. So their true description and true title is Christians. The scholars who write history, from Muslims and non-Muslims, have continued to call them Christians, until the Christian state became mighty and seized many Islamic lands, and named itself by what? By "Messianic."

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Last Day, based on His saying: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Included in belief in the Last Day is everything that occurs after death. So the questioning of the dead person in his grave about his Lord, his religion, and his prophet is among the matters of the Last Day, and likewise the bliss and punishment of the grave, and likewise the people rising from their graves to the Lord of the worlds barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. So everything the Prophet ﷺ informed about that occurs after death is included in belief in the Last Day.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that faith alone is not sufficient, based on His saying: ﴿believed﴾ and ﴿and does righteousness﴾. If a person affirms Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the books, the prophets, and divine decree, but does not have a righteous deed, then he has fear, and he has grief, because Allah only negated fear and grief from those who believe and do righteousness.

If someone says: according to this explanation, do you consider that abandoning righteous deeds, any deed whatsoever, makes a person a disbeliever?

The answer: No. Because declaring someone a disbeliever (takfir) is one thing, and fear of sins and grief over what has passed is another. We do not apply the description of disbelief except to the one whom Allah and His Messenger have declared a disbeliever, and we apply it only to one whom Allah and His Messenger have declared a disbeliever, because takfir is a legal ruling (hukm shar'i) that has great consequences, and legal rulings are only taken from the Law. It is not permissible to describe anyone as a disbeliever unless he is a disbeliever according to the indication of the Book and the Sunnah, nor to deny disbelief from him if the Book and the Sunnah indicate his disbelief. But there remains the question: when the term disbelief occurs in the Qur'an and the Sunnah, do we interpret it as major (akbar) disbelief or minor (asghar) disbelief?

The answer: It is obligatory to interpret it as minor disbelief. This is obligatory, because the default is the continuation of the Muslim's Islam, so we do not remove him from the circle of Islam except with certainty. Why?

Except with certainty, because certainty is not removed except by certainty, and certainty cannot be removed by doubt. So if the Qur'an and the Sunnah use the term disbelief for one who does such-and-such, and we are uncertain whether what is meant is disbelief that removes one from the religion or minor disbelief, then it is obligatory to interpret it as minor disbelief. Why?

Because the default is the continuation of Islam until we are certain that he has left Islam. And because the expression of disbelief in many places is known with certainty by a person to be minor disbelief, by the indication of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. An example of that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Insulting a Muslim is grave sin (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr)" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (48) and Muslim (64/116), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

If someone says: then whoever fights the believers is a disbeliever, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "fighting him is disbelief."

We say: this is not correct, because Allah said in His mighty Book: ﴿If two groups of believers fight, then make reconciliation between them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers, so make reconciliation between your two brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat 9, 10].

If the fighter were a disbeliever with major disbelief, he would not be our brother.

Likewise He said regarding retaliation for one who kills a believer: ﴿Then whoever is pardoned by his brother [i.e., the killer] some of it﴾ [al-Baqarah 178], calling the killer his brother, even though killing a Muslim is disbelief. So it is said: this shows that applying the term disbelief does not necessarily imply leaving Islam. Likewise he said: "Two things among the people are for them disbelief: wailing (niyaha) and slandering lineage (ta'n fi al-nasab)" [[Narrated by Muslim (67/121) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "Two things among the people are for them disbelief: slandering lineage, and wailing over the dead."]].

Such examples are many. Based on this we say: disbelief is a legal ruling, and it is not permissible to apply it except to one to whom Allah and His Messenger have applied it. Then disbelief is of two types, what?

Minor and major. So if we know that this is major disbelief by the indication of the Book and the Sunnah, we say: it is major disbelief. If we do not know, it is obligatory to interpret it as minor disbelief, because Islam is certain, and disbelief with possibility is not certain. Also, one cannot make the blood of a Muslim lawful except by an explicit and clear text.

If someone says: if it is established that this is disbelief, do we apply the ruling to a specific individual or not?

We say: yes, we apply it to a specific individual when the conditions of takfir are met. We judge him to be a disbeliever by name. So if we see a man who never prays, we say: this is a disbeliever with disbelief that removes him from the religion, for the well-known evidences, which are not hidden from many of you.

If someone says: and do we declare him a disbeliever by name?

We say: yes, we declare him a disbeliever by name, and we call him to prayer. If he prays, the disbelief and the death penalty are lifted from him, and if he does not pray, he is executed as a disbeliever by name.

Likewise, if we see a person prostrating to an idol, and prostration to idols is major disbelief that removes one from the religion, we judge him by name to be a disbeliever, and we make his blood and property lawful.

If we hear someone insulting Allah and His Messenger, we judge him by name to be a disbeliever, and we ask him to repent according to the preponderant opinion. If he repents, we lift the execution and the description of disbelief from him. Otherwise we execute him as a disbeliever, and so on.

As for the view of some people that no one is declared a disbeliever by name unless the Qur'an and the Sunnah state that he is a disbeliever by name, this is a grave error, because if we adopted this view, no one would remain a disbeliever. Yes, we do not judge that he is in the Fire unless he is named in the Book and the Sunnah. There is a difference between judging someone as a disbeliever and what?

Testifying that he is in the Fire. We do not testify for him. If we testify that he is a disbeliever, we do not say that he is in the Fire by name, but we say: this is a disbeliever, and every disbeliever is in the Fire. This is correct: every disbeliever is in the Fire. The People of the Sunnah and the early generations (salaf) rejected testifying for a specific person with praise-titles, but they did not reject generalization. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, the Commander of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with him, gave a sermon and said: "You say: So-and-so is a martyr, So-and-so is a martyr. Perhaps he loaded his camel with [stolen goods]. Do not say 'martyr,' but say: whoever is killed in the way of Allah is a martyr" [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i (3349) and Ahmad (285), with the wording: "And another thing they say about one who was killed in your campaigns or died: 'So-and-so was killed as a martyr' or 'So-and-so died as a martyr.' Perhaps he has loaded the burden of his animal or the saddle-bag of his mount with gold or silver, seeking trade. Do not say that, but say as the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever is killed in the way of Allah or dies is in Paradise.'"]].

So you must know the difference between judging someone as a disbeliever and what?

And testifying that he is in the Fire. We have mentioned that a specific person is judged a disbeliever when the conditions of takfir are met. The conditions of takfir must be known:

First: that the person must intend what he says or does. That the person must intend what he says or does. If he does not intend it, there is nothing upon him, because he is overpowered. All utterances over which a person is overpowered have no ruling, neither in disbelief, nor in divorce, nor in manumission, nor in endowment, nor in anything else, because they have no ruling. The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no divorce in compulsion (ighlaq)" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2193) and Ibn Majah (2046), with the wording, from the hadith of 'A'isha: "There is no divorce or manumission in compulsion."]].

And Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah 225]. So intention is necessary.

Based on that, if a person is compelled to disbelieve, he does not become a disbeliever, by the explicit text of the Qur'an: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is forced while his heart remains firm in faith—but whoever opens his breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [an-Nahl 106].

If a person utters a word of disbelief out of extreme anger, he does not become a disbeliever. Why? Because of lack of intention: he did not intend to speak this, but he was overcome until he spoke, so he does not become a disbeliever.

If a person utters a word of disbelief out of extreme joy—the opposite of the first case—he does not become a disbeliever either, because he was overcome and did not intend it. The hadith is explicit on this in the story of the man who lost his mount, which was carrying his food and drink, and despaired of it. He lay down to sleep under a tree, and then suddenly the camel had come back, so he seized its rein and said: "O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord." He erred out of extreme joy [[Narrated by Muslim (2747/7) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]], and there is nothing upon him. His words have no consequence, because they were—what?—without intention. But in extreme joy he made a mistake.

Among this also is error in interpretation (ta'wil). If a person does something that would constitute disbelief, interpreting it so and thinking it is the truth, he does not become a disbeliever, because he did not intend disbelief. Rather, he did this thing or said this thing on the basis that it is true and permissible. Had he known it was disbelief, he would have been among the most averse people to it. The story of the man who was extravagant against himself supports this: he instructed his family, when he died, to burn him and scatter him into the sea, and said: "By Allah, if Allah has power over me, He will punish me with a punishment He has not inflicted upon anyone in the worlds."

He only ordered this out of fear of Allah's punishment, thinking that if Allah resurrected him He would punish him severely. Allah gathered him and asked him: "Why did you do this?" He said: "O Lord, I did it out of fear of You," and Allah forgave him [[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (3481) and Muslim (2756/24) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Allah be praised, Allah forgave him, because he only did this out of fear of Allah's punishment, so he thought it would not harm him. And according to some interpretations, among this is the action of Yunus, peace be upon him: ﴿And Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya 87], and that We would not constrict him more than the constriction that befell him—and the constriction that befell him was greater.

But he, peace be upon him, undoubtedly did not say this except through interpretation, or he only thought it through interpretation. This is an important matter, and Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, in one of his two narrations built upon it that the Kharijites are not disbelievers. Why?

Because they deemed the blood of the Muslims lawful by means of what? By interpretation. They see that they draw near to Allah by killing the Muslims, because they do not see themselves as wrong—that is, they see the Muslims as not being in the right—so they are interpreters (mutawwilah).

Some scholars applied their disbelief absolutely, based on the narrations concerning them. Others said: this applies to the specific Kharijites who rebelled against Ali ibn Abi Talib, and not every rebel is a disbeliever. So the important point now: what have we stipulated? Intention. And this is among the most important things.

The ignorant person: the ignorant one does not intend opposition. Pay close attention to this matter, it is extremely important. The ignorant person who prostrates to an idol, thinking it is not forbidden because he lived in a land of disbelief and was recently Muslim, and thought this does no harm: do we say he is a disbeliever because he is a polytheist, or not?

We do not say this until we teach him that this is shirk. If he persists in it and says: "I found my fathers doing this," then he becomes a disbeliever.

Adultery is forbidden by the consensus of the Muslims. If someone denies its prohibition because he did not know Islam, having recently embraced it, is he—what?—not a disbeliever, because knowledge is necessary. This is indicated by many hadiths and many verses. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra 15].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns until He sends in their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses, and We would not destroy the towns except when their people are wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qasas 59]. And who is the wrongdoer?

The wrongdoer is one who commits the violation deliberately and knowingly. As for one who commits it out of ignorance or error in interpretation or otherwise, he is not a wrongdoer. So these matters must be observed, lest the foot slip and one declare disbelieving one whom Allah and His Messenger did not declare a disbeliever. And if you declare disbelief upon one whom Allah and His Messenger did not declare a disbeliever, the disbelief returns upon you—we ask Allah for well-being—as in the authentic hadith: "Whoever calls a man a disbeliever, or says 'O enemy of Allah' while it is not so, it returns upon him" [[Narrated by Muslim (61/112) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, with the wording: "Whoever calls a man a disbeliever" or said: "enemy of Allah," and it is not so, except that it returns upon him.]]—i.e., it returns to him.

The opposite of that: those who never declare disbelief by abandoning actions, not even accepting what the Sharia has brought. They say: there is no disbelief except in belief alone; as for actions, there is no disbelief in them. He commits adultery, steals, kills, abandons prayer, abandons zakat, abandons Hajj, and he is not a disbeliever. This is an error.

The truth always lies between two extremes: either excess or deficiency. It is obligatory upon us to worship Allah the Exalted by what we mention of His rulings and what we do of His law, so we do not mention of His rulings what He did not mention. If Allah says: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to fabricate against Allah falsehood﴾ [an-Nahl 116], then how much more so is one who says: "This is disbelief and this is Islam." This is more serious, because disbelief, O brothers, entails what?

Great rulings. It entails that the one we have judged a disbeliever has lawful blood and lawful property, he cannot remain married to his wife, he is not buried with the Muslims, and if he is a leader, it is obligatory to rebel against him, and other such great matters.

The matter is not a word that is said; the matter is extremely serious. Then, even so, those who declare disbelief upon one whom Allah and His Messenger did not declare a disbeliever—by what do they become disbelievers? By their fighting the Muslims. Fighting a Muslim is disbelief, as in the authentic hadith [[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (48) and Muslim (64/116) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]. And if we say it is minor disbelief, as the verse of al-Hujurat indicates, we say: but it may lead to sins and major sins, until what? Until he becomes a major disbeliever.

So the important point: we must not advance before Allah and His Messenger; we must not declare disbelief upon one whom Allah and His Messenger did not declare a disbeliever, and we must not hold back from declaring disbelief upon one whom Allah and His Messenger declared a disbeliever. Praise be to Allah, the matter belongs to Allah; it is not ours, nor so-and-so's, nor so-and-so's.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. People come and say that disbelief occurs through actions, and they say: judging by other than what Allah revealed, if it is established and becomes general, not a single matter, but established and legislated, replacing the ruling of Allah the Exalted—he says: whether it is general or in some region, so long as it is established, it is disbelief, and it is obligatory upon us to declare disbelief upon whoever approves this ruling, even if a person who rules by Allah's ruling ninety percent of the time, but he has established ten percent of his rulings by other than what Allah revealed, approved them and defended them. Is this correct or not?

* Shaykh: As I told you: one looks at whether it is intentional, whether it is through interpretation, and whether he wanted to replace the law of Allah with another law. People differ, because one who judges by other than what Allah revealed may be an oppressor, meaning he wants to harm the one judged against, with no other aim; this is an act of disobedience, like taking his wealth without a judgment—clear? Or he wants a benefit for himself; he does not want to take anything from the one judged against, but wants his own benefit, so he judges by other than what Allah revealed. This too is without doubt not disbelief; this is a fasiq (wrongdoer). And sometimes he judges by other than what Allah revealed without being content with Allah's ruling: this is disbelief, because he has denied the Sharia. And sometimes he judges by other than what Allah revealed through interpretation, either by himself or by what is made attractive to him.

Let us give an example: some scholars among the Muslims say: these matters of life, the Sharia left them absolute; a person considers what is more beneficial for people and does it. Then they cite things that are doubts, not proofs, and say: the Messenger ﷺ came to Madinah and found them pollinating the palm trees, and he said to them: "What is this?" As if he were saying: leave them, do not pollinate them. So they left them, and the fruit spoiled. They came to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the fruit has spoiled." He said: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life" [[Narrated by Muslim (2363/141) from the hadith of Aisha.]].

Some people took from his saying: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life" that they—what? That whatever they see as beneficial they do. Even interest in what they call "investment interest": they say it is permissible, because the Messenger said: "You are more knowledgeable," and since the bank, for example, gives this poor man great sums with which he establishes factories or cultivates lands or trades, he benefits, and the poor man benefits; this is a benefit for both parties, and since it is a benefit for both parties, it is lawful. They deceive with such things. If the ruler is ignorant of the legal rulings and advisers come to him confusing the matters, perhaps he inclines to them. But it is obligatory upon the people of knowledge to clarify that this is forbidden and impermissible, and the proof is established against him.

* Student: They say: we rule in general, but as for specific interpretation, no. They say: reaching a specific person in his place, each individual cannot do it by himself. They say: since the matter is specific and has occurred, do we say it is major or minor disbelief? Or do people, each by his own understanding—it is hard for us, they say: we do not want to declare Allah the Exalted's ruling unless we judge by these according to the evidences?

* Shaykh: Unless we declare him a disbeliever.

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Mistaken. This is a grave error. How can you judge him a disbeliever without relying on the conditions? There must be conditions.

* Student: May Allah reward you, Shaykh. We mentioned that the first condition is that the person intended what he said or did. Are there other conditions besides this, Shaykh?

* Shaykh: Knowledge is included in this. The truth is that the only certain condition is this one we mentioned: intention. The ignorant person has intended the act but not the violation. For this reason, the preponderant opinion regarding breaking oaths is that whoever breaks his oath out of ignorance or forgetfulness has no expiation upon him, as if he said: "By Allah, I will not wear this garment," then found a garment hanging and wore it, not knowing it was the garment he swore about—there is nothing upon him, or he forgot. The point is that all the conditions that are mentioned may go back to this.

But someone may say: what is your opinion of the one who mocks—does he become a disbeliever or not?

* Students: He becomes a disbeliever.

* Shaykh: He becomes a disbeliever by the explicit text of the Qur'an. How does this agree with our saying that intention is a condition? We say: yes, because the one who mocks intended—he intended the act or the speech—but he did not know what it entails. Similarly: a person, for example, has intercourse during the day in Ramadan. He knows it is forbidden, but he does not know what it entails; he does not know that this act entails such and such. Yet he knows it is forbidden. We say: he must offer expiation.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed: ﴿Certainly We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed. And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them, then many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is seeing of what they do (71). Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary." And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah—Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire, and there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers" (72). Certainly disbelieved those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three," and there is no god except one God. And if they do not cease from what they say, there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment (73). Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (74). The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; messengers had passed on before him, and his mother was a supporter of truth; they both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs, then look how they are deluded (75). Say, "Do you worship other than Allah that which controls for you no harm or benefit? And Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 70–76].

Shaykh: Well done. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾. The sentence here is emphasized with three emphatics: the implied oath, the lam, and "qad."

The pronoun in His words ﴿We took﴾ refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it came in this form to magnify Himself, blessed and exalted, because He is the Greatest of the great.

His words ﴿the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾: the mithaq (covenant) is a firm pledge, as if the one who made the pledge was bound by it with a strong bond.

In this surah Allah has explained what the covenant taken from them was, and what covenant they have with Allah. Allah said: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve chiefs. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds"﴾. This is the covenant that was taken from them: ﴿If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan﴾. There are five items in this covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel, and He made for them a covenant upon Himself. What is it? ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds.› Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel.

﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾, messengers from among them, some of whom were of the resolute messengers (ulul-azm), such as Musa and Isa, and others who were below that rank. Allah sent messengers to them.

Some scholars have said: The verse may mean that the covenant Allah took from the Children of Israel is what Allah instilled in creation of His tawhid, so that in His words ﴿Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ it refers to tawhid, and ﴿We sent to them messengers﴾ refers to prophethood, combining belief in Allah with belief in the messengers.

﴿We sent to them messengers﴾, and Allah, blessed and exalted, did not specify their number, because what matters is the category, not the number. So what was their response to the messengers? Allah said: ﴿a group they denied, and a group they kill﴾. Some scholars claimed that the verse contains an omission, and the implied meaning is: "We sent to them messengers, and they disobeyed." Apparently we were mistaken.

﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied, and a group they killed﴾:

(Kullama) is a conditional particle, and although it is conditional, it implies repetition. Look at His words, ﴿Every time it lights up for them, they walk in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 20]. What does it imply?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: And the conditional nature means that they do not walk except when it lights up for them. And ﴿every time it lit up for them, they walked in it﴾ here: every time a messenger came to them, they denied a group. Some exegetes claimed that the verse contains an omission, and the implied meaning is: every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they disobeyed, a group they denied and a group they killed. But I see no need for this supposition, and if there is no need for the supposition, brothers, then supposing it is superfluous and has no place. So there is no need for the supposition; rather we say: every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they denied a group of the messengers and killed a group of the messengers.

Let us return to the verse: ﴿Every time a messenger came to them﴾. We said that (kullama) is conditional and implies repetition.

﴿A messenger came to them with what they did not desire﴾, i.e., with what their souls did not want and did not incline to. They did not respond; rather their reaction, as they say, was either killing or denial.

﴿A group they denied﴾: (a group) here is the direct object preceding (they denied), and the clause (they denied) is the response of the condition, the response of (kullama). That is: every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they denied a group. He did not say "they denied him," because some of them denied and escaped being killed, and some were killed, and one is not killed except after denying.

﴿A group they denied and a group they kill﴾. Allah did not mention a third group, because of their small number, namely those who believed in him, meaning a group who believed in him but was few. As we said to you before, a small number is not considered, and for this reason it is always disregarded in mention.

﴿A group they denied﴾: denial is rejecting a report, rejecting the statement of the one who reports. If someone tells you, "Zayd has stood up," and you say, "He has not stood up," that is denial, because you have rejected his report. This is what denial is.

﴿And a group they kill﴾: killing is well known. He used the word ﴿they kill﴾ in the present tense, indicating the continuation of their killing of the prophets, because the present tense indicates continuity, while the past tense indicates a past event that has ended. Perhaps this indicates, and Allah knows best, that they will not cease killing the prophets until the last of them, peace and blessings be upon him, Muhammad (ﷺ).

* This verse contains benefits, among them: emphasizing speech with an oath and other emphatics, even when the report is true. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿We have indeed taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾, where Allah emphasized His speech with the oath, the lam, and "qad."

If someone says: Is not Allah the most truthful of speakers without emphasis?

* The students: Yes.

* Shaykh: The answer is: Yes. But the Noble Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and the matching of speech to what the situation requires, because matching speech to the requirement of the situation is eloquence. If that is so, the Qur'an is the most eloquent speech. When the situation calls for emphasis, the speech is emphasized, and here the situation calls for emphasis. Why? So that the proof may be established against the Children of Israel, that Allah took their covenant and they divided into two groups.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah took the covenant from the Children of Israel and did not limit Himself to that. If we say that the covenant means the innate nature (fitrah), then He sent messengers to them in support of the fitrah.

* Following from this benefit: the mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted, toward His servants, and that He did not leave them, glorified and exalted is He, to what they know by their innate nature, but sent messengers to them to affirm that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah in sending messengers individually and in groups, as in His words ﴿and We sent to them messengers﴾. Among the Children of Israel there were many messengers. For example, Ibrahim and Lut were at what time? At one time; Yusuf and his father were at one time; Ya'qub and Ishaq were at one time. But with the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is impossible for there to be two prophets or two messengers at once, why? Because he is the Seal of the Prophets, peace and blessings be upon him.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the breaking of the covenant by the Children of Israel. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿a group they denied and a group they kill﴾, and so they did not fulfill the covenant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against what the Children of Israel did, namely denying the messengers and aggression against them, because Allah did not relate to us the stories of the prophets and their peoples merely so that we would know them as history, but so that we would take lessons from them, as He said: ﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for those of understanding﴾ [Yusuf 111].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Children of Israel only believe in what agrees with their desires, as shown by His words ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied﴾, and so on to the end.

* Among its benefits: those speakers who built the foundations of their creed on reason, such as the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah, the Ash'ariyyah and their like, have some resemblance to the Jews. When a text comes to them with something their reason does not accept, they deny it if they are able to, or they distort it if they are not able to. This is because they consider the reference for what Allah reports about Himself to be what? Reason. So when a text comes with what does not suit their minds, they deny it, they deny it and reject it if they can deny it. They claim that authentic single-narrator reports (akhbar al-ahad), those established in the two Sahihs and others, are false. They say: single-narrator reports cannot establish a creed, because a single report is subject to conjecture, and conjecture cannot be the basis of a creed. Therefore they reject most of the hadiths on the attributes, because most of them are single-narrator reports.

Then we say to them: Do you accept a single report in rulings, such as commands and prohibitions? They will say: Yes. We say: Your acceptance of that, although the report indicates obligation, prohibition, disapproval or recommendation, is necessary. That is, you must pray while believing that it is what? An obligatory duty. That is a belief regarding what is imposed on a person or what is required of him, while that other belief concerns what Allah affirmed for Himself.

Accordingly we say: Even reports about rulings entail a belief, since every ruling must be believed to be obligatory, recommended, disapproved, or prohibited.

The point is that the People of the Book who rejected what their reason does not allow resemble the Children of Israel, who, when a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, denied a group and killed a group.

* So we say that another benefit of the verse is: caution against the desires of the soul, and that the desire of the soul may lead to destruction and to doing what is ugly both legally and rationally.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a group of the Children of Israel denied the messengers and a group killed the messengers without caring about that, as shown by His words ﴿a group they denied and a group they kill﴾.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾: ﴿Hasibu﴾ means: they thought (ẓannū). ﴿Allā takūna fitnatun﴾ has two readings. The first reading: with a damma on the nūn; the second reading: with a fatha on the nūn. According to the reading with the damma, (anna) is the lightened form of the heavy (anna) — according to the reading of what? — with the damma on the nūn, and its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (lā takūnu) is in the position of a nominative as its predicate. And according to the reading with the fatha, (anna) is a verbal particle (maṣdariyyah) and (lā) is a negation particle, and (takūna) is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by the verbal (anna).

* The Shaykh: I say: there are two readings: ﴿allā takūnu﴾ with a damma on the nūn, ﴿allā takūna﴾ with a fatha on the nūn. According to the reading with the damma, (anna) is the lightened form of the heavy (anna), its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter, and (takūnu) is its predicate, the clause (takūnu) is its predicate. According to the reading with the fatha, (anna) is a verbal particle (maṣdariyyah) and (lā) is a negation particle, and (takūna) is an imperfect verb in the accusative governed by (anna). Here the governing word has been applied to what follows it, with the separation by the negating (lā).

Thereupon it is permissible for us, or it is proper for us, to speak about (anna): when what precedes it is a certainty ('ilm), then the nominative is obligatory; when what precedes it conveys supposition (ẓann), both readings are permissible; and when what precedes it is neither certainty nor supposition, the accusative is obligatory. For example, you say: "It pleases me from the student that he not argue (allā yujādil)." How do we read the lām?

* A student: (allā yujādil) with the accusative.

* The Shaykh: (allā yujādil) with the accusative is required. If it becomes (ẓann), you say: "I knew that they would not be such-and-such (allā yakūnū kadhā)," and (anna) is the lightened form of the heavy (anna); if it is (ẓann), both readings are permissible in it.

In the noble verse: ﴿ḥasibū﴾ means ẓannū (they supposed), and therefore both readings are permissible: the accusative and the nominative: ﴿ḥasibū allā takūnu fitnatun﴾ and ﴿wa-ḥasibū allā takūna fitnatun﴾, meaning: they supposed that there would not be, as a consequence of this their deed — which is denial and killing — any trial; that is, that they would not be tried by the enemies being set over them, so they persisted in their transgression.

﴿Fa-ʿamū wa-ṣammū﴾: they were blind to the truth so that they did not see it, and deaf to it so that they did not hear it.

﴿Thumma tāba Allāhu ʿalayhim﴾: after He had shown them some of the punishment, God relented toward them; then they returned, but not all of them returned. Rather, some of them were rid of this trial after which God relented toward them, and some persisted. This is why He said: ﴿Thumma ʿamū wa-ṣammū kathīrun minhum﴾. So the Children of Israel first: they were all blind and deaf; then what? God relented toward them; then they returned, but not all of them returned, but what? Some did — ﴿ʿamū wa-ṣammū kathīrun minhum﴾ — and those who were neither blind nor deaf are few.

﴿Kathīrun minhum wa-Allāhu baṣīrun bi-mā yaʿmalūn﴾. Some scholars said: this is what God mentioned in Surat al-Isrāʾ: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you would surely become excessively haughty (4). So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes; and it was a promise fulfilled (5). Then We gave back to you the return [of victory] over them (6)...﴾ — this is after the repentance — ﴿and provided you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower. If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is for them. So when the promise of the Hereafter came, they would distress your faces and enter the masjid as they entered it the first time and destroy what they had conquered with destruction﴾ [al-Isrāʾ 4–7].

But the context of the verse in al-Isrāʾ does not fit what is in this sūrah. What is in this sūrah is that they killed and denied, and supposed that it would have no effect; but it did have an effect. What was this effect? We do not know; God knows best. After this effect, what happened to them? Many of them became blind and deaf in this trial — meaning blind to the truth and deaf to it, not that their seeing eyes and hearing ears became blind and deaf. Then God relented toward them and granted them guidance; then many of them became blind and deaf again after that. It is not necessary for us to know what God left ambiguous in the Qur'an; what God has left vague in the Qur'an may contain a benefit, and the aim is to know the story as such.

﴿Thumma ʿamū wa-ṣammū kathīrun minhum﴾: ﴿kathīrun minhum﴾ — some people said: it is the subject (fāʿil) of (ʿamiya wa-ṣamma), and the wāw in (ʿamū wa-ṣammū) is a letter indicating plurality only, like it is in your saying: ʿalaykum, ʿalayhim — it is a letter indicating plurality. So the wāw in (ʿamū wa-ṣammū) is a letter indicating plurality, which is contrary to the well-known usage of the Arabic language, and this language is called what? — "akalūnī al-barāghīth" (the fleas ate me). It was also said: the wāw is the subject in (ʿamū wa-ṣammū), and (kathīr) is a substitute for the wāw, a partial substitution from the whole; and this is the closer view: that God first generalized, then substituted for this generalization what? — that they are many; not all of them. And then we say: the noble Qur'an was not in the dialect of what? — "akalūnī al-barāghīth."

﴿Thumma ʿamū wa-ṣammū kathīrun minhum wa-Allāhu baṣīrun bi-mā yaʿmalūn﴾: God's words ﴿wa-Allāhu baṣīrun﴾ — al-baṣīr here may carry two meanings: the first meaning: seeing with the eye, Mighty and Majestic; the second: knowing by knowledge. Both meanings are combined in regard to God, Mighty and Majestic: He is baṣīr of what they do, He sees it and nothing is hidden from Him; and baṣīr of what they do, He knows it. Have you understood? Because the doer may have a body and be seen, or may lack a body and not be seen; and both are known. So we say: baṣīr includes two meanings: baṣīr in the sense of sight, baṣīr in the sense of knowledge. Which is more general?

* Students: Knowledge.

* The Shaykh: The second is more general.

* Benefits of this noble verse: that among the stupidity of the Children of Israel is that they supposed no trial would befall them while they were killing the messengers and denying a group of them; this indicates stupidity, and that their hearts had been sealed — God forbid — so they cannot distinguish between things.

* Among its benefits: a warning against feeling safe from the plotting of God, and that this is a trait of the Jews: that a person feels safe from the plotting of God and supposes that, through his disobedience, no punishment will follow it; based on His saying: ﴿And they supposed there would be no trial﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that God may relent toward a person after his blindness and deafness. From where is this taken, brother?

* A student: ﴿Thumma tāba Allāhu ʿalayhim﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Thumma tāba Allāhu ʿalayhim﴾, after mentioning that they became blind and deaf.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's compassion toward His servants, and that He relents toward whoever repents; or, if you wish, say: He relents toward whomever He wills of His servants, out of His grace and generosity.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that after repentance and the lifting of the trial from him, a person may not give thanks for this blessing and return to his blindness and deafness; based on His saying: ﴿Thumma ʿamū wa-ṣammū kathīrun minhum﴾. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Why, when Our might came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made pleasing to them what they had been doing﴾ [al-Anʿām 43].

* Among them: caution against the insolence toward blessing that comes from returning to wickedness and ingratitude, because God threatened them with His saying: ﴿And Allah is seeing of what they do﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, of every deed; for the word (mā) in ﴿mā yaʿmalūn﴾ is a relative pronoun indicating generality.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 72 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Certainly, those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary," have disbelieved.﴾ ﴿Certainly, they have disbelieved﴾. This is emphasized how many times? It is emphasized three ways: the implied oath, the lam, and (qad). Allah the Exalted emphasized this in keeping with the habit of the Arabic tongue of emphasizing what deserves emphasis. Otherwise, the report of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is true. Moreover, this, ﴿Certainly, those who disbelieved﴾, is not a bare report but a report and a judgment. Even if we say that it is a judgment that they have disbelieved, it is emphasized lest an objector object and say: "This is not disbelief."

﴿Certainly, those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary," have disbelieved.﴾ Who are these? These are the Christians who did not help 'Isa and were not among his disciples (hawariyyun).

﴿They said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ We ask Allah for well-being. The doubt that Satan created for them is that he was created without a father. It is astonishing that they say: Allah is the Messiah son of Mary, then they say: 'Isa son of Mary was born of fornication. So they slander him from one aspect, they slander his mother from one aspect, and they exalt his mother and elevate her from another aspect, according to their claim.

﴿They said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ The word (huwa) is a pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl). The pronoun of separation has three benefits. Who knows them?
* A student: Emphasis.
* The Shaykh: Emphasis.
* The student: And restriction.
* The Shaykh: And restriction.
* The student: And distinguishing between the predicate and the attribute.
* The Shaykh: And distinguishing between the predicate and the attribute. Separation means distinguishing between whether what follows is a predicate or an attribute.

Here, ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary﴾, (huwa) is a pronoun of separation indicating that these people affirmed emphatically that Allah is the Messiah. It indicates the restriction of Allah the Mighty and Majestic to being the Messiah, and that He does not go beyond it. And it indicates what? That "the Messiah" is a predicate and not an attribute.

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.﴾ "The Messiah" is a descriptive title applied to a man who is one of Allah's friends and also to a man who is one of Allah's enemies. The man who is one of Allah's friends is 'Isa son of Mary, and the man who is one of Allah's enemies is the Dajjal. The Prophet (ﷺ) named him "the Messiah" when he commanded us to seek refuge with Allah from the trial of the Messiah al-Dajjal. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (832), and Muslim (589/129) from 'A'isha.] As for the cleverness of some people, meaning seeking to appear clever, and their statement that the Dajjal is called "al-Masikh" with a kha', this is false, because the most knowledgeable of people about him called him "al-Masih." There is no objection to describing this one as "al-Masih" and that one as "al-Masih," but the one who is wiped differs. 'Isa son of Mary would not wipe anyone afflicted with a defect except that he was healed. He healed the blind-born and the leper by Allah's permission. The Messiah al-Dajjal is wiped in the eye, one-eyed, with a repulsive appearance. So distinguish between this and that. Both are "Messiah," derived from "masḥ" (wiping).

His saying: ﴿Mary﴾ is the daughter of 'Imran. He, peace be upon him, was attributed to his mother because he had no father. Allah commanded Jibril to breathe into the womb of Mary a spirit, and he breathed into her a spirit, and he is 'Isa, peace be upon him.

﴿And the Messiah said: "O Children of Israel..."﴾. Regarding his saying ﴿And the Messiah said﴾, its parsing (i'rab) has two possibilities. The first possibility is that it is a circumstantial clause (hal). According to this possibility, the (qad) must be understood, and the meaning is: "Certainly those who said, 'Indeed Allah is the Messiah son of Mary' have disbelieved, and the Messiah had already said: 'O Children of Israel,'" meaning he refuted them. The second possibility is that the waw is a conjunctive, and his saying ﴿said﴾ is conjoined to ﴿disbelieved﴾. Then this sentence is emphasized with three emphases, because it is conjoined to a sentence emphasized with three emphases, and the meaning is: "Certainly those who said, 'Indeed Allah is the Messiah son of Mary' have disbelieved, and certainly the Messiah son of Mary said: 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'" The first interpretation is more eloquent, because the Messiah, who was described as being God, refuted those who described him so. They disbelieved, and he had said to them, and made clear to them, that he, peace be upon him, is a servant. So he said: ﴿O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾

* A student: May Allah bless you. Many of the attributes Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned about the Children of Israel exist among the Children of Israel who are contemporary with us now, such as obstinacy, stubbornness, and so on. But some of the attributes, O Shaykh, that Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned, the Children of Israel who are with us now have deceit, but they are not stupid. They now dominate the world economically, and are even advanced in industries?
* The Shaykh: These, may Allah bless you, are stupid in terms of understanding the truth. They are not stupid in terms of intelligence. Always keep in mind the saying of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, about the theologians (mutakallimun). He said: "They were given understandings but not knowledge, and they were given intelligence but not purity." And recall the saying of Allah the Exalted about the disbelievers despite their being intelligent: ﴿They do not reason.﴾ So these, in reality, are stupid in terms of the Sharia. Even the least ordinary Muslim knows that their saying that 'Isa is Allah is a tremendous ignorance, and for this they were described as misguided.
* A student: Shaykh, we said that Allah mentioned two categories (...) and was silent about the second. Can one not say, O Shaykh: (...)?
* The Shaykh: ﴿A group they denied.﴾
* The student: The verse after it.
* The Shaykh: Meaning they denied the messengers. Some of them denied the messengers and some of them killed.
* The student: The verse after it?
* The Shaykh: After it?
* The student: ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them.﴾
* The Shaykh: After it, which is independent?
* The student: Is it not in the same context?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but independent of it.
* A student: May Allah pardon you. Some exegetes mentioned the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾ [al-Tahrim 12], and said: the meaning of "chastity" here is the collar of the garment?
* The Shaykh: And what is its meaning in the Arabic language?
* The student: It is the well-known private part.
* The Shaykh: The well-known private part. Why do we deviate?
* The student: They said: because...
* The Shaykh: And ﴿she guarded her chastity﴾ is a problem? Meaning: she guarded only the collar of the garment? And the real private part?
* The student: He said: this is from the eloquence of the Quran.
* The Shaykh: No, not at all. This is from the foolishness of the man. Now, ﴿We breathed into her of Our spirit﴾. It might be said: it is not necessary that Jibril, peace be upon him, opened her garment and breathed into the private part itself. It is not necessary. He may have breathed through the collar and it reached the private part. But the path of conception is the private part, without doubt, not the collar.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. The hadith in Sahih Muslim that the Prophet (ﷺ) "saw the Messiah al-Dajjal circumambulating the House," [Muslim (169/273) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, in which it says: "He showed me on a night at the Ka'bah. I saw a man, brown-skinned, as the best of what you see of brown-skinned men, with hair as the best of what you see of hair, having combed it so that it dripped with water, leaning on two men, or on the shoulders of two men, circumambulating the House. I asked: Who is this? It was said: This is the Messiah son of Mary. Then behold, a man with curly hair, one-eyed, the right eye like a floating grape. I asked: Who is this? It was said: This is the Messiah al-Dajjal."] What is said about this hadith, given that the Messiah al-Dajjal is the most barren of the earth?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. It is said: I do not know what the aspect of this hadith is, because the two visions are one. But the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not see him in reality, because the Dajjal will come after the messengers at a later time, and he is prohibited from entering Makkah. That is why Ibn Sayyad argued that he is not the Dajjal, since he was in Madinah and went to Makkah.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah pardon you. Is every attribute established as an attribute of the Jews or Christians in the Book or the Sunnah permanently theirs until the Day of Resurrection, or must there be evidence that it continues?
* The Shaykh: As for their deeds, they do not continue. That is, what has been mentioned of their deeds may have been at the time the Quran was revealed, or before them, of what those present at the time of the Quran's revelation knew, and it changes. Just as now, the religion of the Children of Israel that they follow is not the religion brought by 'Isa or Musa.
* The student: What is an example of the deeds, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: What are examples of the deeds?
* The Shaykh: Their deeds?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Read what they now have of the books that have been authored, and you will find that they contradict what Allah related of their deeds.
* A student: Regarding His saying: ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾, could the meaning here, O Shaykh, be those who came after the sending of the Messenger (ﷺ), that the truth was established against them, especially since He said "then"?
* The Shaykh: Perhaps this, or also what came before it. Perhaps this, or also before it, refers to some of the Children of Israel upon whom the enemy was given power, or whom drought and famine and other things afflicted.
* A student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. We took from the benefits that the Children of Israel broke their covenant with Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, so some people are deceived. Could this covenant extend, and can we say that one should not make covenants about new matters?
* The Shaykh: That is not correct. The Messenger made a covenant with them when he arrived in Madinah, and a written agreement was made between him and them, but they broke the covenant.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Certainly, those who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary," have disbelieved. And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 72].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Certainly, Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel.﴾ So what is the covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel?
* A student: The covenant is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised from them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them..."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 12]. This is one saying, and some scholars said: the covenant is what Allah instilled in their nature of monotheism toward Him.
* The Shaykh: Good, you are correct. His saying: ﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾, like whom?
* A student: Like 'Isa and Musa.
* The Shaykh: How? Was Musa and 'Isa sent to the Children of Israel? Answer.
* The student: Musa...
* The Shaykh: And 'Isa.
* The student: And 'Isa, peace be upon him...
* The Shaykh: Both were sent to the Children of Israel?
* The student: Yes, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Are you certain?
* The student: 'Isa, yes.
* The Shaykh: And Musa?
* The student: No, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: What is your evidence?
* The student: In the verse: ﴿Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of Dawud and 'Isa son of Mary, that is because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 78].
* The Shaykh: Why did you bring this, and not something more suitable and better than this, better regarding the Children of Israel?
* The student: I brought it to mind.
* A student: Among them is His saying about 'Isa: ﴿And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel"﴾, the verse, and about Musa, the saying of the Mighty and Majestic about Musa to Pharaoh: ﴿Send with us the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 17].
* The Shaykh: And in Surah al-Saff.
* The student: "O Children of Israel..."
* The Shaykh: He mentioned this and that.

And His saying: ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed﴾. It is well known that (kullama)?
* A student: Conditional. (Kullama) is conditional.
* The Shaykh: Conditional.
* The student: It indicates repetition.
* The Shaykh: It indicates repetition. Where is its condition and where is its response?
* The student: The condition is ﴿a messenger came to them﴾, and the response of the condition is ﴿a group they denied﴾, this is the response of the condition.
* The Shaykh: And it was said?
* The student: It was said: there is an omitted verb whose estimation is "they disobeyed," and this is not needed.
* The Shaykh: Because the sentence is sound without it.
What is the wisdom in His saying: ﴿a group they denied and a group they killed﴾, where He used the past tense for denial and the present tense for killing?
* A student: It indicates continuity, and that if a messenger came to them after that, they would kill him. Indeed the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they attempted to kill him with the poisoned sheep offered to him.
* The Shaykh: His saying the Exalted: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾ has two readings. What are they?
* A student: ﴿Allā takūna﴾ and ﴿Allā takūnu﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Allā takūna﴾ with a fatha on the nun.
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And ﴿Allā takūnu﴾.
* The student: With a damma.
* The Shaykh: With a damma. What is the justification for the two readings?
* The student: That if it is the light form (mukhaffafah)...
* A student: Me, Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: It has two readings, ﴿Allā takūna﴾ and ﴿Allā takūnu﴾.
* The Shaykh: The justification for the two readings, because this answer was given by your colleague.
* The student: On the reading with the fatha, (an) is verbal-source (masdariyyah) and (la) is negation, and (takūna) is a present-tense verb in the subjunctive governed by the verbal-source (an). On the reading ﴿Allā takūnu﴾, (an) is the lightened form of the heavy (an), and its subject is the pronoun of the matter and (takūnu) is its predicate.
* The Shaykh: Is what he said correct?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: In the course of the discussion of the justification of the two readings, did we point to a rule about (an)?
* A student: I said: if knowledge precedes it, the nominative is required...
* The Shaykh: The nominative, and that (an) is lightened...
* The student: Lightened from the heavy.
* The Shaykh: Excellent.
* The student: And if supposition precedes it, there are two possibilities: the nominative and the accusative, like this verse. And if neither knowledge nor supposition is established, the accusative is required...
* The Shaykh: It is required that it be verbal-source, so it governs the accusative. May Allah bless you.
Give an example of where the accusative is required?
* A student: His saying the Exalted: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾ [al-Isra' 8].
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: Is the accusative not required?
* The Shaykh: The one after it, no.
* A student: O Shaykh, I like it from a student that he does not argue with you.
* The Shaykh: I like it from a student that he does not argue with you. Is it not permissible to say: "lā yujādilu" (with damma)?
Good. And its example after knowledge?
* A student: This verse.
* The Shaykh: No, this one does not indicate knowledge, and therefore neither the accusative nor the nominative is required in it.
* A student: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word?﴾ [Ta-Ha 89].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word?﴾ And its example after supposition, where two possibilities are permitted?
* A student: The verse, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Which verse?
* The student: The one after it, ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾, correct.
What is the trial that they thought would not occur?
* A student: It is better to say: the text remains with two possibilities.
* The Shaykh: Yes. And what is the trial?
* The student: The enemies being empowered over them.
* The Shaykh: In more general terms: any punishment by which they are chastised, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And fear a trial﴾, meaning a punishment, ﴿which will not strike those among you who have wronged in particular﴾ [al-Anfal 25].
There is a difficulty in the verse regarding His saying: ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them.﴾ What is it?
* A student: The difficulty is the presence of...
* The Shaykh: What is the difficulty?
* The student: The presence of two subjects...
* The Shaykh: Two subjects for one verb? Good, what is the answer?
