Therefore, when the truth becomes clear to you, do not argue. Do not try to go right and left to justify your opinion. You are in danger. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾ [Qaf 50:5]: mixed up, the truth becomes confused for them with falsehood. When they deny the truth when it comes to them, pay attention to this benefit, you who are a student of knowledge. Some people may oppose you in accordance with evidence, but you want to impose your opinion. This is a great error. Follow the truth wherever it is, and people will follow you wherever you are, because people seek the truth. When they see that whenever the truth becomes clear to you, you return to it, they return too.

So humility before the truth is in reality exaltation, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is humble for the sake of Allah, He raises him,"[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (8307), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (7790), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]] and its opposite is arrogance. Arrogance, may Allah protect us, makes a person unwilling to accept the truth and unwilling to follow it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of these people who believe in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that ﴿when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears﴾. There is no doubt that their eyes overflowing with tears is evidence of what? Of faith, belief, and being affected. Because whenever a person believes, he increases in humility.

Now, if you remember your fathers, brothers, and friends who have passed away and died, you may weep more than if you remembered something else believed in, because these you experienced through the senses. As faith grows stronger, the believer becomes as if he sees the thing with his own eye, so his faith, humility, and weeping increase.

Let us take the benefits of the individual words. Among the benefits of His saying: ﴿what has been revealed to the Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:83] is that the Qur'an came from Allah, because this is in the passive form, ﴿has been revealed﴾, since its agent is known: it is Allah who revealed it.

From this is derived that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and that is so. He spoke it, the Glorified and Exalted, in truth, speaking it in an audible manner. Who heard it? Jibril heard it, and he is trustworthy and strong. He descended with it upon the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, who retained and understood it, until his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, said to him: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:16–17]. It will never be scattered; it is gathered for you. ﴿So when We have recited it﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:18], meaning Jibril recited it, ﴿then follow its recitation. Then indeed upon Us is its clarification﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:18–19].

These are great commitments from Allah the Mighty and Majestic regarding this Qur'an, which show Allah's care for it, Glorified and Exalted. ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its clarification﴾: We clarify it for the people in wording and in meaning. That is why we say: there cannot be in the Book of Allah anything whose meaning people do not know. If its knowledge is hidden from some, others know it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the highlighting of the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, from His saying: ﴿the Messenger﴾, because the definite article here is *al-'ahd al-dhihni* (the mental reference), meaning as if it is a known and understood messenger, not hidden from anyone.

Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood, and that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, whom Allah sent as a mercy to the worlds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:107].

Among the benefits of this noble verse: we say, is it praiseworthy to praise the one who weeps upon hearing the Qur'an? Yes, we say it is praiseworthy to praise the one who weeps upon hearing the Qur'an. But know that weeping is of two kinds: artificial, contrived weeping, which is of no benefit, just as applying kohl to the eyes is not the same as the eyes being truly sore; and the other weeping, which comes from softness of heart. This is the beneficial kind, because it proceeds from the heart, from faith.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the effect upon these people was due to their knowing the truth. That is why He said: ﴿for what they recognized of the truth﴾. The more a person knows the truth, the more his faith in it increases, and the more he is affected by it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿They say: Our Lord, we have believed﴾ and so on to the end.

Among the benefits of this sentence: praise of those who believed in what was sent down to the Messenger ﷺ, that they proclaim their faith, ﴿they say: Our Lord, we have believed﴾. They do not conceal their faith, because they are believers, and a believer in truth proclaims his faith, especially when they are priests and monks, because they are examples for the people.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the acknowledgment by the nations that this Ummah is the witness over the nations, from His saying: ﴿so write us among the witnesses﴾. They are the Ummah of Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:143].

**Student:** Our explanation of His saying: ﴿nearest in affection﴾: can it be inferred from the verse that the Christians are enemies of the Muslims, and that they are the opposite of what people understand today?

**Shaykh:** Yes indeed. We mentioned this so that it is not misunderstood. Their saying ﴿nearest in affection﴾ does not mean they entered into affection, nor that they have affection. Otherwise it would have said: "strongest in affection."

**Student:** Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Steadfastness: if the heart is hard, a person recites the Qur'an and perhaps finds no softness, so he feigns weeping. If we say it is of no benefit, Shaykh, perhaps feigning weeping softens his heart.

**Shaykh:** No, no. This is not feigning. Feigned weeping is different from artificial weeping. Some people do not weep, but make their voice sound as if they are weeping, while they are not weeping.

**Student:** That is ostentation (*riya'*).

**Shaykh:** That is it.

**Student:** May Allah honor you, Shaykh. The problem, Shaykh, is the difference between humility (*tawadu'*) and condescension (*taraffu'*). Some people, for example, when they relax with the common people, may be belittled in their eyes, especially if he is a student of knowledge or a scholar. Should he then avoid relaxing?

**Shaykh:** This is a misconception; it is not correct. I am not saying: be humble to the common people, bring them your shoes and lower your back for them to ride on. No. But meet them with a cheerful face and generosity, because some people, even among students of knowledge, you find them speaking to a commoner through one nostril, not with the whole nose, and looking down. We cannot say anything. Be humble, my brother. People now praise the man who is humble. We hear them praising so-and-so because he is humble. But that does not mean you make yourself abased before them. No. Humility is not abasement.

**Student:** Shaykh, may Allah bless you. What is the minimum that a student of knowledge should not fall short of in worship?

**Shaykh:** I think the minimum regarding prayer is the five daily prayers with their sunnah prayers, the witr, and what has its own causes. Likewise regarding spending wealth, the zakat and charity.

**Student:** And the daily portion of the Qur'an?

**Shaykh:** What do you mean by a daily portion of the Qur'an? That he recites some of the Qur'an? I might say: according to his energy. But I fear that saying this makes a person lax, because if he recites according to his energy, one day he recites perhaps two or three parts, and another day he recites nothing, and time is wasted. That is why the scholars said: he should have a fixed portion that he is keen to maintain. I think two parts a day, God willing, carry blessing. If he recites two parts every day, he completes the Qur'an twice a month. That is a blessing.

**Student:** Fasting?

**Shaykh:** The Prophet did not fast constantly. But sometimes a person loves fasting, and it was of the guidance of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that he would fast so much that it was said: "He never breaks his fast," and break it so much that it was said: "He never fasts."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1969) and Muslim (1156/175), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] But the thing we should be constant upon is fasting three days of every month, because the Messenger did not neglect fasting three days of every month,[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1981) and Muslim (721/85), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] and he did not mind whether he fasted them at the beginning, middle, or end of the month.

**Student:** May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. How do we reconcile Allah's mention, relating the statement of these people, with the Qur'an being inimitable (*mu'jiz*)?

**Shaykh:** What is the contradiction?

**Student:** That they said it. Someone might say that their statement is inimitable.

**Shaykh:** Their statement is inimitable?! No, there is no problem with this. The brother is saying: how can we say they spoke with this wording? They did not speak with this wording. The Qur'an relates the statements of others by meaning. That is why look at the statement of the magicians: ﴿They said: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun﴾ [al-A'raf 7:121–122], and in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿They said: We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:70]. The statement is one, but Allah mentioned Harun first in Surah Ta-Ha for the sake of the harmony of the verses. So everything Allah relates about earlier people is by meaning, because we know they did not speak in Arabic; their language is not Arabic, and their word order is not like the order of the Qur'an, as far as we know, and Allah knows best. It may be said that Allah related their statement, but He formulated it, Glorified and Exalted, or spoke of it as He willed.

**Student:** Shaykh, may Allah be good to you: is devoting oneself to worship and seeking knowledge, and leaving employment, appropriate if wealth is available?

**Shaykh:** If he has what suffices him, then devoting himself is undoubtedly better, unless the position requires his presence, because some positions need the person, such as judicial posts, notaries, and many other things. A person must consider the public interests.

**Student:** Regarding His saying: ﴿so write us among the witnesses﴾, can it be derived from it that the general meaning is following?

**Shaykh:** No. Do you mean absolute companionship?

**Student:** General following.

**Shaykh:** Why?

**Student:** Because of what the messengers brought.

**Shaykh:** "Write us with them," meaning: we will do as they do.

**Student:** Those who deny the speech of Allah say the Qur'an is not the speech of Allah, but is an expression of the speech of Allah. What is the meaning of this statement, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** They say: Allah the Glorified and Exalted did not speak it, but created sounds to express what is in His self, and Jibril heard them and descended with them. This is a statement without knowledge. In reality, if you reflect upon their words, you will arrive at the conclusion that Allah is nothing: He does not speak, does not ascend over the Throne, does not descend, does not come to judge between His servants, does not rejoice, has no hand, has no face, has no eye. O Allah, to You be praise. We ask Allah for guidance.

[Note: the passage given is not solely a translation source in the usual sense; I translate it as instructed.]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verses 82–85 (part 4 of 5):

* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of the Blazing Fire. O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors. And eat of what Allah has provided for you as lawful and good, and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 86–88].
* Shaykh: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: as we began last week, we resolved to start with some of the rules of tafsir (qawa'id al-tafsir). This is good, but it requires you to record the rule we discussed, so that it is not repeated, since we do not have a book in front of us to read from, and so we are safe from repetition. Last week we spoke of rules in...?
* Student: Interpreting a verse by its content (tafsir al-ayah bil-mudmun).
* Shaykh: To where do we return in tafsir?
* Student: The first rule we discussed was whether it (tafsir) is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) or a collective obligation (fard kifayah). We mentioned the detail: what the person's religion cannot stand without is an individual obligation, so every Muslim must know its tafsir; anything beyond that is a collective obligation. This is the first rule.
The second rule is: by what is the tafsir of the Qur'an effected? We mentioned three divisions. The first division: tafsir of the Qur'an by the Qur'an; when this is present, there is no turning away from it, because the speaker of the Qur'an is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He is most knowing of His intent. The second level: tafsir of the Qur'an by the Sunnah, because the Messenger ﷺ is the most knowledgeable of creation about the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The third: tafsir of the Qur'an by the statements of the early generations (salaf), because the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, are the most aware of people of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said.
* Shaykh: The fourth: tafsir according to the requirements of the Arabic language. Is there anything else?
* Student: Observing the meaning?
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: Like His saying, Exalted is He (...). Is it better to pause at...?
* Shaykh: No, pausing and continuing (al-waqf wal-wasl) is not part of tafsir.
* Student: We mentioned that the best method in tafsir is that a person interprets by himself and tries to derive the meanings.
* Shaykh: Yes, this is also important: that a person tries to know the meaning of the Qur'an by himself first, then after that returns to what the exegetes said. This does not mean that he should adopt what he himself has seen, but he forms a meaning in his own mind, then returns to the statements of the exegetes, so that he does not go astray. But if he reads the statements of the exegetes only in a cursory reading, as if he were a child being suckled by a wet nurse, he will not benefit the desired benefit.
Now tonight it is about abrogation (naskh). We are now speaking about naskh: can abrogation occur in the Qur'an or not? It is said: the correct view is that it is possible, abrogation can occur, and it has actually occurred; this is what the majority of the Ummah holds, and we are not concerned with those who deny it. For example, the Jews said: abrogation of the laws (shara'i') is impossible, because if we permit abrogation we would permit al-bada' (a change of view) for Allah, meaning that a benefit appears to Him after it had been hidden from Him, so He rules on something and then turns away from it, because He did not know the consequences of what He had first decreed.
It is known that it is not permissible for a person to describe his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, with ignorance and then al-bada'. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refuted them, saying: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed﴾ [Ali 'Imran 93]. So He made clear that abrogation occurs, and it is so. Because of their denial of abrogation, they denied the prophethood of 'Isa and the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, and they said: their two laws abrogated the law of the Torah, and this is not permissible.
The Muslims are in agreement on the permissibility of abrogation rationally, and its occurrence according to the Sharia, except that Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, may Allah have mercy on him, said: there is no abrogation in the Qur'an, and he interpreted the abrogation established in the Qur'an as specification (takhsis).
An example of this: Allah obligated the Muslims in jihad that one should endure against ten. Then that was abrogated and He said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened it for you﴾ [Al-Anfal 66]. It is clear that this is abrogation. Likewise in the hadith: «I had forbidden you to visit graves, so visit them» [Muslim (977/106) from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb]. This too is clear abrogation, established by the Qur'an itself and the Sunnah itself.
He, may Allah have mercy on him, claimed that this is specification and not abrogation, and he justified his statement by saying: the abrogated ruling was general in all times and in all circumstances, then it was abrogated, so the period in which it remains was excluded by the abrogation, and he said: this is specification.
Based on this justification, the disagreement between him and the majority of the Ummah becomes a verbal disagreement with no benefit in it, since we agree that this general ruling could be, in every time, every place, every nation and every situation, something that may be cancelled at some point in time. This is abrogation; call it specification or call it abrogation.
Then it is said to him, may Allah have mercy on him: what is the benefit of avoiding the word "abrogation" when Allah, the Exalted, says in the Qur'an: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 106].
Returning to the rational permissibility of abrogation: its occurrence according to the Sharia is beyond doubt. But how is it rationally permissible? Is it not permissible that what the Jews raised be refuted? That Allah would manifest a view after it had been hidden from Him, that the ruling is abrogated, is not sound?
The answer: No. Rulings are established according to the conditions of nations. Obligation, for instance, may be a benefit for the nation at one time and not a benefit at another time, is that not so?
And abrogation may be for testing the mukallaf (the responsible person): Allah tests him, whether he complies or does not comply, and then abrogation comes; because some people may not accept abrogation, like those who apostatized when the qiblah was changed, because they said: how can we face Bayt al-Maqdis yesterday and now face the Ka'bah? It is impossible. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels﴾ [Al-Baqarah 143]. This suffices as wisdom.
So if changing and abrogating a ruling has wisdoms, it does not follow that al-bada' is imposed on Allah, because He, glorified and exalted, legislates for His servants rulings through which the interests of their religion and their worldly life are served. Consider: if you assigned your son a task, then you saw that this task was hard for him, is it in his interest to keep him in this hard task, or to move him to another task? You move him to another task; this is what reason requires. Then what the Jews claimed is nullified, that it entails al-bada' upon Allah, meaning manifestation after concealment.
Thus abrogation is rationally permissible and occurs according to the Sharia. Then abrogation occurs in three ways: abrogation of the ruling while the wording remains, abrogation of the wording while the ruling remains, and abrogation of both together: three divisions.
The first: abrogation of the ruling with the wording remaining. This is common, like the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [Al-Baqarah 149]. This is abrogation, why? For the first qiblah. Does the wording remain or not? It remains; because Allah said: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah which you will like. So turn your face﴾ [Al-Baqarah 144]. And like the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, about fasting: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves, so He turned to you and pardoned you. So now have relations with them and seek what Allah has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread at dawn. Then complete the fast until night﴾ [Al-Baqarah 187]. And like His saying concerning the verse on steadfastness against the enemy, that Allah obligated the Muslims to endure against ten times their number, then that was abrogated. This is abrogation of what? Abrogation of the ruling with the wording remaining.
Here a question arises: what is the benefit of abrogating the ruling while the wording remains? Why was the wording not abrogated, since the action by the wording has ended? It is said: the benefit regarding the Qur'an is, first: increase in reward through recitation; and second: reminding the servants of Allah's blessing upon them, in that He moved them from the harder to the lighter, or the reverse, or to an equivalent; but the main point is reminding them of the blessing.
The second division is the reverse of this matter: abrogation of the wording with the ruling remaining. Its example is the verse of stoning. The verse of stoning was a Qur'an that was recited.
'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «We read it and we understood it, and the Prophet ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6829), Muslim (1691/15)]. So it was present in the Qur'an. Where is its wording? It is not present. There is nothing in the Qur'an that a married person (thayyib) who commits adultery is stoned. So the wording is not present, I mean the abrogated wording. And the abrogating wording? Is the abrogating text present or not? ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, lash each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [An-Nur 2]; and the thayyib came in the Sunnah. So here the verse of stoning is not in the Qur'an; its wording is not present.
What is the verse that was abrogated? It is reported that its wording was: "The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them absolutely as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty and Wise" [Ahmad (21207) from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b]. But this is not authentic; this wording does not match the ruling, because the ruling depends on what? On being thayyib (previously married), not on being old. And 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, says: «Indeed stoning is a established truth in the Book of Allah for whoever commits adultery when he is muhsan (married and free), if there is pregnancy or confession» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6829), Muslim (1691/15)].
So his saying: it is an established truth in the Qur'an for whoever commits adultery when he is muhsan, he did not say: when he is old; he said: when he is muhsan. It becomes clear that the wording of the abrogated verse is not as it was narrated; and for this reason, if an old man commits adultery while he is a virgin, he is not stoned, and if a young man commits adultery while he is thayyib, he is stoned. So the verse is of unknown wording, but we know it is a wording indicating what 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned.
If someone says: what is the wisdom in abrogating the wording while the ruling remains? Because we mentioned that the remaining of the wording has a benefit, which is recitation; but here what is the benefit? The benefit, and Allah knows best, is that the virtue of this Ummah over those before it becomes manifest. The Jews tried to hide the verse of stoning, although it is present in the Torah, but they abandoned acting upon it, and the reason for abandoning it was that adultery spread among their nobles, and it was difficult for them to kill their nobles, so they invented an unjust ruling not in the Sharia of Allah.
This Ummah, praise be to Allah, acted upon a ruling whose text is not present, so it manifested the ruling despite the hiddenness of the evidence; while the Jews, on the contrary, nullified the ruling despite the presence of the evidence. This is what became clear of the wisdom.
It may be said that there is another wisdom, which is: the heinousness of the crime, because adultery by a thayyib is undoubtedly heinous, and worse than adultery by a young unmarried man; and for this reason its punishment is stoning, unlike the non-muhsan.
The latter: a person hesitates whether this is the wisdom, because he would say: this is the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and this is difficult; because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned what is more heinous than this, which is intercourse with males, sodomy, explicitly: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 165, 166].
But the first aspect, which is showing the virtue of this Ummah over those before it, is clear.
The third division remains: abrogation of both the wording and the ruling. This has an example, which is the hadith of 'A'ishah concerning nursing: «There was revealed ten known sucklings that make marriage prohibited, then they were abrogated by five known sucklings» [Muslim (1452/24)]. Now you do not find ten sucklings, neither in the Qur'an nor in the ruling; acting upon ten sucklings is abrogated, until five. The five is abrogated in wording but not in ruling, and the ten is abrogated in wording and ruling.
There are other divisions of abrogation too, but time has run short on us; we will postpone them, God willing, to the next lesson.
* * *
Returning to our lesson. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and that is the reward of the doers of good﴾. Its discussion and its benefits have already passed.
Allah the Exalted said about these Christians who embraced Islam: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah﴾ to the end.
* From the benefits of this verse: repelling blame from oneself. A person should repel blame from himself, and not expose his honour to the servants of Allah who do whatever they wish with it. And for this there is a basis in the Sunnah: when the Prophet ﷺ stood to accompany one of his wives, Safiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, after she had stayed with him, he stood to walk with her, and two men of the Ansar passed by him. When they saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his wife, they were embarrassed and hurried. So he said to them: «Slow down, both of you; she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy». They said: Subhan Allah, meaning it is impossible that anything would enter our hearts. He said to them: «Indeed Satan flows through the son of Adam like blood, and I feared that he might cast into your hearts evil» or he said: «something» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2035), Muslim (2175/24) from the hadith of Safiyyah bint Huyayy].
* From the benefits of this noble verse also, in its second aspect in His saying: ﴿And why should we not believe﴾: urging the soul, when whisperings occur, toward faith and righteous deeds. That is, if you see in yourself slackness, strengthen it, strengthen its resolve; because we mentioned in His saying: ﴿And why should we not believe﴾ two possibilities.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Messenger ﷺ brought is true, by the testimony of those who preceded from the nations; by His saying: ﴿And what has come to us of the truth﴾.
Is the testimony of the earlier nations relied upon? The answer: Yes, it is relied upon; by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who read the Book before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord﴾ [Yunus 94].
* From the benefits of this noble verse: a person should not be self-admiring regarding his deeds, so that he testifies for himself that he is among the people of Paradise; by their saying: ﴿And we hope that our Lord will admit us﴾, and they did not affirm that with certainty.
For this reason, whatever righteous deed you do that is based on faith, do not purify yourself; you do not know, perhaps there is a secret in the heart that you do not perceive—may Allah protect us and you from hypocrisy: «Indeed a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is among the people of the Fire» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2898), Muslim (112/179) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd].
Can we take from this that no one is testified to be in Paradise merely for being a believer who does righteous deeds? Yes, it is possible; and for this reason it is from the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah that we do not testify for anyone to Paradise except those whom the Messenger ﷺ testified for.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that choosing a righteous companion is to be sought; by His saying: ﴿And we hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people﴾. This is a matter the Sunnah indicates clearly: the Prophet ﷺ said: «The likeness of the good companion is like the carrier of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find from him a pleasant fragrance» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534), Muslim (2628/146) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari].
Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿So Allah rewarded them﴾ to the end.
* In this noble verse: the manifestation of the grace of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He rewarded those upon whom He bestowed faith with this great reward.
* And from its benefits: affirmation of causes (asbab); by His saying: ﴿for what they said, gardens﴾.

If someone says: how do we reconcile this noble verse and its like with the Prophet's ﷺ saying, "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds," and they said, "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (2816 / 75) from Abu Hurayrah.]]. Here he negated that anyone enters Paradise by his deeds, although the texts are many that a person enters Paradise by his deeds?

The answer is: the particle "bi" (الباء, the letter "ba'") sometimes denotes causation (sababiyyah) and sometimes denotes exchange (ʿiwad). When you say, "I sold you this garment for a dirham" (بعت عليك هذا الثوب بدرهم), the "bi" denotes exchange, and it cannot denote causation. When you say, "I honoured you for what you honoured me with" (أكرمتك بما أكرمتني), it denotes causation. What is negated is that the "bi" in "by his deeds" denotes exchange: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds" means that it is impossible for deeds to be like the dirham in relation to the garment in a sale. This is impossible, because if Allah, glorified and exalted, were to call us to account for our deeds, then one single blessing of His would encompass all our deeds. Indeed, our being granted success in righteous deeds, O brothers, is itself a blessing that requires gratitude.

Therefore, our entry into Paradise _and I ask Allah to admit me and you into it_ cannot be an exchange for deeds, but it is a cause. With this reconciliation the difficulty disappears. Know that a contradiction can never occur between the texts of the Book and the Sunnah at all. Either there is no contradiction, or the appearance of contradiction arises from the understanding of the one who derives the evidence. As for a contradiction existing between the words of Allah, some with others, or between the words of Allah and what is authentically established from the Sunnah of the Messenger, or between the sayings of the Messenger some with others, this is impossible.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of Paradise and that it consists of kinds, based on His saying: ﴿gardens﴾ (جَنَّاتٍ).

* Among its benefits: that Paradise has rivers flowing beneath these palaces and trees, and a person cannot truly imagine that magnificent, delightful and joyful scene, because Paradise surpasses what we can perceive. As Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is in the Qur'an. And as He, exalted, said: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to a human heart"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3244) and Muslim (2824 / 2) from Abu Hurayrah.]]. This is in a hadith qudsi (ḥadīth qudsī, a hadith in which the meaning is from Allah and the wording is the Prophet's ﷺ, or a report of Allah's words outside the Qur'an).

* Among the benefits of this verse: that the rivers in Paradise are of various kinds, from the plural: ﴿the rivers﴾ (الْأَنْهَارُ), and we have already passed the explanation of their kinds.

* Among its benefits: that the bliss of Paradise is everlasting, based on His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾ (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا). We have established that khulud (الخلود, eternity) is not merely a long stay; it is a permanent stay, unless there is evidence otherwise.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the encouragement to excellence (ihsan), based on His saying: ﴿That is the reward of the good-doers﴾ (وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ). Ihsan is in worshipping Allah and in being good to the servants of Allah. "Do not belittle any act of kindness, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face"[[Narrated by Muslim (2626 / 144) from Abu Dharr.]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exalted status of this reward, based on His saying: ﴿That﴾ (وَذَلِكَ), where He referred to it with a demonstrative used for the distant.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah. And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests (qissisin) and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses." And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord admit us among the righteous people?" Then Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the reward of the doers of good. And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Hellfire.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 82–86]

* **The Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity…﴾. I think we have already explained this.

In any case, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah.﴾ His words ﴿You will surely find﴾: this sentence is emphasized by three emphatic elements. The first is the implied oath, indicated by the lam in His words ﴿la-tajidanna﴾. This is why the grammarians call this lam "the preparatory lam for the oath." The second is the lam itself, and the third is the nun (of emphasis) in ﴿la-tajidanna﴾. The address in it is either to the Messenger (ﷺ). In that case, the discussion in this verse about the Jews, Christians, and polytheists refers to those who lived in the time of whom? The Messenger (ﷺ). Or the address is to everyone to whom the address is directed, in which case these attributes are general for these people until the Day of Resurrection. So the verse admits both readings. Even if we say it is general, it does not encompass every single Jew, every single Christian, and every single polytheist. Rather, this judgment is in the manner of generalization.

Rulings always come in the manner of generalization. You say, "Men are better than women," meaning this category is better than that category. Yet among women there are some who are better than many men, and among men there are some who are worse than many women.

So the address may be to whom? To the Messenger (ﷺ). In that case the ruling applies specifically to those who came after the Messenger (ﷺ). It may also be general, and the intended meaning is the category, not each individual.

﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews﴾. In ﴿ashadda﴾ it is permissible for it to be the second object placed first, and it is also permissible for it to be the first object. According to the first, the sense is: "You will surely find the Jews and those who associated partners with Allah to be the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe." This is if we make ﴿ashadda﴾ the first object. If we make it the second, it comes first. Pay attention: ﴿the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe﴾ may have ﴿ashadda﴾ as the first object, and the meaning is then an information about the most intense of people in enmity. It may also be that ﴿ashadda﴾ is the second object, and the meaning is an information about these two groups, the Jews and the Christians, that they are the most intense of people in enmity. Which of these is greater? Should we make ﴿ashadda﴾ the first object and ﴿the Jews and those who associated partners﴾ the second object? Or the reverse? The first is stronger. That is, if you asked about the most intense of people in enmity, you would find them to be whom? The Jews and those who associated partners.

So we say: ﴿ashadda﴾ is the first object and it occupies the position of the subject, because (wajada, "to find") takes two objects whose original form is subject and predicate. In that case its meaning is information about the most intense of people in enmity. If we make ﴿ashadda﴾ the second object placed first, the meaning becomes information about the Jews and those who associated partners, that they are the most intense of people in enmity. But the first meaning is stronger and greater.

﴿the most intense of people in enmity﴾. Enmity is the opposite of allegiance (wilayah). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel evil with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend﴾ [Fussilat 34]. That is, a sincere friend. So enmity is the opposite of what? The opposite of allegiance.

His words ﴿to those who believe﴾ mean the believers in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), if we make the address to whom? To the Messenger (ﷺ). If we make it general, the intended meaning is those who believe at every time. The Jews are those who claim to be followers of Moses. They say, "We are the chosen people of Allah," and they despise all other peoples. They were known for arrogance, haughtiness, and insolence, even toward their prophet Moses, peace be upon him. They were called Jews (Yahud). It has been said that the name is derived from His words, ﴿Those who are Jews﴾ [al-Baqarah 62], and their saying, ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf 156]. It has also been said that it is the name of their forefather, and that his name was Yahudha, but with Arabization the dhal became a dal.

Whatever the case, they are well known. They are a group from the Children of Israel who claim to be followers of whom? Of Moses.

﴿And those who associated partners﴾: those who associated partners among the Arabs and others. These two categories of the children of Adam are the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers. As for the Jews, the reason for their enmity is that they envied the Arabs because the universal, eternal message was among them. The Jews had previously sought victory over those who disbelieved, saying, "A prophet will be sent, and we will follow him and be victorious over you." When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent from among the Arabs, they envied them and denied that. As for those who associated partners, they are the polytheists, and they became the most intense of people in enmity because they are opposed to monotheism (tawhid). The believers are monotheists, and the polytheist hates and detests the monotheist and considers him the most intense of enemies to him.

He said: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians."﴾ ﴿You will surely find﴾: we say about it what we said about the first.

Here He said ﴿the nearest of them in affection﴾ and did not say "the most affectionate of them," meaning that there is no affection in them. Rather, they are nearer. About the Jews He said ﴿the most intense of people in enmity﴾, but about these He said ﴿the nearest of them in affection﴾. It is known that nearness is not the same as arrival. So they do not have affection for the believers, I mean the Christians, but they are nearer in affection than others. Had they had affection, He would have said "the most affectionate of people" or something similar.

﴿Affection﴾ (mawaddah) comes from wadd, which is pure love. Among the names of Allah is al-Wadud, meaning the one who loves and the one who is loved.

﴿Those who say, "We are Christians"﴾: we say about it grammatically what we said about ﴿ashadda﴾.

﴿Those who say, "We are Christians"﴾, especially in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Christians in the time of the Messenger, peace be upon him, were near to the believers, and for this reason a great many of them embraced Islam. Among those who embraced Islam was the king of Abyssinia, may Allah have mercy on him. He believed in the Messenger, peace be upon him, and sheltered the emigrants from among his Companions, a shelter for which he is to be thanked. We ask Allah to reward him with the fullest reward. He believed, so much so that the Prophet, peace be upon him, described him as a brother to the Companions and as righteous when he died. He said: «Indeed, a righteous brother of yours has died today.»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3877), and Muslim (952/65), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, with similar wording.]] So he described him with righteousness and brotherhood. May Allah have mercy on him.

Likewise, many Christians embraced Islam, because the Christians were closer in time to the message than the Jews. Between their prophet, Jesus, peace be upon him, and our prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) there was no other messenger.

﴿Those who say, "We are Christians"﴾: the Christians are the Ansar (helpers). This is the best thing said in tafsir, because it is supported by His words in Surat as-Saff: ﴿Who are my helpers for Allah? The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 52]. Then Allah the Exalted gave reasons for that: ﴿That﴾, the referent being the nearness of the Christians in affection to those who believe, ﴿is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. And why should we not believe in Allah…"﴾ These are five things.

﴿That﴾: that is, what? That is, the cause of their being the nearest of people in affection to those who believe ﴿is because among them are priests and monks﴾. The qissis (priest) is the great scholar. The scholar has knowledge, knows the truth, and acts upon it, especially since the Torah and the Gospel contain a description of the Messenger (ﷺ) that matches him completely. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and allows for them as good things and prohibits for them as evil, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ [al-A'raf 157]. All these attributes are present in the Torah and the Gospel. So they have knowledge, I mean the qissisin.

The second is the monks (ruhban). Among them are monks. The ruhban are the worshippers, because the Christians imposed upon themselves a monastic life that was not prescribed for them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them﴾ [al-Hadid 27]. That is, We did not prescribe it for them, but they seek the pleasure of Allah, desiring by it the pleasure of Allah, while it was not prescribed for them. The equivalent of this among us in the Islamic nation are the Sufis. They have a monasticism they invented, which Allah did not prescribe for them, but they seek by it the pleasure of Allah. If they had reflected on themselves, they would have known that the pleasure of Allah comes only through following, not through innovation.

The second cause: ﴿and because they are not arrogant﴾. They have no arrogance. Do the polytheists have arrogance? Yes, they have arrogance. Listen: ﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in ridicule: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan 41]. The hamzah here is an interrogative of contempt, of belittlement. And they say: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from one of the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 31]. They know, by Allah, that the greatest man in the two cities and in the whole earth is Muhammad (ﷺ), but it is obstinacy and arrogance. «When he gathered them and called them to Allah, they said: "Ruin to you! Is this why you gathered us?"»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4770), and Muslim (208/355), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]] As for the Jews, speak of arrogance and there is no end to it, to the point that they said to their prophet: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'idah 24]. This is clear arrogance. ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here﴾: sitting on chairs, on the ground, on carpets, while you go and fight. After this arrogance, is there anything more? No. They are arrogant. If this was their saying to their prophet, what about a prophet sent from among the Arabs? ﴿And that they are not arrogant.﴾

The third: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized.﴾ The historians and commentators also reported that when those who emigrated to Abyssinia recited the Qur'an to the Negus and those around him, they began to weep, their eyes overflowing with tears, meaning filling up, from the expression "the vessel overflowed," when the vessel is full and the water spills from its edges. Their eyes began to well up with tears and overflow because of what they recognized as the truth. They said, "This is what was revealed to Jesus." So they recognized that this was the truth, as Waraqah ibn Nawfal said when the Messenger, peace be upon him, told him of the truth that had been revealed to him. He said: «This is the Namus (divine revelation) that was sent down to Moses.»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3), and Muslim (160/252), from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.]] So they recognized the truth and wept. Yes, this will come in the benefits.

﴿because of the truth they have recognized﴾. ﴿They say﴾: is this also a third cause?

* **Student:** The fourth.

* **The Shaykh:** ﴿…that among them are priests and monks, and that they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized.﴾

The fourth: they have no arrogance. They submit to the truth from the moment they recognize it. ﴿They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾

The commentators also said that when those who emigrated to Abyssinia recited the Qur'an to the Negus and those around him, they began to weep, their eyes overflowing with tears, meaning filling up, from the expression "the vessel overflowed," when the vessel is full and the water spills from its edges. Their eyes began to well up with tears and overflow, ﴿because of the truth they have recognized﴾. They said, "This is what was revealed to Jesus," so they recognized that this was the truth, as Waraqah ibn Nawfal said when the Messenger, peace be upon him, told him of the truth that had been revealed to him. He said: «This is the Namus that was sent down to Moses.»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3), and Muslim (160/252), from the hadith of Aisha.]] So they recognized the truth and wept. ﴿because of the truth they have recognized, they say﴾: this is also a third cause.

* **Student:** (...)

* **The Shaykh:** ﴿…that among them are priests and monks, and that they are not arrogant, and when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 82, 83]

The fourth: they have no arrogance; they submit to the truth from the moment they recognize it.

﴿They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ It is an acknowledgment of lordship in their saying ﴿our Lord﴾, and of the religion of Allah in their saying ﴿we have believed﴾.

﴿So register us﴾: the fa' here is causal. That is, because of our acknowledgment of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and our faith in Him, register us among the witnesses. Would one who asks Allah to register him among the witnesses be arrogant toward the religion of the witnesses? That is impossible. They ask for this. ﴿So register us among the witnesses.﴾ Who are they?

The scholars said: The witnesses are Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, praise be to Allah, because Allah says: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾ [al-Baqarah 143], meaning just and excellent. No nation is more just than this nation, may Allah make us among them. No one is more just than it.

﴿That you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. We bear witness over the people, and the Messenger (ﷺ) bears witness over us that he conveyed to us, and that we acknowledged his conveyance.

So ﴿among the witnesses﴾ means: with Muhammad and the believers. They were witnesses because they are the last of the nations. All the previous nations have passed and are known to them. But does the first nation bear witness over those who come after it? No, it does not bear witness. That is why, if we were asked, "Which nation is the witnessing nation?" we would say: the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), because it is the last of the nations; it knows what happened to the nations and bears witness to it.

﴿So register us among the witnesses.﴾ Then He said: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth﴾ [al-Ma'idah 84]. This statement: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth?﴾ may be an inner speech, meaning that one of them says: how could I not believe when the truth is clear? It may also be a rejection of a blame directed at them. That is, it was said to them: why do you believe in Muhammad? So they said: ﴿And why should we not believe?﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verses 82–85 (part 2 of 5):

Can this and that both be the case? It is possible that one of them struggles with himself, and his own self says to him: "Why do you believe?" He answers: ﴿And why should we not believe in God﴾. When they reflect, they see that they must believe, because the truth is clear.

It is also possible that if someone blames them and says: "How can you believe?", they reply: ﴿And why should we not﴾, meaning: what is preventing us, what is stopping us, ﴿from believing in God and from what has come to us of the truth﴾. This shows the completeness of their intellect.

He says: ﴿And we long that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people.﴾ Glory be to God! This is the expression of the believer: ﴿we long that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people.﴾ The "righteous people" includes whoever was righteous from this Ummah and whoever was righteous from other than it. In the first statement they said: "Write us among the witnesses," meaning with this Ummah. In the second, which is the hope of entering Paradise, they said: ﴿we long that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people﴾, because Paradise is a home for this Ummah and for the righteous from other communities. Therefore they said: ﴿And we long that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people.﴾ The difference between the two expressions is clear: in the first they asked God to write them among the witnesses, and in the second they hoped that God would admit them among the righteous, meaning: that He would admit them to Paradise, because Paradise is for the righteous of this Ummah and of others.

* Student: What supports the possibility of the various meanings of the verse?
* Shaykh: Which of the meanings?
* Student: That this verse was revealed addressing the Prophet (...) concerning those who became Christians in his time. His saying ﴿those who say: "We are Christians"﴾, although many verses come describing them as Christians, indicates that this verse includes a description of them with this...
* Shaykh: Perhaps this strengthens it, but the word ﴿said﴾ may use the past tense to express the future, to narrate the state of affairs (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl).
* Student: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them﴾ [al-Hadid 27]. This is a blame. Yet what is mentioned here in the verse, that they accept the truth and that they are nearest in affection to the believers because among them are priests and monks, how is this reconciled?
* Shaykh: Because there came to them no messenger after 'Isa (peace be upon him). He died, and no messenger came after him, so they innovated in the religion of God what was not part of it. But after Muhammad came, they recognized the truth.
* Student: Is monasticism now a remnant of what they innovated? Meaning, is this an ongoing innovation among them?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it continues. When the Messenger came and they followed the truth, they abandoned it. But the monk is closer to accepting the truth, because he seeks the pleasure of God.
* Student: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe﴾. Do the qualities mentioned in the verse require that they be the most affectionate?
* Shaykh: No. ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks﴾, and that they ﴿when they hear﴾. These descriptions apply to those among them who believed, but in a general sense and in terms of the category as a whole. Those who said ﴿We are Christians﴾ are the category. I mentioned to you a moment ago the difference between the category and the individual. Now, do we say: every Jew is the strongest of people in enmity toward the believers, and every Christian is the nearest of them in affection? No. This is said in terms of the category.
* Student: May God bless you. The question, Shaykh, is: Does what is mentioned in the verse indicate that more of those who embrace Islam now are from among the Christians? And then how do we respond to those who call for bringing religions closer together and say: "This verse is evidence for us, so we approach the Christians (...)"?
* Shaykh: This will come in the benefits (fawa'id), God willing. This question belongs in the benefits.
* Student: What is the wisdom in using the expression "we long" (naṭma') in their saying ﴿And we long﴾?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Because a person does not affirm with certainty. God, may He be mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They call upon their Lord in fear and in hope﴾ [as-Sajdah 16]. A person does not affirm with certainty. Indeed, if a person is certain for himself that he is among the people of Paradise, that is a grave error. Rather, he hopes and longs. If he were certain that he is among the people of Paradise, it would follow from this that he has purified himself and testified for himself to Paradise, and this is extremely dangerous for a person, because it means that he is confident his deeds are accepted and that there is no fault in him that would prevent him from entering Paradise.
* Student: We mentioned in the principles of tafsir (qawa'id al-tafsir) that it is better for a person to try to interpret for himself. What is the minimum level of knowledge that enables a person to attempt tafsir on his own?
* Shaykh: A student of knowledge, a person who knows, a student of knowledge. We do not say to a layman who knows nothing but his shop: "Come, try to interpret the Qur'an." He is not a scholar.
* Student: The meanings of the words. Does he read the meanings of the words?
* Shaykh: The meanings of the words are not necessary. What matters is the general meaning and what the verse revolves around. A person knows this. Every student of knowledge can try and understand it.
* Student: Are those who ﴿are not arrogant﴾ all Christians in general, or only their priests and monks?
* Shaykh: No, all Christians in general. But as I told you: the intended meaning is the category, meaning that among them there is not the arrogance of the polytheists and the Jews, although some of them may be more arrogant than the Jews and polytheists.

* Shaykh: Do you know when this started? It started after colonialism. Otherwise, you will find the words of the scholars, may God have mercy on them, until colonialism began and the Muslims were humbled before the power of colonialism. You will find them using only the term "Christians." Look at the books of the earlier scholars, may God have mercy on them, until the West colonized the Islamic countries, and then they said "Masihiyyin." The writers who lived under the weight of colonialism followed them, because, as Ibn Khaldun said in his Muqaddimah: "The general rule is that the subjugated submits to the powerful and follows him." Otherwise, they are not Masihiyyin. When Jesus descends at the end of time, what will he do? He will break the cross, kill the swine, and accept nothing but Islam. Even the jizyah will not be accepted at that time.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2222) and Muslim (155 / 242) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

* * *

God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Ma'idah 85].

﴿Rewarded (athābahum)﴾ means: He gave them a reward (thawab). Reward is the recompense of the worker for his work. God said: ﴿Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 36].

His saying: ﴿for what they said﴾ means: because of their saying, which is: ﴿"We believe, so write us among the witnesses." And why should we not believe in God﴾ [al-Ma'idah 83–84], and so on to the end.

The letter bā' in His saying ﴿for what they said﴾ indicates causation (sababiyyah). The word mā may be a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawṣūlah). If we take it as a verbal-noun particle, the meaning becomes: God rewarded them for their saying. If we take it as a relative noun, the meaning becomes: God rewarded them for that which they said. In that case there must be a returning pronoun (ā'id) referring back to the relative noun, which here is omitted, and the meaning is: for what they said (it).

His saying: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. ﴿Gardens (jannāt)﴾ here is the plural of (jannah). God sometimes refers to it in the singular, "the Garden (al-jannah)", and sometimes in the plural, "gardens (jannāt)". When it is mentioned in the singular, what is meant is the category. When it is mentioned in the plural, what is meant is its kinds. You know that God mentioned in Surat ar-Rahman four kinds: two gardens, and two gardens. And in the hadith: "There are two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (180 / 296) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]

As for His saying ﴿gardens (jannāt)﴾: if we want to trace it to its linguistic meaning, we say: the jannāt are gardens with many trees, and they were named so because their trees cover (tujinn) their ground, meaning they conceal it, because of their abundance and spread. But if this explanation were given to the common people, the value of Paradise would decline in their eyes, and they would imagine that it is of the same kind as the gardens of this world. Therefore, in explaining it we say: it is the abode that God, may He be mighty and majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, so that a person may know that this Paradise has no equal.

His saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: beneath its palaces and trees, and the intended meaning is not beneath its ground, because what is beneath its ground is not of use, but rather beneath its trees and palaces. The word "rivers (anhār)" is the plural of "river (nahr)". There are four kinds, mentioned in Surat Muhammad in His saying: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. God created these rivers differently from the way He created them on earth. Water on earth comes out by digging wells, or from rain and torrents. But in Paradise it is not like this: rivers flow without a trench and without digging channels, but by the power of God, may He be mighty and majestic.

﴿Rivers of milk whose taste does not change﴾: not from cows, nor camels, nor sheep, but rivers that God created from this.

﴿Rivers of wine﴾: not grape juice, nor barley, nor anything else, but it is created in this form.

﴿And rivers of honey﴾: from bees? No. Honey that God created and which became rivers flowing in Paradise. These are four kinds of rivers, which God has mentioned to us.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾. Khalid (abiding forever) means remaining, and the basic meaning of khulūd (eternity) is lasting permanence. This is the basic meaning. Sometimes it is emphasized with the word "forever (abadan)", and sometimes it is not intended to mean permanence, by an indication from context. So khulūd basically means lasting permanence. It may be emphasized by eternity, and it may not be intended as eternity. As for what is emphasized by eternity, it is common in the Qur'an, both for the people of Paradise and for the people of Hell. As for what is not intended as eternity by another proof, such as His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and God will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa' 93]. Here ﴿abiding (khālidan)﴾ does not mean eternity, because killing a believer intentionally does not take one out of faith, except for one who considers it lawful. Whoever considers it lawful is a disbeliever because of his considering it lawful, not because of the killing itself, since whoever considers killing a believer lawful is a disbeliever, whether he kills or not.

In sum, keep in mind what khulūd is: lasting permanence. It may be emphasized by eternity, and it may not be intended as eternity by a proof.

﴿Abiding therein. That﴾: the referent is what God rewarded them with, the gardens.

﴿Is the recompense of the doers of good (al-muḥsinīn)﴾, meaning: their reward for their deeds. The muḥsin (doer of good) includes whoever does good in worshipping God and whoever does good to God's servants. As for excellence (iḥsān) in the worship of God, the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it in his saying: "Excellence is that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9 / 5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

So he made iḥsān two levels. The first: that one worships God as if he sees Him, and this is worship out of desire, because you desire and seek what you see. "If you do not see Him" means: if you do not reach this state, "then He sees you," meaning: worship Him out of fear and flight from His punishment. Thus the Prophet (ﷺ) made these two levels for a person.

As for excellence toward God's servants, it is extending kindness to them with wealth, body, status, and other things. It is the extension of kindness. Whoever gives you a dirham is a doer of good. Whoever smiles in your face and brings joy to you is a doer of good. Whoever intercedes for you in a matter is a doer of good. So excellence occurs in worshipping God, and it occurs in dealing with God's servants.

When God, may He be glorified and exalted, mentioned the reward of these doers of good, He said: ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of Hellfire﴾ [al-Ma'idah 86]. The noble Qur'an is ma-thānī (oft-repeated pairs), in which meanings are paired. When the reward of the doers of good is mentioned, the reward of the evildoers is mentioned, and when the reward of the evildoers is mentioned, the reward of the doers of good is mentioned, so that a person remains between desire and fear.

﴿Those who disbelieved and denied﴾: they disbelieved in the command and denied the report. They disbelieved in the command, so they did not carry out obedience and did not refrain from disobedience. They denied the report, so they did not affirm it. Whoever denies the resurrection, which of the two categories is he in? He is a denier, but he is also a disbeliever. He is a denier and a disbeliever. ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected﴾ [at-Taghabun 7]. And whoever does not pray is a disbeliever.

If someone asks: Do we say that disbelief and denial must be combined? The answer: No. If disbelief exists, the penalty is established. If denial exists, the penalty is established.

Therefore, if someone said: "The five daily prayers are not obligatory, and I do not believe they are obligatory," but he prays and never misses a prayer, what do we say about him? He is a disbeliever, because he is a denier. So combining them is not a condition. Rather, if either one exists, the ruling is established.

His saying: ﴿Our signs (āyātinā)﴾ includes the cosmic signs and the legislative signs. Whoever claims that there is a creator alongside God is a denier of the cosmic signs. Whoever acknowledges the Creator but does not accept His law is a denier of the legislative signs. Some may deny both together. And whoever denies some and affirms others is a disbeliever, because God says: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [an-Nisa' 151].

His saying: ﴿Those are the companions of Hellfire (ṣaḥāb al-jaḥīm)﴾. The demonstrative here (ulā'ika), is it for distance or for nearness? For distance. But distance may be distance of lowliness or distance of elevation. If the distance refers to a high rank, it is distance of elevation, like His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 1–2]. It is right in front of us now, not far away, but because of its lofty rank and nobility, it is referred to with the demonstrative of distance. And He said: ﴿And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it, those are the righteous﴾ [az-Zumar 33], pointing to them with the demonstrative of distance because of their elevated station.

In this verse: ﴿Those are the companions of Hellfire﴾. Which of the two distances is meant? Lowliness. Distance of lowliness.

His saying: ﴿companions of Hellfire (aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm)﴾. Know that when God mentions the companions of the Fire, the companions of Hellfire, this refers to the pure disbelievers, because the companion (ṣāḥib) is the one who remains constantly with something, and no one remains constantly in Hellfire, meaning the Fire, except one who will not enter Paradise. So ﴿those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of Hellfire﴾.

* It is derived from this noble verse, and likewise from the verse before it, that the people most hostile to the believers are the Jews and the polytheists. And what is meant by "the people"? What is meant is the category. We mean by this that some Jews may not be the most hostile, and likewise some polytheists. For example, we find Abu Talib was a polytheist, yet did the Messenger (ﷺ) love him? Yes, he loved him. But the category is that the polytheists and the Jews are the most hostile of people.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that the enmity of these people is apparent, from His saying: ﴿You will surely find the strongest of people in enmity﴾. But know that apparentness and hiddenness are relative matters. Meaning, some people see what is hidden from another, and some people fail to see what is apparent to another. But whoever examines matters and considers them will see this clearly. If someone says, for example: "We do not find this," we say: if you do not find it, that is because of your dullness, because you are dull and do not know.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that non-Muslims differ in their enmity toward Muslims. From where do we derive this?
* Student: ﴿the strongest of people in enmity﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾ and ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾: is it a noun?

**Student:** It is a comparative (*ism tafdil*).

**Shaykh:** It is an *ism tafdil*, indicating that these enemies differ in degree. That is indeed the reality. But how do we know who is the "strongest" (*ashadd*) in enmity? We know it through its effects. If they support one another against us, form alliances against us, and the like, then we know they are enemies.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the people closest in affection to the believers are the Christians. We have already explained the reason for this in the commentary.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: every ruling has a cause. This is consistent, my brothers. Every legal or divine-decreed ruling has a cause. However, some causes are known and some are not known, because Allah the Exalted has not informed us of everything. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿That is because among them are priests (*qissisin*) and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾, and so on to the end.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of Allah the Mighty and Majestic's instruction in His Mighty Book. When He mentions a ruling, He sometimes mentions its cause. Here He mentioned a divine-decreed ruling, namely the closeness of the Christians to the affection of the Muslims. This is a divine-decreed ruling, and He mentioned its cause.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted has mentioned many legal rulings together with their wisdoms, such as His saying: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:222], and His saying: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it, except that it be carrion, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure﴾ [al-An'am 6:145]. "It" here refers to this food. Whoever says that "it" refers to the flesh of swine is mistaken, because if we return the end of the sentence to its beginning, the beginning says: ﴿except that it be﴾, meaning that food; ﴿carrion, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it﴾, meaning the food, ﴿is impure﴾. It does not refer to the flesh of swine.

The point is that it is part of the excellent instruction of Allah the Mighty and Majestic that when He mentions a ruling, He mentions its cause, whether the ruling is divine-decreed or legislated. Likewise in the Sunnah, the cause is sometimes mentioned. The Prophet ﷺ commanded Abu Talhah, who then proclaimed: "Indeed Allah and His Messenger forbid you the flesh of domestic donkeys, for indeed it is impure."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5528) and Muslim (1940/35), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the closeness of the Christians' affection for the believers has causes. How many?

**Student:** Five causes.

**Shaykh:** Let us see. First: ﴿that among them are priests and monks﴾. From this it is derived that knowledge is beneficial even for non-Muslims, and that worship softens the heart. The first is derived from His saying: ﴿that among them are priests﴾, and the second from His saying: ﴿and monks﴾, because the monk only took this path seeking the pleasure of Allah. He is not arrogant, but seeks the pleasure of Allah. So when the truth becomes clear to him, he is among the people closest to acting upon it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the children of Adam are divided into scholars and worshippers. But can they be scholars who are also worshippers? Yes, and that is common: one can be a scholar and a worshipper. However, some people are dominated by knowledge and others by worship. Among those who are characterized by both knowledge and worship, some are dominated by the side of knowledge, so you find them always in research, investigation, and review. Others are dominated by worship. That is why you find in the biographies of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, that when they describe some scholar they say: "He was abundant in worship."

Which is better in a scholar: that he be abundant in worship, or abundant in review? Abundance in review is undoubtedly better. But whoever is abundant in review must also review his heart. If he finds in himself hardness, let him occupy himself with worship for a while, because at times, with much review, study, and debate, a person becomes like a warrior between two lines, not turning, for example, to prayer, night vigil, and the like. If you see in yourself that you have become distant from worship, return to it so that you do not neglect it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: among the causes of accepting the truth and of affection for the believers is humility, from His saying: ﴿and because they are not arrogant﴾.

It is also derived from it that arrogance is a cause of rejecting the truth, and that is so. Humility is a cause of accepting the truth, because a person does not see himself as infallible. When the truth becomes clear to him, he follows it. This is why in the letter of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "Do not let a judgment you issued today prevent you from returning to the truth tomorrow,"[[Narrated by al-Daraqutni (4471), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/150).]] or words similar to that, meaning that you follow the truth wherever it is, becoming compliant to the truth and humble before it.

Does this humility before the truth oblige a person to be humble among people? No. "Whoever is humble for the sake of Allah, Allah raises him."[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (8307), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (7790), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]] Whoever is humble before the truth is granted success in the truth. The sign of this is that when the truth becomes clear to you, you follow it immediately, without hesitation and without dispute. If you hesitate or argue, that is a very great danger to you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes﴾, why? ﴿as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 6:110].

Therefore, when the truth becomes clear to you, do not argue. Do not try to go right and left to justify your opinion. You are in danger. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾ [Qaf 50:5]: mixed up, the truth becomes confused for them with falsehood. When they deny the truth when it comes to them, pay attention to this benefit, you who are a student of knowledge. Some people may oppose you in accordance with evidence, but you want to impose your opinion. This is a great error. Follow the truth wherever it is, and people will follow you wherever you are, because people seek the truth. When they see that whenever the truth becomes clear to you, you return to it, they return too.

So humility before the truth is in reality exaltation, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is humble for the sake of Allah, He raises him,"[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (8307), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (7790), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]] and its opposite is arrogance. Arrogance, may Allah protect us, makes a person unwilling to accept the truth and unwilling to follow it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of these people who believe in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that ﴿when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears﴾. There is no doubt that their eyes overflowing with tears is evidence of what? Of faith, belief, and being affected. Because whenever a person believes, he increases in humility.

Now, if you remember your fathers, brothers, and friends who have passed away and died, you may weep more than if you remembered something else believed in, because these you experienced through the senses. As faith grows stronger, the believer becomes as if he sees the thing with his own eye, so his faith, humility, and weeping increase.

Let us take the benefits of the individual words. Among the benefits of His saying: ﴿what has been revealed to the Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:83] is that the Qur'an came from Allah, because this is in the passive form, ﴿has been revealed﴾, since its agent is known: it is Allah who revealed it.

From this is derived that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and that is so. He spoke it, the Glorified and Exalted, in truth, speaking it in an audible manner. Who heard it? Jibril heard it, and he is trustworthy and strong. He descended with it upon the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, who retained and understood it, until his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, said to him: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:16–17]. It will never be scattered; it is gathered for you. ﴿So when We have recited it﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:18], meaning Jibril recited it, ﴿then follow its recitation. Then indeed upon Us is its clarification﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:18–19].

These are great commitments from Allah the Mighty and Majestic regarding this Qur'an, which show Allah's care for it, Glorified and Exalted. ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its clarification﴾: We clarify it for the people in wording and in meaning. That is why we say: there cannot be in the Book of Allah anything whose meaning people do not know. If its knowledge is hidden from some, others know it.
