When a person feels that Allah loves him, he rejoices and grows in love for acts of obedience and in aversion to sins, because he knows that his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, loves him from above the seven heavens. If the meaning were merely that He rewards him, then He rewards any of the servants who deserves reward; so they were deprived of the delight of Allah's love because they denied it.
So the main point is that the verse affirms love. If someone asks: what is the way to establish it?
We say: because negating it from the transgressors indicates the establishment of its root; for if its root were not established, there would be no benefit in negating it from the transgressors. This is like the argument of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, for the seeing of Allah from the negation of seeing for the wicked, when the Exalted said: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 15].
He said: if all creation were veiled from Allah, there would be no benefit in negating the veiling of vision from the wicked. The negation of vision from the wicked is evidence of its establishment for whom?
* Students: For the righteous.
* A student: For the pious.
* The Shaykh: For the righteous.
* Among the benefits of the following verse: commanding a person to eat of what Allah has provided. Its opposite is not eating. Not eating of what Allah has provided has three categories. First: abstaining from eating when there is fear of death if he does not eat; here abstaining from eating is forbidden, because a person is obligated to save himself. From this we know the foolishness of those who go on hunger strikes, and we know their foolishness in their minds and their error in their religion. Some of them are hospitalized like corpses. This is unquestionably forbidden. Second: if there is no dire necessity to eat, but he needs to eat to strengthen the body, then eating here is what? Recommended, because if he abstains he would not die, but he has a need, so we say: do not deprive yourself. Third: what? Abstaining from eating out of asceticism, and this is forbidden, and it is said to him: eat of what Allah has permitted for you. Some people abstain from good food out of piety and asceticism; what do we say about them?
We say: this is an error. The best of creation, Muhammad, peace be upon him, used to choose good food. Did they not bring him good dates instead of poor dates? Yes, and yet he did not forbid them; he did not say, "Why do you bring me good food?" Rather he guided them to bring good food, but by a permissible means.
So for some people to abstain from good things out of piety and asceticism, we say: no. You are now deviating from piety, because piety is following the sharia, and asceticism is abandoning what does not benefit in the Hereafter, while following the sharia is what benefits in the Hereafter. So you are now neither ascetic nor pious. Yes, if it is assumed that a person, in his particular case, finds in himself that if he chose good things it would lead to arrogance and exultation, then here we may say: abandon good things lest you be afflicted with arrogance and exultation. But we treat that beforehand with another remedy: we say, it is not permissible that enjoying the blessings of Allah lead you to arrogance and exultation. If you are unable and insist that it will lead you, then we say: now abandon them. For the reality of some people is that when they wear fine clothes, the fine cloak, the fine ghutrah, they swell up and become haughty and arrogant. To such a person we say: abandon this, or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: We say: abandon it. Whereas we say: do not be arrogant. But if he says, "I am unable," we say: praise be to Allah; leave these for those who do not become arrogant when they wear them. But this is a specific remedy, just as we treat the person who is affected by eating good things in another way, by saying: leave them and let them be for those who are not affected by them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory for a person to have good food, because of the Exalted's words: what? ﴿lawful and good﴾. So earnings that are unlawful, even if in themselves lawful, for example earning dirhams, where dirhams are originally a lawful acquisition: if he earns them through something unlawful, we say: they are unlawful for you, and it is forbidden for you to eat from them. Why?
Because they are not good. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever gives charity from something good, and Allah accepts only what is good"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1410) and Muslim (1014/63), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording.]].
His words "from something good" mean: good in its acquisition and in itself, for Allah accepts such charity.
Now, if money is unlawful because of how it was acquired, is it lawful for someone other than the earner if he acquired it by a permissible means?
The answer: yes. This principle is indicated by the fact that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, "ate from the food of the Jews"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2617) and Muslim (2190/45), from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: a Jewish woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it.]], and they are known for what?
* Students: For usury.
* The Shaykh: For consuming usury, illicit gain, and bribery. And he ate from it, because it was obtained by a permissible means: he was permitted to do so, or it was given to him as a gift. Except if you know that this property is the very property of another man, as with a thief who steals a sheep and slaughters it to host you while you know he stole it. In that case it is not permissible for you to eat it, because this is unlawful in its very essence, meaning that this earner did not own this item, so it is not permissible for you to eat it. But if someone invites you to a feast, and he is known for having all his wealth unlawful, acquired through plain usury or through usury disguised by trickery, is it permissible for you to eat from it?

Yes, I may eat from it, unless I know that if I refrain from accepting his invitation and eating his food, that will become a cause for his repentance. In that case, yes, it is not permissible for me to accept his invitation or to eat from his food, because when people see that he has been boycotted, and they do not accept his invitations or eat his food, this will undoubtedly affect him, unless his heart is dead.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: belief in Allah, mighty and majestic, necessarily entails taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him, as shown by His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾. That is: because of your belief, taqwa is binding upon you. True belief necessarily entails taqwa. Whoever claims to be a believer but does not fear Allah is either entirely lacking in faith or deficient in faith.

If someone says: "He commits sins, and when it is said to him, 'O so-and-so, fear Allah, do not disobey Allah,' he stands up, strikes his chest and says: 'The taqwa is here, the taqwa is here, the taqwa is here.' What do we say to him?"

We say: this is the statement of the Messenger ﷺ, there is no doubt about it, and we have no doubt about it. But if taqwa were truly where he claims, it would have affected his hand, foot, eye and tongue, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599 / 107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] So if there were taqwa in that place, it would have shown upon his limbs (...).

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾ [O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors].

* طالب: يا شيخ، أحسن الله إليك، فيما يتعلق بالنسخ (naskh, abrogation)، بعض العلماء يقول: إن اصطلاح المتقدمين من الصحابة وبعض التابعين للنسخ أوسع من اصطلاح المتأخِّرين.
* الشيخ: صحيح، بعض السلف يطلق التخصيص (takhsis, specification) على النسخ، مثل قوله تعالى: ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ [المؤمنون ٦] [except from their wives or what their right hands possess]، أجاز بعض السلف أن يجمع الإنسان بين الأختين في ملك اليمين، يعني يطأهما، وقال: الآية عامة، لكن عبَّر بعض السلف قال: هذه الآية نسختها آية: ﴿وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ﴾ [النساء ٢٣] [and that you combine two sisters], فقال: نسختها، ويريد بذلك التخصيص، وله وجه؛ لأن التخصيص نَسْخٌ للعموم، فله وجه.
* الطالب: سورة البقرة، آخر آية هل هي نسخ أو بالتخصيص ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ [Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity] [البقرة ٢٨٦]؟
* الشيخ: لا، الظاهر -والله أعلم- إطلاق النسخ عليها من باب التخصيص، أو التبيين أيضًا؛ لأن الله يقول: ﴿وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾ [Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it] [البقرة ٢٨٤] هذا من الأمور العملية والقلبية، أما مجرد الفكر فقد تجاوز الله عنه.
* طالب: شيخ، أحسن الله إليك، هل نسخ القرآن بالسنة، هل السنة نسخت الـ..؟
* الشيخ: فيه مثال وهو قول الله تعالى: ﴿وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا﴾ أي: الفاحشة، ﴿مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا فَإِنْ تَابَا وَأَصْلَحَا فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابًا رَحِيمًا﴾ [And the two who commit it among you, then harm them. But if they repent and make amends, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful] [النساء ١٦]، والحديث الذي صحَّحه كثير من الأئمة: «مَنْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ يَعْمَلُ عَمَلَ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ فَاقْتُلُوا الْفَاعِلَ وَالْمَفْعُولَ بِهِ»[[أخرجه أبو داود (٤٤٦٢)، والترمذي (١٤٥٦) من حديث عبد الله بن عباس.]] ["Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one it is done to"]، فهذا الحديث ينسخ قوله تعالى: ﴿فَآذُوهُمَا﴾، الحديث ينسخ الآية، هذا نسخ القرآن بالسنة، والمثال عزيز جدًّا، يعني قليل جدًّا جدًّا.
كما أن القرآن يخصِّص السنة، مثل اشتراط النبي (ﷺ) في صلح الحديبية أن مَن جاء من المشركين مسلمًا فإنه يُرَدُّ عليهم[[أخرجه البخاري (٢٧٣٢) من حديث المسور بن مخرمة.]]، وهذا عام للرجال والنساء، فقال الله عز وجل: ﴿إِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ فَلَا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ [If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers] [الممتحنة ١٠]، وهذا من الأمور العزيزة النادرة؛ أن يكون القرآن يخصِّص عموم السنة.
* طالب: أحسن الله إليك، قوله تعالى: ﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَدَاوَةً﴾ [You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity], ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾ هذا إذا جعلناه مفعول أول أبلغ من لو جعلناه مفعولًا ثانيًا، أحسن الله إليك، ما فهمت وجه إنه أبلغ.
* الشيخ: تفهم إن شاء الله هذا في وقت آخر؛ لأنه تكلمنا عليها كثيرًا.
* طالب: أسأل الله أن يحسن إليك، كما لا يخفى أن الخوف والرجاء من العبادات القلبية، فكيف يستطيع الإنسان يحقق الخوف والرجاء ويعرف أنه يمشي بين هذين؟
* الشيخ: وهذا ليس انفعالًا في الواقع، وإذا قُدِّر انفعالًا فإننا نقول: الإنسان إذا مُنِّيَ بشيء يحبه أيرجوه أو لا؟ يرجوه، وإذا خُوِّف يخاف، لو أن رجلًا كريمًا قال: من عمل هذا فله كذا وكذا، فعمله إنسان، يرجو أو يخاف؟ يرجو، كذلك بالعكس لو أن رجلًا ظالمًا قال: من فعل كذا عاقبته بكذا، فالإنسان يخاف، وإن كان انفعالًا، لكن لا بد أن يتأثر الإنسان بما يكون أمامه من طمع أو خوف.
* طالب: عفا الله عنك يا شيخ، إذا ثبت أن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وأرضاهم فهموا وقرروا وعملوا به يا شيخ، والحقيقة تقصر عقولنا عنهم فهمًا وعملًا، كيف (...) يا شيخ؟
* الشيخ: مثل أيش؟
* الطالب: مثل كلام عمر رضي الله عنه وأرضاه في آية الرجم، بعض الناس يطالب يقول: الدليل، ما فيه دليل، بعض من الناس الحين، آية الرجم؟
* الشيخ: سبحان الله! عمر رضي الله عنه موفَّق للصواب، وعنده فراسة عجيبة، هو نفسه رضي الله عنه قال: «أخاف إن طال بالناس زمان أن يقولوا: لا نجد الرجم في كتاب الله»[[متفق عليه؛ البخاري (٦٨٢٩)، ومسلم (١٦٩١ / ١٥).]]، وهذا الذي ذكرت الآن هو ما توقعه عمر، وإلا هو يُعلِن على منبر الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام بهذا الكلام، هل يمكن أن يعلن على منبر الرسول ويكون الأمر على خلاف ما قال ويسكت الصحابة؟ لا يمكن.
* طالب: شيخ، بارك الله فيك، ما مدى صحة قول من يقول: إن النار دركات، وكل دركة لها اسم؟
* الشيخ: يعني معناه يجعل الأسماء هذه بحسب الدركات، ما هو صحيح، الصحيح أنها أسماء لمسمى واحد.
* الطالب: (...) الدرك الأسفل من النار؟
* الشيخ: إي نعم، كما أن البيت اسم واحد، وفيه سطح، وفيه مصباح، وفيه بدروم، وغيره.
إذا خُوّف يخاف، لو أن رجلًا كريمًا قال: من عمل هذا فله كذا وكذا، فعمله إنسان يرجو أو يخاف؟ يرجو، كذلك بالعكس لو أن رجلًا ظالمًا قال: من فعل كذا عاقبته بكذا، فالإنسان يخاف، وإن كان انفعالًا، لكن لا بد أن يتأثر الإنسان بما يكون أمامه من طمع أو خوف.
* طالب: عفا الله عنك يا شيخ، إذا ثبت أن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وأرضاهم حكم وأقروه وعملوا به يا شيخ، تقصر عقولنا عنه فهمًا وعملًا، كيف العدول عنه يا شيخ؟
* الشيخ: مثل أيش؟
* الطالب: مثل كلام عمر رضي الله عنه وأرضاه في آية الرجم، بعض الناس يطالب يقول: الدليل؟ ما فيه دليل (...) آية الرجم؟
* الشيخ: سبحان الله! عمر رضي الله عنه موفّق بالصواب، وعنده فراسة عجيبة، هو نفسه رضي الله عنه قال: «أخاف إن طال بالناس زمان أن يقولوا: لا نجد الرجم في كتاب الله»[[متفق عليه؛ البخاري (٦٨٢٩)، ومسلم (١٦٩١ / ١٥) من حديث عمر بن الخطاب.]]، وهذا الذي ذكرت الآن هو ما توقعه عمر فهمت؟ وإلا هو يُعلن على منبر الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام بهذا الكلام، هل يمكن أن يعلن على منبر الرسول ويكون الأمر على خلاف ما قال ويسكت الصحابة؟ لا يمكن.
* طالب: ما مدى صحة قول من يقول: إن النار دركات؟
* الشيخ: يعني معناها يجعل أسماء هذه بحسب الدركات؟ ما هو صحيح، الصحيح أنها أسماء لمسمى واحد.
* طالب: في الدرك الأسفل من النار.
* الشيخ: إي، كما أن البيت اسم واحد، وفيه سطح، وفيه مصباح، وفيه بدروم وغيره.
الفرق بينهما أن مطلق الشيء يعني الجزء منه والشيء منه؛ يعني معناه أنه يسمى شيئًا، مطلق الشيء يسمى شيئًا، والشيء المطلق يعني الشيء الكامل، المطلق يعني من غير قيد اللي ما يُقال: إنه قليل، ولا يقال: إنه ضعيف، ولا شيء، فالشيء المطلق الكامل من الشيء، ومطلق الشيء يعني الذي يصدق عليه أنه شيء وإن لم يكن كاملًا.
* طالب: لذلك قلنا: فيه إطلاق.
* الشيخ: لا، بس فرق بين أن تضيف الإطلاق إلى النوع أو إلى الجنس، وأن تصف النوع بالإطلاق، الشيء المطلق يعني الكامل، مطلق الشيء يعني معناه أنه ما يصدق عليه الشيء وإن لم يكن كاملًا.
* * *
نكمل ما تقدم في النسْخ حتى يكمل البحث فيه. ذكرنا أمس أن النسخ جائز عقلًا وواقع شرعًا، علل لجوازه عقلًا؟
* طالب: (...).
* الشيخ: لا.
* طالب: يقال في معظم الأحكام: إذا شرعت في زمان معين لأمة معينة، فتصلح له، وقد لا تصلح لغيرها، فيكون من الحكمة أن يشرع لمن بعدها خلاف ما شرع لمن قبلها حيث..
* الشيخ: لأن أحكام الله تعالى يُراد بها مصالح العباد، وهي تختلف في كل زمان أو مكان أو حال، فلذلك كان مقتضى الحكمة أيش؟
* الطالب: نسخ الأحكام.
* الشيخ: نعم، نسخ الأحكام. واقع شرعًا هات مثالًا؟
* طالب: قوله تعالى: ﴿مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا﴾ [We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten] [البقرة ١٠٦] ودليل وقوعه؟
* الشيخ: إي، وقوعه.
* الطالب: ﴿الْآنَ خَفَّفَ﴾ [Now Allah has lightened] [الأنفال ٦٦].
* الشيخ: واقع شرعًا.
* الطالب: ﴿الْآنَ خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ﴾ [Now Allah has lightened your burden].
* الشيخ: ﴿الْآنَ خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ﴾ بعد أن قال؟
* الطالب: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفًا﴾ [If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one hundred, they will overcome a thousand] [الأنفال ٦٥].
* الشيخ: ﴿مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ (٦٥) الْآن﴾ [...one thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not comprehend (65). Now] [الأنفال ٦٥، ٦٦].
* الطالب: ﴿خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًا﴾ [Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness].
* الشيخ: كمِّل.
* الطالب: ﴿فَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ﴾ [So if there are among you one hundred steadfast].
* الشيخ: صحيح ﴿صَابِرَةٌ﴾.
* الطالب: ﴿يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ﴾ [they will overcome two hundred].
* الشيخ: ﴿وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفَيْنِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [And if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah] [الأنفال ٦٦]. بارك الله فيك.
النسخ يكون نسخ لفظ، أو نسخ حكم، أو نسخهما، نسخ اللفظ؟
* طالب: أن يُنسخ اللفظ ويبقى الحكم.
* الشيخ: نعم، أن يُنسخ اللفظ ويبقى الحكم، مثاله؟
* الطالب: آية الرجم التي نُسخت فكانت..
* الشيخ: الرجم يعني رجم أيش؟
* الطالب: رجم المحصَن.
* الشيخ: الزاني المحصن، نعم.
* الطالب: نُسخت، وبقي حكمها.
* الشيخ: كانت تُقرأ في كتاب الله، ثم نسخ لفظها، وبقي حكمها، ما هو الدليل؟
* الطالب: قول عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: «إن مما أنزل من القرآن آية الرجم»[[متفق عليه؛ البخاري (٦٨٣٠)، ومسلم (١٦٩١ / ١٥) من حديث عمر بن الخطاب.]] (...) هذا الدليل.
* الشيخ: كمّل: «إن مما أنزل الله تعالى على رسوله آية الرجم قرأناها، وحفظناها، ووعيناها، ورجم النبي (ﷺ) ورجمنا بعده. وإن الرجم حق ثابت في كتاب الله على من زنى إذا أحصن، وكان الحبَل أو الاعتراف»[[متفق عليه؛ البخاري (٦٨٣٠)، ومسلم (١٦٩١ / ١٥) من حديث عمر بن الخطاب.]]. أفهمت؟ إذا قامت البينة وكان الحبل أو الاعتراف.
ما هي الحكمة من نسخ اللفظ دون الحكم؟
* طالب: نسخ اللفظ دون الحكم لتذكير العباد بنعمة الله عز وجل.
* الشيخ: لا.
* الطالب: أو لتبيين فضل هذه الأمة على غيرها.
* الشيخ: نعم؛ لتبيين فضل هذه الأمة على غيرها؛ حيث عملت بالرجم مع أنه لا يوجد لفظه في كتاب الله، واليهود بالعكس جحدوا آية الرجم حتى إنهم لما جاؤوا بالتوراة وضع الذي يقرأ يده على آية الرجم حتى لا تَبين.
الثاني: نسخ الحكم وبقاء اللفظ، مثاله؟
* طالب: ﴿الْآنَ خَفَّفَ﴾، الآية في الأول: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ (٦٥) الْآنَ خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًا﴾ [O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred... Now Allah has lightened your burden...] [الأنفال ٦٥، ٦٦].
* الشيخ: أين المنسوخ؟
* الطالب: الأول.
* الشيخ: الآية الأولى نُسخ حكمها، وبقي لفظها، بارك الله فيك، الحكمة؟
* طالب: أن بقاء اللفظ فيه (...) أخرى مثل زيادة الأجر كما في الصلاة.
* الشيخ: أن في بقاء اللفظ زيادة الأجر.
* الطالب: وأيضًا تذكُّر نعمة الله سبحانه وتعالى.
* الشيخ: التذكير بنعمة الله عز وجل، الثالث؟
* الطالب: نسخ الحكم واللفظ معًا.
* الشيخ: نعم، نسخ اللفظ والحكم معًا، مثاله؟
* طالب: العشر رضعات.
* الشيخ: مثل العشر رضعات؟ يعني عشر رضعات نُسخت إلى خمس عشرة رضعة؟!
* الطالب: حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: «ما أنزل عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن، ثم نسخن بخمس معلومات فتوفي رسول الله (ﷺ) وهي فيما يقرأ من القرآن»[[أخرجه مسلم (١٤٥٢ / ٢٤) من حديث عائشة.]]، العشر إلى خمس، الأولى منسوخة لفظًا وحكمًا.
* الشيخ: العشر منسوخة لفظًا وحكمًا؛ لأن حكمها نُسخ بخمس ولفظها لا يوجد.
فيه تقسيم آخر للنسخ: النسخ تارة يُنسخ إلى أثقل، وتارة ينسخ إلى أخف، وتارة ينسخ إلى مساوٍ، ثلاثة أقسام: تارة ينسخ إلى أثقل، مثال ذلك: الصوم، أول ما فرض الصوم (...) الناس مخيرون بين أن يصوم الإنسان أو يفدي، ثبت ذلك في الصحيحين من حديث سلمة بن الأكوع رضي الله عنه، أول ما نزل الصيام صام من شاء صام ومن شاء افتدى، ثم تعيّن الصوم، أيهما أثقل؟
* طالب: الناسخ.
* الشيخ: تعيين الصوم؛ لأن المخيّر إن شاء هذا أو هذا، فإذا تعين الصوم صار أثقل.
الثاني: إلى أخف، مثاله: آية المصابرة التي قرأنا ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ﴾ [الأنفال ٦٥] إلى آخره، هذه نسخت إلى أخف، ومما نسخ إلى أخف؛ الصلوات الخمس نُسخت من خمسين إلى خمس.
الثالث: النسخ إلى مساوٍ، بالنسبة لفعل المكلف لا فرق بين هذا وهذا كنسخ استقبال بيت المقدس باستقبال الكعبة، فهنا الفعل بالنسبة للمكلف واحد، الإنسان لا فرق أن يتجه يمينًا أو شمالًا، فلننظر إذا نسخ من أخف إلى أشد ففيه فائدتان؛ الفائدة الأولى: زيادة الأجر؛ لأن العمل إذا شق على المكلف لا بفعل نفسه واختياره فله أجر يزداد أجره. انتبه للقيد! إذا شق على المكلف أيش؟
* طالب: لا بفعله واختياره.
* الشيخ: لا بفعله واختياره فهو أفضل، ولهذا قال النبي (ﷺ) لعائشة: «أَجْرُكِ عَلَى قَدْرِ نَصَبِكِ»[[متفق عليه؛ البخاري (١٧٨٧)، ومسلم (١٢١١ / ١٢٦) من حديث عائشة بلفظ: «وَلَكِنَّهَا عَلَى قَدْرِ نَفَقَتِكِ أَوْ نَصَبِكِ».]] ["Your reward is according to the measure of your toil"]. يعني على قدر المشقة، أما ما كان بفعل المكلف واختياره فهو إلى الإثم أقرب منه إلى الأجر، مثال الأول: إنسان قام يتوضأ في البر، وليس عنده إلا ماء بارد، وليس عنده ما يسخن به، فتوضأ بالماء البارد، فيه مشقة ولَّا لا؟
* طلبة: فيه.
* الشيخ: فيه مشقة، آخر قام يتوضأ وعنده ماء ساخن، وماء بارد فتوضأ بالماء البارد، أيكون أفضل مما لو توضأ بالماء الساخن؟
لا، بل هو إلى الإثم أقرب منه إلى السلامة؛ لأن هذا باختياره، إذن النسخ من الأخف إلى الأشد فيه أيش؟
* طلبة: زيادة الأجر.
* الشيخ: زيادة الأجر، فيه أيضًا بيان حكمة التشريع، حيث يتبين للإنسان أن التشريع في هذه الشريعة الإسلامية يأتي بالتدريج الأسهل فالأسهل حتى لا يصطدم الناس بالشريعة الكاملة، وانظر إلى تحريم الخمر، تحريم الخمر جاء على درجات: درجة تعريض، درجة مؤقتة بوقت معين، درجة محرمة نهائيًّا، التعريض يبينه لنا الأخ، تحريم الخمر بالتعريض؟
* طالب: قال الله تعالى: (...).
* الشيخ: لا.
* طالب آخر: قوله تعالى: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾ [They ask you about wine and gambling] [البقرة ٢١٩].
* الشيخ: قوله تعالى: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ التحريم ما هو الإباحة.
* طلبة: التعريض.
* الشيخ: التعريض ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾، فهنا لما قال: ﴿فِيهِمَا إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثْمُهُمَا أَكْبَرُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِمَا﴾ [In them is great sin and [some] benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit] العاقل ما يفعل.
التحريم في وقت معين في قوله تعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾؟
* طالب: ﴿لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَى حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ﴾ [Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying] [النساء ٤٣].
* الشيخ: نعم، ﴿حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ﴾، فهنا حرم شرب الخمر في وقت قريب من الصلاة؛ لأنه إذا شرب في وقت قريب من الصلاة لزم أن تأتي الصلاة وهو سكران.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 87–88 (part 2 of 3):

Third: the final prohibition in the words of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificial] stones, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it﴾ [al-Ma'idah 90].
So what does this make clear?
* Students: The wisdom of legislation (hikmat al-tashri').
* The Shaykh: The wisdom of legislation in the Islamic sharia. Does this wisdom still apply today? That is: if we see a person drinking intoxicants, may we say, "Give up intoxicants gradually," or should we say, "Now"?
* Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: If the second is possible, there is no harm. But if he says it is not possible, then we tell him gradually. Likewise with smoking tobacco: gradually, if nothing else is possible, and there is no harm in that, since when perfection is unattainable we take up what is possible little by little. We have remained with what?
The third category: the equivalent (al-musawi), such as the change of direction from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah. Someone may say: what is the benefit of this?
We say: this abrogation can only be for a reason. For example, which is more noble, the Ka'bah or Bayt al-Maqdis?
There is no doubt that the Ka'bah is superior. But even if we suppose there is no difference between them at all, its benefit is the testing of the accountable person: does he follow the sharia of God, or does he follow his desires?
He says: why does God abrogate this to that when they are equal? I will do as I wish.
So the benefit of abrogation to an equal is what? Testing the accountable person: whether he submits completely to the sharia of God or follows his own desires. With this we have concluded what we wished to discuss on the topic of abrogation.
* A student: The wisdom of abrogation to what is lighter.
* The Shaykh: Did we not mention it?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: Yes. The wisdom of abrogation from the more severe to the lighter is very clear: it is lightening the burden upon the Ummah.
* * *
The Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors﴾ [al-Ma'idah 87].
These are three sentences, or rather four. The first: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Opening the address with a call indicates its importance, because the call requires the addressee's attention. Addressing them with the description of faith indicates that what will be mentioned consists of qualities of faith, and that opposing it is a deficiency in faith. Moreover, there is an incitement to comply, for when you describe a person with a quality in order to command or forbid him, this is a form of incitement through that quality. Hence you say to someone: "You are a man, how can you do such-and-such?!"
Your saying "You are a man" means: the requirement of manliness is what? That he not do it. And you say: "O so-and-so, you are generous, and this is a beggar," meaning: give to him.
The second sentence: ﴿do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾. This is a prohibition, ﴿do not prohibit﴾, meaning: do not make it forbidden. Prohibiting what Allah has made lawful divides into three categories, and let us examine which is meant: a statement (khabar), a performative act (insha'), or refraining (imtina').
The statement: that one says, "Sheep is forbidden," reporting. To this we say: you are lying. Why? Because sheep is lawful, and he claimed falsely that it is forbidden.
The performative act: prohibiting what Allah has made lawful, as the people of the pre-Islamic era did with the sa'ibah, the wasilah, and the ham. ﴿And they say: what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females﴾ [al-An'am 139]. This prohibition is what? A performative act; that is, he intends to rule that this thing is forbidden to all people. This is what the noble verse targets, and its reality is judging by other than the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
The third: refraining. That is, one intends to abstain. He does not mean that it is forbidden, nor does he intend to issue a ruling of prohibition on it, nor does he intend to report it; rather he intends only to abstain. Its ruling is the ruling of an oath, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tahrim 1]. Have you understood now, or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Clear? If he says, "This bread is forbidden to me," intending to abstain, and he did not mean that its ruling is forbidden in the sharia of God, nor that he is reporting that it is forbidden, but he wished to abstain, then its ruling is the ruling of an oath. The evidence: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ [al-Tahrim 1–2].
These are three categories of prohibition: reporting, performative, and refraining. Which is meant? The performative. For this reason He said: ﴿do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾, because it is good, and because it is lawful. How then would you prohibit it?!
﴿And do not transgress﴾, that is, do not exceed your limits, for a person has limits. His making lawful and unlawful is transgression. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to attribute falsehood to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 116].
﴿And do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors﴾ is the third sentence. He, the Mighty and Majestic, informed that He does not love transgressors, whether in His right or in the rights of His servants, because Allah is just, the most judicious of judges, so He does not like anyone to transgress, neither in His right nor in the rights of the servants.
﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good﴾ [al-Ma'idah 88].
﴿Eat﴾ is an imperative verb, and in its meaning it is shared between permissibility, obligation, and recommendation. Whoever's life depends on eating, eating is obligatory for him. Whoever is in need but not in dire necessity, eating is recommended for him. Whoever is not in need and not compelled, the command is for permissibility.
﴿Of what Allah has provided for you﴾, that is, of what He has given you.
﴿Lawful﴾, that is, in the state of being lawful, meaning made lawful; it is a verbal noun in the sense of a passive participle.
﴿Good﴾, that is, not vile. Is the attribute here an inherent attribute, meaning that every lawful thing is good, or does the meaning mean lawful and good in its acquisition, so that the meaning is that it is lawful in itself and good in how it is acquired?
The second is preferable, because when it is uncertain whether the statement is establishing (mu'assis) or emphasizing (mu'akkid), it is more appropriate to take it as establishing. So we say: ﴿lawful﴾ meaning made lawful by Allah, and ﴿good﴾ meaning in terms of acquisition.
﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, adhere to the piety of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
﴿In whom you are believers﴾. This is an exhortation to piety: that is, as long as you are believers in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, fear Him. In the words ﴿in whom you are believers﴾ there is a nominal sentence indicating stability: that is, faith in Allah has been established among you, and if that is so, then fear Allah.
* There are benefits in these two verses. Among them: the prohibition of making unlawful the good things Allah has made lawful, by His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 87]. Does this prohibition encompass the three categories we mentioned?
Yes, it encompasses them, but some are more severe than others. The performative prohibition is the most severe, since it is a sharing with Allah in His ruling. The reporting prohibition is forbidden because it is a lie. The refraining prohibition is also forbidden, because Allah rebuked His Prophet, peace be upon him, in His words: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ [al-Tahrim 1]; and because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever swears, let him swear by Allah or remain silent"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2679) and Muslim (1646/3), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]].
* Among the benefits of this verse: the prohibition of transgression, that is, exceeding limits in whose right? In the right of Allah and in the rights of the servants.
* Also: an indication that prohibiting what Allah has made lawful is a form of transgression, since Allah said: "do not prohibit and do not transgress," which indicates that this is a form of transgression. And which is more severe: to prohibit the lawful, or to permit the unlawful?
* Students: The first.
* The Shaykh: To prohibit the lawful, because prohibiting the lawful is constricting the servants of Allah without knowledge, while permitting the unlawful, if it is assumed to be unlawful, is based on the original ruling. What is the original ruling concerning things? Permissibility, except for the legislated matters, where the original stance is caution.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication of the favor of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, upon His servants in what He has made lawful for them.
﴿The good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾. Had Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed, He could have prohibited for us, He could have prohibited for us good things made lawful for us, just as He prohibited them for the Children of Israel, when He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them﴾ [al-Nisa' 160]. That is, because of their wrongdoing and disobedience, Allah prohibited good things for them. Legislative prohibition of good things due to wrongdoing is like the decreed (qadari) prohibition due to wrongdoing. A person may be deprived of good things by a decreed prohibition because of his disobedience, such as a man who, when he eats meat, is affected and becomes ill; this means he must avoid eating meat. Is this prohibition decreed or legislated?
* Students: Decreed.
* The Shaykh: Decreed. Someone who, for example, has diabetes: if he eats sweets, his sugar increases and harms him, so he avoids sugar. What is this prohibition?
* Students: Decreed.
* The Shaykh: Decreed. So do not think that prohibition due to sins is only legislative; it is also decreed.
Among decreed prohibitions: that Allah withholds the produce of the earth because of sins, as He said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done that they might return﴾ [al-Rum 41].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's love, by His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors﴾.
If someone says: this is a negation, not an affirmation?
We say: negating His love for transgressors indicates the establishment of the basic attribute of love. Had He not loved at all, there would be no benefit in negating His love for transgressors, since He does not love in the first place. Those who say that Allah does not love did not deny love entirely; rather they distorted it. So the verse contains a refutation of those who deny the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such as whom?
The Ash'arites, who are the closest of the people of ta'til (denial of attributes) to Ahl al-Sunnah, deny Allah's love. They say: Allah does not love anyone; He does not love even the Messenger? They say: did not our Messenger say: "Allah has taken me as a khalil (intimate friend)"? They say: yes, but He increased his reward; for love is reward, or the will of reward. They interpreted it as will, because they affirm will. The reality is that we ask Allah to pardon them and to guide their living: they have been deprived of the delight of Allah's love. When a person feels that Allah loves him, he rejoices and grows in love for acts of obedience and in aversion to sins, because he knows that his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, loves him from above the seven heavens. If the meaning were merely that He rewards him, then He rewards any of the servants who deserves reward; so they were deprived of the delight of Allah's love because they denied it.
So the main point is that the verse affirms love. If someone asks: what is the way to establish it?
We say: because negating it from the transgressors indicates the establishment of its root; for if its root were not established, there would be no benefit in negating it from the transgressors. This is like the argument of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, for the seeing of Allah from the negation of seeing for the wicked, when the Exalted said: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 15].
He said: if all creation were veiled from Allah, there would be no benefit in negating the veiling of vision from the wicked. The negation of vision from the wicked is evidence of its establishment for whom?
* Students: For the righteous.
* A student: For the pious.
* The Shaykh: For the righteous.
* Among the benefits of the following verse: commanding a person to eat of what Allah has provided. Its opposite is not eating. Not eating of what Allah has provided has three categories. First: abstaining from eating when there is fear of death if he does not eat; here abstaining from eating is forbidden, because a person is obligated to save himself. From this we know the foolishness of those who go on hunger strikes, and we know their foolishness in their minds and their error in their religion. Some of them are hospitalized like corpses. This is unquestionably forbidden. Second: if there is no dire necessity to eat, but he needs to eat to strengthen the body, then eating here is what? Recommended, because if he abstains he would not die, but he has a need, so we say: do not deprive yourself. Third: what? Abstaining from eating out of asceticism, and this is forbidden, and it is said to him: eat of what Allah has permitted for you. Some people abstain from good food out of piety and asceticism; what do we say about them?
We say: this is an error. The best of creation, Muhammad, peace be upon him, used to choose good food. Did they not bring him good dates instead of poor dates? Yes, and yet he did not forbid them; he did not say, "Why do you bring me good food?" Rather he guided them to bring good food, but by a permissible means.
So for some people to abstain from good things out of piety and asceticism, we say: no. You are now deviating from piety, because piety is following the sharia, and asceticism is abandoning what does not benefit in the Hereafter, while following the sharia is what benefits in the Hereafter. So you are now neither ascetic nor pious. Yes, if it is assumed that a person, in his particular case, finds in himself that if he chose good things it would lead to arrogance and exultation, then here we may say: abandon good things lest you be afflicted with arrogance and exultation. But we treat that beforehand with another remedy: we say, it is not permissible that enjoying the blessings of Allah lead you to arrogance and exultation. If you are unable and insist that it will lead you, then we say: now abandon them. For the reality of some people is that when they wear fine clothes, the fine cloak, the fine ghutrah, they swell up and become haughty and arrogant. To such a person we say: abandon this, or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: We say: abandon it. Whereas we say: do not be arrogant. But if he says, "I am unable," we say: praise be to Allah; leave these for those who do not become arrogant when they wear them. But this is a specific remedy, just as we treat the person who is affected by eating good things in another way, by saying: leave them and let them be for those who are not affected by them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory for a person to have good food, because of the Exalted's words: what? ﴿lawful and good﴾. So earnings that are unlawful, even if in themselves lawful, for example earning dirhams, where dirhams are originally a lawful acquisition: if he earns them through something unlawful, we say: they are unlawful for you, and it is forbidden for you to eat from them. Why?
Because they are not good. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever gives charity from something good, and Allah accepts only what is good"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1410) and Muslim (1014/63), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording.]].
His words "from something good" mean: good in its acquisition and in itself, for Allah accepts such charity.
Now, if money is unlawful because of how it was acquired, is it lawful for someone other than the earner if he acquired it by a permissible means?
The answer: yes. This principle is indicated by the fact that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, "ate from the food of the Jews"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2617) and Muslim (2190/45), from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: a Jewish woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it.]], and they are known for what?
* Students: For usury.
* The Shaykh: For consuming usury, illicit gain, and bribery. And he ate from it, because it was obtained by a permissible means: he was permitted to do so, or it was given to him as a gift. Except if you know that this property is the very property of another man, as with a thief who steals a sheep and slaughters it to host you while you know he stole it. In that case it is not permissible for you to eat it, because this is unlawful in its very essence, meaning that this earner did not own this item, so it is not permissible for you to eat it. But if someone invites you to a feast, and he is known for having all his wealth unlawful, acquired through plain usury or through usury disguised by trickery, is it permissible for you to eat from it?

Yes, I may eat from it, unless I know that if I refrain from accepting his invitation and eating his food, that will become a cause for his repentance. In that case, yes, it is not permissible for me to accept his invitation or to eat from his food, because when people see that he has been boycotted, and they do not accept his invitations or eat his food, this will undoubtedly affect him, unless his heart is dead.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: belief in Allah, mighty and majestic, necessarily entails taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him, as shown by His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾. That is: because of your belief, taqwa is binding upon you. True belief necessarily entails taqwa. Whoever claims to be a believer but does not fear Allah is either entirely lacking in faith or deficient in faith.

If someone says: "He commits sins, and when it is said to him, 'O so-and-so, fear Allah, do not disobey Allah,' he stands up, strikes his chest and says: 'The taqwa is here, the taqwa is here, the taqwa is here.' What do we say to him?"

We say: this is the statement of the Messenger ﷺ, there is no doubt about it, and we have no doubt about it. But if taqwa were truly where he claims, it would have affected his hand, foot, eye and tongue, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599 / 107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] So if there were taqwa in that place, it would have shown upon his limbs (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 89 (part 1 of 3):

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the vain oaths in your oaths﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 89].

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable﴾ means He will not punish you or call you to account.

﴿for the vain oaths in your oaths﴾: al-laghw (vain, unintended) is what is not intended. The evidence is His saying: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what you have intended in oaths﴾.

We have mentioned that one of the methods of tafsir (Qur'anic interpretation) is to set a word that is obscure beside something clear, so that its meaning becomes evident from what it is paired with. We gave an example of this: the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿So go forth in separate groups (thubat) or go forth all together﴾ [An-Nisa': 71]. The word ثُبَاتٍ (thubat) is not understood quickly, but when you compare it with its counterpart, ﴿or go forth all together﴾, it becomes clear that the meaning of ثُبَاتٍ is "individually, dispersed." Here, He says: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what you have intended﴾.

So al-laghw is that which is uttered by the tongue without intention. This happens often. Your companion says to you: "Do you want us to go to so-and-so?" and you say: "No, by Allah, I do not want to go to him." Or he says: "Go and greet so-and-so," and you say: "No, by Allah, I will not go," in the manner of idle speech and not of oath-swearing. An oath of this kind, by its name, is vain, and no ruling follows from it. Also, avoiding such things can be difficult.

The phrase ﴿in your oaths﴾: (yamin, pl. aymān) means an oath.

﴿But He holds you accountable for what you have intended﴾ means for what you have deliberately bound yourselves to. In this word there are three readings: عَاقَدْتُمُ ('aqadtum) and عَقَدْتُمُ ('aqadtum), and the meaning is one: for what you intended to bind yourselves to of oaths.

﴿Its expiation is feeding ten needy persons﴾ (kaffarah, expiation). Is the expiation due when you swear, or when you swear and then break the oath?

The second: that is, the verse contains an omitted element. The expiation is due if you break the oath, meaning the expiation that atones for it, and no accountability attaches to it, is feeding ten needy persons. Allah left the feeding unspecified, so it is referred to custom (al-'urf). This is because we have a principle: whatever is stated in general terms in the Qur'an and Sunnah is interpreted according to people's custom.

﴿ten needy persons﴾: (miskin, pl. masakin) is one who does not have sufficient means. He is called miskin because poverty makes him still (askanahu). Typically the wealthy person is active, has a presence, meets people, speaks with them, takes and gives. The poor person is generally the opposite, so the poor man is called miskin.

﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ means not from the best nor from the worst, but from the average.

The words ﴿or clothing them﴾ are joined to ﴿feeding﴾.

﴿or clothing them﴾: kiswah (clothing) is what a person covers his body with. Clothing varies with times, places and circumstances. That is why, during the seasons of Hajj and 'Umrah, you see a great difference in people's clothing. So this is referred to custom. In our country, this clothing consists of a shirt, trousers, a ghutrah and a taqiyah. This is the clothing; if any of these is missing, the clothing is incomplete. Allah's words ﴿or clothing them﴾ are not restricted to the average of what you clothe your families with, so one takes whatever counts as clothing.

﴿or freeing a slave﴾: that is, freeing him. Manumission is called tahrir (liberation) because the slave is freed by it from ownership, the ownership of his master, who would oblige him to be an obedient servant. In the verse there is an ascent from the easier to the more difficult, for if you look, you will generally find that feeding is easier than clothing, and clothing is easier than freeing a slave.

﴿So whoever does not find﴾ means: whoever does not find the feeding, the clothing, or the freeing, or finds it but does not find anyone to feed, clothe or free. For example, the community may be wealthy, all of them rich, with no poor person among them, and there may be no slaves who could be freed. Then he moves to the fourth category of expiation, which is fasting for three days. Allah did not restrict these days to consecutive fasting. When fasting is mentioned without qualification, it is unrestricted and does not require consecutiveness. The evidence for this is that when Allah, Exalted is He, wants fasting to be consecutive, He specifies it, as in the verse of zihar (a type of divorce formula): ﴿So whoever does not find [means], then fasting two months consecutively﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 4], and as in the verse of killing: ﴿So whoever does not find [means], then fasting two months consecutively﴾ [An-Nisa': 92]. When it is unspecified, consecutiveness is not obligatory. However, a reading of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) requires consecutiveness; he recited: "fasting three days consecutively." In this way, the reading of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud restricts this unqualified wording: "fasting three consecutive days."

﴿That is the expiation of your oaths﴾: the referent of ﴿that﴾ is these four: feeding ten needy persons, clothing them, freeing a slave, or fasting three days, according to the order and the option stated in the verse.

﴿the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾ means when you swear and break the oath. As for when you do not break it, nothing is due from you. So if a person swears not to do something and does not do it, nothing is due from him. Or if he swears to do something and does it, nothing is due from him.

He says: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾. It has three meanings:

The first meaning: guard them against breaking; that is, be careful not to break them.

The second: guard your oaths; that is, do not swear often. Do not make them cheap. Do not swear about everything, but swear only when there is need or necessity.

The third: guard them by not neglecting the expiation for them.

These three meanings are correct. They do not contradict one another, so the verse includes all of them.

﴿Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you﴾: ﴿thus﴾ means like that clarification. In that case, the kaf (ك, "like") is an absolute object, since it is added to the verbal noun. That is, Allah makes His signs clear to you in the manner of that clarification. The "signs" here means the legal signs, since the context indicates this. There is no doubt that Allah has clarified for us both the legal signs and the cosmic signs. In His creation there are great signs, as He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain. And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 20–21].

﴿so that you may be grateful﴾: (la'alla) indicates reasoning, meaning: so that you may thank Allah, Exalted is He, for the clarification of the signs. Gratitude (shukr) is performing obedience to the Benefactor. This is the most comprehensive definition given of it. It includes performing obedience to the Benefactor in speech, in action, and in belief. So the locus of gratitude is threefold: the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. On this is the poet's saying:

"Blessings have given you from me three things:
my hand, my tongue, and the hidden heart."

This is the most comprehensive verse concerning oaths. Otherwise, something similar appears in Al-Baqarah, such as His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the vain oaths in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 225]. But this verse is detailed.

* Among its many benefits: first, the breadth of Allah's forbearance and pardon, in that He negated accountability for vain oaths. This is because they are frequent and it is difficult to guard against them. This is based on what? On the fact that the intended meaning is oaths that are not intended, which occur in the course of speech.

Some scholars said: among vain oaths is swearing about a past matter that one believes to be true but which did not happen, such as saying: "By Allah, so-and-so arrived in the town yesterday," based on what? Based on his seeing a man who resembled him, so he thought it was him, and swore that he had arrived when he had not. But the correct view is otherwise, that this is not vain, because he intended to bind himself: he swore by Allah that the man had come, and said: "By Allah, he came, by Allah, I saw him." But this involves no breaking of the oath, because the man swore about what he believed, and he still believes it. He says: "I still think this," so he swore about what he thought. For this reason, according to the correct view, no distinction is made between past and future. A future example is saying: "By Allah, Zayd will certainly arrive tomorrow," based on what he heard from reports, or from what he heard from the speaker that he would arrive tomorrow, and he said: "By Allah, Zayd will certainly arrive tomorrow." Then the day passed and he did not arrive. Here, there is no breaking of the oath on him, although he did bind himself and swore. But we say: the man swore about what was in his mind, and he says: "I still think this," even if the day ends and he has not come. He is still on his supposition. That reality turns out contrary to his supposition is not up to him, nor is it from his action or his disposal. Therefore, if he said: "By Allah, Zayd will certainly arrive tomorrow," based on the belief that he would compel him to arrive and he did not arrive, then he breaks the oath. Is this clear?

So the preponderant view is that an oath a person swears on the basis of his supposition is not vain oath. Vain oath is only that which is not intended.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the criterion is what is in the hearts. This is like the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended» [Reported by al-Bukhari (1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab]. Many rulings in oaths, divorce, sales, endowments and others are based on this. The evidence that the criterion is what is in the hearts is His saying: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what you have intended in oaths﴾, and in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿for what your hearts have earned﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: there is no breaking of an oath unless it was binding (mun'aqidah).

The scholars said: a binding oath is one where the intention is to bind oneself to a possible future matter. If the intention to bind is absent, it is vain. If one binds oneself to a past matter, it falls into three categories. Either he binds himself to a past matter that he is certain of. There is nothing due on him for this, but it is not appropriate except when there is need, such as saying: "By Allah, it rained yesterday in our town," and he knows that it rained. Is this permissible or not?

* Students: Permissible.

* The Shaykh: Permissible. But it is better not to do it except for need.

The second: he intends to bind himself to a past matter that he knows to be false. This is forbidden. For example, he says... give an example.

* Student: The perjurious oath (yamin ghamus), he means?

* The Shaykh: No, I am not asking you about the description of the oath. Give an example.

* Student: On?

* The Shaykh: On what I mentioned.

* Student: On the one that (...).

* The Shaykh: On what I mentioned.

* Student: Like: "By Allah, I prayed yesterday in the Masjid al-Haram," and he did not pray.

* The Shaykh: Yes, correct. Is that his example?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, such as saying: "By Allah, I prayed yesterday in the Masjid al-Haram," when he did not pray. Without doubt, this person is sinful, because he combined two sins: the first sin is lying, and the second sin is treating the oath by Allah lightly. An oath, as we all know, is the affirmation of a matter by mentioning something revered. But is this a perjurious oath, or does the perjurious oath only involve consuming wealth wrongfully or aggressing against others?

* Student: The second.

* The Shaykh: The first opinion is that every false oath about a past matter is a perjurious oath. There is no doubt that an oath about a past matter, when he knows it is false, is forbidden, and is more severe than if he had reported it without an oath. But what appears to be correct is that the perjurious oath is that by which a person swears deceitfully in order to seize the property of a Muslim. For example: he claims against a person that he owes him a thousand riyals, and he brings a witness, a false witness, and swears. Here he is judged to receive the thousand. We call this oath a perjurious oath, because by it he seized the property of a Muslim. Or he denies by it the property of a Muslim, such as when he is claimed against for a thousand riyals and says: "Never, you have nothing from me," and swears to this. This is a perjurious oath. So the preponderant view is that the perjurious oath is that by which the property of a Muslim is seized.

The third category of swearing about the past: he swears about a past matter that he believes to be true, but which is not true. Our jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, call this vain oath. That is, they consider it part of vain oaths. The correct view is that it is not vain oath, but rather an oath that he fulfilled, because he swore about what?

* Students: His supposition.

* The Shaykh: About his supposition, and he still holds to his supposition. Nevertheless, it is better not to swear about something on the basis of supposition unless there is need. Alright, we said: the oath that is intended to bind oneself to a possible future matter. What is the opposite of possible? Impossible. An oath about this is not binding, because if it is about bringing it into existence, what do we say to him?

We say: if it is about bringing it into existence, we say: this is not possible, so he breaks it immediately, and expiation is due from him, because he cannot bring it into existence. If it is about its non-existence, there is no expiation in it, because this is the reality.

Some scholars said: swearing about the impossible has no expiation at all, because swearing about something whose existence is impossible is vain, so there is no breaking of it.

There remain some matters: is it required that it be by choice? That is, that he swears by his own choice?

The answer: yes, it is required that his oath be by choice. If he is forced to swear, the oath is not binding. But here there is a question: if he is compelled to swear and swears intending the oath, that is, if he is compelled and swears, either he intends by the oath to repel the compulsion, or he intends the oath but was compelled to it. These are two cases. Sometimes he swears to repel compulsion from himself and to escape the aggression of the coercer. Sometimes he swears intending the oath, but compulsion led him to it. As for when he intends to repel compulsion, there is no doubt that no breaking is incurred by him. Why?

Because he did not intend the oath at all. He intended escape from the one who compelled him. As for when he swears intending the oath, but he was driven to it, there is a difference of opinion. The correct view is that it is like the first. This is especially so when it comes from an ordinary person. When an ordinary person is compelled to do something, he does it, and it does not occur to him that he did it to repel compulsion, or because he was compelled to it. Is that not so?

* Students: Indeed.

* The Shaykh: This would only happen to a student of knowledge who understands. So the correct view is that the oath of a compelled person is not binding, whether he intended by it to repel compulsion or...?

* Student: The binding of the oath.

* The Shaykh: The binding of the oath is for compulsion. Is it required that he be legally accountable (mukallaf), or is it not required?

The correct view is that it is required that he be legally accountable, because one who is not legally accountable is not obligated to anything, neither by the origin of the Shari'ah nor by binding himself. For this reason, a vow made by him is not binding, since he is not legally accountable. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «The pen is lifted from three» [Reported by Abu Dawud (4398) from the hadith of 'A'ishah]. So if someone who is ten years old swears not to buy a certain thing, then reaches maturity and buys it, does he break the oath or not?

* Student: No.

* The Shaykh: No, because his oath is not binding. If he swore while legally accountable and mature, and then broke it while he was not legally accountable, does he break it?

* Students: He breaks it.

* The Shaykh: Does he break it or not?

* Students: He breaks it.

* Student: He does not break it.

* The Shaykh: Think about it now.

* Student: He does not break it.

* The Shaykh: He swore while legally accountable, and broke it while not legally accountable.

* Students: He does not break it.

* The Shaykh: Nothing is due from him?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Is this conceivable?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes?

* Students: A madman.

* The Shaykh: A sane person who became insane. Correct. So the oath is not binding from one who is not a mature sane person, because he is not legally accountable, and an oath involves a kind of obligation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: what we pointed out at the beginning, which is the consideration of intention and purpose. Many rulings follow from this, and among the most important, which often occurs, is when a man divorces his wife on the basis that she was speaking with men on the phone, and then it becomes clear that she was speaking with her relatives, her mahram. Here, does the divorce take effect or not?

* Students: It does not take effect.

* The Shaykh: It does not take effect. A man swears not to enter this town because he believes its ruler is oppressive, so he says: "What do I have to do with an oppressive ruler!" Then it becomes clear that its ruler is not oppressive. Is anything due from him?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, because he only swore intending that this attribute was what prevented him from entering the town. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what you have intended in oaths﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: breaking an oath is not appropriate unless it is for good, because of His saying: ﴿Its expiation﴾, and expiation is only in exchange for a sin or something similar. For this reason, at the end of the verse He says: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 89 (part 2 of 3):

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the expiation for breaking an oath is a choice among three things: feeding the poor, clothing them, or freeing a slave. This is the optional arrangement. If one cannot do any of these, then fasting for three days. What is widespread among the common people, that the expiation for an oath is fasting, is a mistake. Students of knowledge should clarify to people that fasting is not permitted for someone who is able to do one of the three options mentioned before it.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: feeding (al-iṭ‘ām) is unrestricted and does not require transferring ownership (al-tamlīk). Allah, Exalted is He, did not say "fa-lil-masākīn" (then to the poor). Had He said that, ownership would be required, as He said regarding zakat: ﴿Zakat is only for the poor﴾ [al-Tawbah 60]. But here He said "feeding ten needy persons." So whatever constitutes feeding is sufficient. If he provides them with lunch or dinner, it suffices without doubt, because it truly applies that he fed them. If he gives them something they cook themselves, that is, they prepare it on their own, does it suffice or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: The apparent ruling is that it suffices, because if he gives them, for example, enough grain and meat, and similar things with which grain is prepared as food, it truly applies that he fed ten needy persons.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: if he feeds someone who eats food, even a child, it suffices, based on His saying: ﴿the feeding of ten needy persons﴾. If the one is a child, the needy person does not eat food. Would it be sufficient to give him milk? No, because this contradicts the apparent meaning of the wording.
If someone says: "If I cannot find ten needy persons, and in the town I find only five, should I switch to fasting or repeat the feeding for the five?"
There is a possibility, because His saying: ﴿But whoever does not find﴾ refers to what came before. And what came before was what number?
* Student: Ten.
* The Shaykh: Ten. ﴿But whoever does not find﴾, meaning whoever does not find ten, ﴿then fasting for three days.﴾ It may also be said: as long as he finds needy persons, he repeats the feeding for them. So if he finds five, he repeats it twice.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah in what He legislates for His servants. If you compare the feeding of ten needy persons, clothing them, and freeing a slave, you will find a great difference. But Allah has wisdom in what He legislates. So no objector can say: "Why were they not twenty? Why were they not three, like fasting, for example?"
We say: this is the ruling of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and this is among the matters of worship (ta‘abbudī), meaning that determining the number of those to whom expiations are given is a matter of worship in which reason has no role, like the number of prayers.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: what is obligatory for a person is the middle (wasaṭ). For example, zakat on sheep is obligatory at the middle level. What is obligatory? 
* Student: The middle.
* The Shaykh: The middle. Zakat on fruits is also obligatory at the middle level.
* From this great lesson follows the justice of Islam, because the middle contains no injustice either to the one who is obligated or to the one to whom it is owed, and this is undoubtedly part of justice.
If someone says: "What do you say if he feeds them from the best of what is available? Is that permissible or not?"
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It is permissible, because that is more perfect.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the obligation to spend on one's family, based on His saying: ﴿from the middle of what you feed your families﴾. It means that this is a settled matter: that a man feeds his family. Undoubtedly, a man is obligated to spend on his family. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [from their wealth]﴾ [al-Nisa’ 34]. Continue.
* Student: ﴿And what they spend﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And what they spend from their wealth﴾.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: clothing is also unrestricted, like feeding. Whatever is called clothing suffices, and this varies according to circumstances, times, places, and peoples. Can we also say that there is a correspondence between the two kinds of covering: the inner and the outer? Because feeding covers the inner, and clothing covers the outer. We may say this, because Allah, Exalted is He, said to Adam (peace be upon him): ﴿Indeed, it is [granted] for you that you will not go hungry therein or be naked﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 118]. Hunger is nakedness of the inner body, the emptiness of the stomach. And nakedness is what? The nakedness of the outer body. He said: ﴿And that you will not thirst therein or be exposed to the sun.﴾ Thirst is the heat of the inner body, and ﴿exposed to the sun﴾ is the heat of the outer body. It may occur to weak minds that the wording should have been: "that you will not hunger therein or thirst, and not be naked or exposed to the sun," since nakedness exposes the body to the sun and clothing covers it. But the great eloquence lies in what the Qur’an brought.
* Student: Shaykh, does swearing by other than Allah fall under vain oaths (al-laghw)?
* The Shaykh: No. Swearing by other than Allah is not valid at all.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is not valid at all, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected." [[Related by Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of ‘Aishah.]]
Swearing by other than Allah is not in accordance with the command of Allah and His Messenger.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. The verse: "Favors from me have bestowed upon you three things..." What does it mean? Three things.
* The Shaykh: No. "Three things" means that you have acquired three things from me:
....................... ∗∗∗ "my hand, my tongue, and the veiled heart."
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No. "Have bestowed upon you" means that you have acquired this: you have acquired my speech, my heart, and my actions. The meaning is clear, and it is supported by the word "al-ḍamīra al-muḥajjaba" (the veiled conscience), which is in the accusative case.
* Student: What confused me is that it is in the accusative. If it were in the nominative, it would not have been confusing.
* The Shaykh: Yes. I say: your understanding is what caused the confusion. The poet is addressing those whom he addresses, saying: your favors upon me have made you possessors of my heart and my tongue, so he praises you as if you were his masters. Likewise, I serve you with my limbs.
* Student: (...) with his heart, his tongue, and his limbs.
* The Shaykh: But these people possessed him by that, they possessed these three things by his favors. This is the meaning. I see no problem in the meaning. As for the wording, his saying "(and the veiled conscience)" requires it to be in the accusative. (...)
* * *
Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintended in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have intended [in] the oaths you deliberately made.﴾ Are there readings for it?
* Student: There are three readings. The first: ﴿‘aqqadtum﴾ is a reading. The second: ﴿‘āqadtum﴾. The third: ﴿‘aqadtum﴾.
* The Shaykh: Good. All of them have one meaning. Regarding His saying: ﴿then its expiation is feeding﴾, is there an omission in it?
* Student: No, (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, because if it were omitted..
* Student: It is not permissible (...).
* The Shaykh: Simply by the context, the sentence is complete with His saying: ﴿feeding ten needy persons.﴾ Is it restricted to a specific quantity or type?
* Student: (...) unrestricted.
* The Shaykh: Good. Is ﴿from the middle of what you feed﴾ not a restriction?
* Student: There is a restriction in this.
* The Shaykh: Because it is from the middle of what we feed our families. Is it required in feeding that we transfer ownership of it to them?
* Student: It is not required.
* The Shaykh: It is not required according to the preponderant opinion. Indeed, feeding them cooked food is better than transferring ownership to them, because it conforms to the apparent meaning of the verse.
His saying: ﴿But whoever does not find﴾, find what?
* Student: Whoever does not find (...).
* The Shaykh: Correct. That includes whoever does not find someone to feed, clothe, or free, and whoever has nothing to feed, clothe, or free with. Are the days consecutive?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Why did we not say that they are consecutive even though it is not stated?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because if Allah had intended consecutiveness, He would have mentioned it, right? But we say that the reading of Ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him) restricts this.
What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾?
* Student: Guard them from breaking them.
* The Shaykh: Guard them from breaking them. That is one meaning.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, do not swear too often.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Meaning: if you break them, then make expiation. May Allah bless you.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: it is necessary to feed this number, that is ten, and to clothe them. If one repeats feeding the same person ten days, it does not suffice, because Allah specified the number, and it is obligatory to follow what Allah specified. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have said that sometimes the recipient is specified without specifying the amount given, as in this verse. How many are fed?
* Student: Ten.
* The Shaykh: And the feeding is not restricted. It is not said: a ṣā‘ or a mudd. Sometimes the amount given is specified without specifying the recipient, as in the zakat al-fitr (charity at the end of Ramadan). The amount given is specified: how much? A ṣā‘ of food. The recipient is not specified. Therefore it is permissible to give one ṣā‘ of charity to several poor people, and it is permissible to give a meal to one person.
The third category: both the amount given and the recipient are specified, as in the ransom for harm (fidyat al-adhā). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "Feed six needy persons, half a ṣā‘ for each needy person." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1816) and Muslim (1201/85), with similar wording, from the hadith of Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah.]] So the amount given and the recipient are both specified.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the expiation for oaths is not given to those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu’allafah qulūbuhum), nor to debtors (al-gharimīn). It is only feeding the needy, just as we say this also regarding zakat al-fitr, which is given only to the poor.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the perfection of Allah's justice, Mighty and Majestic, in obligating the middle. Because if He had obligated the best and highest, it would have been harmful to whom?
* Student: To the giver.
* The Shaykh: Yes, to the one who swears. If He had obligated the lowest, it would have been harmful to the one who receives the gift.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: clothing is unrestricted, not specified by any particular item or number. For example, one is not required to give two garments, three, or ten. Whatever fulfills this name, which is clothing, discharges the obligation.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: an indication that breaking an oath is a serious matter. For this reason, only freeing a slave expiates it, through which the one who frees is freed from the Fire. But Allah, in His forbearance and mercy, lightened things for His servants. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿or freeing a slave﴾.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: determining acts of worship in quantity, type, and manner is left to the Shari‘ah. That is why feeding ten needy persons and fasting three days are not equivalent or comparable, is that not so?
If we look at the expiation for zihar (kaffarat al-zihār), the obligation there is two consecutive months of fasting. If one cannot, then feeding sixty needy persons. Here, the feeding for the poor corresponds to one day of fasting. But here the situation is different. Perhaps the reason, and Allah knows best, is that in the expiation for zihar, feeding is a substitute for fasting, because whoever cannot fast feeds. And if it is a substitute for fasting, the ruling is that each day of fasting is substituted by feeding one needy person, as with someone who is unable to fast due to a permanent incapacity that is not expected to end, who feeds one needy person for each day. But in the expiation for oaths and the ransom for harm, the matter is not like that, because the matter there is optional. Each of the types of expiation is an independent category in itself. Have you understood this or not? Feeding in the expiation for zihar is a substitute for fasting. Have you understood this or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Fasting is two months, and usually it is sixty days. So its substitute was feeding sixty needy persons, just as we say in Ramadan: if a person is unable to fast due to a continuous incapacity, he feeds what for each day? One needy person for each day, because feeding is a substitute for fasting. In the expiation for oaths, it is feeding ten or fasting three days. But each one is independent by itself, is that not so?
* Students: Indeed.
* The Shaykh: Since each one is independent by itself, each one has become characterized by a description suited to it, according to the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The ransom for harm is feeding six needy persons or fasting three days. Because fasting three days is not a substitute for feeding six needy persons, and feeding six needy persons is not a substitute for fasting. Rather, the person has the choice between this and that, so each one is independent by itself, meaning each is a category independent in itself. This is what has become clear to us, and Allah knows best what He legislated.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: refuting the common people's misconception that the expiation for oaths is three days of fasting. For this reason you find some saying: "I will not fast three days," so fasting three days prevents him from breaking the oath. It is said: the principle is that what is obligatory is feeding ten needy persons.
If someone says: "Is it permissible to obligate the wealthy person to fast three days, because it is harder on him than feeding ten needy persons?"
* People: No.
* The Shaykh: This is not permissible. For this reason some scholars erred who obligated one of the kings, in the expiation for zihar, to fast two consecutive months. They said that this is harder on him than freeing a slave, because he is a sultan and a prince who can free ten slaves. But fasting two consecutive months is harder for him. It is said: this is an error, because it contradicts the explicit text, and Allah, glorified is He, loves that slaves be freed in what He has obligated.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: what is legislated is respecting oaths and guarding them. That is correct. But the Sunnah came with details on this. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will not swear to an oath and then see something else better than it, except that I make expiation for my oath and do what is better." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5518) and Muslim (1649/10), from the hadith of Abu Musa.]]
Based on this, we say: breaking an oath is divided into categories. Sometimes breaking it is obligatory, sometimes forbidden, sometimes recommended, and sometimes disliked. If a person swears not to pray with the congregation, then breaking the oath is obligatory. That is, he must pray and make expiation. If a wicked person swears to drink wine, what is the ruling? Breaking the oath is obligatory. If he swears to drink wine, we say: it is obligatory for you not to drink and to make expiation for your oath. But the difference between this and the first is that the first concerns abandoning an obligation, and this concerns doing a forbidden act. If someone swears not to visit his relative, and maintaining family ties is obligatory, what is the ruling on breaking the oath? It is obligatory. He must visit his relative and make expiation for his oath. And if someone swears to do a forbidden act?
* Students: Breaking the oath is obligatory.
* The Shaykh: Breaking the oath is obligatory. An example?
* Students: He drinks wine.
* The Shaykh: He swears to drink wine. We say: breaking the oath is obligatory, meaning: do not drink wine and make expiation. If he swears not to drink wine, then breaking the oath is forbidden, because if he drank wine, he would have committed a forbidden act. If someone swears not to eat onions, breaking the oath is disliked. Why? Because eating onions is disliked for someone who intends to pray. And if he swears not to pray the regular sunnah prayer before dawn, breaking the oath is recommended. We say: pray and make expiation.
So the principle is that breaking an oath is recommended when it is good, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said. Sometimes breaking it is obligatory and sometimes forbidden. The original ruling is that breaking an oath is permissible, but not breaking it is better, based on His saying: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾ [al-Ma’idah 89].
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has made clear to His servants from His signs everything they need, based on His saying: ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs﴾.
* Among its lessons: it is obligatory for us to thank Allah for making the signs clear, based on His saying: ﴿that you may be grateful﴾.
* Among its lessons: Allah's love for gratitude, since He made the signs clear for the sake of gratitude.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: knowledge is one of the blessings of Allah that we are obligated to thank. Because through the clarification of the signs, a person knows the signs of Allah. If Allah makes them clear so that we may thank Him for them, this shows that knowledge of the Shari‘ah and of the signs of Allah is a blessing that a person must thank, based on the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿that you may be grateful﴾.

* Among its benefits: the rationale (ta'lil) of God's rulings, the Mighty and Majestic, and that they are joined with wisdom (hikmah). This is because ﴿so that you may give thanks﴾ expresses purpose (ta'lil), and purpose conveys wisdom. Thus all of God's acts and all of His rulings are for a wisdom, but some of that wisdom is known and some of it is not known.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 90–91 (part 1 of 4):

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 90]. This verse combines a statement and a command. The statement is His saying: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan﴾, and the command is His saying: ﴿so avoid it that you may be successful﴾. In this verse, Allah begins the address with ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and this form of address has been repeated.
