He would never remain silent, because this man did not know that it had been prohibited, so how would he know it was impure? Thus it becomes clear that the impurity of intoxicants is moral impurity. Although only a few of the Ummah have held this, the majority of scholars are with the evidence, and the majority say it is sensorily impure. But as you have seen, the evidences now are clear that its impurity is moral.

Based on this: what about things that now contain alcohol, such as spirit, and similarly what is used to anoint wounds and the like? Are they impure or pure? Pure, because if the basis, which is intoxicants, is pure according to what has become clear to us from the Qur'an and Sunnah, then whatever contains some of it is even more fitting to be pure.

If it is said: Do you permit a person to perfume himself with these scents or to anoint himself with these ointments?

We say: when there is need, we permit it, and by God's praise there is no difficulty for us in this. For example, a wound needs to be swabbed with spirit or something else to make it easier to stitch with a needle. There is no doubt that this is permitted, because a doubtful ruling is permitted by need, even if its origin is prohibition.

If one is not in need but uses it as perfume, is this forbidden or not? We consider: His saying, may He be blessed and exalted, ﴿so avoid it﴾. Does it mean avoiding its drinking, which leads to harm, or avoiding it absolutely? We say: since God says ﴿so avoid it﴾, then ﴿Satan only wants﴾ to the end of the verse, we know that the command to avoid refers to avoiding drinking. There is no doubt about this; avoiding anything other than drinking is a matter of doubt. Caution (wara') requires that a person does not do this except out of need, that he does not anoint himself with these things except when necessary, such as sterilizing a wound and the like.

If someone says: If these scents contain a proportion of alcohol but it is small, say five percent, does it have an effect? The answer: It has no effect. Only what affects the mixture as a whole has an effect. If it does not affect, it is not forbidden, based on the case of a man who has a vessel of water into which an impurity has fallen but has not changed it. What is that water? It is pure, because it has not been affected. Accordingly, we say: if the proportion is small even in these scents, there is no doubt that they are permissible, because a small proportion has no effect.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of God, may He be blessed and exalted, toward His servants whom He created for His worship, since He warned them against everything harmful and explained the good outcomes to them, based on His saying ﴿so avoid it that you may be successful﴾.

Then God, may He be mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Satan only wants﴾ to the end.

* In this noble verse: affirmation of will (iradah) for Satan, based on His saying ﴿Satan only wants﴾. There is no doubt that he has will. Have you considered God's saying to the angels: ﴿Prostrate to Adam,﴾ so they prostrated except Iblis [al-Baqarah 2:34], and he argued with his Lord out of will or without will? Out of will. So Satan has will.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the evil will of Satan toward the children of Adam, which is to cause enmity and hatred among them, which necessitates division.

* Among its benefits: the division of the Ummah is among the things Satan wants, since enmity and hatred undoubtedly lead to division. So everything that leads to division is among what Satan wants.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the principle we have just pointed to, that everything that leads to division is among what Satan wants. Thousands of issues fall under this: selling over the sale of a Muslim brother causes hatred and division; bidding over his bid; proposing over his proposal; and the like. So everything that leads to division is among what Satan wants.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God's dislike, may He be blessed and exalted, for enmity and hatred among Muslims, since this is a warning beyond which there is no warning: ﴿Satan only wants to cause﴾ to the end. This is clear, because God, may He be exalted, commanded unity and forbade division. He, may He be majestic and exalted, said: ﴿And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:103]; He said: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:105]; He said: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have nothing to do with them﴾ [al-An'am 6:159]; He said: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [al-Shura 42:13]; and He said: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Anfal 8:46]. The two foundational sources, the Book and the Sunnah, are filled with this, that is, with the call to unity and the prohibition of division.

Is this included in that too? The students of knowledge, all the more so. But, unfortunately, when students of knowledge differ over a matter of ijtihad (independent reasoning), some of them become enemies of one another, except those whom God spares, and one of them speaks against his brother's reputation without restraint. He thus wrongs himself first, wrongs his brother second, and wrongs the servants of God who benefit from his brother, because when his brother's standing and esteem in their eyes fall, they will not benefit from his knowledge. So this person wrongs himself, wrongs his brother, and wrongs everyone who benefits from his brother's knowledge.

Therefore, one must be attentive to this, and you must believe that whoever opposes you in a matter of ijtihad has in reality agreed with you, because both of you seek the truth. He sees the truth in this matter, and you see the truth in its opposite. Which of you is the messenger of the other, whose following is obligatory? Of the two of you in this situation, who? No one. So he is right in following what he thought the evidence indicates, and you are right in following what you thought the evidence indicates. Let the hearts be pure.

* Student: Shaykh, may God bless you (...) abstaining from it and using it.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, because His saying ﴿so avoid it﴾ is a general expression: avoid it in every respect, in use and in drinking. But we do not assert with certainty that it refers to use, because of His saying: ﴿Satan only wishes to cause enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling﴾. Therefore we have seen it as one of the matters of scrupulousness (wara') to abandon it.
* Student: May God be good to you. We said: if the proportion of alcohol in these oils is small, it does no harm. Would the same apply, O Shaykh, to some drinks in which there is something of .. is it permitted or forbidden?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. If it is little, drink from it. But I want to advise you: when you drink, say "In the name of God," and when you finish, say "Praise be to God."
* Student: Perhaps people (...) the prohibition of donkeys, as Asma' (may God be pleased with her) mentioned, regarding the slaughter of the horse, because eating horses is not known among people today?
* The Shaykh: No, I want to add to this for you. Among people, the front of the horse is prohibited and its rear is permitted. The common folk say: the front of the horse's body is forbidden, because it is the side one faces the enemy with in jihad. As for its rear, it is permitted, because the rear is toward the enemy when turning away, so let it be eaten.
* Student: O Shaykh, I am asking about history (...). Should we ask about it or not?
* The Shaykh: No, ask about history. Donkeys were prohibited at Khaybar, and Asma' bint Abi Bakr narrated this as evidence for the permissibility of horses. Had she not known that horses were eaten after Khaybar, she would not have mentioned this as an argument.
* Student: May God be good to you, O Shaykh. As you have mentioned, perhaps some rancor exists in a man's heart, but O Shaykh (...) with the successful remedy in (...)?
* The Shaykh: His heart? By God, my brother, I have something that is not easy. Did you understand the question? He says: a person may find, I mean, rancor or envy in his heart toward his brother, so how does he treat it? He treats it by saying to himself: you want the truth, and the matter is not a text; the matter is ijtihad. But if it were a text, we would not accept excusing him. However, if it is ijtihad, then all of us are following ijtihad.
* Student: I want an answer about the hadith: "God has cursed wine, its presser, and its drinker" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3674) and Ibn Majah (3380), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both.]], and so on, from (...), although (...) and only one drank?
* The Shaykh: Because these people assist him; this is for assisting him in it, like the curse on the one who consumes riba, its agent, its two witnesses, and its scribe.
* Student: May God bless you. Some scholars cite the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibiting treatment with wine, and say: other things are analogized to it, such as using wine for other than medicine, and perfumes and the like, a fortiori. So it is forbidden...
* The Shaykh: But treatment with it by drinking is the case here. For this reason the scholars (may God have mercy on them) said: it is not permitted to treat with it, even for thirst; it is not permitted to drink wine for thirst. They gave as the reason that when a person drinks wine out of thirst, it only increases his thirst. Some scholars hold that it is permitted for thirst, and they do not concede that it only increases thirst. But if a person chokes on a morsel and has nothing but a cup of wine, and he chokes, and either he dies by suffocation or he drinks the cup and the morsel passes, what should he do? Does he use it? Yes indeed, he uses it out of necessity, because God, glorified and exalted, said in a general verse: ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ [al-An'am 119]. This is more general than His saying, when He prohibited carrion, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than God: ﴿But whoever is forced by severe hunger, not inclining to sin, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], and the verse ... ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ is more general.
Student: May God bless you. Some of them take the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibiting treatment with wine (...) and say: other things are analogized to it for use only, other than treatment, a fortiori?
* The Shaykh: Analogized to it?
* Student: The use only, other than treatment; like perfumes and others, a fortiori, I mean.
* The Shaykh: But treatment with it by drinking is the case here. For this reason the scholars (may God have mercy on them) said: it is not permitted to treat with it, even for thirst; it is not permitted to drink wine for thirst. They gave as the reason that when a person drinks wine out of thirst, it only increases his thirst. Some scholars hold that it is permitted for thirst, and they do not concede that it only increases thirst. But if a person chokes on a morsel and has nothing but a cup of wine, and he chokes, either he dies by suffocation or he drinks the cup and the morsel passes, what should he do? Does he use it? Yes indeed, he uses it out of necessity, because God, glorified and exalted, said in a general verse: ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ [al-An'am 119]. This is more general than His saying, when He prohibited carrion, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than God: ﴿But whoever is forced by severe hunger, not inclining to sin, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], and the verse ... ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ is more general.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. ﴿Satan only wishes to cause enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ (91) ﴿And obey God and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.﴾ (92) ﴿There is no blame upon those who believed and did righteous deeds for what they have eaten, if they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear God and believe, then fear God and do good; and God loves the doers of good.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 91–93].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. God, blessed and exalted, said, explaining what Satan wants from the children of Adam: ﴿Satan only wishes to cause enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling.﴾ What is the opposite of enmity?
* Student: Friendship (muwalah).
* The Shaykh: Friendship. And hatred (baghda')? Love; that is, love is the opposite of hatred. So he wants to scatter hearts and bodies. And I think we have taken the benefits.
* Student: Five benefits.
* The Shaykh: From where are the five benefits?
* Student: God's dislike of enmity and hatred among Muslims; this is the last one. Shall I say them all?
* The Shaykh: Fine.
* Student:
- Affirmation of Satan's will.
- The evil of Satan's will toward the children of Adam.
- That the division of nations is among Satan's aims.
- That everything that leads to division is among Satan's aims.
- God's dislike of enmity and hatred among Muslims.
* The Shaykh: Well done.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes (asbab). The basis of this is that God, exalted, informed that intoxicants and gambling are a cause of enmity and hatred, and there is no doubt about this, and no one denies it except a fool. Everyone knows that whoever is plunged into the sea will drown, and whoever is thrown into fire will burn, is it not so? Some people denied causes, and others went to extremes in affirming them. As for those who denied causes, they claimed that by their denial they were exalting God above having partners, so they went to extremes in transcendence. As for those who affirmed causes as the actual agents, they associated others with God.
As for the people of truth, they said: causes have an effect, but who made them have an effect? God. So the effect of causes is not by themselves, but by the powers God has placed in them.
This is supported by the fact that there are causes that necessitate a thing by God's decree, yet this necessitation may be lifted. Among examples: fire burns, and when Abraham was thrown into it, God said to it: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69], so it became coolness and safety; burning and heat were removed. Had causes been effective by themselves, Abraham, peace be upon him, would have burned. Likewise the man whom the Dajjal cuts in two pieces and then says to him: stand up, and he stands. We know that the Dajjal was not the cause of his revival; rather that is up to God, mighty and majestic. For this reason, when he kills him a third time, he cannot kill him, for God does not give him power over him after that.
So we say: causes have an effect, but not by themselves; rather by the powers God has placed in them. The evidences for this, in revelation, reason, and observation, are countless.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that everything that averts from the remembrance of God is among the commands of Satan. We have previously noted that the remembrance of God, blessed and exalted, is...?
* Student: That it is preserved by God, mighty and majestic.
* The Shaykh: No (...).
* Student: It is by the heart.
* The Shaykh: It is by the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. So everything that averts you from the remembrance of God by these things is among the commands and wishes of Satan.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of prayer, since it is singled out for mention from among the remembrance of God, mighty and majestic. This indicates its nobility and excellence over others, as in His saying, exalted: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4]. "The Spirit" is Gabriel, who is among the angels, yet God singled him out for mention because of his nobility.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: caution against Satan diverting us from prayer, either by occupying us with our wealth, our children, our entertainment, or our pursuits, or by any other means, or by making us perform it with our bodies while our hearts are absent. So beware of Satan diverting you from prayer.
* And among its benefits: whenever a reluctance toward prayer enters your heart, know that it is from Satan and is Satan's desire.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the emphasis on the prohibition of intoxicants and gambling, as shown by His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ The emphasis is that He used the form of interrogation: meaning, after this clarification, will you desist or will you persist? What was the answer of the Companions, O brothers? "We have desisted, we have desisted."

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah 92]. "Aṭī'ū" (obey) is an imperative verb from ṭā'ah (obedience), which means submission (inqiyād). Here, obedience means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. Accordingly, if someone asks, "What is meant by obeying Allah?", we say: doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

﴿And obey the Messenger﴾: the address is undoubtedly to this Ummah. On this basis, the "al" in "al-Rasūl" (the Messenger) is for a known reference (al-'ahd al-dhihnī, a mentally known reference), meaning: obey the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, whom Allah, mighty and majestic, sent.

If someone says: What is the proof that Allah sent him?

We say: the proof that Allah sent him is the miracles with which He supported him, the greatest of which is the Noble Qur'an, and then the sensory signs that are witnessed, which no human being can bring, neither the Messenger nor anyone else—clear signs of his prophethood, and they are more than can be counted.

Whoever wants more of this should refer to the end of the book al-Jawāb al-Ṣaḥīḥ by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, for he devoted a very beneficial chapter to the signs of the Prophet ﷺ. And whoever wants more as well should consult what al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in al-Bidāyah wa'l-Nihāyah at the end of the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, for he mentioned many signs in the heavens and on earth, in humans and in animals. There is no need for us to mention much of them, but they exist, and praise be to Allah.

We should be keen to know these signs, because man is human and Satan is eager; he may attack the heart and weaken faith in the Messenger ﷺ. But when one reviews the signs, his faith increases thereby, so keep to them.

﴿And obey the Messenger and beware﴾: "beware" (iḥdharū) means: beware of disobedience to Allah and His Messenger; that is, beware of sin, the disobedience of Allah and His Messenger. Allah the Exalted has not commanded us with anything except for our benefit, and has not forbidden anything except for our harm.

﴿But if you turn away﴾: i.e., you turn away from obeying Allah and obeying the Messenger of Allah; then you will not harm Allah or the Messenger of Allah—you will never harm Allah, and you will never harm the Messenger of Allah. As for a person not harming Allah by his disobedience, this is an evident matter. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And for Allah is the right over the people to visit the House—for whoever is able to find thereto a way. And whoever disbelieves—indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 97]. He also said: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free of need from you﴾ [al-Zumar 7]. And Allah said in a ḥadīth qudsī: "O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, and you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me."[[Recorded by Muslim (2577/55) from the ḥadīth of Abū Dharr.]]

Likewise, the one who turns away does not harm the Prophet ﷺ. Why? Because the Prophet ﷺ has conveyed and fulfilled the trust, and is not blamed for the sin of others, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt 54]. They will not harm the Messenger ﷺ by disobeying Allah, because he has conveyed, fulfilled the trust, and advised the Ummah. Hence He said: ﴿Then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾. "I'lamū" (know) is an imperative of knowledge, and it is known that we must know everything Allah has informed us of about Himself and about others, but this is a specific knowledge: ﴿know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾. Here we ask about the i'rāb (grammatical analysis) of ﴿innamā ʿalā rasūlinā al-balāghu al-mubīn﴾. How do we parse ﴿innamā ʿalā rasūlinā al-balāghu al-mubīn﴾?

* A student: "Innamā" is a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr) with no place in i'rāb; "ʿalā rasūlinā" is a prepositional phrase (jār wa-majrūr), "rasūl" is in the genitive after "ʿalā," and "nā" is a possessive pronoun (muḍāf ilayhi); the phrase is in the place of the nominative as a subject (mubtada').
* The Shaykh: Help your brother.
* Another student: "(...)" is the predicate of a fronted subject, and "al-balāgh" is a delayed subject in the nominative, its sign of nominative being the visible ḍammah, and "al-mubīn" is an adjective.
* The Shaykh: An adjective.
* The student: An adjective of "al-balāgh."
* A student: And the clause formed from the particle of restriction and what follows it is in the accusative place, filling the role of the two objects of "iʿlamū."
* The Shaykh: Is it possible that there is another way of parsing it, and that we say: "alladhī ʿalā rasūlinā al-balāgh al-mubīn" (that which is upon Our Messenger is the clear notification)? Look at the writing: "anna" is joined with "mā." This is with me and with you likewise. If it were a relative pronoun (mā mawṣūlah), it would be separated from "anna," because the relative "mā," when it is the name of "anna" or "inna," is separated from it.

Here someone may say: Perhaps this rule—that the relative "mā" is joined to "inna"—was an old rule in the orthography of the Muṣḥaf?

We say: The principle is that what was as it was remains; and that when "mā" is joined to "inna" or "anna," it restrains them from operating and makes the clause following it a restriction.

His saying: ﴿innamā ʿalā rasūlinā al-balāgh﴾ means the conveying (al-tabligh). The origin of "tabligh" is from "balagha al-shay'a kadhā," i.e., it reached it; that is, it is incumbent upon him to deliver the revelation that Allah revealed to him to the one to whom it is sent. This is his duty; he has no more than this function.

﴿al-balāgh al-mubīn﴾ is from "abāna" in its transitive form, not from "abāna" in its intransitive form. Intransitive "abāna" is what you say: "abāna al-ṣubḥu" (the dawn became clear), just as you say "bāna al-ṣubḥu." Transitive "abāna" takes a direct object. So here we say: "al-mubīn" is from what? From transitive "abāna" or intransitive? Transitive—that is, the notification that made the truth clear, and that is due to his eloquence, peace and blessings be upon him, the sweetness of his speech, its reaching the heart when it reaches the ear, and the soul's conviction in it. For these qualities, the notification of the Prophet ﷺ was clear through what he conveyed, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him.

In this noble verse there is a connection to what precedes it: when Allah commanded abstaining from and avoiding wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows, He commanded obedience to Him in general and warned against opposing Him.

Among its benefits, then:
* First: the obligation to obey Allah and His Messenger, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾.
* And among its benefits: that obedience to the Prophet ﷺ is independent, meaning that if the Prophet ﷺ commands something, we do not ask whether this command exists in the Qur'an or not; rather, his obedience is independent.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ messengership, based on His saying: ﴿Obey the Messenger﴾.
* And among its benefits: that the Prophet ﷺ is distinguished from others by messengership, and is not distinguished from others by being a lord who does whatever He wills; rather, he himself does not possess for himself benefit or harm, based on His saying: ﴿And obey the Messenger﴾.
* And among its benefits: that messengership is among the most honorable attributes a servant can have, based on His saying: ﴿the Messenger﴾. There is no doubt that a messenger is honored and ennobled according to the rank of the one who sent him. Do you agree with this statement? Yes, you agree, God willing. Yes, if a messenger came from a noble man of high rank, would he be in your souls like a messenger who came from common people? Certainly not; rather, in our souls this messenger would have the measure of the rank deserved by the one who sent him. Accordingly, messengership becomes an honor for the one who sent him.

Is the station of prophethood more excellent, or the station of messengership?

The station of messengership, because the Messenger attained the station of prophethood and the station of messengership: the station of prophethood in what was revealed to him, and the station of messengership in what he was charged to convey, so it is more noble. This is contrary to the people of falsehood who say: "The best of the children of Adam is the walī (saint), then the prophet, then the messenger," giving the reason that the messenger is a servant, the prophet derives from "nubuwwah," which means elevation and height, and the walī derives from "wilāyah," which is more specific. Their poet says:

The station of prophethood is in an isthmus
Above the Messenger and below the walī

May Allah fight them! "Above the Messenger" would mean there is no clear difference with him; as for the walī, it is far, "below the walī." They have indeed strayed into manifest error, because the prophet is a walī and more, and the messenger is a walī, a prophet, and a messenger. But Allah says: ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ [al-Nūr 40].

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning against disobeying Allah and His Messenger, based on His saying: ﴿And beware﴾. The word "beware" (iḥdharū) whose object is omitted is more forceful in effect than "beware" with its object mentioned, because it is more emphatic in producing fear, as if the speaker limited himself to it without its complements.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the default for the commands of Allah and His Messenger is obligation, because warning is only given about something for which a person incurs sin; what carries no sin is not something one beware of. This matter is one on which the scholars of usūl (the principles of jurisprudence) differ. Some say: the default for a command is obligation; some say: its default is recommendation; and some say: in matters of etiquette it is for recommendation, while in acts of worship that are Allah's right it is for obligation. The matter is elaborated in the science of uṣūl al-fiqh, but what concerns us is that when a person hears the command of Allah and His Messenger, he should not hesitate, saying: "Is the command for obligation or for desirability?" This is a criticized expression: "Is the command for obligation or for desirability?" The default is that a command directed to you by your Creator or His Messenger whom He sent to you is binding; this is the default. And up to this hour, and up to your hour, it has not been known of the Companions that when the Messenger ﷺ commanded them with a matter they said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this obligatory upon us or recommended?" Never; and it is better for us to follow his footsteps.

Yes, if a person became entangled in disobedience, then asking whether the command is for obligation or recommendation may be appropriate. How so? If it was obligatory, he must repent of it and turn to Allah from it; but if it was not obligatory, the matter is easy. However, my speech is about the first moment the command reaches you: do not hesitate; do what you are able. As for when a ruling comes from the Messenger ﷺ that you are given a choice, then you have a choice, as the Prophet ﷺ instructed Barīrah to return to her husband Mughīth. Barīrah had been freed while her husband was a slave; when she was freed she owned herself, so the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice, saying: "If you wish to remain with Mughīth, then remain; and if you wish not to remain, then do not (...)." She said: "I do not want to remain with him." Mughīth grieved over her and began to weep behind her in the markets of Madinah, wanting her to return to him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you not marvel at Mughīth's love for Barīrah and Barīrah's hatred for Mughīth?"[[Recorded by al-Bukhārī (5283) from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās.]] What is your answer? Indeed we marvel, because generally when hearts are attached, they become attached from both sides. He commanded her to return to him, and she said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, if it is a command, then I hear and obey" — and she did not say "if it is a command in the sense of obligation" — "if it is a command, then I hear and obey; and if it is a suggestion, then I have no desire for it." He said: "Rather, it is a suggestion." Here the Prophet ﷺ clarified that the command was not for obligation, but for suggestion.

When he said: "Indeed Allah has enjoined upon you the Ḥajj, so perform it," al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He said: "No."[[Recorded by Muslim (1337/412) from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah.]]

The conclusion, then: we say the default for a command is obligation, and you should do what you are commanded and not ask hesitantly, because the matter is grave if you hesitate. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'ām 110]. May Allah protect us and you from that. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them﴾, followed by ﴿so they are in a matter confused﴾ [Qāf 5]—unsettled and unstable, because they denied the truth when it came to them. So accept the truth, my brother, and do not hesitate, and do not say: "obligatory or recommended." But as I told you: if you become entangled in something, there is no harm.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that people turning away from what the Prophet ﷺ calls to does not harm him, based on His saying: ﴿So know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾.

It follows from this that the caller to Allah in our time and in times before us is not harmed if people do not accept from him, because he has fulfilled the obligation, and he should gladden himself that he has fulfilled the obligation, and not grieve over their not accepting his call, because Allah the Exalted said to the Messenger: ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress over what they plot﴾ [al-Naḥl 127]. But perhaps we might say: he grieves over the non-acceptance of the Sharī'ah, not over their non-acceptance of him, and the difference between this and that is clear.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet ﷺ cannot guide anyone, because he conveyed the clear notification, and despite that opposition and turning away occurred.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Prophet ﷺ conveyed the clear notification, which refutes the view of the Mufawwidah (those who delegate meaning) concerning the names and attributes of Allah, who said that the Messenger ﷺ did not convey the clear notification and did not know what he said, but rather threw out words to people as if they were letters of the alphabet or riddles.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the notification of the Messenger ﷺ is a clear notification, with no incoherence, no complication, and no ambiguity; rather it is clear in itself and makes things clear to others, based on His saying: ﴿the clear notification﴾.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to return to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, based on His saying: ﴿So know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾, and that he, peace and blessings be upon him, performed the obligation, so it is incumbent upon us to perform the obligation.

Can we derive from it that one who has not received the message is excused?

We can derive from it that one who has not received the message is excused, or one who received it in a confused manner is excused. But the second, who received it in a confused manner, is obligated to seek the correct description of this message that reached him, and not to remain silent saying: "The matter has not become clear to me, and it does not bind me"; rather he must investigate. As for when the matter was not known to him at all, then since the proof has not been established upon him, he is excused. So if we saw a man who had never heard anything about the Sharī'ah, about Islam, in caves, mountains, and thickets, tending sheep and milking camels, knowing nothing, would we say he is excused or not excused? Excused; there is no doubt he is excused. But if it is mentioned to him that there is a message, then he is obligated to investigate, and at that point we may say that the proof is established against one to whom it has reached, because the obligation is to ask.

The noble verse: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Nisā' 59]. Can the obedience to Allah and the obedience to His Messenger conflict?

It cannot. And the obedience to the Prophet ﷺ cannot conflict with the texts transmitted from him. So if we see a ḥadīth contradicting what is in the Qur'an, we judge it to be rejected, even if we do not know its chain; and even if we know its chain, we say: this is munkar (rejected) if it contradicts the Qur'an. It is impossible that Allah would command obedience to Him, with obedience to Him placed before everything, and obedience to the Messenger; if we were to take what contradicts the Book and the Sunnah, that would be impossible.

Among that is what is related from the Prophet ﷺ concerning beef: that its flesh is a disease and that its milk is a remedy or cure. Without even looking at its chain, we judge that it is baseless and not authentic. If its flesh were a disease, could Allah have made it lawful for His servants? Impossible; if its flesh were a disease, Allah would never have made it lawful for the servants, because Allah the Exalted does not make lawful for His servants what is harmful to them.

Even if someone said: we could interpret this ḥadīth as referring to eating beef without cooking—is that valid? No. Why? Because eating it uncooked is rare, and a ḥadīth cannot be interpreted as referring to a rare case; and "a thing is mentioned with its like." Among such is the ḥadīth of ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Whoever dies with fasting owed, his guardian shall fast on his behalf"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (1952) and Muslim (1147/153) from the ḥadīth of ʿĀ'ishah.]]. Some scholars say: the meaning is that whoever dies owing a vowed fast, his guardian fasts on his behalf; but the obligatory fast, such as the fast of Ramaḍān and expiation, is not fasted on behalf of the dead.

It is said: Glory be to Allah! You authenticate the hadith and then trim down its intended meaning. Is fasting owed through a vow compared with obligatory fasting and expiation (kaffarah) common or rare? It is rare. How can you apply the hadith to a rare case and leave aside the common one? For this reason the stronger view is that whoever dies owing fasting, whether it was obligated by a vow or by the basic sacred law (al-asl al-shar'i), then fasting is performed on his behalf.

* Student: I am troubled by the case where a person has been conveyed the religion in a confused manner. Are we not excusing him for ignorance? Shaykh, does this mean that such a conveying is no conveying at all?

* Shaykh: No, wait. We do not say "no." We say: we may not excuse him, because he neglected a duty, which is inquiry.

* Student: A layman, or an elderly person inside Europe and the like, whom the media has overshadowed so that they know nothing?

* Shaykh: Glory be to Allah! Everything is possible. If he has been told that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, that he was sent to all of mankind, that whoever opposes him is in the Fire, and whoever follows him is in Paradise, and he hears this...

* Student: (...) an Arab says that he is a messenger.

* Shaykh: And he is not truthful. Yes, he may well be excused, especially if the one who informed him is among their religious leaders. He may well be excused. For this reason, when Umar disapproved of the man who recited a reading of Surah al-Furqan different from what Umar knew, Umar denounced it as an error in the Book of Allah, thinking the man had made a mistake in it, until they both went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It was revealed this way," regarding the man's recitation, and "It was revealed this way," regarding Umar's recitation.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2419), and Muslim (818 (270)), from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]

On this matter, people fall into two extremes and a middle position. One extreme goes too far in takfir (declaring others to be disbelievers) and rushes into it, saying: ignorance is not excused in the basics of the religion. This is not correct. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know, [with] clear proofs and scriptures﴾ [an-Nahl 43, 44]. Another group goes too far in removing takfir, even when a person is in a state where his disbelief is judged, saying: no. The middle position is the moderate one: we say that whoever has not been reached by the message is excused, and whoever has been reached by it but did not understand it is excused, because not understanding is like not knowing. If a non-Arabic speaker came to you and began speaking in his language about something, would you know what he is saying? You would not know what he is saying. He is excused. So understanding is a condition. Mere conveying is not sufficient.

As for Allah's saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby, and whomever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am 19], does the meaning here refer to "whoever it reaches even if he does not understand it," or to "whoever it has reached and he has grasped it"? The second is what is intended.

* Student: Some people claim to be Muslims while opposing the textual evidences of the sacred law (...).

* Shaykh: No...

* Student: Like the Rafidah (a Shi'i sect), Shaykh. They say: Allah betrayed the worlds, they betray Jibril, they revile Umar, Abu Bakr and A'ishah, and they openly challenge the Muslims...

* Shaykh: There is no doubt that whoever reviles Abu Bakr and Umar has nothing of the religion in him.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: May Allah spare us their evil and guide them.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, it is obligatory to hate them. How can someone say it is obligatory to love them? It is obligatory to hate them. There is no problem with that. But we ask Allah to guide them.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ [al-Ma'idah 93]. ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game that your hands and spears can reach, so that Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 93, 94].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾. Is it possible for the command of Allah and the command of the Messenger to contradict each other?

* Student: It is not possible.

* Shaykh: What is the aspect of this in the verse?

* Student: The conjunction: His saying, ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾.

* Shaykh: What is its aspect exactly?

* Student: That he joined the obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ) to the obedience to Allah.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: That he repeated the verb.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: The aspect is that the waw (and) is for general joining (...).

* Shaykh: (...).

* Student: Obedience to the Messenger is something commanded by Allah the Mighty and Majestic (...) obedience to Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: That Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, placing them in opposition to whoever turns away from obedience, like His saying: ﴿But whoever turns away﴾ [Ali 'Imran 82] (...).

* Shaykh: Contradiction does not occur, because if contradiction occurred, obedience to the Messenger would be disobedience to Allah and obedience to Allah would be disobedience to the Messenger. That is contradiction, since in contradiction the one opposite has a ruling opposite to the ruling of its counterpart. So if we say that contradiction occurs, it would follow that obedience to Allah is disobedience to the Messenger and obedience to the Messenger is disobedience to Allah.

Is there anything in the verse indicating that obedience to the Messenger is independent, meaning that we do not need a witness from the Qur'an for what the Messenger (ﷺ) commanded?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence?

* Student: Because he repeated the verb here, saying: ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾.

* Shaykh: Because he repeated the verb, saying: ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾, and repeating the verb indicates that obedience is independent.

Is there in the Qur'an anything resembling His saying: ﴿and beware﴾ (...)? Is there anything in the Qur'an resembling this warning?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: A verse indicating caution against opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger?

* Student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein eternally, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾ [an-Nisa' 14].

* Student: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [an-Nur 63]. Imam Ahmad said: Do you know what the trial is? The trial is shirk. Perhaps if some of his words are rejected, something of deviation will enter his heart and he will perish.

* Shaykh: Is the Prophet (ﷺ) blamed for not accepting his call?

* Student: He is not blamed (...).

* Shaykh: And from this verse, he is not blamed, because of His saying: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not one to be blamed﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 54]. But from this verse here?

* Student: Here, because of His saying: ﴿But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾.

* Shaykh: So if upon him is only the conveyance, then his being turned away from will not harm him, and he will not be blamed for it.

﴿al-Mubin﴾: is it in the sense of "the clarifier" (al-mubin) or "the clear" (al-bayyin)?

* Student: "The clarifier."

* Shaykh: And does al-mubin come in the sense of al-bayyin?

* Student: Yes, it may come.

* Shaykh: An example?

* Student: "Abana al-subh" (the dawn became clear).

* Shaykh: "Abana al-subh," but this "abana" is a verb, whereas we want the active participle "mubin." ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were in clear misguidance﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2]. That is, "clear" (bayyin).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah⦆ [al-Ma'idah 93]. (Laysa) is a particle of negation, and it is a past-tense verb that is invariable (jamid). In the terminology of the grammarians, the invariable (jamid) is that which does not undergo conjugation. Invariability may be total, or it may be partial, such that conjugation is prevented in one respect but not another. Here the invariability is total: laysa cannot change, since it is for negation.

﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾: they believed with their hearts and did righteous deeds with their bodies, and this encompasses the whole of religion, because the whole of religion is faith and action.

His saying: ﴿and done righteous deeds﴾ means they did righteous actions, and actions cannot have this description unless they conform to the Shari'ah, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Whatever condition is not in the Book of Allah is void» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2168) and Muslim (1504/8) from 'A'ishah]; that is, invalid. Thus righteous actions are those that agree with the Shari'ah, and they cannot agree with the Shari'ah unless they agree with it in six matters: the cause (al-sabab), the kind (al-jins), the quantity (al-qadr), the manner (al-kayfiyyah), the time (al-zaman), and the place (al-makan).

That is, an act of worship cannot be lawful and valid unless it agrees with the Shari'ah in these six matters. The first: the cause; the second: the kind; the third: the quantity; the fourth: the manner; the fifth: the time; the sixth: the place. If it contradicts the Shari'ah in any one of these six, it is not lawful and not accepted. These are the conditions of conformity with the Shari'ah:

First, the cause: if a person invents a cause and worships Allah on its basis, when it is not lawfully prescribed, his act is rejected. For example, if a person, whenever he belches, says: "Alhamdulillah." Belching is known among you, or not? It is known. Here he has instituted an act of worship to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, namely praise, for a cause, namely belching. Has the Shari'ah stated that belching is a cause for praise? No. Therefore it is not accepted from him, because he has worshipped Allah with what He did not prescribe.

Second, as we said, the kind: it is well known that sacrificial animals are from the grazing livestock (bahimat al-an'am), namely camels, cattle and sheep. So if a person sacrifices a horse, it is not accepted from him, why? Because it contravenes the Shari'ah in its kind. If he sacrifices an ostrich, it is not accepted from him; if he sacrifices a dove, it is not accepted from him, because it contravenes the Shari'ah in its kind. Although the Shari'ah has required a sheep as a penalty if a dove is killed by one in the state of ihram, the Shari'ah has not come with a person sacrificing a dove. By this we recognize the error of those who say that sacrificing chickens and roosters is permissible, because the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the man who bathes in his house and goes out to the mosque on Friday at the fourth hour, said: «it is as if he had offered a chicken» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (881) and Muslim (850/10) from Abu Hurayrah]. They said: this shows that a chicken is valid for drawing near to Allah. Our reply to this is that its meaning is: he draws near to Allah by giving it in charity, not by slaughtering it. And there is no doubt that if a person slaughtered a chicken and gave it in charity to the poor, it would suffice him. Thus it is necessary that the act agree with the Shari'ah in its kind.

Third, the quantity: if a person worships Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a sixth prayer which he makes at the time the sun has risen the length of a spear, and says that he draws near to Allah through this prayer because the sun has risen the length of a spear, not because it is the forenoon prayer, this is a worship that is not accepted. That is, he wanted to make it, what? He wanted to make it a sixth prayer along with the five; it is not accepted, because he has added a prayer for which Allah has sent down no authority. And if he prayed Dhuhr with five rak'ahs, it would not be accepted, for contravening the Shari'ah in quantity.

Fourth, the manner: if a person worships Allah with ablution, and performs a complete ablution including all the limbs, but he begins with the feet, then the head, then the hands, then the face, the worship is not accepted, because it contravenes the Shari'ah in its manner. Likewise, if he prostrates before bowing, the prayer is not accepted, because it contravenes the Shari'ah in its manner.

Fifth, the time: if a person sacrifices on the Feast of Fitr and says: "A feast like a feast," analogy suggests that one sacrifices on the Feast of Fitr as one sacrifices on the Feast of Adha, it is not accepted. Why? Because it contravenes the Shari'ah in the time or in the period.

The place: if a person performs i'tikaf in Ramadan in his house, or a woman in her prayer place which is in the house, it does not suffice. Why? Because it contravenes the Shari'ah in the place.

It remains to ask: is a person sinful if he worships Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with something that contravenes the Shari'ah in one of these?

The answer: he is sinful, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Beware of newly invented matters, for every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance» [Abu Dawud (4607), who narrated it with this wording, and al-Tirmidhi (2676), from al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah].

﴿and done righteous deeds﴾: therefore "righteous" (al-salihat) is an attribute of a noun that has been omitted, the implied meaning being: the righteous deeds.

﴿blame﴾ means sin, and this is what is negated; so there is no sin upon the believer who does righteous deeds, in what he has eaten, ﴿when they fear Allah﴾. "In what they have eaten" is more general than "what they have eaten" (akalu), so it includes eating and drinking, because drinking is also tasted and so is food. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah will test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, said by whom? Talut ﴿and whoever does not taste it is of me﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. ﴿Does not taste it⦆ means the river. Is the river eaten or drunk? It is drunk.

So His saying: ﴿in what they have eaten⦆ encompasses everything that has taste in the mouth, of food and drink, but with conditions. There is no blame upon them for what they have eaten, under conditions. The first condition: ﴿when they fear Allah﴾; the second: ﴿and believe﴾; the third: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾; the fourth: ﴿then fear Allah﴾; the fifth: ﴿and believe﴾; the sixth: ﴿fear Allah﴾; and the seventh: ﴿do good﴾. These are five restrictions, and they are not repeated; each has its own meaning.

His saying: ﴿when they fear Allah﴾ means they fear what is forbidden to them of food, not general piety. "When they fear what is forbidden to them of what is eaten" — this is the first. ﴿and believe﴾ means they believe in Allah, because faith is undoubtedly the foundation for the acceptance of deeds. ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ is a condition: that is, they do righteous deeds in what they eat of permissible things, so they do not use them to commit what is forbidden. If they use them to commit what is forbidden, while they are permissible, they become forbidden, because Allah conditioned that they do righteous deeds with them. He said: ﴿then fear Allah and believe﴾. The word ﴿then⦆ indicates that this is a different type from the first, because coordination, especially with "then" which indicates a delay and sequence, shows that the second is other than the first. So the meaning of ﴿then fear Allah and believe﴾ is: then continue in their piety regarding what is forbidden of this food. And His saying: ﴿believe⦆ means persist in their faith; and the command to believe may be intended to mean steadfastness in it and perseverance in it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa' 136]. ﴿Then fear Allah and do good﴾: this is general piety; fear all prohibitions and do good by performing all acts of obedience, ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾.

This verse may be understood in two states. The first state is that of one who turns to asceticism and fears permissible luxury, so he avoids fruit, tender meat and tasty things, worshipping Allah. It has another interpretation concerning those who died before the prohibition of wine. They drank wine, which is forbidden; was it forbidden or permitted? In the end it is forbidden, but at the time they drank it, it was permitted, because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, did not prohibit it outright until after their death. Verses had been revealed that present it as prohibited and restrict its permissibility, as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people﴾ [al-Baqarah 219], and in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa' 43]. The state of these people became a source of confusion for the Companions. When wine was prohibited, the state of those who had died before it became unclear to the Companions, so Allah revealed this verse: that there is no blame upon them, because they did not violate what Allah prohibited; rather they were believers, God-fearing, and good-doers. So it is interpreted in two ways: concerning one who drank wine before its prohibition; and also, if we say: now, and before he knew of its prohibition, this includes that there is no blame upon him. The second: those who abstained from what Allah had permitted them out of fear of sin. It is said to them: there is no blame upon you for what you have eaten, if these conditions are fulfilled.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾. Love, if we wished to define it, we could not; a person can never define love. Can any of you define it? Loves among ourselves, can anyone? Something that is part of your daily life inside the house and outside the house, and yet you do not define it?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes. Defining the known increases one in ignorance, or increases ignorance by it. For this reason, when Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned the definition of love in his book Rawdat al-Muhibbin, he said: these natural matters cannot be defined; you cannot define love, nor hatred, nor enmity, nor fear, nor joy. You cannot, because these are matters latent in the soul, and everyone knows them. Yes, they have signs, without doubt. So if you say, for example: love is to incline towards a thing that benefits you or by which you repel harm, what do you say as its definition?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is the effect of love. Love is to see a man whose face is illumined and who is joyfully glad; the effect of something cannot be defined. Therefore love is known, and if you wish, say: it is recognized; and defining the known increases one in ignorance.

* Among the benefits of the verse: first, the negation of blame regarding foods and drinks, under these conditions.

* And among its benefits: that the disbelievers bear blame for what they have eaten. Why? What is its reason? They are not believers. So if a disbeliever raises a morsel to his mouth or drinks a cup of water, he is held accountable for it and bears sin for it. This is supported by the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions? Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world, purely for them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-A'raf 32]. Is it for non-believers in the life of this world? As for decree (qadaran), yes, is it not so? As for legislation (shar'an), no. For this reason He said regarding the believers: ﴿purely for them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, and for non-believers it is not purely theirs.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strict restrictions in negating sin from one who eats or drinks in what he eats and drinks. Do you now know how many times piety is mentioned?

* Students: Three times.

* The Shaykh: And faith twice, and excellence (ihsan) once. These are severe and great restrictions, so beware, O Muslim brother, lest there be sin upon you in what you eat because you have not fulfilled these restrictions. I ask Allah to help us and you to them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever eats what is lawful from unlawful earnings bears sin. Why? Because he did not fear Allah in his earning, and one must fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is the non-earner like the earner in this sin? We say: if the thing is specified, the forbidden thing being specific, then the eater is like the earner; such as if I know that this sheep which he slaughtered to honour me was stolen by him from so-and-so, then it is forbidden for me to eat it. But if this person deals in usury and earns from usury with the consent of its owner, the usurer, then there is no harm in eating from his wealth, unless your abstention from it would lead to his repentance; then abstain. But if it is all equal, then eat, and there is no blame upon you. This is supported by the fact that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ate from the property of the Jews and bought from the property of the Jews, although they were well known for consuming the unlawful and taking usury, and he did not inquire nor ask anyone: did you earn it by usury?

Based on this, if a deceased person dies and we know that he dealt in usury and dealt in what is permissible, must the heirs investigate how he earned it? They are not obliged to. The sin is upon the earner, unless we know that this is the very property of another, in which case it is obligatory upon us to return it to its owner, it is obligatory upon us to return it because we know it is not his possession. But if I doubt whether it is his possession and he took it by a lawful means or by theft, what is the default? The default is that it is his. We are not obliged to say to everyone who gives us a gift: from where? Did you steal it, or did it come to you by a permissible means? If we were charged with this, it would be an extremely severe burden. But, praise be to Allah, matters are taken at their apparent state. Just as a people asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about people who bring them meat, while they were recent converts to disbelief, who had recently embraced Islam, and the recipient of the meat did not know whether they had mentioned the name of Allah or not. He said to them: «Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat» [al-Bukhari (5507) and Ibn Majah (3174), from 'A'ishah]; because the default is permissibility until prohibition becomes clear.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of faith and piety, and that they are a cause for good food and lawful food.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of excellence (ihsan) towards whom? Excellence towards creation, and excellence in worshipping the Creator. Excellence towards creation is that you spend your standing, spend your wealth, spend your service, and your bodily benefit. Excellence in worshipping the Creator was explained by the most knowledgeable of people in its meaning, namely the Prophet (ﷺ), in his saying: «That you worship Allah as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then He sees you» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5), from Abu Hurayrah].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah loves, due to His saying: ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾. This attribute, like the other attributes, obliges the servant to affirm it concerning his Lord, and to take the words of his Lord in their apparent sense and according to what the Arabic language requires; because Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning, We made it in the Arabic language, ﴿that you may understand﴾ [al-Zukhruf 3], so that we may understand this Qur'an and comprehend it. Accordingly, it is obligatory that we believe that Allah loves. If we interpreted it other than its apparent sense, we would be transgressing against the text in two respects: the first being diverting it from its apparent sense, and the second being affirming a meaning contrary to the apparent. This is an offence against the texts and a distortion of words from their places. Among those who are undoubtedly Muslims, there are those who interpret love as reward, meaning He rewards the good-doers. We say: may Allah pardon whoever has died, and we ask for guidance for whoever remains. This interpretation is a distortion of words from their places, because reward is one thing and love is another, and although love necessarily involves reward, one cannot interpret something by its necessary consequence without evidence. Moreover, which is more forceful in urging excellence: that we say the meaning of the verse is "Allah rewards the good-doers," or that we say "Allah loves the good-doers"? The second, without doubt.

This is why, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran 31], He did not say: "If you love Allah, follow me," so that you might be truthful in your claim, but He said: ﴿Allah will love you﴾, because the love of Allah is the goal — may Allah make me and you among His beloved — it is the goal. Therefore we also say that interpreting it as reward diminishes its indication and its content, because the soul is not stirred when it means reward; rather love is taken in its apparent sense, and it is not permissible to divert it from its apparent sense.

If someone says: Do you apply this principle to all texts?

Answer: Yes, we must apply this principle to all the texts, because the Companions were unanimous on it (ijmāʿ, consensus). None of them ever interpreted the Qur'an contrary to its apparent meaning. So regarding the attributes of Allah, we must affirm them, but on an important basis that Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned in His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11]. Whatever Allah has affirmed for Himself, it is on this principle. What is it? ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. By this you will find rest and be spared many objections. Among them: nowadays there is frequent questioning about whether we affirm boredom (al-malal) for Allah or not, citing the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah does not tire until you tire"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1970), Muslim (782 / 215), and Abu Dawud (1368), and the wording is his, from the hadith of ʿAʾishah.]]. It is said: What prompted you to scratch something until the bone comes out? What prompted you to this: do you affirm boredom for Allah or not? Those who are better than you, from those who preceded you in this Ummah, and the best of this Ummah, never asked the Messenger ﷺ about this at all. They understood the meaning and left the wording as it is. What prompted you? Is the hadith explicit that Allah becomes bored? It is not explicit, it is not explicit. Its context is: "Take on of the deeds what you are able to bear – meaning, bear of them what you are able to – for Allah does not tire until you tire"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1970), Muslim (782 / 215), and Abu Dawud (1368), and the wording is his, from the hadith of ʿAʾishah.]]. That is, He does not tire of rewarding you until you tire of the deed. This is its meaning, and it is clear. And if it indicates the affirmation of tiring for Allah, then tiring, like the other attributes, is a tiring befitting Allah, not resembling the tiring of created beings. The tiring of a created being is fatigue, exhaustion and shortness of breath, but this is not affirmed for Allah, may He be exalted, at all. Is this clear, brothers?

Like anger. Now, Allah has affirmed anger for Himself. There is no problem with this, in the Qur'an in several places, and in the Sunnah likewise. If someone said: anger is the boiling of the blood of the heart seeking revenge; anger drives the angry person to bad conduct, to the extent that he breaks utensils, divorces wives, frees slaves, endows properties, and tears up papers. Is that not so? Yes. Some people reach this extent. If someone said: Is the anger of Allah, which we truly affirm, like the anger of a created being?
No. When Allah, may He be exalted, becomes angry, He will not act except for wisdom, He will not act except for wisdom. His anger is evidence of His strength, may He be exalted, and the strength of His dominion, because anger does not arise except from one able to take revenge. Is it not so? The weak one cannot become angry; he cannot become angry. If you hit a boy, will he become angry at you and come to take revenge on you? Answer, brothers: what will he do? He cries, grieves, goes to his mother and says: "This one hit me and did such-and-such." But the one with authority is the one who becomes angry and takes revenge. So anger is a praiseworthy attribute, but on the condition that it does not take the angry person beyond his proper measure. For this reason we say: Allah, may He be exalted, becomes angry, but not like the anger of a created being, who goes beyond his measure until he acts in an unbefitting way. Measure everything by this. When you affirm for Allah what He has affirmed for Himself, and you observe proper manners with Allah so that you do not exceed what Allah, may He be exalted, has mentioned, and you affirm this according to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11], then you will be safe in your creed and your thinking, and from the confusion that Satan casts into your heart. But if you move in these texts to the right and to the left, you are on the edge of a crumbling precipice.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the exhortation to good conduct towards creation, and to excellence in worshipping the Creator. Because when Allah informs us that He loves the good-doers, what does He want from us? That we act so that we attain this great rank, which is the love of Allah. I ask Allah to make me and you among His beloved. Therefore, from it is derived the exhortation to excellence.
* Student: Those who deny pleasure and anger, in the story of Moses, the removal of Moses from Pharaoh (...)?
* Shaykh: They cannot turn it away.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: They are incapable.
* Student: (...) the human mind cannot conceive it. Is this pleasure or anger?
* Shaykh: There is no doubt it is anger, and the deliverance of Moses is pleasure. They – may Allah bless you – they do not have minds. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, described them with a precise description. He said: they have been given understandings but not given knowledge (ʿilm); so they have no knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, they have understanding. And they have been given cleverness but not purity; they have no piety towards Allah, may He be exalted. Otherwise, if they feared Allah, may He be exalted, they would respect the texts of the Book and the Sunnah. At the least we can say of them: they are ignorant. That is, the lack of piety in them may not be deliberate, but based on the assumption that they are upon guidance, and they think they are upon something while they are astray.
* Student: Arab emigrants in European countries do work mixed between lawful and unlawful, like shopkeepers..
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: Some Muslims work in European countries, selling, for example, items in shops, some of which are unlawful and some lawful, such as wine and pork and the like. If a person is invited by them, for example, or eats at their place, is there anything upon him?
* Shaykh: There is nothing upon him if he eats what is permissible. If he eats what is permissible, there is nothing upon him. But as (...) if there is a benefit in not accepting the invitation, then here accepting the invitation is not obligatory.
* Student: What is your opinion, Shaykh, regarding the one who says: the Prophet ﷺ ate the food of the Jews and accepted their gifts because they were Jews, disbelievers, not upon a correct religion; but now the Muslims have knowledge from the Book and the Sunnah of the prohibition of that for them?
* Shaykh: This is an incorrect answer, because Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned that they eat illicit gain and take usury. Did He mention this as praise for them or as blame for them?
* Student: As blame for them.
* Shaykh: For this reason He said: ﴿And they had been forbidden from it﴾ [al-Nisa 161]. So they are forbidden from it. But some people want to make unlawful the property of one who eats of it mixed with the unlawful, and then defend this with a weak argument.
* Student: Is his wealth considered (...) unlawful?
* Shaykh: No, it is not unlawful; it is an unlawful earning.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game that your hands and spears can reach, that Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen. And whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment. (94) O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally, then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, as judged by two just men among you as an offering to be delivered to the Kaʿbah, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the bad consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94, 95].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game﴾.
Before we begin tonight's lesson, we wish to examine His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good﴾. What is the meaning of the first?
* Student: ﴿If they fear Allah﴾ means the prohibited things, ﴿and believe﴾ means with their hearts..
* Shaykh: I want the meaning of the first fear.
* Student: Fear the prohibited things.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The prohibited things among the foods.
* Shaykh: And the second?
* Student: Persist in their fear.
* Shaykh: Persist in fear and in abandoning the prohibited things. And the third?
* Student: General fear.
* Shaykh: General fear. So there is no repetition, because each one is carried to a different meaning.
His saying: ﴿and believe﴾. ﴿If they fear Allah and believe﴾ ﴿then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good﴾. The first?
* Student: The first, believe in the resolution of these mentioned matters.
* Shaykh: In their resolution?
* Student: Believe in what must be believed in.
* Shaykh: Yes, that is, in general. The second, believe?
* Student: That is, persist in their belief.
* Shaykh: That is, persist in their belief.
It was previously mentioned that one of the benefits of the verse is the affirmation of an attribute of Allah, may He be exalted?
* Student: The affirmation of love.
* Shaykh: The affirmation of love as an attribute of Allah.
Perhaps you recall from before whether love is one of the essential attributes or the active attributes?
* Student: Active.
* Shaykh: Active. Why?
* Student: When Allah wants to love a person, He loves him.
* Shaykh: Because it is related to His will, and every attribute that is tied to a cause is among the active attributes, because it is dependent on that cause.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 94:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 94]. A report from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning this form of address, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, has come down to us. Is there a saying of Ibn Mas'ud on it?

* Student: He said: "When you hear Allah say ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your ear, for it is either good that you are commanded to do or evil that you are forbidden from."

* The Shaykh: He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your ear – listen, pay attention – for it is either good you are commanded to do or evil you are forbidden from."[[Related by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50).]]

Let us now look at ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game﴾ etc. [Al-Ma'idah: 94]. The sentence here is declarative, and it is emphasized by three emphatic devices. What are they?

* Student: The lam, and the nun of emphasis.

* The Shaykh: And the nun of emphasis: ﴿will surely test you﴾ (layabluwannakum).

* Student: And the oath.

* The Shaykh: The implied oath; for the lam is a preparatory lam (lam al-mutawati'ah) introducing the oath.

The meaning of "yabluwnakum" is "will test you." And by what does the testing occur? He said: ﴿that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen﴾.

﴿with something of the game﴾ that you hunt, which is forbidden to you while in a state of ihram..

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you﴾. A report from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning this form of address, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, has come down to us, a saying in which he said (may Allah be pleased with him): "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your ear – listen, pay attention – for it is either good you are commanded to do or evil you are forbidden from."[[Related by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50).]]

Let us now look at ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game﴾ to its end. The sentence here is declarative and emphasized by three devices. What are they?

* Student: The lam.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the lam.

* Student: And the nun of emphasis.

* The Shaykh: And the nun of emphasis: ﴿will surely test you﴾.

* Student: And the oath.

* The Shaykh: The implied oath, for the lam is a preparatory lam introducing the oath. The meaning of "yabluwannakum" is "will test you." And by what does the testing occur?

He said: ﴿that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen﴾.

﴿with something of the game﴾ that you hunt, which is forbidden to you during the state of ihram.

﴿that your hands and your spears can reach﴾, meaning: you hunt it with the hand and you hunt it with spears. This varies according to the condition of the game: what walks on the ground, they could reach with their hands, and what flies, they could reach with their spears, because the bird is higher and flight is faster than crawling. Yet even so, the bird may be low and calm in its flight, since the One who holds it in the expanse of the sky, who is it? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He is able, Mighty and Majestic, to bring it down near the earth and to make its flight gentle.

We said that testing means trial. For what? He said: ﴿that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen﴾.

﴿that Allah may know﴾: the lam here expresses purpose, and "yaʿlama" means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, perceives who fears Him in the unseen, that is, who fears Allah.

﴿in the unseen﴾ has two meanings. The first: he fears Him while He, Glorified and Exalted, is out of his sight, as in His saying: "If you do not see Him, indeed He sees you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

Also, "in the unseen" has a second meaning: during His absence from people, such as being in the night, or in the shade of a tree, or behind a hill, or on a game trail, or the like.

So "that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen" has two meanings. The first: that he fears his Lord despite His being unseen by him, since he has not seen his Lord but has known Him through His signs.

The second meaning: "in the unseen" means in His absence from people, because among people there are those who display the fear of Allah outwardly but inwardly do not fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The one who is praised is the one who fears Allah in the unseen. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord in the unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Al-Mulk 12].

﴿that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen; so whoever transgresses after that﴾: meaning, whoever oversteps the sacred prohibitions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, after Allah has made the ruling clear to him, ﴿for him is a painful punishment﴾: meaning a painful punishment, either in this world or in the Hereafter, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

* In the noble verse: an explanation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, testing His servants by making the means of disobedience easy for them, so that He may know who fears Him in the unseen and who fears Him only in the open. Its indication from the verse is clear: ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach, that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), who are the vanguard of this Ummah, through their fear of Allah, their not devising tricks against the sacred prohibitions of Allah, and their not violating the sanctities of Allah. For this game with which they were tested did in fact occur, since Allah informed that He would do so and He did. Yet not one of them is reported to have taken a single game animal. They feared Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they magnified His prohibitions. This is a great virtue for this Ummah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that this Ummah surpasses all other nations, foremost among them the Jewish nation. For the Jewish nation was tested by Allah, Exalted, with something similar, but they devised tricks against the prohibitions of Allah. Allah tested them with hunting, the sea game and not the land game. He forbade them to catch fish on the Sabbath, so they devised a way around this: they set nets on Friday and took the fish or the whales on Sunday. Allah then tested them by making the fish come to them on the Sabbath in such abundance that they were visible on the surface of the water. They devised this trick, and Allah, Exalted, said to them: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [Al-Baqarah 65]. So they became apes – we seek Allah's refuge – all the people of that town became howling like apes howl, because they had devised tricks against the prohibitions of Allah through what outwardly appeared to be permissible, so Allah turned them into animals closest to humans.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person should be watchful over himself when the means of disobedience are made easy for him, and that Satan should not lead him step by step. For a person may find the means of disobedience made easy for him without realizing it about himself, then he becomes absorbed until he falls into what is forbidden. So a person should beware of the facilitation or ease of the means of disobedience lest he fall into disobedience.
