As for His saying: ﴿and the qala'id﴾, there are two views concerning it. The first view: in the Jahiliyyah, when a person performed hajj or 'umrah, he would make a garland from tree bark, from fruit or something else, and wear it, so that it would be known that he was a pilgrim and would be respected. Look at the wonders! Strange customs: when he performed hajj or 'umrah, he made a garland to wear, and if anyone saw him, he would say: this is a pilgrim or one performing 'umrah.

The second view: the qala'id refers to what is hung on the hady. The hady is garlanded around its neck with something that indicates it is a hady, namely: waterskin straps, or worn-out sandals hung on the necks of the hady as a sign that it is a hady, so that it is respected. Some of them said: a man in the Jahiliyyah would eat sinew from hunger, and could not slaughter or sacrifice this hady, because it bore a sign, which is the garlands.

Garlands are placed on sheep, on camels, and on cattle. The camel is additionally marked with ish'ar, which is cutting its hump until the blood flows, so that people know this is from the hady. All of these, Allah the Exalted made a means of stability for the people.

Let us look at the grammar: ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability﴾. Where is the first object of ﴿made (ja'ala)﴾?
* Students: ﴿the Ka'bah﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿the Ka'bah﴾, and the second is ﴿a means of stability﴾.

His saying: ﴿and the Sacred Month﴾ is also coordinated with ﴿the Ka'bah﴾. On this basis, the second object of the coordinated items is implied: that is, and the Sacred Month a means of stability, and the hady a means of stability, and the qala'id a means of stability for the people.

* Student: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to honour the Sacred Months. Did they take this from an earlier religion, or...?
* Shaykh: I do not know that it came from an earlier religion, but it was practised among them and was well known. However, I do not know that it came from an earlier religion.

* Student: O Shaykh, what is the wisdom in forbidding land game during ihram (the state of ritual consecration), while sea game is permitted to the one in ihram? Is there a preference between them, O Shaykh, or is this a wisdom Allah placed for people?
* Shaykh: No, there is a distinction. We mentioned regarding the prohibition of land game that the wisdom behind it is so that a person does not become distracted and pursue the game. As for the sea, this does not happen there. First, hardly anyone is in ihram while at sea, except one who passes by it. Second, even if we suppose that someone entered ihram on land, he might wade into the sea and hunt, but this is rare; therefore it has no ruling.
* Student: So the permission and prohibition are not equal?
* Shaykh: No, there is a clear difference. Sea game is permitted because people are not much distracted by it during ihram. As for within the Sacred Area (haram), there is no sea within its boundaries. But if we suppose an artificial lake that contains fish, then it is permitted, because it is sea game.
* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, on the coast of the sea there are animals that have no blood.
* Shaykh: They have no blood?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes, like what?
* Student: They are known only to the people of the coast, with strange names.
* Shaykh: But do they live on land, or not?
* Student: They live on land, and perhaps they live in the sea. The last one I saw was on the coast.
* Shaykh: Some scholars say: if most of its life is in the sea, then it is a sea creature even if it lives on land. Others say: no, as long as it lives on land, it is not a sea creature, unless its life on land is like the movement of a slaughtered animal, meaning when a fish is taken out and continues to convulse until it dies. That is not considered.
* Student: And birds that feed on fish?
* Shaykh: On fish?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: They are land birds.
* Student: Land birds, but they eat only fish.
* Shaykh: That makes no difference.
* Student: Is it lawful or unlawful?
* Shaykh: No, hunting them is unlawful, because they are land game.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people, and the Sacred Month, and the hady and the qala'id. That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things (97). Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (98). The Messenger's duty is only to convey, and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal (99). Say: not equal are the wicked and the good, even if the abundance of the wicked impresses you. So fear Allah, O people of understanding, that you may succeed﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 97-100].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people﴾. It has already passed that fish and dead sea creatures are lawful. From where is this derived?
* Student: His saying the Exalted: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food﴾.
* Shaykh: What is the basis of the inference?
* Student: It means: everything in the sea is lawful.
* Shaykh: But what is the basis for saying that dead animals are lawful?
* Student: "Game of the land" means the thing hunted.
* Shaykh: No, we are speaking of the game of the sea. If it is found dead, is it lawful or unlawful? Your companion says it is lawful and brought the verse, but did not explain the basis of the inference?
* Student: ﴿And its food﴾, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: ﴿And its food﴾.
* Student: It means: what is not hunted but is dead by nature, its food. That is the meaning.
* Shaykh: So its food is what is found?
* Student: Dead.
* Shaykh: Dead. Good. This was reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.[[Recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (20007) from a hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

His saying: ﴿and for the travellers﴾. From it we derived evidence for what?
* Student: That it is permitted to store meat.
* Shaykh: Storing meat is permitted, and eating it after storing it. Is this restricted by anything?
* Student: Yes, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: What is it?
* Student: As long as it has not spoiled, so that it does not become harmful.
* Shaykh: As long as it has not spoiled, so that it does not become harmful. Then it is not permitted.
From where do we take that it is forbidden?
* Student: The implication of the verse: ﴿Lawful for you﴾.
* Shaykh: You see, we do not need to derive the ruling from this verse.
* Student: ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3].
* Shaykh: No, I do not know that. It is not forbidden.
* Student: "There shall be no harm and no reciprocating harm."[[Recorded by Ibn Majah (2341) from a hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]
* Shaykh: We have something clearer and more authentic than it, because this hadith has what it has of discussion among the scholars. Do you recite the Qur'an? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [An-Nisa 29]. Do you understand? Answer, say: yes or no?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Good, this verse indicates this.
If someone says: this verse indicates that whatever leads to destruction is forbidden, and what falls short of killing is not included in the verse?
* Student: It is answered by the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the expedition of Dhat al-Salasil, when he performed tayammum (dry ablution) because he feared the cold. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you lead your companions in prayer while you were in a state of major impurity?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (334) from a hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As.]] (...) The Prophet (ﷺ) while (...).
* Shaykh: Well done. We say: although the verse indicates that what is forbidden is killing, 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, used it as evidence for the permissibility of tayammum out of fear of cold or illness, and the Prophet (ﷺ) approved of that.

The hunting of land game is forbidden?
* Student: The hunting of land game is forbidden, due to His saying the Exalted: ﴿And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in ihram﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, but what is the land game? What is the forbidden thing? Is everything on land forbidden?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: Every animal.
* Shaykh: Every animal.
* Student: Land animal.
* Shaykh: Land animal.
* Student: Wild.
* Shaykh: Wild.
* Student: Lawful.
* Shaykh: Lawful.
What is the meaning of your saying "land"?
* Student: "Land" means not domesticated.
* Shaykh: Wrong. Is it wild or domesticated?
* Student: "Land" is what lives on land.
* Shaykh: That means what lives only on land.
What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿to Him you will be gathered﴾?
* Student: The benefit of His saying "you will be gathered" is that the gathering is to Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection.
* Shaykh: But what is the benefit of mentioning it after He said: ﴿fear Allah﴾?
* Student: It conveys the Last Day.
* Shaykh: But what is the benefit of its coming after His saying: ﴿fear Allah﴾?
* Student: Warning.
* Shaykh: Warning; that is, there is no escape for you from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, so fear Him.
What is the benefit of placing the prepositional phrase first?
* Student: Restriction (hasr).
* Shaykh: Restriction, well done.
Is there a rule on which this answer is based?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: What is it?
* Student: When something whose place is to be delayed is placed first, it conveys restriction.
* Shaykh: Well done, good, this is a well-known rule among the rhetoricians and the jurists of principles.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people﴾. Is this making legislative or pre-destined?
* Student: No, legislative.
* Shaykh: Legislative only?
* Student: Entirely pre-destined.
* Shaykh: Both legislative and pre-destined.
* Student: No, legislative.
* Shaykh: Answer: is it legislative or pre-destined?
* Student: Both legislative and pre-destined.
* Shaykh: Both legislative and pre-destined.

﴿The Sacred House﴾: is it an explanatory apposition (atf bayan) or a qualifier (qayd)?
* Student: Apposition.
* Another student: A qualifier.
* Shaykh: A qualifier, which excludes?
* Student: It excludes all Ka'bahs other than the Ka'bah of Makkah.
* Shaykh: Other than the honoured Ka'bah, correct. That is, if a person built a Ka'bah, meaning a square building, and said: this is a Ka'bah, perform hajj to it, we would say: no, because the Ka'bah that Allah made a means of stability is the Sacred House, and it is the specific one.

His saying: ﴿the Sacred Month﴾: one, or three, or four, or five?
* Student: It is a category, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: It includes?
* Student: All the Sacred Months.
* Shaykh: All the Sacred Months. And their number?
* Student: Four.
* Shaykh: Four. What are they?
* Student: Dhu al-Qi'dah.
* Shaykh: Dhu al-Qa'dah.
* Student: Dhu al-Hijjah.
* Shaykh: Dhu al-Hijjah is more eloquent.
* Student: Muharram, and Rajab.
* Shaykh: Well done, correct. So this is general.
What is the aspect of these months being a means of stability for the people?
* Student: His saying: ﴿a means of stability for the people﴾ (...) fighting is forbidden in them.
* Shaykh: Fighting is forbidden in them, so the people are secure in their journeys and in their homelands, because they are months of honour, even in...
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to the making. That is, We made that not out of ignorance, for example, but out of knowledge.
﴿That you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth﴾: Allah the Exalted made that out of knowledge of the benefits contained in these four things, and so He made them a means of stability for the people. Allah mentioned this only so that people would be assured that Allah made them a means of stability, and that this making proceeds from the knowledge of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth﴾. "What" (ma) is one of the forms of generality, so it includes everything in the heavens and everything on the earth. "Heavens" is the plural of "sky," and their number is seven. This is established by the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 86]. The Sunnah on this is mutawatir (widely transmitted) or mashhur (well known).

His saying: ﴿the earth﴾ is in the singular form, but its number is seven, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ [At-Talaq 12]. It is well known that the likeness here cannot be in size, extent and similar things, because of the enormous difference between the sky and the earth. Rather, the likeness is in number, based on what came in the Sunnah: "Whoever unjustly takes a handspan of land, Allah will collar him with it on the Day of Resurrection, from seven earths."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2452) and Muslim (1610/137), the wording of Muslim, from a hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl.]] So "the earth" here refers to the category, and it includes the seven earths.

﴿And that Allah﴾ means: and that you may also know ﴿that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah is knowing of all things, nothing is hidden from Him. The knowledge of Allah, blessed and exalted, is one of His essential attributes. He knows what will occur until the Day of Resurrection and what lies beyond the Day of Resurrection. He has always been knowing of that from eternity without beginning. Forgetfulness does not befall His knowledge, and ignorance does not precede it, glorified and exalted is He.

In the verse there are many benefits. Among them: God, glorified and exalted, has magnified this noble Ka'bah, in that He made it a means of standing (qiyam) for the people, by which the affairs of their religion and their worldly life are upheld.

Among them: it is for God, glorified and exalted, to favor whomever He wills of His creation. This is a known matter, and it has examples in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have certainly favored some of the prophets over others﴾ [al-Isra' 55], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those messengers — some of them We have caused to exceed others. Among them are those to whom God spoke, and some He raised in degrees﴾ [al-Baqarah 253], and God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit﴾ [al-Ra'd 4]. So it is for God, glorified and exalted, to favor whomever He wills of His creation.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Ka'bah is sacred (haram), that is, respected and magnified; and for this reason, what surrounds it is also sacred, so its game may not be killed and its trees may not be cut.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of God, blessed and exalted, toward creation, in that He places among His creatures that by which the interests of their religion and their worldly life are upheld.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnifying of the sacred months, and that they are a means of standing for the people. Their magnification has come in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [al-Tawbah 36]. Likewise it has come in the Sunnah, as the Prophet (ﷺ) affirmed when he said: "Indeed your blood, your property and your honor are sacred to you, as the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4406) and Muslim (1679/30) from the hadith of Abu Bakrah.]].

If someone says: Is fighting forbidden in them?

The answer: The scholars differed on this. Some of them said that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months has been abrogated (mansukh), and others said that it is muhkam (decisive, not abrogated). The first view, held by the majority, is that it is abrogated, because of the generality of the evidences indicating the fighting of the polytheists without restriction. The second view is the preferred one: that fighting in them is prohibited. Whatever comes in general or absolute form in other texts is, like other generals and absolutes, restricted by what the Book and the Sunnah indicate regarding the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months.

If someone says: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not fight in the sacred months, as in the battle of Hunayn?

The answer: Yes, but that was a continuation of the conquest of Makkah, and the conquest of Makkah did not take place in the sacred months but in Ramadan. On this basis we say: if the disbelievers attack us in the sacred months, we may fight them, even in the sacred months, because our fighting in that case is defense, and a person must defend himself in any place and at any time. For example, in Makkah, is fighting there forbidden or not? It is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. But if the people of Makkah, or anyone other than its people, fight us in Makkah, we fight him, because of the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿So if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 191].

So we say: if the enemy initiates fighting against us in the sacred months, we may fight him. Then, is this obligatory, recommended, or permissible? That is to be considered. But the discussion concerns the continuing prohibition of fighting in the sacred months, except when it is a continuation of an earlier raid, or when our enemies initiate fighting against us.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnifying of the sacrificial animals (hady) and encouragement toward them, because of His saying: ﴿and the hady﴾; that is, God made it a means of standing for the people.

But is the hady tied to the rite of pilgrimage (nusuk), or is it permissible for a person to send a hady to the House even if it is not a rite of worship?

The answer: The second. It is permissible for a person to send a hady to Makkah even if he is in his own land, as the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5566) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her.]]

If someone says: Is it sunnah to drive the hady in 'umrah as in Hajj?

The answer: Yes, it is sunnah, "as the Prophet (ﷺ) did at the Battle of Hudaybiyyah, for he drove the hady in an 'umrah." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1694), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (18910), with his wording, from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the legitimacy of garlands (qala'id), because of His saying: ﴿and the garlands﴾. The reason is that in them there is a display of the rites of God, the Mighty and Majestic, for everyone who sees these garlanded animals knows that they are hady, so he magnifies and respects them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of wisdom in the rulings of God, the Mighty and Majestic, because of His saying: ﴿That is so that you may know﴾. The lam here denotes causation (ta'lil), and among the names of God, blessed and exalted, is al-Hakim (the All-Wise), the One who places things in their proper places.

* Branching from this great benefit: we must believe that everything God has legislated or done is for a wisdom. Then we are not obliged to search for the wisdom or to strain to find a distant wisdom that may not be what God intends, the Mighty and Majestic. If the wisdom becomes clear to us easily, then there is no doubt that this is a blessing from God and it increases a person's tranquility. If it does not become clear, we know that it is for a wisdom, but our minds are too limited to grasp the wisdom of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in what He has legislated.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the urging to know the attributes of God, the Mighty and Majestic, because of His saying: ﴿that you may know that God knows﴾. So it is fitting for you to seek knowledge of the attributes of God, blessed and exalted, whether the attributes that have no names or the attributes contained in the names. Seek, for the more you know God and His names and attributes, the more certainty you gain.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against opposing God, the Mighty and Majestic. Its basis: the affirmation of knowledge, that God knows what is in the heavens and the earth. For every person who intends a disobedience, whether abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, if he is certain that God knows of it, he will fear and refrain.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge, glorified and exalted, of what is in the heavens and the earth. From where do we take it? From the relative pronoun in ﴿what is in the heavens﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation that the heavens are of a number. But how many is this number? It is explained in other evidences that they are seven heavens.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the repetition of praise of God, the Mighty and Majestic, for God repeated the generality of His knowledge with His saying: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, then He emphasized the generality with what is more comprehensive in His saying: ﴿and that God is Knowing of all things﴾. That is, this includes what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, including what will be after the passing away of the heavens and the earth: ﴿Knowing of all things﴾.

Know that knowledge, meaning the attribute of knowledge, is among the most comprehensive of the attributes, if not the most comprehensive, because knowledge relates to the necessary, the possible, and the impossible, the past and the future. So it is among the most comprehensive of attributes. Among its relation to the impossible is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿If there were within them gods other than God, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]. Is it possible for there to be gods in them other than God? It is not possible. Yet God, the Mighty and Majestic, informed us of the result of supposing it: that they, that is the heavens and the earth, would be ruined.

As for its relation to the necessary, it is everything God informs about Himself of the attributes of perfection, for that is knowledge of the necessary, since the attributes of perfection are necessary for God.

As for its relation to the possible, it is everything God informs about His creatures, and this falls under the relation of knowledge to the possible.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said, after mentioning His comprehensive knowledge following these great rulings: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾. ﴿Know﴾, meaning: knowledge by which compliance is achieved. ﴿Know﴾: it is obligatory for us to know, because Allah has commanded us to do so. ﴿That Allah is severe in punishment﴾, meaning: the taking to account for sin. The taking to account for sin is called punishment ('iqab) because it follows (ta'qubu) the sin. ﴿Severe in punishment﴾ means: strong, in quantity and quality, or in quality only?

* Students: The first.

* The Shaykh: Consider it.

* Students: In quantity.

* Other students: The first.

* The Shaykh: Strength in quantity is not possible, because Allah says: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof﴾ [al-An'am 160]. But strength in quality is correct: ﴿severe in punishment﴾ means strong in punishment when He punishes the sinner.

﴿And that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾. This means: know also that, along with the severity of His punishment, He is forgiving of sins and merciful to His servants, Mighty and Majestic. He does not burden them with what is hard for them, and if they fall short in it, He shows them mercy by pardoning them, Mighty and Majestic.

Compare this verse with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr 49-50]. You will find a difference between them. The difference is that the verse ﴿Inform﴾ is a command from Allah to the Messenger to inform the creation. The attribute of forgiveness and mercy was placed before the painful punishment, because the intent is to report the attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so the aspect containing gentleness and kindness is placed first. This verse, however, was mentioned right after great rulings that a person may neglect, so the aspect placed first in it is what? The aspect of warning (tahdid).

﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

* In this noble verse: the obligation of knowing with certainty, from His saying: ﴿Know﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah, Exalted, is severe in punishment toward whoever opposes His command, whether by doing what He forbade or by abandoning what He made obligatory.

If someone says: the apparent meaning of this verse is that Allah will punish whoever opposes His command in every case?

The answer: when you read the end of the verse, it becomes clear that in contrast to that, He is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful. Then pair it with another verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa 48].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming punishment, which is taking the sinner to account by the penalty he deserves.

* Among its benefits: affirming these two noble names, al-Ghafur (the Oft-Forgiving) and ar-Rahim (the Most Merciful). Al-Ghafur means the one possessing forgiveness, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [ar-Ra'd 6]. Ar-Rahim means the one possessing mercy, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord is the Free of need, the Possessor of mercy﴾ [al-An'am 133]. So we affirm these two names for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and we affirm the attributes they indicate: forgiveness in (Ghafur) and mercy in (Rahim).

Does the effect (athar) also follow, meaning the ruling that results from this attribute?

The answer: yes. He forgives whom He wills, and has mercy on whom He wills.

What follows from these two names and from believing in them? It follows that a person exposes himself to the forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by doing the means that bring it about, and exposes himself to what? To mercy, by doing the means through which mercy is obtained. This is the opposite of what some common people (al-'awwam) think. When you forbid some common people from a sin, they say: "Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful," and they imagine that this is a way of making the transgression easy for the servant. It is not so. Rather, this is an encouragement for the servant to do what brings forgiveness and mercy.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the combining of Allah's names, Blessed and Exalted, from whose combination arises an attribute added to the attribute each name conveys when standing alone.

For example, when we say He is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, the meaning becomes: He forgives sins, and He grants what is sought in acts of obedience. For this reason, one sin is recorded as one, while one act of obedience is recorded as ten, up to seven hundred times, and up to many multiples.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 5, verse 99:**

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to deliver (the message), and Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal.﴾

﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾: *ma* is a negation particle, *ʿalā al-rasūl* is the predicate placed before its subject, and *al-balāgh* is the postponed subject.

As for his saying ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾: the *al* here is for *al-ʿahd* (reference to a known thing), meaning which known thing?

* A student: The mental one.

* The Shaykh: The mental one. So *al* is for *al-ʿahd al-dhihnī* (the mental reference, where the referent is known in the mind).

Who is known in the mind as the Messenger for this ummah? Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, peace be upon him.

﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ means "the one sent." His saying ﴿إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾ means the delivery of the message. As for guiding people, it is not upon the Messenger, peace be upon him. He is only to deliver, and once he has delivered, his duty is complete. For this reason, He said: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ﴾, meaning what you show, ﴿وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾, meaning what you hide. The meaning is that your deeds are not the responsibility of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and he is not accountable for them. Rather, the One who will call you to account for them is Allah, who knows what you show and what you conceal.

* A student: Does avoiding sins in the sacred months have a special merit? That is, is the sin greater?

* The Shaykh: This depends on His saying: ﴿فَلَا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ [At-Tawbah 36]. Does the pronoun in *fīhinna* refer to the sacred months, or to ﴿اثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا﴾ (twelve months)? There is a difference of opinion on this. But there is no doubt that sins in the sacred months are greater, because whether we say the pronoun refers to all of them or to these months, it indicates the emphasis of the prohibition of wrongdoing in these four months. The scholars have a principle on this matter: they say that good deeds and bad deeds are multiplied in every time and place that is virtuous.

* A student: Shaykh, as for disbelievers and people of sin, they live in this world in health, with wealth and abundant provision. But what about the Hereafter, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: In the Hereafter, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in the *ḥadīth qudsī* (sacred hadith) to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4850) and Muslim (2846/34), from Abu Hurayrah.]] And they are not its people, so there is no mercy for them. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to them: ﴿اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 108], "Be silent in it and do not speak to Me." But their punishment is a mercy to the believers, that they see their enemies being punished in the Fire. Yes indeed.

* A student: Some people, Shaykh, use wealth, health and well-being as evidence for people of sin. They say: if Allah were displeased with them, He would not have given them this wealth, nor ...?

* The Shaykh: Some common people think the opposite. I hear some common people say, for example: "His giving proves His pleasure with him." That is not necessarily so. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Al-A'raf 182], "And those who deny Our signs, We will lead them gradually (to destruction) from where they do not know." This is *istidrāj* (gradual enticement) from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The Prophet, peace be upon him, informed us: "Allah gives worldly things to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He gives religion only to whom He loves."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3672) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (94), from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] May Allah make us and you among those He loves.

* A student: May Allah reward you well, Shaykh. What is meant by His saying: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 22], "If there were in them gods other than Allah, they would both be ruined"? Does it mean gods who manage and direct the affairs of the universe, or gods who are only worshipped?

* The Shaykh: No, the first. Or he said: gods of truth. Because the gods that are worshipped besides Allah, even if they are called gods, are as Allah, Exalted, said about them: ﴿إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا﴾ [An-Najm 23], "They are nothing but names you have named," merely names without realities behind them.

* A student: May Allah protect you. In yesterday's lesson, someone asked during the call to prayer about animals that live both on land and in the sea, living a full life rather than the movement of a slaughtered animal: crocodiles, frogs, turtles. I do not know, Shaykh: is the land aspect dominant, so that they are considered forbidden?

* The Shaykh: No, because those that live with the movement of a slaughtered animal, many large fish do not die immediately. They remain for hours, but they are agitated and unconscious, and then they die later.

* The student: But those that live a full life, laying eggs on land and living in the sea?

* The Shaykh: Yes. Some scholars say: the predominant aspect is what counts. If it lives in both, the predominant one is what counts, because the dominant characteristic is the one that is considered. Others say: no, it is forbidden, giving precedence to the side of prohibition.

* The student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, caution is to leave it. But if it were assumed that he found a carcass of land game or this, then that is more appropriate (to avoid).

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. We said "knowledge" (ʿilm), and its aspect (wajh). I did not understand the aspect of the relation of knowledge: Allah's knowledge of possibilities (mumkinat) or of what is permissible (jā'iz)? What is its aspect?

* The Shaykh: What do you mean by "its aspect"?

* The student: That is, its explanation.

* The Shaykh: For example, the existence of creation: is it possible, impossible, or obligatory?

* The student: Possible.

* The Shaykh: Possible. Allah, Exalted, speaks about created things: He created the heavens in six days, He established Himself upon the Throne, and similar things. This is knowledge of possibilities. Is that right?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good. His knowledge also includes the punishments of sinners and the reward of the obedient. Is this knowledge?

* The student: Of possibilities.

* The Shaykh: Of possibilities. His knowledge of what is obligatory: when He, Glorified and Exalted, speaks of His perfection, this is speaking of knowledge of something necessary. Is it clear?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: The impossible, as you heard.

* The student: Some say: "permissible" is no longer "possible," Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: No. Permissible and possible are the same. That is, some express it as "permissible" and some express it as "possible," and there is no difference.

* A student: There are some types of fish that are caught but are not eaten unless their taste has changed, when they have changed and nearly...

* The Shaykh: You mean they stink?

* The student: They rot, and people eat them. What is their ruling?

* The Shaykh: And before that?

* The student: They are desirable in this state.

* The Shaykh: Perhaps. Some people like *al-mukhanaz* (a fish that is fermented)? Some people like this?

* The student: This, Shaykh, is found in large quantities.

* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know.

* A student: This type of fish is found in large quantities in some countries.

* The Shaykh: What is its name?

* The student: Its name is *al-buri* fish, which...

* The Shaykh: *al-buri*?

* The student: This *buri* is made into what is called *fasīkh* (fermented fish). It is taken and placed in the sun, and spread out in the hot sun until it rots and swells. Then after that it is placed in barrels, with salt on it, and the barrels are tightly sealed for about six months, more or less. Then they are sold, and...

* The Shaykh: And delicious?

* The student: Yes, delicious.

* Another student: Shaykh, there is another method, Shaykh: it is put in salt without being put in the sun.

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: It is put in salt and vinegar and covered, without being left... that is, it rots (...), salt and vinegar are put on it and it is covered until the salt affects it and it ripens.

* A student: This is the same method; it decomposes, that is...

* The Shaykh: In any case, you people of the seas, we do not know it. Unless you bring us some of it, as the certainty of sight (*ʿayn al-yaqīn*), then we eat from it, God willing, and it will be the certainty of truth (*ḥaqq al-yaqīn*).

* * *

* A student: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to deliver (the message), and Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal. (99) Say: Not equal are the evil and the good, even though the abundance of evil may please you. So fear Allah, O people of understanding, that you may succeed. (100) O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Quran is being revealed, they will be made apparent to you. Allah has pardoned that, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing. (101) A people before you asked about such things, and then became disbelievers because of them.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 99–102].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to deliver﴾. This refers to Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and his family. On this basis, the *al* is for *al-ʿahd al-dhihnī*.

As for His saying ﴿إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾, meaning: only the delivery of what was revealed to him. This restriction, as is clear, is a *ḥaṣr idāfī* (a restriction relative to a particular context). The Prophet (ﷺ) has other obligations: prayer, almsgiving, fasting, pilgrimage, jihad, and other things. But his duty toward you is only delivery, meaning that he conveys to you, and it is not upon him to guide you. Guidance is in the hand of Allah. So this restriction is relative: what does *idāfī* mean? That is, relative to what is obligatory for you upon him. ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾, meaning toward you, is ﴿إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾. As for guidance, it belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾: this is what a person is accountable for. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ﴾ means what you manifest of deeds, both verbal and physical. Did He know them before they existed, or after they existed? Before they existed, and after they existed.

His saying ﴿وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ means what you hide within yourselves, which are the actions of the heart. Indeed, even more than actions of the heart is what the heart whispers. As Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾ [Qaf 16], "We created man and We know what his soul whispers to him." This means that their reckoning is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not with the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and his family.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of conveying revelation upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because *ʿalā* (upon) clearly indicates obligation. Where is *ʿalā*?

* A student: ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not have the right to compel people to be guided. Many verses support this, including His saying: ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Yunus 99], "Will you then compel the people until they become believers?"

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), by His saying: ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾.

* From its benefits: a warning to those who convey (the message) against opposition, by His saying: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾. His informing about His knowledge after saying ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ﴾ contains a threat and warning against those who oppose.

* From it: the breadth and generality of Allah's knowledge, by His saying: ﴿مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾. This applies to the entire ummah, and *mā* here, as you know, is a relative pronoun that includes both little and much.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that the deeds of servants are divided into two parts: a part that appears to people, and a part that does not appear. By His saying: ﴿مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾.

If someone asks: Is it better for a person to show what he has done, or to conceal what he has done?

We say: both are good, because Allah praised those who spend their wealth secretly and openly. But which of the two is better? One considers the public interest (*maṣlaḥa*). If the public interest lies in announcing, then he announces, such as a person who is followed and emulated, so it is better that he announces it, so that people emulate him and know that this is the truth, and thereby he becomes a leader for those who follow him. But if concealment is better, then concealment is better. For example, if a person gives charity to a modest person who does not like to be seen, then here what is better? Secrecy. Even if the two are equal, and usually they are not equal in every respect, but supposing they are equal in every respect, then secrecy is better, because it is a stronger indication of sincerity and closer to sincerity.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the Jabriyya (determinists), who say that a person has no will. This is taken from His saying: ﴿مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾. A person wants to show and wants to conceal, and this is the affirmation of the servant's will.

The Jabriyya are a people who say that a person is not free to choose but is compelled. They rely on verses, including His saying: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيَخْتَارُ مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [Al-Qasas 68], "Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. Choice is not theirs. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate." They said: He negated that the servant has choice. Their argument is strong, but there is no doubt that this argument is false, because what is meant by His saying ﴿مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ is: in His act, Mighty and Majestic. For example: ﴿قَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 31], "They said: Why was this Quran not sent down upon a great man from one of the two cities?" They wanted to choose for themselves who would be a messenger. So Allah said: ﴿أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 32], "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?" So the meaning of His saying ﴿مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ is: in what Allah does. As for their own actions, they have choice.

The evidence for this is many verses, including: the options in the expiation for breaking an oath, where three options are given by choice: feeding ten needy people, clothing them, or freeing a slave, and other evidence.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that the people of knowledge, who are the heirs of the prophets, are free of responsibility when they have conveyed (the knowledge).

But must they convey it in every case, or only if there is benefit, or what? We say: the principle is that conveying is obligatory in every case. This is the principle, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Convey from me, even if it is a single verse."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3461), from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] However, conveying may not be obligatory in some cases, and it is permissible to withhold knowledge until a time when he sees benefit in doing so, as Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, did when he did not convey the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The right of the servants upon Allah is that He does not punish whoever does not associate anything with Him." He did not convey it except at his death, out of fear of sin.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2856) and Muslim (30/49), from Mu'adh.]] Otherwise, the principle is the obligation of conveying.

As for when a person is asked about knowledge: if the questioner is seeking guidance, it is obligatory to inform him. This is if he is seeking guidance. But if he is testing, then the person has a choice: if he wishes, he conveys; if he wishes, he refrains. This is because this questioner is not seeking guidance and does not want knowledge. He wants to test the one being asked, so the latter has a choice.

Is it better to convey or better not to convey? In this there is detail. If withholding the answer would humiliate and disgrace this questioner, then he should withhold it. But if withholding it would increase his evil and his transgression, then he must convey and explain his error to him. So the matter returns to considerations of benefit.

If you say: what is the measure of benefits? We say: each person is responsible for himself, and each matter has its ruling. For this reason, you will sometimes encounter in answers to some evidences the statement that it is a particular case, and each person acts according to what he sees, and Allah is his reckoner.

Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-Karīm) on Surah 5, verse 100:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾. Say, O Muhammad: they are not equal. The opening of the ruling with "Say" (قل) indicates that it is of great importance. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say the entire Qurʾān, to convey it to people and deliver it. But when a specific matter is mentioned explicitly, this indicates its particular importance. It is like specifying after generalizing, which conveys emphasis.

﴿Say﴾, meaning: say, O Muhammad, to everyone whose address is valid and who comprehends your address: ﴿the evil and the good are not equal﴾. Allah has spoken the truth. The evil and the good are not equal, whether among persons, deeds or objects. It is impossible for this and that to be equal. Right? They are not equal. Are prayer to Allah and prostration to an idol equal? They are not equal. This is among deeds.

Among objects: Are pure drink extracted from good fruits and wine equal? They are not equal.

As for persons: Are the good believer and the evil disbeliever equal? No. And so on.

So the evil and the good apply to everything: persons, objects, statements and actions, everything. Are the remembrance of Allah and backbiting equal? No. Therefore this is general: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾.

﴿Even if the abundance of the evil should impress you﴾. The statement ﴿even if it impresses you﴾: the address here is not to the Messenger (ﷺ), because the Messenger is not impressed by the abundance of the evil. Rather, it is addressed to you, O listener; that is, say to the person: the evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you, O listener. ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾. The address is not to the Messenger (ﷺ), because we know with certainty that he (ﷺ) is not impressed by the abundance of the evil.

﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾, meaning: it impresses you, that is, it reaches the point of admiration in you.

If you apply this to the children of Adam, which is more numerous: the evil or the good?

* Students: The evil (...).

* Shaykh: The evil?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: The evil among the children of Adam is more numerous?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Correct. The evil among the children of Adam is more numerous. Even if it impresses you. Likewise, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you with its power and production, it should not concern you, as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he impresses you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:221]. It should not concern you.

The evil is falsehood, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and thereupon it departs, vanishing﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ 21:18]. Look at these powerful words: ﴿We hurl﴾ means We throw with force. ﴿It crushes it﴾ means it strikes its brain, does not let it escape, and does not leave it for even the blink of an eye. For this reason He said: ﴿and thereupon it departs, vanishing﴾. The fāʾ (الفاء) indicates sequence and immediacy, and idhā (إذا) here is fajāʾiyya (إذا فجائية), indicating the suddenness of the vanishing, and that the vanishing almost occurs before it is crushed. ﴿And thereupon it departs, vanishing. And woe to you for what you describe﴾. But notice, brothers, that the sword is in the hand of the one who wields it. That is, the truth necessarily requires its bearer to be strong in the cause of Allah, not caring about anyone in the cause of Allah. Then falsehood will be routed and the truth will stand.

﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you, so fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾ [al-Māʾidah 5:100]. The fāʾ (الفاء) here is lil-tafrīʿ (للتفريع), meaning: based on that and on the abundance of the evil, fear Allah. Do not let the abundance of the evil impress you. Through fear of Allah the desired is attained and the feared is removed.

And His saying: ﴿O people of understanding﴾. Look how the address penetrates the heart: ﴿O people of understanding﴾, that is, O people of intellects, O possessors of minds. What is meant by intellects are those who possess right guidance and good judgment, not the intellect of perception. The disbeliever may have more of the intellect of perception than the believer, but the intellect of right guidance is entirely negated from the disbeliever (...) the intellect of right guidance, because if he had the intellect of right guidance.

* A student: He would not have disbelieved.

* Another student: He would have believed.

* Shaykh: He would have believed and not disbelieved. But he does not have the intellect of right guidance. So, O possessors of intellects, which intellects?

* Students: The rightly guided ones.

* Shaykh: The rightly guided ones, who know what benefits them so they act upon it, and what harms them so they avoid it.

And ﴿so that you may prosper﴾, that is, in order that you may prosper. Here la-ʿalla (لعل) indicates purpose (lil-taʿlīl). Where is the thing being explained (al-muʿallal)?

* A student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, this...

* A student: (...).

* Shaykh: The taqwā (fear of Allah). Fearing Allah, that is, so that you may prosper if you fear Allah the Mighty and Majestic. And falāḥ (prosperity) is a comprehensive word meaning success in attaining what is desired and deliverance from what is feared. This is falāḥ.

* A student: May Allah bless you. A person always faces some evil deeds, and they are numerous, and he is perplexed about whether to denounce them or not. If it were not a great evil, and if he denounced it, good might result, or good might not result. He might face mockery, for example.

* Shaykh: As for mockery, it is generally inevitable, it is inevitable. But does harm result?

* The student: Yes, to my soul, yes.

* Shaykh: No, not to your soul. Only physical harm.

* The student: No.

* Shaykh: Harm does not result. The person should be patient and seek reward. Many a word has benefited one of these people, and it benefits him. But it is not a condition that the matter be declared publicly in this way. He can take hold of the leaders, especially of these people, and speak with them calmly and explain to them. When leaders are granted guidance, many people are guided by their guidance.

* The student: Shaykh, sometimes a person faces a man whose appearance, I mean, I do not speak to him (...) I am compelled.

* Shaykh: How often this happens, and how often benefit is gained. You see some people whose appearance is not (what you expect), their appearance is sound, meaning you think that he (...) but you find his heart soft. This is tested. You may say: he is clean-shaven, with his garment trailing, his face is not the face of a righteous man. But, glory be to Allah, his heart is soft. At the least he will say, if you do not approach him harshly: May Allah reward you with good, and I ask Allah for guidance. This is tested. Take his hand gently. Lead him aside from the road a little and speak to him, and you will find much good. But our affliction comes from ourselves: when a person sees someone opposing him, he becomes jealous, he cannot bear it, and then he begins speaking in a way that drives his companion away.

* A student: We have mentioned that the principle is the obligation of conveying. But the problem, O Shaykh, is that it is reported from some imams and scholars that they said: I do not give my knowledge except to one who deserves knowledge, and I do not disseminate it except among its people. Is there a contradiction with their statement?

* Shaykh: No. He intended, if this report is authentic, to sit with people, knowing that he sits only with people who truly want knowledge, not those who want to make fun of beards.

* The student: But Shaykh, sometimes a person is riding in a car with a group of people, and he knows they do not want advice, and he wants to make use of the time. Should he, for example, advise them, remind them, give them...

* Shaykh: No, this is not correct. Sometimes the rider of a car does not immediately begin by saying: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and then intends to deliver sermons. They are not prepared to bear this. But he can enter their minds with things: either stories, and let them be amusing stories, it does not matter, or unusual scholarly questions which he presents to them, so that their minds are prepared for this. Otherwise, it is known that if a person sits in a gathering and says: Come on, in the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and starts admonishing them, they may find this burdensome. Every situation has its own speech.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Sometimes a person sits with a group who are upon an evil. If he stood up, he would gain nothing from them, and they would gain nothing from him. If he denounced them directly, they would not accept it from him. So should he force himself and sit in this place unwillingly?

* Shaykh: There is no harm. Like the doctor who cuts the wound and smells a foul odor in order to heal it. One of the scholars had a profound influence in some regions of the kingdom. He would enter into their evil with them and celebrate with them at their celebrations (...).

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would concern you; but if you ask about them while the Qurʾān is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing. A people before you asked about such matters, then became disbelievers because of them﴾ [al-Māʾidah 5:101–102].

* Shaykh: We seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would concern you﴾.

* Students: The benefits of the previous verse.

* Shaykh: The benefits of the one before it, only the verse just before it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to deliver, and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾ [al-Māʾidah 5:99]. This verse is a continuation of what precedes it, in His saying: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Māʾidah 5:98], meaning: He will hold you accountable. Then He explained the function of the Messenger (ﷺ). In the verse: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to deliver﴾.

* Students: (...) the benefits of the previous one.

* Shaykh: You have taken them. Good. ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾, to the end [al-Māʾidah 5:100].

* Among its benefits: The evil and the good are not equal before Allah the Mighty and Majestic, nor before people of intellect. This applies to their ranks before Allah and before those of understanding. As for matters of worldly affairs, the evil may be more numerous in deeds, as is observed now. The disbelieving nations are more advanced than the Muslim nations in matters relating to worldly affairs.

* Among the benefits of this verse: A person should not judge by quantity but by quality, not by number, based on His saying: ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾.

* Among its benefits: If a group gathers for consultation and then disputes over a matter, we consider the one closer to the correct view, if the difference is slight. If they are equal, then here we consider the majority, because the aim is the truth. If we know that these few are on the side of truth in terms of knowledge, trustworthiness, honesty and understanding, they are given precedence over the majority. But if they are equal, we consider the majority, because there is no way for us to prefer one side except this.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: The attribute of evil and good applies to deeds and also to objects. The believer is good in his essence and his deeds, and the disbeliever is evil and impure in his essence and his deeds. But his impurity in essence is not a physical impurity like the impurity of the mule and the donkey, but a moral impurity.

* Among the benefits of this verse: A person may be impressed by what is not worthy of admiration, based on His saying: ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: The obligation of fearing Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that among the fear of Allah is that a person should not be impressed by the evil even if it is abundant, because He mentioned the command to fear Allah after His saying: ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Those who are addressed with fear of Allah and with such great rulings are people of understanding, based on His saying: ﴿O people of understanding﴾, and what is meant by intellects here is the intellect of right guidance, not the intellect of perception.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Fear of Allah is the cause of prosperity, based on His saying: ﴿so that you may prosper﴾, and the meaning of prosperity has already been mentioned.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾, and so on to the end.

The address ﴿O you who believe﴾ has been discussed many times before, so there is no need to repeat it.

﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾. The word (ashya') here is diptotic (mamnu' min al-sarf, not inflected with nunation). The morphologists (al-sarfiyyun, specialists in morphology) gave as the reason for this that the hamza in it is a feminine marker and not a root letter (...). However, there is a morphological alteration (i'lal, a change in the form of a word's letters) through transposition of its letters, in that the middle hamza was moved to the beginning, so it became (ashya'). Accordingly, if you want to weigh it, its measure is (fa'la'). 

﴿about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾ means: if the answer about them were made known to you, the answer would distress you. This covers everything the Law has remained silent about. Asking about such things then becomes a cause of hardship for people and of their being troubled by what occurs. Among examples of this is that some of the Muslims used to ask the Prophet (ﷺ). A man would ask: "Who is my father?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (92), and Muslim (2360 / 138), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] and "Where is my father?"[[Recorded by Muslim (203 / 247), from the hadith of Anas.]] and similar questions. Such matters are among those about which silence must be kept. If a man said to the Messenger (ﷺ): "Who is my father?" and he replied: "Your father is so-and-so," other than his real father, this would be a disgrace to him, to his father and to his mother. Therefore, remaining silent about it is good manners. Likewise, if he asks: "Where is my father?" and the Messenger (ﷺ) says: "Your father is in the Fire," this would undoubtedly distress him, and it would also be a distress to whom? To the father.

Likewise regarding obligatory matters: when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has prescribed for you the Hajj," al-Aqra' ibn Habis said: "Is it every year?"[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (1721), al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (2620), and Ibn Majah (2886), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] This is an inappropriate question, because if the Prophet (ﷺ) had said "Yes," it would have become obligatory, and that would have been hard on the Muslims, both individuals and groups. For individuals, because if it were imposed on a person to perform Hajj every year, it would be a hardship on him. For groups: if the Muslim nation were told: "Whoever among you is able to perform Hajj, let him perform it every year," what land would contain them? The land would not contain them. Therefore the question was out of place. How great is the sin of one who asks about something that has not been made unlawful, so that it becomes unlawful because of his question, or about something that has not been made obligatory, so that it becomes obligatory because of his question.

He said: ﴿if they were made known to you﴾, meaning: if their answer became apparent to you, ﴿would distress you﴾. ﴿And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you﴾, meaning: if you ask about them during the time of revelation, when the Qur'an is being sent down, they will be made known to you. Who makes them known? Allah makes them known through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ) to whom the question is addressed.

﴿Allah has pardoned that﴾, meaning Allah has pardoned what He has remained silent about. For this reason a hadith says: "And what He has kept silent about, that is a pardon."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (1726), and Ibn Majah (3367), from the hadith of Salman al-Farisi.]]

﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾: Forgiving of sins, Forbearing in punishment, so He does not hasten to punish His servants, as He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they earn, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature; but He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing﴾ [Fatir 45].

* There are benefits in this verse. First: it is among the things that contradict the completeness of faith for a person to ask about something he has not been obligated to. This is based on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask﴾.

Does this include the time of revelation and what comes after it, or is it specific to the time of revelation, when a ruling of prohibition or obligation could be established through it?

The second point: during the time of revelation. As for after revelation, a person must ask about his religion. Therefore we say: what some laypeople do, when they are told "This is prohibited" or "This is obligatory," and they are told "Ask the scholars," and they say: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾, this is prohibited, prohibited for two reasons. The first: he refrained from asking although the reason for asking exists. The second: he applied the verse in other than its intended application, not as Allah intended.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may be distressed by what Allah, mighty and majestic, has legislated, whether an obligation or a prohibition. But the believer, although he may dislike it by his nature, does not dislike it insofar as it is the Law of Allah, mighty and majestic. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, while it is hateful to you﴾ [al-Baqarah 216]. What is hateful? Is it fighting or its being obligatory? Fighting, not its obligation. The believer is content with everything Allah has made obligatory, everything He has commanded and everything He has forbidden and prohibited, but he may dislike it because of its hardship, its toil, and similar things.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: any question that arises during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) must be answered, based on His saying: ﴿And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you﴾. For this reason you find in the Noble Qur'an many questions addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ), which Allah answers: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: "The surplus."﴾ [al-Baqarah 219]; ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: "In them is great sin."﴾ [al-Baqarah 219]; ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: "Improving their affairs is good."﴾ [al-Baqarah 220]. So it must be answered, based on His saying: ﴿if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you﴾.

But if someone says: Does the Prophet (ﷺ) not sometimes get asked and not answer? We say: Yes, but he does not answer because no revelation about it has come down to him. If revelation had come down to him about it, he would have answered.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whatever Allah has remained silent about is pardoned, based on His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned that, and Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾.

We give an example of this: many women ask about the ruling on removing hair from the legs or the arms. Is it prohibited or permitted?

Let us consider: hair is divided into three categories. One category is that whose removal is forbidden; one category is that whose removal is commanded; and one category is that about which silence is kept. Among what is commanded to be removed is what is mentioned in the fitra (natural practices). Among what is forbidden to be removed is the beard. Among what is left silent is the rest of the hair. So do we say it is among what is left silent, and therefore permissible, or do we say: the basic principle regarding altering the creation of Allah is that it is prohibited, and therefore it is prohibited?

The answer: the first. It is among what is left silent, and had Allah, mighty and majestic, willed, He would have revealed a Qur'an about it, or the Prophet (ﷺ) would have spoken about it.

Insects and the like fall into three categories: one category is commanded to be killed, one category is forbidden to be killed, and one category is left silent. Among what is commanded to be killed, what is it?

* Student: The dog and the scorpion.

* The Shaykh: The scorpion, the snake, and the rabid dog. Among what is forbidden to be killed are the ant, the bee, the hoopoe, and the owl. The rest is left silent. So do we say that the rest may be killed without harm, or do we say no? The basic principle is that it is a creature Allah created to be a sign of His power, the breadth of His knowledge and His mercy, and because it glorifies Allah, so it is not killed unless it causes harm.

On this there are three opinions. Two are well known to me until now, which I have not forgotten; the third I have forgotten. The first: it is disliked to kill these insects when they do no harm. If they cause harm, they may be killed, but killing them is disliked, because they glorify Allah, and because in them is one of the signs of Allah, namely that whenever a person reflects on them he recognises the breadth of Allah's knowledge, provision and mercy. So there is benefit for the servants in them, and they should not be killed, but this is on the basis of disliking it.

The second opinion: that it is permissible, because it is among what Allah and His Messenger have remained silent about, and what Allah has remained silent about is pardoned.

The third: that it is prohibited. But I have not favoured it, because if they do no harm, killing them is mere pointless act, and it also trains the soul in aggression. This applies if they do not harm. But if they do harm, there is no doubt that killing them is permissible. Still, it is better to repel them with what is easier. For example, if a snake enters its hole, and it is among what is commanded to be killed, and killing it becomes either by drowning it in water or burning it with fire, which is preferable? Water, the first, with water. As for these insects that were neither commanded nor forbidden to be killed, we say: if there is some kind of harm from them, then if it is possible to drive them away so you are safe from the harm without killing, that is better; and if it is not possible except by killing, then kill them and there is no blame on you.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an was sent down by whom?

* Students: By Allah.

* The Shaykh: ﴿the Qur'an is being revealed﴾. The agent is not mentioned but is omitted because it is known, since the one who sends down the Qur'an is Allah, mighty and majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is a conveyor of the message from Allah, based on His saying: ﴿they will be made known to you﴾, because the one who makes them directly manifest to mankind is the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: reliance on the original principle of the innocence of the obligation (bara'at al-dhimma), derived from His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned that﴾. The basic principle is that the obligation is not burdened by an obligation or a prohibition.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, mighty and majestic: the Forgiving (al-Ghafur) and the Forbearing (al-Halim). He is Forgiving of sins and Forbearing at the time of punishment, so He does not hasten. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

He is the Forbearing, so He does not hasten
His servant with punishment, that he may repent from disobedience.

[Student:] May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Some insects are by nature harmful, but no harm has appeared from them. Should one kill them?

[Shaykh:] Like what?

[Student:] A snake, for example. Its nature is harmful, and so is the scorpion. Does merely seeing it mean...?

[Shaykh:] Yes, due to the general command to kill them. Then, if no harm comes from it, and this is the case with the snake: a snake is sometimes tested and never bites at all. I myself saw with my own eyes one crawl over the leg of a woman who had stretched out her legs, and it did not harm her. As for the scorpion, woe to whoever it touches. It gives no chance at all. We have never heard of a scorpion that does not sting, except perhaps the scorpions of Africa, we do not know.

[Student:] Here and there are the same.

[Shaykh:] Yes, its nature is to sting immediately and not give a respite.

[Student:] Shaykh, what is your view on some people who use this verse as a proverb? A teacher, for example, asks in a subject: "Is this with us?" And he says: ﴿O you who have believed...﴾.

[Shaykh:] It is not permissible, because the question that was asked does not fit the meaning of the verse.

[Student:] May Allah bless you. Is everything that negates the perfection of faith forbidden?

[Shaykh:] Yes. Indeed, Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, says: Everything from which faith is negated for its doer is among the major sins.

[Student:] Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, there is a device for killing insects with electricity (...)?

[Shaykh:] Perhaps you mean this, yes, and the question?

[Student:] Is it permissible to use it to kill insects?

[Shaykh:] Yes, it is permissible, because it does not burn by electric shock. Moreover, if this harmful creature cannot be eliminated except by burning, there is no harm, just as "the Prophet ﷺ burned the palm trees of Banu an-Nadir",[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2326) and Muslim (1746/29), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] although palm trees usually contain nestlings of birds and others.

[Student:] Shaykh, may Allah bless you, is it considered harmful that the spider builds a house on walls and in mosques? Is this its nature?

[Shaykh:] By Allah, no. In reality it varies. Some spiders build houses and bring things that are visually harmful, which they hang up. These are harmful without doubt. Likewise, in the library, they may nest on books, and this is harmful. But the strange thing is that people say: it is not permissible to kill a spider at all, even if it nests on your head. Why?

[Students:] (...).

[Shaykh:] They say: because it nested on the Prophet ﷺ in the cave. This is not correct. The spider's web over the Prophet ﷺ in the cave is absolutely not authentic, and what prevented the disbelievers from seeing him was only the protection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Hence Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, if one of them were to look at his feet, he would see us."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3653) and Muslim (2381/1), from Abu Bakr.]] Some scholars cited a hadith, but it is weak: "He commanded the killing of spiders."[[Abu Dawud narrated it in al-Marasil (499) with the wording: "The spider is a devil, so kill it," from the hadith of Yazid ibn Murthad al-Mad'i.]] We say: there is no command and no prohibition. It is among the creatures for which leaving them is better. But if harm comes from it, even a little, there is no harm in killing it.

[Student:] And the original state of it is that it builds its known house (...). So must a person kill it as soon as he sees it?

[Shaykh:] But if we assume that, for example, there is a degree in the first construction, of wood and palm fronds, and it built between the wood and the fronds, this does not affect anything. But in a building of reinforced concrete now, there is no doubt that it disfigures the appearance. It brings, by the grace of Allah, from what stores food, it brings things.

[Student:] It has benefits, the spider.

[Shaykh:] Benefits? What are they?

[Student:] It kills ants, Shaykh.

[Shaykh:] Ants.

[Student:] Small ants.

[Shaykh:] This must be established. Bring us a spider and an ant tomorrow, God willing, and we will see. No, in reality it kills flies. You find it lying in wait for them and holding itself still, until when one comes near it leaps. Glory be to Allah, who gave everything its creation and then guided it.

[Student:] May Allah pardon you, Shaykh. The one called the snake, Shaykh, the name "snake" is a type of creeping creature, but large. Among them is the swift creature which (...). This (...).

[Shaykh:] Which what? (...).

[Student:] And this snake is slow in its walking.

[Shaykh:] You are right. This one I saw crawled over the leg or foot of the woman like this, somewhat long.

[Student:] Yes. As for the snake that comes short (...), this one, Shaykh, does not leave anyone alone.

[Shaykh:] Yes, this is so. That is why "the Prophet ﷺ forbade killing the jinn that are found in houses, except the abtar and the dhu at-tufyatayn",[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3310) and Muslim (2233/136), from Abu Lubaba.]] the abtar: as you described, it is short and thick, and its tail is also short. This one is severe.

[Student:] Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. Sometimes questions occur to a person, that is, questions come to a person's mind. If he asks about them, they may be strange questions, or they may be classed as innovated questions or something. If he keeps silent about these questions, he would be opposing the command of Allah Most High: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance﴾ [an-Nahl 43].

[Shaykh:] If it is something a person must believe or do, he must ask.

[Student:] Even if it is strange, Shaykh?

[Shaykh:] Even if it is strange. But if it is of excessive literalism and over-burdening oneself, like the one who said: how did He settle on the Throne, for example, this is not to be asked (...).

* * *
[Student:] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿They had already asked it of people before you, then they became disbelievers therein. Allah did not ordain any bahirah, saibah, wasilah, or ham; but those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason. And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 102–104].

[Shaykh:] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. When Allah, glorified and exalted, forbade this nation to ask about things on which He had remained silent, and stated that if they asked about them, they must be made clear to them at the time the Qur'an was revealed, so that Muslims would not remain in confusion about their religion, and so that there would be no deficiency in the religion.

Mighty and Majestic, He explained that such questions had already been asked by a people before this nation, but they did not fulfill what they were obligated to. A clear example of this is the story of the cow, when a slain person was found and they disputed about who had killed him, and their prophet Musa ﷺ commanded them to slaughter a cow. They thought he was mocking them, and ﴿they said: "Do you take us for a laughingstock?" He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant."﴾ [al-Baqarah 67]. "Among the ignorant" means: among the transgressors, not from ignorance which is the opposite of knowledge, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said about man: ﴿Indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab 72], meaning: I will not transgress and so mock you. ﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is." He said: "Indeed He says it is a cow neither old, ﴾ meaning: advanced in age, ﴿nor virgin﴾ young, ﴿but between that, so do what you are commanded"﴾ [al-Baqarah 68]. Is this question of theirs necessary? No, it is not necessary. Slaughter a cow, and they would slaughter it; any cow that exists and the command is fulfilled, because the cow is known by its kind. As for it being known by its color, or known by its age, or known by its action, this is not required.

They moved on to another question: ﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what its color is."﴾ [al-Baqarah 69]. Glory be to Allah! Were they required to have a specific color? No. ﴿He said: "Indeed He says it is a yellow cow, bright in its color, pleasing to the beholders"﴾, meaning there is nothing in it but yellow, ﴿pleasing to the beholders﴾ in its size, its flesh, its fatness, and its build. Did they stop at this? No. ﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, cows look alike to us"﴾ [al-Baqarah 70]. But they are cows! ﴿Indeed, cows look alike to us, and we, if Allah wills, will be guided.﴾ Would cows look alike after these first and second descriptions? They do not look alike. Yet they said: ﴿if Allah wills, we will be guided﴾. So they did not affirm guidance with certainty. I do not think, and Allah knows best, that they mentioned that for blessing. ﴿He said: "Indeed He says it is a cow neither broken to plow the earth nor irrigating the tilth, sound, with no blemish in it"﴾ [al-Baqarah 71]: four descriptions, with which He made it strict upon them. ﴿They said: "Now you have brought the truth."﴾ Now? And before? Had they not brought the truth? ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they nearly did not do it.﴾ That is, they slaughtered it after much back and forth and nearly did not do it. But they saw that they had to do it. This is from excessive questioning. Had they slaughtered a cow from the very beginning, the matter would have ended and there would have been no difficulty.
