Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 6]. The questioning of those to whom they were sent is that it will be said to them: "What response did you give to the messengers?" And the questioning of the messengers is that it will be said: "What response did you receive?" Is this questioning for the purpose of seeking information?

The answer: No, because nothing is hidden from Allah in the earth or in the heavens.

Is it for rebuke? That is, rebuking those to whom they were sent, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried girl is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾ [at-Takwīr 8–9]? The buried girl had no sin, and she is asked for what sin she was killed, as a rebuke to whom? As a rebuke to her killers. So ﴿فَيَقُولُ مَاذَا أُجِبْتُمْ﴾ is intended as a rebuke to those to whom they were sent. This is without doubt the correct view. As for seeking information, it is not applicable.

As for their saying ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا﴾ (we have no knowledge): there is no doubt that a person finds this negation problematic, as it is an absolute, general negation, since it uses the negation of the genus. How can the messengers have no knowledge?

The answer to this is from several aspects:

Either it may be said: we have no knowledge of what happened after us, like the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning those who come to the Basin, when they are brought forward and then driven away from it, and he says: "My companions!" It will be said: "You do not know what they innovated after you." [Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhārī (4625) and Muslim (2860/58) from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās.] So ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا﴾ means: concerning what? Concerning what happened after us. This is true: they have no knowledge. This is one aspect.

Another aspect: ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا﴾ concerning what is in the inner thoughts of those who responded, because among those who responded to the messengers were hypocrites, and the messengers do not know what is in their hearts. This is also a strong view, for the messengers, peace be upon them, do not know what is in the hearts of those who display following. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have known them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muḥammad 30]. And knowledge by the tone of speech is based on an indication, not on something perceptible and certain. This is one aspect.

The third aspect: ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا﴾ (we have no knowledge except what You taught us), and You know what response we were given, because You are the Knower of the unseen. This has some validity, but it is not that strong. The best thing to say is: we have no knowledge of what happened after us, or we have no knowledge of what lies in the inner aspects of matters.

There is a fourth possibility: that they said "we have no knowledge" out of courtesy toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic, as a student says to his teacher, "I have no knowledge," out of courtesy to him, even though he has knowledge. It seems that Ibn Jarīr, may Allah have mercy on him, inclines to this view: that the meaning of their saying "we have no knowledge" is out of courtesy toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic, because they know that Allah did not ask them to seek information, since He is All-Knowing.

As for His saying ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾: here, ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ (You) — do we say it is an emphasis for the ﴿كَ﴾ in ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾? Or do we say it is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) that has no place in parsing? Or do we say it is a subject whose predicate is ﴿عَلَّامُ﴾?

All of this is possible, and the grammatical possibilities are numerous. For this reason they say: "The arguments of the grammarians are the nāqiʾāʾ of the jerboas."

Do you know the jerboas? And do you know the nāqiʾāʾ?

The nāqiʾāʾ is the burrow-exit of the jerboa. The jerboa is clever: it digs a burrow in the ground and proceeds in it, then digs at its end upward, until only a thin crust remains, which it leaves. If someone blocks the entrance, the nāqiʾāʾ makes it easy to exit, so it leaves through the nāqiʾāʾ. They say: whenever you block the grammarians from one side and say, "This is not valid," they bring another aspect, even if the possibility is remote. For this reason a strong grammarian is never defeated in grammar. He cannot be defeated; whenever you present an argument against him, he brings you what justifies his statement. So we say: the word ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ is either a separating pronoun, or an emphasis for the ﴿كَ﴾, or a subject.

As for His saying ﴿عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾: this is an attribution and an intensification in fact. That is, He, glorified and exalted, is the Knower of the unseen, meaning He possesses far-reaching knowledge of the unseen. ﴿الْغُيُوبِ﴾ is the plural of (ghayb), which is what is hidden from creation. So Allah, majestic and exalted, is the Knower of the unseen. Nothing unseen in the heavens and the earth is hidden, except that it is in a clear Book. He knows even what has not existed, how it would be if it existed. He does not only know what exists, but what is hidden from the creatures; indeed, He knows what has not been, how it would have been, the Mighty and Majestic.

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: a person must remember this great day, to consider what response the messengers were given. On the Day of Resurrection the messengers will be gathered and questioned.

* Among them: the perfection of the power of Allah, blessed and exalted, by His gathering the messengers in that great station, where human beings, wild beasts, predators, camels and others are mixed together. Allah gathers the messengers, glorified and exalted, by His power and permission.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of the messengers, peace be upon them, since Allah, glorified and exalted, cares for them to this degree, so much so that He questions them on the Day of Resurrection in this great scene: what response were they given? As an honor to them and a display of their conveyance of the message.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾ (then He says). The affirmation of speech for Allah has filled the Qur'an and filled the Sunnah, and the affirmation of speech for Allah has become one of the definite, certain matters: that Allah, glorified and exalted, speaks.

* Among its benefits: that He speaks with a letter and a sound. The evidence: what is spoken is His saying ﴿مَاذَا أُجِبْتُمْ﴾, and these are letters. The indication of sound: He addresses the messengers, so the address must be audible to them, otherwise it would have no benefit. This is what we have established in affirming that Allah speaks, and that He speaks with a letter and a sound is what the people of the Sunnah, their imams and their followers have agreed upon. Whoever says otherwise is an innovator and astray. Whoever says that Allah is not described as speaking, and that what is attributed to Him of speech is an expression of created sounds which Allah created to express what is in His self, this view is among the most invalid views. Shaykh al-Islām, may Allah have mercy on him, refuted it in a treatise called al-Tisʿīniyya, "of ninety aspects," may Allah have mercy on him, and it deserves refutation, because it is self-contradictory and corrupt. What is troubling is that many people today hold this view, because it is the prevailing doctrine of the Ashʿarites among much of the Muslim nation, although it is false, and no one with a sound natural disposition (fiṭra) could accept it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the courtesy of the messengers, peace be upon them, toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic, in that they said ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا﴾ (we have no knowledge). This is one aspect.

The second aspect: they recognized their own worth, and that they do not know the unseen.

The third aspect: they knew that the nations after them, they have no knowledge of them, according to the possibilities we mentioned concerning the aspect of His saying ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of knowledge of the unseen for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, by the saying of the messengers, peace be upon them: ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾ (indeed You, You are the Knower of the unseen), meaning: not You other than Him. Whoever claims knowledge of the unseen is a disbeliever, because he contradicts the noble Qur'an and what the Muslims have agreed upon. Whoever says that something will happen on such and such a day, such and such, is a liar, and a disbeliever. Soothsayers report about the unseen future, but they have certain people among the jinn who listen to the revelation, steal it, and convey it to the soothsayer, and the soothsayer adds many lies to it, and believes it because of a single word. This does not contradict the statement that Allah alone is the Knower of the unseen, because Allah the Exalted said concerning those who eavesdrop: ﴿except one who snatches a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾ [al-Ḥijr 18]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made an exception, saying: ﴿except one who snatches a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 110 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When Allah said: O Jesus, son of Mary﴾. We say concerning ﴿When Allah said: O Jesus﴾ what we said concerning ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the Messengers﴾: that ﴿idh (when)﴾ is an object of a verb omitted, whose estimate is: "Remember" (udhkur).

His saying: ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary﴾ is a vocative and a description, or an appositive (ʿatf bayān). ﴿Jesus (ʿĪsā)﴾ is a vocative built on damm (ḍamm), because it is a proper name (ʿalam), and every proper name in the vocative that is not idafa (annexed) is built on damm in a position of naṣb (accusative). So you say: yā Zaydu, and you do not say: yā Zaydan. Every proper name that is not annexed is built on damm. As for ﴿son of Mary (ibn Maryam)﴾, it is a description or an appositive and is in the accusative because it is annexed. ﴿Maryam (Mary)﴾ is the name of his mother, and he is attributed to her because he had no father, for he was created from a mother without a father.

﴿Remember My favour upon you﴾: this is the content of the saying: ﴿Remember My favour upon you and upon your mother﴾. Then He explained that, saying: ﴿when I supported you with the Holy Spirit﴾. This ﴿idh (when)﴾ is connected to the word "favour" (niʿma), and niʿma is the object of ﴿remember (udhkur)﴾. ﴿idh (when)﴾, meaning this is connected to "favour": ﴿when I supported you with the Holy Spirit (ayyadtuka bi-rūḥ al-qudus)﴾. ﴿ayyadtuka (I supported you)﴾, meaning a concealed subject; meaning (I), its estimate is (I). The subject, if its estimate is (I), or (we), or (you), is obligatorily concealed; and if its estimate is (he) or (she), it is concealed permissibly, except in some cases such as the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub), where the estimated subject is (he), yet it is obligatorily concealed.

His saying: ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾ is connected to ﴿ayyada (supported)﴾.

﴿You speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾: this is an explanation of the favour, so the sentence is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).

His saying: ﴿tukallimu (you speak)﴾: the subject is concealed, its estimate is "you", and ﴿al-nās (the people)﴾ is the object.

﴿in the cradle (fī al-mahd)﴾, meaning: while you are in the cradle, and ﴿kahlan (in maturity)﴾, meaning: and while you are mature.

﴿And when I taught you (wa-idh ʿallamtuka)﴾, meaning: and remember My favour upon you also, ﴿when I taught you the Book (idh ʿallamtuka al-kitāb)﴾. So the waw is a conjunction particle, and ﴿idh (when)﴾ is conjoined to the first ﴿idh (when)﴾.

His saying: ﴿ʿallamtuka al-kitāb (I taught you the Book)﴾: this ʿallama (taught) takes two objects: the first object is the kāf (you), and the second is al-kitāb (the Book). ﴿al-ḥikmah (wisdom)﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿al-Tawrāh and al-Injīl (the Torah and the Gospel)﴾ are conjoined. ﴿And when you create (wa-idh takhluqu)﴾ is conjoined to ﴿idh ayyadtuka (when I supported you)﴾, so it is from Allah's favour upon him, and it is therefore in the accusative position.

﴿takhluqu (you create)﴾, meaning: you ﴿from clay (min al-ṭīn) like the form of a bird (ka-hayʾat al-ṭayr)﴾. The kāf is a noun meaning "like", meaning: like the form of a bird. It is annexed, though it is a particle, to hayʾa, and hayʾa is annexed to ﴿al-ṭayr (the bird)﴾. ﴿bi-idhnī (by My permission)﴾ is connected to ﴿takhluqu (you create)﴾. ﴿fa-tanfukhu (then you breathe)﴾ is conjoined to ﴿takhluqu (you create)﴾.

﴿fīhā (into it)﴾, meaning: into this created thing that you made. ﴿ṭayran (a bird)﴾ is the predicate of ﴿takūnu (it becomes)﴾. Is its subject concealed obligatorily or permissibly, so that it is "she"?
* Students: Permissibly.
* The Shaykh: Permissibly. ﴿bi-idhnī (by My permission)﴾ is connected to takūnu. ﴿tubriʾu (you heal)﴾ is conjoined to ﴿takhluqu (you create)﴾; meaning: and when you heal the blind and the leper.

﴿tubriʾu (you heal)﴾ is an imperfect verb, and its subject is obligatorily concealed, its estimate is "you". ﴿al-akmah wa-al-abraṣ (the born blind and the leper)﴾ is the object and conjoined to it. ﴿bi-idhnī (by My permission)﴾ is connected to ﴿tubriʾu (you heal)﴾.

﴿And when you bring forth the dead by My permission (wa-idh tukhriju al-mawtā bi-idhnī)﴾: we say concerning its grammatical analysis what we said concerning the grammatical analysis of ﴿tubriʾu al-akmah (you heal the blind)﴾.

﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you (wa-idh kafaftu)﴾ is conjoined to the first ﴿idh (when)﴾, ﴿idh ayyadtuka (when I supported you)﴾; meaning: and remember My favour upon you when I restrained the Children of Israel from you.

﴿Banī Isrāʾīl (the Children of Israel)﴾ is the object of ﴿kafaftu (I restrained)﴾.
﴿ʿankа (from you)﴾ is connected to ﴿kafaftu (I restrained)﴾.
﴿idh jiʾtahum bi-al-bayyināt (when you came to them with clear signs)﴾ is also connected to ﴿kafaftu (I restrained)﴾.
﴿bi-al-bayyināt (with clear signs)﴾ is an adjective of an omitted noun, and the estimate is: "with the clear signs".

﴿Then those of them who disbelieved said: "This is nothing but evident magic (in hadha illā siḥrun mubīn)"﴾, meaning: those among the Children of Israel.

His saying: ﴿in hadhā illā siḥrun mubīn (this is nothing but evident magic)﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying in "said (qāla)". ﴿in (in)﴾ is a negation particle, ﴿hādhā (this)﴾ is the subject, ﴿illā (except)﴾ is a particle of restriction, ﴿siḥrun (magic)﴾ is the predicate of the subject, and ﴿mubīn (evident)﴾ is its adjective.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, reminding Jesus, peace be upon him, of these favours: ﴿When Allah said: O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you﴾. Jesus is the son of Mary, and he is from the Children of Israel, and from the offspring of whom? From the offspring of Abraham, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And among his offspring: David and Solomon﴾, to the end [al-Anʿām 6:84].

His saying: ﴿remember My favour upon you﴾ is the object of "said (qāla)". The meaning: remember the favour with which I bestowed you and your mother. As for His favour upon him, He mentioned it and enumerated what He enumerated. As for His favour upon the mother, He prepared for her, and facilitated for her the place where she would deliver her burden, and placed beside her fresh dates and a stream, according to one opinion regarding the meaning of ﴿sariyyan (a stream)﴾ [Maryam 19:24]. Among His favours upon his mother also is that He made Jesus speak in the cradle to clear his mother's innocence of what the Jews had accused her of, who said to her: ﴿O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother a woman unchaste﴾ [Maryam 19:28], meaning: and how did you come to this state?

His saying: ﴿idh ayyadtuka (when I supported you)﴾: meaning, I strengthened you. The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him, who supports him in everything in which he needs support. ﴿You speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾: this is among Allah's favours upon him, that he spoke to the people while in the cradle, that is, a small child carried in the arms, and it is customary that such a one does not speak.

﴿And in maturity (kahlan)﴾, meaning: an adult. As for kahl, it was said: between thirty and fifty; and it was said: between thirty and forty. Allah mentioned his speaking in the cradle, and his speaking in maturity, to make clear that his speech when in the cradle was like his speech when he was mature, without difference. It is well known that a small child does not speak, and that if he spoke his speech would not be like that of an adult, neither in its expression, nor its arrangement, nor its meaning. But the speech of Jesus while in the cradle was like his speech when he was mature.

Therefore, if someone said: What is the benefit of His saying "and in maturity", since a person's speech in maturity is a known matter?
We say: to make clear that his speech when he was mature was like his speech when he was in the cradle.

His saying: ﴿And when I taught you (wa-idh ʿallamtuka)﴾, meaning: remember when I taught you the Book and the wisdom. As for "the Book", it was said: it is writing, because the intended meaning is not the revealed Book, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and the Torah and the Gospel﴾. So "the Book" would mean what? Writing.

﴿And the wisdom (al-ḥikmah)﴾ is knowledge, understanding, and sound reason, by which things are placed in their proper positions; since he was one of the noble messengers, wisdom is therefore knowledge, understanding and right guidance, that is, placing things in their proper places.

﴿And the Torah and the Gospel﴾: the Torah is the Book that Allah sent down to Moses, and the Gospel is the Book that Allah sent down to Jesus. It is a branch of the Torah, because the origin is the Torah; but the Gospel came with some matters that were not in the Torah, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:50].

﴿And when you create (wa-idh takhluqu)﴾ is also among Allah's favours upon him: ﴿when you create from clay﴾, meaning: you make from clay something in the form of a bird.

﴿Then you breathe into it (fa-tanfukhu fīhā)﴾, meaning: into what you made of that form. ﴿Then it becomes a bird (fa-takūnu ṭayran)﴾. In another reading: ﴿ṭāʾiran bi-idhnī (a bird by My permission)﴾, meaning he creates the shape of a bird. Let us say the shape of a dove; he breathes into it a single breath and it becomes a bird, that is, a living bird. The second reading: ﴿ṭāʾiran (flying)﴾, meaning that it actually flies. No one can do this except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or one whom He permits to do so.

﴿And you heal the blind (wa-tubriʾu al-akmah)﴾: ﴿tubriʾu (you heal)﴾, meaning: you cure ﴿al-akmah (the blind)﴾ of his illness. The best of what has been said about the akmah is that he is one born without sight, either because the eyelids never opened, and this has occurred; meaning that a child has been born in our time who is akmah, with eyelids closed and never opened; or the meaning is the one with weak sight who sees by night and does not see by day, or the reverse. But the first meaning is more eloquent in the verse, that he was created without sight, and he cures him by Allah's permission, Mighty and Majestic. As for the leper, it is well known.

His saying: ﴿bi-idhnī (by My permission)﴾: He repeated it to make clear that this great sign was not except by Allah's permission. In Āl ʿImrān the permission is repeated twice, but in what is in Āl ʿImrān, who said it? Did Allah address Jesus, or did Jesus address his people? Jesus addressed his people, so the two differ.

His saying: ﴿And when you bring forth the dead by My permission (wa-idh tukhriju al-mawtā bi-idhnī)﴾: ﴿idh tukhriju al-mawtā (when you bring forth the dead)﴾, meaning: from their graves; he would stand over the grave and say: "O so-and-so, come out!" and he would come out by Allah's permission, Mighty and Majestic.

In the verse of Āl ʿImrān he says: ﴿I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:49]. So when you combine this with that, it becomes that Jesus, peace be upon him, brings the dead to life before they are buried, and brings them to life after they are buried; you bring forth the dead by Allah's permission.

The final favour: ﴿when I restrained the Children of Israel from you﴾. ﴿idh kafaftu (when I restrained)﴾, meaning: I kept them away from you, because they intended to kill him. The story of the crucifixion is well known: they gathered to kill him, then some of them volunteered for that, and Allah cast the likeness upon one of them, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised. This one upon whom the likeness was cast cried out: "I am not Jesus!" but they disbelieved him, saying: "You are Jesus," so they killed him and crucified him. The Children of Israel claimed that they had killed Jesus and crucified him, but Allah refuted them, so He, Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not kill him with certainty﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 4:157]; rather, he is alive and remaining, and he will descend at the end of time.

His saying: ﴿when you came to them with clear signs (idh jiʾtahum bi-al-bayyināt)﴾, meaning: when you came to them with clear signs, they intended to kill you after the matter had become apparent and clear, and you brought clear signs. ﴿Then those of them who disbelieved said: "This is nothing but evident magic"﴾, meaning: they said that Jesus had bewitched us: how does he heal the blind? How does he create something from clay in the form of a bird and breathe into it so that it becomes a flying bird?

"This is nothing but magic," and they denied him. So it is with those who deny the messengers: they all say that the messengers are sorcerers, because the messengers bring signs that human beings cannot produce; so they deceive the common people and say: "They have bewitched you." Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them but they said: "A sorcerer or a madman"﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt 51:52]. This verse is general: all the messengers were told this, "a sorcerer or a madman."

His saying: ﴿in hadhā illā siḥrun mubīn (this is nothing but evident magic)﴾, meaning: clear, manifest. For "abāna" is used both transitively and intransitively; it is said "abāna al-fajr" meaning it rose, and "abāna al-amr" meaning he made it clear. It depends on the context: sometimes it has the meaning of "abāna" (to make clear), and sometimes the meaning of "bāna" (to be evident). Here it is derived from "bāna", that is: this is evident, manifest magic.

There are benefits in the verse that will come, God willing, in the next lesson, since the questions have their time for resolution.

* Student: What is the grammatical analysis of ﴿innaka anta (indeed You, You)﴾? If we say: ﴿anta (You)﴾ is the subject and ﴿ʿallām (Knower of the unseen)﴾ is the predicate, does it convey the meaning that ﴿anta (You)﴾ conveys when it is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl), or emphasis?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it may convey it; because when the two parts of the sentence are both definite, it conveys restriction (ḥaṣr), but the separating pronoun is stronger in restriction.
* Student: Why is the cross sacred to the Christians?
* The Shaykh: Yes. They say that Jesus, peace be upon him, according to their claim, agreed to redeem the world with his own self, so he accepted death and crucifixion; for that reason we venerate it. In reality, if they were rational they would break the cross, because their prophet, according to their claim, was crucified upon it; so the sight of the cross should have been the most hateful to them. But, as you know, the Christians are astray, and they have no minds.
* Student: Allah said: ﴿Revive the dead﴾, so when Jesus revives, does he live after that?
* The Shaykh: As for me, I was not present. Is the answer sound or unsound?! I ask you, because this question is out of place. The purpose is to show that he revives the dead. As for whether he remains alive or not, this inquiry is not sound, and asking about it is not good. I always tell you: in matters of the unseen, confine yourselves to what has been reported, and the important thing is that he is brought to life after death, not that he dies after living.
* Student: Regarding His saying ﴿by My permission﴾: we said that in Āl ʿImrān it is repeated more than in this verse, because the context there was Jesus addressing his people, while here Allah, Glorified, addresses Jesus, peace be upon him. Shaykh, the thought that comes to mind is that Jesus, when addressing his people, should have repeated this more, lest they exaggerate about him?
* The Shaykh: No, this is in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān. He attributed it to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to make clear that the true God is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; this is the important point. As for here, it is so that no one is deceived by his bringing the dead to life, so He said: ﴿by My permission﴾. It will come to us, God willing, in the benefits, so that Jesus, peace be upon him, knows that he acts only by Allah's permission, Mighty and Majestic.
* Student: May Allah reward you well. When Jesus descends at the end of time, will he descend with other miracles, or will these miracles be with him?
* The Shaykh: Apparently he will not bring these miracles, because it will come to us, God willing, that Allah gave him these signs; for medicine in his time had advanced to a far point, so Allah gave him signs that physicians cannot match.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples: "Believe in Me and My Messenger." They said: "We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims" (111). When the disciples said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" He said: "Fear Allah, if you are believers" (112). They said: "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know you have told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses" (113). Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers" (114). Allah said: "I am sending it down to you; but whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds"﴾ [al-Māʾidah 5:111–115].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples: "Believe in Me and My Messenger." They said: "We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾. Before we speak on the lesson of this day, we will speak on the benefits of the previous lesson, as you claimed.

Among the benefits of Allah's saying ﴿When Allah said: O Jesus﴾ to its end:
* Among its benefits: reminding this nation of what happened to the earlier nations with their prophets and those sent to them; because ﴿When Allah said﴾ is connected to an omitted word, and the estimate is: what? "Remember when Allah said."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 5, verse 110 (part 2 of 3):

* Among its benefits: affirmation that Allah, exalted is He, speaks and says with letters and sound; for the thing said is ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary﴾ to the end, and these are letters. Speech is only directed to one who hears it. Had the speech of Allah not been subsisting in Himself, it would not be correct to say ﴿When Allah said, "O Jesus"﴾. In this there is a refutation of the Ash'aris, who said: the speech of Allah and the words of Allah are the meaning subsisting in the self, not what is heard; what is heard are sounds that Allah, mighty and majestic, creates to express what is in His self. This view is false from many aspects. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him and reward him on behalf of this ummah with good, wrote a treatise called (al-Tis'iniyya) which refutes this view from ninety aspects. It is worthy of being refuted and discarded, because it is self-contradictory. What is strange is that they and the Mu'tazila agreed that what is in the mushaf is created. But the Mu'tazila said: it is the speech of Allah, while these said: it is an expression of the speech of Allah. So the Mu'tazila and the Jahmiyya were, in this respect, happier with the truth than they, though all of them are in error. For these (the Ash'aris) say: what is in the mushaf is not the speech of Allah, it is an expression of it; and those say: the speech of Allah is created; and they say: it is an expression of the speech of Allah, which is created. Whoever reflects on this view will find it in the extreme of falsehood.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a reminder from Allah, glorified and exalted, to His servants of His blessings upon them. This appears in the Qur'an in many places, such as His saying ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. Sometimes it is general, as in this verse, and sometimes specific, such as His saying ﴿And remember when you were few and He made you many﴾ [al-A'raf 86], and what is similar to that. Allah reminds the servants of blessings only for the sake of the obligation of thanking them, because the obligation of thanking the Benefactor is established by revelation and by reason. As for revelation, the Qur'an is full of it: "Be thankful", "Be thankful to Me", "Be thankful to Allah", and what is similar. As for reason, it is because it is not chivalry to repay a blessing with wrongdoing and disbelief. Thus thanking the Benefactor is obligatory by revelation and by reason. And the benefit of reminding of blessings is what? Carrying out thanks.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of ascribing a person to his mother if he has no father, by His saying ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary﴾. Can a person have a mother without a father? The answer: yes, that is in the case where the husband disowns the child, and he is disowned under the conditions mentioned by the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them. Likewise, the child of fornication, if the fornicator does not claim him, has a mother but no father. If the fornicator does claim him, the matter is subject to a well-known disagreement, and the majority of scholars hold that he is not attributed to him, based on the general statement of the Prophet ﷺ: "For the fornicator is the stone." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2053) and Muslim (1457/36) from the hadith of 'A'isha.]

But if someone says: if ascribing him to his mother brings questions, and breaks his heart, and his mother is harmed, is it to be avoided?
The answer: yes, it is to be avoided, because ascribing him to his mother when he has no father is by way of permissibility and allowance. When it entails what harms its owner, it is avoided in favour of ascribing him to another. To whom? We say: he is ascribed to a name that is valid for every person, such as: 'Abd Allah, 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Abd al-Karim, 'Abd al-Latif, and what is similar. So based on this, we say: the original rule for one who has no father is that he be ascribed to his mother. If harm or injury is feared from that, he is ascribed to one whose name fits everyone.

* Among the benefits of the verse: that the prophets, peace be upon them, are obliged to give thanks just as those to whom they were sent are obliged. For Allah commanded Jesus to mention His blessing upon him and upon his mother. We say: yes, it is obligatory, and they (the prophets) are the most diligent of people in giving thanks for blessings. Indeed, "their leader Muhammad ﷺ used to stand in prayer at night until his feet swelled and cracked, and it was said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your earlier and later sins?' He said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1130) and Muslim (2819/79) from the hadith of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah's blessing upon the parents is a blessing upon the child, by His saying ﴿upon you and upon your mother﴾. There is no doubt that it is a blessing upon the child just as it is a blessing upon the parent. Is a blessing upon the child a blessing upon the parent by equality or by priority? By priority, because the child is a part of his father, as the Prophet ﷺ said of Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her: "She is a part of me; what troubles her troubles me." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5230) and Muslim (2449/93) from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama.] So Allah's blessing upon the child is, in reality, a blessing from Allah upon the parent.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, exalted is He, strengthens human beings with angels, by His saying ﴿when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit﴾.

* Among its benefits: this distinction for Jibril, peace be upon him: that he strengthens the prophets and messengers.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the honourable title for whom? For Jibril: ﴿the Holy Spirit﴾. Al-Quds means purity and freedom from every defect. He, that is Jibril, peace be upon him, is "dhu mirra", meaning of good form, and he is strong, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿possessor of power﴾ [al-Takwir 20], and he has a standing with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿with the Possessor of the Throne, honoured﴾.

The Jews hate Jibril, while the Muslims love Jibril, because Jibril is charged with revelation, by which the life of the ummah is brought. Those (the Jews) dislike Jibril and say that he brings punishment; but he brings punishment upon whom? Upon the one who deserves it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this great sign which Allah gave to Jesus: that he speaks to people in the cradle and in middle age alike. That is, he speaks with weighty, eloquent, wondrous speech while in the cradle, whereas people usually do not speak in the cradle; rather they produce incomprehensible sounds. But this is one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, just as Jesus's very origin was one of the signs of Allah. We have already mentioned what Allah, exalted is He, related of Jesus's speech in the cradle when the people of Mary said to her: ﴿Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste﴾ [Maryam 28], ﴿so she pointed to him﴾ [Maryam 29]. Then he said?
* Students: ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ [Maryam 29].
* The Shaykh: Yes, they said: how can we speak? But he said: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive. And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a tyrant or wretched. And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I will die, and the day I will be raised alive﴾ [Maryam 30-33]. Wondrous, eloquent speech. But Allah is over all things competent.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the specification of blessing by knowledge, nobility and wisdom, and that it is more specific than blessing in general. For general blessing was mentioned earlier: ﴿Remember My favour upon you and upon your mother﴾. But knowledge was singled out, when He said: ﴿and when I taught you the Scripture and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel﴾. Accordingly, the seeker of knowledge must thank Allah, exalted is He, for His blessing upon him in singling him out with knowledge, which has been denied to many people. When Allah bestows upon him, along with knowledge, worship and calling to Allah, it becomes a blessing above a blessing. How many people have strayed from the right path! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 116]. When a person feels Allah's blessing upon him in knowledge, worship and calling, he increases in joy, happiness, perseverance and patience in what he is upon: seeking knowledge, increasing worship, and strengthening the call to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the specification of wisdom, which is knowing the secrets of the Shari'a, its aims and its fruits. Knowing this undoubtedly increases faith and increases a person's insight into the laws of Allah.
And they (the laws) are from one Wise and All-Knowing. For this reason we say: it is not possible that in clear reason there exists anything that contradicts sound transmitted text. This principle, take it as a consistent rule: it is not possible that in clear reason there exists anything that contradicts sound transmitted text. If you find something that contradicts it, know that the matter is necessarily one of two things: either your reason is not clear, meaning there are doubts which caused the truth to be hidden from it, or desires which have obliterated it; we ask Allah for well-being. Or the text is not sound: it is a weak hadith, or fabricated against the Messenger ﷺ, or something similar. As for clear reason free from doubts and desires, and sound transmission, it is impossible for them to contradict each other ever.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Torah and the Gospel are two books from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We have said before that joining them to "the Book" is an instance of the specific joined to the general, if we do not say that what is meant by "the Book" is writing.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, power to give life to the dead and to breathe spirit into inanimate matter, from His saying ﴿and when you shape from clay like the form of a bird﴾.

* Among its benefits: the use of the word "creation" for what the maker has made. For example, if you make a door you say: "I created a door." What supports this is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun 14], and His saying in the authentic hadith: "It is said to the image-makers: give life to what you have created." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2105) and Muslim (2107/96) from the hadith of 'A'isha.]
If someone says: if you establish the attribute of creating for the created being, what is the difference between the creating of the Creator and the creating of the created being?
The answer: the difference is very great. The creating of the Creator is bringing into existence from non-existence, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills: ﴿He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran 6]. The creating of the created being is transforming what Allah created into another attribute. Otherwise, where does the origin come from? From Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Can anyone make gold from stone? No. But one can make jewellery from gold, and make from it the shape of an animal, as the Children of Israel made the ornaments they had taken from the people of Pharaoh into a calf. So the creating attributed to the Creator and the creating attributed to the created being have diverged. The creating of the created being means transforming a thing from one thing into another, not its essence but its attributes. As for the creating of the Creator, it is bringing into existence from non-existence, and no one can do this.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave Jesus a sign that baffles the scholars of the craft which was famous in his time. It is said that Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, was famous in his time for medicine and had advanced greatly in it. So Jesus brought signs which the physicians could not perform, just as magic was widespread in the time of Moses, so Moses brought signs that nullified their magic; and just as eloquence was widespread among the Arabs in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, so Allah, exalted is He, brought a Book which defeated them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that He, glorified and exalted, chooses from among the signs those that are most miraculous. He did not bless Jesus with creating a rabbit or a cat or something similar, but a bird, because flight in the air is more eloquent than walking on the ground. So Allah chose for him to create what? A bird, that is, in the form of a bird.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that breathing has an effect on bodies when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills it to have an effect. For he breathed into the bird he had made and it became what? It became a bird, as in the other reading. When he breathed into it, it became a living creature among the birds, then it flew, to confirm that the spirit had entered it. Hence the recitation for the sick is by way of spitting (nafth), and spitting, as we all know, involves breath and saliva, and this is effective by Allah's permission. For this reason, if the reciter were to recite and take saliva on his finger and moisten the place of pain with it, or moisten the patient with it, I do not think it would benefit; there must be breath together with saliva.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: what Allah, exalted is He, gave Jesus of signs in healing the one born blind, who was created without eyes or sight. This is evidence of Allah's power. It appears, and Allah knows best, that he healed him immediately, without needing treatment or waiting. It appears that he healed him at once, as happened to the Prophet ﷺ with the eye of Abu Qatada, may Allah be pleased with him, when it was struck at Uhud and protruded onto his cheek. The eye had come out onto the cheek, so he was brought to the Messenger, peace be upon him, who took the eye and returned it to its place, and it came back as it was immediately. [Related by Abu Ya'la (1549) from the hadith of Qatada ibn al-Nu'man.] Glory be to Allah the Mighty! No physician can reach such power. It appears that Jesus's healing of the blind and the leper occurred immediately, without treatment or hesitation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this great sign given to Jesus, that he brings the dead out of their graves, by His saying ﴿and when you bring forth the dead by My permission﴾. No one is able to do this. As for whether the dead person remains alive after coming out or does not remain, we have no say in this, and we should not speak of it. Why? Because the verse restricts it to bringing him out of his grave. As for whether he remains and lives among people, or dies after coming out and appearing to people and is then buried again, we have no interest in knowing this, and we have no right to ask about it, because the verse is accomplished without it.

In these four sentences (the bird, healing the blind, healing the leper, raising the dead) there is evidence that no human, however much he is given, can achieve his purpose except by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For every sentence or every word was restricted by Allah, exalted is He, to what? To His permission, lest a claimant claim that creatures have independent action in their deeds. This benefit has a branch, which is: the refutation of the Qadariyya. Who are the Qadariyya? They are those who say that a human is independent in his deeds, and Allah has no will in them. The human eats and drinks, enters and leaves, moves and rests by complete will, with which Allah has no connection. This amounts to affirming a creator alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or affirming a cause of events alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the Qadariyya were called the Magians of this ummah, because the Magians say that cosmic events have two creators: darkness and light. These (the Qadariyya) say that events in the universe have two originators, each independent of the other: the actions of servants are independent by the servants, to the extent that some of them say that Allah does not know the actions of servants except what has occurred, and what has not occurred He does not know, Mighty and Majestic. Thus they ascribed ignorance to Allah, blessed and exalted, in what is within His dominion, blessed and exalted.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's permission, and it should be known that permission attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, divides into two kinds: cosmic, decreed permission, and legislative, devotional permission. An example of cosmic permission is this verse: ﴿by My permission﴾. An example of legislative permission is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [al-Shura 21]. Did Allah not permit it legislatively or decreed? Legislatively? 
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And decreed? He has permitted it, for He enabled these people to legislate for their peoples what Allah had not permitted, and enabled the peoples to worship by this innovated law, but not legislatively. So the permission attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, divides into?
* Student: Yes (...).

Shaykh: Good. The example of the cosmic permission is this verse: ﴿You bring forth the dead by My permission﴾. The example of the legislative permission is: ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [ash-Shura 21]. The benefit of knowing the two types is this: we believe that what Allah has permitted by decree must occur, and what He has not permitted cannot occur. As for the legislative permission, what Allah has permitted legislatively may or may not occur, and what He has not permitted may or may not occur. Yes, this is the difference.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warding off harm from a person is one of Allah's blessings upon him. For this reason Allah bestowed it as a favour upon the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe﴾ [al-Hajj 38]. Whenever a person is firmer in faith in Allah, the Almighty, the more Allah defends him. The empowering of some people over him to harm him is nothing but like the afflicting of the messengers and prophets with illness, for the sake of what? The elevation of ranks. Otherwise, there is no doubt that there were imams of this ummah who were harmed most severely. Indeed, the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, were harmed, as the Almighty said: ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient﴾ [al-Ahqaf 35], and ﴿Messengers before you were indeed denounced﴾ [al-An'am 34]. Yes, ﴿they were patient over what they were denied and harmed﴾. But this is by way of elevation of ranks. From where do we take this benefit, that Allah defends the believers? From His saying: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110].

* Among the benefits of the verse: encouragement of the caller to Allah, the Almighty, who brings clear signs, for he is exposed to what? To harm. This is because of His saying: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs.﴾ Every person who calls to Allah and brings proofs and evidences will inevitably be subjected to whoever subjects him, but Allah, the Exalted, by His power and might, turns it away from him: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs.﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebellion of the Children of Israel who disbelieved, as they claimed that this was sorcery. Rather, they limited it to: ﴿This is nothing but manifest magic﴾, meaning it cannot possibly be true.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that magic may be hidden, or that the cause of magic may be concealed. They said: how can 'Isa heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life by Allah's permission? How can this be? This is magic. If someone stood over a lifeless body and said, "Rise," and it rose, what would people say?

* Student: A sorcerer.

* Shaykh: Yes, they would say: "This is a sorcerer. How can the dead rise?" They deceived, may Allah protect us, the servants of Allah, and they called the signs of the prophets "manifest magic."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the believers perceive the truth and know that it is true, because such a statement as ﴿This is nothing but manifest magic﴾ comes only from the people of disbelief. As for the believer, he believes in the signs, sees that they are true, and his faith in them increases.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that 'Isa, upon him be blessings and peace, like the other messengers, brought clear signs, meaning manifest ones that are not unclear to anyone. The Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, informed that: "There is no prophet whom Allah sent except that He gave him signs such that people would believe upon their like."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (4981) and Muslim (152/239) from Abu Hurayrah.]] Were it not for this, people would have an excuse not to believe; that is, were it not for the signs with the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, people would have an excuse for not believing. Accordingly, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [an-Nisa' 165] is restricted to their having been given what? Signs upon the like of which people believe. The signs of the prophets are of many kinds, unified by being both immaterial and sensory. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned a very, very valuable chapter at the end of his book al-Jawab al-Sahih liman baddala din al-Masih, in which he mentioned the signs of the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, and said: his signs are of two types, sensory and immaterial, and the sensory ones are of the horizons and of the earth. He explained this fully. The greatest of his signs, indeed the greatest signs, is this Qur'an, which was a sign in its own time and after it until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason he, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "What I have been given is a revelation Allah revealed to me," or words similar to it, "so I hope to be the most numerous of them in following on the Day of Resurrection."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (4981) and Muslim (152/239) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] Because the Qur'an remains, whereas the signs of the prophets ended with their lifetimes only. Their peoples soon altered the books after them: neither the People of the Torah, nor the People of the Gospel, nor the other books.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, what is the difference between irade (will) and idhn (permission)?

* Shaykh: And idhn? No, they are close in meaning, but idhn is more forceful in effect. For example, I want you to do something, and I permit you to do it; the latter is stronger. But with respect to the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, they are close.

* Student: We said that the creation of Allah, glorified and exalted, is bringing into existence from nothing, and the creation of servants is transforming one thing into another. Is 'Isa's making of a bird from this the creation of Allah...?

* Shaykh: No, it is the creation of the created. Every person can make something and fashion it into the shape of a bird.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: He did not bring this into existence. Its origin is clay, and clay is created by Allah, the Almighty, before it was shaped into the form of a bird.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And when I inspired the disciples, saying: "Believe in Me and in My Messenger." They said: "We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims." (111) When the disciples said: "O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table spread from the heaven?" He said: "Fear Allah, if you are believers." (112) They said: "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that you have indeed spoken truth to us, and that we may be among its witnesses." (113) Isa, son of Maryam, said: "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread from the heaven, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers." (114) Allah said: "Indeed I will send it down upon you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 111–115].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and My Messenger﴾. The (idh) here, as we have already gone over, is an object of a verb omitted, the estimate being: "Remember when I inspired." And His saying: ﴿to believe in Me﴾, the (an) here is explanatory (tafsiriyyah), because when it occurs after a verb that contains the meaning of speech without its letters, it is called explanatory; and inspiration (wahy) is a verb that contains the meaning of speech without its letters. Among examples of this is His saying: ﴿We inspired to him: "Construct the ship"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 27]. So (an) here, the grammarians parse it as explanatory. ﴿to believe in Me and in My Messenger﴾: he repeated the preposition in His saying ﴿and in My Messenger﴾, and it is coordinated with His saying ﴿in Me﴾, because when it is coordinated upon an attached pronoun, the preposition that was in the first element is repeated; this is the most well-known usage in the Arabic language, though speech sometimes departs from the original, such as His saying: ﴿and fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ according to one reading, while the well-known reading is ﴿and the wombs﴾ [an-Nisa 1], and such as His saying: ﴿and disbelief in Him and the Sacred Masjid﴾ [al-Baqarah 217], and He did not say "and in the Sacred Masjid." Otherwise, the rule is that when it is coordinated upon an attached pronoun, the preposition is repeated.

﴿They said: "We believe"﴾ — this is the answer to ﴿to believe in Me﴾. ﴿and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾. In such a case — i.e., ﴿that we are Muslims﴾ — it is permissible that the nun be doubled (shaddah) and that it not be doubled. If it is doubled, the pronoun ﴿bi-annana﴾ must be brought; and if it is not doubled, the nun is assimilated into the nun of the pronoun, becoming: "bi-anna muslimun." This has come in the Qur'an.

﴿When the disciples said﴾: this is also a resumptive sentence (jumlah isti'nafiyyah); the operator of (idh) is omitted, the estimate being: "Remember when the disciples said: O Isa, son of Maryam." Isa is a vocative (munada), and in such a case it is built on the damma in a position of nasb; but (ibn) came in the accusative, being an adjective or an appositive (ʿatf bayan), and it did not follow its described noun. Why? Because it is in an idafah construction. Therefore you say: "Ya Zaydu bna Abdillah," and do not say "Ya Zaydu bnu Abdillah," because if the operator — namely the governing element — were applied to it directly, it would put it in the accusative. So if the operator, when applied directly, would put it in the accusative, how much more so when the operator reaches it only through an intermediary. What intermediary?

Student: The substitution (badaliyyah).

Shaykh: The first noun is an appositive or a substitute.

﴿can your Lord﴾ has two readings: the reading ﴿hal yastatiʿu rabbuka﴾ and the reading ﴿hal tastatiʿu rabbaka﴾, and both are among the seven canonical readings. As for ﴿hal yastatiʿu rabbuka﴾, it is verb and subject; as for ﴿hal tastatiʿu rabbaka﴾, it is verb, attached subject, and object. The attached subject in (hal tastatiʿu) refers back to whom? To Isa.

﴿that He send down upon us a table spread from the heaven﴾: His saying ﴿from the heaven﴾ is a prepositional phrase functioning as an adjective of (ma'idah), because when a prepositional phrase or verb comes after an indefinite noun, it is an adjective, and if it comes after a definite noun, it is a circumstantial (hal).

He said: ﴿Fear Allah, if you are believers﴾. His saying ﴿if you are believers﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿Fear Allah﴾, because faith implies God-consciousness, and it is the condition in His saying ﴿Fear Allah﴾.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples﴾: is ﴿inspired﴾ here the legislative revelation (wahy shar'i) or the cosmic inspirational revelation (wahy kawni ilhami)? On this there are two opinions among the scholars. Some said it is legislative revelation, meaning: I inspired them through Isa; for it is known that legislative revelation is only for prophets and messengers, but I inspired them legislatively through their prophet Isa, peace be upon him. As for if it is cosmic revelation, then what is meant is inspiration (ilham), as in His saying: ﴿And We inspired the mother of Musa: "Suckle him"﴾ [al-Qasas 7] — We inspired, inspiration of ilham or legislative revelation? Ilham. And as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee: "Take for yourself houses in the mountains"﴾ [an-Nahl 68] — this is inspiration of ilham, and it is cosmic revelation, since it concerns creation.

If someone says: Is it not possible to take the verse as meaning both meanings together, so that Allah inspired their prophet Isa to convey that to them, and inspired them to accept it? The answer: yes, or no? Yes, it is possible to take the revelation as both meanings together.

And His saying ﴿the disciples﴾: the disciples (al-hawariyyun) are the pure, select companions. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every prophet has a disciple (hawari), and my disciple is az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7261) and Muslim (2415/48) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah] — may Allah be pleased with him. So the disciples are the select companions. Consider how these were the select companions of his, and what they did afterwards while being select. Compare these select ones with the select of this Ummah, and you will find a great difference, just as if you compared the select of the people of Musa you would find a great difference between them and the select of this Ummah — which shows you the virtue of this Ummah, which Allah chose to follow this noble Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

﴿to believe in Me and in My Messenger﴾: ﴿to believe in Me﴾: faith in Allah the Mighty and Majestic includes belief in His existence, belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes — meaning it includes four things. Belief in His existence is against those communists who say: there is no lord; there are only natures interacting and producing one another, and otherwise there is no lord — and Allah forbid — for He has sealed their hearts; we ask Allah for well-being. Belief in His lordship is a refutation of those who say that Allah the Exalted has a helper in creation or has a partner. For this reason Allah negated that in His saying: ﴿Say: "Call upon those you claim besides Allah; they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in them, and He has no supporter among them." And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba 22–23].

Belief in His divinity, meaning His being singled out in divinity, is a refutation of whom? Of those who set up with Allah another god to worship as they worship Allah, like the polytheists of Quraysh. Belief in His names and attributes is a refutation of two groups: the Mu'attilah and the Mumaththilah. The Mumaththilah associated partners with Allah, saying for example: "Allah has a face like our faces, and a hand like our hands, and an eye like our eyes," and such things; these are polytheists, are they not?

The second: the Mu'attilah, who negate the face, hand, eye, foot, descent, and istiwa' and such things; these are negators, and they have a share in the saying of Pharaoh: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ [al-Qasas 38], even though they do not negate divinity but negate the names and attributes. Whoever believes in a lord who is not described with hearing or sight, nor wisdom or might, nor power, nor coming or istiwa' — has he believed in a true Lord? No.

So belief in Allah the Mighty and Majestic includes four matters: belief in His existence, belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes, and what is meant is singling Him out in these things.

﴿and in My Messenger﴾: that is Isa, peace be upon him. Belief in one messenger includes the command to believe in all the messengers; the command to believe in one messenger includes belief in all the messengers, because denying one messenger is denying all the messengers. Have you not read the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 105], and was there any messenger before Nuh? No, there was no messenger before Nuh; yet He said ﴿denied the messengers﴾, because whoever denies one of a kind has denied the whole kind. If they believe in Isa, they have believed in all the messengers, including Muhammad, peace be upon him, for Isa gave glad tidings of him.

﴿They said: "We believe"﴾: they said with their tongues, "We believe." ﴿and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾: to whom did they say this? To Allah or to Isa? If Isa was the one who commanded them, they would be saying it to Isa: "We believe," and "bear witness that we are Muslims." They confessed and called upon witnesses. When a person confesses and calls witnesses, the witnessing of others prevents him from denying later; for a person may confess by himself, but if there is no one to testify against him, he may deny. But they confessed with their tongues and called upon witnesses — whom did they call upon? They called upon Isa, if the meaning of "they said" is to Isa. But if the meaning is that they said it to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, then the one called as witness here is Allah, blessed and exalted.

﴿that we are Muslims﴾: i.e., submissive to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. There is no submission except with faith that Allah the Exalted is the One who commands and forbids. Know that when Islam is mentioned alone it includes faith, and when faith is mentioned alone it includes Islam; and when both are combined, Islam becomes the outward and faith the inward: Islam is the outward deeds, the utterances of the tongue and actions of the limbs; faith is the inward deeds, beliefs of the hearts, their love, hope, and other things.

﴿When the disciples said﴾: i.e., remember, O Muhammad, when the disciples — the chosen ones from the people of Isa — said:

﴿O Isa, son of Maryam﴾: look at this dry address — they did not say "O Messenger of Allah" or "O Prophet of Allah." They said: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table spread from the heaven?﴾ "Can He send down": this poses a great difficulty with this reading, because their doubt about the power of Allah implies disbelief. So scholars were troubled: how could they say this, being the disciples?

We answer in response to this: either "istita'ah" (ability) is interpreted as "irada" (will), and this is permissible in the speech of the Arabs. You say to your companion: "O so-and-so, can you walk with me to so-and-so? I will visit him," while you know he is able; but what is meant? Do you want to walk with me? So ﴿can your Lord﴾ means "does your Lord will," and there is no doubt in their minds about His being capable, the Mighty and Majestic.

Or another answer is given: they believe in His general power, but a person may have doubt about a specific power, like the man who said to his family, while he was extravagant against himself: "When I die, burn me, then scatter me in the sea — that is, in the sea — for by Allah, if Allah has power over me He will punish me with a punishment with which He will not punish anyone among the worlds" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3481) and Muslim (2756/25) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Was that man fearful or not? He was fearful of Allah, and had no doubt that He is capable, but in general; as for this specific act, he said: perhaps if he is burned and scattered in the sea, Allah will not be able over him.

So the answer becomes twofold: the first aspect: that "istita'ah" means "qudrah" (power); the second aspect: that they had faith in Allah's power over everything, but in the details a person may hesitate about their occurrence and need added reassurance. Look at Zakariyya and look at Maryam: when Allah gave him the good news that He would grant him a son, what did he say? He said: ﴿"How can I have a son, when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?"﴾ [Maryam 8]. How could this be? Allah said to him: ﴿"So said your Lord: it is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing"﴾ [Maryam 9] — meaning, look at your origin: ﴿I created you before, when you were nothing﴾. So He is capable of creating a child; yet he asked for a sign of the realization of what he was given good news of.

There is a third opinion which says: ﴿hal yastatiʿu﴾ is not from "istita'ah" in the sense of inability, but from "ita'ah" (obedience): i.e., will your Lord obey you if you ask Him to send down a table to us, or will He not obey? This opinion returns to the first meaning, which is "irada" (will), because "ita'ah" means submission: so the meaning is: if you ask your Lord, will He obey you? So "istita'ah" here is not from the category of capacity and power, but from the category of obedience, which is submission when asked.

﴿He said: "Fear Allah, if you are believers"﴾: "Fear Allah" means: refrain from this request, or from this question which contains a request. ﴿if you are believers﴾: i.e., believers in His decree, content with His judgment: if He enriches you, He enriches you; if He deprives you, He deprives you; for the one who is truly a believer and truly God-fearing is content with Allah's decree and destiny, and does not ask for things outside the bounds of custom.

This is on the reading ﴿hal yastatiʿu﴾. As for the reading ﴿hal tastatiʿu rabbaka﴾, the meaning is: can you ask your Lord to send down to us a table from the heaven? Here "istita'ah" refers back to whom? To Isa: i.e., can you ask Allah, or are you too shy and do not ask? On this reading there is no difficulty, praise be to Allah. On the first reading you have learned the aspects by which the difficulty is answered.

﴿that He send down upon us a table spread from the heaven﴾: "ma'idah" is sometimes applied to food, and its original usage is to the platform upon which the food is placed; this is the original, but it may also be applied to the food. Here the meaning — and Allah knows best — is both together: a food platform, which is a tray (khiwan or khuwwan — I do not vouch for the vocalization), and upon it the food.

﴿from the heaven﴾: i.e., from above.

﴿They said: "We wish"﴾: i.e., they informed him of the reason, that they asked this strange question. ﴿"We wish to eat from it"﴾: so they were hungry. And this resembles, in some respects, though what is better than it is what the people of Musa said to him: ﴿"Call upon your Lord to bring forth for us of what the earth grows: its herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions"﴾ [al-Baqarah 61]. But these asked for something to descend from heaven: ﴿"We wish to eat from it."﴾ Second: ﴿"and that our hearts may be at rest"﴾: "tatma'inn" means to settle, with no unease or doubt. This is a second purpose. Third: ﴿"and that we may know that you have indeed spoken truth to us"﴾. How can they know that he spoke truly? Yes: he told them he was the Messenger of Allah; if he brought a clear sign, then he spoke truly, and if not, then he did not. But how can they say ﴿"and that we may know that you have indeed spoken truth to us"﴾ when they had already affirmed his truthfulness? This is a difficulty. The answer: either the meaning is "and that we may increase in knowledge that you have spoken truth to us" — and there is no doubt that whenever signs indicating the truthfulness of the speaker are found, knowledge of the speaker's truthfulness increases; or some of them had hesitation, and knowledge removes doubt and hesitation. But which is preferable: to think well of them and say "we know," meaning "we increase in knowledge," or to say that perhaps some of them had hesitation?

The first meaning is better: ﴿وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا﴾ means "you have informed us of the truth." It is said: sadaqahu (he told him the truth), meaning he informed him of the truth. It is also said: sadaqahu, meaning he fulfilled what he promised him, as in the saying of Allah, ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ [Al 'Imran 152], meaning: "when you were killing them by His permission," so it means He fulfilled what He had promised. It is also said: sadaqahu, when he informs him of the truth even if what he informed of did not come to pass, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Devil: "He spoke the truth to you, though he is a liar." [Reported by al-Bukhari (3275) from Abu Hurayrah.]

﴿وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ This is a fourth matter: that we witness it with our own eyes without being told about it, for reports are not like direct witnessing.

* From the benefits of the two verses: the affirmation of the revelation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; from His saying ﴿إِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ﴾. The revelation of Allah is divided into two kinds: revelation of legislation (wahy shar') and revelation of inspiration (wahy ilham). The first relates to the Shari'ah, and the second relates to the cosmos, and you have heard examples of this in the tafsir.

* From the benefits of this verse: that 'Isa (peace be upon him) had disciples (hawariyyun), meaning: companions who were pure in their affection. Mention the end of Surah al-Saff: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصَارَ اللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنْصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Saff 14]. And as you have heard in the hadith: "Every prophet has a hawari, and my hawari is al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7261) and Muslim (2415/48) from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.] This is without doubt a virtue of al-Zubayr. But Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If I were to take a close friend (khalil) from my Ummah, I would have taken Abu Bakr." [Reported by al-Bukhari (3656) from Ibn 'Abbas.]

* From the benefits of this noble verse: faith in Allah is not complete except with faith in His messengers; from His saying ﴿أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained that faith is "to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in divine decree, both its good and its bad." [Reported by Muslim (8/1) from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.] These pillars are necessary in faith, so whoever lacks one of them is not a believer.

* From the benefits of this verse: the response of the disciples to what was revealed to them, when they said: "We believe."

* From the benefits of the verse: the permissibility of omitting what is known. From where? ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا﴾ without saying "in You and in Your messenger," because this is understood. The absolute is interpreted in light of the restricted when it is known. So if a person concludes a contract and mentions conditions at the offer, and the other says "I accept," or "I accept the sale," for example, and he says: "I sell you this house on condition that I live in it for a year," and the other says: "I accept the sale," does the condition hold? Yes, it holds, because the wording of the sale implies this condition even if it is not stated, since it is known from the context.

* From the benefits of this verse: the permissibility of establishing a matter by calling witnesses to it; from His saying ﴿اشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾. In the transmitted supplication: "O Allah, I have entered the evening calling You to witness, and calling to witness the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels, Your prophets, and all of Your creation, that You are Allah, there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger." [Reported by Abu Dawud (5069) and al-Tirmidhi (3501) from Anas ibn Malik, without the phrase "and Your prophets." In al-Mu'jam al-Awsat of al-Tabarani (9356): "and I call to witness Your angels, Your prophets and Your messengers, and all of Your creation, to my testimony against myself that I testify that You are Allah, there is no god but You."] This is among the morning and evening remembrances, though there is disagreement over the authenticity of the hadith.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that faith is Islam. From His saying ﴿آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 111]. They did not say "believers"; they said "Muslims," which indicates that faith is Islam. A group of scholars held this view and said there is no difference between Islam and faith, citing verses like this one, and also citing the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَنْ كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٣٥) فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35, 36]. However, this view stated absolutely is open to question. The correct position is that when Islam is mentioned alone, it includes faith, and when it is mentioned together with faith, it has a different meaning. This distinction is shown by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ [al-Hujurat 14], meaning it has not entered yet but it is close to entering, since "lamma" indicates negation with the nearness of what is negated. ﴿وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾. So how do we explain this verse? We explain it by saying that they combined faith and Islam, so faith is in the hearts and Islam is in the limbs, meaning they believed and submitted completely to the commands of Allah and His messenger.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ﴾ to the end [al-Ma'idah 112].

* From the benefits of this verse: that the disciples, despite being sincere, had some discourtesy; from their saying: ﴿يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾.

If someone says: perhaps their law permitted them to call their prophet by his name, unlike this law, since Allah says: ﴿لَا تَجْعَلُوا دُعَاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعَاءِ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضًا﴾ [al-Nur 63]? We say: let that be so, but is it good manners for them to address 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) by his name, while they want him to ask Allah to send this table, or is it more fitting, since they want him to ask Allah, to call him by the description of prophethood and messengerhood, since that is more appropriate and closer to the answering of their request? The answer: the second, without doubt. In any case, this address certainly contains some discourtesy.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that these disciples wanted from the signs what would fill their bellies. The evidence: the first thing they began with was eating: ﴿نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْهَا﴾, as soon as they began. This resembles the saying of the Jews when they were told: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا﴾ [al-Nisa 154]. What did they do? They entered upon their posteriors, on their buttocks, saying "hintah" (wheat), when they were commanded to say "hittah" (meaning: remove our sins from us). But they said: no, we want something else, which is filling the belly: wheat. These resemble that, and the origin is one, O brothers, the origin is one; they are all from the Children of Israel, so it is no wonder that their requests are similar. And Allah knows best.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوَارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ (١١١) إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ قَالَ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (١١٢) قَالُوا نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْهَا وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (١١٣) قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ وَارْزُقْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ (١١٤) قَالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَابًا لَا أُعَذِّبُهُ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 111-115].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوَارِيِّينَ﴾, and its tafsir has already been covered. Is this revelation to the disciples, or what?

* The student: There are two opinions: one is revelation through their prophet 'Isa; the second is inspiration.

* The Shaykh: That is, He revealed it to them through 'Isa.

* The student: Yes, and the second opinion is that it is inspiration.

* The Shaykh: That His revealing to them means inspiration.
Which of them is stronger?

* The student: We say the meaning includes both: legislative revelation and cosmic revelation.

* The Shaykh: Allah revealed to 'Isa a legislative revelation, and He revealed to them a decreed (qadari) revelation.
What is the meaning of al-hawariyyun?

* Student: The pure ones among his companions.

* The Shaykh: The pure ones among his companions.
The saying of Allah: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ has two readings. Recite them.

* Student: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ and ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ and ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ﴾.
On the first reading, is there a problem? This suggests they doubted Allah's power. What is the answer to that?

* Student: (...)

* The Shaykh: No, this example is not correct. It is like a man saying to his brother: "Can you walk with me? Can you go or come?" The point is that istita'ah means qudrah (ability). Another aspect?

* Student: That they believed in Allah's general power, but in the particular (...)

* The Shaykh: That is, they had faith in general power, but the power over a specific thing... this is one aspect of the answer. Second?

* Student: The meaning of ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ is: would your Lord obey you if you asked Him.

* Another student: They say it does not mean ability, but obedience: istita'ah means ita'ah.

* The Shaykh: Meaning?

* Student: Meaning, if you ask Him, i.e., can you ask Him.

* The Shaykh: That is, ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ means: would your Lord respond. This is the summary: would your Lord respond, from obedience in the sense of submission.

On the reading ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ﴾?

* Student: No problem.

* The Shaykh: No problem. What is the meaning?

* Student: That is, can you ask your Lord.

* The Shaykh: Can you ask your Lord? On this, there is no problem.

* Student: (...)

* The Shaykh: This resembles the saying of the Jews: "hintah," when they were told: "say hittah."

* From the benefits of this verse: that the occurrence of a thing gives more certainty than being informed about it. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The report is not like witnessing directly."
